29be9776c3b0.title: Wan-Move Motion-Control Image to Video
29be9776c3b0.description: Generate videos from a single image using Wan-Move, with fine-grained point-level motion control via trajectory guidance.
29be9776c3b0.metaDescription: Transform images into videos with precise motion control using the Wan-Move workflow in ComfyUI. Perfect for detailed image animations.
29be9776c3b0.extendedDescription: The Wan-Move Motion-Control Image to Video workflow is a sophisticated process designed to transform a single image into a dynamic video. Utilizing the Wan2.1 and Wan models, this workflow allows users to apply fine-grained motion control to specific points within an image, creating a seamless video output. At its core, the workflow leverages nodes such as WanMoveVisualizeTracks and GenerateTracks to define and visualize motion trajectories. The user can guide these motions using trajectory guidance, ensuring precise and controlled animation of image elements. The CreateVideo and SaveVideo nodes then compile these movements into a cohesive video file. This workflow is particularly useful for creators looking to animate still images with detailed motion paths, offering a high level of customization and control over the final video output.
howToUse: Load the workflow into ComfyUI and ensure all required models, such as Wan2.1 and Wan, are installed.
Use the LoadImage node to import the image you wish to animate.
Utilize the GenerateTracks node to define motion paths for specific points in the image. Visualize these paths with the WanMoveVisualizeTracks node.
Adjust the motion paths using the WanMoveTracksFromCoords node for precise control over the animation.
Compile the animated frames into a video using the CreateVideo node, then save the output with the SaveVideo node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating animated marketing materials from static images.
Developing educational content with dynamic visual aids.
Enhancing social media posts with engaging video content.
Producing artistic video projects from photographic stills.
Animating architectural or design visualizations for presentations.

faqItems.question: What models do I need for this workflow?
faqItems.answer: You need the Wan2.1 and Wan models to effectively use this workflow.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for any image?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can use any image, but results may vary based on the complexity and detail of the motion paths you create.

faqItems.question: How do I create motion paths?
faqItems.answer: You can create motion paths using the GenerateTracks node and visualize them with the WanMoveVisualizeTracks node. For more control, use the WanMoveTracksFromCoords node.

faqItems.question: Is there a way to preview the motion before finalizing the video?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can use the PreviewImage node to see how your motion paths will affect the image before creating the final video.

2a95da601676.title: Video Aspect Ratio Extension
2a95da601676.description: Extend any video to a custom aspect ratio. Convert vertical videos to horizontal format and vice versa. Includes an application mode for easy use.
2a95da601676.metaDescription: Extend videos from vertical to horizontal (and vice versa) with Kling O3 outpainting in ComfyUI. App mode UI, slicing, and audio passthrough included.
2a95da601676.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow converts vertical videos to horizontal (and vice versa) by outpainting new canvas areas while keeping the original content intact. It uses LoadVideo and GetVideoComponents to pull frames, FPS, and audio, then normalizes frame size with JWImageResizeByShorterSide so the shorter side matches your target resolution. A masking stage—powered by masquerade-nodes-comfyui and a custom utility node (UUID: 7594b5c0-2b90-4aeb-846b-e3eb8fa89f33)—defines where to synthesize new content versus where to preserve the source. The core transformation happens in KlingOmniProEditVideoNode running the Kling O3 model, which content-aware outpaints the added side bands to reach your target aspect. Video Slice lets you process in manageable chunks for stability and VRAM efficiency, and CreateVideo + SaveVideo assemble and write the final file, with optional audio passthrough from GetVideoComponents.

What makes this useful is that you don’t have to crop away important action. Instead, you reframe with horizontal/vertical offsets and extend the scene, maintaining motion continuity and subject integrity. The workflow is organized into groups—Input Video, Video Resize and Extend, and Video Outpaint—and includes an application mode for a simplified UI: set the target aspect, tweak offsets, and run. Note: this pipeline is optimized for 9:16 ↔ 16:9 conversions. For minor aspect changes or square (1:1), the Kling video edit node isn’t recommended; consider basic crop/pad instead.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the Input Video group. In LoadVideo, select your source clip. GetVideoComponents will expose frames, FPS, and audio.
In Video Resize and Extend, set JWImageResizeByShorterSide to your base resolution (e.g., 1080). This resizes frames by the shorter edge while preserving content for outpainting.

Choose your target orientation (16:9 or 9:16) and adjust the horizontal/vertical offsets as noted in the Note node. Reframe the subject before extension so the new canvas grows in the desired direction.

In the Video Outpaint group, verify the mask settings (masquerade-nodes-comfyui and the custom UUID node) so protected regions cover the subject and the outpaint area lies in the added borders. If exposed, widen the mask or increase feather.

Open the KlingOmniProEditVideoNode and select the Kling O3 model. Review strength/consistency parameters (if present) and ensure Video Slice is set to a chunk size your GPU can handle. For 1080p, start with moderate slices.

CreateVideo should receive frames and FPS (and audio if desired) from GetVideoComponents. Connect to SaveVideo, pick an output path, then run. Review results; if artifacts appear, reduce the outpaint width or refine offsets/mask and re-run.
suggestedUseCases: Reformat TikTok/Reels (9:16) footage for YouTube 16:9 without cropping out key action.
Convert landscape webinars or demos into vertical stories while preserving presenters and slides.
Extend gameplay or B‑roll to fill 9:16 for Shorts without letterboxing.
Reframe talking‑head interviews and outpaint background edges for platform‑specific aspect ratios.
Prepare ad creatives once and repurpose across vertical and horizontal placements.

faqItems.question: Does this preserve audio?
faqItems.answer: Yes—if you wire audio from GetVideoComponents into CreateVideo, the audio track is passed through. If you omit it, the output will be silent.

faqItems.question: What if I only need a slight aspect ratio change or a 1:1 square?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is optimized for 9:16 ↔ 16:9 conversions. For small tweaks or 1:1, use a basic crop/pad/resize pipeline instead of KlingOmniProEditVideoNode.

faqItems.question: How do I avoid artifacts or stretching in the outpainted borders?
faqItems.answer: Reduce the extension amount, improve your subject mask (wider and slightly feathered), and keep the subject centered with the offset controls. If available, increase temporal consistency in the Kling node and process with moderate Video Slice sizes.

faqItems.question: What are the hardware and performance tips?
faqItems.answer: For 1080p, a 12–16 GB GPU is recommended. If you hit VRAM limits, lower JWImageResizeByShorterSide, reduce outpaint width, and shorten Video Slice lengths. Passing original FPS from GetVideoComponents helps maintain smooth motion.

2a9b4417b44f.title: Z-Image: Text to Image
2a9b4417b44f.description: Foundation for creative freedom. Diverse aesthetics with exceptional photorealistic quality; ideal for fine-tuning; responsive to negative prompts; high generation diversity.
2a9b4417b44f.metaDescription: Transform text into stunning images with Z-Image: Text to Image workflow, offering photorealistic quality and diverse aesthetics.
2a9b4417b44f.extendedDescription:
The Z-Image: Text to Image workflow is designed to transform textual descriptions into high-quality images with a focus on photorealism and aesthetic diversity. Utilizing the Z-Image model, this workflow is particularly adept at producing images that are not only visually stunning but also highly responsive to both positive and negative prompts, allowing for fine-tuning and creative exploration. The workflow employs specific nodes such as SaveImage for output management and MarkdownNote for documentation, alongside a unique node type identified by the ID 9b9009e4-2d3d-445f-9be5-6063f465757e, which plays a crucial role in the image generation process.

Technically, this workflow leverages the qwen_3_4b.safetensors text encoder and the z_image_bf16.safetensors diffusion model to interpret and render textual inputs into images. The process involves running the diffusion model for 30 to 50 steps with a classifier-free guidance (cfg) scale of 3 to 5, ensuring a balance between adhering to the prompt and introducing creative variability. This setup makes the workflow particularly useful for artists and designers seeking to generate diverse image outputs from textual descriptions, providing a foundation for creative freedom and exploration.
howToUse: Load the Z-Image: Text to Image workflow in ComfyUI.
Input your desired text description into the text prompt field.
Adjust the diffusion steps between 30 to 50 for desired detail.
Set the cfg scale between 3 to 5 to control adherence to the prompt.
Run the workflow to generate the image.
Save the output using the SaveImage node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating concept art for visual storytelling.
Generating photorealistic images for marketing materials.
Exploring diverse aesthetic styles for design projects.
Producing fine-tuned images for digital art portfolios.
Developing responsive visual content for social media campaigns.

faqItems.question: What type of images can I generate with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: You can generate a wide range of images, from photorealistic scenes to diverse aesthetic styles, depending on your text prompts.

faqItems.question: How do negative prompts affect the image generation?
faqItems.answer: Negative prompts help steer the model away from undesired elements, allowing for more refined and targeted image outputs.

faqItems.question: What are the optimal settings for diffusion steps and cfg scale?
faqItems.answer: For most cases, 30 to 50 diffusion steps with a cfg scale of 3 to 5 provide a good balance between detail and creative variability.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for commercial projects?
faqItems.answer: Yes, as long as you comply with the licensing terms of the models and assets used within the workflow.

2c2f85053453.title: Tripo P1: Text to Model
2c2f85053453.description: Input a text description of a 3D model. Generate a game-ready 3D model with clean topology and optimized polygon counts
2c2f85053453.metaDescription: Text-to-3D in ComfyUI with Tripo P1. Generate, texture, (optionally) rig and retarget, then export clean .glb assets ready for real-time use.
2c2f85053453.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a short text description into a usable 3D asset using Tripo’s P1 text-to-3D model generation. The pipeline starts with TripoP1TextToModelNode, which sends your prompt to the Tripo model to synthesize an initial mesh. TripoConversionNode then prepares the geometry for real-time use—handling format conversion and typical cleanup tasks like scaling and orientation alignment—before TripoTextureNodeV2 bakes or refines PBR textures. If your asset needs to move, TripoRigNode can auto-rig compatible meshes, and TripoRetargetNode transfers motion from a reference rig or animation onto the new skeleton. Finally, SaveGLB exports a single .glb file you can preview on the web or import into DCC tools and engines.

Technically, the workflow keeps you inside ComfyUI while delegating the heavy 3D synthesis to Tripo via its dedicated nodes. Each stage is modular: you can generate a static prop from text and save immediately, or enable rigging and retargeting when producing characters. By chaining TripoP1TextToModelNode → TripoConversionNode → TripoTextureNodeV2 → (optional) TripoRigNode → (optional) TripoRetargetNode → SaveGLB, you get a clean, optimized, and consistently exported asset with minimal manual intervention. It’s especially useful for rapid prototyping, blockouts, and generating game-ready starting points that you can refine further in your preferred 3D tool.
howToUse: Load the workflow and enable the Tripo Toolset group: select the group and press Ctrl+B so its nodes are active.

Open TripoP1TextToModelNode and enter a concise prompt describing the object (e.g., "low-poly wooden chair, PBR, realistic"). If authentication is required for Tripo, add your credentials where the node or extension requests them.

Configure TripoConversionNode for your target scale/orientation and any mesh optimization options exposed by the node. Then set texture parameters in TripoTextureNodeV2 (e.g., texture resolution and material packing) to match your engine or DCC needs.

For animated or skinned assets, enable TripoRigNode to auto-rig (when applicable). Provide a compatible reference rig or animation to TripoRetargetNode if you want to transfer motion onto the new skeleton.
Run the graph. Inspect intermediate previews (mesh and textures) if your UI shows them. Make prompt or parameter adjustments if the silhouette, topology density, or texture fidelity need refinement.
When satisfied, use SaveGLB to export the final model as .glb. Test the asset in your DCC or game engine, and iterate on polycount/texture size/rig settings as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid prototyping of game props and level blockouts from quick text briefs.
Creating simple rigged characters for early animation tests using auto-rig + retarget.
Generating PBR-textured product mockups for AR or web previews.
Concept exploration for 3D art teams to align on style and silhouette before manual polish.
Educational demos to teach text-to-3D pipelines and real-time asset preparation.

faqItems.question: Do I need a Tripo account or API key?
faqItems.answer: If the Tripo nodes in your setup use the online service, you’ll be prompted to authenticate (e.g., API key or login) in the node or extension settings. Follow the prompts in TripoP1TextToModelNode and related nodes.

faqItems.question: Can I control polycount and texture size?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Use TripoConversionNode for geometry preparation (scale/orientation and any optimization controls exposed) and TripoTextureNodeV2 to set texture resolution and packing. Lower resolutions and simpler materials help keep assets lightweight for real-time.

faqItems.question: What kinds of prompts work best?
faqItems.answer: Be specific about object type, style, and materials (e.g., "stylized sci‑fi crate, hard-surface, orange painted metal, worn edges, 2k textures"). Avoid multi-object scenes; focus on a single, well-defined asset with a clear silhouette.

faqItems.question: How do I use the rigging and retargeting steps?
faqItems.answer: Enable TripoRigNode to add a compatible skeleton (best for humanoids or clearly segmentable creatures). Then feed a reference rig or animation into TripoRetargetNode to transfer motion. Verify bone naming/orientation matches your target for stable results.

2c4b652466d9.title: SDXL Simple
2c4b652466d9.metaDescription: Generate high-quality images with the SDXL model using ComfyUI's SDXL Simple workflow. Perfect for artists and designers.
2c4b652466d9.extendedDescription:
The 'SDXL Simple' workflow is designed to generate high-quality images by leveraging the capabilities of the SDXL model. This workflow utilizes a series of nodes to transform text prompts into stunning visual representations. The process begins with the 'CheckpointLoaderSimple' node, which loads the SDXL model with optimal settings. The 'CLIPTextEncode' node encodes the input text prompts, which are then processed by the 'KSamplerAdvanced' node to generate latent images with added noise. This noise is crucial as it allows the model to effectively denoise and refine the image. The 'VAEDecode' node plays a critical role by converting the latent data into visible images, which are subsequently saved using the 'SaveImage' node.

This workflow is particularly useful for artists and designers looking to create detailed and high-resolution images with minimal effort. By using the SDXL model, users can ensure that their images are generated with state-of-the-art techniques in AI image synthesis. The workflow's flexibility allows for the use of different SD model versions, making it adaptable to various creative needs. The inclusion of nodes like 'PrimitiveNode' and 'MarkdownNote' provides additional customization and documentation options, enhancing the user experience.
howToUse: Load the SDXL Simple workflow in ComfyUI.
Select your local SDXL model using the 'CheckpointLoaderSimple' node.
Input your desired text prompt in the 'CLIPTextEncode' node.
Run the workflow to generate a latent image with the 'KSamplerAdvanced' node.
Decode the latent image using the 'VAEDecode' node to view the final result.
Save the generated image using the 'SaveImage' node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating high-resolution concept art for digital media projects.
Generating unique backgrounds for graphic design work.
Producing detailed illustrations for storytelling or comics.
Developing custom visuals for marketing and advertising campaigns.
Exploring creative ideas and visual brainstorming.

faqItems.question: What models can I use with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: You can use the Base SDXL model, as well as SD1.5 and SD2.x models, by selecting them in the 'CheckpointLoaderSimple' node.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow handle text prompts?
faqItems.answer: The 'CLIPTextEncode' node encodes text prompts using optimal CLIP settings, allowing the model to accurately interpret and generate images based on the input text.

faqItems.question: Why is noise added to the latent image?
faqItems.answer: Noise is added to help the model denoise and refine the image, which is a crucial step in generating high-quality visuals.

faqItems.question: Can I customize the workflow settings?
faqItems.answer: Yes, while the workflow is set up with optimal settings, you can adjust nodes like 'PrimitiveNode' and 'MarkdownNote' for additional customization and documentation.

2cf9f9f6d205.title: Character & Outfit to Fashion Video
2cf9f9f6d205.description: Upload your character and clothing items or accessories. Generate a fashion photograph base and use as a reference to 8x grid images, together with multi-KeyFrame Video Stitching
2cf9f9f6d205.metaDescription: Transform character and outfit images into dynamic fashion videos using ComfyUI's Character & Outfit to Fashion Video workflow.
2cf9f9f6d205.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow, titled 'Character & Outfit to Fashion Video,' is designed to transform static images of characters and their clothing into dynamic fashion videos. The process begins by uploading images of characters and clothing items, which are then used to generate a fashion photograph base. This base image serves as a reference to create an 8x grid of images. The workflow utilizes a variety of models, including Google Gemini Image and Nano Banana Pro, to enhance the image-to-video conversion process. Key nodes like GeminiImage2Node and ImageBatch play a crucial role in processing and managing image data, while custom nodes such as comfyui-kjnodes and comfyui_essentials facilitate specific functionalities tailored to fashion video generation.

The technical backbone of this workflow involves a series of node operations that stitch together multiple keyframes into a seamless video. Nodes like SaveImage and LoadImage handle the initial image input and output, while RegexReplace and PrimitiveStringMultiline manage text and metadata processing. The workflow also employs advanced techniques such as multi-KeyFrame Video Stitching, enabled by nodes like SaveVideo and GetImagesFromBatchIndexed, to ensure smooth transitions and high-quality video output. This workflow is particularly useful for fashion designers, marketers, and content creators who wish to showcase clothing designs in a visually engaging format, leveraging AI to automate and enhance the creative process.
howToUse: Load the ComfyUI 'Character & Outfit to Fashion Video' workflow.
Upload your character and clothing images using the LoadImage node.
Generate a fashion photograph base with the GeminiImage2Node.
Create an 8x grid of images using the ImageBatch node for reference.
Utilize multi-KeyFrame Video Stitching to compile images into a video.
Save the final video output using the SaveVideo node.
suggestedUseCases: Fashion designers can create promotional videos for new clothing lines.
Content creators can generate dynamic video content for social media platforms.
Marketers can produce engaging advertisements showcasing fashion collections.
E-commerce platforms can enhance product listings with animated fashion videos.
Virtual fashion shows can be created for online audiences using this workflow.

faqItems.question: What types of images should I upload to this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Upload high-quality images of characters and clothing items for the best results.

faqItems.question: Can I customize the grid size for the image references?
faqItems.answer: The workflow is set to create an 8x grid by default, but you can adjust this by modifying the ImageBatch node settings.

faqItems.question: How long does it take to generate a video using this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The processing time depends on the complexity of the images and the performance of your hardware, but it typically takes a few minutes.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to add audio to the generated fashion video?
faqItems.answer: This workflow focuses on video generation; you can add audio using video editing software after exporting the video.

2da831d21d09.title: Batch Process Text Prompts From List
2da831d21d09.description: Loads and executes a workflow sequentially using prompts from a text list. Iterates through each entry to generate multiple outputs from a single batch operation.
2da831d21d09.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow that batch-processes a list of text prompts with Z-Image-Turbo, selecting one line per step via FL_PromptSelectorBasic and saving each image.
2da831d21d09.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow automates running a list of text prompts one-by-one and saving an image for each entry. It uses the custom FL_PromptSelectorBasic node to read a multiline prompt list and select a single line based on an index provided by a PrimitiveInt node. That selected prompt is then fed into the generation chain powered by the Z-Image-Turbo model, and the resulting image is written to disk by SaveImage. A MarkdownNote in the graph documents the intent and wiring so you can quickly see how the pieces fit together.

Under the hood, FL_PromptSelectorBasic exposes a text field where you paste prompts (one per line). The PrimitiveInt node supplies an index that determines which line is currently active. In a batch run, the index advances one step per batch iteration (when driven by your generation/driver node; listed here as ca7506c4-0f1a-4a77-9d2e-b9077eaf58d5), so each iteration consumes the next prompt from the list. This pattern is ideal for prompt A/B testing, producing sets of assets, or iterating through a campaign brief without manually editing the graph between runs.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and wait for all nodes to appear. Confirm Z-Image-Turbo is available in your models and that SaveImage is connected at the end of the chain.
Open FL_PromptSelectorBasic and paste your prompts into its prompts field, one prompt per line. Avoid quotes or commas; just one clean prompt per line.
Set the PrimitiveInt node to the line index you want to test (e.g., 0 for the first line) and run a single inference to verify the prompt flows into Z-Image-Turbo and produces an image.

For a full batch run, configure your generation/driver node (ca7506c4-0f1a-4a77-9d2e-b9077eaf58d5 in this workflow) to iterate once per prompt line. The FL_PromptSelectorBasic will advance one prompt per batch step via the connected index.
Optionally adjust SaveImage (e.g., filename prefix) so outputs are easy to identify. Then queue the batch. Each step will use the next prompt and save its result.
Review the outputs in your ComfyUI/output directory. If any prompt needs refinement, edit that line in FL_PromptSelectorBasic and re-run just that index with PrimitiveInt.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid prompt A/B testing to compare phrasing and subject variations side by side.
Producing cohesive social or marketing asset sets from a pre-approved prompt list.
Generating small datasets for prototyping or fine-tuning workflows that need varied prompts.
Creative exploration: iterate style or camera directions across the same subject list.
Content QA pipelines where each prompt maps to a checklist item or acceptance test.

faqItems.question: How does the index map to lines in FL_PromptSelectorBasic?
faqItems.answer: The PrimitiveInt provides the selected line’s index. Use 0 for the first line, 1 for the second, and so on. In batch mode, the connected driver advances the index one step per iteration.

faqItems.question: What happens if there are more batch steps than prompt lines?
faqItems.answer: When the index exceeds the number of lines, the selector returns an empty prompt. This can yield generic or unintended images. Match your batch iterations to the number of lines, or trim trailing blank lines.

faqItems.question: Can I keep my negative prompt and other generation settings fixed?
faqItems.answer: Yes. FL_PromptSelectorBasic only swaps the main text prompt. Keep your negative prompt, seed, and other generation parameters set in the Z-Image-Turbo chain and they will apply to every iteration.

faqItems.question: Where are images saved and how do I keep them organized?
faqItems.answer: SaveImage writes to the ComfyUI/output directory using its configured filename prefix. Set a clear prefix (e.g., zturbo_list_run_01) before batching so files are easy to track against your prompt list.

2da9ee24ad74.title: Seedance 2.0 + LLM Prompt Helper
2da9ee24ad74.description: This workflow uses two reference images and a simple text description to automatically generate a detailed Seedance 2.0-style prompt using an LLM. Instead of spending time figuring out complex prompting structure, the workflow analyzes your references and builds the prompt for you, making it much faster and easier to create high-quality results. The included LLM helper is designed to match the style and formatting that works well with Seedance 2.0, helping streamline the entire process while still giving you full control over the final output. Just drop in your references, describe the scene or motion you want, and the workflow handles the prompt generation automatically.
2da9ee24ad74.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Use two reference images and Gemini to auto-build Seedance 2.0 prompts, then generate consistent, high-quality videos fast.
2da9ee24ad74.extendedDescription:
Seedance 2.0 + LLM Prompt Helper is a ComfyUI workflow that turns two reference images and a short scene description into a detailed, Seedance-optimized prompt—then renders your video. It uses GeminiNode to analyze your references and expand your brief into the style and structure Seedance 2.0 expects, so you spend less time wrestling with prompt formatting and more time iterating on look, motion, and composition. The Seedance 2.0 generation runs through ByteDance2ReferenceNode, giving you reference-driven consistency from first frame to last.

Technically, the Reference Images group uses LoadImage to bring in two guides and ImageConcanate to combine them for quick visual context, previewed with PreviewImage. Your short description and the two images feed the LLM group, where GeminiNode produces a refined Seedance-style prompt that’s displayed via MarkdownNote for easy review and edits. That text flows to the Seedance 2.0 group: ByteDance2ReferenceNode conditions on the two references plus the generated prompt to synthesize frames, which you can inspect in PreviewAny and export with SaveVideo. The result is a streamlined loop: drop images, describe the motion, let the LLM draft the prompt, tweak if needed, and render.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm required nodes are available: GeminiNode and ByteDance2ReferenceNode (plus built-ins like LoadImage, PreviewImage/PreviewAny, ImageConcanate, SaveVideo). Ensure GeminiNode is configured with a valid API key.
Add your two reference images in the Reference Images group using the LoadImage nodes. The ImageConcanate node will combine them for a side-by-side preview (check it with PreviewImage).
Type a short description of the scene or motion you want in the LLM input. Temporarily bypass the Seedance generation (select ByteDance2ReferenceNode and press Ctrl+B) so only the LLM runs.
Queue the graph to run the LLM. Review the generated Seedance-style prompt in the MarkdownNote. Edit or refine the text there if you want more specificity (subjects, camera moves, lighting, pacing).

Re-enable ByteDance2ReferenceNode (Ctrl+B again). Optionally adjust its key settings (e.g., reference weighting, steps, guidance, resolution, and frame count if exposed). Queue the graph to generate frames and preview them in PreviewAny.
When satisfied, use SaveVideo to export the result. Set filename and basic video options (e.g., fps) as needed, then queue to write the final clip.
suggestedUseCases: Style-locked character or product motion: keep design consistent across shots by anchoring on two reference angles.
Fast concept iterations: explore multiple motion directions by quickly re-running the LLM with small prompt edits.
Shot continuity for short-form content: maintain look and feel across a sequence of clips using the same reference pair.
Previs and storyboarding: generate motion studies from rough references before committing to full production.

faqItems.question: Do I have to use the LLM, or can I write the Seedance prompt myself?
faqItems.answer: You can do either. The LLM (GeminiNode) is optional—use it to draft a Seedance 2.0–style prompt, then edit it in MarkdownNote. If you already have a strong prompt, skip the LLM and feed your text directly to ByteDance2ReferenceNode.

faqItems.question: Why two reference images?
faqItems.answer: Using two references gives Seedance 2.0 a clearer target for subject, style, and context (e.g., front and three-quarter views, or subject plus environment). This typically improves consistency and reduces drift compared to a single reference.

faqItems.question: The LLM isn’t running—what should I check?
faqItems.answer: Make sure GeminiNode is configured with a valid API key and internet access, and that you’re only running the LLM at first (bypass ByteDance2ReferenceNode with Ctrl+B). If the request exceeds model limits, shorten your description or resize references before retrying.

faqItems.question: How do I improve quality or stabilize motion?
faqItems.answer: Start with better references (clear subject, lighting, and style). In ByteDance2ReferenceNode, increase steps or guidance for sharper detail, and adjust reference weighting to keep the look locked in. If available, reduce resolution or frame count during exploration and scale up once you like the motion.

2e37304a2fbd.title: Outpaint to Any Aspect Ratio - Nano Banana Pro
2e37304a2fbd.description: Upload your image, input your desired aspect ratio and the images position (as a percentage) in the new aspect ratio composite. Uses Nano Banana Pro to generate an outpainted version of your image to fit the new dimensions.
2e37304a2fbd.metaDescription: Outpaint any image to a new aspect ratio without cropping. Anchor the original by percentage and let Nano Banana Pro fill the rest seamlessly in ComfyUI.
2e37304a2fbd.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow outpaints a single image to any target aspect ratio without cropping or distorting your original. You load an image with LoadImage, then the custom Image Extender node (b26cc822-68bf-4fd0-b66f-bb3f99cd1443) builds a new canvas based on your chosen aspect ratio and anchors the original at a user-defined position (in percent). Only the newly added canvas area is generated—your original pixels remain intact. Under the hood, the Image Extender wraps the diffusion process using the Nano Banana Pro model to synthesize surrounding content that blends naturally with the source.

Supporting nodes make the process clear and repeatable: GetImageSize reads the source dimensions, ImageResizeKJv2 optionally scales inputs or outputs for cleaner detail, and PreviewImage/ImageCompare help you evaluate before/after results. If you prefer guided generation, GeminiImage2Node can provide an image-aware prompt that feeds into the Image Extender. When you’re satisfied, SaveImage writes the final outpainted result. The combination of precise placement controls, aspect ratio targeting, and a capable outpainting model makes this a practical tool for repurposing images for social, web, and print formats without losing key content.
howToUse: Load the workflow and drop your source image into the LoadImage node. Use GetImageSize and PreviewImage to confirm the input looks correct.

Open the Image Extender node (b26cc822-68bf-4fd0-b66f-bb3f99cd1443) and set your target aspect ratio (e.g., 16:9 or 9:16). Set the image position as percentages (X% and Y%), where 0%/0% is top-left and 100%/100% is bottom-right.

Optional: If you want prompt guidance, connect GeminiImage2Node to analyze the input image and feed a descriptive prompt to the Image Extender, or enter your own prompt/style text directly in the node if it exposes a prompt field.
Optional: Use ImageResizeKJv2 to scale the input (or target output) so dimensions are reasonable for your GPU and are multiples of 8 for diffusion stability.
Run the graph. Inspect the outpainted result with PreviewImage and compare it to the original using ImageCompare. Adjust aspect ratio, position, or prompt as needed and re-run.
When satisfied, save the final image with SaveImage.
suggestedUseCases: Convert landscape photos to vertical 9:16 for Reels/Stories without cropping the subject.
Extend product photos into banner-ready 16:9 or 21:9 hero images while preserving the original packshot.
Reformat film stills or key art to multiple storefront aspect ratios from a single master image.
Add safe margins around UI mockups or screenshots for device frames and captions.
Turn a portrait into a desktop wallpaper by outpainting cohesive background scenery.

faqItems.question: How does the aspect ratio and position control work?
faqItems.answer: The Image Extender creates a new canvas sized to your target aspect ratio, then places the original image at the specified X/Y percentages. Percentages map to the canvas: 0% is left/top, 50% is centered, and 100% is right/bottom. The empty regions are filled by Nano Banana Pro, while the original pixels are preserved.

faqItems.question: Will my original image be altered or blurred?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow composites the untouched original over the generated content. Only the newly added canvas area is synthesized; the source pixels remain exactly as loaded.

faqItems.question: Do I need a prompt for good results?
faqItems.answer: Not strictly. Nano Banana Pro can infer context from the source image, but a short prompt often improves style consistency (e.g., "soft natural light, cohesive background"). You can type a prompt directly in the Image Extender (if available) or use GeminiImage2Node to auto-suggest one from the image.

faqItems.question: Any tips to reduce artifacts or seams?
faqItems.answer: Keep expansions moderate for the first pass and ensure output dimensions are multiples of 8. If the Image Extender exposes settings like steps or denoise, increase them slightly and re-run. Repositioning the subject (position percentages) to give the model more room on the outpaint side can also help. If VRAM is limited, downscale with ImageResizeKJv2, outpaint, then upscale later.

2ed55f103c73.title: Kling 4.0: Reference to Video
2ed55f103c73.description: Hold a character and a location from two reference images and shoot a three-shot fashion fragment between them: an extreme close-up with a snap zoom, a mid-hall turn with a whip-pan, and a 120-degree orbit under the arched window. Each cut lands on a new position inside the same room, with two hard cuts in five seconds and stereo audio generated for the space.
2ed55f103c73.metaDescription: ComfyUI Kling 4.0 Reference-to-Video: turn character and location images into a 5s three-shot cinematic clip with hard cuts and stereo room audio.
2ed55f103c73.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns two still images into a cohesive, cinematic 5‑second video using Kling 4.0’s Reference‑to‑Video capability. A character image anchors identity (face, hair, wardrobe) while a location image anchors the room’s materials, lighting, and camera blocking. Two LoadImage nodes feed those references into a single Kling4ReferenceToVideoNode, which orchestrates a three‑shot fashion fragment: an extreme close‑up with a snap zoom, a mid‑hall turn with a whip‑pan, and a 120‑degree orbit beneath the arched window. The sequence uses two hard cuts to jump to new positions while staying inside the same room, and stereo spatial audio is generated to match the space.

Technically, the Kling4ReferenceToVideoNode fuses appearance guidance from the character reference with spatial cues from the location reference, then renders frames along predefined camera paths and transitions. The node returns a video stream (with embedded stereo audio when enabled), which the SaveVideo node writes to an MP4 in your output directory. A MarkdownNote block in the template documents the shot plan and usage tips. Swap in your own references to change subject and room; timing, resolution, aspect ratio, and motion intensity can be adjusted inside the Kling node when those controls are exposed by your install and API plan.
howToUse: Open the template in ComfyUI and verify the Kling4ReferenceToVideoNode is available and authenticated (Kling account/API key configured as your build requires).

Load the two reference images: a clean character portrait (e.g., kling4_r2v_woman_copper_bob.png) and a single-room location photo (e.g., kling4_r2v_brutalist_hall.png). Use high‑resolution, well‑lit images.

Open the Kling4ReferenceToVideoNode and confirm the preset for the three‑shot sequence (extreme close‑up → mid‑hall whip‑pan → 120° orbit), total duration ~5 seconds, and stereo audio enabled (if supported).
Optionally adjust output settings the node exposes (e.g., resolution/aspect ratio, FPS, cut timing, motion intensity, seed for repeatability), keeping within your API plan limits.
Run the graph. The Kling node will call the service and stream results; the SaveVideo node will write an MP4 with embedded audio to your ComfyUI output folder.

Review the clip. If identity or wardrobe drift, use a clearer character reference (frontal, minimal background) or match the target aspect ratio when cropping. If the room wobbles, choose a location image with distinctive geometry and lighting, then rerun with the same seed for controlled comparisons.
suggestedUseCases: Fashion lookbook micro‑sequences created from a model portrait and a campaign location still.
Character intro reels or casting tests that maintain a performer’s look across dynamic camera moves.
Interior or architecture mood snippets that showcase a space using a single reference photo.
Product hero shots staged consistently in a branded environment from a packshot and room image.
Social shorts or story bumpers with cinematic cuts generated from two curated stills.

faqItems.question: Do I need an internet connection or API key to run this?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Kling4ReferenceToVideoNode calls the Kling 4.0 service. Configure your Kling credentials (API key or auth method) as required by your ComfyUI extension. Offline execution is not supported.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the character’s identity and outfit consistent?
faqItems.answer: Use a high‑quality, unobstructed character image with clear facial features and visible wardrobe. Avoid multiple people or busy backgrounds. If the node exposes a seed or reference strength, keep the seed fixed and increase reference influence. Consistent aspect ratio between reference and output also helps.

faqItems.question: Can I change aspect ratio, FPS, or duration?
faqItems.answer: The template defaults to about 5 seconds with two hard cuts. You can change duration, frame rate, and resolution/aspect ratio if those controls are available in your Kling node and allowed by your API plan. Higher resolution and longer duration increase cost and render time.

faqItems.question: Will the video always include stereo audio?
faqItems.answer: The template is set to generate stereo room audio when supported by your Kling build and plan. If audio isn’t available, the output will be silent; SaveVideo will still write a valid MP4. Audio loudness and reverb are determined by the service rather than ComfyUI.

2f10814fd823.title: Cinematic Bridge Video
2f10814fd823.description: Generate or use a final frame, then create a cinematic transition from the input frame to the end frame.
2f10814fd823.metaDescription: Create a cinematic video that bridges a starting frame to a generated or supplied final frame using Gemini and Seedance 2.0 in ComfyUI.
2f10814fd823.extendedDescription:
Cinematic Bridge Video is a first-to-last frame translator that turns a single starting image into a short, cinematic clip that arrives at a chosen destination image. You can either supply your own end frame or let the workflow generate one for you. The flow begins with LoadImage for the opening frame. If you don’t have a final frame, a Prompt group uses GeminiNode to expand or refine your idea, then GeminiImage2Node synthesizes a dramatic endpoint image in the same story world and resolution. Both frames are previewed with PreviewAny, and SaveImage can archive the generated endpoint for reuse.

The actual motion is created by Seedance 2.0 via ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode, which interpolates between the first and last frames to produce a smooth, cinematic transition. You control duration and pacing by adjusting frame count and FPS, and you can nudge motion strength and consistency to balance creativity with subject fidelity. Finally, SaveVideo writes the bridge clip to disk, while SaveImage can optionally save key frames or the generated endpoint. MarkdownNote blocks in the canvas document recommended settings and usage tips.

This setup is ideal when you want story-consistent reveals or scene transitions without animating a full sequence from scratch. Keeping both frames aligned in subject, lighting, and aspect ratio helps Seedance 2.0 generate stable, believable in-betweens with minimal flicker.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the three groups: Prompt, First to Last Frame Translator, and Seedance 2.0.

In the Prompt group: Load your first frame with LoadImage. If you already have a final frame, load it with another LoadImage node. Otherwise, enter a concise description in GeminiNode and feed it to GeminiImage2Node to generate the end frame. Match the end frame’s resolution to the first frame.

Open the Seedance 2.0 group and set ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode to use your first and last frames. Adjust key parameters such as total frame count (or duration) and FPS to control clip length and pacing. Tune motion/consistency controls as needed to keep subjects stable.

Use PreviewAny to inspect the generated endpoint image and quick test runs from the translator. If the look isn’t right, refine the Gemini prompt, adjust seeds (for reproducibility and variation), or regenerate the end frame.
When satisfied, run the full graph. SaveImage will export the generated final frame (if you created one), and SaveVideo will write the finished bridge clip to disk.

Review the output. If you see jitter or mismatched composition, bring the first and last frames closer in framing/lighting, lower motion strength, or slightly increase duration for a smoother blend, then rerun.
suggestedUseCases: Product or character reveal: start from a neutral shot and transition into a hero pose or branded key art.
Storyboard polishing: bridge a rough opening frame to a refined concept frame for pitch-ready motion previews.
Before-and-after demos: smoothly morph from an original scene to a retouched or redesigned endpoint.
Title or scene transitions: move from a live-action still into a styled title card or environment matte.
Social teasers: create short cinematic bridges for platform-friendly reveals and announcements.

faqItems.question: Do I need to provide the final frame, or can the workflow generate it?
faqItems.answer: Either works. If you already have a destination image, load it with LoadImage. If not, enter a description in GeminiNode and use GeminiImage2Node to synthesize a cinematic endpoint that matches your story and resolution.

faqItems.question: How do I change the clip length and pacing?
faqItems.answer: In ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode (Seedance 2.0), set the total frame count (or duration) and FPS. More frames or a higher FPS lengthens the clip and smooths motion. For punchier pacing, reduce frames or use a slightly lower FPS.

faqItems.question: My video flickers or warps. How can I stabilize it?
faqItems.answer: Keep both frames the same size and aspect ratio, and ensure similar composition and lighting. Make the endpoint semantically close to the start (same subject, pose, wardrobe). In Seedance 2.0, reduce motion strength or increase duration. If available, set a fixed seed for reproducibility and regenerate.

faqItems.question: What resolution should I use?
faqItems.answer: Use matching dimensions for the first and last frames. If generating the endpoint with GeminiImage2Node, set its output size to match the loaded first frame. If you import your own end frame, crop/resize externally so both inputs have identical width and height.

2f1457114ce1.title: Remove Background: Qwen Image 2.1
2f1457114ce1.description: Remove image backgrounds with Qwen Image 2.1, which natively supports 2K output and RGBA transparency for direct transparent results. It takes 1 input image and returns 1 background-free image plus a comparison view showing the before and after. Ideal for e-commerce product photos, profile pictures, and marketing graphics needing clean cutouts.
2f1457114ce1.metaDescription: Compare Qwen Image 2.1 background removal before/after and 1024 vs 2048 pixel budgets in ComfyUI. Evaluate RGBA transparency, edge quality, and cutout fidelity.
2f1457114ce1.extendedDescription:
This workflow compares your original image against a background-removed result from Qwen Image 2.1 inside ComfyUI. The core subgraph invokes the Qwen-Image-2.1 model to generate an RGBA cutout (transparent background) and feeds both the source and the cutout into ImageCompare for a side-by-side or swipe-style before/after view. Because Qwen Image 2.1 natively supports up to a 2K (2048×2048) pixel budget and outputs an alpha channel directly, you can evaluate edge fidelity, haloing, and how semi-transparent areas (like glass or wisps) are handled without extra matting steps.

Beyond before/after, you can also compare output quality at different pixel budgets (e.g., 1024 vs 2048) to understand the trade-off between speed and fine-edge detail. The template defaults to no resizing beyond a multiple-of-32 alignment, preserves aspect ratio, and treats resolution as a total pixel budget rather than a fixed width or height. Use SaveImageAdvanced to write true-transparency PNGs, then examine how different budgets affect edges, tiny details, and compression artifacts.
howToUse: Load your image with LoadImage (try angry_broccoli.png to start). Confirm the ImageCompare node is wired to show Source (left) vs Cutout (right).

Set the Qwen Image 2.1 subgraph’s resolution/pixel budget. Start at 1024 (official default) for a quick pass, or 2048 for maximum edge fidelity. If set to 0, it will keep native size aligned to a multiple of 32.
Run the workflow. Inspect the ImageCompare view to check subject edges, flyaway details, and semi-transparent regions. Look for halos or missed regions.
Save the transparent result with SaveImageAdvanced as PNG to preserve RGBA. Avoid JPEG if you need transparency (JPEG will flatten the background).
Optional resolution check: re-run at a different budget (e.g., 2048), save the second result, and flip between outputs to judge improvements vs runtime.
Use the comparison to decide the smallest acceptable budget that meets your quality bar for your target use (web thumbnails, marketplace listings, print, etc.).
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce product photography: compare 1024 vs 2048 budgets to standardize cutout quality for marketplace requirements.
Profile pictures and avatars: validate hair and edge handling before publishing to social platforms that require transparent PNGs.
Marketing and design production: quickly assess whether the RGBA cutout is clean enough to composite over brand backdrops or gradients.
Catalog and batch QA: spot-check before/after results to catch halos, missed gaps, or edge artifacts across a set of assets.
Editorial and presentation graphics: ensure semi-transparent objects (glass, smoke, fabric) retain natural edges at a chosen pixel budget.

faqItems.question: What exactly is being compared in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Primarily, the workflow compares your original image against the Qwen Image 2.1 background-removed output via the ImageCompare node. You can also re-run at different pixel budgets (e.g., 1024 vs 2048) and compare saved outputs to evaluate edge fidelity vs speed.

faqItems.question: How does the resolution setting work with Qwen Image 2.1?
faqItems.answer: Resolution is a total pixel budget, not a fixed width or height. The model preserves aspect ratio and scales to meet the budget (official default is 1024, supports up to 2048). The template starts at 0 to avoid unnecessary resizing beyond a multiple-of-32 alignment; increase to 1024 or 2048 if you need sharper edges.

faqItems.question: How do I preserve transparency in the output?
faqItems.answer: Use SaveImageAdvanced and export as PNG to retain the RGBA alpha channel produced by Qwen Image 2.1. Formats like JPEG do not support transparency and will flatten the background.

faqItems.question: When should I choose 1024 vs 2048?
faqItems.answer: Use 1024 for faster runs and web-sized outputs where minor edge softness is acceptable. Choose 2048 for maximum detail, challenging edges (hair, fur, glass), or when assets will be displayed large or composited over complex backgrounds.

2fabcab898db.title: Wan 2.2 14B Fun Inpaint
2fabcab898db.description: Generate videos from start and end frames using Wan 2.2 Fun Inpaint.
2fabcab898db.metaDescription: Turn start and end images into a smooth video with Wan 2.2 Fun Inpaint in ComfyUI. Includes a faster LoRA option and low‑VRAM defaults.
2fabcab898db.extendedDescription:
Wan 2.2 14B Fun Inpaint turns two keyframes (a start image and an end image) into a short, coherent video by inpainting the motion between them. The workflow loads your images with LoadImage, encodes your text prompt with CLIPLoader + CLIPTextEncode, and runs Wan 2.2 via UNETLoader. Diffusion is driven by ModelSamplingSD3 and KSamplerAdvanced, while WanFunInpaintToVideo performs the keyframe-to-video interpolation/inpainting in latent space. Frames are decoded with VAELoader + VAEDecode and assembled with CreateVideo and SaveVideo.

Two execution groups are included: "Wan2.2_fun_Inp fp8_scaled" (recommended for best dynamics) and "Wan2.2_fun_Inp fp8_scaled + 4 steps LoRA" (faster, using LoraLoaderModelOnly to apply the Wan2.2 Lighting LoRA). The LoRA variant trades some motion dynamics for speed and shorter runtimes. The "Step 4 - Video size & length" group centralizes width/height, frame count, and FPS so you can scale to your GPU memory. Default settings are conservative to fit lower‑VRAM cards; increase resolution or frames as your hardware allows.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then enable exactly one execution group with Ctrl + B: either "Wan2.2_fun_Inp fp8_scaled" (better motion) or "fp8_scaled + 4 steps LoRA" (faster). Avoid running both at once.

Step 1 – Load models: In UNETLoader select the Wan 2.2 UNet. Load the matching VAE in VAELoader and the text encoder in CLIPLoader. If using the faster path, point LoraLoaderModelOnly to the Wan2.2 Lighting LoRA. (Models are available via Comfy-Org/Wan_2.2_ComfyUI_Repackaged.)
Step 2 – Upload start and end images: Use the two LoadImage nodes. For best results, keep both images the same resolution/aspect ratio and align the subject roughly similarly across frames.

Step 3 – Prompt: Enter your positive prompt in CLIPTextEncode and, if provided in the template, set a negative prompt to suppress artifacts (e.g., compression noise or deformities). In KSamplerAdvanced set seed, CFG, and steps; the LoRA group is configured for 4 steps, while the base fp8 path can use a few more steps.
Step 4 – Video size & length: Set width/height, frame count, and FPS in the provided controls. Start small (e.g., 512–768 on the short side) if VRAM is limited, then scale up as your GPU allows.

Run the graph: Queue the workflow. Preview frames after VAEDecode and review the final output from CreateVideo/SaveVideo. If results look static or off‑target, refine the prompt, adjust CFG/steps, or switch between the base fp8 path and the LoRA path.
suggestedUseCases: Turning two storyboard frames into a quick animated beat for previsualization.
Product transformation shots (e.g., closed-to-open view) with smooth, guided motion.
Character pose or expression changes that morph cleanly between two portraits.
Environment transitions (day-to-night, season change) driven by prompt and keyframes.
Design iterations: evolve a sketch into a refined render between two keyframes.

faqItems.question: Which group should I use: fp8_scaled or fp8_scaled + 4 steps LoRA?
faqItems.answer: Use fp8_scaled for richer motion dynamics and better temporal variation. Use fp8_scaled + 4 steps LoRA when you want faster generation and shorter runtimes; it applies the Wan2.2 Lighting LoRA via LoraLoaderModelOnly, but typically reduces video dynamics. Enable only one group at a time with Ctrl + B.

faqItems.question: How do I avoid artifacts or weak motion between the start and end frames?
faqItems.answer: Match aspect ratio and resolution for both images, keep the subject similarly framed, and provide a clear action in the prompt (e.g., "turns head and smiles"). Add a negative prompt to suppress known issues. If motion is too weak, try the base fp8 path (not the LoRA path), modestly increase steps/CFG in KSamplerAdvanced, or choose start/end frames with more discernible change.

faqItems.question: What are the VRAM requirements and how can I reduce memory use?
faqItems.answer: Defaults are set for lower-VRAM GPUs. To save memory: reduce resolution in Step 4, lower the frame count, and prefer the fp8_scaled + 4 steps LoRA group for quicker runs. Ensure only one execution group is enabled; running both will increase memory load.

faqItems.question: Where do I control length, FPS, and output format?
faqItems.answer: Use the "Step 4 – Video size & length" controls to set resolution, frame count, and FPS. Frames are assembled with CreateVideo and written by SaveVideo; the exact container/codec depends on the node configuration. Increasing frame count lengthens the clip but also raises compute and memory needs.

300efdae24f6.title: Image Editing (New)
300efdae24f6.description: Edit your images with Qwen-Image-Edit, the latest OSS model
300efdae24f6.metaDescription: Discover Qwen-Image-Edit: a breakthrough in image editing with cutting-edge precision and flexibility for seamless background and object modifications.
300efdae24f6.extendedDescription:
The Qwen-Image-Edit model represents a significant leap forward in the realm of image editing, leveraging advanced open-source technology to offer unparalleled flexibility and precision. Unlike previous models that often required multiple steps and manual adjustments, Qwen-Image-Edit simplifies the process by integrating cutting-edge algorithms capable of understanding and executing complex edits. This model excels in tasks such as background alteration, object replacement, and character outfit changes, providing users with a seamless editing experience.

What sets Qwen-Image-Edit apart is its ability to maintain high image fidelity while executing intricate edits. Traditional models often struggle with preserving the original image's quality, especially when performing substantial modifications. However, Qwen-Image-Edit employs sophisticated techniques that ensure the final output retains the original's visual integrity. This makes it an invaluable tool for professionals and hobbyists alike who demand precision and quality in their image editing projects.
howToUse: Load your image using the LoadImage node in ComfyUI.
Select the Qwen-Image-Edit model from the available options.
Configure the desired edits, such as background changes or object replacements, using the interface.
Process the image through the workflow to apply the edits.
Review and save the edited image using the SaveImage node.
suggestedUseCases: Professional photo retouching for marketing materials.
Creative projects requiring complex scene alterations.
Fashion industry applications for virtual outfit changes.
Film and media production for seamless background modifications.
Augmented reality applications needing precise image edits.

faqItems.question: What makes Qwen-Image-Edit different from other image editing models?
faqItems.answer: Qwen-Image-Edit offers advanced algorithms that provide high precision and maintain image quality, making complex edits easier and more effective.

faqItems.question: Can Qwen-Image-Edit handle high-resolution images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, Qwen-Image-Edit is designed to work with high-resolution images, ensuring that the quality is preserved even after extensive editing.

faqItems.question: Is Qwen-Image-Edit suitable for beginners?
faqItems.answer: Absolutely. The model's intuitive interface and automated processes make it accessible for users of all skill levels, from beginners to professionals.

faqItems.question: What types of edits can Qwen-Image-Edit perform?
faqItems.answer: The model can perform a variety of edits, including background changes, object replacements, and outfit modifications, among others.

31c0a94fd0a5.title: Video Upscale: Topaz Astra 2 Creative
31c0a94fd0a5.description: Upscale GenAI video footage with Astra 2's creative diffusion, adding dynamic detail and texture. Adjust creativity, sharpness, and prompt-based guidance for precise stylization of AI-generated content.
31c0a94fd0a5.metaDescription: Upscale AI videos with Topaz Astra 2 Creative in ComfyUI. Control creativity, sharpness, and optional prompt guidance for detailed, stylized results.
31c0a94fd0a5.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow upscales AI-generated video using Topaz’s Astra 2 Creative model to add dynamic, stylistic detail while preserving motion consistency. The pipeline is simple and robust: LoadVideo ingests and decodes your source clip, TopazVideoEnhanceV2 sends the frames to the Astra 2 Creative model for enhancement and controlled stylization, and SaveVideo encodes the result to your chosen format. Because Astra 2 is purpose-built for video enhancement, it maintains temporal coherence across frames, reducing flicker and jitter common to naive per-frame processing.

Technically, the TopazVideoEnhanceV2 node is the centerpiece. In this workflow it’s configured for upscaling plus creative diffusion. You can dial in the look using three key controls: Creativity (how strongly diffusion adds new detail/texture), Sharpness (edge clarity and micro-contrast), and an optional text Prompt (to nudge the aesthetic when you want a particular vibe). Leave the prompt empty to keep the model neutral and more preservation-focused. SaveVideo then packages the enhanced frames using ffmpeg settings you choose (codec, quality, and frame rate), producing a ready-to-share output that balances size and quality for your target platform.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the TopazVideoEnhanceV2 custom node is installed. If it uses the Topaz API, add your API key/credentials in the node or environment as instructed by the node’s documentation.
Open LoadVideo and select your source clip. Keep default settings for auto-detected resolution and frame rate unless you have a reason to override them.

In TopazVideoEnhanceV2, select the Astra 2 Creative model and set your upscale factor (e.g., 2x or 4x). Adjust Creativity to control how much new detail/texture is introduced, tweak Sharpness for edge clarity, and optionally enter a Prompt if you want guided stylization. Leave Prompt empty for a more natural, preservation-first upscale.

Configure SaveVideo: choose container (e.g., MP4), codec (H.264/H.265), and quality (CRF/bitrate). By default, keep the source FPS to preserve motion; only change if you have a specific delivery requirement.
Queue and run the workflow. Monitor the ComfyUI console for processing status from the TopazVideoEnhanceV2 node. Processing time scales with clip length, upscale factor, and creativity strength.

Review the output. If the look is too strong, lower Creativity or remove the Prompt; if edges feel soft, increase Sharpness slightly. Re-run until you hit your preferred balance of fidelity and style.
suggestedUseCases: Refining diffusion-generated animations for social posts while adding tasteful, consistent texture.
Elevating low-res AI b‑roll to 4K with controllable stylization for editorial or product videos.
Polishing stylized motion graphics or lyric videos where extra micro-detail enhances the aesthetic.
Upscaling anime- or toon-styled AI clips while preserving line integrity and reducing flicker.
Unifying the look of multi-shot AI edits by applying consistent creative guidance across clips.

faqItems.question: Do I need a Topaz account or API key for this workflow?
faqItems.answer: If your TopazVideoEnhanceV2 build uses the Topaz cloud/API, you’ll need valid credentials and an active plan. Enter them where the node documentation specifies. Some installations may support local engines—follow the node’s setup guide.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the result close to my original look without heavy stylization?
faqItems.answer: Lower the Creativity value and leave Prompt empty. Start with modest Sharpness (e.g., a slight bump) and a 2x upscale. This prioritizes fidelity and temporal stability over added texture.

faqItems.question: Why does my output look too crunchy or over-detailed?
faqItems.answer: Reduce Creativity first, then back off Sharpness. If you used a Prompt, clear it or make it less prescriptive. Also ensure your source dimensions are reasonable—avoid extreme 4x on already clean footage unless necessary.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow keep audio from the original video?
faqItems.answer: No. The standard SaveVideo node encodes the processed frames only. If you need audio, remux it from the source clip after rendering (e.g., with ffmpeg or your NLE) to sync the original audio back to the upscaled video.

31dc5fe0b89c.title: FLUX 3 Max: Text to Video
31dc5fe0b89c.description: Generate a video with synchronized audio from a single text prompt with FLUX 3 Max, which reasons about and expands the prompt before rendering. Outputs one clip of 5 to 20 seconds at 720p or 1080p, at any aspect ratio from 9:16 to 21:9, with ambient sound, speech, and effects created alongside the picture and no input files required. Ideal for cinematic concept clips, ad mockups, and social videos that need matching sound design.
31dc5fe0b89c.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate 5–20s 720p/1080p videos with synchronized audio from one text prompt using FLUX 3 Max. No inputs required—just prompt and render.
31dc5fe0b89c.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single text prompt into a fully rendered video with synchronized audio using the FLUX 3 Max model. The Flux3MaxTextToVideoNode interprets and expands your prompt, plans shots and timing, generates the visual sequence, and synthesizes matching sound (ambient, effects, and spoken dialogue) in one pass—no reference images or audio required. You control the core parameters directly on the node: video length (5–20 seconds), resolution (720p or 1080p), and aspect ratio anywhere from 9:16 to 21:9, making it easy to target vertical, square, or widescreen formats.

Inside ComfyUI, the pipeline is intentionally minimal: Flux3MaxTextToVideoNode does the model-side reasoning and generation, and SaveVideo encodes the final result to disk as an MP4 with the audio track embedded. To steer results, write prompts that specify scene content, pacing, and camera moves, and include explicit sound cues (e.g., “distant thunder, soft footsteps”) or dialogue in quotes for spoken lines. This combination yields cinematic concept clips, ad mockups, and social-first videos with picture and sound designed together from the same text brief.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm it contains Flux3MaxTextToVideoNode connected to SaveVideo.
Open Flux3MaxTextToVideoNode and enter a clear prompt describing visuals, pacing, and sound. Include dialogue in quotes and mention key sound cues (e.g., crowd ambience, footsteps, whoosh).
Set the core parameters on Flux3MaxTextToVideoNode: choose a duration between 5–20 seconds, a resolution (720p for faster renders or 1080p for higher detail), and an aspect ratio from 9:16 to 21:9.

suggestedUseCases: Cinematic concept clips for previsualization and mood exploration.

faqItems.question: Do I need any input images, video, or audio to get started?

faqItems.question: How do I control duration, resolution, and aspect ratio?

faqItems.question: How can I get spoken dialogue or specific sound effects?

faqItems.question: What format is the output and does it include audio?

Set the desired video length for the loop.

320aaba28a06.title: RTX Video Enhance: HDR
320aaba28a06.description: Upload a video and chain Nvidia's three RTX video nodes in one pass: super resolution upscale, frame generation and SDR-to-HDR conversion, running locally on your Nvidia RTX GPU. Built for VFX artists and professional video creators.
320aaba28a06.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow that upscales, frame-interpolates, and converts SDR to HDR using NVIDIA RTX nodes—fast, local, and ideal for professional video finishing.
320aaba28a06.extendedDescription:
RTX Video Enhance: HDR is a one-pass ComfyUI workflow that upgrades standard SDR footage into modern, high-fidelity output by chaining three NVIDIA RTX video operators on your local GPU. It loads your source with LoadVideo, splits it into frames, FPS, and audio via GetVideoComponents, then processes each frame through RTXVideoSuperResolution for upscaling and deartifacting, RTXVideoFrameGeneration to interpolate extra frames for smoother motion, and RTXTrueHDR to expand dynamic range from SDR to HDR. The processed frames and the original audio are reassembled using CreateVideo and written to disk with SaveVideo, while SaveImageAdvanced can optionally export preview frames for quick QC before committing to a full render.

Technically, the pipeline keeps timing consistent by using PrimitiveInt and ComfyMathExpression to compute the correct target frame rate after interpolation (for example, doubling 24 fps to 48 or 60 depending on your target). Upscaling happens first to give the frame generator more detail to work with, followed by HDR conversion so the final encode reflects the enhanced luminance range. Because it uses NVIDIA’s RTX video nodes (RTXVideoSuperResolution, RTXVideoFrameGeneration, RTXTrueHDR) instead of diffusion models, it runs fast and locally on an RTX GPU—ideal for VFX artists and video creators who need clean upscales, smoother motion, and HDR output without leaving ComfyUI.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the graph. Locate the main path: LoadVideo -> GetVideoComponents -> RTXVideoSuperResolution -> RTXVideoFrameGeneration -> RTXTrueHDR -> CreateVideo -> SaveVideo. SaveImageAdvanced branches can be used for preview frames.
In LoadVideo, select your source clip. GetVideoComponents will extract frames, read the input FPS, and pass along the audio stream for later remuxing.

Configure RTXVideoSuperResolution: choose your upscale factor (e.g., 1x/2x/4x) and adjust artifact reduction/sharpening strength as needed. For older or compressed footage, use stronger deartifacting; for clean sources, use lighter settings.

Set up RTXVideoFrameGeneration: pick your interpolation multiplier or target FPS (e.g., aiming for 60 fps). Verify the PrimitiveInt and ComfyMathExpression nodes compute the intended output FPS (for example, input_fps * 2). Adjust these values if you need a different target.

Tune RTXTrueHDR: select the HDR conversion strength/intent to preserve natural skin tones and highlights. Use SaveImageAdvanced to export a few preview frames and confirm that contrast and highlight roll-off look correct before final rendering.

In CreateVideo, choose container/codec. For HDR delivery, use a 10-bit capable encoder if available (e.g., HEVC Main10). If your CreateVideo options are limited, export frames via SaveImageAdvanced and encode externally. Then run the graph; SaveVideo will write the final file with the upscaled, frame-generated, HDR imagery and original audio.
suggestedUseCases: Upscaling archive SDR footage to UHD with smoother motion and HDR for broadcast or streaming deliverables.
Enhancing smartphone or social clips to look clean and cinematic with deartifacting, interpolation, and HDR pop.
Polishing gameplay captures to 4K HDR60 for YouTube or portfolio reels.
Reframing and finishing corporate b-roll or interview material for HDR marketing content.
Improving stylized or CG previews where added resolution and temporal smoothness help client reviews.

faqItems.question: What hardware and drivers do I need?
faqItems.answer: You need an NVIDIA RTX GPU and recent NVIDIA drivers that support the RTX video features used by RTXVideoSuperResolution, RTXVideoFrameGeneration, and RTXTrueHDR. Performance scales with GPU capability, and more VRAM helps when using higher upscales (e.g., 4x) or longer clips.

faqItems.question: Can I keep the original audio untouched?
faqItems.answer: Yes. GetVideoComponents passes the audio track, and CreateVideo remuxes it with the processed frames. Frame generation only changes the video frame rate; audio is preserved. If you notice sync drift in edge cases, export audio separately and remux in a dedicated editor.

faqItems.question: Should I run RTXTrueHDR on footage that is already HDR?
faqItems.answer: No. If your source is HDR, bypass or disable RTXTrueHDR to avoid double conversion. Use RTXVideoSuperResolution (and optionally frame generation) alone, and retain the original HDR color pipeline in your encode settings.

faqItems.question: How do I avoid artifacts from upscaling or frame interpolation?
faqItems.answer: Use conservative settings: reduce sharpening/deartifacting if you see halos or ringing, and keep frame generation to modest targets (e.g., 48 or 60 fps) for footage with fast, complex motion. Preview a short segment with SaveImageAdvanced before rendering the full clip.

Optionally adjust any available node fields relevant to quality or consistency (e.g., keep the same settings when iterating to compare changes).

Press Queue Prompt (or Execute). The image returned by ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3 will be saved by SaveImageAdvanced as a single file in your chosen directory.

Storyboards and concept frames that benefit from dramatic lighting and precise labels.
App splash screens or landing page headers with branded text.

faqItems.question: Do I need a local model or GPU?
faqItems.answer: No local checkpoint is required. ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3 calls the Seedream 5.0 Flash API. Ensure your access is configured in the node or your ComfyUI integration, then run as usual.

faqItems.question: How can I improve text accuracy in the image?

faqItems.question: Where are outputs saved and how do I change filenames?

325247297bf2.title: Qwen Image Edit 2511 - Material Replacement

32f98268638e.title: Fish Audio: Voice Clone to Speech
32f98268638e.description: Clone any voice from a short recording, then use it to speak any script with Fish Audio. Record 2-3 clips of 15-20 seconds, connect them to the Instant Voice Clone node, and the cloned voice feeds straight into text to speech with no training wait. Add emotion tags to control how your cloned voice delivers each line. Great for personalized narration, character voices, and content in your own voice.
32f98268638e.metaDescription: Clone a voice from 2–3 short clips and synthesize speech instantly in ComfyUI with Fish Audio. Includes preset-voice option and flexible audio export.
32f98268638e.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow lets you clone any voice from a few short recordings and immediately synthesize new speech with that voice using Fish Audio. In Option 1 (Voice Clone), you feed clean voice samples from RecordAudio or LoadAudio into FishAudioInstantVoiceClone. The node returns a clone handle that plugs straight into FishAudioTextToSpeech, so you can type any script and get an instant read—no training wait. In Option 2 (Preset Audio), you skip cloning entirely by selecting a built-in voice with FishAudioVoiceSelector and send it directly to FishAudioTextToSpeech for quick, predictable results.

Under the hood, the audio path is simple and fast: RecordAudio/LoadAudio → FishAudioInstantVoiceClone (Option 1) or FishAudioVoiceSelector (Option 2) → FishAudioTextToSpeech → SaveAudioAdvanced. Text prompts can include emotion/style tags supported by Fish Audio to influence delivery (tone, pacing, emphasis). SaveAudioAdvanced lets you export the result in your preferred format and quality. All Fish Audio nodes are API-based, so you’ll authenticate with your ComfyUI account and pay per use.

For best clones, provide 2–3 samples of 15–20 seconds each with clear, expressive speech and minimal background noise. Vary your prosody slightly (neutral, upbeat, calm) so the Instant Voice Clone has enough information to capture timbre and delivery. Then iterate quickly: adjust your script and tags, re-queue, and export takes until you land the read you want.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and sign in with your ComfyUI account to enable API nodes (Fish Audio nodes are pay-per-use).
Choose a path: select the Option 1: Voice Clone group or the Option 2: Preset Audio group, then press Ctrl‑B to enable it. Bypass or disable the other path.
Option 1 (Voice Clone): Provide 2–3 clean voice samples (15–20s each) via RecordAudio or LoadAudio, then connect them to FishAudioInstantVoiceClone. Wait for the clone handle to be ready.
Option 2 (Preset Audio): Use FishAudioVoiceSelector to pick a preset voice and connect its output to FishAudioTextToSpeech.

In FishAudioTextToSpeech, paste or type your script. Optionally add Fish Audio emotion/style tags to control tone, pacing, and emphasis (see the node’s help for supported tags). Ensure the voice input comes from your clone (Option 1) or the selector (Option 2).
Click Queue Prompt to generate audio. Review the preview/output, then configure SaveAudioAdvanced (format, sample rate/bitrate, filename) and run it to export your final file.
suggestedUseCases: Personalized narration for tutorials, explainers, and product demos in your own voice.
Character voices for game prototypes, animatics, and storyboards without casting delays.
Podcast intros/outros and social video hooks where you need fast, consistent delivery.
Audiobook and e-learning samples to test tone, pacing, and clarity before full production.
Multilingual drafts using the same cloned voice to explore localization options.

faqItems.question: How many and what kind of samples do I need for a good clone?
faqItems.answer: Record or load 2–3 clips, each 15–20 seconds, with clean speech and minimal background noise. Speak naturally and vary prosody slightly (neutral, upbeat, calm). Avoid music, heavy compression, or room echo.

faqItems.question: Do I need a GPU or model training to clone a voice?
faqItems.answer: No local training is required. FishAudioInstantVoiceClone and FishAudioTextToSpeech run through the Fish Audio API. Just authenticate in ComfyUI, provide your samples or select a preset voice, and generate speech instantly.

faqItems.question: How do I control emotion, speed, or pauses in the speech?
faqItems.answer: Use the emotion/style tags supported by Fish Audio in the FishAudioTextToSpeech text field. You can influence tone, pacing, emphasis, and pauses by placing tags inline or at the start of lines. Refer to the node’s help/docs for the exact tag formats.

faqItems.question: What’s the difference between Voice Clone and Preset Audio paths?
faqItems.answer: Voice Clone (RecordAudio/LoadAudio → FishAudioInstantVoiceClone) captures a specific speaker’s timbre for personalized results. Preset Audio (FishAudioVoiceSelector) uses ready-made voices for fast, predictable output without providing samples.
