The result is a clean, reproducible image-to-video pipeline that’s easy to iterate: swap the input image, adjust motion/duration parameters, and re-run to explore different looks.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and review the MarkdownNote for the partner-node setup link and network requirements (localhost/127.0.0.1 and HTTPS).
In the RunwayImageToVideoNodeGen4 node, add your Runway API credentials (token/key) if prompted, and verify your machine can reach the API over HTTPS.
Use the LoadImage node to select your source image. For best results, choose a clean, high-resolution image and crop to the aspect ratio you want in the final video.
Configure the RunwayImageToVideoNodeGen4 settings: set duration (seconds), target frame rate (fps), and any motion/style controls exposed by the node. Start with moderate motion for fewer artifacts.
Set SaveVideo parameters (output path and fps). Match fps to the Runway node’s output to avoid timing mismatches.
Queue and run the workflow. Inspect the saved clip; iterate by adjusting duration, motion intensity, or trying alternative source images.
suggestedUseCases: Give static product shots subtle camera motion for social posts or landing pages.
Animate concept art or key visuals to create quick motion studies and mood pieces.
Add gentle parallax and subject movement to portraits or editorial images.
Create short teaser loops and background motion for slides, reels, or hero banners.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key to use Runway Gen4 Turbo in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The RunwayImageToVideoNodeGen4 node is a partner/API node and requires valid Runway credentials. Enter your token/key in the node’s settings and ensure outbound HTTPS access.

faqItems.question: What image sizes and aspect ratios work best?
faqItems.answer: Use clean, high-quality images cropped to your target aspect ratio. Avoid extreme aspect ratios and cluttered backgrounds. If your output looks stretched or cropped, resize/crop the input image to match the intended video aspect.

faqItems.question: How do I reduce flicker or artifacts in the generated video?
faqItems.answer: Try lowering motion intensity or complexity in the Runway node settings, shorten the duration, and use higher-quality, well-lit source images. Subtle motion generally produces cleaner results. Re-run with small tweaks until the motion stabilizes.

faqItems.question: I get connection errors—how do I fix them?
faqItems.answer: Follow the partner-node requirements: run ComfyUI locally (localhost/127.0.0.1), ensure your environment allows HTTPS, and that your firewall/proxy is not blocking the Runway API. See the "About API Node" link in the workflow’s MarkdownNote for setup details.

3eb92c1b2380.title: AI on the Lot 2026 - Final WF - t2v
3eb92c1b2380.description: The sixth and final workflow released for AI on the Lot 2026, made available for ComfyUI 101 workshop attendees to open and follow along if they choose. A text-to-video workflow that brings together everything built and used in the previous workflows into one complete setup.
3eb92c1b2380.metaDescription: End-to-end ComfyUI text-to-video workflow using Qwen-VL prompt enhancement, keyframe synthesis, and video assembly with preview and export.
3eb92c1b2380.extendedDescription:
AI on the Lot 2026 - Final WF - t2v is a complete text-to-video pipeline that stitches together prompt design, image synthesis, and video assembly inside ComfyUI. It uses AILab_QwenVL and AILab_QwenVL_PromptEnhancer to turn a simple idea into a rich, structured prompt. From there, the workflow generates high-quality keyframes with the image synthesis stage (node ID e9d2dda8-2509-4d8d-9702-a9bf00c26650), previews results with PreviewAny, and then builds a cohesive video clip in the video stage (node ID 99c27236-513e-427c-9ed4-49406365f0d3). SaveImage and SaveVideo provide clean, reproducible exports at each stage.

Technically, the flow is: your base text prompt (and optionally a reference image) goes into AILab_QwenVL to extract and enrich scene details. AILab_QwenVL_PromptEnhancer refines the text into a model-friendly prompt with clearer subjects, styles, and shot descriptors. That prompt feeds the image generator node (e9d2dda8-2509-4d8d-9702-a9bf00c26650) to produce one or more seed-controlled keyframes at your chosen resolution. Those frames are then passed to the video node (99c27236-513e-427c-9ed4-49406365f0d3), which synthesizes a clip based on duration and motion/consistency settings. PreviewAny helps you iterate quickly, while SaveImage and SaveVideo lock in stills or a final video once you’re happy. Because the stages are modular, you can use it for text-to-image only, image-to-video only, or end-to-end text-to-video with the same graph.
howToUse: Load the "AI on the Lot 2026 - Final WF - t2v" JSON in ComfyUI and confirm all custom nodes load without errors. Look for AILab_QwenVL, AILab_QwenVL_PromptEnhancer, PreviewAny, SaveImage, and SaveVideo in the graph.

Enter your base prompt in the AILab_QwenVL_PromptEnhancer input. Optionally provide a reference image to AILab_QwenVL if the workflow exposes that input—this grounds the enhanced prompt in your visual reference.

Configure the image generation stage (node ID e9d2dda8-2509-4d8d-9702-a9bf00c26650): set width/height (aspect ratio), steps, guidance/CFG, and seed. Use PreviewAny to check a quick keyframe and SaveImage to export promising stills.

Adjust the video stage (node ID 99c27236-513e-427c-9ed4-49406365f0d3): set clip length (frames or seconds), frames per second, and motion/consistency parameters. Keep resolution modest while iterating for faster previews.

Run a short test render. If you see flicker or drift, try increasing consistency, reducing noise strength, or fixing the seed in the image stage. Iterate on the prompt with AILab_QwenVL_PromptEnhancer for clearer subjects and style.
When satisfied, raise quality settings (steps/resolution if supported), then render the final and export with SaveVideo. Use SaveImage to archive keyframes and thumbnails for future reference.
suggestedUseCases: Storyboard and previsualization: generate keyframes from a script prompt, then assemble short motion tests.
Product and logo stingers: produce a single stylized keyframe and animate it into a short looping reveal.
Social micro‑videos: craft a compact prompt, iterate quickly at low resolution, then export a final 5–10s clip.
Concept art to motion: use a reference image via AILab_QwenVL to guide style, then animate into a mood clip.
Educational snippets: turn concise textual explanations into illustrative short videos for courses or posts.

faqItems.question: Do I need specific models installed for this to work?
faqItems.answer: You need the custom AILab_QwenVL nodes to load successfully; they will rely on Qwen‑VL assets for prompt enhancement. The image and video synthesis nodes (e9d2dda8‑… and 99c27236‑…) use whatever model/checkpoint configuration the workflow provides or you connect. If ComfyUI reports missing models, follow the node warnings to download or point to the correct files.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce flicker or subject drift between frames?
faqItems.answer: Try increasing motion/consistency strength in the video node, lowering noise strength, and keeping a fixed seed in the image stage. Clear, specific prompts from AILab_QwenVL_PromptEnhancer (subjects, camera, style) also help. Shorter clips and moderate resolutions are easier to stabilize during iteration.

faqItems.question: What settings should I change for faster previews?
faqItems.answer: Lower resolution, reduce steps in the image node (e9d2dda8‑…), use a smaller clip length or fps in the video node (99c27236‑…), and keep a fixed seed. Use PreviewAny to validate direction before committing to a full‑quality render.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow do image‑to‑video or just text‑to‑video?
faqItems.answer: Both. You can stop after the image stage and export stills (SaveImage), or feed existing/reference imagery through the prompt and video stages to produce motion. The end‑to‑end path is text‑to‑video, but the stages are modular so you can mix and match.

3edd38b87be6.title: Inpainting: Bria Generative Fill
3edd38b87be6.description: Use Bria's Generative Fill API to regenerate a specific region of an image while keeping everything outside the mask pixel-perfect unchanged. Paint a mask over the target area, write a detailed prompt for the replacement content, and compare the before/after side-by-side before exporting. Ideal for product photography corrections, object removal or replacement, and creative compositing where precise control over the edited region matters.
3edd38b87be6.metaDescription: Side-by-side compare Bria Generative Fill edits vs the original. Test prompts and mask strategies to choose the best inpainting result.
3edd38b87be6.extendedDescription:
This comparison workflow evaluates Bria's Generative Fill (via the BriaGenFill node) against the unedited original image using a consistent, mask-based inpainting setup. You load an image (LoadImage), brush a precise target region (Painter), and prompt Bria to regenerate only what’s inside the mask while the background stays pixel-perfect unchanged. The ImageCompare node then presents a side-by-side view so you can assess edge integration, texture fidelity, color continuity, and prompt adherence.

Beyond a simple before/after, the workflow is designed for controlled A/B testing of inpainting choices. Keep the input image and mask constant while varying only the prompt to see how specificity, style cues, and context words affect results. You can also compare mask strategies—tight vs slightly expanded or softer brush edges—to observe trade-offs between boundary precision and seam-free blending. SaveImageAdvanced lets you export the preferred version once you’ve identified the best balance for your use case.
howToUse: Load your source image with LoadImage (use the provided asset to start or your own).
Paint the target region with Painter: white/opaque marks what to replace; leave the rest unpainted to keep it unchanged.
Enter a clear, context-rich prompt in BriaGenFill describing the replacement content (style, material, lighting, perspective). Run the graph.
Use ImageCompare to review original vs edited side-by-side. Check edges, color matching, and semantic fit.
Iterate comparisons: keep the same image and mask, then vary only the prompt or use a slightly softer/wider mask to see blending differences.
Export the chosen result with SaveImageAdvanced, setting your file format and naming as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Product photography cleanup: remove scuffs, swap labels, or replace small props without touching the background.
Object removal in lifestyle shots: paint out distractions while preserving scene details outside the mask.
Creative compositing: replace specific elements (e.g., sky patches, signage) with precise prompt control over style and lighting.
Portrait fixes: regenerate hair flyaways, small accessories, or background gaps while keeping facial details intact.
Branding updates: replace logos or packaging panels and compare multiple design prompts quickly.

faqItems.question: What exactly is being compared in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Primarily the original image vs the BriaGenFill result, shown side-by-side with ImageCompare. You can also run A/B tests by holding the image and mask constant and changing only the prompt or mask softness to compare outcomes.

faqItems.question: Will areas outside the mask ever change?
faqItems.answer: No—by design, Bria’s Generative Fill keeps pixels outside the mask unchanged. Use a slightly soft or marginally expanded mask if you notice visible seams right at the boundary.

faqItems.question: How should I write prompts for the most reliable comparison?
faqItems.answer: Be specific about subject, material, color, lighting, perspective, and style (e.g., "matte black leather wallet, soft daylight, top-down"). When comparing, vary one factor at a time (e.g., color or style) so differences are attributable and easy to judge.

faqItems.question: How do mask choices impact the result at the edges?
faqItems.answer: Tight, hard-edged masks maximize precision but may show seams; softer or slightly overpainted masks improve blending where old and new content meet. Use Painter’s soft brush to test both approaches with otherwise identical settings.

3ef4de40106b.title: Song Generator
3ef4de40106b.description: This app uses Ace-Step 1.5XL to generate a full song and allows you to choose the genre and write the lyrics, either automatically or manually.
3ef4de40106b.metaDescription: ComfyUI Song Generator: use Ace-Step 1.5XL to auto-write BPM/duration-aware lyrics or use your own, then generate and export a complete song.
3ef4de40106b.extendedDescription:
Song Generator is a ComfyUI workflow that synthesizes complete songs with the Ace-Step 1.5XL audio model. It supports two lyric paths: automatic, where a short topic is expanded into BPM- and duration-aware lyrics, and manual, where you paste your own text. A ComfySwitchNode routes between these paths before the lyrics are encoded by TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5 and used to guide the audio model. You can preview the result with PreviewAny and export with SaveAudioAdvanced.

Under the hood, UNETLoader and VAELoader load the Ace-Step 1.5XL checkpoints. EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio allocates a latent audio canvas sized to your target duration. ModelSamplingAuraFlow configures the sampler for the model, and KSampler performs the iterative denoising on that latent using the conditioning produced by TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5. ConditioningZeroOut is included to safely zero optional negative conditioning when not used. After sampling, VAEDecodeAudio converts the latent to a waveform for monitoring and export.

The BPM/duration-aware lyric module uses PrimitiveInt/PrimitiveFloat to capture BPM and target length, StringReplace to inject those values into a songwriter instruction, and TextGenerate to create structured verses/choruses sized for the track. StringCompare helps detect empty input, and the ComfySwitchNode cleanly selects between the auto-lyrics and a PrimitiveStringMultiline node for manual lyrics. DualCLIPLoader/CLIPLoader are available for workflows that optionally mix in CLIP-style text conditioning, though the primary path uses TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5 for Ace-Step.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then point UNETLoader and VAELoader to your Ace-Step 1.5XL UNet and VAE checkpoints.
Pick your lyric mode: set the ComfySwitchNode to Auto (use Topic + BPM + Duration) or Manual (paste lyrics in PrimitiveStringMultiline).
For Auto lyrics: enter a short Topic, set BPM (PrimitiveInt) and Duration (PrimitiveFloat). The StringReplace/TextGenerate nodes will produce structured lyrics sized to your track.
For Manual lyrics: paste your lyrics and, if desired, add style or mood descriptors in the Prompt group strings that feed TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5.

Configure generation basics: set seed/steps/CFG in KSampler, confirm duration in EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio, and leave ModelSamplingAuraFlow at its default unless you know you need a different sampler.
Queue the workflow to generate. Use PreviewAny to audition, then adjust prompts or sampler settings as needed. When satisfied, set filename/format in SaveAudioAdvanced and run to export.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid song ideation from a topic and target BPM/duration for demos or writer’s rooms.
Creating tight-length jingles, intros, or outros that must hit a specific runtime.
Generating alternative lyric drafts over a consistent musical style for songwriting exploration.
Producing quick temp tracks for video editors or game prototyping with approximate timing.

faqItems.question: Do I need specific model files for this to work?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Point UNETLoader and VAELoader to the Ace-Step 1.5XL UNet and VAE checkpoints. The workflow relies on TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5 for conditioning, so ensure the corresponding text encoder resources are available as packaged with Ace-Step.

faqItems.question: How accurate are the BPM and duration settings?
faqItems.answer: Duration is enforced by the latent length from EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio, so the output length will match closely. BPM guides the lyric density via TextGenerate and prompt injection but does not force strict metronomic alignment; treat it as a strong narrative/timing hint rather than a beat-locked constraint.

faqItems.question: Can I use my own lyrics?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Switch to the Manual path and paste lyrics into PrimitiveStringMultiline. The ComfySwitchNode routes your text directly to TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5 for conditioning before generation.

faqItems.question: How do I improve audio quality or reduce artifacts?
faqItems.answer: Try increasing KSampler steps moderately, lowering CFG if the sound is harsh, and keeping prompts concise and specific. Ensure the correct Ace-Step VAE is loaded, and avoid overly long durations on a single pass if you encounter instability.

3efed399a12d.title: Flux.1 Dev fp8: Text to Image
3efed399a12d.description: Generate images using Flux.1 Dev fp8 quantized version. Suitable for devices with limited VRAM, requires only one model file, but image quality is slightly lower than the full version.
3efed399a12d.metaDescription: Efficient Text to Image generation using Flux.1 Dev fp8 for devices with limited VRAM, balancing performance and quality.
3efed399a12d.extendedDescription:
The Flux.1 Dev fp8: Text to Image workflow is designed to generate images from text prompts using a quantized version of the Flux.1 model. This workflow is particularly useful for devices with limited VRAM, as it requires only one model file and operates efficiently with reduced memory demands. The trade-off for this efficiency is a slight reduction in image quality compared to the full version of the model. Technically, the workflow leverages the Flux.1 model, which has been optimized for lower resource consumption by employing an fp8 quantization technique. This reduces the precision of the model's weights, allowing it to run on less powerful hardware without significant performance loss.

The workflow includes several key nodes: the SaveImage node, which handles the output of generated images, and the MarkdownNote node, which provides documentation and notes within the workflow for easier understanding and modification. The ddd1571b-c923-4645-9eba-e238fb45ee9e node is a custom node that facilitates the integration of these components, ensuring smooth operation and efficient processing. This setup makes the workflow not only accessible to users with limited hardware capabilities but also provides a streamlined process for generating images from text prompts, making it highly practical for quick prototyping and experimentation.
howToUse: Load the Flux.1 Dev fp8: Text to Image workflow into ComfyUI.
Prepare your text prompt that describes the image you want to generate.
Ensure the Flux.1 model file is available and properly configured in your environment.
Run the workflow, which will process the text prompt and generate an image.
Use the SaveImage node to save the generated image to your desired location.
Review the MarkdownNote node for additional documentation and tips.
suggestedUseCases: Generating concept art for projects with limited hardware resources.
Creating quick visual prototypes for design brainstorming sessions.
Developing educational materials where high-end graphic quality is not critical.
Producing images for social media content where speed is prioritized over quality.
Experimenting with AI-generated art on devices with minimal VRAM.

faqItems.question: What is fp8 quantization and why is it used?
faqItems.answer: Fp8 quantization reduces the precision of the model's weights, allowing it to run on devices with limited VRAM by decreasing memory usage at the cost of slight image quality reduction.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow on any device?
faqItems.answer: Yes, this workflow is designed to work on devices with limited VRAM, making it suitable for a wide range of hardware, including less powerful devices.

faqItems.question: How does the image quality compare to the full version of the model?
faqItems.answer: The image quality is slightly lower than the full version due to the fp8 quantization, but it remains effective for many practical applications.

faqItems.question: Do I need any special setup to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Ensure you have the Flux.1 model file and that your ComfyUI is updated. No additional special setup is required.

3f2afb56cdb2.title: Recraft 4.1 flash: Text to Image
3f2afb56cdb2.description: Generate images from text prompts using Recraft V4.1 Flash, a fast, low-cost model that produces one image output with no file inputs required. Ideal for high-volume generation, rapid iteration, photography and portraits, atmospheric scenes, and quick logo concept exploration.
3f2afb56cdb2.metaDescription: Fast ComfyUI text-to-image with Recraft V4.1 Flash. Enter a prompt, generate one image, auto-save to output. Ideal for rapid iteration and bulk tasks.
3f2afb56cdb2.extendedDescription:
This minimal, fast text-to-image workflow uses the RecraftV4TextToImageNode to call the Recraft V4.1 Flash model and return a single image from your prompt. It’s designed for speed and low cost, making it ideal for rapid iteration, high-volume generation, photography/portrait drafts, atmospheric scene ideation, and quick logo concept exploration. There are no file inputs—just write a prompt, run the node, and get one image back.

Technically, the RecraftV4TextToImageNode serializes your prompt and sends it to the Recraft API for inference with the V4.1 Flash backend, then outputs a ComfyUI image tensor. That tensor flows directly into SaveImage, which writes the result to your ComfyUI/output directory using the filename prefix and format set in the node. Depending on the node’s implementation, you may also have common controls (such as image size and seed). Because the workflow produces exactly one image per execution, it’s straightforward to queue many runs for A/B testing or bulk prompt variations.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the RecraftV4TextToImageNode is available. If required, add your Recraft API key in the node or in your environment per the node’s instructions.
Open the RecraftV4TextToImageNode, enter a clear text prompt, and (if exposed) adjust basic settings like output size or seed.
Select the SaveImage node and set a filename prefix and desired format (e.g., PNG or JPG).
Click Queue Prompt/Execute to run the graph. The Recraft node will request a single image from the V4.1 Flash model.
Preview the result in ComfyUI’s viewer. The image is saved automatically by SaveImage to the ComfyUI/output folder.
Iterate quickly: refine your prompt and re-run. For multiple variations, queue several prompts or duplicate the node with different settings.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid moodboards and concept exploration for scenes and atmospherics
Photography and portrait drafts to test framing, lighting, and style directions
Quick logo and mark ideation to explore shape, style, and composition
High-volume generation of prompt variations for marketing and social content
Fast iteration during creative reviews or live prototyping sessions

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key to use Recraft V4.1 Flash?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The RecraftV4TextToImageNode uses the Recraft API. Provide your API key in the node or via environment/settings as documented by the node. Without valid credentials, requests will fail.

faqItems.question: Can I control image size or aspect ratio?
faqItems.answer: If the node exposes width/height or aspect fields, set them there before running. Note that larger outputs may increase latency and API cost. If these fields are not present, the size is controlled by the node’s defaults.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow generate multiple images per run?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is configured to produce one image per execution. To create multiple results, enqueue several runs with different prompts or seeds, or duplicate the node and queue them together.

faqItems.question: Where are results saved and how do I change the filename?
faqItems.answer: SaveImage writes to your ComfyUI/output directory. In the SaveImage node, set the filename prefix and choose the file format (e.g., PNG or JPG) before running.

3f488d8d6100.title: Remove Background: Bria
3f488d8d6100.description: Upload an image to automatically remove its background using the Bria API. The workflow processes the request asynchronously and returns the edited image with a transparent background.
3f488d8d6100.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: remove image backgrounds via the Bria API, preview with ImageCompare, and save transparent PNG cutouts.
3f488d8d6100.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow shows you how to remove an image’s background using the Bria API, then preview and save the cutout with a transparent alpha channel. It chains four nodes: LoadImage to bring your source image into the graph, BriaRemoveImageBackground to call the BRIA background-removal model asynchronously, ImageCompare to preview the original versus the result, and SaveImage to write the transparent PNG to disk.

Technically, the BriaRemoveImageBackground node submits your image to Bria’s server-side model and waits for the job to complete, returning an RGBA image with the background removed. Because the call is asynchronous, the node handles polling until the result is ready. ImageCompare gives you a quick, visual before/after check so you can spot edge issues (like hair or fine objects) before saving. SaveImage then outputs a transparent PNG by default, preserving the alpha channel for clean compositing in design tools or downstream pipelines.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. You should see LoadImage → BriaRemoveImageBackground → ImageCompare → SaveImage.
Open the BriaRemoveImageBackground node and add your Bria API key (or configure it per the node’s documentation, e.g., via environment variable).
In LoadImage, select the photo you want to process (JPG or PNG work well). Keep the image reasonably high quality for better edge detection.
Optionally review any exposed options on BriaRemoveImageBackground (leave defaults for a clean transparent background).

Click Queue/Execute. The BriaRemoveImageBackground node sends the image to the BRIA model and waits asynchronously for the result. When complete, ImageCompare will display the original vs. the cutout.
Inspect the preview. If satisfied, set your output folder/filename in SaveImage and run it to write the transparent PNG. If not, try a higher-resolution image or a different source and run again.
suggestedUseCases: E‑commerce product photos: create clean, transparent cutouts for consistent catalog layouts.
Portraits and headshots: remove cluttered backgrounds for resumes, profiles, and ID badges.
Marketing and social creatives: quickly isolate subjects for overlays, carousels, and ads.
Slide decks and infographics: place subjects on brand-colored backgrounds without halos.
Dataset preparation: generate alpha-matted assets for compositing or training pipelines.

faqItems.question: Do I need a Bria API key to run this?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The BriaRemoveImageBackground node requires a valid Bria API key. Enter it in the node’s API key field or configure it as instructed by the node’s documentation (e.g., environment variable).

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported and will the result be transparent?
faqItems.answer: You can load common formats like JPG and PNG. The node returns a cutout with an alpha channel, and SaveImage preserves transparency when saving as PNG. Exporting to JPG will flatten the background and remove transparency.

faqItems.question: How long does processing take and what if it seems to stall?
faqItems.answer: Processing time depends on image size, network conditions, and API load. The node handles the asynchronous request and polls for completion. If it fails or times out, check your API key, network, and any Bria rate/size limits, then re-queue.

faqItems.question: How can I improve edge quality around hair or fine details?
faqItems.answer: Start with a clear, higher-resolution source image with good subject-background contrast and minimal motion blur. Use ImageCompare to verify edges before saving; if results are inconsistent, try a sharper photo or different lighting.

faqItems.question: Is my image processed locally?
faqItems.answer: No. Your image is sent to Bria’s servers for background removal. Review Bria’s documentation for privacy, data handling, size limits, and billing details.

3fc5cc355cfa.title: Tripo H3.1: Multiview to Model
3fc5cc355cfa.description: Upload multiview images of your object. Generate a high-detail 3D model with dense geometry and PBR-ready materials.
3fc5cc355cfa.metaDescription: Turn multiview photos into a dense, PBR-textured 3D model in ComfyUI with Tripo H3.1. Optional rigging/retargeting plus one-click GLB export.
3fc5cc355cfa.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial walks you through turning a set of multiview photos into a detailed 3D asset using the Tripo H3.1 model. The workflow ingests your image set with LoadImage nodes, reconstructs a dense triangle mesh via TripoMultiviewToModelNode, then generates PBR-ready materials with TripoTextureNodeV2. TripoConversionNode prepares the asset for clean export (scale/orientation/material packaging), and SaveGLB writes a single GLB with embedded textures.

The pipeline is modular: keep it simple for object captures, or enable advanced steps when needed. The Tripo Toolset group (select it and press Ctrl+B) exposes optional post-processes, including TripoRigNode for automatic skeleton creation and TripoRetargetNode for mapping existing motion to compatible meshes—useful when your subject is humanoid or otherwise riggable. Together, these nodes provide a practical, end-to-end path from photos to production-friendly assets you can drop into DCCs, game engines, or WebGL viewers.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the Tripo Toolset group. Select the group and press Ctrl+B to enable it if it’s bypassed.
Add your photos: connect multiple LoadImage nodes (one per view) or a batched input to feed all angles of your object into TripoMultiviewToModelNode. Use consistent lighting and cover all sides.
Open TripoMultiviewToModelNode and set the Tripo H3.1 model/preset. If your setup uses cloud inference, provide your Tripo API key in the node or environment as instructed by the node’s settings.

Run the reconstruction to generate the mesh. Review the output by exporting a quick GLB via SaveGLB and inspecting it in a 3D viewer. If you see holes or distortions, add more views or improve coverage/lighting, then re-run.

Enable texturing: connect the mesh to TripoTextureNodeV2 to bake PBR maps. Use TripoConversionNode to normalize scale and orientation as needed, and wire its output to SaveGLB to embed geometry and textures in one file.
Optional for characters: enable TripoRigNode to create a skeleton and TripoRetargetNode to map external motion. When satisfied, finalize with SaveGLB for a ready-to-use asset.
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce and product visualization: turn-packshots into web-ready GLB models with PBR materials.
Game and AR prototyping: quickly create environment props or hero objects from reference photos.
Cultural heritage and archival: digitize small artifacts with detailed geometry and faithful textures.
Lookdev and concept iteration: generate textured models for turntables and material exploration.
Character bases (optional): capture a static pose and add a simple rig/retargeting for animation tests.

faqItems.question: How many photos do I need for a good reconstruction?
faqItems.answer: Use enough overlapping views to fully cover the object (front, back, sides, top, and bottom where possible). Even spacing around the subject and consistent lighting matter more than a fixed number. Avoid motion blur and large exposure changes between shots.

faqItems.question: What texture maps does TripoTextureNodeV2 produce?
faqItems.answer: It outputs PBR-ready textures such as base color (albedo) and normal, and can include roughness/metallic (and optionally ambient occlusion) depending on the node’s configuration. These are embedded into the GLB when routed through SaveGLB.

faqItems.question: When should I use TripoConversionNode?
faqItems.answer: Use it before export to standardize scale, orientation (up-axis), and material packing so your GLB imports cleanly into DCCs and game engines. It helps ensure consistent units and correct handedness across tools.

faqItems.question: Can I rig and animate the reconstructed model?
faqItems.answer: Yes—if the subject is suitable. Enable TripoRigNode to generate a skeleton and use TripoRetargetNode to map existing animations. For non-riggable objects (e.g., rigid props), skip these nodes and export directly with SaveGLB.

40108d07c469.title: HY 3D 2.1: Single View to Model
40108d07c469.description: Reconstruct a 3D model from a single photo using Hunyuan3D 2.1, converting one input image into a raw white-mesh geometry without textures or materials. Ideal for rapid 3D concepting, blockout prototyping, and asset preparation before texturing or retopology.
40108d07c469.metaDescription: Convert a single photo into a clean, textureless 3D GLB using Tencent Hunyuan3D 2.1 in ComfyUI. Fast white-mesh reconstruction for concepting and blockouts.
40108d07c469.extendedDescription:
HY 3D 2.1: Single View to Model turns a single photo into a clean, textureless 3D mesh using Tencent’s Hunyuan3D 2.1 model. The workflow is streamlined for speed and simplicity: LoadImage brings in your reference photo, a Subgraph wraps the custom Hunyuan3D 2.1 inference node (134b0aa2-0237-4237-8366-558c4a007c68) to reconstruct geometry from that single view, and SaveGLB writes the result to disk as a GLB. A MarkdownNote is included in the canvas to provide tips and links, including ComfyUI’s Subgraph guide for quick onboarding.

Technically, the Hunyuan3D node infers the object’s shape directly from the image and outputs a triangular mesh (vertices, faces, normals) without textures or materials. This produces a neutral “white-mesh” GLB that’s ideal as a base for retopology, UVs, and texturing in your DCC of choice (e.g., Blender, Maya, Substance). The focus is on rapid reconstruction and consistent outputs: one input image in, one raw mesh out—ready for concepting, blockout, and downstream asset prep.

What makes this useful is its minimal configuration and predictable results. You don’t need multi-view photography or photogrammetry; the Subgraph encapsulates all the heavy lifting so you can iterate quickly by simply swapping the input image or adjusting any exposed detail/scale parameters inside the Subgraph when needed.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the Hunyuan3D 2.1 weights are installed (see Hugging Face: Comfy-Org/hunyuan3D_2.1). Restart ComfyUI after placing the model files as instructed by the node’s documentation.
Open the LoadImage node and select your reference photo. Aim for a clear, centered subject with minimal occlusion and a simple background. If needed, crop externally before loading.
Optionally open the Subgraph to review any exposed parameters (e.g., reconstruction/detail settings or output file naming). For a first pass, keep defaults.
Queue and run the workflow. The Hunyuan3D inference node reconstructs the mesh; SaveGLB writes a textureless GLB to your ComfyUI output folder (the node console shows the saved path).
Inspect the GLB in a 3D viewer or DCC (e.g., Blender). If the shape needs improvement, refine the input image (better crop/contrast) or adjust Subgraph parameters, then rerun.
Optional: Perform retopology, UV unwrapping, and texturing in your DCC, or decimate/smooth the mesh for real-time use.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid 3D concepting and blockout from a single reference photo.
Creating base meshes for game assets before retopology and PBR texturing.
Industrial/product design mockups from marketing or sketch renders.
Previsualization for film/AR where quick geometry is more important than materials.
Kitbashing workflows that need fast, textureless shapes to iterate on form.

faqItems.question: Does this generate textures or materials?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow outputs a raw, textureless white mesh (GLB) with geometry only. Add UVs, materials, and textures later in your DCC or texturing tool.

faqItems.question: What kind of input image works best?
faqItems.answer: Use a clear front or 3/4 view with the subject centered, minimal occlusions, and a simple background. Higher-quality images help; 512–1024 px on the short side is a good starting point.

faqItems.question: What are the system or VRAM requirements?
faqItems.answer: Hunyuan3D 2.1 runs on GPU. For stable results, a modern GPU with ample VRAM is recommended. If you encounter out-of-memory errors and the Subgraph exposes resolution/detail controls, lower them and try again.

faqItems.question: Can I use multiple images or get a watertight, production-ready mesh?
faqItems.answer: This template is single-image only and focuses on fast reconstruction, not production-grade topology. The mesh may require cleanup, retopology, and UVs before deployment. For multi-view capture or watertight guarantees, use pipelines designed for that purpose.

404250f61d0a.title: Image Generation
404250f61d0a.metaDescription: Harness the power of Stable Diffusion 1.5 for stunning image generation from text prompts with this comprehensive ComfyUI workflow.
404250f61d0a.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow offers a vivid foray into the world of artistic image generation, utilizing the power of Stable Diffusion 1.5. By leveraging sophisticated nodes like KSampler and CLIPTextEncode, users can transform simple text prompts into visually stunning imagery. The workflow is designed to harness the nuances of Stable Diffusion, trained on 512x512 datasets, ensuring high-quality results for appropriately sized images. Whether you're crafting a picturesque landscape with 'beautiful scenery nature glass bottle' or experimenting with abstract concepts like 'purple galaxy bottle,' the combination of nodes in this workflow allows for intricate detail and creative depth.

The workflow's structure, which includes steps for loading models, setting image sizes, and crafting prompts, provides a seamless experience for both novice and experienced users. The inclusion of a MarkdownNote node offers a layer of documentation, making it easy to annotate and iterate on creative projects. The use of positive and negative prompts further enhances creative control, enabling users to specify and refine the desired visual outcomes effectively. Overall, this workflow is a testament to the creative possibilities unlocked by advanced AI models and intuitive UI design.
howToUse: Load the Stable Diffusion 1.5 model using the CheckpointLoaderSimple node.
Set your desired image size, keeping in mind the 512x512 optimal size for best results.
Craft a text prompt that captures your creative vision using the CLIPTextEncode node.
Adjust positive and negative prompts to refine the image outcome.
Generate the image with the KSampler node and view the result with VAEDecode.
Save your image using the SaveImage node, either automatically or manually.
suggestedUseCases: Create surreal landscapes for digital art projects.
Design unique backgrounds for video game environments.
Generate concept art for visual storytelling.
Experiment with abstract art styles for personal expression.
Develop educational visuals for teaching complex concepts.

faqItems.question: How can I refine the details in my generated images?
faqItems.answer: Utilize positive prompts to emphasize specific elements and negative prompts to minimize unwanted details.

faqItems.question: What image size works best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow is optimized for 512x512 images, as the Stable Diffusion 1.5 model is trained on datasets of this size.

faqItems.question: Can I use my own custom prompts?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can craft custom text prompts using the CLIPTextEncode node to guide the image generation process.

faqItems.question: How do I save my generated images?
faqItems.answer: Images auto-save to the ComfyUI/output folder, or you can manually save by right-clicking on the SaveImage node.

40770c9eb41b.title: LTX-2 Text to Video
40770c9eb41b.description: Generate high-quality videos from text prompts with synchronized audio-video generation using LTX-2. Features expressive lip sync, dynamic motion generation, and efficient performance.
40770c9eb41b.metaDescription: Generate high-quality videos from text prompts with the LTX-2 workflow, featuring expressive lip sync and dynamic motion generation.
40770c9eb41b.extendedDescription: The LTX-2 Text to Video workflow in ComfyUI is designed to transform text prompts into high-quality videos with synchronized audio and video generation. This workflow leverages the LTX-2 model, developed by Lightricks, which is renowned for its expressive lip-sync capabilities and dynamic motion generation. The workflow efficiently processes text inputs to create videos that not only match the described actions but also maintain a high level of visual fidelity. Technically, it utilizes nodes such as SaveVideo and a subgraph node identified by b7c2d337-c38d-4c04-922b-2d638449d13e, which are crucial for saving the output and managing the complex video generation process. The MarkdownNote node is used for documentation and guidance within the workflow, ensuring users understand each step and parameter involved.
howToUse: Load the LTX-2 Text to Video workflow in ComfyUI.
Input your text prompt, ensuring to describe core actions and visual details.
Set the video resolution, ensuring width and height are divisible by 64.
Adjust the frame count to be divisible by 8 plus 1 for optimal results.
Run the workflow to generate your video, which will automatically save using the SaveVideo node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating educational videos with synchronized speech and visuals.
Generating promotional content with dynamic and engaging visuals.
Producing short films or animations based on script descriptions.
Developing interactive storytelling experiences with visual and audio elements.

faqItems.question: What resolution should I use for the best results?
faqItems.answer: By default, the workflow uses 720p resolution. You can try 1920x1088 if your system can handle higher resolutions, ensuring width and height are divisible by 64.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the frame count is correct?
faqItems.answer: Make sure the frame count is divisible by 8 plus 1. The workflow will adjust to the closest valid parameters if incorrect values are used.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for real-time video generation?
faqItems.answer: The LTX-2 workflow is optimized for high-quality video generation, which may not be suitable for real-time applications due to processing requirements.

faqItems.question: What kind of text prompts work best?
faqItems.answer: Prompts that clearly describe actions over time and include detailed visual descriptions yield the best results.

4099f26a2b9a.title: Depth Map: Depth Anything v2
4099f26a2b9a.description: Convert a Video to a temporally stable Depth Map
4099f26a2b9a.metaDescription: Convert a video into a depth-map video in ComfyUI with Depth Anything v2 and VHS nodes—perfect for ControlNet depth conditioning and depth-aware effects.
4099f26a2b9a.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow converts any input video into a depth-map video using Depth Anything v2. Frames are loaded with VHS_LoadVideo, inspected with VHS_VideoInfo to retain the original FPS and resolution, and then passed frame-by-frame through the DepthAnything_V2 node for monocular depth estimation. The model weights (depth_anything_v2_vitl_fp32.safetensors) are fetched automatically via DownloadAndLoadDepthAnythingV2Model, so you don’t need to place files manually. Finally, VHS_VideoCombine stitches the per-frame depth maps back into a video, preserving timing and delivering a clean, consistent depth sequence.

Technically, this graph performs deterministic per-frame inference with the same model and settings across the entire clip, which helps produce visually stable depth over time. There’s no optical-flow smoothing or temporal filtering here—stability comes from consistent processing and the robustness of Depth Anything v2’s ViT-L backbone. The resulting grayscale depth video is ideal as a ControlNet depth conditioning source, or as an input for depth-aware post effects like parallax, relighting previews, or compositing. The depth estimation block is encapsulated as a Subgraph, making it easy to reuse or swap models while keeping the video I/O steps intact.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI. Ensure the Video Helper Suite (VHS) and DepthAnything_V2 custom nodes are installed. On first run, DownloadAndLoadDepthAnythingV2Model will fetch depth_anything_v2_vitl_fp32.safetensors automatically.

Open VHS_LoadVideo and select your source video. Keep the default settings if you want to preserve the original frame order and resolution. Use VHS_VideoInfo to confirm FPS and resolution are read correctly.

Inspect the DepthAnything_V2 subgraph block. It will receive frames from VHS_LoadVideo and the loaded model from DownloadAndLoadDepthAnythingV2Model. No extra configuration is required for a baseline run.
Run the graph. DepthAnything_V2 will estimate per-frame depth and output a sequence of grayscale depth images. Monitor the queue to see progress through the clip.

Open VHS_VideoCombine. Set the output path/filename, choose a codec (e.g., H.264), and feed its FPS input from VHS_VideoInfo to match the source timing. Execute the node (or run the whole graph) to generate the depth-map video.

Review the output. If you need less flicker, stick to the original FPS, avoid frame skipping, and use high-quality input. For faster runs or lower VRAM, process a shorter clip or a lower-resolution source.
suggestedUseCases: ControlNet depth conditioning for video-to-video stylization or consistent scene transfers.
Depth-aware parallax (2.5D) and Ken Burns effects in video editors or compositors.
Precomputing depth passes for relighting previews or atmospheric effects (fog, DOF).
Generating depth references for motion graphics, masking, or quick scene layout checks.

faqItems.question: How is temporal stability achieved without optical-flow smoothing?
faqItems.answer: This workflow applies the same Depth Anything v2 model and settings to every frame in order. The consistency of the model and fixed parameters helps reduce per-frame drift. There is no explicit temporal filtering in this graph; stability will still depend on your footage (motion blur, lighting changes, compression).

faqItems.question: Which model does this use and how is it loaded?
faqItems.answer: It uses Depth Anything v2 (ViT-L, FP32). The DownloadAndLoadDepthAnythingV2Model node automatically downloads and loads depth_anything_v2_vitl_fp32.safetensors from the provided Hugging Face link on first run.

faqItems.question: What output format does VHS_VideoCombine produce?
faqItems.answer: VHS_VideoCombine encodes the processed frames into a standard video file. You can set the codec (e.g., H.264) and output path. Feed its FPS input from VHS_VideoInfo to preserve the source timing.

faqItems.question: Why do I still see some flicker in the depth video?
faqItems.answer: Monocular depth is computed per frame, so fast motion, heavy compression, and exposure changes can introduce variation. Use high-quality source video, avoid frame skipping, keep FPS consistent, and consider downscaling only if necessary to fit VRAM.

40a427168ef7.title: 1 image input Split Stack - Nano Banana 2 + Kling 3.0
40a427168ef7.description: Upload 1 input image and generate 5 alternate angles to be used as start frames with Kling 3.0. Each video is stacked horizontally in a final 9x16 video.
40a427168ef7.metaDescription: Turn one image into five Kling 3.0 videos from alternate angles and auto-stack them into a single 9:16 comparison clip in ComfyUI.
40a427168ef7.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow takes a single reference image and generates five alternate camera angles to use as starting frames for Kling 3.0 image-to-video. A set of utility nodes (including Reroute and PrimitiveNode) fans out your input from LoadImage into five branches, where a preconfigured "Nano Banana 2" angle-synthesis group produces varied viewpoints of the same subject. Each start frame is saved via SaveImage so you can verify framing and subject integrity before video generation.

Each of the five frames is then sent to KlingVideoNode to create short motion clips guided by your prompt (e.g., orbit, pan, dolly). Finally, the clips are tiled into a single portrait output using CreateVideo and saved with SaveVideo. The stacker uses a horizontal strip layout inside a 9:16 canvas, so you can compare all five angles in one shareable video. Optional GeminiImage2Node can auto-caption the input image to augment your motion prompt; if not used, the workflow falls back to manual text from a PrimitiveNode. This setup is practical when you need consistent, multi-angle starters for Kling 3.0 without hand-authoring separate variations.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the LoadImage node. Import a single, high-quality image with a clear subject and minimal motion blur.

If you use GeminiImage2Node, add your API key (if required) and enable it to generate a descriptive caption/tags. Otherwise, set your manual motion prompt (e.g., subtle orbit) in the provided PrimitiveNode connected to KlingVideoNode.

Adjust parameters exposed via PrimitiveNode/Reroute controls: duration and fps for KlingVideoNode, and the output resolution/aspect for CreateVideo (author presets include options like 720p, 2K, 16:9; final is arranged on a 9:16 canvas).

Run the first stage to generate the five alternate angles. Check the SaveImage outputs to confirm each start frame looks correct (subject centered, no cropping issues). If needed, tweak angle spacing or framing controls provided in the Nano Banana 2 group.
Run the KlingVideoNode stage to create five motion clips from the generated start frames. Keep motion prompts modest for realism (small orbit, gentle pan/dolly).
Run the final CreateVideo/SaveVideo stage to tile the five Kling clips into a single 9:16 stacked video. Review the composite and export the final file for sharing.
suggestedUseCases: Product spins and turnarounds: Generate multi-angle starters and compare motion variants in one vertical clip.
Character or portrait motion tests: Subtle head/torso or camera orbits from a single hero image.
Environment reveals: Pan/dolly variants across a scene to choose the most cinematic motion.
Social media A/B testing: One 9:16 stacked video showing five angles to quickly gather feedback.
Previsualization: Rapidly explore angle and motion direction before committing to longer renders.

faqItems.question: Do I need a Kling 3.0 account or API key?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The KlingVideoNode requires valid credentials. Enter your API key or session token in the node’s settings (or environment, if supported by your install) before running the video stage.

faqItems.question: What does the Nano Banana 2 step do?
faqItems.answer: It’s a preconfigured angle-synthesis group that takes your single input image and produces five alternate viewpoints to use as start frames for Kling 3.0. This helps you preview different angles without manually crafting separate inputs.

faqItems.question: Can I change the number of angles or their spacing?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The workflow is set up for five branches by default. You can duplicate or remove a branch after the Reroute fan-out, then update the tiling/stacking inputs going into CreateVideo so the composite matches the new count. Angle spacing controls (if exposed) live inside the Nano Banana 2 group.

faqItems.question: Why is the final video 9:16 if my source clips are 16:9?
faqItems.answer: The compositor tiles the five Kling outputs into a portrait canvas for mobile/social viewing. If you prefer landscape, change the aspect/size in the CreateVideo node (author presets include 720p/2K/16:9). Ensure all branches feed the compositor at the same resolution.

40dea2f852c3.title: Meshy 6: Text to Model
40dea2f852c3.description: Generate high-quality 3D models from text prompts using Meshy 6. Create characters with refined geometry, mechanical objects with sharp edges, or game-ready low-poly assets.
40dea2f852c3.metaDescription: Generate high-quality 3D models from text prompts with Meshy 6. Perfect for creating characters, mechanical objects, and game-ready assets.
40dea2f852c3.extendedDescription:
The 'Meshy 6: Text to Model' workflow is an innovative approach to generating high-quality 3D models directly from text prompts. Utilizing the Meshy suite of nodes, this workflow allows users to create a diverse range of 3D assets, from detailed character models to mechanical objects with precise geometry. At the core of this workflow is the MeshyTextToModelNode, which interprets textual descriptions and transforms them into initial 3D forms. The MeshyRefineNode then enhances these models, improving the geometry and adding intricate details. This is particularly useful for creating game-ready assets or detailed characters for animations.

The workflow also includes nodes like MeshyTextureNode for applying textures, and MeshyRigModelNode for adding skeletal structures to models, making them ready for animation. For those interested in animating their creations, the MeshyAnimateModelNode provides the tools necessary to bring models to life. Finally, the Preview3D node allows users to visualize their models in real-time, while the SaveGLB node enables exporting the final product in a widely-used 3D format. This comprehensive workflow is ideal for artists and developers looking to streamline their 3D model creation process using AI-driven techniques.
howToUse: Load the 'Meshy 6: Text to Model' workflow in ComfyUI.
Enter your text prompt into the MeshyTextToModelNode to generate an initial 3D model.
Use the MeshyRefineNode to enhance the model's geometry and details.
Apply textures using the MeshyTextureNode for a more realistic appearance.
If needed, add a rig to your model with the MeshyRigModelNode for animation purposes.
Preview your model with the Preview3D node and export it using the SaveGLB node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating detailed character models for video games or animations.
Designing mechanical objects with precise geometry for industrial design.
Generating low-poly assets for mobile games or VR applications.
Rapid prototyping of 3D models for concept art or visualization.
Developing custom 3D models for educational or training simulations.

faqItems.question: What types of text prompts work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Descriptive prompts with specific details about the desired model's features, such as shape, texture, and function, yield the best results.

faqItems.question: Can I animate the models created with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes, by using the MeshyRigModelNode and MeshyAnimateModelNode, you can rig and animate your models for various applications.

faqItems.question: What file format are the models exported in?
faqItems.answer: Models are exported in the GLB format, which is widely used and compatible with many 3D applications.

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for creating high-poly models?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the MeshyRefineNode can enhance models to a high level of detail, making it suitable for high-poly model creation.

414a6f8e0c33.title: Capybara: Text to Image
414a6f8e0c33.description: Input a text prompt to generate an image. This workflow uses the Capybara unified model for text-to-image synthesis.
414a6f8e0c33.metaDescription: Transform text prompts into images using the Capybara model in ComfyUI. Ideal for artists and designers seeking quick visualization.
414a6f8e0c33.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow, titled 'Capybara: Text to Image', leverages the Capybara unified model to transform text prompts into vivid images. At its core, the workflow utilizes a series of nodes, including the SaveImage node and a unique identifier node (4f4ddf39-1508-4d34-a35c-ff10e6ce995b), to process and output the generated images. The Capybara model is renowned for its ability to synthesize high-quality images from textual descriptions, making it an invaluable tool for artists, designers, and content creators seeking to visualize concepts quickly.

Technically, the workflow is designed to handle various aspect ratios and resolutions, from 480p at a 16:9 ratio to a square 1:1 format. However, for enhanced image quality, users are encouraged to increase the steps to 50. The integration of MarkdownNote allows users to document their creative process within the workflow, further enhancing its utility for iterative design and experimentation.

41f029c74cd4.title: Stylize Video - Frame by Frame - Flux.2 Klein 4b
41f029c74cd4.description: Create a stylized frame by frame effect on your input video by using Flux.2 Klein 4b Distilled image editing model.
41f029c74cd4.metaDescription: Stylize any video frame-by-frame with Flux.2 Klein 4b Distilled. Load, prompt-cycle, and reassemble frames for consistent, artistic video-to-video results.
41f029c74cd4.extendedDescription:
This workflow applies a consistent, frame-by-frame style transfer to any input video using the Flux.2 Klein 4b Distilled image editing model. It decodes your video with LoadVideo and reads resolution/FPS via GetVideoComponents, then uses VHS_SelectEveryNthImage to choose how densely to process frames (every frame, or every Nth for speed). Frames are organized with ImpactImageBatchToImageList so each image can be paired with a per-frame prompt.

Style prompts are generated and aligned with frames using a small prompt pipeline: GeminiNode can draft style-transfer lines following the Author Notes, RegexReplace cleans and normalizes the text (for example, removing numbering and enforcing "the source frame" phrasing), and FL_PromptMulti distributes one prompt per frame in a repeating cycle. Each frame and its corresponding prompt are fed into the Flux.2 Klein 4b editing node (the Flux.2 Klein 4b Distilled image editing model) to produce a stylized image while preserving the source frame’s structure. The processed images are repacked with ImageListToImageBatch, converted to a video using CreateVideo (matching the original FPS from GetVideoComponents), previewed via PreviewAny as needed, and written to disk with SaveVideo.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and drag in your source video to the LoadVideo node. GetVideoComponents will auto-read the video’s width/height/FPS.
Set the frame stride in VHS_SelectEveryNthImage. Use 1 to stylize every frame (best quality), or 2–4 to speed up tests with fewer frames.

Prepare prompts: either paste a multiline list into PrimitiveStringMultiline following the Author Notes format, or let GeminiNode draft them (ensure your Gemini API key is configured). RegexReplace will clean numbering and enforce the phrase “the source frame.”
Use FL_PromptMulti to map exactly one prompt per frame in a repeating cycle. Confirm prompt–frame pairing by sampling a few results in PreviewAny.
Run the Flux.2 Klein 4b Distilled image editing node to stylize frames. If results are too strong or inconsistent, simplify prompt wording and emphasize “the source frame.”
Rebuild the video: ImageListToImageBatch -> CreateVideo (feed FPS from GetVideoComponents) -> SaveVideo. Inspect the output and iterate on prompts or stride as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Music videos and reels that alternate visual treatments in a rhythmic, repeating cycle.
Editorial B-roll stylization for documentaries or YouTube segments without changing scene composition.
Motion tests for concept art: rapidly try multiple looks on the same footage by cycling prompts.
Brand experiments: apply a house style to diverse clips using the same prompt template.
Social clips with bold, consistent style transfer while preserving motion and layout.

faqItems.question: How does the prompt cycling work?
faqItems.answer: Provide a multiline list of style prompts or let GeminiNode generate them using the Author Notes’ pattern. FL_PromptMulti assigns one prompt per frame and repeats the list after the final line, ensuring a predictable style cycle across the video.

faqItems.question: Do I have to use GeminiNode for prompts?
faqItems.answer: No. You can paste hand-written prompts into PrimitiveStringMultiline. GeminiNode is optional and helps draft prompts; RegexReplace then normalizes them (e.g., removes numbering and enforces using “the source frame”).

faqItems.question: Will the output have audio?
faqItems.answer: This setup focuses on frame-to-frame visual stylization. If your CreateVideo/SaveVideo configuration doesn’t pass through audio, you can remux the original audio onto the stylized video using a video editor or ffmpeg.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce flicker between frames?
faqItems.answer: Keep prompts concise and consistent, always referencing “the source frame.” Avoid subject re-descriptions, keep style terms stable across frames, and process every frame (Nth=1) for best temporal consistency. Larger N values speed tests but increase perceptual jumps.

4266c2b7ce89.title: FLUX 3 Image Klein: Text to Image
4266c2b7ce89.description: Generate images from text prompts using FLUX 3 Image Klein, producing a single saved image with no file inputs required. Ideal for concept art, marketing visuals, and rapid prototyping of scene ideas from written descriptions.
4266c2b7ce89.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow for FLUX 3 Klein: prompt upsampling, 1024x1024 T2I, optional layout-to-bounding-box control, and fast 15-step er_sde sampling.
4266c2b7ce89.extendedDescription:
This workflow runs Black Forest Labs' FLUX 3 Image Klein locally in ComfyUI for fast, high-quality text-to-image generation. It loads the int8-quantized FLUX 3 Klein base, pairs it with the FLUX 2 VAE for decoding, and uses the Qwen3.5 9B prompt upsampler (qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_w4a8.safetensors) to expand short ideas into rich, well-structured captions before they reach the image model. By default, the main Text to Image (FLUX 3 Image Klein SD) node is configured for 1024x1024 output, 15 sampling steps, CFG 1.0, and the er_sde scheduler with the simple sampler—balanced settings that produce clean results quickly on consumer GPUs.

For spatial control, the workflow includes an optional layout branch built around Flux3LayoutPrompt and CreateBoundingBoxes. Use it to translate a concise layout description into actual region boxes and a synchronized prompt string. Feed the boxes to the model’s layout/bboxes input and the layout prompt STRING into the model’s prompt input for consistent regional guidance. ResolutionSelector makes switching sizes simple, PreviewAny provides quick visual checks (including box overlays), and SaveImage writes final renders to disk. The int8 base keeps VRAM usage modest; if you have 24 GB+ VRAM, you can swap in the bf16 base weights for slightly higher fidelity.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm models resolve: FLUX 3 Image Klein (int8), FLUX 2 VAE, and the Qwen3.5 9B prompt upsampler (w4a8). Use the provided Hugging Face repo if any weights are missing.
Enter a short idea in the Prompt Upsampler input. The Qwen3.5 upsampler will expand it into a detailed caption, which is automatically routed into the Text to Image (FLUX 3 Image Klein SD) node.

Set image size with ResolutionSelector (1024x1024 by default). Keep the default sampler configuration (15 steps, CFG 1.0, scheduler er_sde, sampler simple) for speed and quality; adjust steps upward if you need more detail.

Optional layout control: Describe regions in Flux3LayoutPrompt (e.g., 'top-left: logo; right: product; bottom: tagline'). Send its STRING output to the model’s prompt input and feed CreateBoundingBoxes into the model’s layout/bboxes input. Use PreviewAny to verify box positions before sampling.
Trigger the generation on the Text to Image node. Inspect the live preview; if results drift, lower CFG slightly (around 1.0 is typical for FLUX) or refine the upsampled caption.
When satisfied, SaveImage will write the final image to your output folder. For higher fidelity on 24 GB+ GPUs, swap the base model to bf16 and consider 20–25 steps.
suggestedUseCases: Product hero images with precise composition using regional bounding boxes (logo, product, callout areas).
Poster and social graphics where text or subject placement must hit specific zones.
Concept art and style frames from short prompts, boosted by the prompt upsampler for richer detail.
UI mockups or banners with controlled layout (icons left, imagery right, headline below).
Storyboards that need consistent subject placement across multiple panels.

faqItems.question: What VRAM do I need, and when should I switch to bf16?
faqItems.answer: The int8 FLUX 3 Klein base is designed to run on modest GPUs (commonly 12–16 GB). If you have 24 GB+ VRAM, you can swap to the bf16 base for slightly higher fidelity and stability, especially at larger resolutions.

faqItems.question: When should I use the prompt upsampler versus writing a long prompt myself?
faqItems.answer: Use the Qwen3.5 9B upsampler when starting from a short idea—it produces a strong, structured caption that FLUX responds to well. If you already have a detailed, carefully crafted prompt, you can bypass the upsampler and plug your text directly into the model’s prompt input.

faqItems.question: How do the layout and bounding boxes influence the image?
faqItems.answer: Flux3LayoutPrompt turns your layout description into a synchronized caption, while CreateBoundingBoxes provides explicit regions. Connect the STRING from Flux3LayoutPrompt to the model’s prompt input and the boxes to the model’s layout/bboxes input. This combination nudges subjects into the specified areas without hard masking.

faqItems.question: What sampler settings work best for FLUX 3 Klein?
faqItems.answer: The provided defaults (15 steps, CFG 1.0, er_sde scheduler, simple sampler) are a solid starting point. Increase steps to 20–25 for finer detail or larger resolutions. Keep CFG near 1.0 for FLUX; pushing it much higher can harm coherence.

442984cda980.title: Image Upscale: WaveSpeed
442984cda980.description: Upload an image to upscale its resolution. Generate an enhanced 2K, 4K, or 8K output that preserves details and reduces artifacts in JPEG, PNG, or WEBP format.
442984cda980.metaDescription: Upscale images to 2K, 4K, or 8K in ComfyUI using the WaveSpeed model. Preserve detail, reduce artifacts, and export as JPEG, PNG, or WEBP with visual comparison.
442984cda980.extendedDescription:

It chains LoadImage into WavespeedImageUpscaleNode (running the WaveSpeed model), then routes the result to SaveImage. You select a target resolution (2K/4K/8K) and your preferred file format (JPEG, PNG, or WEBP) for export via SaveImage. howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI. If you plan to use ImageCompare, go to the menu and switch to Nodes 2.0 (Image Compare is only available there).
Load your source image with the LoadImage node (choose a JPEG, PNG, or WEBP). The node outputs the image tensor to the graph.
Open WavespeedImageUpscaleNode and select your target size (2K, 4K, or 8K). Leave other fields at their defaults for a starting point.
Optional: If ImageCompare is available, connect the original (from LoadImage) and the upscaled result (from WavespeedImageUpscaleNode) to ImageCompare to preview differences.
Set up SaveImage to your desired format (JPEG, PNG, or WEBP) and filename/prefix. Connect the upscaled output to SaveImage.
Queue and run the workflow. Review the result (and ImageCompare, if used). If needed, adjust the target resolution or output format and run again.
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce product photos: upscale small catalog images to crisp 2K/4K for storefronts.
Digital art and illustration: prepare high-res exports for prints or portfolio sites.
Photography restoration: enlarge older photos while reducing compression artifacts.

faqItems.question: Which image formats are supported for input and output?

faqItems.question: Will upscaling change my image’s aspect ratio?

faqItems.question: When should I choose 2K vs 4K vs 8K?

44d156cf2723.title: Beeble SwitchX: Video Edit
44d156cf2723.description: Upload a source video and a reference image, then provide a prompt describing the desired environment and lighting. Generate an edited video where masked regions follow your prompt and reference, while unmasked regions preserve the original pixels and motion, plus an alpha matte for compositing.
44d156cf2723.metaDescription: ComfyUI video edit workflow using Beeble SwitchX to relight and replace regions by prompt and reference, preserving motion and outputting an alpha matte.
44d156cf2723.extendedDescription:
Beeble SwitchX: Video Edit is a targeted video editing workflow that lets you change only what you describe, while keeping everything else intact. You load a source video and (optionally) a reference image, then enter a prompt describing the new environment and lighting. The BeebleSwitchXVideoEdit node applies the Beeble SwitchX video-edit model to generate an edited clip where masked regions follow your prompt and reference, while unmasked regions preserve the original pixels and motion. The workflow also produces an alpha matte so you can composite the edited regions over the untouched source in any NLE.

Technically, the graph decodes your clip with LoadVideo, extracts dimensions and frame count via GetVideoComponents, and uses the "Get frame counts (need < 240)" group to help you stay under the model’s recommended frame limit. If your clip is too long, Video Slice trims it to a workable range. LoadImage brings in an optional look reference, and GetImageSize ensures the pipeline accounts for dimension matching. BeebleSwitchXVideoEdit then processes frames with temporal consistency, outputting both the edited video and a per-frame alpha matte. Use PreviewAny to inspect intermediate results, and SaveVideo to render the final edit. The result is a practical, non-destructive way to relight scenes, replace environments, or stylize specific objects without breaking the original motion.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and locate the main nodes: LoadVideo, LoadImage (optional reference), BeebleSwitchXVideoEdit, GetVideoComponents, Video Slice, PreviewAny, and SaveVideo.
In LoadVideo, select your source clip. Check the "Get frame counts (need < 240)" group to see total frames; if it’s over 240, set the in/out range in Video Slice to trim the clip.

Optionally set a reference look with LoadImage (e.g., a lighting or environment photo). Use GetImageSize to confirm dimensions; matching the video’s aspect ratio typically yields more coherent results.

Open BeebleSwitchXVideoEdit and enter a concise prompt describing the desired environment and lighting (e.g., "golden-hour sunset, warm directional light, soft shadows"). Ensure the reference is connected if you want the look to be enforced.

Queue the workflow. Use PreviewAny to check both the edited frames and the generated alpha matte. If the effect bleeds into areas you want untouched, refine your prompt to focus on the intended subject or provide a clearer reference image.
When satisfied, use SaveVideo to export the edited clip. To export the alpha matte as well, connect or duplicate SaveVideo on the matte output branch of BeebleSwitchXVideoEdit.
suggestedUseCases: Relighting a scene to match a specific time of day without re-shooting.
Environment or sky replacement while keeping original actors and camera motion.
Product shots: changing background and mood lighting while preserving the product’s true pixels.
Brand or art-direction alignment using a reference image to lock style and color tone.
Selective cleanup or stylization of a single object while leaving the rest of the frame untouched.

faqItems.question: Do I have to use a reference image?
faqItems.answer: No. The reference is optional. Without it, the edit follows your prompt. With a reference connected via LoadImage, the BeebleSwitchXVideoEdit node can better match style, color, and lighting to that image.

faqItems.question: Why is there a < 240 frame limit and how do I handle longer clips?
faqItems.answer: The workflow is tuned for clips under ~240 frames for memory and consistency. Use GetVideoComponents to inspect frame count and Video Slice to trim your clip to a shorter segment or process in batches.

faqItems.question: How do I keep specific areas unchanged?
faqItems.answer: The node preserves unmasked regions by design. If edits spill into unwanted areas, make your prompt more specific to the target subject or provide a clearer reference image so the internal matte focuses on the correct regions.

faqItems.question: How can I export the alpha matte?
faqItems.answer: Preview the matte with PreviewAny. To save it, route or duplicate SaveVideo on the matte output from BeebleSwitchXVideoEdit so you can export a separate grayscale or RGBA matte video for compositing.

The 'Tripo: Text to Model' workflow is a powerful tool for transforming textual descriptions into detailed 3D models. This workflow leverages the capabilities of the Tripo model, which excels in interpreting descriptive text and converting it into 3D objects. The process begins with the TripoTextToModelNode, which takes your input text and generates an initial 3D model draft. This draft can then be refined using a series of nodes such as TripoRigNode and TripoRetargetNode, which add skeletal structures and adjust the model for animation compatibility. Further refinement is achieved with the TripoConversionNode and TripoTextureNode, which enhance the model's geometry and surface details, respectively.

What sets this workflow apart is its comprehensive toolset for refining and exporting 3D models. The Preview3D node allows users to visualize the model in real-time, making it easier to make iterative adjustments. Once satisfied, the model can be saved in GLB format using the SaveGLB node, ensuring compatibility with various 3D applications. This workflow is particularly useful for artists and designers who need to quickly prototype 3D objects based on conceptual descriptions, streamlining the creative process and reducing the need for manual modeling.
howToUse: Load the 'Tripo: Text to Model' workflow in ComfyUI.
Input your descriptive text into the TripoTextToModelNode.
Use the TripoRigNode and TripoRetargetNode to add and adjust skeletal structures.
Refine the model's geometry and texture with TripoConversionNode and TripoTextureNode.

Export the final model using the SaveGLB node or find it auto-saved in 'ComfyUI/output/'.
