Configure the output settings for your desired video format (portrait or landscape).
Run the workflow to generate and save your video using the SaveVideo node.
Review the video output and make any necessary adjustments to the prompt or reference image for refinement.
suggestedUseCases: Create promotional videos for social media using descriptive text prompts.
Generate educational content with visual aids based on textual descriptions.
Produce personalized video messages with specific themes and actions.
Develop creative storytelling videos by combining text prompts with reference images.
Enhance marketing campaigns with custom video content tailored to specific audiences.

faqItems.question: Do I need to upload an image for the Text to Video generation?
faqItems.answer: Yes, uploading an image is required to provide visual reference and enhance the detail in the generated video.

faqItems.question: Can I generate videos in both portrait and landscape formats?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow is optimized for both portrait and landscape formats, allowing you to choose based on your needs.

faqItems.question: What models does this workflow use?
faqItems.answer: The workflow uses the LTX-2.3 model developed by Lightricks, which is available on Huggingface.

faqItems.question: How can I refine the video output?
faqItems.answer: You can refine the video by adjusting the text prompt for more precise descriptions and uploading different reference images to influence visual details.

4806ab282898.title: Qwen Image 3.0 Pro: Image Edit
4806ab282898.description: Qwen Image 3.0 Pro performs advanced image editing with rich multi-image input, generating complex layouts like newspapers, storyboards, menus, and exam papers in a single pass while preserving fine details down to 10px text, micro-expressions, and individual hairs. Supports native rendering across 12 languages with realistic simulation of web pages, games, and live streams. Ideal for professional content production, interface mockups, and high-fidelity commercial imagery requiring authentic detail.
4806ab282898.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Edit and compose multi-image layouts with Qwen Image 3.0 Pro via QwenImageEditApi. Generate newspapers, storyboards, menus with crisp text.
4806ab282898.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial shows how to perform high-fidelity, multi-image editing and layout composition with Qwen Image 3.0 Pro using the QwenImageEditApi node. The workflow is simple and modular: LoadImage nodes bring in your references (photos, screenshots, product shots), QwenImageEditApi applies the edit and assembles complex layouts from your instructions, and SaveImage writes the final result to disk. It excels at single-pass generation of structured pages—newspapers, storyboards, menus, exam papers—while aiming to preserve fine details such as small text, micro-expressions, and hair strands.

Technically, the QwenImageEditApi node calls the Qwen-Image model (Qwen Image 3.0 Pro) with both text instructions and multiple image inputs. The model is designed for layout-aware editing and native text rendering across 12 languages, enabling realistic simulations of web pages, game HUDs, and live-stream overlays. For best results, provide explicit, ordered layout instructions (for example, sections, columns, panel counts), include the exact copy you want rendered, specify the target language, and choose a sufficiently large output resolution so small elements (around 10px text) remain legible. SaveImage then captures the generated output with a clear filename prefix for versioning.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the three key nodes: LoadImage (your inputs), QwenImageEditApi (the editor/composer), and SaveImage (the output).

Add one or more LoadImage nodes and point each to a reference image you want to use (e.g., product shots, scene stills, UI screenshots). Connect these image outputs to the QwenImageEditApi image inputs.

Open the QwenImageEditApi node: enter your API credentials, select the Qwen-Image (Qwen Image 3.0 Pro) model if needed, and write a clear instruction prompt. Include layout structure (sections, columns, or panels), exact text to render, and the target language. Example: "Create a two-column newspaper front page. Headline: 'City Marathon 2026'. Left column: 3 paragraphs. Right column: 2 photos from inputs with captions in English."

If the node exposes size or quality settings, set an output resolution appropriate to your layout (larger canvases improve small-text clarity). Keep the prompt concise and ordered to reduce ambiguity.
Click Queue/Run. Inspect the generated image preview. If needed, refine the prompt (e.g., adjust section order, change copy, or swap input images) and run again.
In SaveImage, set a filename_prefix and verify the output directory. Re-run to save the final image versions for review or handoff.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid newspaper or magazine mockups combining headlines, body copy, and photo placements in one pass.
Film or game storyboards that assemble multiple scene stills into labeled, sequenced panels.
Multi-language restaurant menus, brochures, or flyers with precise, native text rendering.
Exam papers, worksheets, and study guides mixing typed questions, diagrams, and tables.
Interface mockups for web pages, game HUDs, or live-stream overlays using screenshots as references.

faqItems.question: Do I need an internet connection and an API key?
faqItems.answer: Yes. QwenImageEditApi sends your prompt and images to the Qwen-Image (Qwen Image 3.0 Pro) service. You must provide valid API credentials and be online for generation.

faqItems.question: How should I write prompts for reliable layouts and readable text?
faqItems.answer: Be explicit and structured: specify the layout (columns, panels), the exact text to render (headlines, captions, labels), and the target language. Keep instructions concise and ordered, and choose a sufficiently large output resolution to preserve small details.

faqItems.question: Can I use multiple images, and how many is ideal?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Connect multiple LoadImage nodes to the QwenImageEditApi image inputs. Use only images that are relevant to the final layout to keep the composition focused and avoid conflicting cues.

faqItems.question: How do I preserve key subjects or faces while editing?
faqItems.answer: Include clear constraints in your prompt (e.g., "preserve the person’s face from Image 1; adjust background only"). Provide high-quality references and limit unnecessary inputs so the model can prioritize the specified subjects.

faqItems.question: Does it support multiple languages?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Qwen Image 3.0 Pro supports native rendering across 12 languages. Write your copy directly in the target language or state the desired language in the prompt and provide exact text to minimize errors.

48e3274c52c9.title: Image Outpainting: FLUX.2 Klein 9B
48e3274c52c9.description: Use the FLUX.2 Klein 9B model to intelligently extend and expand image content. Input an image to generate seamless outpainting and extended compositions.
48e3274c52c9.metaDescription: Outpaint images with FLUX.2 Klein 9B in ComfyUI. Mask, prompt, and extend canvases seamlessly using Flux2Scheduler, CFGGuider, and SamplerCustomAdvanced.
48e3274c52c9.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates clean, controllable image outpainting using the FLUX.2 Klein 9B model. It pads your input image to a larger canvas with ImagePadForOutpaint, lets you paint exactly where new content should appear via DrawMaskOnImage, and preserves the original content by encoding it with VAELoader + VAEEncode. The UNETLoader loads the Flux.2 Klein model, while CLIPLoader + CLIPTextEncode handle positive and negative prompts that guide the newly generated regions. ReferenceLatent ties the original latents and the mask together so the sampler knows what to keep and where to invent new pixels.

Under the hood, SamplerCustomAdvanced drives the diffusion steps using Flux2Scheduler for step timing and RandomNoise (seeded) for reproducibility. CFGGuider applies classifier-free guidance strength to balance fidelity and creativity, and ConditioningZeroOut helps attenuate prompt influence where you want strict preservation. ImageScaleToTotalPixels and GetImageSize control working resolution to fit your GPU memory, while EmptyFlux2LatentImage initializes a target latent that matches the padded canvas. After sampling, VAEDecode reconstructs the extended image, and SaveImage writes the final result to disk. The workflow groups (Upload Image, Pad Image, Models, Prompt, Sampler, Compare, Result) keep the process organized and easy to iterate.

The result is seamless, prompt-aware outpainting that respects your source image while filling new borders with coherent detail. Whether you need extra background for layout changes, social crops, or wide cinematic frames, this setup offers precise mask control, stable prompting, and consistent outputs through seed management.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure models are set: UNETLoader to FLUX.2 Klein 9B, CLIPLoader to the matching text encoder, and VAELoader to the compatible VAE.
Upload your source image in the Upload Image group (LoadImage). If needed, control target working size with ImageScaleToTotalPixels to fit your GPU memory.

Pad the canvas using ImagePadForOutpaint to add space on chosen sides. Then refine the generation area with DrawMaskOnImage: paint the regions to be generated (typically the newly padded borders) and leave preserved areas unmasked.

Write your prompt in CLIPTextEncode (positive) and optional negative prompt. Use KSamplerSelect to pick the sampler mode, set steps and guidance in Flux2Scheduler and CFGGuider, and set a seed in RandomNoise for reproducibility.
Run the graph. The workflow encodes the input (VAEEncode), binds mask and latents with ReferenceLatent and ConditioningZeroOut, samples with SamplerCustomAdvanced, then decodes with VAEDecode.

Review the result in the Compare/Result groups and SaveImage to export. If you see seams or drift, slightly overlap the mask into the original image, lower CFG in CFGGuider, adjust steps in Flux2Scheduler, or refine the prompt.
suggestedUseCases: Extend backgrounds for product photos to match new aspect ratios without reshooting.
Create cinematic widescreen frames by expanding scenery around a key subject.
Add clean margins for social media crops, text-safe areas, and graphic layouts.
Rebuild cropped elements or restore missing borders in scans and archival photos.
Concept art scene expansion: continue architecture, terrain, or skies beyond the frame.

faqItems.question: How does this differ from a basic outpaint/inpaint workflow?
faqItems.answer: This setup uses ReferenceLatent to anchor the original image latents and a mask so the sampler respects what should be preserved. ConditioningZeroOut further reduces prompt influence in protected areas, and Flux2Scheduler with SamplerCustomAdvanced is tuned for FLUX.2-style sampling. The result is tighter fidelity and fewer artifacts at the boundary.

faqItems.question: What settings help avoid visible seams at the edges?
faqItems.answer: Feather the mask edge in DrawMaskOnImage and overlap a few pixels into the original content, keep CFGGuider at a moderate value, add descriptive cues about existing content in your prompt (colors, lighting), and increase steps slightly in Flux2Scheduler if detail looks underdeveloped.

faqItems.question: What resolution should I use?
faqItems.answer: Use ImageScaleToTotalPixels to cap total pixels so it fits your VRAM. Larger canvases need more memory and time. Start conservatively, then increase total pixels as your hardware allows. Keep batch size at 1 for outpainting stability.

faqItems.question: How can I make results reproducible or explore variations?
faqItems.answer: Set a fixed seed in RandomNoise for reproducible outputs. To explore variations, change the seed, tweak CFGGuider slightly, or adjust the mask shape. For targeted tweaks, keep the same seed and modify only the prompt or mask.

490b1f4c2d0f.title: MiniMax H3 Max: Text to Video
490b1f4c2d0f.description: Generate polished, prompt-faithful video from text using Minimax H3 Max, producing a single finished video clip with no input files required. Ideal for rapid concept exploration, cinematic text-to-video scenes, and high-throughput creative iteration where speed and visual quality matter.
490b1f4c2d0f.metaDescription: MiniMax H3 Max text-to-video in ComfyUI with optional prompt enhancement and 2K upscale. Generate polished clips from text—no input files required.
490b1f4c2d0f.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI template builds a complete text-to-video pipeline around MiniMax H3 Max (Hailuo 03). At its core, MinimaxHailuo03TextToVideoNode turns your prompt from PrimitiveStringMultiline into a polished video, which is then written to disk by SaveVideo. SaveText also records the exact prompt that reached the generator so you can reproduce results later.

Two optional stages are wired behind ComfySwitchNode gates (visually marked in red) and controlled from the Feature Flags group. First, the Prompt Enhancer (Optional) can route your text through MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode before generation, producing a context IR object that the downstream node can use. Second, the Upscale Video to 2K (Optional) stage uses MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode to request a higher-resolution version of the same result. Important: the upscale stage only accepts a 768p source; set the base generator to 768p if you enable the Upscale to 2K boolean. This design lets you move quickly from idea to finished clip, then optionally refine fidelity and resolution without changing your base prompt.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm your MiniMax API settings in the MinimaxHailuo03* nodes (use your key or environment configuration as required).
Open the User Inputs group and write your prompt in PrimitiveStringMultiline. Be explicit about subject, motion, camera, lighting, and style for best results.
In Feature Flags, choose whether to enable the Prompt Enhancer and/or Upscale to 2K. The red ComfySwitchNode blocks on the canvas indicate which path will be active.
If you turn on Upscale to 2K, set the base generation resolution to 768p in MinimaxHailuo03TextToVideoNode. The upscale stage only works when the source video is 768p.

Run the Video Generation (Core) path. When optional stages are enabled, the switches will route through MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode (prompt enhancer) and then to MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode (2K upscale).

Retrieve your outputs: SaveVideo writes the final video to your ComfyUI output folder, and SaveText stores the resolved prompt for reference. Iterate by refining the prompt or toggling the feature flags as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept exploration for ads, trailers, and mood pieces with no input assets.
Cinematic establishing shots or short scenes generated from concise text direction.
Previsualization for storyboards and animatics before committing to full production.
Social media loops and shorts where quick iteration and prompt faithfulness matter.
High-throughput ideation sprints across multiple style and camera directions.

faqItems.question: Do I need any input images or footage?
faqItems.answer: No. This template is text-only. Enter your description in PrimitiveStringMultiline and the MinimaxHailuo03TextToVideoNode generates a complete clip.

faqItems.question: How do the red switch nodes affect the run?
faqItems.answer: They are ComfySwitchNode gates for optional paths. Feature Flags toggles decide whether your prompt flows through MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode (enhancer) and whether the output is sent to MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode for a 2K upscale.

faqItems.question: Why does the 2K upscale fail or get skipped?
faqItems.answer: The upscale stage only accepts a 768p source. Set MinimaxHailuo03TextToVideoNode to generate 768p before enabling the Upscale to 2K boolean. Other source resolutions are not supported for this step.

faqItems.question: Where do I find the outputs and how can I reproduce a result?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo writes the final clip to your ComfyUI output folder (path set in the node). SaveText stores the resolved prompt used for the run, helping you recreate or iterate on the same setup.

49544ae3e1b4.title: Qwen Image Edit 2511: SYSTMS ACTION LoRA
49544ae3e1b4.description: Upload your target image and use the trigger phrase "action the [thing]" (e.g., "action the scene"). Generate a toy or action figure version of your subject with articulated joints, plastic materials, and painted details.
49544ae3e1b4.metaDescription: Convert photos into action-figure style images using Qwen-Image-Edit and a LoRA trigger phrase: “action the [thing]”. Fast, repeatable toy-look image editing.
49544ae3e1b4.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow turns any photo into a stylized action figure or toy, guided by the Qwen-Image-Edit model and a SYSTMS ACTION LoRA. You load a source image with the LoadImage node, pass it to the Qwen Image Edit node (node ID cdb2cf24-c432-439b-b5c8-5f69838580c9), and use the trigger phrase "action the [thing]" to direct the edit. The LoRA biases the model toward plastic materials, articulated joints, and painted surface details while preserving the core composition of your input.

Under the hood, the custom Qwen-Image-Edit node handles instruction-based editing on the uploaded image. The MarkdownNote included in the graph provides inline tips, and SaveImage writes the results to your ComfyUI output folder. Because the aesthetic comes from a targeted LoRA plus a simple, consistent trigger phrase, you can iterate quickly—swapping subjects, adjusting prompt wording, and balancing stylization versus fidelity—without rebuilding the graph.
howToUse: Install the Qwen Image nodes and weights: download from Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI and Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-Edit_ComfyUI (see links in the workflow’s MarkdownNote), then place the model files where your ComfyUI setup expects them.

Open the workflow in ComfyUI. In the Qwen Image Edit node (ID cdb2cf24-c432-439b-b5c8-5f69838580c9), confirm the Qwen-Image-Edit model is detected and that the SYSTMS ACTION LoRA configuration is loaded as provided by the workflow.
Use the LoadImage node to select your target photo. For best results, choose a well-lit image with a clear subject and minimal motion blur.

In the Qwen Image Edit node’s prompt, use the trigger phrase: “action the [thing]” (e.g., “action the scene”, “action the person”, “action the car”) and, if desired, add concise descriptors like “plastic, articulated joints, painted details”.
Queue and run the workflow. The SaveImage node will export your results to the ComfyUI/output folder. Inspect the output and note how strongly the toy aesthetic is applied.

Iterate: adjust the wording around the trigger, try different subjects, and tweak any available strength/guidance controls in the Qwen Image Edit node to trade off between faithful structure and a stronger action-figure look.
suggestedUseCases: Product concept art: turn real product photos into collectible action-figure mockups for pitches and thumbnails.
Character look-dev: convert portraits or cosplay shots into toy-line visuals to explore materials and jointing.
Social content and posters: stylize everyday scenes into toy dioramas for playful campaigns or event promos.
Storyboard and mood frames: reimagine key frames as miniature plastic sets to communicate tone and props.
Packaging previews: generate toy-like renderings to visualize front-of-box hero shots.

faqItems.question: Why use the phrase “action the [thing]”?
faqItems.answer: The SYSTMS ACTION LoRA is trained to respond to this trigger, pushing the edit toward toy-like plastic materials, articulated joints, and painted details. Keeping the trigger consistent improves reliability.

faqItems.question: Does this work on any kind of photo?
faqItems.answer: It works best on images with a clear, well-lit subject and moderate complexity. Busy backgrounds or heavy motion blur can reduce how cleanly the action-figure style transfers.

faqItems.question: How can I keep the original composition and identity?
faqItems.answer: Use concise prompts centered on the trigger phrase, avoid adding many new objects, and reduce any available edit/strength settings in the Qwen Image Edit node to preserve structure and facial identity.

faqItems.question: Can I limit the edit to only part of the image?
faqItems.answer: This starter workflow does not include a mask. If you need selective edits, add a masking branch (e.g., a separate Mask or Alpha workflow) before feeding the image into the Qwen Image Edit node.

4982784a9a49.title: Qwen Image 2512: 360 Panorama Image
4982784a9a49.description: Generate 360-degree equirectangular projection images from text descriptions using a rank 128 LoRA on the 20B MMDiT model.
4982784a9a49.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate 360° equirectangular panoramas from text using Qwen-Image 2512 with a rank-128 LoRA. Fast text-to-360 images ready for VR and web.
4982784a9a49.extendedDescription:
This workflow generates true 360-degree panoramas in equirectangular format directly from text prompts using Qwen-Image 2512, a 20B MMDiT model, enhanced with a rank-128 Qwen 360 Diffusion LoRA. The core generation is encapsulated in a Subgraph node (c3c58f7e-2004-43ae-8b06-a956294bf7f4), which loads the Qwen-Image model and applies the LoRA to bias the model toward consistent 2:1 panoramic scenes. A PrimitiveStringMultiline node captures your natural-language prompt, and a StringConcatenate node appends essential keywords like "equirectangular," "360 image," and "360 panorama" to reinforce the correct projection during sampling.

Technically, this design keeps the UI simple while encoding best practices for 360 generation inside the Subgraph. You supply a scene description (e.g., "sunset over a coastal city with reflective water, modern skyline"), and the concatenated keywords ensure the model composes the environment as a wrapped sphere mapped to an equirectangular (2:1) frame. The SaveImage node writes the final panorama to disk, ready for any 360-capable viewer. Embedded MarkdownNote guidance in the graph explains what each part does and links to ComfyUI’s Subgraph documentation for deeper customization. With the LoRA trained on tens of thousands of 2:1 panoramas (landscapes, interiors, people, objects), this setup reliably produces seamless horizons suited for VR, 360 web embeds, and skybox pipelines.
howToUse: Install the Qwen-Image integration for ComfyUI and place the model files from Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI (Hugging Face or ModelScope) in the locations specified by that repo. Download the Qwen 360 Diffusion LoRA and put it in your ComfyUI lora folder.
Load the provided workflow. Open the PrimitiveStringMultiline node and enter your scene description (e.g., interior, landscape, time of day, mood, materials, lighting).

Leave the StringConcatenate node as-is so the workflow appends panorama-specific keywords (e.g., “equirectangular”, “360 panorama”) to your prompt. This helps enforce correct 2:1 spherical projection.

In the Subgraph node (c3c58f7e-2004-43ae-8b06-a956294bf7f4), select a 2:1 resolution (e.g., 2048×1024 or 3072×1536) appropriate for your GPU memory. If exposed, adjust seed, steps, and LoRA strength to taste. For advanced tuning, open the Subgraph to edit internal sampler settings. See: docs.comfy.org/interface/features/subgraph.
Set your SaveImage node output directory and filename pattern so each render is saved with a unique name.
Click Queue/Execute. Preview the output; if needed, refine your prompt (keep the panorama keywords), adjust resolution or LoRA strength, and re-run until you achieve a seamless 360 image.
suggestedUseCases: VR/AR previews and virtual tours: generate immersive 360 scenes for quick spatial ideation.
Architectural interiors and real-estate mockups: full-room views with consistent horizons.
Game development skyboxes or environment concepts: fast iteration on lighting and mood.
360 web embeds and social media posts that support equirectangular images.
Product showcases in context-rich, wraparound environments.

faqItems.question: What output size should I use for 360 equirectangular images?
faqItems.answer: Always use a 2:1 aspect ratio (width:height). Common sizes are 2048×1024, 3072×1536, and 4096×2048. Higher resolutions improve clarity in VR but require more GPU memory.

faqItems.question: How do I view the result as an interactive 360 panorama?
faqItems.answer: Use any 360-capable viewer that supports equirectangular images (2:1). Options include web-based 360 viewers, desktop panorama viewers, or platforms like Facebook 360. If a viewer doesn’t auto-detect the projection, add standard GPano/XMP tags with an external tool.

faqItems.question: My image shows seams or warping—how can I improve it?
faqItems.answer: Keep the panorama keywords (e.g., “equirectangular, 360 panorama”) in the prompt, use a strict 2:1 resolution, and try slightly increasing sampling steps. If exposed, reduce LoRA strength for subtler bias or raise it for stronger panoramic consistency. Large, high-contrast objects crossing the wrap point can accent seams—rephrase prompts to balance scene composition.

faqItems.question: Do I need a negative prompt or special settings?
faqItems.answer: Negative prompts are optional and depend on your style goals and what the Subgraph exposes. Start with the default setup (positive prompt + appended panorama keywords). For finer control, open the Subgraph to adjust sampler, steps, guidance, or LoRA strength as needed.

498e6ce100c7.title: Wan Dancer: Music to Dance
498e6ce100c7.description: Generate minute-scale coherent dance videos from music using a hierarchical Wan Dancer framework. Input a music file and reference image to produce high-resolution dance videos with global structure and temporal continuity.
498e6ce100c7.metaDescription: Generate a 5-second dance video from music and a reference image in ComfyUI using Wan Dancer. Coherent motion, easy export.
498e6ce100c7.extendedDescription:
Wan Dancer: Music to Dance is a ComfyUI workflow that turns a music clip and a single reference image into a coherent, short dance video. It uses the Wan Dancer model inside a Subgraph (node ID f7467834-35a6-42fe-b525-7f17383beb4f) to generate all frames in one pass, preserving global structure and temporal continuity. You provide a portrait or full-body image in LoadImage and an audio file in LoadAudio; the subgraph handles conditioning and sampling, and SaveVideo assembles the output clip.

Technically, the subgraph packs the full Wan Dancer pipeline: it encodes your reference image as appearance/style conditioning, derives audio conditioning from the waveform, and samples a fixed-length video (149 frames by default) with long-range temporal attention so poses and motion stay consistent across time. The default configuration produces a ~5 second clip. Because the model samples many frames at once, it is VRAM-intensive and benefits from a high-memory GPU. SaveVideo then writes the frames to a video file at an appropriate frame rate for smooth playback.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the Wan Dancer weights are installed (see Comfy-Org/Wan-Dancer on Hugging Face or ModelScope). Restart ComfyUI after placing the files as instructed by the model repo.
In the LoadImage node, select a clear reference image (single subject, good lighting, minimal background). Full-body images generally help with more complete motion.
In the LoadAudio node, choose your music clip. The default graph outputs ~5 seconds, so use or trim audio accordingly (the workflow will use the first 5 seconds by default).

Optionally, open the Wan Dancer Subgraph (node f7467834-35a6-42fe-b525-7f17383beb4f) to review any exposed parameters (e.g., resolution, seed, duration/frames if available). Keep in mind the model samples 149 frames at once and is VRAM-heavy.
Click Queue/Execute. The subgraph will generate 149 frames in one pass; SaveVideo will assemble them into a playable video with smooth timing.
Preview the result. Iterate by adjusting the reference image (pose, framing) or trying a different audio segment. For longer sequences, generate multiple clips and stitch them in a video editor.
suggestedUseCases: Choreography previews: Quickly visualize how a look or character might move to a song segment.
Social media loops: Create short, music-driven dance clips for posts or stories.
Music video ideation: Prototype concepts and motion beats before a full production.
Avatar movement tests: Explore how a branded character or VTuber-style avatar dances to various tracks.

faqItems.question: What hardware do I need to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Wan Dancer samples 149 frames at once and uses a large amount of VRAM. A high-memory GPU is strongly recommended. If you encounter out-of-memory errors, lower the output resolution (if exposed in the subgraph) or close other GPU-intensive applications.

faqItems.question: Can I change the clip duration or frame rate?
faqItems.answer: By default, the workflow outputs ~5 seconds. If the subgraph exposes duration/frames, you can adjust them—but note longer clips require even more VRAM. Otherwise, generate multiple 5-second segments and stitch them in an editor. The SaveVideo node will use a suitable frame rate for smooth playback.

faqItems.question: What kind of reference image works best?
faqItems.answer: Use a sharp, well-lit image of a single subject with minimal background clutter. Full-body or at least upper-body framing helps the model infer motion more completely. Avoid multiple people, extreme occlusions, or tiny subjects.

faqItems.question: Which audio formats are supported?
faqItems.answer: LoadAudio typically supports common formats. If you run into issues, convert your file to WAV and try again. The workflow uses the first ~5 seconds of the selected audio by default.

49a2f3a0811f.title: Seedance 2.0 + LLM Prompt Helper
49a2f3a0811f.description:
This workflow uses two reference images and a simple text description to automatically generate a detailed Seedance 2.0-style prompt using an LLM. Instead of spending time figuring out complex prompting structure, the workflow analyzes your references and builds the prompt for you, making it much faster and easier to create high-quality results.

The included LLM helper is designed to match the style and formatting that works well with Seedance 2.0, helping streamline the entire process while still giving you full control over the final output. Just drop in your references, describe the scene or motion you want, and the workflow handles the prompt generation automatically.
49a2f3a0811f.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow that uses two reference images and an LLM to auto-generate Seedance 2.0 prompts, then renders and saves video with ByteDance2ReferenceNode.
49a2f3a0811f.extendedDescription:
Seedance 2.0 + LLM Prompt Helper streamlines prompt creation for ByteDance/Seedance-style video generation by pairing two reference images with a short scene description. The workflow routes your images through LoadImage and ImageConcanate to form a clear, side-by-side visual context, which the GeminiNode then analyzes along with your text to draft a Seedance 2.0–formatted prompt. PreviewAny lets you inspect and copy the LLM’s output before it’s sent on, while PreviewImage helps you sanity-check your references.

Once you’re happy with the generated prompt, it feeds into ByteDance2ReferenceNode (the Seedance 2.0 runner) to produce the motion result. You can review frames with PreviewAny/PreviewImage (as applicable) and export the final animation via SaveVideo. A MarkdownNote in the canvas documents tips and conventions the LLM uses so the prompt it produces aligns with Seedance 2.0’s expected structure and tags. The result: you spend less time reverse-engineering prompt syntax and more time iterating on visuals and motion.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then open the Reference Images group. Use the two LoadImage nodes to import your subject and style/location references. Use PreviewImage to confirm they’re clean, well-lit, and correctly oriented.
Optionally concatenate the references for context: ensure both LoadImage outputs feed into ImageConcanate. This combined image helps the GeminiNode see both references side-by-side.

Open the LLM group. In the GeminiNode, enter a concise scene or motion description (e.g., “slow dolly-in on a dancer under neon lights, subtle hair movement”). Queue the LLM subgraph with the Seedance node bypassed: select ByteDance2ReferenceNode and press Ctrl+B to bypass so only the prompt helper runs.

Inspect the generated prompt: connect GeminiNode’s text output to PreviewAny (already wired in the template). Review tags, camera cues, and style notes. Edit the text (either in the GeminiNode prompt, re-run, or paste and refine directly into the ByteDance2ReferenceNode’s prompt field).

Un-bypass the ByteDance2ReferenceNode (Ctrl+B again) when the prompt looks right. Queue the full workflow. The Seedance 2.0 node will use the two references and the LLM-refined prompt to render the motion sequence.

Use SaveVideo to export your result. Adjust SaveVideo settings (e.g., fps/quality if exposed) and save to your desired location. Iterate: tweak the text prompt, swap references, or re-run for variations.
suggestedUseCases: Style transfer for motion: use a subject reference plus a separate aesthetic reference to guide the look while generating Seedance 2.0 motion.
Product motion previews: pair a clean product shot with an environment/style reference to draft quick marketing loops.
Character motion studies: combine a character render with a lighting/mood reference to test subtle motion and camera moves.
Location scouting mockups: mix a subject with a venue reference to preview how motion and framing might play together.
Social-ready loops: rapidly iterate on short, on-brand motion clips using repeatable prompt patterns.

faqItems.question: Do I need the LLM to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No. The LLM (GeminiNode) is optional. You can bypass it and write your own Seedance 2.0–style prompt directly in ByteDance2ReferenceNode. The LLM simply drafts a well-structured prompt from your references and description.

faqItems.question: How are the two reference images used?
faqItems.answer: They ground the content and style the LLM describes and guide Seedance 2.0’s final render. Use one image for the subject and one for style or environment. The ImageConcanate node provides a side-by-side composite to give the LLM clearer context.

faqItems.question: Does GeminiNode require an internet connection or API key?
faqItems.answer: Yes, GeminiNode typically relies on the Google Gemini API. You’ll need a valid API key configured in your ComfyUI environment and a working internet connection. If that isn’t available, bypass the LLM and input prompts manually.

faqItems.question: How can I improve consistency and quality?
faqItems.answer: Use high-resolution, clean references without heavy text/watermarks. Keep the subject well-centered, match lighting between references, and be explicit in your description about camera motion (e.g., “slow pan left”), timing, and mood. Iterate by refining the LLM prompt and re-running.

4a4da321a45d.title: Light Migration for Character Portrait
4a4da321a45d.description: Upload a portrait of your character and a reference lighting image. Generate an image with reference lighting applied and character consistency.
4a4da321a45d.metaDescription: Apply reference lighting to character portraits with consistency using the Light Migration workflow in ComfyUI.
4a4da321a45d.extendedDescription:
The 'Light Migration for Character Portrait' workflow is designed to seamlessly integrate a reference lighting style into a character portrait, while maintaining the character's original features. Utilizing the Qwen-Image-Edit model, this workflow allows users to upload a portrait and a reference image that demonstrates the desired lighting conditions. The workflow then processes these inputs to generate a new image that applies the reference lighting to the character portrait, ensuring consistency and realism. This is achieved through a series of nodes, including 'LoadImage' for importing images, 'SaveImage' for exporting the final result, and a specialized node for applying the lighting transformation.

Technically, the workflow leverages the Qwen model's capabilities in image editing and transformation. The process begins with loading the character portrait and reference lighting image using the 'LoadImage' node. The Qwen-Image-Edit model then analyzes the lighting conditions in the reference image and applies these to the character portrait. This ensures that the lighting appears natural and coherent with the character's existing features. The workflow concludes with saving the newly generated image using the 'SaveImage' node. This technique is particularly useful for artists and designers who need to visualize characters under different lighting scenarios without compromising on character integrity.
howToUse: Load the 'Light Migration for Character Portrait' workflow in ComfyUI.
Upload your character portrait using the 'LoadImage' node.
Upload the reference lighting image using another 'LoadImage' node.
Run the workflow to process the images using the Qwen-Image-Edit model.
Review the generated image with applied lighting and save it using the 'SaveImage' node.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing character portraits with dramatic lighting for digital art.
Creating consistent lighting conditions across a series of character illustrations.
Visualizing characters in different environments for game design.
Improving the realism of portraits for marketing materials.
Testing lighting scenarios for animated character development.

faqItems.question: Can I use any image as a reference for lighting?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can use any image that clearly demonstrates the desired lighting conditions. The model will analyze and apply these to your character portrait.

faqItems.question: Will the character's features change with the new lighting?
faqItems.answer: No, the workflow is designed to maintain the character's original features while applying the new lighting, ensuring consistency and realism.

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported for image uploads?
faqItems.answer: The 'LoadImage' node supports common image formats such as JPEG, PNG, and BMP for both the character portrait and reference lighting image.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to adjust the intensity of the applied lighting?
faqItems.answer: Currently, the workflow applies the lighting as detected from the reference image. For custom adjustments, additional editing might be required post-process.

4a6697085e75.title: Graphic Design Recomposer
4a6697085e75.description: Upload a graphic design and select your desired aspect ratio. This workflow generates and recomposes the graphic to fit the new aspect ratio.
4a6697085e75.metaDescription: Recompose any design to a new aspect ratio in ComfyUI using smart crop, letterbox, or outpainting. Load, set ratio, and save clean, ready-to-use variants.
4a6697085e75.extendedDescription:
Graphic Design Recomposer takes any existing graphic (logos, posters, social tiles, UI mockups) and reformats it to a new aspect ratio without manual layout work. The workflow is intentionally lean: LoadImage ingests your source file, a custom recomposition node (UUID 172f1008-9337-4d2f-9212-ee081cb4faf5) analyzes the target aspect and adapts the layout, and SaveImage writes the final result. Depending on your settings, it can scale-to-fit with letterboxing, crop-to-fill, or extend the canvas and synthesize new surrounding content for a seamless look.

Technically, the recomposer node computes the optimal scale and offset for the source image relative to the requested aspect ratio, then applies one of three strategies: smart crop, letterbox padding, or canvas expansion with outpainting. For outpainting, the node builds a border mask around the newly created areas and fills them using context from adjacent pixels to minimize visible seams—no prompt required. Feathering around mask edges and adaptive blending reduce halos or sharp transitions. The result is saved via SaveImage, making it quick to generate multiple aspect variants ready for web, print, or social placements.

This is especially useful when you need consistent assets across 1:1, 4:5, 16:9, or 9:16 formats without redrawing layouts. By keeping the pipeline simple and node-local (LoadImage → 172f1008-9337-4d2f-9212-ee081cb4faf5 → SaveImage), you get predictable results with minimal setup, and you can iterate fast by adjusting aspect, crop/fit/extend behavior, and seam smoothing.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the LoadImage node. Select your source graphic (PNG/JPG).
Open the recomposer node (UUID 172f1008-9337-4d2f-9212-ee081cb4faf5). Set your target aspect ratio (e.g., 1:1, 4:5, 16:9, 9:16) or enter explicit width/height.
Choose the recomposition mode: Fit (letterbox with no cropping), Fill (smart crop to fully occupy the frame), or Extend (outpaint to expand canvas).
If using Extend/outpainting, adjust border size, edge feathering, and synthesis strength to control how much new content is generated and how softly it blends with the original.
Confirm the recomposer’s output is connected to SaveImage. In SaveImage, set filename prefix, output folder, and format (e.g., PNG).
Click Queue Prompt to run. Review the output, then fine-tune aspect, mode, or feathering and re-run until you’re satisfied.
suggestedUseCases: Repurpose a square social post into vertical story and horizontal banner variants without redesigning.
Adapt print posters to web hero images while preserving key focal elements.
Create platform-optimized ad sets (1:1, 4:5, 16:9) from a single master graphic.
Generate clean video thumbnails by smart-cropping or extending backgrounds to avoid awkward letterboxing.
Localize or reformat UI mockups to different device aspect ratios while maintaining composition.

faqItems.question: Do I need a text prompt or extra models for outpainting?
faqItems.answer: No. This workflow uses the custom recomposer node (UUID 172f1008-9337-4d2f-9212-ee081cb4faf5) to handle cropping, fitting, and outpainting directly—no prompt required. Just load your image, choose the aspect and mode, and run.

faqItems.question: How can I avoid stretching or distorting logos and text?
faqItems.answer: Use Fit (letterbox) to preserve geometry or Extend (outpaint) to add surrounding context. Avoid Fill when critical text sits near edges; if you must fill, adjust the anchor/focus so important elements remain inside the safe area.

faqItems.question: I see seams or halos at the extended edges. How do I fix that?
faqItems.answer: Increase edge feathering, reduce the outpaint/border size, or try Fit instead of Extend for minimal synthesis. Running a smaller extend in multiple passes can also reduce artifacts.

faqItems.question: What resolution can I export?
faqItems.answer: Set your desired aspect and, if available, explicit width/height in the recomposer node. SaveImage will write exactly that resolution. For lossless results, export PNG; for lighter files, use JPG with appropriate quality.

4ab928487496.title: SYSTMS ACTION: QWEN IMAGE EDIT 2511
4ab928487496.description: Turn just about anything into a toy with the ACTION Qwen Image Edit 2511 LoRA! Simply upload an image and prompt it by writing "action the [subject]"!
4ab928487496.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Edit any photo into a toy-like version using Qwen Image Edit 2511, ACTION LoRA, and Qwen VL text encoder with instruction prompts.
4ab928487496.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow demonstrates instruction-based image editing with Qwen Image Edit 2511 and a targeted "ACTION" LoRA that turns subjects into toy-like versions. It loads the Qwen Image Edit 2511 diffusion model with UNETLoader and applies the ACTION LoRA via LoraLoaderModelOnly to bias the aesthetic toward playful, miniature, or collectible-toy looks. The QwenEditTextEncode_EditUtils node pairs a dedicated Qwen 2.5 VL text encoder with your input image and instruction (for example, "action the cat") to create edit-aware conditioning, while RandomNoise initializes the latent. SamplerCustomAdvanced runs the diffusion process using your chosen sampler from KSamplerSelect and the schedule from BasicScheduler, with CFGGuider controlling classifier-free guidance strength.

The input image is prepared for the model using ResizeImagesByLongerEdge and ImageCrop+ to standardize dimensions, with GetImageSize and PrimitiveInt passing size info to the sampler. After sampling, VAELoader and VAEDecode convert latents back to an RGB image, and SaveImage writes the result. Because this is an instruction-following edit model, you don’t need an init-latent path—your original photo is consumed by the Qwen encoder as a visual reference while the LoRA steers the result toward a consistent toy style. The included Note node documents the prompt pattern ("action the [subject]") so you can quickly produce consistent outputs.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. In UNETLoader, select the Qwen Image Edit 2511 model (qwen_image_edit_2511_fp8mixed.safetensors). In LoraLoaderModelOnly, choose the ACTION LoRA. In QwenEditTextEncode_EditUtils, point to the Qwen 2.5 VL text encoder.

Install the model files from the author’s links: place the diffusion model in ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models and the Qwen text encoder in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders. Load or confirm a compatible VAE in VAELoader.
Use LoadImage to import your photo. The ResizeImagesByLongerEdge and ImageCrop+ nodes will adapt it to a model-friendly size; you can adjust the long edge or crop settings to control framing.
In QwenEditTextEncode_EditUtils, write an instruction like: "action the dog" or "action the vintage camera". Keep it concise and literal; the LoRA is tuned to "action the [subject]" phrasing.

Set your sampling options: choose a sampler in KSamplerSelect (e.g., DPM++ or Euler), set steps (e.g., 20–30), and guidance in CFGGuider (start low-to-moderate, e.g., 3–6, to preserve identity). Fix a seed in RandomNoise for repeatable results.
Run the workflow. Inspect the output from SaveImage. If the toy style is too strong or too weak, adjust the LoRA strength in LoraLoaderModelOnly and guidance in CFGGuider, then re-run.
suggestedUseCases: Turn product shots into collectible toy mockups for playful campaign variations.
Create toy-style character portraits or avatars from selfies or studio photos.
Generate concept art for toy packaging or merchandising pitches.
Produce kid-friendly, miniature versions of everyday objects for educational visuals.
Make a series of consistent toy-themed social media posts from existing images.

faqItems.question: Which models do I need, and where do they go?
faqItems.answer: Download the Qwen Image Edit 2511 diffusion model (UNET) and the Qwen 2.5 VL text encoder from the links provided. Place the diffusion model in ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models and the text encoder in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders. Load a compatible VAE in VAELoader. The ACTION LoRA is loaded via LoraLoaderModelOnly.

faqItems.question: How do I control how "toy-like" the result is?
faqItems.answer: Increase or decrease the ACTION LoRA strength in LoraLoaderModelOnly and tune CFG in CFGGuider. Higher LoRA strength and higher CFG generally intensify the toy effect; lowering them preserves more of the original look. You can also adjust steps for detail (more) vs. speed (fewer).

faqItems.question: Do I need an init image strength or img2img denoise setting?
faqItems.answer: No. This workflow uses instruction-based editing: the input image and text instruction are encoded together by QwenEditTextEncode_EditUtils, and the diffusion starts from noise. Control intensity via LoRA strength, guidance (CFGGuider), sampler choice, and steps.

faqItems.question: What sampler and resolution should I use?
faqItems.answer: Start with a balanced sampler like DPM++ 2M Karras or Euler and 20–30 steps. The ResizeImagesByLongerEdge and ImageCrop+ nodes set a consistent canvas—use a size appropriate for your GPU. Higher resolutions need more VRAM and time; if you see OOM errors, lower the long edge size or steps.

4b042b6638a6.title: 2.3 Creator: Image Upscale & Analysis
4b042b6638a6.description: Learn how to upscale an image and auto-generate a prompt using Z Image Turbo.
4b042b6638a6.metaDescription: Upscale images and auto-generate detailed prompts using Z Image Turbo with ComfyUI's 2.3 Creator workflow.
4b042b6638a6.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow, titled '2.3 Creator: Image Upscale & Analysis,' is designed to enhance image resolution while simultaneously generating a detailed prompt from the image using the Z Image Turbo model. The workflow employs a combination of nodes, including LoadImage, SaveImage, and Florence2Run, to effectively upscale an image and analyze its content. The Florence2Run node uses the Florence-2 multimodal model to extract detailed information from the image, such as object attributes, spatial relationships, and scene context, which are then used to create a comprehensive prompt. This dual approach not only improves the visual quality of the image but also enriches the metadata associated with it, making it particularly useful for applications that require both high-quality visuals and detailed descriptive data.

The upscaling process is achieved through diffusion techniques that increase the image's resolution by adding denoised pixels, thereby preserving the original content and structure while enhancing clarity. The workflow uses a low denoise value in the Z Image Turbo model to ensure that the upscaled image retains its original details. This makes it an excellent tool for applications where image quality is paramount, such as digital art, photography, and media production. By combining image upscaling with automatic image analysis, this workflow offers a comprehensive solution for enhancing and understanding visual content.
howToUse: Load the workflow into ComfyUI by selecting '2.3 Creator: Image Upscale & Analysis' from the available templates.
Use the LoadImage node to import the image you wish to upscale and analyze.
Configure the Florence2Run node to enable detailed image analysis and prompt generation.
Adjust the Z Image Turbo settings, ensuring a low denoise value for optimal upscaling results.
Run the workflow to process the image, generating both an upscaled version and a detailed prompt.
Use the SaveImage node to export the enhanced image and review the generated prompt for further use.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing digital artwork for high-resolution displays.
Improving the quality of photographs for professional portfolios.
Generating detailed image descriptions for content management systems.
Creating high-quality visuals for marketing and advertising materials.
Analyzing images for research purposes, extracting detailed contextual information.

faqItems.question: What is the purpose of the Florence2Run node?
faqItems.answer: The Florence2Run node uses the Florence-2 multimodal model to analyze images and generate detailed prompts, capturing object attributes, spatial relationships, and scene context.

faqItems.question: How does the upscaling process work in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The upscaling process uses diffusion techniques with low denoise values in the Z Image Turbo model to increase image resolution while preserving original details.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow be used for any type of image?
faqItems.answer: Yes, this workflow is versatile and can be used to upscale and analyze a wide range of image types, including digital art, photographs, and more.

faqItems.question: What are the ideal settings for the Z Image Turbo model?
faqItems.answer: For best results, use a low denoise value between 0.2 and 0.35 to ensure the upscaled image retains its original details and clarity.

4b23697cd68c.title: SVD Text to Image to Video
4b23697cd68c.description: Generate videos by first creating images from text prompts.
4b23697cd68c.metaDescription: Transform text into dynamic videos with ComfyUI's SVD Text to Image to Video workflow. Perfect for creating engaging video content from simple prompts.
4b23697cd68c.extendedDescription:
The 'SVD Text to Image to Video' workflow in ComfyUI is designed to transform textual descriptions into dynamic video content. This process begins with generating images from text prompts using a combination of nodes like CLIPTextEncode, which encodes the text into a format that the image generation models can interpret. The workflow leverages powerful models such as SVD and Stability to ensure high-quality image outputs. Once the images are created, the workflow transitions into video generation using nodes like SVD_img2vid_Conditioning and VideoLinearCFGGuidance, which guide the transformation of static images into fluid video sequences. This workflow is particularly useful for creators looking to produce engaging video content from simple text inputs without needing extensive video editing skills.

Technically, the workflow is structured to maximize the quality and coherence of both images and videos. The KSampler node plays a crucial role in sampling latent spaces to produce varied and creative outputs, while the VAEDecode node decodes these latent representations into visible images. The CreateVideo node then compiles these images into a seamless video, which can be previewed and saved using PreviewImage and SaveVideo nodes, respectively. This approach is not only efficient but also allows for a high degree of customization and creativity, making it an invaluable tool for artists and marketers alike.
howToUse: Load the SVD Text to Image to Video workflow in ComfyUI.
Input your desired text prompt into the CLIPTextEncode node.
Run the workflow to generate images using the KSampler and VAEDecode nodes.
Use the SVD_img2vid_Conditioning and VideoLinearCFGGuidance nodes to convert images into a video sequence.
Preview the video using the PreviewImage node and save it with the SaveVideo node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating promotional videos from product descriptions.
Generating educational content by visualizing complex topics.
Producing artistic video interpretations of poetry or literature.
Developing social media content that combines text and visuals.
Experimenting with automated video creation for storytelling.

faqItems.question: What type of text prompts work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Descriptive prompts that include visual details like colors, objects, and settings tend to produce the best results.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the style of the generated video?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can tweak the parameters in the KSampler and VideoLinearCFGGuidance nodes to influence the style and dynamics of the video.

faqItems.question: How long does it take to generate a video?
faqItems.answer: The time varies based on the complexity of the prompt and the desired video length, but typically it takes a few minutes to process.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to use custom models with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can load custom models into the ImageOnlyCheckpointLoader and CheckpointLoaderSimple nodes for tailored results.

4b5d896ad23f.title: Green Screen: Bria
4b5d896ad23f.description: Upload a video to generate a green screen version with a transparent or solid background.
4b5d896ad23f.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow using BRIA to remove video backgrounds. Export transparent or green-screen videos with LoadVideo → BriaVideoGreenScreen → SaveVideo.
4b5d896ad23f.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns any uploaded video into a clean cutout with either a transparent background or a solid chroma color (green by default). It chains three nodes: LoadVideo reads and decodes your clip, BriaVideoGreenScreen calls the BRIA model to segment the subject and generate an alpha matte per frame, and SaveVideo assembles the processed frames back into a shareable video. The result is ready for compositing in your editor or for quick background swaps inside ComfyUI.

Technically, BriaVideoGreenScreen performs foreground segmentation via the BRIA API, producing an alpha channel or compositing the subject over a solid color. Because the processing is frame-by-frame, it preserves the source timing; resolution and frame rate typically follow the input unless you change encoding settings in SaveVideo. If your SaveVideo build supports codecs with alpha (e.g., WEBM with VP9+alpha), you can export true transparency; otherwise export a solid green background and pull a clean key later in your NLE or motion graphics tool.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the LoadVideo node. Select your source video file.
Open the BriaVideoGreenScreen node and enter your BRIA API credentials if required. Choose your background mode: Transparent (alpha) or Solid (e.g., green).
Optionally review any quality or smoothing options exposed by the node. If unsure, use the defaults for a first pass.

Configure the SaveVideo node: set an output path and choose a container/codec. If your setup supports alpha (e.g., WEBM with VP9+alpha), pick that for transparent output; otherwise plan to export a solid green background.
Click Queue/Execute. The workflow will decode the clip, process each frame through BRIA, and write the result via SaveVideo.
Import the result into your editor: composite transparent videos directly over any background, or apply a standard chroma key if you exported a solid green background.
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce product videos: remove cluttered studio floors and replace with branded or seasonal backdrops.
Talking-head and creator content: swap home-office backgrounds for clean studio looks without a physical green screen.
Marketing and social ads: produce quick cutouts for motion graphics overlays and dynamic layouts.
Training and explainers: place presenters over slides or app UIs for clearer, distraction-free visuals.

faqItems.question: Do I need a BRIA account or API key?
faqItems.answer: Yes. BriaVideoGreenScreen calls the BRIA background removal service. Provide your BRIA API key in the node (or in the integration’s settings if supported) before running the workflow.

faqItems.question: How do I export true transparency?
faqItems.answer: Choose Transparent in BriaVideoGreenScreen and use a video format that supports alpha in SaveVideo (commonly WEBM with VP9+alpha, if available in your build). MP4/H.264 does not support an alpha channel. If alpha export isn’t available, select a solid green background and key it in your editor.

faqItems.question: Will my audio be preserved?
faqItems.answer: Typically, SaveVideo in ComfyUI encodes the processed video stream only and does not copy audio. If you need audio, reattach the original track in your video editor after exporting the processed video.

faqItems.question: How can I get cleaner edges and better hair detail?
faqItems.answer: Use well-lit footage with clear subject–background separation and minimal motion blur or noise. Avoid clothing colors similar to your chosen solid background (if using green). For compositing, prefer the Transparent output to avoid green spill; if using green, fine-tune your chroma keyer’s edge and spill settings in post.

4b64f0419f57.title: Recraft v4: Text to Image
4b64f0419f57.description: Input a text prompt to generate a high-resolution image. Use the Recraft V4 model for enhanced realism, text accuracy, and detailed vector graphics. Output a 1024x1024 or 2048x2048 image based on your selected version.
4b64f0419f57.metaDescription: Generate high-resolution images from text prompts using Recraft v4 for enhanced realism and detail. Perfect for creative and professional projects.

This workflow leverages several nodes, including the RecraftV4TextToImageNode, which is the core component responsible for interpreting textual descriptions and generating corresponding visuals. The RecraftControls node provides users with the ability to fine-tune color settings, ensuring that the output aligns with specific aesthetic preferences. Additionally, the SaveImage node allows for easy storage of the generated images, making it convenient to manage and share results.

Technically, this workflow stands out due to its focus on realism and precision. The Recraft V4 model is renowned for its ability to produce images with high text accuracy and detailed vector graphics, making it particularly useful for applications that require intricate designs or clear textual elements. Users can choose between generating images at 1024x1024 or 2048x2048 resolutions, offering flexibility depending on the project requirements. This workflow is especially beneficial for creatives and professionals who need high-quality visuals quickly and efficiently.
howToUse: Load the 'Recraft v4: Text to Image' workflow in ComfyUI.
Enter your desired text prompt into the RecraftV4TextToImageNode.
Adjust color settings using the RecraftControls node if specific color precision is needed.
Select your preferred output resolution: 1024x1024 or 2048x2048.
Run the workflow to generate the image.

suggestedUseCases: Creating detailed illustrations for digital art projects.

Developing educational content with accurate visual representations.

faqItems.question: What makes the Recraft V4 model special?
faqItems.answer: The Recraft V4 model is known for its enhanced realism and ability to accurately render text and detailed vector graphics, making it ideal for high-quality image generation.

faqItems.question: Can I control the colors in the generated image?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can use the RecraftControls node to adjust color settings for more precise control over the image's appearance.

faqItems.question: What resolutions are available for the output images?

faqItems.question: How do I save the generated images?

4b9a8e7ef740.title: Layer Decomposition: Qwen-Image-Layered Control
4b9a8e7ef740.description: Describe the elements you want in the image and decompose it precisely from the image.
4b9a8e7ef740.metaDescription: Decompose images into editable layers in ComfyUI with Qwen-Image-Layered. Text-guided control, smart resizing, and clean exports for precise compositing.
4b9a8e7ef740.extendedDescription:
This tutorial workflow shows you how to break a single image into clean, editable layers using the Qwen-Image-Layered model inside ComfyUI. Starting with LoadImage, your input is resized via ImageScaleToMaxDimension (recommended 640 px for speed, 1024 px for higher fidelity) before being fed into the Qwen-Image-Layered node (custom node, ID f754a936-daaf-4b6e-9658-41fdc54d301d). The model can run with or without a prompt: leave it blank for automatic decomposition, or add a short prompt describing the main elements you want isolated (for example: "product on table, shadow, background"). The outputs are then written to disk via SaveImage as separate layer images, typically suitable for compositing workflows (e.g., PNGs with transparency).

Under the hood, the Qwen-Image-Layered node performs text-guided, iterative inference to separate the scene into distinct layers. It exposes diffusion-style controls internally—most notably Steps (default ~50) and CFG (~4.0)—which directly affect both quality and speed. Higher resolution and more steps improve separation and edge quality but increase runtime. The workflow also includes MarkdownNote instructions and is organized as a Subgraph so you can drop the entire layer-decomposition block into your own pipelines with minimal wiring.

Because the model is computationally intensive, expect longer runtimes at higher resolutions or with larger step counts. Start at 640 px with Steps ~50 and CFG ~4.0, then iterate. Use concise prompts to nudge which elements are split into their own layers, and export results with SaveImage for further editing in tools like Photoshop, After Effects, or any compositor.
howToUse: Update ComfyUI to the latest version and open the provided workflow. Ensure the Qwen-Image-Layered model required by the custom node is downloaded and placed where the node expects (see the node’s documentation).
Load your image using the LoadImage node. Set ImageScaleToMaxDimension to 640 for faster previews or 1024 for high-res outputs.

Open the Qwen-Image-Layered node (ID f754a936-daaf-4b6e-9658-41fdc54d301d). Optionally enter a brief prompt describing the elements you want separated (e.g., “person, sky, building”). Keep it concise and high-level.
Set initial sampler parameters inside the node: Steps ≈ 50 and CFG ≈ 4.0 (the defaults). These are slow but reliable starting points; reducing Steps speeds up tests.
Run the workflow. Inspect the outputs. Each decomposed layer will be routed to SaveImage so you can review the exported files (typically RGBA images).
Iterate: refine the prompt (fewer, clearer nouns), adjust Steps/CFG, or switch between 640 and 1024 max dimension to balance speed and quality. Re-run and export final layers.
suggestedUseCases: Product photography cleanup: isolate subject, shadow, and background for non-destructive retouching and background replacement.
Parallax and 2.5D animation: split an image into foreground, midground, and background layers for motion design.
App/UI mockups: separate interface elements and backgrounds from screenshots for quick redesigns and overlays.
Targeted color grading: isolate skies, people, or objects into separate layers for precise corrections without affecting the whole image.
VFX compositing: extract key objects or regions for replacement, relighting, or adding effects on individual layers.

faqItems.question: Do I need a prompt, or can it decompose automatically?
faqItems.answer: A prompt is optional. The model can attempt automatic decomposition, but a short prompt that names the key elements (e.g., “subject, shadow, background”) usually produces cleaner, more controlled layers.

faqItems.question: Why is inference slow, and how can I speed it up?
faqItems.answer: Runtime increases with image size and sampling parameters. To speed up: use a 640 px max dimension, lower Steps (e.g., 30–40 for previews), and keep CFG near 3.5–4.0. Increase Steps and/or resolution only for final passes.

faqItems.question: What formats do the layers export to?
faqItems.answer: SaveImage typically writes PNGs or JPGs, but PNG is recommended for layers due to transparency support. Connect each layer output from the Qwen-Image-Layered node to a SaveImage node to export them as separate files.

faqItems.question: Can I integrate this into my own graphs?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The layer decomposition is packaged as a Subgraph, so you can drop it into larger pipelines. Feed it an image (and optional prompt), then wire the outputs to your own compositing or editing branches.

4c3bfe1f75fb.title: Reve: Image Remix And Edit
4c3bfe1f75fb.description: Remix and edit images using Reve's advanced model. Combine multiple reference images into a single output
4c3bfe1f75fb.metaDescription: Remix and edit images effortlessly with Reve's advanced model, combining multiple references into one cohesive output.

The 'Reve: Image Remix And Edit' workflow is designed to empower users with the ability to creatively remix and edit images by leveraging the advanced capabilities of the Reve model. This workflow allows you to combine multiple reference images into a single cohesive output, making it an invaluable tool for artists and designers looking to experiment with visual styles and compositions. At the core of this workflow is the ReveImageRemixNode, which intelligently blends the visual elements of the input images, preserving key features while generating a harmonious final image. 

Technically, this workflow begins with the LoadImage node, which imports your chosen reference images into the system. These images are then processed by the ReveImageRemixNode, where the model's sophisticated algorithms analyze and merge the images based on their visual characteristics. Finally, the SaveImage node is used to output the remixed image, allowing you to save your creative work for further use or sharing. This workflow is particularly useful for those in creative industries, as it provides a seamless way to explore new visual ideas and edit images in a novel manner.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure all nodes are properly connected.
Use the LoadImage node to import your reference images into the system.
Configure the ReveImageRemixNode by selecting the appropriate parameters for image blending.
Run the workflow to process the images and generate a remixed output.
Use the SaveImage node to save your final image to your desired location.
Review and refine your output as needed, adjusting parameters for different results.
suggestedUseCases: Creating unique artwork by blending multiple styles from different reference images.
Developing new product designs by remixing existing images for inspiration.
Enhancing marketing materials with creative and visually appealing image edits.
Generating content for social media that stands out through innovative image combinations.
Exploring new visual concepts for digital art projects.

faqItems.question: Can I use more than two reference images in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can input multiple reference images using the LoadImage node, and the ReveImageRemixNode will blend them into a single output.

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported for input and output images?

faqItems.question: How can I adjust the blending intensity between images?

faqItems.question: Is it possible to preview the remixed image before saving?
