5652fbe7f479.title: Character + Clothing Virtual Try on Studio Photoshoot
5652fbe7f479.description: Upload an image of your character and a flat lay image of your clothing items. Generate 4 fashion editorial photographs of your character in the outfit. Select which image to upscale and add back details.
5652fbe7f479.metaDescription: Virtual try-on for characters: upload a character and flat-lay outfit, generate 4 styled poses, then upscale your favorite to 2048 with consistent details.
5652fbe7f479.extendedDescription:
This workflow builds a fast, reference-guided virtual try‑on pipeline for characters. You provide two images via LoadImage: a clear character image (face and body framing) and a flat‑lay of the clothing. A prompt entered with PrimitiveStringMultiline describes pose, studio lighting, background, and styling cues. OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 then generates a batch of four fashion‑editorial variations and arranges them into a 2×2 contact sheet for quick review. PreviewImage shows the grid, and ImageCompare can be used to examine differences side‑by‑side.

Under the hood, the same references (character and clothing) drive both the initial batch and the upscale path to preserve facial identity and outfit details. A utility node (663da6e9-8b62-4291-a9d6-e4b8fd672197) in this graph is wired to handle the 2×2 grid output and crop it back into four 1K (approx. 1024×1024) tiles. You select one tile with ImageFromBatch by setting batch_index (0–3, starting at top‑left) and feed it into the Upscale Selected Image group. The upscale pass uses OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 again at 2048×2048 while reusing your original references for consistency, then writes results with SaveImage. MarkdownNote and Note nodes in the canvas provide inline reminders and tips.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 is configured (API key/model as required in your setup).
Open the two LoadImage nodes and upload: (1) your character photo (neutral background recommended), and (2) a flat-lay image of the clothing with the garment fully visible.
Edit the PrimitiveStringMultiline prompt to describe pose, camera framing, studio lighting, background (e.g., seamless gray), and any styling notes you want reflected in the shots.

Run the 2x2 Grid Generation group. Inspect the 2×2 grid in PreviewImage and use ImageCompare if you want to A/B details. The tiles are indexed as: top-left = 0, top-right = 1, bottom-left = 2, bottom-right = 3.

In the Upscale Selected Image group, set the ImageFromBatch node’s batch_index to the tile you want to upscale. Run the upscale pass to generate a 2048×2048 refinement that reuses your character and outfit references.
Use SaveImage outputs from both groups to export the 1K tiles and the final 2K selection. If needed, adjust the prompt or references and rerun for new poses.
suggestedUseCases: Lookbook and catalog mockups for original characters or avatars wearing new outfits.
Previsualizing cosplay or wardrobe combinations before a photoshoot.
Social media content creation: quick editorial poses with consistent styling.
Character design iteration: testing silhouettes and fabrics across different studio setups.
Indie fashion previews: showcasing a garment on a consistent character model without a full shoot.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow keep the face and outfit consistent between the grid and the upscale?
faqItems.answer: Both stages use the same character and flat-lay clothing images as references in OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2. The upscale pass reuses those references, so identity and garment details are reinforced rather than regenerated from scratch.

faqItems.question: What input images work best for reliable try-on results?
faqItems.answer: For the character: a clear, well-lit image with the face unobstructed and minimal background clutter. For the garment: a flat-lay on a plain background with the full front of the item visible, not folded, and without heavy occlusions or busy patterns in the backdrop.

faqItems.question: How do I pick which of the four images to upscale?
faqItems.answer: Use the ImageFromBatch node and set batch_index to the tile you want (0=top-left, 1=top-right, 2=bottom-left, 3=bottom-right). The author note reminds that indexing starts at 0.

faqItems.question: Can I change pose, camera, or background without swapping images?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Edit the PrimitiveStringMultiline prompt to specify pose direction (e.g., three-quarter, walking stride), focal length or framing (full body, mid-shot), lighting (softbox, rim light), and background (seamless, colored paper). Re-run the 2×2 Grid Generation group to preview new variations.

566774e56057.title: Grok Imagine Video 1.5: Image to Video
566774e56057.description: Upload an image and optional text prompt to generate a video with native audio, realistic motion, and high-quality output up to 720p resolution.
566774e56057.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Turn a single image into a 720p video with optional prompt using Grok Imagine Video 1.5. Includes native audio when available.
566774e56057.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow turns a single still image into a short, realistic video using the Grok Imagine Video 1.5 model. It’s a simple three-node graph: LoadImage brings your source frame into the graph, GrokVideoNode sends that image (and an optional text prompt) to the Grok video generation API, and SaveVideo writes the returned clip to disk. The result is a 720p-ready video with plausible motion; when the API response includes audio, the workflow preserves that native audio in the saved file.

Under the hood, your image is used as visual conditioning for Grok’s video generator. If you add a prompt, it provides high-level guidance about motion, style, or scene dynamics (for example, “gentle camera push-in with drifting particles”). GrokVideoNode handles the API call and returns a ready-to-save video up to 720p, so you don’t have to manage frame assembly yourself. SaveVideo then persists the clip to your chosen output folder.

This workflow is ideal when you need quick, high-quality motion from a single frame—product hero shots, thumbnails that come to life, storyboards turned into moving beats, or social posts with motion and optional native audio—without deep node chains or manual post-processing.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the three nodes are present: LoadImage → GrokVideoNode → SaveVideo.
Open GrokVideoNode and configure your API credentials/endpoints if required by your setup. Leave defaults if already configured.
Select your source image in the LoadImage node. For best results, use a clean, high-resolution image that matches your target aspect ratio (16:9 for 1280×720).
Optionally add a short, clear text prompt in GrokVideoNode to steer motion or style (e.g., camera movement, atmosphere). If you leave it empty, the model will infer motion from the image.
In GrokVideoNode, set output resolution up to 720p as supported by the model. Then set your output filename/path in SaveVideo.
Queue and run the workflow. When it completes, find the rendered video from SaveVideo. If the Grok response includes audio, it will be preserved in the saved file.
suggestedUseCases: Animating product shots or hero images for social posts or storefronts.
Turning a character key art or portrait into a subtle cinematic intro.
Creating motion previews for storyboards and design stills.
Generating looping background shots or cinemagraph-style clips from photos.
Adding movement to static thumbnails for higher engagement.

faqItems.question: Do I need to write a text prompt, or will it work with just an image?
faqItems.answer: A prompt is optional. With image-only input, Grok will infer plausible motion. A short, specific prompt can better control camera moves, pacing, or mood.

faqItems.question: Can I control resolution and duration?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports up to 720p as exposed by GrokVideoNode. Duration and other generation limits depend on the Grok API. If duration settings are available in your GrokVideoNode, adjust them there; otherwise the clip length follows the model’s default.

faqItems.question: Will the output have audio?
faqItems.answer: If the Grok API returns a video with embedded audio, SaveVideo will preserve it. If the model returns a silent clip, this workflow won’t add audio. To customize sound, add audio in a video editor after export.

faqItems.question: How do I get the best visual quality?
faqItems.answer: Use a clean, high-quality source image that matches your target aspect ratio (16:9 for 720p). Keep the subject well-lit and centered, avoid heavy compression artifacts, and use a concise prompt to describe motion (e.g., “slow parallax push-in, soft depth haze”).

58a3f7167dba.title: Minimax H3 Video Restyling
58a3f7167dba.description: Using the open-weights version of Minimax H3, restyle a video's background and lighting using a guided key art image. You can also do a full character swap and voice/language replacement as well. A super powerful workflow for your VFX toolbox!
58a3f7167dba.metaDescription: Restyle video with MiniMax H3 using key art or character swap. Control lighting, palette, and identity; prompt via LLM; preserve or replace audio.
58a3f7167dba.extendedDescription:
This workflow restyles an existing video using the open-weights MiniMax H3 model, guided by a reference “key art” image or a character image. In key art mode, it transfers background, palette, and lighting while preserving the performance; in character swap mode, it targets the subject’s appearance for a full identity change. The core is the MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo node, driven by UNETLoader (MiniMax H3), CLIPLoader (text conditioning), RandomNoise, and a sampler chain built from KSamplerSelect, BasicScheduler, SamplerCustomAdvanced, and BasicGuider. VAELoader and VAEDecode convert generated latents back to frames, and ImageFromBatch lets you QC results mid-run.

ResolutionSelector and VHS_VideoInfo handle the practicalities—frame size, fps, and clip duration (the clip length parameter expects whole seconds). SetNode/GetNode are used as convenient toggles and parameter routers, including the mode switch between key art swap and character swap. LoadImage supplies your guiding key art or character reference, while OpenRouterLLMNode (in the GENERATE PROMPT group) can help draft a shot-specific prompt that CLIPLoader uses for text conditioning. A VOICE OPTIONS branch can keep your original audio or pass it to a voice-replacement path; VAEDecodeAudio decodes the final audio stream for muxing with the new visuals.

The result is a VFX-friendly process for look development and restyling: keep the motion and timing of your source while re-lighting the scene, shifting color mood, replacing backgrounds, or swapping a character—useful for previz, mood boards, and quick creative iterations.
howToUse: Load the workflow and open the SETUP groups. Point the source video input to your clip, then use VHS_VideoInfo to verify fps and duration. Set the clip length parameter in whole seconds and pick your output resolution with ResolutionSelector.

In MODELS, load the open-weights MiniMax H3 in UNETLoader, the matching text encoder in CLIPLoader, and the appropriate VAE in VAELoader. Confirm your sampler path: choose a method in KSamplerSelect, with BasicScheduler, SamplerCustomAdvanced, and BasicGuider connected to MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo.

Import your guide with LoadImage. Use the SetNode/GetNode toggle to choose between key art swap (scene/background + lighting restyle) and character swap (subject identity). Ensure the selected image is well-framed and high quality.

Write a concise shot-aware prompt (camera, lighting, environment, style cues) in the GENERATE PROMPT group. Optionally, use OpenRouterLLMNode to expand your brief into a detailed prompt, then feed it into CLIPLoader. Add a negative prompt if needed (e.g., artifacts to avoid).

Tune strength and consistency via the MODIFY group parameters (PrimitiveFloat and ComfyMathExpression feed key weights such as style/denoise strength, reference influence, and temporal coherence into MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo and the sampler). Lower strength preserves more of the original look; higher strength pushes the restyle further.

Run a short preview range first. Inspect frames with ImageFromBatch to confirm identity, lighting, and texture stability. When satisfied, render the full clip. In VOICE OPTIONS, choose to keep original audio or route to voice/language replacement (VAEDecodeAudio handles final audio decoding).
suggestedUseCases: Look development: quickly test different lighting palettes and art directions on existing footage using a single key art image.
Background and environment restyling for previz or social content while preserving the original performance and timing.
Character swap for concept tests and pitch frames without reshooting, using a clean character reference image.
Localized content: swap style and language/voice for regional variants while keeping the same edit.
Mood boards and dailies: generate consistent restyled passes to align teams on visual targets.

faqItems.question: What’s the difference between key art swap and character swap modes?
faqItems.answer: Key art swap emphasizes scene-level changes (background, lighting, color palette) using your key art as guidance while preserving the subject. Character swap targets the subject’s identity and attire to match a character reference. The mode toggle is handled via SetNode/GetNode, which routes the reference conditioning into MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo differently.

faqItems.question: How do I get stable results across frames?
faqItems.answer: Keep your source clip well-lit and steady, use a high-quality guide image, and tune the MODIFY parameters. Lowering denoise/style strength preserves more original structure; increasing temporal/consistency weights (fed by PrimitiveFloat/ComfyMathExpression into MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo and the sampler) reduces flicker. Preview a short segment and adjust before rendering the full clip.

faqItems.question: Which models do I need to load?
faqItems.answer: Load the open-weights MiniMax H3 in UNETLoader, a compatible text encoder in CLIPLoader, and a matching VAE in VAELoader. The sampler path uses KSamplerSelect, BasicScheduler, SamplerCustomAdvanced, and BasicGuider to drive diffusion steps for MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo.

faqItems.question: Do I have to replace the audio?
faqItems.answer: No. In VOICE OPTIONS you can keep the original audio or use the replacement path if configured. VAEDecodeAudio handles the final audio decoding. If you choose replacement, set the language/voice options provided in that group; otherwise, pass through the source audio.

59065edf5592.title: Hunyuan3D: Model Retopology and UV Unwrapping
59065edf5592.description: Input a dense mesh (from AI generation or photogrammetry scans) and create a lightweight model with good topology and unwrapped UV. Great for 3D game asset optimization.
59065edf5592.metaDescription: Optimize dense 3D meshes with Hunyuan3D: automatic retopology and UV unwrapping in ComfyUI, then export a clean, game‑ready GLB.
59065edf5592.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow converts a dense, messy mesh (from AI generation or photogrammetry) into a lightweight, game‑ready model with clean topology and an unwrapped UV set. It begins with Load3D to bring your source mesh into the graph, then uses TencentSmartTopologyNode inside the HUNYUAN 3D RETOPO group to perform automatic retopology via Tencent’s Hunyuan3D service. The result is a significantly reduced polygon count while preserving the model’s silhouette and major features—ideal for real‑time engines and mobile targets.

Next, the HUNYUAN 3D UV UNWRAP group runs TencentModelTo3DUVNode to generate a consistent UV layout. This step detects logical seams, flattens the surface, and packs islands so your asset is ready for texturing in tools like Substance 3D Painter. Finally, SaveGLB writes the optimized mesh and UVs to a GLB file. Under the hood, both Tencent* nodes call the Hunyuan3D API, so you get high‑quality, cloud‑powered retopology and UV unwrapping with minimal setup inside ComfyUI.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the Hunyuan3D nodes are installed. Configure your Tencent Hunyuan3D API credentials as required by TencentSmartTopologyNode and TencentModelTo3DUVNode.

Use the Load3D node to import your high‑poly source mesh (e.g., from AI generation or a scan). Verify the mesh is watertight where possible and free of extreme artifacts to improve retopology results.

In the HUNYUAN 3D RETOPO group, select your retopology settings (e.g., desired reduction/quality balance) and run TencentSmartTopologyNode. Inspect the output geometry to ensure the face count and edge flow meet your needs.

In the HUNYUAN 3D UV UNWRAP group, run TencentModelTo3DUVNode to generate a UV layout. If exposed, adjust unwrapping/packing quality to balance seam count and texel use, then validate the UVs in your DCC if needed.
Connect the retopologized, UV‑unwrapped mesh to SaveGLB and export. Choose a filename and location. The GLB will contain your optimized geometry and UVs.
Import the GLB into your DCC or game engine to confirm scale/orientation, shading, and UV integrity. Iterate retopo/UV settings if you need different poly density or seam placement.
suggestedUseCases: Game asset optimization: convert dense AI‑generated or scanned meshes into engine‑friendly models.
AR/VR and mobile: reduce polycount and create UVs for performance‑constrained platforms.
Texturing prep: quickly unwrap UVs before painting in Substance 3D Painter or similar tools.
Realtime product visualization: prepare clean, lightweight assets with reliable UVs for web viewers.
Marketplace asset cleanup: standardize topology and UVs across third‑party models.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes. TencentSmartTopologyNode and TencentModelTo3DUVNode call the Hunyuan3D cloud API. Provide valid credentials in the node settings or via your environment as documented by the node extension.

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported for input and output?
faqItems.answer: Load3D typically accepts common 3D mesh formats (varies by build/extension—check the node tooltip or docs). The workflow exports GLB via SaveGLB, which includes the optimized geometry and UVs.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow bake textures, normals, or AO?
faqItems.answer: No. It focuses on topology and UVs. Use your DCC or a separate baking pipeline to generate textures, normal maps, and AO after exporting the GLB.

faqItems.question: Will scale or orientation change during processing?
faqItems.answer: Geometry scale and orientation are generally preserved, but glTF/GLB conventions and unit settings can differ across tools. Always verify in your target DCC or engine and adjust if needed.

5a99bbb504dc.metaDescription: Outpaint images in ComfyUI with BriaExpandImage. Expand canvas by ratio or custom size, set placement, add optional prompts, and save clean, seamless composites.
5a99bbb504dc.extendedDescription:
This tutorial workflow shows how to outpaint (expand) any image cleanly using Bria’s Expand API from inside ComfyUI. The graph is simple and purposeful: LoadImage brings your source into the graph, BriaExpandImage sends it to the BRIA outpainting service with your chosen canvas and placement settings, and SaveImageAdvanced writes the finished composite to disk. The original pixels remain intact while the surrounding regions are synthesized to match the image’s lighting, perspective, and texture. You can steer the generation with a short prompt, or leave it blank to let the node auto-generate a description from the image.

Technically, BriaExpandImage constructs a larger target canvas (via preset aspect ratios or custom width/height) and positions the source within it (manual canvas placement or anchors). It then requests new pixels from Bria’s model to fill the added space, returning a composite where only the padded areas are generated. This is ideal for reframing without cropping: extend backgrounds for hero banners, add breathing room for layouts, or convert photos to new formats. MarkdownNote in the graph provides quick reminders, while SaveImageAdvanced offers control over filenames, format, and output folder for a repeatable production workflow.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then open the LoadImage node and select your source image (e.g., a product shot or artwork).
Open the BriaExpandImage node: add your Bria API key if required, choose a preset aspect ratio or enter custom width/height for the expanded canvas.
Set canvas placement: use anchors or manual offsets to decide which sides should grow (e.g., anchor left to expand to the right).
Optionally add a brief prompt to guide the new content (e.g., “wet city street at night, reflections”). Leave blank to auto-generate a prompt from the image.
Click Queue Prompt to run. If you hit an API or size error, reduce the target dimensions or try a smaller step-up.
Review the preview and output. Adjust aspect ratio, placement, or prompt for refinements, then let SaveImageAdvanced write the final image to your chosen folder.
suggestedUseCases: Adapting images to social media or ad formats (1:1, 4:5, 16:9, 9:16) without cropping key content.
Adding print bleed or extending backgrounds for magazine covers, posters, and brochures.
Creating hero banners by extending product shots or portraits with on-brand background space for text and UI.
Converting standard photos into panoramic or desktop wallpaper formats while preserving scene coherence.
Reframing illustrations or concept art to new aspect ratios for portfolio or marketplace listings.

faqItems.question: Do I need a Bria account or API key?
faqItems.answer: Yes. BriaExpandImage calls Bria’s outpainting API and typically requires an API key. Enter it in the node’s settings (or your environment) before running.

faqItems.question: Does this modify my original image content?
faqItems.answer: No. The original pixels are preserved. The node generates new content only in the added canvas area and composites it around your source.

faqItems.question: How do I control which side gets expanded?
faqItems.answer: Choose a target aspect ratio or custom dimensions, then set placement via anchors or manual offsets. For example, anchoring top expands down; anchoring left expands right.

faqItems.question: What settings yield the most natural results?
faqItems.answer: Start with modest expansions (about 10–40% larger than the original) and use a concise prompt that matches the scene. For large changes, expand in stages and iterate.

5ad29d3f3cae.title: MiniMax H3: Text to Image
5ad29d3f3cae.description: Generate a single still image from a text prompt with MiniMax H3, an omni-modal video model used here for its first-frame decode. No file inputs required: the graph samples an empty latent and decodes it through the H3 video VAE. Best suited to a single subject with a defined light source and a simple or blurred background.
5ad29d3f3cae.metaDescription: Text-to-image with MiniMax H3 in ComfyUI. Generate a single, detailed still from a prompt using first-frame decode. Best for simple scenes and clear lighting.
5ad29d3f3cae.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a plain text prompt into a single, high-quality still image using MiniMax H3, a video diffusion model repurposed here for first‑frame decoding. The graph samples an empty latent (no image inputs required), conditions it with your prompt inside the MiniMax H3 node (26ae0bb9-8bee-49c8-bca0-2897ee957e33), and decodes through H3’s video VAE to produce a coherent, photo‑like frame. It’s especially effective for a single subject with clear, directional lighting and a simple or softly blurred background.

Technically, ResolutionSelector sets the output size, the H3 node loads the minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors diffusion checkpoint and runs the denoising loop for a chosen number of steps, and SaveImage writes the final image to your ComfyUI output folder. The int8 pruned checkpoint helps keep VRAM use modest. Step count matters: H3 continues to refine texture and micro‑detail with more steps—30 is a fast, good‑quality default, while 50 yields noticeably finer detail at the cost of time. A MarkdownNote in the canvas provides links and author tips for quick reference.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the MarkdownNote shows the MiniMax H3 model link. If needed, download minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors from the linked repo and place it in your diffusion_models folder.

Open the MiniMax H3 node (26ae0bb9-8bee-49c8-bca0-2897ee957e33) and select the minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors checkpoint. Enter your text prompt describing a single subject, lighting direction, and a simple or blurred background.
Set the step count: use 30 for a quick, clean result; raise to 50 for maximum texture and skin/detail fidelity. Expect longer render times at higher steps.
Use the ResolutionSelector to pick an aspect ratio and size appropriate for your subject. Start with a moderate resolution; increase only if your GPU has headroom.
Optionally, set a fixed seed (if exposed on the H3 node) for repeatable results. Keep batch size at 1 for stability unless you know your VRAM limits.
Click Queue Prompt. When the preview looks good, let SaveImage write the output to the default ComfyUI output directory. Iterate on prompt wording, steps, and resolution to refine the look.
suggestedUseCases: Product hero shots with a single item under defined lighting and a soft studio backdrop.
Portrait-style renders emphasizing skin, fabric, or hair detail against a simple background.
Concept thumbnails exploring lighting direction and mood on a central subject.
Social or blog visuals where a clean subject stands out from a subtly blurred environment.

faqItems.question: Why use a video model (MiniMax H3) for still images?
faqItems.answer: This workflow uses H3’s first-frame decode via its video VAE. The model’s temporal priors tend to produce coherent lighting and subject structure in a single frame, making it strong for one-subject scenes.

faqItems.question: How many diffusion steps should I use?
faqItems.answer: 30 steps is the default and balances speed with quality. Increasing to 50 adds noticeable fine texture and skin/detail fidelity. Very low step counts will lose micro‑detail first.

faqItems.question: What resolutions and aspect ratios work best?
faqItems.answer: Start with moderate presets from ResolutionSelector (standard 1:1, 3:4/4:3, or 16:9). Extremely large or unusual aspect ratios can introduce artifacts or out‑of‑memory errors. Scale up only if your GPU allows.

faqItems.question: Do I need image inputs or negative prompts?
faqItems.answer: No image inputs are required—the graph samples an empty latent. If the H3 node exposes a negative prompt field, you can use it to steer away from unwanted elements, but it’s optional for this workflow.

5ad4348c8417.title: Magnific: Creative Image Upscale
5ad4348c8417.description: Upload an image and set the magnification level. Generate an upscaled version of your image with support for up to 16x enlargement.
5ad4348c8417.metaDescription: Enhance image resolution up to 16x with the Magnific Creative Image Upscale workflow. Perfect for high-quality enlargements.
5ad4348c8417.extendedDescription: The 'Magnific: Creative Image Upscale' workflow is designed to enhance the resolution of images while preserving their quality and details. This workflow leverages the Magnific model, known for its ability to upscale images up to 16 times their original size. It is particularly useful for applications where high-resolution images are crucial, such as printing, digital art, and detailed visual presentations. The workflow begins with the LoadImage node, which allows users to upload their desired image. The core of the process is the MagnificImageUpscalerCreativeNode, which applies sophisticated algorithms to upscale the image creatively. This node is configured to maintain the artistic integrity of the image while enhancing its resolution. Finally, the SaveImage node allows users to save the upscaled image, and the ImageCompare node provides a side-by-side comparison of the original and upscaled images, ensuring users can evaluate the improvements made.
howToUse: Load the ComfyUI interface and select the 'Magnific: Creative Image Upscale' workflow.
Use the LoadImage node to upload the image you wish to upscale.
Configure the MagnificImageUpscalerCreativeNode by setting the desired magnification level (up to 16x).
Run the workflow to process the image using the Magnific model.
Use the ImageCompare node to view the original and upscaled images side-by-side.
Save the enhanced image using the SaveImage node to your desired location.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing digital artwork for large-scale prints.
Improving the quality of low-resolution images for professional presentations.
Upscaling photos for high-resolution displays or detailed analysis.
Preparing images for publication in high-quality print media.
Restoring and enlarging old photographs for archival purposes.

faqItems.question: What is the maximum magnification level supported by this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports up to 16x magnification, allowing for significant enlargement of images while maintaining quality.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow be used for any type of image?
faqItems.answer: Yes, it can be used for various types of images, but results may vary depending on the original image quality and content.

faqItems.question: How does the ImageCompare node help in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The ImageCompare node provides a side-by-side comparison of the original and upscaled images, helping users assess the quality improvements.

faqItems.question: Is there a way to adjust the artistic style during upscaling?
faqItems.answer: While the MagnificImageUpscalerCreativeNode focuses on maintaining artistic integrity, specific style adjustments are not a feature of this workflow.

5ae006b13a36.title: Ideogram v4: Text to Image (API)
5ae006b13a36.description: Input a text prompt in structured JSON format. Generate a high-quality image with precise layout control, text rendering, and color palette support.
5ae006b13a36.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Use Ideogram v4 with a structured JSON prompt for precise layout, crisp in-image text, and brand-safe color palettes. Save high-quality results.
5ae006b13a36.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow demonstrates how to drive Ideogram v4 via a structured JSON prompt to get clean text rendering, consistent brand colors, and reliable layout control. Instead of a single free-form sentence, you build a compact JSON object that describes the scene, in-image text, a color palette, and per-object bounding boxes. That JSON is fed into the IdeogramV4 partner API node, which returns a high-quality image that adheres to your specified layout as closely as the model allows. The output flows directly to SaveImage.

To make authoring easier, the JSON Prompt Builder group (enable it by selecting the group and pressing Ctrl+B) includes a MarkdownNote with a schema/template and an optional GeminiNode that can transform a plain brief into a well-formed JSON prompt. You can preview the structured prompt with PreviewAny before sending it to IdeogramV4, iterate on bounding boxes or palette values, and then render the final image. This approach is ideal when you need reliable in-image text, brand-safe palettes, and object placement that a natural-language prompt alone struggles to achieve.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the IdeogramV4 node is configured (API access, model selection, and any required credentials per your setup).
Enable the JSON Prompt Builder group (select it and press Ctrl+B). Open the MarkdownNote to copy the provided JSON template and schema tips.
Author your structured JSON: define the scene prompt, optional palette (hex colors), and layout items (e.g., text or objects) with bounding boxes. Use PreviewAny to quickly inspect the JSON.
Optional: Use the GeminiNode to draft or refine the JSON from a plain-language brief, then review and edit the output to match the template in the MarkdownNote.
Paste the final JSON into the IdeogramV4 node’s prompt field and execute the node (or the whole graph). Watch the image preview in ComfyUI; adjust your JSON and re-run as needed.
When satisfied, SaveImage will write the rendered result to disk. Iterate on bounding boxes, text content, and palette to tighten alignment and style.
suggestedUseCases: Poster and flyer concepts with headline/subhead text locked into specific regions.
Product mockups that combine brand-safe colors, hero imagery, and on-image copy.
Social graphics or ads where logo, CTA, and legal text must appear in fixed boxes.
Infographics or UI-themed visuals that benefit from structured regions and labels.
Storyboards or pitch frames with consistent layout and readable in-frame captions.

faqItems.question: Do I have to use structured JSON, or can I just type a normal prompt?
faqItems.answer: You can enter plain natural language directly into the IdeogramV4 node. However, this workflow is optimized for a structured JSON prompt, which gives much stronger control over in-image text, color palette, and object placement via bounding boxes.

faqItems.question: What does the JSON look like?
faqItems.answer: Use the template in the MarkdownNote as your source of truth. A minimal example might include: prompt (overall description), palette (array of hex colors), and layout items with type, text/subject, and a bbox [x, y, w, h] in normalized 0–1 coordinates. Example (keys may vary by template): { "prompt": "retro poster of a mountain sunrise", "palette": ["#0F0F0F", "#FF6A00", "#FFD54D"], "layout": { "items": [ {"type": "text", "text": "SUMMER FEST", "bbox": [0.1, 0.05, 0.8, 0.2]}, {"type": "image", "subject": "mountain sunrise", "bbox": [0.1, 0.28, 0.8, 0.55]} ] } }

faqItems.question: My text is cropped or misaligned. How can I fix it?
faqItems.answer: Increase padding in the text item’s bounding box, reduce the text length, and avoid overlapping boxes. Keep bbox values within 0–1, ensure items don’t collide, and iterate—small bbox adjustments often resolve clipping and alignment issues.

faqItems.question: How do I keep brand colors consistent?
faqItems.answer: Define a concise palette array of your brand hex colors in the JSON. Limit it to a few key colors to nudge the model strongly. If results drift, simplify the palette, reduce conflicting style cues, and re-run. The model aims to respect your palette while balancing overall image quality.

5b8156052b93.title: Recraft: Style Control Image Generation
5b8156052b93.description: Control style with visual examples, align positioning, and fine-tune objects. Store and share styles for perfect brand consistency.
5b8156052b93.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate on-brand images with Recraft styles, color control, and optional SVG export using RecraftTextToImage and vectorization nodes.
5b8156052b93.extendedDescription:
This workflow demonstrates style-controlled image generation with Recraft inside ComfyUI. It centers on RecraftTextToImageNode for raster image synthesis and uses dedicated style selector nodes—RecraftStyleV3LogoRaster, RecraftStyleV3DigitalIllustration, and RecraftStyleV3RealisticImage—to quickly switch aesthetics without rewriting prompts. RecraftColorRGB lets you lock brand hues, while RecraftControls aggregates global parameters that the generator uses to keep outputs consistent. Results are saved via SaveImage, and MarkdownNote provides in-graph guidance.

For brand-ready deliverables, the optional Convert into SVG (need credits) group routes raster outputs through RecraftVectorizeImageNode and exports clean vectors using SaveSVGNode. This is especially useful for logos and flat graphics that need to scale. Note: in these Recraft nodes, the seed value only determines whether the node should re-run; it does not make results deterministic. To explore new variations, change the seed to trigger a fresh run or refine the style and color inputs.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm Recraft API access per the Author Notes (local/https context and connectivity). If the partner nodes show connection errors, resolve those before proceeding.
Choose a style: connect exactly one of RecraftStyleV3LogoRaster, RecraftStyleV3DigitalIllustration, or RecraftStyleV3RealisticImage to the style input used by RecraftTextToImageNode.
Set color constraints: edit RecraftColorRGB to your brand color (hex/RGB) and ensure it is wired into the controls path (via RecraftControls) that feeds RecraftTextToImageNode.

Enter your prompt in RecraftTextToImageNode. Run the graph to generate the first result. To request a new variation without changing your setup, change the seed value to force the node to re-run (seed does not control the visual result).

Save your raster output with SaveImage. For vectors, enable the Convert into SVG group: route the generated image into RecraftVectorizeImageNode and then into SaveSVGNode to export an .svg (this may require credits as noted).
Iterate for consistency: switch between style nodes for different looks, fine-tune RecraftControls to adjust behavior, and keep RecraftColorRGB fixed to enforce brand colors across a batch.
suggestedUseCases: Logo and icon exploration with quick style switching and optional SVG export for scalable assets.
Brand illustration systems: maintain consistent hues and aesthetics across multiple scenes.
Social and ad creatives where color and style consistency matter across formats.
Product or feature mockups rendered in a realistic style for presentations and landing pages.
Internal concept boards: rapidly compare LogoRaster vs. DigitalIllustration vs. RealisticImage looks from the same prompt.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between the Recraft style nodes?
faqItems.answer: Each style node configures the generator for a distinct aesthetic. RecraftStyleV3LogoRaster suits flat, logo-like marks; RecraftStyleV3DigitalIllustration targets stylized drawings and clean illustrations; RecraftStyleV3RealisticImage aims for photographic realism. Swap the node to change the overall look without rewriting your prompt.

faqItems.question: How do I enforce brand colors?
faqItems.answer: Use RecraftColorRGB to set your desired color and keep it connected in the controls path (via RecraftControls) that feeds RecraftTextToImageNode. This constrains the palette around your specified hue for better brand consistency. For multi-color palettes, iterate with different RecraftColorRGB settings or vectorize and adjust colors downstream.

faqItems.question: Why doesn’t the same seed reproduce the same image?
faqItems.answer: In this workflow the seed is only used to determine whether a node should re-run; it does not make the result deterministic. To explore new variations, change the seed to force a fresh run, or adjust your prompt, style node, and color settings to guide the output.

faqItems.question: How do I get vector (SVG) output and when do I need credits?
faqItems.answer: Enable the Convert into SVG group: send your raster result into RecraftVectorizeImageNode and then into SaveSVGNode to write an .svg file. Vectorization quality is best on simple, high-contrast graphics (e.g., logos). As noted in the workflow group, this step may require Recraft credits. For API details, see the partner-node docs: https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/partner-nodes/overview and the Recraft tutorial: https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/partner-nodes/recraft/recraft-text-to-image.

5b94a8f404fa.title: Seamless Video Transitions - LTX 2.3 FLW LoRA
5b94a8f404fa.description: Upload two input videos and generate a seamless transition between the two shots.
5b94a8f404fa.metaDescription: Create seamless transitions between two videos in ComfyUI using LTX 2.3 FLW LoRA. Load videos, set the transition window, and export a smooth merged clip.
5b94a8f404fa.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow creates a seamless, learned transition between two input clips using an LTX 2.3 FLW LoRA. You feed one video into each LoadVideo node, and a dedicated transition node (UUID: 63482e7d-23c9-4396-a7a2-cd4ca2316eac) synthesizes a smooth handoff from the end of the first shot to the start of the second. The SaveVideo node then assembles the processed frames into a single output clip. A built-in MarkdownNote provides an at-a-glance guide to recommended settings and practical tips.

Technically, the workflow performs diffusion-based video-to-video generation guided by the LTX 2.3 FLW LoRA to harmonize color, texture, and motion across the cut. For temporal consistency, inference runs over the full frame range (not just the transition window). That design keeps the look stable across the entire sequence but also means longer clips and higher resolutions will increase runtime and VRAM use. You’ll typically set the in/out ranges for each source clip, define a transition length, and adjust the LoRA influence/strength and seed in the transition node. SaveVideo controls the output frame rate and file name for export.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the LTX 2.3 FLW LoRA transition node (UUID: 63482e7d-23c9-4396-a7a2-cd4ca2316eac) loads without errors. Review the embedded MarkdownNote for quick tips.

Use the two LoadVideo nodes to import your source clips (A and B). If possible, match resolution and FPS between the clips, and trim or set frame ranges so the key visual moments you want to bridge are near the cut.

In the transition node, set the start/end frames for the handoff, choose a transition duration (in frames), and adjust the LoRA influence/strength and seed. Start with a moderate strength and a longer transition window if your shots differ a lot.
Configure the SaveVideo node (e.g., output filename and FPS). Keep resolution and FPS consistent with your inputs to minimize artifacts and speed up generation.
Run the workflow. Review the output for flicker or warping at the handoff; if needed, tweak transition length and LoRA strength, or move the cut to frames with more shared structure, then re-run.
suggestedUseCases: Softening hard cuts in edits to create fluid, stylized transitions between contrasting scenes.
Bridging shots with different lighting or framing by harmonizing color and texture across the handoff.
Smoothing jump cuts in talking-head or product footage by inserting a learned transition segment.
Creating dynamic, eye-catching scene changes for reels, shorts, and social content.
Linking still or minimally moving shots with a subtle morph-like motion for montage sequences.

faqItems.question: Why does the workflow process every frame if I only need the transition?
faqItems.answer: To maintain temporal consistency. Running inference across the full frame range helps keep the look stable and reduces popping before and after the handoff. If you need faster runs, trim your inputs to just the necessary ranges, reduce resolution/FPS, or shorten the clips.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce artifacts like flicker or warping at the transition?
faqItems.answer: Try increasing the transition duration, lowering the LoRA influence/strength, and locking the seed for repeatable results. Place the cut around frames with similar composition (camera angle, subject size), and ensure both inputs share the same resolution and FPS.

faqItems.question: What GPU/VRAM do I need?
faqItems.answer: Requirements scale with resolution, clip length, and transition duration. Start with short clips at a modest resolution to gauge performance. Longer sequences or HD+ resolutions benefit from GPUs with more VRAM; if you hit limits, downscale or shorten the frame ranges.

faqItems.question: Does the output include audio?
faqItems.answer: The SaveVideo node outputs a silent video. If you need audio, export the video and reattach audio from one of the source clips (or a music track) in your video editor.

5c7bc03c018f.title: Z-Image-Turbo Int8: Text to Image
5c7bc03c018f.description: Generate photorealistic images using the Z-Image-Turbo int8 model, a distilled 6B-parameter variant optimized for sub-second inference through efficient 8-step sampling. The workflow takes a text prompt as input and outputs a single high-quality image. Ideal for rapid creative iteration, realistic concept art, and production-ready visual prototyping.
5c7bc03c018f.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate fast, photorealistic images from text with Z-Image-Turbo int8 using an 8-step sampler. Simple Subgraph, quick setup, and SaveImage output.
5c7bc03c018f.extendedDescription:
This tutorial workflow wraps the Z-Image-Turbo int8 text-to-image pipeline into a clean, single-click Subgraph so you can go from prompt to photorealistic image in seconds. At its core is the Z-Image-Turbo distilled 6B-parameter model quantized to int8 for low VRAM use and fast turnaround. The Subgraph (node id f2fdebf6-dfaf-43b6-9eb2-7f70613cfdc1) exposes just the essentials—prompt, resolution, steps, and seed—while the SaveImage node writes the result to your output folder. A MarkdownNote in the canvas provides at-a-glance setup tips.

Technically, the Subgraph handles text encoding, denoising, and decoding internally so you don’t have to wire individual components. Z-Image-Turbo is optimized for efficient 8-step sampling, enabling rapid iteration on capable GPUs. The model package includes text encoders (e.g., a Qwen-based encoder listed under text_encoders/qwen_3_4...) to translate your prompt into conditioning for the denoiser. This minimal surface area makes the workflow ideal for both newcomers and power users who want speed without sacrificing realistic detail. You can open the Subgraph to inspect or extend the internals any time.
howToUse: Load the workflow: Drag and drop the Z-Image-Turbo Int8 JSON into the ComfyUI canvas (or use Load > Load Workflow).

Install the model: Use the provided Hugging Face or ModelScope links to download the Z-Image-Turbo assets. Follow any placement notes in the workflow’s MarkdownNote, then Refresh Models or restart ComfyUI. If you see a missing model message, open the Subgraph and point its model inputs to your local files.
Enter your prompt: Open the Subgraph (f2fdebf6-dfaf-43b6-9eb2-7f70613cfdc1), paste a clear, specific text prompt, and set the seed if you want repeatable results.

Adjust quality-speed tradeoffs: Keep steps at the default 8 for best speed; you can try modest increases (e.g., 10–12) if exposed for finer details. Choose a resolution that fits your VRAM (start with a moderate size before going larger).
Run the workflow: Click Queue Prompt. The Subgraph handles text encoding and denoising; the SaveImage node will write the final image to your ComfyUI/output directory.
Iterate: Refine your prompt (lighting, camera terms, materials) and seed to explore variations quickly. Compare results and settle on the best image.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept art and moodboards for previsualization.
Product mockups and material studies with photoreal lighting.
Pitch decks and storyboards where fast, consistent output matters.
Thumbnail and hero image ideation for web or social.
A/B testing of prompts to lock in art direction quickly.

faqItems.question: What hardware do I need for Z-Image-Turbo int8?
faqItems.answer: A modern NVIDIA GPU is recommended for best performance. The int8 quantization lowers VRAM requirements and improves speed compared to higher-precision variants. While CPU inference may work, it will be significantly slower. Actual latency depends on your GPU, resolution, and step count.

faqItems.question: Why 8 steps, and can I change it?
faqItems.answer: The model is tuned for efficient 8-step sampling to balance speed and fidelity. If the Subgraph exposes a steps input, you can try 10–12 for slightly more detail at the cost of speed. Going much higher often yields diminishing returns with this model.

faqItems.question: I get a missing model or path error. How do I fix it?
faqItems.answer: Download the model files from the linked Hugging Face or ModelScope repo. Then open the Subgraph and point any model loader inputs to your local files. Use ComfyUI’s Refresh Models or restart after placing files. The MarkdownNote in the workflow also includes quick setup pointers.

faqItems.question: How can I improve photorealism without slowing things down too much?
faqItems.answer: Use concise, specific prompts (camera type, focal length, lighting, material terms), keep steps near 8–12, and start at a moderate resolution that fits your VRAM. Lock a seed for consistency when iterating small prompt tweaks. Increase resolution only after you’re happy with composition and style.

5cd417e793b8.title: LTX 2.3 Audio-Reactive LoRA
5cd417e793b8.description: Create audio-reactive videos with LTX 2.3 and the Audio-Reactive LoRA.
5cd417e793b8.metaDescription: Turn a single image into an audio‑reactive video with LTX 2.3 and an Audio‑Reactive LoRA. Load image + audio, auto‑prompt with Gemini, preview, and export.
5cd417e793b8.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single still image into an audio‑reactive video using the LTX‑Video 2.3 model enhanced with the Audio‑Reactive LoRA. You provide one image via LoadImage and an audio track via LoadAudio; a GeminiNode in the Create Audio‑Reactive LoRA Prompt group helps craft a clean, descriptive text prompt from your idea (and optionally your image context). That prompt, together with the image and audio, flows into the LTX 2.3 video generator node (dacae91a-7342-43be-a654-227b303c33bc), where the Audio‑Reactive LoRA modulates motion and visual rhythm in response to the soundtrack. You can preview output with PreviewAny and export the final result with SaveVideo.

Technically, the workflow applies the Audio‑Reactive LoRA from https://huggingface.co/100percentrobot/LTX-2.3-Audio-Reactive-LORA at inference time on top of LTX 2.3. The LoRA strength parameter controls how strongly the audio‑driven behavior influences the video: use 1.0–2.0 overall, with 1.4+ for more pronounced reactivity. This design is practical for fast, beat‑aware animations of posters, album art, and social posts: you focus on a concise prompt and good source media, while the LTX node handles frame synthesis and timing, and SaveVideo writes a ready‑to‑share clip.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and expand the groups: Load Image, Load Audio, Create Audio‑Reactive LoRA Prompt, and LTX 2.3 Audio‑Reactive LoRA.
In Load Image, select a single, high‑quality PNG/JPG. Choose an aspect ratio that matches your target output to avoid cropping.
In Load Audio, load your soundtrack (e.g., WAV/MP3). If the track is long, plan a segment length that fits your desired video duration.

In Create Audio‑Reactive LoRA Prompt, enter a brief style/subject description in the GeminiNode to auto‑generate a clean prompt. If you prefer, bypass Gemini and feed a manual text prompt directly into the LTX 2.3 node’s prompt input.

In the LTX 2.3 Audio‑Reactive LoRA group, set the LoRA strength between 1.0 and 2.0 (start at 1.4 for stronger effects). Optionally set seed, duration/frame count, and any resolution/FPS fields to suit your output and audio length.
Queue/Run the workflow. Use PreviewAny to check motion and timing, then render the full sequence and save the final clip with SaveVideo.
suggestedUseCases: Music‑driven cover art or poster animations for social posts and reels
Album or single teasers that pulse and morph with the beat
Animated title cards for YouTube, Twitch, or podcast intros
Looping VJ backdrops that respond to ambient tracks
Motion‑enhanced slides for event screens or installations

faqItems.question: What LoRA strength should I use?
faqItems.answer: Use 1.0–2.0 overall. Start at 1.4 for a stronger, more noticeable audio‑reactive effect and lower it if the motion feels too intense or stylization overrides the source image.

faqItems.question: Do I need the GeminiNode to write prompts?
faqItems.answer: No. The GeminiNode helps auto‑format prompts, but you can disable/bypass it and connect a manual text prompt directly to the LTX 2.3 node’s prompt input if you prefer full control.

faqItems.question: How precise is the audio sync?
faqItems.answer: The Audio‑Reactive LoRA drives motion based on the audio’s energy/rhythm. It produces convincing beat‑aware visuals, but it’s not frame‑accurate editing. For tight cuts, adjust your audio segment and video duration/frame count and fine‑tune LoRA strength.

faqItems.question: Which formats are supported?
faqItems.answer: LoadImage typically accepts PNG/JPG and LoadAudio commonly supports WAV/MP3. SaveVideo outputs a standard video file (commonly MP4). If a format fails, convert your media to these common types.

5ce89ce6ed7c.title: MOSS Image - Color-Depth-Control LoRA
5ce89ce6ed7c.description: Control adapter trained by darask0 for MOSS Image.
5ce89ce6ed7c.metaDescription: Guide MOSS Image with a Color-Depth Control LoRA by darask0. Preserve structure via depth maps and control color for consistent, depth-aware image variations.
5ce89ce6ed7c.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates how to guide MOSS Image generation with a Color-Depth Control LoRA trained by darask0. It lets you steer structure with a depth map while preserving or modulating color from a reference image, making it easy to create style variations that keep geometry intact. At its core, LoadImage brings in your RGB reference and (optionally) a precomputed depth map, while PreviewImage and ImageCompare help you iterate quickly and check differences across runs. SaveImageAdvanced handles clean, configurable exports.

The heavy lifting happens in two custom MOSS Image nodes (IDs: 3d58c0bd-7a87-40a7-bdb5-a209a27f10d7 and 882218ff-0ea7-4047-9b12-b79cdc4e9faa). Together, they wrap the MOSS Image base model and apply the Color-Depth Control LoRA at inference, injecting depth-aware conditioning so the output adheres to your scene layout and perspective. By pairing color information from the source image with structural cues from the depth map, the workflow produces edits and variations that maintain shape, scale, and composition—ideal for product shots, architecture, and concept iterations where consistency matters.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and verify the nodes are connected: LoadImage inputs, the two custom MOSS Image nodes (IDs 3d58c0bd-7a87-40a7-bdb5-a209a27f10d7 and 882218ff-0ea7-4047-9b12-b79cdc4e9faa), PreviewImage, ImageCompare, and SaveImageAdvanced.

In the LoadImage node(s), add your reference RGB image and (recommended) a matching-resolution grayscale depth map. If you don’t have a depth map, generate one first with a depth-preprocessor node (e.g., MiDaS/Depth Anything) or an external tool, then reload it here.

Open the custom MOSS nodes and select the required assets: the MOSS Image base model and the Color-Depth Control LoRA trained by darask0. Make sure ComfyUI can find these files in your models directories, then apply/refresh so the nodes pick them up.

Adjust key parameters exposed by the custom nodes: set image resolution, choose or fix a seed for repeatability, and tune the control/adapter strength so depth strongly anchors structure while color either matches or gently diverges from the reference (start mid-range, then refine).

Queue the workflow. Use PreviewImage to inspect results after each run and ImageCompare to evaluate variations side-by-side (e.g., different adapter strengths or seeds). Iterate until you reach the desired balance of structural fidelity and color styling.
Export final images with SaveImageAdvanced. Use its filename patterning and metadata options to keep track of settings (e.g., seed, strength), which helps reproduce or batch-refine results later.
suggestedUseCases: Product imagery updates: keep proportions and camera geometry via depth while exploring new surface colors and materials.
Architectural and interior concepting: preserve layout and perspective with depth guidance while testing palettes and lighting moods.
Illustration restyling: maintain character/scene structure from depth maps while shifting color schemes or textures.
Previs and blocking: start from a depth pass to lock composition, then iterate color/look quickly for client reviews.

faqItems.question: Do I need a depth map, or can I run color-only?
faqItems.answer: The workflow is designed to leverage a depth map for structural guidance, which is strongly recommended for best results. If you don’t have one, generate it first with a depth-preprocessor node (e.g., MiDaS/Depth Anything) or an external tool, then load it alongside your color image.

faqItems.question: Which models are required and where do I put them?
faqItems.answer: You’ll need the MOSS Image base model and the Color-Depth Control LoRA trained by darask0. Place them in your ComfyUI model directories where your installation expects checkpoints/LoRAs, then select them inside the custom MOSS nodes (IDs 3d58c0bd-7a87-40a7-bdb5-a209a27f10d7 and 882218ff-0ea7-4047-9b12-b79cdc4e9faa). Reload models if they don’t appear.

faqItems.question: My output looks misaligned or distorted. How can I fix it?
faqItems.answer: Ensure the RGB image and depth map share the same resolution and alignment. Use standard grayscale depth maps (near=brighter, far=darker) and avoid extreme upscaling. If you still see artifacts, lower the adapter/control strength, reduce output resolution, and keep a fixed seed while you iterate.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow be used for pure text-to-image?
faqItems.answer: This workflow focuses on image-guided control (color+depth). For pure text-to-image with MOSS, use a text-to-image workflow built for that purpose. You can still combine prompts with this pipeline if the custom node exposes text inputs, but depth guidance remains the main driver.

5d1279276e1c.title: MiniMax H3 Max: FLF2V
5d1279276e1c.description: Generate polished, prompt-faithful videos faster than real time with MiniMax H3 Max, a post-trained model tuned for stronger prompt adherence and vivid cinematic aesthetics. This workflow supports text-to-video, image-to-video animation, and directed first-to-last-frame transitions, delivering clean compositions and cohesive lighting directly from the model. Ideal for rapid concept exploration, cinematic motion graphics, and high-throughput video comparison.
5d1279276e1c.metaDescription: Compare MiniMax H3 Max text-to-video vs first-frame vs first-to-last-frame guidance, with optional prompt enhancement and 2K upscaling in one ComfyUI workflow.
5d1279276e1c.extendedDescription:
This comparison workflow pits three guidance modes of the MiniMax H3 Max model against each other: pure text-to-video, first-frame-to-video (animate from a single image), and first-to-last-frame-to-video (FLF2V). All three paths use the same base model but differ in how much visual constraint you provide. The text-only path is driven by your prompt (via MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode), the first-frame path anchors the opening composition, and the FLF2V path uses both the first and last frames (MinimaxHailuo03FirstLastFrameNode) to tightly direct motion, continuity, and lighting from start to finish. The graph also includes an optional Prompt Enhancer stage and an optional 2K upscale branch controlled by ComfySwitchNode and PrimitiveBoolean flags, so you can compare raw vs enhanced prompts and base vs upscaled output in one place.

Methodologically, you run multiple passes with a shared prompt and seed, changing only the guidance mode and/or feature flags. SaveVideo captures each render, while SaveText logs the active settings (prompt, flags, and mode) so you can verify that only a single variable changed between runs. If you enable MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode, you can produce controlled alternates—holding the same inputs constant—so differences are attributable to sampling rather than setup drift. Compare the results for prompt faithfulness, motion between keyframes, lighting stability, composition cleanliness, and edge fidelity. For convenience, try the included example assets (dream_face_first.png and dream_face_last.png) to see how first-only vs FLF2V affects transitions.
howToUse: Prepare inputs: Enter your prompt in PrimitiveStringMultiline (User Inputs). Optionally load dream_face_first.png and dream_face_last.png (LoadImage) for first/last-frame guidance. Set duration and base resolution. If you plan to upscale, generate at 768p.

Choose guidance mode and run baselines: a) Text-only (use the text path via MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode without supplying images), b) First-frame only (provide only the first image), c) FLF2V (provide both first and last images to MinimaxHailuo03FirstLastFrameNode). Keep seed and prompt constant across these runs.

Optional: Toggle the Prompt Enhancer (Prompt Enhancer group) with its ComfySwitchNode to compare raw vs enhanced prompts. SaveText will record which setting was active so you can attribute differences correctly.

Optional: Enable the PrimitiveBoolean flag for Upscale to 2K. Important: the upscale branch only accepts 768p source, so set base generation to 768p before enabling. Render again to compare base vs 2K upscaled outputs.

Generate controlled alternates: Use MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode to create 1–2 additional takes per mode with the same inputs. This reveals variability due to sampling while holding the guidance constant. Review the saved videos side-by-side and consult the SaveText logs to confirm run settings.
suggestedUseCases: Select the right guidance level for a project: free-form text ideation vs anchored first-frame motion vs tightly directed first-to-last transitions.
Previsualization for cinematics: test how closely FLF2V can hit a target final frame and lighting continuity compared to text-only generation.
Brand and product shots: compare stability and composition cleanliness when anchoring with a designed first frame versus letting the model choose.
Motion graphics and title sequences: evaluate how prompt enhancement affects typography legibility, lighting, and consistency.
High-throughput A/B testing: run multiple controlled variants (with Regenerate) to pick the most prompt-faithful take at 768p, then selectively upscale to 2K.

faqItems.question: What’s the practical difference between text-only, first-frame, and first-to-last-frame (FLF2V) guidance?
faqItems.answer: Text-only relies entirely on the prompt (via MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode), giving the model maximum creative freedom but less deterministic composition. First-frame guidance anchors the opening look and layout, improving consistency at the start while allowing freer evolution later. FLF2V (MinimaxHailuo03FirstLastFrameNode) constrains both endpoints, producing the most directed motion, transitions, and lighting continuity across the clip.

faqItems.question: How should I use the 2K upscale option without breaking the pipeline?
faqItems.answer: Turn on the PrimitiveBoolean flag for Upscale to 2K only when your source video is generated at 768p. The upscale branch accepts 768p input exclusively; other base resolutions are not supported. Generate at 768p first, then enable the upscale switch and re-run to produce the 2K comparison.

faqItems.question: What does MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode change compared to simply re-running the graph?
faqItems.answer: Regenerate triggers a controlled new take from the same setup, preserving your prompt, images, and settings while varying the sampling. This helps you compare variability within a mode without accidentally changing other parameters. SaveText captures the run context so you can verify consistency.

faqItems.question: Will enabling the Prompt Enhancer affect prompt adherence?
faqItems.answer: Often, yes. The Prompt Enhancer can clarify intent and structure, which may improve scene coherence and lighting consistency. However, it can also reduce open-ended creativity. Use the ComfySwitchNode to toggle it on/off and compare. The rewritten prompt and active flags are logged by SaveText for transparent A/B evaluation.

5e07754e7d06.title: Image Upscale: Recraft Creative
5e07754e7d06.description: Upload an image to enhance and upscale it. Recraft's AI reconstructs details and improves textures, outputting a higher-quality image with a natural appearance.
5e07754e7d06.metaDescription: Upscale and enhance images in ComfyUI using Recraft Creative Upscale with side-by-side compare. Works up to 2048×2048 and 5MB for natural-looking results.
5e07754e7d06.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow upscales and enhances a single image using Recraft’s Creative Upscale, then lets you visually verify the improvement before saving. The pipeline is minimal and focused: LoadImage brings your source file into the graph, RecraftCreativeUpscaleNode sends it to Recraft’s upscaling service for reconstruction and texture refinement, ImageCompare (Nodes 2.0) shows a side-by-side before/after, and SaveImage writes the result to disk. A MarkdownNote on the canvas provides quick, in-workflow reminders.

Technically, the RecraftCreativeUpscaleNode calls Recraft’s model to reconstruct fine details rather than just stretching pixels. This learned reconstruction preserves structure (edges, shapes, and content) while smoothing compression artifacts and improving textures for a natural look. It’s designed for practical enhancement—no prompts or stylization needed—making it a reliable drop-in step for preparing higher-quality assets. Note the input limits: images should be no larger than 5MB and 2048×2048, and ImageCompare is available under Nodes 2.0 (enable it via the menu).
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI (drag the JSON onto the canvas or use Load). If ImageCompare is missing, open the menu and switch to Nodes 2.0.
Open the LoadImage node and select your source image. Keep it under 5MB and 2048×2048 to meet the workflow’s constraints.
Check the RecraftCreativeUpscaleNode: ensure your Recraft access is configured (API credentials or model auth as required by your setup). No prompt is needed.
Queue and run the workflow. The image is sent to Recraft for detail reconstruction and upscaling, then returned to the graph.
Use the ImageCompare node (Nodes 2.0) to review the before/after and confirm that edges, textures, and skin/fabric details look natural.
When satisfied, save the result via the SaveImage node and retrieve the output from your ComfyUI output location.
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce product photos: improve clarity and texture while preserving brand-consistent appearance.
Social media and web graphics: upscale small assets to platform-ready sizes without harsh sharpening.
Photography touch-ups: clean up phone snapshots or compressed JPEGs for portfolios and blogs.
Design and illustration handoffs: upscale concepts or UI assets for presentations and print proofs.

faqItems.question: Do I need a Recraft account or API key for this to work?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The RecraftCreativeUpscaleNode calls an external service. Configure your Recraft credentials where your ComfyUI setup expects them (e.g., in the node or environment).

faqItems.question: What input limits should I follow?
faqItems.answer: Keep images at or below 5MB and 2048×2048. If your source is larger, downscale it before loading, or the request may fail or be auto-resized.

faqItems.question: Will the upscaler change my image’s style?
faqItems.answer: The goal is a natural, structure-preserving upscale. Expect cleaner edges and improved textures, not added content or stylization.

faqItems.question: Why can’t I find the ImageCompare node?
faqItems.answer: ImageCompare is part of Nodes 2.0. Open the ComfyUI menu and switch to Nodes 2.0, then reload the workflow so the node becomes available.

5f0ab474a355.title: Image Upscale: SeedVR2 7B Int8
5f0ab474a355.description: Upscale images using SeedVR2 7B Int8, a one-step diffusion model that enhances resolution through adversarial training and adaptive window attention. Input 1 image and receive 1 upscaled output with improved detail and clarity. Ideal for restoring low-resolution photos, preparing assets for print, or sharpening lightly degraded digital images.
5f0ab474a355.metaDescription: Upscale images in one step with SeedVR2 7B Int8 in ComfyUI. Load, compare, and save fast, detailed, print-ready results with minimal setup.
5f0ab474a355.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow shows how to upscale a single image using SeedVR2 7B Int8, a one-step diffusion model trained with adversarial objectives and adaptive window attention. Instead of iterative sampling, SeedVR2 performs a single forward pass to enhance resolution and restore detail, making it fast and consistent. The Int8 quantized weights reduce memory usage while preserving most of the model’s fidelity, which is helpful on mid-range GPUs.

Technically, the graph is straightforward: LoadImage feeds your source into the SeedVR2 7B Int8 node (ID: 1970dcb4-982a-4c01-a373-4d239a3041e4), which wraps the SeedVR2 checkpoint and its paired VAE (seedvr2_ema_vae_fp16.safetensors). The model outputs an upscaled image in a single step, which you can preview with ImageCompare (original vs upscaled) and then export via SaveImage. A MarkdownNote in the graph provides quick tips and references. Because it’s a one-step diffusion upscaler, you don’t need to tune sampler steps or schedulers—just set your desired output size (or keep defaults), run, and review.
howToUse: Install the model files: download SeedVR2 (Int8) and the VAE (seedvr2_ema_vae_fp16.safetensors) from the linked model pages. Place the weights in the folders recommended by the repository (typically ComfyUI/models/checkpoints for the model and ComfyUI/models/vae for the VAE).

Open the provided workflow (or subgraph) in ComfyUI. You should see LoadImage → SeedVR2 7B Int8 (node ID 1970dcb4-982a-4c01-a373-4d239a3041e4) → ImageCompare → SaveImage, plus a MarkdownNote with usage tips.
Load your source image using the LoadImage node. Use photographs or lightly degraded digital images for best results.
Select the SeedVR2 node and configure the output resolution or keep the default settings. Because SeedVR2 is one-step, there are no sampler steps to tune.
Queue and run the workflow. Inspect the result with the ImageCompare node (view at 100% to judge fine detail). If needed, adjust the target size or input image and re-run.
When satisfied, save the upscaled output using the SaveImage node. Choose a lossless format (e.g., PNG) if you plan further edits or print.
suggestedUseCases: Restoring low-resolution photos for archival or personal albums.
Preparing social media images for high-quality prints or large-format displays.
Sharpening lightly degraded digital assets such as UI elements, concept art, or web graphics.
Enhancing game textures or mod assets while preserving overall look and feel.
Improving product photos for e-commerce listings where clarity is critical.

faqItems.question: What makes SeedVR2 7B Int8 different from traditional upscalers?
faqItems.answer: SeedVR2 is a one-step diffusion upscaler trained with adversarial objectives and adaptive window attention. It enhances detail in a single forward pass (no iterative sampling), offering fast, consistent results compared to multi-step diffusion or classic GAN upscalers.

faqItems.question: Does Int8 quantization reduce quality compared to FP16?
faqItems.answer: Int8 substantially lowers VRAM and can improve speed. In most cases, quality differences from FP16 are minor, but extremely fine textures may show subtle changes. If you have ample VRAM and need maximum fidelity, try an FP16 variant; otherwise, Int8 is a strong default.

faqItems.question: How large can I upscale in one pass?
faqItems.answer: That depends on your GPU memory and the node’s settings. Moderate upscales (e.g., 2×–4× area increases) are typically reliable. Very large jumps may soften details or introduce artifacts; if needed, upscale in stages by running the output back through the node.

faqItems.question: Do I need to set steps, samplers, or CFG?
faqItems.answer: No. SeedVR2 is a one-step model, so there are no sampler steps or schedulers to configure. Focus on selecting a sensible output size and evaluating results with ImageCompare.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow with any image format?

faqItems.question: How can I ensure the animation is smooth?
