faqItems.answer: Check the resolution settings in the ImageScale node and ensure the video settings in the CreateVideo node are set to high quality.

5f8b74d92e62.title: Wan 2.2 14B Text to Video
5f8b74d92e62.description: Generate high-quality videos from text prompts with cinematic aesthetic control and dynamic motion generation using Wan 2.2.
5f8b74d92e62.metaDescription: Convert text prompts to cinematic videos with Wan 2.2 in ComfyUI, using advanced nodes for dynamic motion and aesthetic control.
5f8b74d92e62.extendedDescription:
The 'Wan 2.2 14B Text to Video' workflow in ComfyUI is a sophisticated tool designed to convert text prompts into high-quality videos with a cinematic aesthetic. This workflow leverages the Wan2.2 model, known for its dynamic motion generation and control over video aesthetics, to produce visually engaging content from textual descriptions. The workflow incorporates several key nodes, including the CLIPLoader and CLIPTextEncode for text processing, VAELoader for latent space manipulation, and the UNETLoader for image synthesis.

Technically, the workflow is structured into several groups that handle different stages of video generation. The 'Step1 - Load models' group initializes the necessary models, while 'Step2 - Video size' configures the output dimensions. The 'Wan2.2 T2V fp8_scaled' group is crucial for the text-to-video conversion process, utilizing advanced sampling techniques with the KSamplerAdvanced node. This structured approach ensures that users can generate videos with precise control over quality and style, making it an invaluable tool for creators looking to produce cinematic video content from simple text prompts.
howToUse: Load the 'Wan 2.2 14B Text to Video' workflow in ComfyUI.
Initialize the models by activating the 'Step1 - Load models' group.
Set your desired video size in the 'Step2 - Video size' group, adjusting for your VRAM capacity.
Enter your text prompt in the 'Step3 Prompt' group using the CLIPTextEncode node.
Enable the 'Wan2.2 T2V fp8_scaled' group to start the text-to-video conversion process.
Once the video is generated, use the SaveVideo node to export your final video.
suggestedUseCases: Creating promotional videos with specific stylistic elements from text descriptions.
Generating educational content where visual representation of concepts is required.
Producing artistic video installations or digital art pieces from textual themes.
Developing dynamic video content for social media platforms from trending topics.
Enhancing storytelling by visualizing narrative elements described in text.

faqItems.question: What models are used in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow uses the Wan2.2 model for text-to-video conversion, along with supporting nodes like CLIPLoader, VAELoader, and UNETLoader.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the video quality?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can adjust the video quality by modifying the video size in the 'Step2 - Video size' group, depending on your VRAM capacity.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to generate static images instead of videos?
faqItems.answer: Yes, by setting the video length to 1, you can use the Wan2.2 model as a text-to-image generator.

faqItems.question: How does the Lighting LoRA affect video generation?
faqItems.answer: Using the Wan2.2 Lighting LoRA can reduce generation time but may result in the loss of dynamic motion in the video.

5f8cb3a5e8f9.title: Meshy 6: Multi-Image to Model
5f8cb3a5e8f9.description: Create high-quality 3D models from multiple images using Meshy 6. More photos mean better detail capture, accurate proportions, and cleaner mesh structure.
5f8cb3a5e8f9.metaDescription: Transform multiple images into a detailed 3D model with Meshy 6. Capture accurate proportions and clean mesh structures effortlessly.
5f8cb3a5e8f9.extendedDescription: The 'Meshy 6: Multi-Image to Model' workflow is designed to transform a series of images into a high-quality 3D model. By leveraging the MeshyMultiImageToModelNode, this workflow allows for the integration of multiple images to enhance detail capture and ensure accurate proportions in the resulting 3D model. This process is further refined with the MeshyRefineNode, which cleans up the mesh structure for a more polished output. The workflow also includes nodes like MeshyTextureNode and MeshyAnimateModelNode to apply textures and animations, providing a comprehensive toolset for 3D model creation. The inclusion of Preview3D and SaveGLB nodes allows users to visualize and export their models easily. This workflow is particularly useful for applications requiring detailed and accurate 3D representations, such as virtual reality, gaming, and digital art.
howToUse: Load the 'Meshy 6: Multi-Image to Model' workflow in ComfyUI.
Import your images using the LoadImage node to provide multiple perspectives of the object you want to model.
Activate the MeshyMultiImageToModelNode to process the images into a preliminary 3D model.
Refine the model using the MeshyRefineNode to enhance detail and clean up the mesh structure.
Preview the model using the Preview3D node to check for accuracy and detail.
Export the final model using the SaveGLB node, or use the export feature in the Preview3D node to download it.
suggestedUseCases: Creating detailed 3D models for virtual reality environments.
Developing assets for video games with accurate proportions and textures.
Producing digital art that requires high-quality 3D representations.
Generating 3D models for educational purposes, such as anatomy or architecture.
Enhancing product visualization in e-commerce with realistic 3D models.

faqItems.question: How many images should I use for the best results?
faqItems.answer: Using more images from different angles will provide better detail capture and more accurate proportions in the 3D model.

faqItems.question: Can I animate the model within this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can use the MeshyAnimateModelNode to apply basic animations to your 3D model.

faqItems.question: Where is the final model saved?
faqItems.answer: The output model is automatically saved to the 'ComfyUI/output/' directory, or you can export it using the Preview3D node.

faqItems.question: What file format is the model exported in?
faqItems.answer: The model is exported in the GLB format, which is widely used for 3D models and compatible with various applications.

5fa9b44388cb.title: Hunyuan Video Text to Video
5fa9b44388cb.description: Generate videos from text prompts using Hunyuan model.
5fa9b44388cb.metaDescription: Tutorial: Generate text-to-video with Tencent Hunyuan in ComfyUI using SD3-style sampling, tiled VAE decode, and FluxGuidance for clean, coherent motion.
5fa9b44388cb.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns short text prompts into coherent, multi‑frame videos using Tencent’s Hunyuan Video model. It starts by loading the model stack in Step1 - Load models: DualCLIPLoader provides the text encoders, CLIPTextEncode converts your positive and negative prompts into embeddings, and UNETLoader brings in the Hunyuan Video UNet weights. ModelSamplingSD3 configures the sampler for Hunyuan’s SD3‑style noise schedule, while FluxGuidance applies classifier‑free guidance during denoising. Step2 - Video size uses EmptyHunyuanLatentVideo to define width, height, frame count/fps, and duration, and RandomNoise seeds the initial latent video. The Custom sampler section (SamplerCustomAdvanced with KSamplerSelect and BasicScheduler) then iteratively denoises the video latents into a structured animation.

After sampling, the pipeline decodes latents back to RGB frames using VAELoader with VAEDecodeTiled (recommended by default for most GPUs) or VAEDecode, then assembles and writes the result via CreateVideo and SaveVideo. The workflow is designed for practical iteration: adjust prompt wording in Step3 - Prompt, tweak steps and guidance for fidelity and motion, and manage memory with VAEDecodeTiled and fp8 weight_dtype in UNETLoader when needed. For details and tips specific to Hunyuan Video, see the linked documentation.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then open Step1 - Load models. In UNETLoader, select the Hunyuan Video checkpoint. In VAELoader, choose the matching VAE. If VRAM is tight, set UNETLoader weight_dtype to fp8 (if your hardware supports it).

Go to Step2 - Video size. In EmptyHunyuanLatentVideo, set width and height (use multiples of 16), fps, and either frames or seconds to define the clip length. Set a seed in RandomNoise for reproducibility or leave it random for variety.

Open Step3 - Prompt. Enter a clear positive prompt in CLIPTextEncode (e.g., the provided anime example) and add a concise negative prompt to avoid unwanted elements (e.g., blurry, low detail, jitter).

In Custom sampler, pick a sampler in KSamplerSelect (start with dpmpp_2m or euler) and set steps in BasicScheduler (e.g., 20–35). Use FluxGuidance to adjust guidance scale (CFG); higher values follow the prompt more strongly but can introduce artifacts.

Use VAEDecodeTiled for decoding by default. If you encounter out‑of‑memory errors, lower tile_size and increase overlap slightly to hide seams. Only switch to VAEDecode if you have ample VRAM and need maximum speed.

Queue the workflow. Inspect the frames and motion. If motion is weak, increase steps or modestly raise guidance; if flicker appears, reduce guidance or steps. When satisfied, CreateVideo and SaveVideo will export the final clip.
suggestedUseCases: Concept animations for characters, products, or environments from quick text prompts
Stylized social clips (e.g., anime loops, abstract visuals) for shorts and stories
Previsualization for motion and framing before commissioning full production
Background ambience loops for streams, events, or digital signage
Education and research demos illustrating text‑conditioned motion synthesis

faqItems.question: I’m running out of VRAM. How can I make this workflow lighter?
faqItems.answer: Use VAEDecodeTiled (default) and reduce tile_size while increasing overlap slightly to hide seams. In UNETLoader, choose fp8 weight_dtype if supported by your GPU. Lower resolution, shorten duration (fewer frames), or reduce steps in BasicScheduler.

faqItems.question: What settings give stable, coherent motion?
faqItems.answer: Keep width/height as multiples of 16 and start with 20–35 steps. Set a fixed seed in RandomNoise. Use FluxGuidance with a moderate guidance scale; too high can cause flicker, too low weakens prompt adherence. Refine prompts to be specific but not overly long.

faqItems.question: When should I use VAEDecode vs. VAEDecodeTiled?
faqItems.answer: Use VAEDecodeTiled by default—it’s memory‑efficient and recommended for most GPUs. Switch to VAEDecode only if you have sufficient VRAM and want faster decoding without tiling. If you see seams with tiled decode, increase overlap or lower tile_size.

faqItems.question: Which sampler and schedule should I choose?
faqItems.answer: Keep ModelSamplingSD3 as provided for Hunyuan. Start with dpmpp_2m or euler in KSamplerSelect and 20–35 steps in BasicScheduler. If details smear, try more steps; if results are noisy, reduce steps or lower guidance in FluxGuidance.

5fbe136ba6f9.title: Qwen Image 2.1: Image Edit
5fbe136ba6f9.description: Edit images with Qwen-Image-2.1 by feeding two reference images through a single checkpoint that handles both generation and editing, then comparing the result against the original. Ideal for character-consistent edits, product cutout compositing with real transparency, and style-transfer passes at native 2K.
5fbe136ba6f9.metaDescription: Edit images with Qwen-Image-2.1 using two references, preserve transparency, and compare before/after. Native 2K output with ResolutionSelector in ComfyUI.
5fbe136ba6f9.extendedDescription:
This workflow demonstrates image-to-image editing with Qwen-Image-2.1 by feeding two reference images into a single checkpoint that handles both generation and editing. The first image (image_1) is your base subject, and the second image (image_2) is the visual guide for what you want to change—such as clothing, style, or material. A ResolutionSelector node controls canvas size: by default it preserves image_1’s aspect ratio at approximately resolution×resolution (default 1024, rounded to a multiple of 32). Qwen-Image-2.1 supports native 2K (2048×2048) output, or you can set resolution to 0 to keep the original pixel dimensions (again rounded to a multiple of 32).

Technically, the LoadImage nodes feed both references into the Qwen-Image-2.1 checkpoint node (bc1c967a-7f6a-4be9-a372-dad16e4f28e3), which fuses them to produce an edited image anchored to the content of image_1 and guided by the appearance, style, or cutout mask in image_2. This makes it well-suited for character-consistent edits, product cutout compositing with real transparency (when your guide image has an alpha channel), and style-transfer passes at high resolution. The ImageCompare node shows before/after frames side-by-side for quick review, and SaveImageAdvanced lets you export clean PNGs to preserve transparency. MarkdownNote and Note nodes in the graph provide inline tips, and the Qwen edit block is organized as a Subgraph for easy navigation.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI. If prompted for missing components, ensure the Qwen-Image-2.1 checkpoint/node (bc1c967a-7f6a-4be9-a372-dad16e4f28e3) is available.
Load your base image into the first LoadImage node (image_1). For a quick test, use portrait_model_denim.png from the provided assets.
Load your guide/reference image into the second LoadImage node (image_2). For clothing or product swaps, use a PNG with an alpha channel such as clothing_light_blue_denim_shirt.png.

Set output size with ResolutionSelector: leave at the default (≈1024) to preserve image_1’s aspect ratio, set to 2048 for native 2K, or set to 0 to keep original pixel dimensions (all rounded to multiples of 32).
Queue the workflow. The Qwen-Image-2.1 node produces the edited image; ImageCompare displays the original (image_1) side-by-side with the result for quick quality checks.
Save your output with SaveImageAdvanced. Choose PNG to keep real transparency when your guide image includes alpha (useful for product cutouts and compositing).
suggestedUseCases: Wardrobe swaps on portraits while maintaining the subject’s identity and pose.
Product cutout compositing with true transparency for e‑commerce listings and catalogs.
High-resolution (2K) style-transfer passes for lookbooks, mood boards, and concept iterations.
Before/after comparisons for client reviews using ImageCompare to validate edits quickly.
Consistent character or brand styling across a series of images with the same base subject.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow decide the output size?
faqItems.answer: ResolutionSelector preserves the aspect ratio of image_1 and scales to about resolution×resolution (default 1024), rounded to a multiple of 32. Set resolution to 2048 for native 2K, or 0 to keep the original pixel dimensions (also rounded to a multiple of 32).

faqItems.question: Do I need a text prompt for edits?
faqItems.answer: No. This workflow uses two reference images. The base image (image_1) anchors content and composition, while the guide image (image_2) drives the visual change, such as clothing or style.

faqItems.question: Can it preserve transparency for product cutouts?
faqItems.answer: Yes. If your guide image (image_2) includes an alpha channel, the workflow can maintain real transparency in the result. Export with SaveImageAdvanced set to PNG to preserve the alpha channel.

faqItems.question: What if I run out of VRAM at higher resolutions?
faqItems.answer: Reduce the ResolutionSelector value (e.g., to 1024) or keep original size with resolution=0 if it’s smaller. Native 2K (2048×2048) is supported by Qwen-Image-2.1 but requires more GPU memory.

5fc145bb102e.title: TripoSplat: Image to Gaussian Splat
5fc145bb102e.description: Upload a single 2D image. Generate a high-quality 3D Gaussian splat representation with controllable density and budget for rendering.
5fc145bb102e.metaDescription: Turn a single 2D image into a controllable 3D Gaussian Splat. Preview, render a turntable, and export as splat or GLB with TripoSplat in ComfyUI.
5fc145bb102e.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow converts a single 2D image into a viewable and exportable 3D Gaussian Splat using TripoSplat. You start with LoadImage to bring in your source photo, then pass it through a bundled TripoSplat subgraph (shown as node b64333d5-4e6f-4e99-9506-2ec4f63259fe) that runs the Tripo model to predict a colored Gaussian point cloud from one view. The subgraph exposes practical controls like density/opacity scaling and a point budget (max splats) so you can balance detail against speed and memory. A MarkdownNote on the canvas summarizes the key options, and the author has packaged the core logic as a Subgraph to keep the graph clean and easy to tweak.

For inspection and presentation, the pipeline uses CreateCameraInfo to define a simple orbit/turntable path, RenderSplat to rasterize the Gaussian splats into frames, then CreateVideo and SaveVideo to encode the sequence. When you’re ready to export, SplatToFile3D writes the native splat representation for use in external 3DGS viewers, while SplatToMesh followed by SaveGLB converts and saves a mesh-based GLB if you need a traditional 3D asset for DCC tools, game engines, or AR/VR pipelines. The approach is fast, works best on clean, stylized objects, and provides intuitive control over reconstruction density and runtime budget. For background on the method, see TripoSplat (VAST-AI-Research) and the paper on arXiv.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and review the on-canvas MarkdownNote. Ensure required models are available (Tripo for the splat reconstruction; optional BiRefNet if included by your subgraph).
Use LoadImage to add your source image. For best results, choose a clear subject with minimal background clutter (stylized objects work especially well).

Open the TripoSplat subgraph (node b64333d5-4e6f-4e99-9506-2ec4f63259fe) and adjust key controls: set the point budget/max splats to balance quality vs. speed, and tune density/opacity scaling to reduce fuzz or fill thin areas.
Preview the result: set an orbit path with CreateCameraInfo (number of frames, radius, elevation, FOV), connect to RenderSplat, and view the rendered frames to check shape, coverage, and density.
Export 3D assets: use SplatToFile3D to write a splat file compatible with Gaussian Splat viewers; or convert with SplatToMesh and then SaveGLB if you need a mesh/GLB for DCC tools or engines.
Create a turntable video: feed RenderSplat frames into CreateVideo, then SaveVideo to write an MP4 (or your chosen container). Adjust camera path and resolution for your final output.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid product or prop previews from a single reference image (for moodboards or client reviews).
Stylized asset ideation for games or animation where fast 3D context is more important than watertight meshes.
AR/VR prototyping with lightweight splat assets and controlled point budgets.
Concept turntables for pitch decks and social media using quick orbit renders.
Reference geometry for layout/blocking before committing to full modeling.

faqItems.question: What’s the difference between a Gaussian Splat and a mesh, and which should I export?
faqItems.answer: A Gaussian Splat is a point-based representation that renders fast and looks great from many angles, but it isn’t a watertight surface. Export a splat (SplatToFile3D) when you’ll view it in splat-capable tools or want speed and fidelity to the reconstruction. Convert with SplatToMesh + SaveGLB if you need a conventional mesh for DCC tools, game engines, physics, or editing.

faqItems.question: How do I get cleaner shapes or fewer floaters?
faqItems.answer: Use a subject-focused image (plain background helps), reduce the point budget to limit noise, and slightly lower density/opacity scaling to suppress fuzzy halos. Re-render with a smaller camera FOV for a tighter look. If your workflow version includes optional foreground matting (e.g., BiRefNet inside the subgraph), enable it to isolate the subject.

faqItems.question: It runs slowly or runs out of memory. What can I change?
faqItems.answer: Lower the point budget/max splats in the TripoSplat subgraph, reduce RenderSplat resolution, and shorten the camera path (fewer frames) before creating the video. On lower VRAM GPUs, preview at half resolution first, then bump settings for the final render.

faqItems.question: Can I use any photo, and does it work with people or complex scenes?
faqItems.answer: It works best on single, stylized objects with clear boundaries. Complex scenes or thin structures may produce artifacts or incomplete geometry. For people or busy backgrounds, crop or mask the subject first and keep expectations to quick previews rather than production meshes.

5fd7dc1f9db5.title: SDPose-OOD: Video to Pose Map
5fd7dc1f9db5.description: Upload a video to extract pose keypoints and generate a pose map. The workflow supports multiple person detection and uses an enhanced SDPose model for accurate whole-body feature extraction.
5fd7dc1f9db5.metaDescription: Extract multi-person whole-body pose maps from video with SDPose-OOD in ComfyUI, then export a pose-map video aligned to the original timing.
5fd7dc1f9db5.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial walks you through SDPose-OOD: Video to Pose Map — a workflow that converts any input video into a clean pose map sequence. The pipeline starts with LoadVideo to decode frames, runs each frame through the SDPose-OOD pose extractor (backed by the sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors checkpoint) to detect whole-body keypoints, and then assembles the pose frames into a final clip with CreateVideo and SaveVideo. The SDPose-OOD node (type ID 01b6a731-fb78-4070-9a38-c87146da9604) supports multi-person detection and outputs a rendered pose map per frame, covering body, hands, and face landmarks.

Technically, the SDPose-OOD model estimates 2D keypoints for every visible person in each frame, then the node renders those landmarks as a pose map image (skeleton/lines and joints) that’s consistent across the sequence. By keeping the original frame rate and dimensions from LoadVideo, CreateVideo can produce a pose video that aligns one-to-one with the source timing, making it ideal as conditioning for downstream generation (e.g., pose-guided image/video synthesis) or for motion analysis and pre-visualization. SaveVideo finalizes the result to your chosen location and codec.
howToUse: Download the sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors checkpoint and place it in ComfyUI/models/checkpoints/.
Open the SDPose-OOD: Video to Pose Map workflow in ComfyUI. In LoadVideo, select your source video; confirm the frame rate and resolution detected are as expected.

In the SDPose-OOD (WholeBody) node (type 01b6a731-fb78-4070-9a38-c87146da9604), select the sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors model. Optionally adjust detection settings such as enabling multi-person and setting a reasonable confidence threshold.

Preview a few frames by running the graph to ensure poses are detected cleanly for all subjects. If detection is unstable, try a lower input resolution for speed or raise the confidence threshold for fewer false positives.
Connect the SDPose-OOD output to CreateVideo, pass through the frame rate from LoadVideo, and set your desired output size (usually matching the input).
Use SaveVideo to choose an output filename and format (e.g., MP4). Execute the workflow to generate and save the pose-map video.
suggestedUseCases: Pose conditioning for image/video generation (e.g., guiding a diffusion model with pose maps for consistent motion).
Pre-visualization for animation and motion studies, capturing full body, hand, and face landmarks.
Privacy-preserving motion sharing by replacing footage with anonymized pose skeletons.
Dataset creation for action recognition or pose-based analytics, exporting synchronized pose-map clips.
Rotoscoping and motion reference extraction for VFX and choreography planning.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow support multiple people in the same frame?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The SDPose-OOD node supports multi-person detection and will render pose maps for all detected subjects per frame. For crowded scenes, consider raising the confidence threshold to reduce false positives.

faqItems.question: Which model file do I need and where should it go?
faqItems.answer: Use sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors. Place it in ComfyUI/models/checkpoints/. Then select it in the SDPose-OOD node before running the workflow.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the output aligned with the source video?
faqItems.answer: Pass the frame rate from LoadVideo into CreateVideo, and keep the output resolution consistent with the input. This preserves one-to-one timing and sizing for downstream use.

faqItems.question: What can I do if detection is jittery or misses hands/face?
faqItems.answer: Try increasing the input resolution for clearer details, raise the detection confidence to reduce noise, and ensure good lighting and contrast in the source. For performance-constrained GPUs, balance resolution and frame skip to maintain stability.

60079360588d.title: Video Upscale: SeedVR2
60079360588d.description: Upload a video to upscale and enhance its resolution using the SeedVR2 model for high-definition output.
60079360588d.metaDescription: Upscale videos to HD with SeedVR2 in ComfyUI. Load, enhance with height-based scaling, and export high-quality results while preserving original timing.
60079360588d.extendedDescription:
This workflow upscales an input video to a higher resolution using the SeedVR2 model, converting low- to mid-resolution clips into sharper, high-definition output. It reads your source clip with LoadVideo, extracts frames and timing via GetVideoComponents, then runs each frame through the SeedVR2_VideoUpscaler node (model: SeedVR2). After enhancement, it reassembles the sequence into a video using CreateVideo and writes the result to disk with SaveVideo.

Technically, the SeedVR2_VideoUpscaler’s Resolution control is height-based: you choose a target output height (e.g., typical 720/1080/1440/2160-style heights), and the node preserves aspect ratio while scaling width accordingly. ImageScale is available if you want to pre-size frames before the model runs (e.g., to avoid extreme scaling jumps). ImageFromBatch is included for quick frame-level previews, but it will clip the video to a single image; disable it (select the node and press Ctrl-B) to process the full video. The original frame rate from GetVideoComponents can be passed forward to CreateVideo to maintain the source timing and motion cadence.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and load your source clip into the LoadVideo node.
Inspect GetVideoComponents to ensure frames and FPS are detected. Keep its FPS output connected to CreateVideo to preserve original timing.
In SeedVR2_VideoUpscaler, set the Resolution value by target height (e.g., a typical 720/1080/1440/2160-style height). The node keeps your aspect ratio automatically.
If you only want to preview a single frame, keep ImageFromBatch enabled. For full-video processing, select ImageFromBatch and press Ctrl-B to disable it.
Optionally adjust ImageScale to gently resize frames before the model (useful if your source is very small or if you want to avoid extreme upscaling).
Set your output location in SaveVideo, then queue the workflow. When it finishes, your upscaled video will be saved to the specified path.
suggestedUseCases: Upscaling screen recordings or tutorials to a sharper, more readable HD output.
Enhancing smartphone or webcam footage for social media or presentations.
Restoring older low-resolution clips for archival or portfolio use.
Improving product demo videos where UI text and edges need to be crisp.

faqItems.question: How does the Resolution setting work in SeedVR2_VideoUpscaler?
faqItems.answer: Resolution is based on output height. Pick a target height (e.g., a typical 720/1080/1440/2160-style value), and the node scales width to match while preserving aspect ratio.

faqItems.question: Why am I only getting a single frame instead of the full video?
faqItems.answer: The ImageFromBatch node is for frame previews and will clip the video. Select it and press Ctrl-B to disable/bypass it to process the entire video.

faqItems.question: Will the workflow keep my video’s original frame rate?
faqItems.answer: Yes, if you pass the FPS from GetVideoComponents to CreateVideo. This maintains the source timing and motion cadence in the output.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow handle audio?
faqItems.answer: No. It focuses on visual upscaling. If you need audio, export the upscaled video and then merge it with the original audio track using a video editor or ffmpeg.

603b2d01feb0.title: Comfy for Advertising - B-Roll Creation
603b2d01feb0.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow to create ad-ready product B-roll via text prompt, reference images, or light video edits using ByteDance2 text-to-video and reference nodes.
603b2d01feb0.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds polished product B‑roll shots for ads using three practical paths: prompt-only generation, reference-guided inserts, and light video edits. At its core, ByteDance2TextToVideoNode synthesizes short clips from your text prompt, while ByteDance2ReferenceNode lets you anchor style and object identity with one or more images (for example, a product packshot and a scene still). LoadImage and LoadVideo nodes bring your assets into the graph, PrimitiveNode supplies key parameters (resolution, frame count, FPS, seed), Video Slice isolates a target segment from an input clip, and SaveVideo writes the final result. MarkdownNote inside the workflow documents the intended usage and includes example prompts.

Method 1 (Prompt Only) is the fastest way to create a fresh B‑roll shot: write a descriptive prompt (e.g., the provided smartphone-in-forest orbit example), set frames/FPS/size via PrimitiveNode, and render with ByteDance2TextToVideoNode. Method 2 (Reference Images) adds control: feed a product image and a scene still into ByteDance2ReferenceNode to match lighting, color, and composition before generation, producing an insert shot that blends into an existing edit. Method 3 (Video Edit) is for subtle replacements: use LoadVideo and Video Slice to define a segment you want to enhance, mirror its timing and dimensions with PrimitiveNode, guide generation with prompt and references, then export with SaveVideo for drop‑in replacement in your NLE.

Because the key parameters are explicit, it’s easy to keep outputs consistent: lock the seed for reproducibility, match FPS and resolution to your timeline, and keep clip lengths short (3–5 seconds) for sharper detail and steadier motion. The reference path is especially effective for maintaining product identity and scene continuity while still exploring creative camera moves or lighting within your prompt.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote for an overview of the three methods.
Set global parameters via PrimitiveNode: resolution (width/height), number of frames (duration), FPS, and seed. Match these to your target edit whenever possible.

Method 1 – Prompt Only: Open ByteDance2TextToVideoNode, enter your descriptive prompt (e.g., the smartphone forest orbit), confirm frames/FPS/size from PrimitiveNode are connected, then queue and render.

Method 2 – Reference Images: Use LoadImage to bring in a product reference and, optionally, a scene still. Connect them to ByteDance2ReferenceNode, route that into ByteDance2TextToVideoNode along with your prompt, adjust reference strength if exposed, then render.

Method 3 – Video Edit: Import your source clip with LoadVideo and set an in/out range using Video Slice to identify the segment you’ll replace. Mirror the segment’s resolution/FPS/duration in PrimitiveNode, guide generation with prompt and ByteDance2ReferenceNode (using a product still and/or a frame from the clip), then render.
Preview the result and export with SaveVideo. If you’re replacing part of an existing edit, ensure FPS, duration, and aspect ratio match so the shot drops in cleanly.
suggestedUseCases: Create clean product insert shots that match an existing scene’s look and lighting.
Generate on-brand B‑roll for social ads and landing pages from a single prompt.
Replace a problematic or missing pickup shot in a commercial while preserving continuity.
Produce multiple stylistic variations of the same product shot by swapping references or seeds.
Quickly mock up creative directions (camera move, environment, mood) for client reviews.

faqItems.question: What’s the difference between the three methods?
faqItems.answer: Method 1 generates a clip purely from your prompt (fastest, most flexible). Method 2 adds product/scene control by conditioning with reference images for better continuity. Method 3 times your output to a selected portion of an existing video so you can replace or enhance that segment in post.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the product consistent across variations?
faqItems.answer: Use Method 2 and feed a high-quality, front-facing product image into ByteDance2ReferenceNode. Keep resolution, FPS, and seed fixed in PrimitiveNode, and reuse the same scene still to maintain lighting and composition. Change only one variable (prompt or seed) at a time.

faqItems.question: What settings work best for ad B‑roll?
faqItems.answer: Keep clips short (3–5 seconds) at 24–30 FPS for smoother motion and better detail. Match your timeline’s resolution (e.g., 1080p or 4K) in PrimitiveNode. If motion looks jittery, reduce scene complexity in the prompt or slightly increase the frame count for the same duration.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the generated clip fits into my existing edit?
faqItems.answer: In Method 3, use Video Slice to mark the exact segment you’ll replace. Copy its resolution, FPS, and duration into PrimitiveNode, and render your new shot with those same values. Export via SaveVideo and drop it into your NLE to replace the original segment.

606ca8b29a3f.title: Depth Estimation: Lotus
606ca8b29a3f.description: Run Lotus Depth in ComfyUI for zero-shot, efficient monocular depth estimation with high detail retention.
606ca8b29a3f.metaDescription: ComfyUI Lotus Depth workflow for fast, zero-shot monocular depth maps. Load an image, estimate depth, and save for SD1.5 ControlNet or 3D tasks.
606ca8b29a3f.extendedDescription:
This workflow runs Lotus Depth for zero-shot monocular depth estimation directly inside ComfyUI. It is intentionally minimal: LoadImage brings in your source photo, a Lotus Depth Subgraph node (id: c7d32155-757f-4e5d-a139-7e438da96f2f) predicts a per-pixel depth map, and SaveImage writes the result to disk. A MarkdownNote on the canvas provides quick tips and links. The output is a clean, high-detail grayscale depth map suitable for visualization or as guidance for downstream tasks.

Technically, the encapsulated subgraph handles preprocessing, model inference, and normalization so you can drop in any single image and get an immediate depth result with no prompt engineering. The workflow pairs well with Stable Diffusion 1.5 pipelines from Stability AI: the saved depth can be fed into a ControlNet-Depth setup for depth-guided text-to-image generation, keeping scene composition while allowing creative style changes. Because it uses a subgraph, you can double-click to inspect or adapt internals without cluttering your main canvas.
howToUse: Update ComfyUI to the latest version and prepare the required Lotus Depth model files as instructed by the node or repository (see update guide: https://docs.comfy.org/installation/update_comfyui).
Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and open the canvas. Use the LoadImage node to select the image you want to process.
Optional: Double-click the Lotus Depth Subgraph node (id: c7d32155-757f-4e5d-a139-7e438da96f2f) to view or adjust any exposed parameters, then collapse it back when done.
Set a filename prefix on the SaveImage node if desired. Click Queue Prompt to run the depth estimation.
Preview the generated depth map on the SaveImage node and check the outputs folder for the saved PNG.
Optional: Feed the saved depth map into your Stable Diffusion 1.5 + ControlNet Depth workflow to create depth-guided text-to-image results.
suggestedUseCases: Depth-guided text-to-image generation with SD1.5 and ControlNet Depth to preserve structure while changing style or content.
Pre-visualization for relighting, compositing, and VFX where scene geometry cues are helpful.
2D-to-3D workflows: use the depth map to bootstrap normals or rough meshes in external DCC tools.
Depth-aware upscaling, matting, and background replacement for photography and design.
Robust depth estimation for robotics or AR prototypes where quick, zero-shot inference is valuable.

faqItems.question: What models or files do I need and where do they go?
faqItems.answer: Install the Lotus Depth weights required by the subgraph node. Follow the node’s README or tooltip for the exact filename and folder (typically under ComfyUI/models in a model-specific subfolder). Update ComfyUI first to ensure the node is recognized.

faqItems.question: How do I get the most detailed and stable depth maps?
faqItems.answer: Start with a clean, reasonably high-resolution input (avoid heavy JPEG compression). Load the image close to your target generation size if you plan to use SD1.5 later. Keep the subject well-lit and avoid extreme motion blur. If the subgraph exposes quality or scale settings, increase them moderately and re-run.

faqItems.question: Can I use these depth maps with Stable Diffusion 1.5 and Stability models?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The saved grayscale depth map works as input for ControlNet-Depth in SD1.5 pipelines, letting you guide composition while generating new styles or content. Match the depth map resolution to your SD canvas for best alignment.

faqItems.question: What hardware do I need and how fast is it?
faqItems.answer: A CUDA-capable GPU (8 GB VRAM or more recommended) provides practical inference speed. CPU execution may be possible but is typically very slow. Batch size is 1 in this simple workflow; process multiple images sequentially for consistency.

60e1839cbb34.title: Branded Comfy Thumbnail
60e1839cbb34.description: Generate Thumbnails with your brand guidelines as references.
60e1839cbb34.metaDescription: A ComfyUI workflow to extract video frames and compose 2-up or 4-up branded YouTube thumbnails using your logo and brand references.
60e1839cbb34.extendedDescription:
Branded Comfy Thumbnail is a frame-selection and composition workflow that turns moments from your video into on-brand YouTube thumbnails. It centers on a simple pipeline: LoadVideo ingests your source clip, GetVideoComponents exposes frame data, and ImageFromBatch lets you pick exact frames by index. Those selected frames are grouped with BatchImagesNode and then composited in a grid by a custom Merge Images node (shown in the graph with the ID 2f633b06-929a-4f4c-afff-ffea89d93a76). Brand references such as a logo, color swatches, or a background plate are brought in with LoadImage. You can review choices at each step with PreviewImage and export the final design with SaveImage.

What makes this workflow practical is its focus on speed and control for real-world thumbnail creation—no diffusion model required. The YouTube Thumbnail Generator group provides a clean 2-up or 4-up layout toggle (per the author note: switch off for 2 images, on for 4 images), so you can quickly compare options or output a final composite. A GeminiNanoBanana2 utility node is included to assist with on-brand text ideas or file naming guidance; it does not render text onto the image in this version. MarkdownNote blocks are sprinkled in to document settings and remind you of best practices while you work.
howToUse: Open the workflow and review the groups: Brand Guidelines, Load Video, Select Frames, and YouTube Thumbnail Generator. Read any MarkdownNote hints on the canvas.
In Brand Guidelines, use LoadImage to bring in your logo, brand color board, or background plate. Keep these images in your project folder for consistent reuse.
In Load Video, point LoadVideo to your source clip. Use GetVideoComponents to inspect frame count and fps, then preview a few frames with PreviewImage to gauge content.
In Select Frames, use ImageFromBatch (or multiple instances) to pull specific frames by index. Tip: index ≈ seconds × fps. Collect your chosen 2 or 4 frames with BatchImagesNode.

In YouTube Thumbnail Generator, set the Merge Images toggle per the author note: switch off for 2 images, switch on for 4 images. Feed in your selected frames (and any brand plate/logo inputs if provided), then check the result with PreviewImage.

Once satisfied, use SaveImage to export. Iterate by adjusting frame indices or swapping brand assets until you have a strong, on-brand thumbnail at your target aspect ratio (commonly 1280×720 for YouTube).
suggestedUseCases: Create fast, on-brand YouTube thumbnails from talking-head or screencast videos.
Produce consistent cover images for podcast episodes or interview series.
Generate lesson and module thumbnails for online courses and tutorials.
Design recap/announcement graphics for webinars and live streams.
Batch-select strong frames for A/B testing thumbnail variants.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow generate images from text or a model prompt?
faqItems.answer: No. It composes thumbnails from your existing video frames and brand images. There is no diffusion or generative image model in this graph; the focus is selection and layout.

faqItems.question: How do I choose an exact moment from the video?
faqItems.answer: Use GetVideoComponents to note the fps, then set ImageFromBatch index ≈ desired_seconds × fps. Add multiple ImageFromBatch nodes (with different indices) to capture several candidate frames.

faqItems.question: How do I switch between 2-up and 4-up layouts?
faqItems.answer: Use the Merge Images node’s toggle noted by the author: switch off for 2 images, on for 4 images. Make sure you supply the correct number of inputs to match the selected layout.

faqItems.question: What is the GeminiNanoBanana2 node doing here?
faqItems.answer: It’s an auxiliary helper for generating on-brand caption ideas or keywords you can use in titles, descriptions, or filenames. It does not overlay text onto the thumbnail in this version.

60ed2d7ede2e.title: GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst: Text to Image
60ed2d7ede2e.description: GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst is a high-fidelity image editing and generation template for creating polished, detail-rich visuals. It preserves subject identity, complex materials, lighting consistency and scene structure across iterations. Suitable for concept refinement, product visuals, character scenes, cinematic backgrounds and finished artwork that requires precision, realism and visual depth.
60ed2d7ede2e.metaDescription: ComfyUI template for high-fidelity text-to-image via OpenAI. Use a structured Sunburst prompt to preserve identity, materials, and lighting across iterations.
60ed2d7ede2e.extendedDescription:
GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst: Text to Image is a focused ComfyUI template that turns carefully structured prompts into polished, detail-rich images using OpenAI’s image generation API. The core of the workflow is OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2, which packages your prompt (using a "Sunburst" structure that calls out subject, materials, lighting, camera, and composition) and sends it to the selected OpenAI image model. The resulting image stream is then handed to SaveImage, which writes the outputs to your ComfyUI output directory.

Technically, the node exposes common OpenAI image parameters such as model, size/aspect, quality/style, number of outputs, and output format. The Sunburst prompt structure helps preserve subject identity, complex materials, lighting consistency, and scene layout by keeping a stable "anchor" block in your prompt across iterations. You iterate by adjusting only the variable parts (e.g., pose, background, or mood) while leaving the anchor descriptors unchanged—yielding high-fidelity refinements without rebuilding the entire scene each time.
howToUse: Load the workflow: Open ComfyUI and import the "GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst: Text to Image" workflow JSON.
Configure API access: In OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2, select your OpenAI image model and set your API key (via the node’s field or the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable).

Write a Sunburst prompt: Create a structured prompt with stable anchors (e.g., Subject, Materials, Lighting, Camera/Composition) and a small variable section for changes. Keep anchors identical across iterations.
Set generation parameters: In OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2, choose size/aspect, quality/style, number of images to generate, and output format. Use the same settings when iterating for consistent results.
Run the workflow: Queue the prompt. OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 generates the image(s), and SaveImage writes them to your ComfyUI output folder.
Refine: For new variations, only edit the variable part of the prompt (e.g., pose or background). Keep the anchor block and node settings unchanged to preserve identity and materials.
suggestedUseCases: Product hero shots that require consistent materials, finishes, and lighting across multiple angles.
Character concept frames where identity, costume details, and facial structure must remain stable over iterations.
Cinematic background plates with controlled mood, lensing, and scene composition for continuity.
Material and lighting studies to compare how different surfaces behave under a fixed lighting setup.
Refined key visuals for presentations where realism and repeatability are important.

faqItems.question: What model does this workflow use?
faqItems.answer: It uses OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 to call OpenAI’s image generation API. You can select the model inside the node (e.g., an available OpenAI image model on your account). The node also exposes typical options like size/aspect, quality/style, and number of outputs.

faqItems.question: How do I keep a character or product consistent across runs?
faqItems.answer: Repeat the same Sunburst anchor details every time (subject traits, materials, key props, lighting, lens/camera, and composition), and keep node parameters (model, size/aspect, quality) unchanged. OpenAI image models are non-deterministic, so exact pixel matches aren’t guaranteed, but stable anchors greatly improve identity and material consistency.

faqItems.question: Where are my images saved, and can I change the location?
faqItems.answer: SaveImage writes files to your ComfyUI output directory. You can set a custom subfolder or filename prefix directly in the SaveImage node to organize outputs per project or prompt.

faqItems.question: Does this work offline or with no API key?
faqItems.answer: No. OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 sends requests to OpenAI’s servers, so you need an active internet connection and a valid OpenAI API key. Usage is billed by your OpenAI account based on the model and settings you choose.

615266189e02.title: LTX-2.5 (Pro): Image to Video
615266189e02.description: Generate video from a single image using LTX-2.5's fast distilled model, delivering cinematic multi-shot sequences with consistent characters, lighting, and style across cuts. The workflow outputs a video file with native multishot support and automatic duration prediction. Ideal for rapid storyboarding, social media content creation, and pre-visualization in commercial production pipelines.
615266189e02.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Turn one image into a cinematic multi-shot video with LTX-2.5. Native multishot, auto duration, and consistent style across cuts.
615266189e02.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single reference image into a cinematic, multi-shot video using the LTX-2.5 fast distilled model. It links three nodes end-to-end: LoadImage brings your source still into the graph, LtxApi25ImageToVideo sends that image to the LTX-2.5 API for motion synthesis and shot generation, and SaveVideo writes the returned clip to disk. Because LTX-2.5 supports native multishot generation and automatic duration prediction, the result feels like a short edited sequence rather than a single continuous pan or zoom.

Technically, the LtxApi25ImageToVideo node conditions all shots on the same input frame, which helps maintain character, lighting, and style consistency across cuts. The node handles request/response with the remote service, queues generation, and outputs a ready-to-save video. SaveVideo then encodes the result at your chosen filename and frame rate. This makes the workflow ideal for rapid storyboarding, social posts, and pre-visualization: drop in one clean reference image, let the API infer pacing and camera moves, and export a cohesive multi-shot clip in minutes.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the three core nodes: LoadImage -> LtxApi25ImageToVideo -> SaveVideo.
In LoadImage, select a clean, well-lit source image that clearly shows your subject and overall scene style. A 16:9 composition works well for cinematic results.

Open LtxApi25ImageToVideo and add your API credentials if required. Configure generation options as exposed by the node (e.g., enable native multishot, keep automatic duration on, or set a target duration if you prefer manual control).

Optionally refine settings that affect pacing and look if available in your template (such as number of shots, motion intensity, aspect, or repeatability controls). Keep defaults for a fast first pass.
Run the workflow. The node will upload your image and settings, generate a multi-shot sequence via the LTX-2.5 model, and return a video clip.
In SaveVideo, choose the output path, filename, and frame rate. Execute to write the final video file to disk, then review and iterate on the input image or node settings as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid storyboarding: visualize coverage and pacing from a single concept frame.
Social media teasers or reels that need consistent character and style across quick cuts.
Pre-visualization for ads or product spots using one hero image to explore camera moves.
Look development: test lighting, color, and motion language before a full production.
Mood films or pitch videos generated swiftly from key art.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key and is processing local?
faqItems.answer: LtxApi25ImageToVideo calls a remote service; most deployments require an API key. Your source image and parameters are sent to the provider for generation. Check the node’s credentials field and the provider’s documentation and terms before use.

faqItems.question: Can I control duration and the number of shots?
faqItems.answer: The node supports native multishot and automatic duration prediction. If your template exposes overrides, you can set a target duration and/or shot count; otherwise, leave auto duration enabled for best pacing.

faqItems.question: What image works best as input?
faqItems.answer: Use a clean, high-quality image with clear subject separation and coherent lighting. Keep faces unobstructed, avoid heavy motion blur, and compose for the aspect ratio you plan to export (16:9 is a solid default).

faqItems.question: How does the workflow keep characters and style consistent across cuts?
faqItems.answer: All shots are conditioned on the same input image inside the LTX-2.5 model via the LtxApi25ImageToVideo node. This shared conditioning helps preserve character identity, lighting, and overall style from shot to shot.

6268b5850a94.title: Video Segmentation: SAM3
6268b5850a94.description: Use the SAM3 model to segment the main subject or content from a video, isolating specific objects or regions. Input a video and receive a segmented mask output.
6268b5850a94.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Segment subjects from video with SAM3 using text prompts, preview masks, and export results. Supports multi-object prompts with counts.
6268b5850a94.extendedDescription:
This workflow demonstrates end-to-end video segmentation with the SAM3 model in ComfyUI. It takes a video input, detects and isolates subjects you describe in text, and produces a per-frame segmentation mask you can preview or export. The processing graph is simple and readable: LoadVideo decodes frames, the SAM3 Segmenter node (a6f60fa7-1c86-4060-bf6f-01a10288e343) runs text-prompted segmentation on each frame, and MaskPreview lets you visually inspect masks as an overlay or standalone mask. A MarkdownNote in the canvas provides quick guidance and links.

Under the hood, the SAM3 node loads the Comfy-Org/sam3.1 weights (e.g., sam3.1_multiplex_fp16.safetensors) and applies prompt-based segmentation with a strict 32-token prompt limit. You can target multiple subjects in a single pass by separating prompts with commas and constraining the number of detected instances per subject via :N syntax (for example: "eye:2, window panels:4"). This makes it practical to isolate key subjects or repeated elements across a sequence without hand-drawn masks. If you plan to reuse the segmenter in other projects, see the Subgraph feature guide linked in the MarkdownNote—wrapping the SAM3 steps into a Subgraph makes them easy to drop into larger pipelines.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI (drag the JSON onto the canvas or use the Load button).

Download the SAM3 weights (e.g., sam3.1_multiplex_fp16.safetensors) from the linked model pages and place them in your ComfyUI models directory. In the SAM3 Segmenter node (a6f60fa7-1c86-4060-bf6f-01a10288e343), confirm the checkpoint path resolves.
Open LoadVideo and select your input video. Keep in mind that higher resolution videos will take longer and use more VRAM.
In the SAM3 Segmenter node, enter a concise text prompt (max 32 tokens). For multiple subjects and counts, separate with commas and use :N (e.g., "eye:2, window panels:4").
Run the graph. Inspect results in MaskPreview. If masks miss or over-include regions, refine your prompt (short nouns and attributes usually work best) and re-run.
Export the masks: use the preview panel’s save button or add a save node (e.g., SaveImage/SaveVideo) connected to the mask output to write files to disk.
suggestedUseCases: Subject isolation for editorial workflows (keep person/object, replace or blur the background).
Pre-masking for VFX/compositing to speed up roto on specific objects across a shot.
Selective color grading or effects limited to segmented regions (e.g., only the product or clothing).
Rapid dataset preparation: auto-generate per-frame masks for training or evaluation.

faqItems.question: How do I prompt multiple objects or control how many instances are segmented?
faqItems.answer: Separate subjects with commas and set per-subject counts using :N. Example: "eye:2, window panels:4" will segment up to 2 eyes and 4 window panels. Keep the entire prompt within 32 tokens.

faqItems.question: Why does my prompt get cut off or seem ignored?
faqItems.answer: SAM3 enforces a 32-token limit. Use short, specific nouns and attributes (e.g., "red car, person:1") and avoid long sentences. If needed, split tasks into multiple runs with simpler prompts.

faqItems.question: Where do I get the model and which checkpoint should I use?
faqItems.answer: Download from Comfy-Org/sam3.1 (Hugging Face or ModelScope). The workflow is set up for sam3.1_multiplex_fp16.safetensors, which offers reduced memory use and fast inference on modern GPUs.

faqItems.question: How do I save the mask output as a file?
faqItems.answer: Preview results in MaskPreview and use the preview panel’s save option. For automated export, add a SaveImage or SaveVideo node to the mask output and set the output path and format.

62cb2b168265.title: Nano Banana 2 Lite: Image Edit
62cb2b168265.description: Edit an image using Nano Banana 2 Lite, the fastest image generation model from Google’s Gemini series, producing a side-by-side comparison of the original and edited result.
62cb2b168265.metaDescription: Compare before/after image edits using Gemini Nano Banana 2 Lite in ComfyUI. Load, edit, view side-by-side with ImageCompare, and save results.
62cb2b168265.extendedDescription:
This comparison workflow shows a clean, side-by-side view of how Nano Banana 2 Lite (via the GeminiNanoBanana2V2 node) transforms a source image based on your edit instruction. The pipeline loads your original image, applies the edit with the model, and then places the original and result next to each other using ImageCompare so you can quickly judge what changed and what stayed consistent.

Methodologically, the comparison is controlled: both panes derive from the exact same source image (LoadImage), and only the model-driven edit differs. This makes it easy to evaluate trade-offs such as speed versus fidelity, the extent of stylistic drift, and the preservation of structure or identity. Expect Nano Banana 2 Lite to prioritize responsiveness and efficient edits; in practice, that can mean fast, coherent changes for common tasks (color tweaks, small object additions/removals), while very intricate or large, global transformations may require tighter instructions or iterative passes.
howToUse: Load your source image with the LoadImage node and verify resolution/aspect ratio are appropriate for your edit goal.

Open the GeminiNanoBanana2V2 node and enter a clear edit instruction (e.g., "brighten the sky and add warm sunset tones"). Adjust any available parameters relevant to edit scope or quality. If the node requires API credentials, ensure they’re configured.
Run the workflow to generate the edited output from GeminiNanoBanana2V2.
Use the ImageCompare node’s output to review the side-by-side result. Look for preservation of composition/identity, color consistency, edges, and any unintended artifacts.
If needed, refine the instruction (more specific guidance usually reduces drift) and re-run to produce an additional comparison.
Save the comparison and edited image with SaveImageAdvanced, setting your preferred output folder and filename pattern for versioning.
suggestedUseCases: Creative direction reviews: Present before/after boards for quick stakeholder feedback on color grading, style shifts, or minor retouching.
Product photo iterations: Compare subtle edits like background cleanup, glare reduction, or color normalization before publishing.
Marketing variants: Rapidly test small stylistic changes (e.g., warmer tones, light vignette) and choose the most brand-consistent result.
Content quality control: Verify that edits do not introduce artifacts or unwanted changes by inspecting the side-by-side output.

faqItems.question: What exactly is being compared in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow compares the original image (from LoadImage) with the edited image generated by GeminiNanoBanana2V2. ImageCompare places them side-by-side for visual assessment; no numeric metrics are computed.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure a fair, readable comparison?
faqItems.answer: Keep the source image constant and change only the edit instruction or a single parameter at a time. Use consistent output size, and review the same regions (faces, edges, text) for drift or artifacts.

faqItems.question: When should I choose Nano Banana 2 Lite for edits?
faqItems.answer: Choose it when you need fast, coherent edits to an existing image—such as color tweaks, lighting adjustments, or minor object-level changes—where turnaround speed is important.

faqItems.question: Why does the edit sometimes alter areas I didn’t mention?
faqItems.answer: Under-specified instructions can lead to broader changes. Make your intent explicit (what to change and what to keep), and iterate with more targeted guidance to reduce unintended drift.

6332ca621968.title: Qwen-Image 2512 Turbo
6332ca621968.description: Qwen-Image 2512 Image generation with 2-steps Turbo LoRA. Input your text prompt to quickly produce a result, though some quality is sacrificed for speed.
6332ca621968.metaDescription: Quickly generate images from text prompts with Qwen-Image 2512 Turbo. Fast results with a focus on speed over quality.
6332ca621968.extendedDescription:
The Qwen-Image 2512 Turbo workflow is designed for rapid image generation using a streamlined process that leverages the Qwen-Image 2512 model. This workflow is particularly useful for users who need quick visual outputs from text prompts, albeit with a slight compromise on image quality to achieve faster results. The workflow integrates several key nodes, such as the VAELoader, CLIPLoader, and UNETLoader, which are essential for loading and processing the model components. The KSampler node plays a crucial role in generating latent images, while the LoraLoaderModelOnly node is used to apply LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) techniques to enhance the model's efficiency.

This workflow operates in three main steps: loading the necessary models, setting the image size, and processing the text prompt. The ModelSamplingAuraFlow node is crucial for sampling and refining the image output, ensuring that the final result aligns with the user's prompt. By utilizing the CLIPTextEncode node, the workflow effectively translates text prompts into visual concepts, which are then decoded into images using the VAEDecode node. The ConditioningZeroOut node helps in managing the conditioning process, ensuring that the image generation remains consistent and aligned with the input parameters. This workflow is ideal for scenarios where speed is prioritized over high fidelity, making it a practical choice for rapid prototyping and concept visualization.
howToUse: Load the Qwen-Image 2512 Turbo workflow in ComfyUI.
Ensure all necessary models are downloaded and loaded, including VAELoader and CLIPLoader.
Set your desired image size using the provided aspect ratios.
Enter your text prompt in the designated area.
Run the workflow to generate the image.
Save the generated image using the SaveImage node.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid prototyping for fashion photography concepts.
Quick visualization for storyboarding in film and media.
Generating concept art for video games with a focus on speed.
Creating mood boards for marketing and advertising campaigns.
Instant image generation for social media content creation.

faqItems.question: What is the main advantage of using the Qwen-Image 2512 Turbo workflow?
faqItems.answer: The primary advantage is its speed, allowing for quick image generation from text prompts, making it ideal for rapid prototyping and concept visualization.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow compromise on image quality?
faqItems.answer: Yes, to achieve faster results, there is a slight trade-off in image quality. The workflow prioritizes speed over high fidelity.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the image size in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow allows you to set the image size using predefined aspect ratios, ensuring flexibility in output dimensions.

faqItems.question: What models are required for this workflow to function?
faqItems.answer: The workflow requires the Qwen-Image 2512 model, along with VAELoader, CLIPLoader, and other components like UNETLoader and LoraLoaderModelOnly.

6349eb001d4b.title: Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo: Text to Image
6349eb001d4b.description: Generate images from text prompts with Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo, the 8-step accelerated checkpoint, producing a single 1024×1024 image in 8 sampling steps. Same model family with native 2K output, professional typography, and alpha-channel support, plus an optional Qwen 3.5 prompt enhancer. Ideal for poster and layout design, transparent asset creation, and rapid concept visualization.

63cbc1ad946c.title: LTX-2 Image to Video (Distilled)
63cbc1ad946c.description: Transform static images into dynamic videos with synchronized audio-video generation using LTX-2 distilled model. Optimized for faster generation while maintaining quality. Features expressive lip sync, natural motion, and improved speed.
63cbc1ad946c.metaDescription: Animate a still image into video with LTX-2 (distilled) in ComfyUI. Fast, natural motion and lip sync. Validates sizes, saves MP4, and supports audio when available.
63cbc1ad946c.extendedDescription: This ComfyUI workflow turns a single still image into a dynamic video using the distilled LTX-2 model from Lightricks. It wraps the animation pipeline inside a Subgraph node (b7c2d337-c38d-4c04-922b-2d638449d13e) so you can focus on prompting and parameters instead of wiring low-level components. Your source is loaded with LoadImage, conformed to a video-safe size using ResizeImageMaskNode, then animated by the LTX-2 Distilled Subgraph, which generates temporally coherent frames with expressive motion and lip sync. The resulting video (and audio, when provided by the model) is written to disk with SaveVideo. A MarkdownNote in the canvas provides inline guidance and links to Subgraph docs to help you understand and customize the encapsulated graph.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then confirm the LTX-2 distilled Subgraph node (b7c2d337-c38d-4c04-922b-2d638449d13e) and SaveVideo are present. Read the MarkdownNote for quick tips and subgraph documentation.

Add or open the LoadImage node and select your source image. If needed, adjust aspect ratio and size in ResizeImageMaskNode. Set width and height to values divisible by 64 (e.g., 1280x768 or 1920x1088).

Open the LTX-2 Distilled Subgraph node and craft the prompt. Follow LTX-2 prompting tips: describe core actions over time, specify visual details, and include audio/dialogue text if you want lip-sync and audio.

Set video parameters in the Subgraph: choose frame count as 8n+1 (e.g., 9, 17, 25, 33), pick FPS, and (optionally) set a seed for reproducibility. Note: if you enter invalid values, the workflow will silently snap to the closest valid settings.
Queue and run the graph. The Subgraph will generate frames (and audio when available) and SaveVideo will write the output (e.g., MP4) to your selected folder.

Review the result. Iterate by refining the prompt (actions, visuals, dialogue), adjusting resolution (default 720p; you can try 1920x1088), and tuning frame count/FPS to balance motion fidelity and speed.
suggestedUseCases: Talking portraits and interview-style clips with expressive lip sync from a single headshot.
Product hero shots that add subtle rotations, camera moves, and environmental motion from a static render.
Music or podcast teasers that animate cover art and synchronize facial movement to spoken lyrics or dialogue prompts.
Comic panels or concept art turned into short animatics to previsualize a scene.
Social media shorts that add life to brand imagery with quick, loopable motion.

faqItems.question: What resolutions and frame counts are valid for LTX-2 in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Set width and height to values divisible by 64 (e.g., 1280x768, 1920x1088). Use a frame count of the form 8n+1 (e.g., 9, 17, 25, 33). If you enter invalid values, the Subgraph will automatically choose the closest valid parameters, so you won’t see an error but your result may not match the exact numbers you typed.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow generate audio and lip sync from text?
faqItems.answer: The LTX-2 distilled Subgraph can produce expressive lip sync when your prompt includes dialogue in the audio section. When the model returns an audio track, SaveVideo will mux it into the output. If your model build/weights do not output audio, you will get a silent video (you can add audio later in an editor).

faqItems.question: How can I improve motion quality without huge render times?
faqItems.answer: Use the distilled model’s default 720p for faster runs, keep prompts precise about actions over time, and choose a moderate frame count like 17 or 25. If you upscale to 1920x1088, expect longer times. For stability, keep the seed fixed while iterating and avoid overly aggressive motion descriptions in a single short clip.

faqItems.question: Why does my output size or frame count not match what I typed?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is designed to be forgiving: it silently snaps to the nearest valid width/height (multiples of 64) and to frame counts of 8n+1. Double-check the Subgraph’s effective settings after running, and adjust your inputs to the nearest valid target if you need a specific result.

6453aedf71ef.title: Vidu: Video Extension
6453aedf71ef.description: Upload a video and use the Vidu Q2 model to extend it up to 7 seconds and enhance the resolution to 1080p.
6453aedf71ef.metaDescription: Extend videos by up to 7 seconds and enhance resolution to 1080p using the Vidu Q2 model in ComfyUI.
6453aedf71ef.extendedDescription: The Vidu: Video Extension workflow is designed to seamlessly extend video content while enhancing its resolution to 1080p. This workflow leverages the Vidu Q2 model, which is specifically tailored for video extension tasks. By utilizing nodes such as ViduExtendVideoNode and LoadVideo, users can upload an existing video and extend its duration by up to 7 seconds. The workflow also includes nodes like GetVideoComponents and SaveVideo to dissect and reassemble the video content efficiently. This process is particularly useful for creators looking to enhance short video clips without compromising on quality. Technically, the workflow dissects the video into frames, applies the Vidu model to generate additional frames, and then reconstructs the extended video. The use of ImageFromBatch and GetImageSize nodes ensures that the output maintains a high resolution, making it ideal for professional video projects.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure all necessary nodes are active.
Use the LoadVideo node to upload your video file.
Configure the ViduExtendVideoNode to set the desired extension duration, up to 7 seconds.
Run the workflow to process the video and generate additional frames using the Vidu Q2 model.
Review the output video in the SaveVideo node, ensuring the resolution is enhanced to 1080p.
Download the extended video from the specified output location.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing short promotional videos for marketing campaigns.
Extending clips for social media content to meet platform requirements.
Improving the visual quality of archival footage for documentaries.

faqItems.question: Does the extended video retain the original audio?
faqItems.answer: No, the extended video will not retain the original audio. You may need to re-add audio in post-production.

faqItems.question: What is the maximum extension duration this workflow supports?
faqItems.answer: The workflow can extend a video by up to 7 seconds.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow to enhance videos beyond 1080p resolution?

faqItems.question: Is it possible to process multiple videos in a batch?
