78347049a7ac.title: Tripo P2: Image to Model
78347049a7ac.description: Generate a production-ready 3D model from a single reference image using Tripo P2.0 Preview, which builds native quad topology with clean edge flow suited for rigging and animation. It takes 1 input image, with optional multi-view references for better side and back accuracy. Ideal for game characters and props, hard-surface mechanical assets, and high-volume real-time pipelines.
78347049a7ac.metaDescription: Turn a single image into a quad-topology 3D model with Tripo P2 in ComfyUI. Texture, rig, retarget, and export as FBX or GLB. Ideal for games and props.
78347049a7ac.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow turns a single reference image into a production-ready 3D asset using the Tripo P2.0 Preview model. Starting with LoadImage, the image feeds into TripoPSeriesImageToModelNode to reconstruct geometry from the front view. You can optionally connect additional side or back views to improve silhouette and surface accuracy. The pipeline then passes through TripoConversionNode, where you control output topology (quads vs. tris), into TripoTextureNodeV2 to generate a clean texture aligned to the mesh.

For animation-ready output, TripoRigNode creates a basic rig and TripoRetargetNode maps it to a target skeleton for your engine or DCC. Save3DAdvanced handles export: when the quad option is enabled, connect its right slot to export FBX; when disabled, export GLB. Together, these nodes build native quad topology with clean edge flow suited for rigging and animation, making this ideal for game characters and props, hard-surface assets, and fast real-time pipelines.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and enable the Tripo Toolset group (select the group and press Ctrl+B). Ensure ComfyUI is up to date and required Tripo models/dependencies are installed.

Load your main reference with LoadImage (try the included designer_toy_3d.png). For better side/back accuracy, plug additional view images into the extra inputs on TripoPSeriesImageToModelNode if provided.
Run TripoPSeriesImageToModelNode to reconstruct the base mesh, then use TripoConversionNode to choose topology. Enable quad if you plan to rig/animate; leave it off if you prefer a compact GLB.
Generate textures with TripoTextureNodeV2. If the node exposes texture settings in your install, choose an appropriate resolution for your target (e.g., game vs. visualization).
For animation, pass the mesh through TripoRigNode to auto-rig, then through TripoRetargetNode to map it to your target skeleton (configure the target rig in the node’s inputs).
Export with Save3DAdvanced. Important: when quad is enabled, connect Save3DAdvanced to the right output slot to write FBX; when quad is disabled, export GLB. Inspect the result in your DCC or engine.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid prototyping of game-ready characters or props from a single concept or photo.
Creating clean quad-topology assets for rigging and animation in film, TV, or indie projects.
Turning product photos into textured 3D for e-commerce, AR previews, or marketing visuals.
Generating hard-surface mechanical assets with consistent edge flow for subdivision and deformation.
High-volume real-time pipelines where consistent topology, quick texturing, and automated rigging are essential.

faqItems.question: Do I need multiple images to get a good model?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow works from a single front reference via TripoPSeriesImageToModelNode. Providing optional side/back views can improve silhouette and backside accuracy, especially for asymmetric or complex assets.

faqItems.question: How do I choose between FBX and GLB export?
faqItems.answer: Use TripoConversionNode to toggle quad topology. If quad is enabled, connect Save3DAdvanced to the right output slot to export FBX. If quad is disabled, export GLB. This ensures correct format for your topology choice.

faqItems.question: Can I rig and retarget the generated model?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Use TripoRigNode to auto-rig the mesh, then TripoRetargetNode to map it to your target skeleton. This is ideal for getting animation-ready characters or props into your DCC or game engine quickly.

faqItems.question: How can I improve texture and geometry quality?
faqItems.answer: Provide a sharp, front-facing main image with even lighting and minimal occlusion. Add side/back views when available. In TripoTextureNodeV2, pick an appropriate texture size for your target; higher resolutions capture finer detail at the cost of file size.

787cfd599758.title: MiniMax: Text to Video
787cfd599758.description: Generate high-quality videos directly from text prompts. Explore MiniMax's advanced AI capabilities to create diverse visual narratives with professional CGI effects and stylistic elements to bring your descriptions to life.
787cfd599758.metaDescription: ComfyUI MiniMax text-to-video tutorial: set up the API node, craft prompts, and save high-quality clips with SaveVideo in a secure environment.
787cfd599758.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial walks you through a minimal, reliable text-to-video pipeline powered by the MiniMax API. The core of the workflow is the MinimaxTextToVideoNode, which sends your text prompt to MiniMax’s text-to-video service and returns a generated video clip. A MarkdownNote node is included in the graph to remind you of the provider’s secure network requirements (localhost access, HTTPS usage, and ensuring you can reach the API). Finally, a SaveVideo node writes the returned clip to disk so you can review and reuse it in your projects.

Technically, the MinimaxTextToVideoNode handles the API call and response lifecycle inside ComfyUI. You supply the prompt (and any parameters the node exposes, such as clip length or resolution if available), the node waits for the remote job to complete, and then forwards the resulting video to SaveVideo. SaveVideo stores the clip in your ComfyUI output directory using the file name settings you configure. Because inference happens on the MiniMax service, local GPU requirements are minimal—the main considerations are correct API credentials/configuration and meeting the secure networking rules noted in the MarkdownNote.
howToUse: Load the MiniMax: Text to Video workflow JSON into ComfyUI and confirm the MinimaxTextToVideoNode, SaveVideo, and MarkdownNote nodes appear.
Open the MarkdownNote and review the secure environment requirements: run from localhost (127.0.0.1), use HTTPS for web services, and ensure you can reach the MiniMax API.
Select the MinimaxTextToVideoNode and enter your text prompt. If the node exposes fields like duration or resolution, set them as needed. Add your API credentials/endpoint if required.
Configure the SaveVideo node: choose a clear filename prefix and (if available) format settings so your clip is written to the desired output folder.
Click Queue Prompt (or Run) in ComfyUI. Wait for the node to complete the API job and for SaveVideo to write the resulting video.
Open the saved file from the ComfyUI output directory to review. Iterate on your prompt and node parameters to refine motion, style, and composition.
suggestedUseCases: Creating quick concept animations for storyboards or previsualization.
Generating short social media clips with distinct stylistic directions (e.g., cinematic, CGI-inspired).
Producing motion references for VFX and motion design teams during early ideation.
Exploring narrative variations rapidly by iterating on text prompts.
Building a prompt library for consistent brand or artistic looks across multiple clips.

faqItems.question: Do I need a powerful GPU to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No. The MinimaxTextToVideoNode calls the MiniMax API for generation, so heavy compute happens remotely. Your local machine only needs to run ComfyUI and maintain a network connection.

faqItems.question: Why does the node fail or time out?
faqItems.answer: Common causes are networking or credential issues. Confirm you meet the secure environment requirements (localhost access or HTTPS for web services), your API key/endpoint are correct, and your firewall allows outbound requests to the MiniMax API.

faqItems.question: How can I control duration, resolution, or aspect ratio?
faqItems.answer: Use any parameters the MinimaxTextToVideoNode exposes in your workflow. If a setting isn’t available in the node UI, consult the MiniMax provider docs for supported options. Some services may also respect prompt cues (e.g., 9:16) but this is not guaranteed.

faqItems.question: How do I get cleaner, more on-style results?
faqItems.answer: Write specific prompts that include subject, action, environment, and style cues (e.g., cinematic lighting, stylized CGI). Keep motions simple for short clips, avoid overly rapid scene changes, and iterate in small steps. If the node supports it, adjust duration and other parameters conservatively.

7905fe6d550c.title: FLUX.2 [max]: Object Swap
7905fe6d550c.description: Replace objects in images with unmatched quality using FLUX.2 [max]. Perfect for product photography, furniture swaps, and maintaining scene consistency with highest editing precision.
7905fe6d550c.metaDescription: Effortlessly swap objects in images with FLUX.2 [max] for high-quality edits in product photography and more.
7905fe6d550c.extendedDescription:
The FLUX.2 [max]: Object Swap workflow is designed to seamlessly replace objects within images while preserving the overall scene consistency and quality. At the heart of this workflow is the Flux2MaxImageNode, which leverages advanced image processing techniques to ensure precise object swaps. The Flux2MaxImageNode then performs the object swap by identifying and replacing the target object with unmatched precision. The GetImageSize node ensures that the dimensions of the images are consistent throughout the process, while the BatchImagesNode allows for processing multiple images simultaneously, making it efficient for bulk tasks. Finally, the SaveImage node outputs the edited image, ready for use in various applications.
howToUse: Load the image you want to edit using the LoadImage node.
Configure the Flux2MaxImageNode to select the object you wish to replace and the new object to insert.
Use the GetImageSize node to ensure image dimensions are consistent.
For batch processing, add multiple images to the BatchImagesNode.
Execute the workflow to perform the object swap.
Save the edited image using the SaveImage node.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing product photography by swapping out old models with new ones.
Updating interior design images with new furniture without reshooting.
Creating consistent image catalogs with updated products.
Experimenting with different object placements in marketing materials.
Maintaining scene consistency in film and video production stills.

faqItems.question: What types of objects can be swapped using this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow can swap any object as long as the replacement object is compatible in size and perspective with the original scene.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow handle multiple images at once?
faqItems.answer: Yes, by using the BatchImagesNode, you can process multiple images simultaneously, making it ideal for bulk editing tasks.

faqItems.question: Is the original image quality preserved after editing?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the Flux2MaxImageNode is designed to maintain high image quality, ensuring that the edited image is as sharp and clear as the original.

faqItems.question: Do I need any specific skills to use this workflow?

79227f845a2c.title: Reve: Text to Image

7952ece08bbb.title: Arrow2: Image to SVG
7952ece08bbb.description: Convert a raster image into a clean, editable SVG vector using Arrow 2, taking one image and returning one vector output. The model produces cleaner geometry and stronger composition with fewer control points. Ideal for vectorizing sketches, logos, and line art, or preparing scalable brand and product assets.
7952ece08bbb.metaDescription: Convert raster images to clean, editable SVGs in ComfyUI using Arrow 2 (QuiverImageToSVGNode) and SaveSVGNode—perfect for logos, sketches, and brand assets.
7952ece08bbb.extendedDescription:
Arrow2: Image to SVG is a focused ComfyUI workflow that converts a single raster image into a clean, editable SVG vector. It routes your bitmap through LoadImage, vectorizes it with QuiverImageToSVGNode (powered by the Arrow 2 model), and writes the result to disk via SaveSVGNode. The Arrow 2 model is tuned for cleaner geometry and stronger composition, producing fewer control points and more usable paths than traditional auto-tracing.

Under the hood, QuiverImageToSVGNode analyzes edges and regions in the input image and emits a single SVG document composed of paths and shapes. Because the output is vector-based, it scales losslessly and is ideal for logos, icons, sketches, and brand assets. SaveSVGNode persists the SVG to your ComfyUI output folder, while the MarkdownNote node in the graph provides inline tips and a sample file link to help you get started quickly.
howToUse: Open ComfyUI and load the 'Arrow2: Image to SVG' workflow JSON.
In the LoadImage node, select your source image (use the provided retro_office_car_scene.png to test, or drop in your own logo/sketch).
Optionally prepare your image beforehand for best results: crop tightly, increase contrast, remove noisy backgrounds, and use solid fills for logos.
Queue/Run the workflow. QuiverImageToSVGNode will vectorize the bitmap into a single SVG document.
After the run completes, open the file path shown in SaveSVGNode to find your .svg, then view or edit it in a vector editor (e.g., Illustrator, Inkscape, Figma).
Iterate: if the SVG is too complex or noisy, refine the source image (clean edges, simplify colors, adjust resolution) and run again.
suggestedUseCases: Logo and icon vectorization for scalable branding assets.
Digitizing hand-drawn sketches and line art into editable paths.
Preparing product marks, decals, and packaging graphics for print at any size.
Creating clean vectors for CNC, laser cutting, and vinyl plotting workflows.
Upgrading low-resolution graphics into crisp, resolution-independent SVGs.

faqItems.question: What kinds of images work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: High-contrast graphics with clear edges—such as logos, icons, and line art—vectorize best. Photos and gradients can produce many small shapes; simplify or posterize them first for cleaner results.

faqItems.question: Where is the SVG saved?
faqItems.answer: SaveSVGNode writes the output to your ComfyUI output directory. The exact path is shown in the node’s UI after the run; open that folder to access the .svg file.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce the number of points or simplify the result?
faqItems.answer: Start by improving the input: increase contrast, remove noise, and use solid color regions. You can also resize the image smaller before running. After export, apply path simplification in your vector editor if needed.

faqItems.question: Does it preserve colors and transparency?
faqItems.answer: Arrow 2 can capture distinct regions as vector shapes. Solid colors and flat graphics are preserved more cleanly than soft gradients. Transparency handling depends on the source; a clean, uniform background yields the best separation.

795f78f5c9cb.title: Chatter Box: Multi-Speaker Conversation with Cloned Voices

suggestedUseCases: Creating realistic audio for podcasts with multiple speakers.
Producing audiobooks with distinct character voices.
Developing interactive voice applications or virtual assistants.
Generating personalized voicemail messages.
Simulating customer service interactions for training purposes.

faqItems.question: How long should the voice samples be?

faqItems.question: Can I edit the dialog script after uploading?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can edit the dialog script in the FL_ChatterboxDialogTTS node before generating the audio.

faqItems.question: What format is the final audio file saved in?
faqItems.answer: The final audio file is saved in MP3 format using the SaveAudioMP3 node.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to adjust the voice characteristics?
faqItems.answer: Currently, the workflow focuses on cloning the provided voice samples without additional voice characteristic adjustments.

7a6ab8b6e694.title: VFX - Bullet Time Effect
7a6ab8b6e694.description: Upload an image or describe a scene, then get **one optimized prompt** built to reproduce the bullet time effect: **frozen action, slow-motion energy, and a cinematic camera orbit around the subject**.
7a6ab8b6e694.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate a Seedance 2.0 bullet time video from an image or text using Gemini for prompt crafting and ByteDance reference video generation.
7a6ab8b6e694.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds a convincing bullet time sequence from either a reference image or a plain-text scene description. It does this in two stages. First, the Generate Bullet Time Seedance 2.0 Prompt group uses a GeminiNode to synthesize a single, highly focused prompt that emphasizes frozen action, slow‑motion energy, and a cinematic orbit around your subject. If you load a still via LoadImage, that visual context informs the prompt; otherwise, the node relies purely on your text description. A MarkdownNote in the graph explains what the node expects and how to phrase your ideas.

Next, the Generate Video group feeds the optimized prompt (and, when provided, your reference image) into the ByteDance2ReferenceNode, which drives Seedance 2.0 to render the shot. The node is the core video generator: it accepts the guidance prompt and optional reference to anchor subject identity and pose while simulating an orbiting camera and time‑frozen moment. PreviewAny lets you check the output right away, and SaveVideo writes the final clip to disk. The result is a short, loop‑ready bullet time pass you can iterate on quickly by adjusting the prompt, seed, or reference strength.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON titled "VFX - Bullet Time Effect" in ComfyUI. Locate the three groups: Load Images, Generate Bullet Time Seedance 2.0 Prompt, and Generate Video.

Provide your input: either drop a still into the LoadImage node (clear subject, some background margin) or type a concise scene description into the GeminiNode prompt field. Keep it focused on one subject and action to freeze.

Queue the Generate Bullet Time Seedance 2.0 Prompt group. The GeminiNode returns one optimized prompt tuned for the bullet time look (frozen action, slow‑motion energy, orbiting camera). Inspect the generated text if PreviewAny is connected to its output.

Open the ByteDance2ReferenceNode in the Generate Video group. Confirm the optimized prompt is connected and, if you provided an image, that the reference input is wired from LoadImage. Optionally adjust available settings such as duration, resolution, guidance/reference strength, or seed.
Queue the Generate Video group. Watch the clip in PreviewAny; if satisfied, use SaveVideo to export the result to your chosen folder and filename.

Iterate for refinement: tweak the description you give to Gemini (e.g., orbit direction, focal length, debris or confetti suspended), change the seed for variants, or swap the reference image to lock identity and pose more tightly.
suggestedUseCases: Stylized product hero spins where the object appears suspended mid‑air while the camera orbits.
Fashion or portrait bullet time beats for reels or intros that emphasize pose and fabric motion.
Sports action freezes (kick, dunk, serve) that hold the peak moment while circling the athlete.
Fight choreography highlights where the camera wraps around a mid‑strike pose.
Cinematic reveals of gadgets or props with floating particles to sell the time‑stop effect.

faqItems.question: Do I need a reference image, or can it work from text only?

faqItems.question: How do I get a cleaner orbit and fewer artifacts around the subject?

In ByteDance2ReferenceNode, increase reference guidance/strength if available to better anchor identity, and try a different seed for stability. Prompts that explicitly mention orbit direction, focal length (e.g., wide or telephoto), and suspended particles can improve coherence.

faqItems.question: Why doesn’t it do a full 360° around my subject?

faqItems.question: Do I need API keys or special hardware?

Check each node’s docs or your ComfyUI custom node configuration. Because the heavy lifting may be remote, local hardware demands are modest; generation time depends on the service and settings.

7b973ace62af.title: Gemini Omni Flash: Image to Video
7b973ace62af.description: Generate a video from two images using Gemini Omni Flash, which interprets natural language prompts to control duration and aspect ratio. The workflow accepts 2 input images and produces 1 video output. Ideal for creating short brand clips, dynamic social media content, and iterative video edits through conversational prompting.
7b973ace62af.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate a short video from two images with Gemini Omni Flash. Control duration and aspect ratio via prompt. Preview and save the final clip.
7b973ace62af.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns two still images into a short video using Google’s Gemini Omni Flash via the GeminiVideoOmni node. You provide a start image and an end image (two LoadImage nodes), then guide the motion, duration, and framing with a natural-language prompt. A built-in Prompt Constructor subgraph (custom node: b83478ba-1f3e-4e62-9869-c8a0c8e9a5f5) helps you explicitly include the required duration and aspect ratio in the final prompt string—both are mandatory for Gemini Omni Video. The GeminiVideoOmni node then generates a single video clip that you can preview with PreviewAny and export with SaveVideo.

Technically, the workflow wires your two image tensors and the constructed text prompt into GeminiVideoOmni, which requests a video from the Gemini Omni Flash model. Duration and aspect ratio are parsed from the prompt (for example: "duration: 4s, aspect_ratio: 16:9"), while the rest of your text describes the motion (e.g., zooms, pans, morphs, reveals). The MarkdownNote nodes embedded in the graph provide quick reminders and tips as you work. The result is a fast, conversational way to iterate on short brand clips, vertical social posts, and before/after reveals—without manual keyframing.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and review the MarkdownNote tips to understand required inputs and prompt format.
Load your two images: connect the first LoadImage node to your starting frame and the second LoadImage node to your ending frame (recommended: similar framing and resolution).

Open the Prompt Constructor subgraph (custom node b83478ba-1f3e-4e62-9869-c8a0c8e9a5f5). Set duration (e.g., 3s, 5s) and aspect ratio (e.g., 16:9, 9:16), then write a clear motion description. Example: "duration: 4s, aspect_ratio: 9:16. Smooth vertical reveal transitioning from the first image to the second with a gentle camera push-in."

Confirm the Prompt Constructor output feeds into GeminiVideoOmni along with both image inputs. If required by your setup, ensure Gemini API credentials are configured for the GeminiVideoOmni node/extension.
Queue the workflow. Watch the output in PreviewAny once the generation completes. If the motion or framing isn’t right, adjust the prompt (especially duration/aspect_ratio) and re-run.
When satisfied, set the file path/options in SaveVideo and run again to export the final clip.
suggestedUseCases: Brand logo stingers that transition from a product shot to a branded end card.
Before-and-after reveals for marketing, beauty, home improvement, or restoration.

Quick A/B variations of a motion concept by iterating with conversational prompts.

faqItems.question: How do I control video duration and aspect ratio?

7cecbe192fc2.extendedDescription:

It ingests your video with VHS_LoadVideo, trims the timeline using skip_first_frames and frame_count, and then routes the frames through the LTX 2.3 inference group (node id: 2e37ecc9-770a-4ac2-972c-e953901f49d3), where the Googlyeyes LoRA is loaded over the LTX‑Video 2.3 base model. Finally, VHS_VideoCombine reassembles the processed frames back into a video at the original frame rate.

Technically, the pipeline is video‑to‑video: frames decoded by VHS_LoadVideo are processed in sequence by the LTX 2.3 node that applies the LoRA to emphasize and transform eye regions while preserving overall scene structure. Because it runs through a video‑aware model pipeline, the effect tends to remain consistent across adjacent frames. The simple set of controls—especially skip_first_frames and frame_count—makes it practical to target only the part of the timeline you want, saving VRAM and time on longer clips.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure required components are available: Video Helper Suite (VHS_LoadVideo and VHS_VideoCombine) and an LTX‑Video 2.3 pipeline node. Confirm the LTX‑Video 2.3 base model and TheBurgstall “Googlyeyes” LoRA are installed and selectable in the LTX node/group (id: 2e37ecc9-770a-4ac2-972c-e953901f49d3).

Open the VHS_LoadVideo node and choose your source clip. Set skip_first_frames to trim the start of the clip, and set frame_count to the number of frames you want processed (for example, skip_first_frames: 60 and frame_count: 480 to process frames 60–540 of a 600‑frame clip).

In the LTX 2.3 node/group, select the LTX‑Video 2.3 base model and the Googlyeyes LoRA by TheBurgstall. If a LoRA weight/strength control is available, start at 1.0; reduce it for a subtler effect or increase slightly if the eyes aren’t pronounced enough.
Leave other LTX settings at their defaults for a first pass. For longer or high‑resolution videos, consider testing a short segment first by lowering frame_count to verify quality and VRAM usage.
Verify that the output of the LTX node routes into VHS_VideoCombine. Confirm the frame rate is coming from VHS_LoadVideo and set an output filename/preset if exposed by your VHS_VideoCombine version.
Click Queue Prompt to render. When complete, find the resulting video in your ComfyUI output directory. Review and, if needed, adjust LoRA strength or trim controls and re‑queue.
suggestedUseCases: Quick comedic edits for social media or reaction videos where exaggerated googly eyes boost humor.
Lightweight creative masking over faces for internal demos or drafts (not a privacy or de‑identification solution).
Kids’ content and classroom projects that benefit from playful visual effects without complex editing.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce VRAM usage or speed up processing?

7dca0438edf4.title: Adjustment Frame Workflow
7dca0438edf4.description: A Director-style AI workflow that generates a shot, refines camera angle, and produces multiple video takes across top models so you can quickly choose the best result.
7dca0438edf4.metaDescription: Director-style ComfyUI workflow to block a shot, refine camera angle, and generate multiple video takes via Grok, Kling, and Gemini—then pick the best.
7dca0438edf4.extendedDescription:
The Adjustment Frame Workflow is a director-style pipeline for turning a written shot idea into multiple polished video takes you can compare side-by-side. It stages your work like a real set: first you block the shot as a still, then you refine the camera, and finally you roll multiple takes across different model backends. A Text Multiline node captures your prompt (what the image is and the action you want), and the 1A) GENERATE SHOT STILL group produces a reference frame you can review with PreviewImage/PreviewAny before spending any credits.

Next, the 1B) CONTROL CAMERA ANGLE group routes your shot through QwenMultiangleCameraNode to generate camera-aware variations (e.g., wide vs. close-up, low vs. high angle, focal length cues). Utility nodes like RegexExtract and ComfyMathExpression help parse camera directions from your text and normalize values like duration, fps, or resolution. In 2) GENERATE VIDEO(S), you can send the approved composition to one or more API partners—GrokVideoNode, KlingVideoNode, and GeminiNode—optionally anchoring identity or style via ByteDance2ReferenceNode. Image Resize ensures each model receives a compatible resolution, PreviewAny lets you compare takes interactively, and SaveVideo writes out the best result. SetNode/GetNode pass key parameters between groups so your shot intent, camera notes, and timing remain consistent. This workflow is especially useful because you only “roll” once you like the frame and angle—preventing credit waste while getting clear, comparable outputs from top models.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the DIRECTOR'S CHAIR notes to skim the instructions. In the Text Multiline node, describe the subject and the action you want to see.
Run only the 1A) GENERATE SHOT STILL group to create a reference frame. Use PreviewImage/PreviewAny to check composition, subject, and style. Do not press Play on the whole graph yet.

Adjust camera intent in 1B) CONTROL CAMERA ANGLE. In QwenMultiangleCameraNode, add cues like shot size (wide/medium/close-up), angle (low/high/eye-level), and lens hints (24mm/50mm). Re-run 1A/1B until the still and angle look right.

Set technical parameters: use PrimitiveInt and ComfyMathExpression nodes to define clip length/fps or number of takes; match each model’s preferred resolution with Image Resize. If you need character or style consistency, connect a reference image to ByteDance2ReferenceNode.
Enable one video backend at a time in 2) GENERATE VIDEO(S) (e.g., GrokVideoNode, KlingVideoNode, or GeminiNode). These API partner nodes consume credits—verify you have credits before running.
Press Play to generate your first take. Compare outputs in PreviewAny, switch or tweak nodes as needed, and repeat per model. When satisfied, send the chosen take to SaveVideo to export.
suggestedUseCases: Previsualization for directors: quickly test camera angles and motion before a live shoot.
Storyboarding: turn a written beat into multiple angle options to align a team.
Product and explainer clips: lock composition with a still, then iterate motion across models.
Social media content: A/B test tone, pacing, and framing for Reels/TikTok/Shorts.
Character consistency tests: use ByteDance2ReferenceNode to keep a subject’s look stable across takes.

faqItems.question: Which nodes require credits, and how do I avoid wasting them?
faqItems.answer: The API partner nodes—GrokVideoNode, KlingVideoNode, and GeminiNode—consume credits. ByteDance2ReferenceNode typically pairs with an external generation call as well. Work only inside 1A/1B first (local and free nodes like PreviewImage, PreviewAny, Image Resize, ComfyMathExpression, SetNode/GetNode) until your still frame and camera angle are locked. Then enable a single video node and render.

faqItems.question: How do I control the camera angle and framing?
faqItems.answer: Use QwenMultiangleCameraNode in 1B) CONTROL CAMERA ANGLE. Add clear cues such as shot size (e.g., "medium shot"), angle ("low angle"), lens ("35mm"), and motion intent ("slow dolly-in"). RegexExtract helps parse these from your text, and the node produces consistent camera-aware variations you can preview before video generation.

faqItems.question: Can I change video length and resolution?
faqItems.answer: Yes. PrimitiveInt and ComfyMathExpression nodes set timing values like duration/fps. Use Image Resize to match model-specific resolution requirements. Note that supported lengths vary by model—some allow longer clips than others—so check each node’s limits and adjust accordingly.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the subject’s look consistent across takes?
faqItems.answer: Provide a clean, well-lit still as a reference and route it through ByteDance2ReferenceNode before your chosen video backend. Keep the composition similar to your approved still, and avoid large mid-scene camera changes. Small prompt changes can shift identity—lock your description once the still is approved.

7e47ce4777e7.extendedDescription:
The Tripo3.0: Image to Model workflow is designed to seamlessly transform 2D images or sketches into detailed 3D models. This workflow leverages the power of the Tripo model, renowned for its sharp geometry and production-ready PBR (Physically Based Rendering) textures, making it an excellent choice for both hobbyists and professionals in the 3D modeling field. The process begins with the 'LoadImage' node, which imports your 2D image or sketch into the workflow. The 'TripoImageToModelNode' then takes center stage, converting the flat image into a 3D model with remarkable precision.

Once the initial model is created, the workflow employs a series of specialized nodes to refine and enhance the model. The 'TripoRefineNode' ensures that the geometry is sharp and accurate, while the 'TripoTextureNode' applies high-quality textures that are ready for production use. For those looking to animate their models, the 'TripoRigNode' and 'TripoRetargetNode' provide robust rigging and retargeting capabilities. Finally, the 'SaveGLB' node allows users to export their models in the GLB format, suitable for a wide range of applications. This comprehensive workflow not only simplifies the process of creating 3D models from 2D images but also ensures that the output is of high quality and ready for immediate use in various digital environments.
howToUse: Load your 2D image or sketch using the 'LoadImage' node.
Connect the image to the 'TripoImageToModelNode' to generate a 3D model.
Use the 'TripoRefineNode' to enhance the model's geometry.
Apply textures with the 'TripoTextureNode' for a polished finish.
Rig and retarget animations using 'TripoRigNode' and 'TripoRetargetNode'.
Export the final model with the 'SaveGLB' node for use in various applications.
suggestedUseCases: Create detailed 3D models for video game assets from concept art.
Transform architectural sketches into 3D visualizations for presentations.
Generate production-ready models for use in virtual reality environments.
Design custom 3D printed objects from hand-drawn sketches.
Develop animated characters for film and television using rigging and retargeting features.

faqItems.question: What types of images work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: High-contrast sketches or detailed images with clear outlines work best, as they provide more information for the model conversion process.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for creating animated models?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow includes 'TripoRigNode' and 'TripoRetargetNode' for rigging and retargeting, making it suitable for animation projects.

faqItems.question: What file format does the workflow export?
faqItems.answer: The workflow exports models in the GLB format, which is widely used for 3D applications and supports PBR textures.

faqItems.question: Is prior 3D modeling experience required to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No, the workflow is designed to be user-friendly, with nodes that automate much of the complex modeling process, making it accessible to beginners.

7ef74d9a1c56.title: Meshy 7: Image to 3D
7ef74d9a1c56.description: Turn a single image into a production-ready 3D model with Meshy 7, generating a textured mesh that faithfully mirrors your reference's geometry, proportions, and surface details. Ideal for character busts that preserve facial expression, complex mechanical assemblies with correctly placed parts, and dense surface relief like engraved coins or ornate props.
7ef74d9a1c56.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow: convert a single image into a textured 3D GLB with Meshy. Reconstruct, refine, texture, and optionally rig/animate—ideal for busts and props.
7ef74d9a1c56.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a single reference image into a textured 3D asset using Meshy’s cloud API, all orchestrated inside ComfyUI. It starts with LoadImage to bring in your reference, then MeshyImageToModelNode reconstructs a watertight mesh that matches the image’s silhouette, proportions, and major forms. Next, MeshyRefineNode enhances geometry and surface fidelity, and MeshyTextureNode generates and bakes textures so the result reads well from multiple angles. Finally, SaveGLB writes a ready-to-use GLB to disk.

For character busts, coins, or intricate props, optional rigging and motion are included: MeshyRigModelNode adds a basic skeleton where appropriate, and MeshyAnimateModelNode can generate simple animations from that rig. All Meshy nodes call the Meshy model via API (you’ll need an API key), and are grouped under “Meshy Toolset (select and ctrl-b to enable)” for quick toggling. A MarkdownNote is included in the graph to summarize node roles and tips.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and select the “Meshy Toolset” group frame, then press Ctrl+B to enable it.
Open each Meshy node (MeshyImageToModelNode, MeshyRefineNode, MeshyTextureNode, etc.) and set your Meshy API credentials as required. Ensure you’re online.
Use LoadImage to point to input/marble_robot_bust.png (included) or replace it with your own clean, front-facing reference image.
Run MeshyImageToModelNode to generate the initial 3D model from the image. Inspect intermediate outputs or proceed directly to refinement.
Trigger MeshyRefineNode to improve topology and detail, then run MeshyTextureNode to bake textures onto the mesh.
Optionally, run MeshyRigModelNode and MeshyAnimateModelNode for characters that need motion. Use SaveGLB to export the final textured (and optionally rigged) model.
suggestedUseCases: Character busts that preserve facial expression and likeness for look-dev or previs
Mechanical props and assemblies with correctly placed parts for product visuals
Engraved coins, reliefs, and ornate surfaces that need dense surface detail
Collectibles and figurines modeled from concept art for quick iteration
Stylized hero props for games, cinematics, or marketing stills

faqItems.question: What do I need to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: An active internet connection and a Meshy API key. Enter your credentials in the Meshy nodes. ComfyUI must be up to date, and the Meshy nodes need to be installed/enabled.

faqItems.question: How can I get the best reconstruction from a single image?
faqItems.answer: Use a high-resolution, front-facing image with minimal occlusion and a clean background. Keep the subject centered, well-lit, and avoid motion blur. After the initial build, run MeshyRefineNode before texturing for sharper forms and surface detail.

faqItems.question: What does the workflow export?
faqItems.answer: SaveGLB writes a textured GLB. The mesh and baked textures from MeshyTextureNode are included, making the file portable for DCCs, engines, or viewers that support GLB/GLTF.

faqItems.question: Do I have to rig and animate every model?
faqItems.answer: No. Rigging and animation are optional. They work best for character-like subjects. For rigid props or mechanical parts, skip MeshyRigModelNode and MeshyAnimateModelNode—use the refined and textured output instead.

7fb0236e4f28.title: Arrow2: Text to SVG
7fb0236e4f28.description: Generate editable SVG vector graphics directly from text prompts using Arrow 2, producing one image output with no file inputs required. Ideal for illustrations, technical diagrams, logo design, and turning written briefs into clean, scalable vector assets.
7fb0236e4f28.metaDescription: Turn text prompts into editable SVGs in ComfyUI using Arrow 2 with QuiverTextToSVGNode and SaveSVGNode. Ideal for logos, icons, and technical diagrams.
7fb0236e4f28.extendedDescription:
Arrow2: Text to SVG is a focused ComfyUI workflow that converts natural-language prompts into clean, editable vector graphics. It uses QuiverTextToSVGNode to send your prompt to the Arrow 2 text-to-vector model and receive raw SVG markup, then hands that SVG string to SaveSVGNode to write a single .svg file to disk—no image inputs required. Because the output is true SVG, it scales cleanly at any size and is easy to edit in tools like Figma, Illustrator, or Inkscape.

Under the hood, QuiverTextToSVGNode generates an SVG document composed of elements such as <svg>, <path>, <rect>, <circle>, and <polygon> based on your textual instructions (e.g., "flat 2-color icon of a cloud with an up arrow, stroke-only, rounded caps"). SaveSVGNode then persists this vector output with your chosen filename. This setup is ideal for logo ideation, icon sets, technical diagrams, and documentation illustrations where crisp lines, controllable colors, and lightweight files are essential.
howToUse: Load the Arrow2: Text to SVG workflow in ComfyUI.
Open the QuiverTextToSVGNode and enter your text prompt. If required by your setup, provide the Arrow 2 API credentials or endpoint in the node’s configuration.
Refine prompt details to guide structure and style (e.g., specify stroke-only vs. filled shapes, limited color palette with hex codes, geometric or rounded forms, minimal/medium/high detail).
Open SaveSVGNode and set the output filename (ensure the .svg extension) and folder where you want the vector file saved.
Queue and run the workflow. When it finishes, locate the saved SVG in your chosen output directory and open it in a browser or a vector editor to inspect.
Iterate: adjust your prompt to fine-tune composition, color use, and complexity; re-run until you get a clean, on-brief vector result.
suggestedUseCases: Logo and wordmark exploration with quick, scalable vector drafts.
UI iconography and pictograms on consistent grids for web and app design.
Technical diagrams and flowcharts with clear, editable shapes and connectors.
Product manuals and documentation illustrations as crisp line art.
Infographics and schematic figures that remain sharp at any size.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key to use Arrow 2 in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: If your QuiverTextToSVGNode is configured to call an external Arrow 2 API, you’ll need to supply the required credentials (API key or endpoint) in the node settings or environment. Refer to the node’s documentation for the exact configuration method used in your setup.

faqItems.question: Are the outputs true vectors, and how do I scale them?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The node returns standard SVG markup (paths and shapes), so the result is fully vector and resolution-independent. You can scale it by editing the width/height or viewBox attributes in the SVG or by resizing directly in your vector editor.

faqItems.question: How can I control colors, strokes, and overall style?
faqItems.answer: Include specific instructions in your prompt, such as a limited palette with hex codes (e.g., “#111111 and #FF5A5F only”), stroke vs. fill preferences, stroke width, and geometric or rounded aesthetics. You can also fine-tune these later in your vector editor since fills, strokes, and paths are editable.

faqItems.question: The SVG is too complex/heavy. How can I simplify it?
faqItems.answer: Ask for simpler geometry in your prompt (e.g., “minimal paths, few anchor points, no gradients”). After generation, you can further optimize with tools like SVGO or your editor’s path-simplify features to reduce node counts and file size.

80434583707e.title: Wan 2.2 14B Fun Inp
80434583707e.description: Generate videos from start and end frames using Wan 2.2 Fun Inp.
80434583707e.metaDescription: Generate seamless videos from start and end frames using Wan 2.2 Fun Inp in ComfyUI. Perfect for artistic animations and smooth transitions.
80434583707e.extendedDescription: This ComfyUI workflow, titled 'Wan 2.2 14B Fun Inp', is designed to generate videos by interpolating between start and end frames using the Wan 2.2 model. The workflow leverages a series of nodes including CLIPLoader, VAELoader, and ModelSamplingSD3 to load and process the input images, while the WanFunInpaintToVideo node plays a crucial role in creating the video by applying inpainting techniques. The workflow is particularly useful for creating seamless transitions in videos, making it ideal for artistic video projects or animations where smooth morphing between frames is desired. The use of advanced nodes like KSamplerAdvanced and VAEDecode ensures high-quality video output, while the inclusion of LoraLoaderModelOnly allows for flexible model adjustments.
howToUse: Load the Wan 2.2 14B Fun Inp workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadImage node to upload your start and end frames.
Configure video size and length in the corresponding nodes.
Input your desired prompts in the CLIPTextEncode node for video style guidance.
Run the workflow to generate the video, and use SaveVideo to export the result.
suggestedUseCases: Creating artistic animations with smooth transitions between frames.
Generating video content for social media with dynamic visual effects.
Producing educational videos that require visual morphing techniques.
Developing creative video advertisements with unique style transitions.

faqItems.question: What models are used in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow uses the Wan2.2 model along with nodes like CLIPLoader and VAELoader for image processing and video generation.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the video size and length?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow includes nodes for configuring video size and length to suit your VRAM capacity and project needs.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure high-quality video output?
faqItems.answer: Ensure that your input frames are of high quality and use the KSamplerAdvanced and VAEDecode nodes for optimal video processing.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to use different prompts for style guidance?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can input various prompts in the CLIPTextEncode node to guide the video style and appearance according to your preferences.

8108ae4b39c5.title: Image Upscale: Magnific Creative
8108ae4b39c5.description: Upload an image and set the magnification level. Generate an upscaled version of your image with support for up to 16x enlargement.
8108ae4b39c5.metaDescription: Upscale images up to 16x in ComfyUI with Magnific Creative. Load, set magnification, preview side-by-side, and save high-quality results.
8108ae4b39c5.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates creative image upscaling with the Magnific model. Starting from a single input, it produces a high-resolution version at up to 16x enlargement while reconstructing plausible fine details. The core of the graph is the MagnificImageUpscalerCreativeNode, which sends your image and chosen magnification to the Magnific service and returns an upscaled result designed to be both sharp and visually rich.

Technically, the flow is simple and reliable: LoadImage ingests your source file, MagnificImageUpscalerCreativeNode performs the API-based upscale using the Magnific model, ImageCompare lets you review the original and upscaled outputs side-by-side, and SaveImage writes the final image to disk. Because the Magnific upscaler is creatively inclined, it can synthesize detail beyond what’s present in the source while maintaining overall composition, making it useful when conventional interpolation (e.g., bicubic) falls short of producing crisp, print-ready results.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then open the graph to confirm the nodes: LoadImage → MagnificImageUpscalerCreativeNode → ImageCompare and SaveImage.
Open MagnificImageUpscalerCreativeNode and enter your Magnific API key or credentials if required, then set the magnification factor (e.g., 2x, 4x, 8x, or up to 16x).
Use the LoadImage node to pick your source image. For best results, start with the highest-quality version you have (clean, well-exposed, minimal compression).
Queue and run the workflow. The Magnific node will send the image to the API and return the upscaled result.
Inspect the ImageCompare output to evaluate sharpness, texture, and consistency against the original. If needed, adjust the magnification and re-run.
In SaveImage, set a filename prefix (and format if available), then run to write the upscaled image to your ComfyUI output folder.
suggestedUseCases: Preparing large-format prints or posters from smaller originals while maintaining strong perceived detail.
Enhancing product photos for e-commerce listings when re-shooting isn’t possible.
Up-resing concept art, illustrations, or stylized images that benefit from creatively reconstructed textures.
Frame-by-frame upscaling for video pipelines (batching images through the same graph).
Restoring and enlarging legacy assets for presentations or pitch decks.

faqItems.question: What magnification levels are supported?
faqItems.answer: The MagnificImageUpscalerCreativeNode supports up to 16x enlargement. Practical choices are often 2x or 4x for general use; push to 8x–16x when your source is reasonably clean and you need very large outputs.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow require an internet connection or API key?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The MagnificImageUpscalerCreativeNode is API-based and typically requires an active internet connection and valid Magnific credentials. Enter them in the node’s settings if prompted.

faqItems.question: Will the upscaler add or change details?
faqItems.answer: The Magnific Creative upscaler can synthesize plausible fine detail to achieve a sharper look. If you want more conservative results, try lower magnification first or upscale in smaller steps (e.g., 2x → 2x) and compare with ImageCompare.

faqItems.question: How can I get the cleanest results on compressed or noisy images?
faqItems.answer: Start with a modest scale (2x–4x), evaluate with ImageCompare, and only then increase. Heavily compressed or noisy sources benefit from smaller, incremental upscales rather than a single 16x jump.

814fd547d86e.title: Flux.2 [Klein] 4B: Text to Image
814fd547d86e.description: BFL distilled model. Outstanding quality at sub-second speed. Great for real-time generation while retaining quality. Marketing launch will focus on this model.
814fd547d86e.metaDescription: Generate high-quality images from text in real-time using the Flux.2 [Klein] 4B workflow. Ideal for rapid, quality image generation.
814fd547d86e.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow, titled 'Flux.2 [Klein] 4B: Text to Image,' leverages the BFL distilled model to generate high-quality images from text prompts with remarkable speed. The technical foundation of this workflow includes several key nodes: the SaveImage node for outputting generated images, the PrimitiveStringMultiline node for handling text inputs, and the MarkdownNote node for embedding notes and instructions within the workflow. The node identified as '7b34ab90-36f9-45ba-a665-71d418f0df18' plays a crucial role in processing the text input through the Qwen 3.4B text encoder, which is essential for understanding and translating textual descriptions into visual representations. This workflow is particularly useful for users who need to generate images quickly without compromising on quality, such as in marketing or dynamic content creation scenarios.
howToUse: Load the Flux.2 [Klein] 4B workflow into ComfyUI.
Ensure you have the necessary models, such as qwen_3_4b.safetensors, downloaded and configured.
Input your text prompt into the PrimitiveStringMultiline node.
Run the workflow to process the text through the Qwen 3.4B text encoder.
The SaveImage node will output the generated image, ready for use.
suggestedUseCases: Real-time marketing content creation where speed and quality are critical.
Dynamic image generation for interactive applications or games.
Creating visual content for social media platforms that require rapid turnaround.
Developing prototypes or visual drafts for creative projects.
Automating image generation in AI-driven art installations.

faqItems.question: What makes the Flux.2 [Klein] 4B model suitable for real-time generation?
faqItems.answer: The model is designed for high efficiency, allowing it to produce high-quality images in sub-second times, making it ideal for real-time applications.

faqItems.question: Do I need any specific hardware to run this workflow effectively?
faqItems.answer: While the workflow is optimized for speed, a modern GPU is recommended to achieve the best performance and real-time capabilities.

faqItems.question: Can I customize the text prompts for different styles or themes?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the PrimitiveStringMultiline node allows you to input custom text prompts, enabling a wide range of styles and themes in the generated images.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the best image quality with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Ensure that the text prompts are clear and descriptive, and verify that the correct models are loaded and configured properly for optimal results.

81643690b5e9.title: Magnific: Skin Enhancer
81643690b5e9.description: Enhance skin and overall image quality by uploading your image and selecting a preset to adjust lighting, color grading, and realism.
81643690b5e9.metaDescription: Enhance skin and image quality effortlessly with the Magnific: Skin Enhancer workflow. Perfect for portrait enhancements using advanced algorithms.
81643690b5e9.extendedDescription:
The 'Magnific: Skin Enhancer' workflow is designed to improve skin texture and overall image quality with minimal effort. It leverages the MagnificImageSkinEnhancerNode, a specialized node that applies advanced algorithms for skin enhancement, ensuring that the output image maintains a natural and realistic appearance. This workflow is particularly useful for portrait photographers and digital artists who want to enhance their images without compromising on detail or authenticity.

Technically, the workflow begins with the LoadImage node, which allows users to input their desired image. The core enhancement process is handled by the MagnificImageSkinEnhancerNode, where users can select from various presets to adjust lighting, color grading, and realism according to their preference. Once the enhancement is complete, the SaveImage node is used to export the final result. Additionally, the ImageCompare node provides a side-by-side comparison of the original and enhanced images, making it easy to assess the improvements made. This workflow is an invaluable tool for anyone looking to enhance portraits quickly and effectively, without needing extensive post-processing skills.
howToUse: Load your image into the workflow using the LoadImage node.
Select the MagnificImageSkinEnhancerNode and choose a preset that suits your desired enhancement level.
Adjust any additional settings for lighting and color grading if necessary.
Run the workflow to process the image with the selected enhancements.
Use the ImageCompare node to view the original and enhanced images side by side.
Save the enhanced image using the SaveImage node.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing portrait photos for professional photography portfolios.
Improving skin texture and tone in digital art projects.
Quickly adjusting lighting and color grading for social media images.
Refining images for print media with minimal manual editing.
Creating realistic enhancements for character design in gaming.

faqItems.question: Can I customize the presets in the MagnificImageSkinEnhancerNode?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can adjust the presets to fine-tune lighting, color grading, and realism settings to better suit your image.

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for non-portrait images?

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported for input and output?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports common image formats like JPEG and PNG for both input and output, ensuring compatibility with most applications.

faqItems.question: How does the ImageCompare node help in the workflow?
faqItems.answer: The ImageCompare node allows you to see a side-by-side comparison of the original and enhanced images, making it easier to evaluate the changes made.

81ba03930d2b.title: Utility Merge Video
81ba03930d2b.description: Concatenate 2 videos with the Utility Merge Videos (Subgraph).
81ba03930d2b.metaDescription: Concatenate 2 or 4 videos in ComfyUI with a simple subgraph. Load, merge, and save clips end-to-end. Requires matching resolution.
81ba03930d2b.extendedDescription:
Utility Merge Video is a simple, reliable ComfyUI workflow for stitching clips end-to-end. It uses two or four LoadVideo nodes to decode your source files into frame batches, passes them into the Utility Merge Videos (Subgraph) node (ID: fbb76376-8768-4ece-9b41-a646f5e46ac3), and concatenates those frame sequences in order. The merged frames are then written to disk with SaveVideo.

Technically, the subgraph concatenates batches rather than compositing them, so the result plays one clip after another. A switch inside the Utility Merge Videos subgraph lets you choose between 2-input and 4-input modes. All inputs must share the same resolution; otherwise, the graph will error at merge time. The SaveVideo node controls the output file path, format (via extension), and playback FPS; the final FPS you set there determines how the concatenated frames will play back. A MarkdownNote node in the graph provides quick reminders right where you work.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the Utility Merge Videos (Subgraph), LoadVideo nodes, and the SaveVideo node.
In each LoadVideo node, select your source files for Clip A and Clip B (and C, D if needed). Ensure all videos share the same resolution.
Open the Utility Merge Videos (Subgraph) and set its switch to 2-input or 4-input mode. Verify that the inputs (A, B, C, D) are connected in the order you want them to appear.
Open SaveVideo and set the output path and file extension (e.g., .mp4). Choose the target FPS and any quality parameters available in your SaveVideo node.
Queue and run the workflow. ComfyUI will read each source, concatenate the frame batches, and write the merged video to the path you set.
If you encounter a resolution mismatch error, resize your clips beforehand or insert a resize node on each input stream before the subgraph, then re-run.
suggestedUseCases: Join an intro bumper, main segment, and outro into a single deliverable.
Merge AI-generated scene clips from separate runs into one continuous video.
Combine camera takes that were split across multiple files into a single timeline.
Assemble short social posts or stories recorded in parts into one upload-ready clip.
Create a simple before-then-after sequence without using a full video editor.

faqItems.question: Do the input videos need the same resolution and FPS?
faqItems.answer: Resolution must match for all inputs. The final playback FPS comes from the SaveVideo node. If source FPS differs, frames are still concatenated, but the output plays at the SaveVideo FPS you choose.

faqItems.question: How do I change the order of the clips?
faqItems.answer: Connect the LoadVideo outputs to the Utility Merge Videos inputs (A, B, C, D) in the order you want. The subgraph concatenates in that input order.

faqItems.question: Can I keep or merge audio tracks?
faqItems.answer: This workflow focuses on visual frames. Many SaveVideo configurations do not mux audio. If you need audio, remux it in an external tool after export or extend the graph with audio-capable nodes if available in your setup.

faqItems.question: Can I merge more than four videos?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Chain merges by running the workflow multiple times (e.g., merge four clips, then merge the result with more clips) or duplicate the subgraph and build a longer chain.

8200f0fb7636.title: Luma UNI-1: Image Edit
8200f0fb7636.description: Edit existing images with Uni-1's Image Edit mode, preserving composition and core elements. Supports targeted adjustments like lighting and color using prompts and reference images.
8200f0fb7636.metaDescription: Edit images with Luma UNI-1 in ComfyUI. Preserve composition while adjusting lighting, color, and style using prompts and reference images.
8200f0fb7636.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates Luma UNI-1’s Image Edit mode for making controlled changes to an existing image while preserving its composition and key elements. The pipeline is straightforward: LoadImage brings in your source, LumaImageEditNode2 sends that image (plus your text prompt and optional reference images) to Luma’s API for edit inference, and SaveImage writes the result to disk. The LumaImageEditNode2 node is the heart of the flow, applying prompt-driven adjustments such as lighting, color, mood, and minor stylistic shifts without reconstructing the entire scene.

Technically, the Image Edit mode biases the generation toward the input image structure and content. You can modulate how strongly the edit deviates from the original using the node’s edit strength or fidelity controls (naming may vary by version). For style consistency, LumaImageEditNode2 supports multiple reference images with role hints (for example: style, character, color, lighting, composition). Unlike UNI-1’s Create Mode—which produces brand-new compositions—this workflow focuses on targeted adjustments, making it ideal for relighting product photos, harmonizing color palettes, or nudging a photo’s mood while keeping the same subjects and framing.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm LumaImageEditNode2 is installed. Add your Luma API key in the node or environment as required.
Use LoadImage to select your base image. In LumaImageEditNode2, enter a clear edit prompt (e.g., “soft warm golden-hour lighting, subtle teal-orange grade, preserve composition”).
Optionally add reference images to LumaImageEditNode2 (style, lighting, color, character, etc.) and assign roles if the node exposes them. Keep references relevant and consistent.

Tune key parameters in LumaImageEditNode2: lower edit strength/fidelity shift to maintain the original look; increase it for bolder changes. Set seed for repeatability and choose output size/variations if available.
Queue the workflow. Inspect previews and iterate: refine the prompt, adjust strength, or swap references until the balance of preservation and change feels right.
When satisfied, set your desired output path/filename in SaveImage and run again to export the final image.
suggestedUseCases: Product relighting and color harmonization for e-commerce while keeping the same angle and layout.
Portrait and lifestyle photo mood shifts (soften contrast, adjust white balance, gentle skin tone refinement) without changing identity or pose.
Scene and season adjustments for location shots (overcast to sunny, autumn tones, cooler cinematic grade) while preserving composition.
Brand style alignment using reference images to nudge color palettes and lighting across a set of visuals.
Social content cleanup: subtle background de-emphasis, cohesive color grading, and tone matching.

faqItems.question: How do I preserve the original composition and subject identity?
faqItems.answer: Keep the edit strength on the lower side, use prompts that state “preserve composition/subject,” avoid asking for new objects, and rely on reference images only for style or color cues. Use a fixed seed for consistent outcomes during iteration.

faqItems.question: Can I make localized edits with a mask?
faqItems.answer: This template focuses on global edits via LumaImageEditNode2. If your node version supports masks, connect a mask input for targeted changes. Otherwise, consider pre-masking in a separate step or using a mask-capable variant of the node.

faqItems.question: How many reference images can I use and how should I assign roles?
faqItems.answer: LumaImageEditNode2 supports multiple references; the exact number and role fields depend on your installed version. Add only what’s essential (e.g., one for style, one for lighting, one for palette) and label roles to reduce ambiguity.

faqItems.question: What image sizes work best and do I need an API key?
faqItems.answer: Use a reasonable resolution close to your target aspect ratio; very large inputs may be resized by the service. An active Luma API key is required—configure it in the node or your environment before running the workflow.

821350279daf.title: OmniGen2 Text to Image
821350279daf.description: Generate high-quality images from text prompts using OmniGen2's unified 7B multimodal model with dual-path architecture.
821350279daf.metaDescription: Generate high-quality images from text prompts using OmniGen2's advanced multimodal model in this comprehensive ComfyUI workflow tutorial.
821350279daf.extendedDescription:
The OmniGen2 Text to Image workflow leverages the power of the OmniGen2's unified 7B multimodal model to transform text prompts into high-quality images. This workflow is designed to seamlessly interpret textual descriptions and generate visually compelling images that align with the given prompts. At the core of this workflow is the dual-path architecture of OmniGen2, which allows for efficient processing of both text and image data, ensuring that the generated images are not only accurate but also aesthetically pleasing.

Technically, this workflow utilizes several key nodes, including the SaveImage node for storing the generated images, and the MarkdownNote node for embedding notes or instructions within the workflow. Additionally, the node identified by the ID 4b17d220-4312-4981-9eae-9a76bf3b6ec9 plays a crucial role in the image generation process, likely serving as a processing or transformation step. This workflow is particularly useful for artists, designers, and content creators who need to quickly generate visual content from textual ideas, offering a streamlined process from concept to creation.
howToUse: Load the OmniGen2 Text to Image workflow in ComfyUI.
Prepare your text prompt that describes the image you want to generate.
Ensure that the required models, including OmniGen2, are installed and updated.
Run the workflow to process your text prompt and generate the image.
Use the SaveImage node to store your generated image for further use.
Review the MarkdownNote for any additional instructions or notes.
suggestedUseCases: Creating concept art from descriptive text for creative projects.
Generating visual content for marketing materials based on campaign themes.
Producing illustrations for storytelling or educational content.
Designing custom graphics for social media posts from text ideas.
Developing unique visual assets for game design or virtual environments.

faqItems.question: What is the OmniGen2 model used in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: OmniGen2 is a unified 7B multimodal model designed to process and generate high-quality images from text prompts, utilizing a dual-path architecture for efficient data handling.

faqItems.question: Do I need any specific hardware to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: While OmniGen2 is designed to be efficient, a machine with a good GPU is recommended to handle the processing demands of generating high-quality images.

faqItems.question: Can I customize the text prompts for different styles of images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the text prompts can be customized to guide the style and content of the generated images, allowing for a wide range of artistic expressions.

faqItems.question: Where can I find more documentation on using OmniGen2?
