82237f7d19b7.title: LTX-2.3 IC-LoRA: Reference Sheet Control
82237f7d19b7.description: Generate short video clips that stay visually consistent with a reference sheet inventorying characters, props, and locations. Input a composite reference image and a split prompt describing the action, outputting a single video clip. Ideal for character-driven animation, consistent prop visualization, and location-specific scene generation.
82237f7d19b7.metaDescription: ComfyUI LTX-2.3 IC-LoRA workflow: turn a reference sheet into a consistent short video using split prompts. Ideal for characters, props, and locations.
82237f7d19b7.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a composite reference sheet into a short, identity-consistent video using LTX-2.3 with the IC-LoRA Ingredients add-on. You provide a single image that inventories your characters, props, and/or locations, plus a split prompt where one part lists the "ingredients" from the sheet and the other describes the action. The core LTX-2.3 inference (custom node f9f61b10-b689-4d67-b4fa-0acc1d9b5390) uses the IC-LoRA to anchor visual identity to your sheet while animating the described motion.

Technically, the workflow loads your sheet with LoadImage, normalizes it with GetImageSize and ResizeAndPadImage, and then duplicates it across the timeline via RepeatImageBatch so every frame is conditioned on the same visual references. PrimitiveInt values in the Video Settings group (paired with ComfyMathExpression) control fps and total frames. An EmptyImage node defines the target canvas/resolution for generation, and PreviewImage lets you sanity-check inputs and a sample frame. Finally, SaveVideo encodes the generated frame batch into a video file. A MarkdownNote inside the graph includes quick usage tips and links to the official IC-LoRA documentation for prompt formatting and best practices.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and ensure the LTX-2.3 base model and the IC-LoRA Ingredients weights are available as noted (see the Author Notes links to Hugging Face).
Open the LoadImage node and select your composite reference sheet (characters/props/locations in one image). The GetImageSize → ResizeAndPadImage path will adapt it to the target resolution.

In the LTX-2.3 IC-LoRA node (custom f9f61b10-b689-4d67-b4fa-0acc1d9b5390), enter a split prompt: one part enumerating the ingredients from your sheet (names/labels you’ll reuse), and a separate part describing the action/camera or scene. Keep the ingredient list concise and consistent with the sheet.

In the Video Settings group, set fps and duration/frames via the PrimitiveInt nodes. The ComfyMathExpression node computes total frames; RepeatImageBatch will automatically match the reference-sheet conditioning to each frame.
Choose a target resolution using the EmptyImage (canvas) and ensure ResizeAndPadImage keeps aspect ratio. Use PreviewImage to verify the resized sheet and a test frame look correct.

Run the graph. Inspect the first output frames in PreviewImage, then save with SaveVideo. If identities drift, strengthen IC-LoRA adherence (in the LTX node), simplify the action text, or reduce fps/length and re-run.
suggestedUseCases: Character-driven animation where a hero’s look must persist across shots.
Consistent prop visualization (e.g., product variations) in motion.
Location-specific scene generations that preserve a set design or layout.
Storyboard-to-motion drafts while locking key character/prop identities.
Previsualization for ad spots using a fixed brand kit reference sheet.

faqItems.question: How should I structure the reference sheet for best consistency?
faqItems.answer: Place each character/prop/location clearly and non-overlapping on a neutral background, with consistent lighting and angles. Avoid heavy text overlays. Ensure each subject is large enough and well-isolated so the IC-LoRA can bind the visual identity. A single composite image is required—this workflow repeats the same sheet across all frames via RepeatImageBatch.

faqItems.question: What does the split prompt do in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: IC-LoRA Ingredients expects a separation between the list of entities to anchor (ingredients) and the action narration. The ingredients list should reference the same names you intend from the sheet; the action describes motion, camera, or scene. Keeping them distinct helps the model preserve identity while animating. See the official IC-LoRA usage guide for exact formatting recommendations.

faqItems.question: How do I tune video length and resolution without running out of VRAM?
faqItems.answer: Use the Video Settings group: set fps and seconds/frames with PrimitiveInt and let ComfyMathExpression compute total frames. Start with short clips and moderate fps (e.g., ~2–4 seconds). Choose a resolution that’s a multiple of 16 and use ResizeAndPadImage to match the EmptyImage canvas. If you hit VRAM limits, reduce resolution, lower fps, or shorten the clip.

faqItems.question: How can I improve identity stability across frames?
faqItems.answer: Keep the ingredient list concise and consistent with the reference sheet, reduce overly complex action text, and avoid introducing new, unseen entities in the action. Increase IC-LoRA adherence (LoRA strength) in the LTX-2.3 node if available, ensure the reference sheet is high quality, and keep motion/camera changes moderate. Because RepeatImageBatch conditions every frame, stability improves when the reference is clean and unambiguous.

825e6fb23c2c.title: Krea 2 Moodboards
825e6fb23c2c.description: A simple Krea 2 workflow for testing and comparing different Krea moodboard styles. Each section uses a separate prompt, moodboard ID, and save node, making it easy to try multiple visual directions from one workflow. Users can bypass inactive sections, swap in their own Krea moodboard ID, adjust moodboard strength, and generate clean test outputs.
825e6fb23c2c.metaDescription: Test and compare Krea 2 moodboard styles in ComfyUI. Six parallel branches with per‑section prompts, moodboard IDs, and clean SaveImage outputs.
825e6fb23c2c.extendedDescription:
Krea 2 Moodboards is a compact ComfyUI workflow designed to A/B test style directions using Krea's moodboard–conditioned text-to-image generation. Each of the six labeled sections (Ethereal Romanticism, Digitally Broken Realism, Neon Dreams, Technicolor Madhouse, Country Club Surrealism, Liminal Nightmare) runs the same pipeline: PrimitiveNode inputs feed a Krea2ImageNode, and results are written by a dedicated SaveImage node. MarkdownNote nodes annotate each group so you can navigate quickly. Because each section has its own prompt, moodboard_id, moodboard_strength, and save target, you can compare multiple visual directions from one run without cross‑contamination.

Technically, the PrimitiveNode instances hold strings and numbers (prompt text, moodboard ID UUIDs, strength values, optional seed/size if exposed). Those values flow into Krea2ImageNode, which sends a generation request to the Krea 2 image API conditioned by the provided moodboard_id. The SaveImage at the end of each branch writes clean, labeled outputs using per‑section filename prefixes. ComfyUI’s bypass toggle lets you disable inactive sections for faster iteration. The workflow ships with example prompts and moodboard IDs in the Author Notes (e.g., 7947e7b8-750e-4dbd-877a-d554d86f85d1, 176345d7-b1e0-4b44-bf06-ce4d7b8b8062, aa2178a3-36f1-47f6-8d2a-c3578d5329af), making it easy to drop in a style and start testing immediately.
howToUse: Load the Krea 2 Moodboards workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the Krea2ImageNode custom node is installed. Add your Krea API key in the node’s settings or your environment per the node’s documentation.
Decide which sections you want to test first and bypass the others. Use the MarkdownNote labels to find each group (01–06).

For each active group, set the PrimitiveNode values: paste a moodboard_id (you can use the example UUIDs from the Author Notes or your own), write a prompt, and choose a moodboard_strength. Optionally set a seed and size if those inputs are exposed in your Krea2ImageNode version.
Open the SaveImage node in each active group and set a clear filename_prefix (e.g., mb01_ethereal_) so outputs from different styles don’t overwrite each other.
Click Queue Prompt to generate. The Krea2ImageNode will call the Krea 2 API for each active branch, and SaveImage will write results to your output folder.
Iterate: adjust moodboard_strength to balance style vs prompt, refine prompts, swap moodboard IDs, or duplicate a group to add more style variants.
suggestedUseCases: Style A/B testing for art direction and look‑development before committing to a concept
Client reviews: produce side‑by‑side variations aligned to different moodboards
Prompt engineering under controlled style conditions to learn how wording changes outcomes
Building a style library by batch‑generating references per moodboard
Previsualization for campaigns where consistent mood and color language are critical

faqItems.question: What is a moodboard_id and where do I get it?
faqItems.answer: It’s the UUID that identifies a Krea moodboard. Copy it from your Krea account or moodboard page and paste it into the PrimitiveNode feeding the Krea2ImageNode. The workflow includes example IDs in Author Notes you can test with.

faqItems.question: How do I balance the moodboard’s style with my prompt?
faqItems.answer: Use the moodboard_strength input. Lower values give your prompt more control; higher values enforce the moodboard’s look more strongly. Start mid‑range, then nudge up or down based on how much of the board’s palette, composition, and texture you want to see.

faqItems.question: Why are some branches not generating images?
faqItems.answer: Make sure the branch isn’t bypassed, the Krea API key is configured for Krea2ImageNode, and the moodboard_id is valid. Also confirm SaveImage has a writable output path and unique filename_prefix to avoid collisions.

faqItems.question: Can I add more than six moodboards?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Duplicate any Moodboard group (PrimitiveNodes → Krea2ImageNode → SaveImage), update the MarkdownNote label, and point the new PrimitiveNodes to your new moodboard_id and prompt.

8265cda74db1.title: Vidu Q4 Preview: Reference to Video
8265cda74db1.description: Generate expressive videos from two reference images using Vidu Q4 Preview, a flagship model built for vivid character performance, dynamic camera language, and striking visual effects. Ideal for character-driven storytelling, cinematic action sequences, and effect-heavy scenes with explosions, smoke, or particles.
8265cda74db1.metaDescription: Generate expressive videos from two reference images using Vidu Q4 Preview in ComfyUI. Load images, set prompts, and export with SaveVideo.
8265cda74db1.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns two still images into a dynamic video using the Vidu Q4 Preview model. Two LoadImage nodes bring in your reference images (the template includes yellow_fuzzy_smiley.png and clay_man_smiley_sweater.png). These are fed into a single Vidu4ReferenceVideoNode, which uses Vidu to synthesize motion, camera language, and effects while preserving the key visual traits gleaned from both references. The generated clip is written to disk by a SaveVideo node, and an in-graph MarkdownNote summarizes usage tips.

Technically, the Vidu4ReferenceVideoNode fuses the visual features from each reference input to condition the video generation—one image can anchor subject identity while the other can influence style, materials, or expression. You can steer results via the node’s built-in controls (e.g., prompt/text guidance, duration/length, aspect, and seed, depending on your install). Because this node calls the Vidu model, it typically requires a network connection and, if needed, an API key configured in the node. SaveVideo then encodes the frames to a standard file in ComfyUI’s output folder for easy review and iteration.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote for a quick overview.

Open each LoadImage node and swap the provided sample images with your own references (use clear, well-lit PNGs or JPGs). Keep framing and subject size similar across both images for stronger identity transfer.

Open the Vidu4ReferenceVideoNode: confirm the model is set to Vidu Q4 Preview, enter an optional text prompt, and adjust available settings such as duration/length, aspect, and seed (if exposed). If this is your first run, add your Vidu/API credentials in the node or your environment as required.
Run the workflow. The Vidu4ReferenceVideoNode will generate the clip, and SaveVideo will write the result to ComfyUI/output (commonly as an MP4).
Preview the output and iterate: refine your prompt, try swapping the order of the two reference images, or adjust duration/size to better match your target look and motion.
When satisfied, version your inputs and node settings so you can reproduce results (use a fixed seed, if available, to reduce variation between runs).
suggestedUseCases: Character-driven social posts or explainer intros using a brand mascot or avatar.
Cinematic motion tests and camera language studies from a pair of style/identity images.
Previsualization for action beats with smoke, particles, or energetic effects.
Expressive emotes or reaction clips generated from stylized faces or toys.
Mood pieces that blend a subject reference with a distinct art direction image.

faqItems.question: What do the two reference images control?
faqItems.answer: Both images condition the video. One can primarily anchor identity while the other influences style or material cues. The blend depends on the images and node settings—try swapping their order if one image is dominating the look.

faqItems.question: Do I need an internet connection or API key?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Vidu4ReferenceVideoNode integrates the Vidu model via API. You’ll typically need a network connection and valid credentials configured in the node or your environment.

faqItems.question: How can I improve subject consistency across frames?
faqItems.answer: Use clean, high-resolution references with similar framing and lighting. Avoid heavy occlusions. Reduce randomness by setting a fixed seed (if available) and, if exposed, increase reference adherence or reduce creativity-style settings.

faqItems.question: Can I control camera movement and effects?
faqItems.answer: You can guide motion and look via the text prompt. If your Vidu4ReferenceVideoNode exposes controls for duration, intensity, or motion dynamics, adjust them. Otherwise, expect the model to choose cinematic movement consistent with the prompt and references.

8270f76ce235.title: MiniMax H3 Max: Image to Video
8270f76ce235.description: Generate video from a source image using MiniMax H3 Max, animating your still frame while preserving its composition, visual identity, and aspect ratio. The model delivers faster-than-real-time generation with strong prompt adherence and polished cinematic aesthetics. Ideal for bringing character art to life, animating product shots, and creating motion from concept images.
8270f76ce235.metaDescription: Animate a single image into video with MiniMax H3 Max. Preserve framing and identity, optionally upscale from 768p to 2K, and save reproducible results.
8270f76ce235.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI template turns a single still image into a short, cinematic video using MiniMax H3 Max. The core path wires LoadImage and your prompt (PrimitiveStringMultiline) into MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode to package parameters like aspect ratio, duration, and guidance, then drives MinimaxHailuo03FirstLastFrameNode for image-to-video generation with first/last frame consistency. That first/last frame constraint helps preserve the source image’s composition and visual identity from the opening to the closing frame. The final clip is written with SaveVideo, while SaveText can log run metadata for reproducibility.

Two optional stages are provided and start off: a Prompt Enhancer path and a 2K upscale path. ComfySwitchNode routes either your base prompt or an enhanced prompt (if you choose to use it) into the core generator. For higher resolution delivery, the MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode can request a 2K version from a 768p base. A PrimitiveBoolean in the Feature Flags group controls this. Important: the 2K upscale only accepts a 768p source; generate the base at 768p before enabling Upscale to 2K, otherwise the upscale path will be skipped or fail.
howToUse: Load the template in ComfyUI and update to the latest build. In each MiniMax node (MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode, MinimaxHailuo03FirstLastFrameNode, and Regenerate if used), enter your MiniMax API credentials and set any required API parameters.
Add your source image: open LoadImage and select your still (try the provided sneaker_black.png). Set the desired aspect ratio in the context settings to match your image to avoid unwanted cropping.

Enter your text prompt in the PrimitiveStringMultiline node inside the User Inputs group. If the Prompt Enhancer (Optional) group is used, write your refined prompt there and flip the related ComfySwitchNode to route it; otherwise leave the switch off to use the base prompt.

Configure generation in MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode: set clip duration, fps, motion strength, guidance/creativity settings, aspect ratio, and seed. Keep durations modest for best identity preservation.

If you want a 2K delivery, first set the base generation size to 768p, enable the PrimitiveBoolean (Upscale to 2K) in Feature Flags, and confirm the upscale path is connected to MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode. Note: the upscale only works from a 768p source.

Queue the workflow. The core video is produced by MinimaxHailuo03FirstLastFrameNode and saved via SaveVideo; if 2K is enabled, MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode will request the higher-res pass next. SaveText will write run metadata so you can reproduce or iterate later.
suggestedUseCases: Animate product shots for e-commerce or social posts while preserving brand composition.
Bring character illustrations or concept art to life with subtle, camera-ready motion.
Create quick animatics from keyframes to previsualize scenes or motion ideas.
Add cinematic movement to still photography for reels, pitch decks, or mood pieces.

faqItems.question: How does this preserve the image’s framing and identity?
faqItems.answer: The core node MinimaxHailuo03FirstLastFrameNode runs an image-to-video process that uses the source still as the visual anchor from the first to the last frame. Combined with restrained motion settings, this reduces drift and keeps composition and subject identity consistent.

faqItems.question: Why does the 2K upscale require 768p base generation?
faqItems.answer: The Upscale Video to 2K (Optional) stage is wired to accept only a 768p source. Generate your base clip at 768p, then enable the PrimitiveBoolean (Upscale to 2K) to route it through MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode for the higher-resolution pass.

faqItems.question: Where do I put my MiniMax API key?
faqItems.answer: Open the MiniMax nodes (MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode, MinimaxHailuo03FirstLastFrameNode, and MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode if used) and enter your API credentials or key fields as required. Without valid credentials, the API requests will fail.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce artifacts or motion drift?
faqItems.answer: Shorten the clip duration, lower motion intensity, and refine your prompt to avoid conflicting actions. Try a new seed and ensure the aspect ratio matches your source image. Keeping the base generation at moderate resolution (e.g., 768p) before upscaling can also help stability.

834ab8919949.title: Seedance2.5 1080P: Image to Video
834ab8919949.description: Generate cinematic 1080P video clips from a single image using Seedance 2.5, animating the still into a moving scene with synchronized sound, music, and dialogue for clips up to 30 seconds across any aspect ratio. Ideal for breathing life into product shots, extending concept art into motion, and creating engaging social media content from photographs.
834ab8919949.metaDescription: Animate a single image into 1080p video in ComfyUI with Seedance 2.5. Configure motion, duration, and aspect ratio, then export clips up to 30 seconds.
834ab8919949.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single still image into a polished 1080p video clip using Seedance 2.5 via the ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2. The graph is intentionally simple and reliable: LoadImage brings your source frame into the pipeline, ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2 synthesizes motion-conditioned frames from that reference, and SaveVideo encodes the output sequence to a playable MP4 at your chosen frame rate and aspect ratio. You control duration (up to ~30 seconds), FPS, motion strength, and seeding for reproducible results.

Technically, the ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2 uses the input image as a visual prior, generating a temporally coherent frame sequence that preserves identity and structure while introducing camera-like moves (e.g., gentle pans, zooms, and parallax) and scene dynamics. Because resolution and aspect ratio are configurable, you can produce 1920x1080 landscape, 1080x1920 vertical, or square clips while maintaining 1080 on the long edge. SaveVideo then assembles frames at the specified FPS. Note: this minimal graph outputs video only; to add music, dialogue, or foley, mux audio afterward or extend the workflow with audio nodes/external tools.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and verify required nodes are available: LoadImage, ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2 (Seedance 2.5), and SaveVideo.
Load your source still via LoadImage. For best results, pre-crop it to your target aspect ratio (e.g., 16:9, 9:16, or 1:1) to avoid unintended cropping or stretching.

In ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2, set key parameters: duration (seconds, up to ~30), FPS (e.g., 16–24 for efficiency, 30 for smoother motion), motion strength (lower = subtle parallax, higher = bolder movement), and a fixed seed for reproducibility.

Choose your 1080p target size. For landscape, use 1920x1080; for vertical, 1080x1920; for square, 1080x1080. Ensure these dimensions are reflected both in the generation node (if width/height are exposed) and in SaveVideo.
Execute the graph. Inspect the preview frames for artifacts or identity drift; if needed, reduce motion strength or the clip length and re-run with the same seed.
Export with SaveVideo at your chosen FPS. If you need audio (music, VO, or dialogue), add it in a video editor or extend the workflow to mux an external audio track.
suggestedUseCases: Breathing life into product shots with subtle camera moves and parallax for ecommerce or ads.
Extending concept art or keyframes into motion to pitch scenes or mood pieces.
Turning portraits or lifestyle photos into eye-catching vertical clips for social media.
Animating architectural renders to demonstrate space and depth with gentle camera motion.
Creating loopable background visuals from static graphics for events or stream overlays.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow generate audio (music or dialogue) along with the video?
faqItems.answer: No. This graph outputs video only via SaveVideo. To add music, VO, or dialogue, mux an audio file afterward in your editor or extend the workflow with audio/muxing nodes.

faqItems.question: What resolution and aspect ratios are supported?
faqItems.answer: Any common aspect ratio works. For 1080p deliverables, use 1920x1080 (landscape), 1080x1920 (vertical), or 1080x1080 (square). Keep the long edge at 1080 and match your source image’s aspect ratio to minimize cropping.

faqItems.question: How long can the clip be, and what are performance considerations?
faqItems.answer: Up to ~30 seconds is practical. Longer clips and higher FPS increase VRAM and render time. For mid-range GPUs, start with 16–24 FPS and moderate motion strength; if VRAM is limited, consider shorter durations or 720p tests first.

faqItems.question: Can I automate this via the ComfyUI API?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Serialize the workflow JSON and POST it to ComfyUI’s /prompt endpoint. Provide your image as a file path (server-side) or base64. Set duration, FPS, resolution, and seed in the ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2 before triggering the run.

8357db8ead93.title: 3.1 Advanced:  Multi-Shot Video
8357db8ead93.description: Learn how to create a UGC video with your character and product in app mode.
8357db8ead93.metaDescription: Create multi-shot UGC videos with character and product integration using ComfyUI's advanced workflow with Kling 3.0 and Nano Banana 2 models.
8357db8ead93.extendedDescription:
This advanced ComfyUI workflow is designed to create multi-shot user-generated content (UGC) videos featuring your character and product. It leverages the power of the Kling 3.0 and Nano Banana 2 models to seamlessly integrate both elements into a cohesive video narrative. The workflow begins with the 'LoadImage' nodes for uploading your character and product images, followed by the 'GeminiNanoBanana2' node, which performs semantic editing to blend these images effectively. The 'BatchImagesNode' and 'KlingOmniProImageToVideoNode' are then used to generate a series of storyboard shots, which are compiled into a video using the 'SaveVideo' node.

What makes this workflow particularly useful is its ability to produce engaging UGC videos that can be used for marketing or storytelling purposes. By selecting the number of shots and writing specific prompts for each, users can customize the video to match their creative vision. The Kling 3.0 model ensures high-quality video output, while the Nano Banana 2 model provides flexibility in aspect ratio selection, making it adaptable to various platforms and audiences.
howToUse: Load the ComfyUI workflow for multi-shot video creation.
Upload your character image using the 'LoadImage' node.
Upload your product image using another 'LoadImage' node.
Select the desired aspect ratio and number of storyboard shots.
Write a prompt for each storyboard shot to guide the video creation.
Run the workflow to generate and save your UGC video.
suggestedUseCases: Creating promotional videos for social media marketing.
Developing engaging video content for e-commerce product pages.
Producing personalized video messages for brand storytelling.
Generating video content for influencer collaborations.
Crafting dynamic video presentations for product launches.

faqItems.question: What is the purpose of the Nano Banana 2 model?
faqItems.answer: The Nano Banana 2 model is used for semantic editing and selecting aspect ratios, ensuring your character and product images are well-integrated into the video.

faqItems.question: How many storyboard shots can I create?
faqItems.answer: You can select the number of storyboard shots based on your needs, allowing for a customizable video narrative.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for any type of product?
faqItems.answer: Yes, this workflow is versatile and can be used for a wide range of products, making it ideal for various marketing and storytelling applications.

faqItems.question: Is prior video editing experience required to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No prior video editing experience is needed. The workflow is designed to be user-friendly, with step-by-step instructions to guide you through the process.

835a5589f191.title: Video Extend: Grok
835a5589f191.description: Upload a short video and a text prompt describing the next scene. Generate a seamless video extension using Grok extend.
835a5589f191.metaDescription: Extend any short video with a text prompt using Grok in ComfyUI. Load, prompt, and generate a seamless next scene, then save the extended clip.
835a5589f191.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow extends a short video by generating the next moments based on a text prompt. It uses LoadVideo to ingest your source clip, GrokVideoExtendNode to predict and synthesize additional future frames that follow your prompt, and SaveVideo to write a single, continuous output file. The goal is a seamless handoff from the last frames of your input into the newly generated continuation.

Technically, GrokVideoExtendNode sends the tail of your clip and your prompt to the Grok video extension model via API, then returns new frames that align with the existing motion, framing, and style while introducing the content you describe. You control how far to extend (frames or seconds) and can iterate by refining the prompt or parameters to reduce seams and drift. Keeping resolution and frame rate consistent across LoadVideo and SaveVideo helps maintain temporal coherence and avoids stutter.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the three main nodes: LoadVideo -> GrokVideoExtendNode -> SaveVideo.
In LoadVideo, select your source clip. Keep the resolution and FPS you want to preserve in the final output (most ffmpeg-readable formats work).

Open GrokVideoExtendNode and enter a clear text prompt describing the next scene (e.g., "the camera continues forward as neon signs appear"). Set the extension length (in seconds or frames) and any available options like seed or guidance if your installation exposes them.
If required by your setup, add/configure your Grok API credentials in the node or global settings so the node can call the service.
Queue/Execute the workflow. Preview the extended clip in ComfyUI once GrokVideoExtendNode finishes returning frames.
In SaveVideo, choose the output path, codec, and FPS. Match the input FPS to keep motion smooth. Save the final, seamlessly extended video.
suggestedUseCases: Extend an establishing shot to reveal more environment before a cut.
Create longer B-roll by continuing a camera move beyond the original clip.
Storyboard and previs: draft the next beat of a scene from a short reference shot.
Social content: lengthen clips for platform-specific timing without reshoots.
Product demos: continue the scene into a call-to-action or feature reveal.

faqItems.question: How do I avoid visible seams at the transition point?
faqItems.answer: Use a prompt that naturally continues what’s already on screen, keep the original resolution and FPS consistent through LoadVideo and SaveVideo, and extend in modest lengths first (e.g., 2–5 seconds). If your node exposes seed or guidance settings, keep them stable while iterating your prompt to refine continuity.

faqItems.question: How long can I extend a clip?
faqItems.answer: It depends on your Grok API limits and node settings. Longer generations can increase drift. Start with shorter extensions and build up, reviewing results at each step.

faqItems.question: Does audio carry over?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo typically writes a new video stream and may not preserve audio. If you need audio, export it from the original clip and reattach it to the extended video with a video editor or ffmpeg.

faqItems.question: What formats and resolutions are supported?
faqItems.answer: LoadVideo accepts most formats readable by ffmpeg. For best results, keep the original resolution and aspect ratio, and ensure they meet any limits imposed by the Grok API. If you encounter errors, try re-encoding your source to a standard format like MP4 (H.264).

83ff3768d42b.title: Wan2.1 VACE Reference to Video
83ff3768d42b.description: Create videos that match the style and content of a reference image. Perfect for style-consistent video generation.
83ff3768d42b.metaDescription: Generate style-consistent videos from a single image using Wan2.1 VACE in ComfyUI. Guide motion with prompts and export MP4 or animated WebP.
83ff3768d42b.extendedDescription:
Wan2.1 VACE Reference to Video turns a single image into a short video that preserves your reference’s style and subject while introducing motion guided by text prompts. The core of the workflow is the WanVaceToVideo node, which fuses a loaded reference image (LoadImage) with prompt text encoded by CLIPTextEncode. The diffusion backbone is provided by the Wan 2.1 VACE models—use UNETLoader and VAELoader in the “Load models here” group to select either Wan2.1-VACE-1.3B or Wan2.1-VACE-14B. A ModelSamplingSD3 node configures the sampler, and KSampler handles denoising with your chosen steps and cfg scale. If you need stylistic adapters, LoraLoader lets you apply a matching LoRA to the same diffusion model family.

After sampling, VAEDecode reconstructs frames from latents. TrimVideoLatent helps you set exact duration, and the “First Frame control” group (ImageToMask, SolidMask, MaskToImage, RepeatImageBatch) can lock or protect parts of the initial frame for stronger identity or composition retention. PreviewImage nodes allow quick QC during iteration. Finally, CreateVideo aggregates frames and you can export via SaveVideo (MP4) or SaveAnimatedWEBP for lightweight previews. Author guidance: default steps=20 and cfg=6.0 work well; with CausVid LoRA use fewer steps (2–4) and a low cfg (~1.0). For resolution, VACE-1.3B is suited to 480p, while VACE-14B delivers higher quality and supports 480p and 720p at the cost of longer render time.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then open the “Load models here” group. Point UNETLoader and VAELoader to your chosen Wan2.1 VACE checkpoint (1.3B for faster 480p drafts, 14B for higher quality and 720p). Ensure CLIPLoader matches the model family. Optionally add a LoRA in LoraLoader that matches the same base model.
In “Load reference image,” use LoadImage to bring in your source image. Set the target resolution in the “Video Size” group to match your image’s aspect ratio to avoid warping.

Enter your positive and negative prompts in the “Prompt” group via CLIPTextEncode. Keep descriptions specific (subject, motion, camera) and use negatives to filter artifacts. If using a CausVid LoRA, lower steps to 2–4 and cfg to ~1.0 per the notes.
Configure generation in “Sampling & Decoding”: set steps and cfg in KSampler (default 20/6.0). ModelSamplingSD3 should be connected to KSampler as provided. Choose or fix a seed for reproducibility.

Set length and control: in WanVaceToVideo choose the number of frames. The helper in “Value = Length(WanVaceToVideo) - 1” keeps CreateVideo in sync. Use “First Frame control” (ImageToMask/SolidMask/MaskToImage) if you need to preserve identity or parts of the first frame; TrimVideoLatent if you need to shorten the sequence.
Queue the workflow. Inspect PreviewImage outputs to validate frames. When satisfied, export with SaveVideo (MP4) in the “Save Video (Mp4)” group, or use SaveAnimatedWEBP for quick web previews.
suggestedUseCases: Brand or character style continuity: turn a single key image into on-brand motion snippets for social posts.
Product hero spins and parallax moves derived from a catalog photo while preserving materials and design cues.
Concept art turnarounds: bring a static character or creature sheet to life with subtle, guided camera motion.
Animated portraits and intros where identity and art style must remain consistent across frames.
Storyboard previz: rapidly prototype shot motion from a single frame before full production.

faqItems.question: Which model should I pick: VACE-1.3B or VACE-14B?
faqItems.answer: Use 1.3B for faster drafts at 480p and lower VRAM. Choose 14B for better detail, stronger temporal coherence, and 720p support, noting longer render times and higher memory use.

faqItems.question: How do I control video length and frame rate?
faqItems.answer: Set the frame count in WanVaceToVideo. The helper node “Value = Length(WanVaceToVideo) - 1” keeps CreateVideo aligned. Set FPS and output settings in CreateVideo/SaveVideo. Use TrimVideoLatent to shorten or fine-tune duration without re-running the full pipeline.

faqItems.question: How can I keep the subject consistent across frames?
faqItems.answer: Enable the “First Frame control” group. Use SolidMask or ImageToMask to define protected areas, then MaskToImage to apply them. Combine with a moderate cfg (around 6) and a fixed seed in KSampler to improve identity and layout stability.

faqItems.question: Can I use LoRAs with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Load a LoRA via LoraLoader that matches the exact Wan diffusion model family you’re using. Follow the author’s guidance for CausVid LoRA (steps 2–4, cfg ≈1.0). Mismatched LoRAs can degrade quality or fail to load.

840b6e4c3983.title: Wan Animate 2.2 Character Replacement Workflow
840b6e4c3983.description: Wan Animate 2.2 — Character & Scene Replacement - Uses Nano Banana 2 to generate a reference image from the first frame, then swaps the full scene. Optimized for human subjects.
840b6e4c3983.metaDescription: Replace characters in videos with Wan Animate 2.2 for realistic human animations. Optimized for human subjects using advanced AI models.
840b6e4c3983.extendedDescription:
The Wan Animate 2.2 Character Replacement Workflow is designed to replace characters and scenes in video content using advanced AI models. This workflow leverages the power of the Wan 2.2 Animate model, which is specifically optimized for human subjects, ensuring that the character replacement is both stable and convincing. The process begins by utilizing the Nano Banana 2 model to generate a reference image from the first frame of the video. This image serves as the basis for replacing the character throughout the entire video sequence. The workflow employs several custom nodes, including ComfyUI-WanAnimatePreprocess and ComfyUI-segment-anything-2, to segment and process the video frames effectively.

Technically, the workflow uses a combination of nodes such as VHS_LoadVideo to load the video, and GeminiNanoBanana2 to apply the character replacement based on the reference image. The SaveVideo node is then used to output the final animated video. This workflow is particularly useful for creators looking to produce high-quality character animations in video content, offering a seamless integration of AI-driven techniques to enhance video production capabilities. By focusing on human subjects, it ensures that the facial and body features are rendered with high fidelity, making it ideal for projects that require realistic character animations.
howToUse: Load the workflow into ComfyUI and ensure all necessary models and custom nodes are installed.
Import your video file using the VHS_LoadVideo node to start the process.
Select a reference image from the first frame using the GeminiNanoBanana2 node for character replacement.
Run the workflow to process the video frames and apply the character replacement.
Use the SaveVideo node to export the final animated video with the replaced character.
Review the output to ensure the character replacement meets your expectations.
suggestedUseCases: Creating promotional videos with customized characters.
Producing educational content with animated human figures.
Developing short films or animations with unique character designs.
Enhancing social media content with engaging character animations.
Generating marketing materials with personalized video characters.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow be used with non-human subjects?
faqItems.answer: While the workflow is optimized for human subjects, it can technically be used with non-human subjects, but the results may not be as stable or convincing.

faqItems.question: What is the best resolution for input videos?
faqItems.answer: The workflow includes a Target Resolution group to help optimize video resolution. However, starting with a high-resolution video is recommended for the best results.

faqItems.question: How long does it take to process a video?
faqItems.answer: Processing time can vary based on video length and system performance, but typically, it may take several minutes to an hour for a standard-length video.

faqItems.question: Do I need a powerful GPU to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: A powerful GPU is recommended to efficiently run the workflow, especially for high-resolution videos or longer sequences.

847f17f3f95c.title: Qwen Image Edit for Illustration v 1.0
847f17f3f95c.description: This workflow leverages Qwen Edit with a finetuned illustration LoRA for better illustrated content editing.
847f17f3f95c.metaDescription: Turn photos into clean illustrations with Qwen Image Edit + an illustration LoRA. Text-guide your edits and save stylized results directly in ComfyUI.
847f17f3f95c.extendedDescription:
Qwen Image Edit for Illustration v1.0 is a text-guided image editing workflow that turns your existing images into clean, stylized illustrations while preserving structure. It combines the Qwen Image Edit model with an illustration-focused LoRA so you can apply style changes (e.g., "convert this product photo into a flat vector illustration") without redrawing from scratch. The core path is simple: LoadImage brings in your source, PrimitiveStringMultiline captures your edit instruction, the model loader node (c7f5c302-e46e-4a0f-91bd-0aec474e7659) loads the Qwen Image/Qwen Image Edit weights, LoraLoaderModelOnly merges the illustration LoRA into the base model, the edit node (eba40a3a-f6c5-48ac-b58e-55525d06b373) runs inference, and SaveImage writes the result.

Technically, the LoRA is injected on-the-fly by LoraLoaderModelOnly, biasing the Qwen Edit model toward illustrated outputs while keeping the underlying content aligned with your source image. The edit node consumes the input image plus your instruction and uses the merged model to generate a new frame that follows your prompt. The included MarkdownNote provides in-graph tips, and all required model files are available from the Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI and Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-Edit_ComfyUI Hugging Face repos linked in the author notes.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. Ensure you have the Qwen Image/Qwen Image Edit models and the illustration LoRA downloaded from the linked Hugging Face repos.
Open the model loader node (c7f5c302-e46e-4a0f-91bd-0aec474e7659) and point it to your Qwen Image/Qwen Image Edit weights as described in the repository readme.
In LoraLoaderModelOnly, select the illustration LoRA file and set its strength. Start with a moderate value; you can increase it if the style isn’t strong enough.
Use LoadImage to bring in your source image. Keep the resolution moderate for faster iterations, then upscale later if needed.
Enter a clear, single-purpose edit instruction in PrimitiveStringMultiline (e.g., "convert to flat 2D illustration, pastel palette, minimal shading, keep layout and proportions").

Run the workflow. The edit node (eba40a3a-f6c5-48ac-b58e-55525d06b373) will apply the instruction using the LoRA-merged model, and SaveImage will write the result to your ComfyUI output folder. If needed, iterate by adjusting LoRA strength and the edit parameters on the Qwen Edit node.
suggestedUseCases: Turn product photos into flat, on-brand illustrations for catalogs, pitch decks, and e-commerce thumbnails.
Convert character or portrait photos into clean manga/comic styles while preserving facial identity and pose.
Create consistent illustrated variants of UI assets or icons from mixed-source references.
Stylize slide imagery or infographics into cohesive, minimal illustrations for presentations.
Simplify busy backgrounds and unify color palettes to match brand style guides.

faqItems.question: Which models do I need and where do I get them?
faqItems.answer: Download the Qwen Image/Qwen Image Edit weights and the illustration LoRA from the Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI and Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-Edit_ComfyUI Hugging Face repos (see links in the workflow notes). Point the model loader node to the base weights and LoraLoaderModelOnly to the LoRA file.

faqItems.question: How do I control how strong the illustration style looks?
faqItems.answer: Use the LoRA strength in LoraLoaderModelOnly as your primary control. If the node exposes guidance or edit-strength parameters on the Qwen Edit node (eba40a3a-…), adjust those as secondary controls. Increase LoRA strength for bolder style; reduce it to keep more photographic detail.

faqItems.question: Can I make only stylistic changes and keep content intact?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Write instructions that focus on style, color, and rendering (e.g., “flat shading, soft pastel palette”) and avoid adding or removing objects. This nudges the model to preserve composition and subject while changing the look.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow support region-specific edits or masking?
faqItems.answer: This graph is designed for global, instruction-based edits. For targeted regions, use a masking-enabled variant of the Qwen Edit workflow or add a mask path and a compatible edit node that accepts masks.

857e50707831.title: SeedVR2: Image Upscale
857e50707831.description: Upload an image to upscale it with SeedVR2 and generate a high-definition output.
857e50707831.metaDescription: Upscale images with SeedVR2 for high-definition results using ComfyUI. Enhance clarity and detail with this efficient workflow.
857e50707831.extendedDescription:
The SeedVR2: Image Upscale workflow is designed to enhance the resolution of images using the SeedVR2 model, which is renowned for its ability to upscale visuals while maintaining high-definition quality. This workflow leverages several key nodes, including LoadImage, SaveImage, and ImageCompare, alongside the custom node seedvr2_videoupscaler from the comfyui_essentials package. These nodes work in concert to load an image, apply the upscale process, and save the enhanced output, ensuring a seamless transition from input to output. The ImageCompare node is particularly useful for evaluating the quality of the upscaled image against the original, providing a visual confirmation of the improvements made.

Technically, the workflow operates by first loading the input image using the LoadImage node. The image is then processed through the seedvr2_videoupscaler node, which applies advanced algorithms to increase the image resolution. After processing, the SaveImage node stores the high-definition output, while the ImageCompare node allows users to visually assess the differences between the original and upscaled images. This workflow is particularly useful for applications where image clarity and detail are paramount, such as in digital art, photography, and video production.
howToUse: Load the SeedVR2: Image Upscale workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadImage node to upload the image you wish to upscale.
Ensure the seedvr2_videoupscaler node is correctly configured to process your image.
Run the workflow to apply the upscale process.
Use the ImageCompare node to compare the original and upscaled images.
Save the enhanced image using the SaveImage node.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing digital artwork for print or display.
Improving the quality of low-resolution photographs.
Upscaling video frames for higher resolution playback.
Refining textures in game development for better visual fidelity.
Preparing images for high-definition presentations or marketing materials.

faqItems.question: What is the maximum resolution I can achieve with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The maximum resolution depends on the capabilities of the SeedVR2 model and your system's processing power. Typically, it can upscale images to several times their original size while maintaining quality.

faqItems.question: Do I need any special hardware to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: While no special hardware is required, a powerful GPU will significantly speed up the processing time and handle larger images more efficiently.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for batch processing multiple images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can adapt the workflow to process multiple images by iterating over a set of images with the LoadImage node and saving each output individually.

faqItems.question: How does the ImageCompare node help in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The ImageCompare node allows you to visually assess the quality improvements by comparing the original and upscaled images side by side, ensuring the upscale meets your expectations.

8629d9dbb8a4.title: Ideogram 4.5: Text to Image
8629d9dbb8a4.description: Generate images from text prompts using Ideogram 4.5, with controls for canvas size, quality level, automatic prompt rewriting, and seed. No file inputs are required and one image is output. Ideal for typography-led posters, layout-driven design work, marketing visuals, and fast exploration of visual concepts.
8629d9dbb8a4.metaDescription: Generate typography-forward images from text using Ideogram 4.5 in ComfyUI. Control canvas size, quality, auto-rewrite, and seed. One-click, single-image output.
8629d9dbb8a4.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns short text prompts into finished images using Ideogram 4.5, a model known for strong typography and layout composition. It is purpose-built for fast exploration of posters, headline treatments, and marketing visuals without any file inputs. You control canvas size, quality level, automatic prompt rewriting, and seed to balance legibility, style, and reproducibility.

Technically, the IdeogramTextToImageApi node packages your prompt and parameters (width/height canvas size, quality setting, auto-prompt rewrite toggle, and seed) and sends them to the Ideogram 4.5 API. The generated image is returned to ComfyUI and written to disk by SaveImageAdvanced, where you can set the output folder and filename pattern. Use the seed to reproduce a look, increase quality for more detailed results, and toggle automatic prompt rewriting when you want the service to refine phrasing for layout and text handling versus adhering more literally to your wording.

Because the workflow outputs one image per run and has no file inputs, it’s ideal for quick iteration. Queue multiple runs with different seeds or prompt variations to survey a wider design space, then lock in a preferred direction by reusing the same seed and parameters.
howToUse: Load the Ideogram 4.5: Text to Image workflow in ComfyUI and open the IdeogramTextToImageApi node. Ensure your Ideogram API access is configured for this node.

Enter a clear prompt. For best control, separate display text from style, e.g., Text: Hello World; Style: minimal poster, bold sans-serif, high contrast. Choose a canvas width/height that matches your target aspect ratio.
Pick a quality level and decide whether to enable automatic prompt rewriting. Enable it to let the service refine phrasing for layout/typography; disable it for more literal adherence to your prompt.
Set a seed if you want reproducible outputs. Reusing the same prompt, parameters, and seed will help you return to a look later.
Configure SaveImageAdvanced with your output folder and filename prefix. Select your preferred file format and any naming options.
Click Queue Prompt to run. Review the result, then iterate: adjust the prompt, change the seed for variations, try different quality levels, or toggle auto-rewrite to compare outcomes.
suggestedUseCases: Typography-led posters and headline treatments for campaigns or events
Rapid marketing visuals for social posts, ads, or landing pages
Layout exploration for covers, flyers, and presentation slides
Creative word art and display-type concepts for branding directions
Moodboards and concept frames during early visual ideation

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The IdeogramTextToImageApi node calls the Ideogram 4.5 service. Make sure your API access is configured in the node or your ComfyUI environment so requests can be authenticated.

faqItems.question: What does automatic prompt rewriting do?
faqItems.answer: When enabled, the request allows Ideogram to refine or reinterpret your prompt to improve layout and text handling. Turn it off if you want stricter adherence to your exact phrasing. Toggling this setting can noticeably change results.

faqItems.question: How can I reproduce a result?
faqItems.answer: Set and reuse the same seed with the same prompt and parameters (canvas size, quality, and rewrite toggle). This improves consistency across runs, though minor differences can still occur with external API services.

faqItems.question: Why does it produce only one image per run?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is designed for single-image output to keep iteration fast. To explore variations, queue multiple runs with different seeds or prompt tweaks. You can also duplicate the IdeogramTextToImageApi node or integrate batching in a custom workflow if needed.

865f8987823e.title: Runway Aleph2: Video Edit
865f8987823e.description: Generate a single edited video that preserves original motion and timing while applying your chosen changes. Ideal for portrait and product relighting, consistent lighting across photo sets, and e-commerce apparel presentation.
865f8987823e.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Edit videos with Runway Aleph 2. Preserve motion and timing while restyling via prompts, guidance images, and keyframed controls.
865f8987823e.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates in-context video editing with Runway Aleph 2 to restyle footage you already have while preserving the original motion and timing. The core path is straightforward: LoadVideo provides your source clip, RunwayAleph2VideoToVideoNode applies the edit based on your instructions, and SaveVideo writes the rendered result. The optional Guidance Images group lets you LoadImage references and convert them with RunwayAleph2PromptImageNode for style, color, or lighting cues that steer the edit without changing the underlying performance.

Technically, RunwayAleph2VideoToVideoNode sends your source frames, text prompt, and any prompt images to the Runway Aleph 2 API. The model conditions on your footage (in-context) so it can edit appearance while retaining per-frame motion and overall timing. If you want the look to evolve over time, RunwayAleph2KeyframeNode can drive time-varying parameters, such as increasing or reducing edit strength at specific timestamps for gradual transitions. This combination is especially useful for portrait and product relighting, consistent look across a set of clips, and controlled restyles (for example, dark anime or seasonal lighting) without manual, frame-by-frame work.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the Runway Aleph 2 nodes are installed. Set your Runway API key in the node or extension settings so the API calls can authenticate.
Connect LoadVideo to your source clip. Use a short segment for fast iteration, then switch to the full-resolution/full-length version once you like the look.

Write a focused text prompt in RunwayAleph2VideoToVideoNode that describes only the intended change (e.g., warm golden-hour relight, soft rim light, clean studio background). Avoid asking for new motion or new objects.

Optional: In the Guidance Images (Optional) group, add one or more LoadImage nodes with style/lighting references and feed them into RunwayAleph2PromptImageNode. Connect the prompt image output to RunwayAleph2VideoToVideoNode to anchor color, texture, or lighting consistency.

Optional: Use RunwayAleph2KeyframeNode to schedule changes over time (for example, ramp edit intensity, or switch from cool to warm tones mid-clip). Connect its output to the corresponding time-varying input on RunwayAleph2VideoToVideoNode.
Run the graph. Inspect the SaveVideo output in your designated output folder. Iterate on prompt wording, guidance images, and keyframe timing for refinements; then render at your final resolution.
suggestedUseCases: Portrait relighting for interviews or talking-head clips while keeping identity and motion intact.
Product B-roll restyles to unify lighting and color across multiple shots for e-commerce pages.
Seasonal or mood-based restyles (e.g., summer to winter, natural to dark anime) without reshooting.
Apparel presentation with consistent tone and background across a series of short clips.
Brand look alignment by matching footage to a style board via guidance images.

faqItems.question: Will the model preserve my clip’s motion and timing?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Runway Aleph 2 is an in-context video editing model. In this workflow, RunwayAleph2VideoToVideoNode conditions on your source frames so it restyles appearance while keeping existing motion and timing.

faqItems.question: How do I keep faces, products, or backgrounds consistent?
faqItems.answer: Use precise, conservative prompts that state only the change you want (e.g., relight, color shift), add relevant guidance images via RunwayAleph2PromptImageNode, and avoid conflicting references. If needed, lower the edit strength and make adjustments gradually with RunwayAleph2KeyframeNode.

faqItems.question: What clip length and resolution should I start with?
faqItems.answer: For faster iteration, begin with short segments and moderate resolutions (e.g., 720p–1080p). Once you approve the look, render the full clip at your target resolution. Keep in mind overall API limits and processing times.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow keep audio?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo focuses on the visual output and typically does not preserve audio. Export your edited video and reattach the original audio in a video editor if needed.

86efedaffa3e.title: 3.2 Advanced: Control Video Generation
86efedaffa3e.description: Learn how to control a video with Pose Estimation and Wan Animate.
86efedaffa3e.metaDescription: Control video generation with pose estimation and Wan Animate. Learn to guide video creation using pose videos and reference images.
86efedaffa3e.extendedDescription: This advanced ComfyUI workflow is designed to empower users with the ability to control video generation using pose estimation techniques and the Wan Animate model. At its core, the workflow leverages the DWPose Estimator to extract pose information from an input video, creating a 'control video' that serves as a blueprint for generating new video content. This control video is then used in conjunction with the Wan Animate model to produce videos that follow the poses and movements captured in the original footage. The workflow involves several key nodes, including VAEDecode for decoding latent representations, CreateVideo for assembling frames into a video, and SaveVideo for outputting the final product. Additionally, the comfyui_controlnet_aux custom node is utilized to enhance control over the video generation process, ensuring that the output aligns closely with the user's vision. This workflow is particularly useful for animators and content creators who wish to produce videos that maintain consistent motion and style, guided by specific pose references.
howToUse: Load the ComfyUI workflow designed for advanced video generation control.
Upload an image of your character that you wish to animate.
Upload a pose reference video to be used for pose estimation.
The workflow will generate a pose estimation control video using the DWPose Estimator.
Utilize the Wan Animate model to create a new video that follows the poses from the control video.
Save the generated video using the SaveVideo node for your final output.
suggestedUseCases: Creating animated videos where characters follow specific dance routines or movements.
Developing educational content that requires precise motion replication from reference videos.
Producing consistent and stylized animations for marketing or storytelling purposes.
Generating training data for machine learning models that require annotated video content.
Crafting unique video art pieces that blend real-world motion with animated characters.

faqItems.question: What is the purpose of the DWPose Estimator in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The DWPose Estimator extracts pose information from an input video, creating a control video that guides the animation process in generating new content.

faqItems.question: Can I use any video as a pose reference?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can upload any video as a pose reference, but for best results, ensure that the video clearly shows the movements you want to replicate.

faqItems.question: What is the role of Wan Animate in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Wan Animate uses the pose control video and reference images to generate new videos that adhere to the specified poses and styles.

faqItems.question: How can I ensure the output video matches my expectations?
faqItems.answer: Carefully select your reference images and pose videos, and adjust the workflow parameters as needed to fine-tune the output to your desired style and motion.

Generating product images that maintain consistency across multiple views.

faqItems.question: What is the advantage of using quantized weights in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Quantized weights allow the model to run more efficiently, reducing computational load while maintaining high image quality.

faqItems.question: How does multi-reference consistency improve image quality?
faqItems.answer: Multi-reference consistency ensures that elements across the image align correctly, providing a more cohesive and realistic final output.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for text-heavy images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow is designed to handle professional text rendering, making it ideal for images that require significant text integration.

faqItems.question: Is there a way to adjust the image resolution in this workflow?

87a4c3fd695b.title: FLUX 3 Image: Bounding Box Edit
87a4c3fd695b.description: Place objects and text where you want them with FLUX 3 Image by feeding boxes from the Create Bounding Boxes node into the prompt, so each box carries its own description and copy into the render. Boxes are relative to the canvas, so set the output to the same aspect ratio. One image is output, up to 4K. Ideal for poster and layout composition, placing headlines and captions, and controlling where subjects sit in the frame.
87a4c3fd695b.metaDescription: Tutorial: Use FLUX 3 Image with CreateBoundingBoxes in ComfyUI to place objects and text precisely for layout-controlled edits up to 4K.
87a4c3fd695b.extendedDescription:
This workflow teaches layout-controlled image edits with FLUX 3 Image by driving the composition from bounding boxes. You load a base image with LoadImage, define regions and their instructions in CreateBoundingBoxes, and feed those boxes directly into Flux3ImageNode. Each box carries its own localized prompt (for an object, a person, or even a line of text), and the model places or edits content within those regions during generation. Because the boxes are relative to the canvas, matching the output aspect ratio is essential to keep placements where you expect them.

The node chain is simple and transparent: CreateBoundingBoxes emits a list of regions plus per-box text that flows into Flux3ImageNode for a single-image render (up to 4K). PreviewAny lets you quickly inspect results, ImageCompare provides a before/after view against the input image, and SaveImageAdvanced exports the final with metadata for reproducibility. A MarkdownNote inside the graph summarizes usage and tips. The result is a reliable way to art-direct posters, headlines, captions, or product placements by describing what should appear in each box and where it should sit in the frame.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and update ComfyUI if prompted. Open the provided example or your own image in the LoadImage node.
In Flux3ImageNode, set the output width and height. Keep the same aspect ratio as your intended layout (ideally matching the input image) so box positions translate correctly.

Open CreateBoundingBoxes and add one box per element you want to place. For each box, set its position/size and write a clear description (e.g., “large bold headline,” “red umbrella,” or exact copy you want in that area).
Optionally keep the global prompt minimal and let the per-box prompts drive placement. Avoid overlapping many small boxes; start with a few well-sized regions.
Queue the prompt. Use PreviewAny to review the render, and ImageCompare to check changes versus the original image. Adjust box positions, sizes, or wording and re-run as needed.
When satisfied, save the result with SaveImageAdvanced to preserve settings and metadata for later reproduction.
suggestedUseCases: Poster and flyer design: Lock in headline, subhead, and hero subject placement.
Marketing creatives: Place product shots and taglines precisely in promo images.
Magazine or cover mockups: Reserve areas for mastheads, cover lines, and feature images.
Social thumbnails: Keep faces and titles in safe zones across multiple aspect ratios.
Infographics and captions: Allocate text blocks and icons to specific regions.

faqItems.question: Why does placement shift when I change resolution?
faqItems.answer: CreateBoundingBoxes uses coordinates relative to the canvas. If the output aspect ratio changes, the relative positions change too. Keep the same aspect ratio (and ideally the same dimensions) between CreateBoundingBoxes and Flux3ImageNode.

faqItems.question: How many boxes can I use?
faqItems.answer: You can define multiple regions, but practical results are best with a small, clear set of boxes. Too many or heavily overlapping boxes can cause muddled compositions. Start with key regions (headline, subject, logo) and iterate.

faqItems.question: Can it render perfect, spelled-out text?
faqItems.answer: Generative models can produce text-like results, but spelling and fidelity can vary. For cleaner typography, use the boxes to reserve space and style (e.g., “bold sans-serif headline”), then add final text in a design tool. If you do generate text, keep phrases short and unambiguous.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the rest of the image unchanged?
faqItems.answer: Constrain your edits by using boxes only where changes are desired and keep the global prompt neutral. Make boxes large enough to contain the intended subject, and avoid competing instructions in nearby regions.

87f3b4c32e4f.title: LTX-2: Text to Video

87f3b4c32e4f.metaDescription: Transform text into high-quality 4K videos with LTX-2. Supports Fast, Pro, and Ultra modes for diverse production needs. Easy and efficient video creation.

Crafting personalized video messages.

faqItems.question: What are the differences between Fast, Pro, and Ultra modes?

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for commercial purposes?

faqItems.question: What are the network requirements for using this workflow?

87fbc75b952a.title: Nano Banana 2.1: Image Edit
87fbc75b952a.description: Edit images with natural language and mask-based local edits powered by Nano Banana 2.1, taking one input image and returning one edited result alongside a side-by-side comparison view. Ideal for brand marketing posters, e-commerce product shots, and multi-round retouching where subjects and text must stay consistent.
87fbc75b952a.metaDescription: Compare prompt-only vs mask-guided edits in Nano Banana 2.1 using side-by-side before/after to pick the right method for branding and product imagery.
87fbc75b952a.extendedDescription:
This workflow compares two editing strategies in Nano Banana 2.1—prompt-only global edits versus mask-guided local edits—using a single model node (GeminiNanoBanana2V2) and a consistent pipeline. It loads your image (e.g., the provided silver_frame_profile.png), applies your natural-language edit, and renders a side-by-side before/after via ImageCompare so you can judge impact at a glance. Running once without a mask showcases broad, scene-wide transformations; running with a mask constrains changes to selected regions while preserving the rest.

Methodologically, you keep the same prompt and parameters and only toggle whether a mask is supplied to GeminiNanoBanana2V2. This isolates the effect of masking: global edits offer cohesive stylistic shifts but risk drifting subjects and text, while masked edits improve control and identity retention but may show edge artifacts if the mask is hard. SaveImageAdvanced preserves versioned outputs, and MarkdownNote helps you log prompts, mask intent, and observations across runs for repeatable, defensible comparisons.
howToUse: Load your input with LoadImage (start with silver_frame_profile.png if you want a known baseline). Enter a clear natural-language edit in GeminiNanoBanana2V2.
Run a global edit first: leave the mask input empty/disconnected. ImageCompare will show original vs edited for quick visual assessment.
Save the result with SaveImageAdvanced (e.g., add a suffix like _global) and record your prompt/notes in MarkdownNote.
Prepare a black/white mask where white = editable regions and black = protected content. Connect this mask to GeminiNanoBanana2V2 and rerun using the same prompt and parameters.
Review the masked run in ImageCompare, then save it (e.g., _masked). Compare trade-offs: check if identity, text, and layout remain stable; look for edge seams or color mismatch at mask boundaries.

If available in your setup, keep the seed fixed across runs to reduce randomness. Iterate by refining the mask (feathering, coverage) or tightening the prompt until the masked edit balances control and visual cohesion.
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce product retouching: Compare global color/style shifts against precise local edits (e.g., change background only) to preserve product fidelity.
Brand marketing posters: Test broad stylistic direction versus localized tweaks that respect logos, typography, and brand colors.
Portrait cleanup: Weigh full-scene enhancements against targeted edits (skin, teeth, background) to maintain subject identity.
Creative A/B testing: Rapidly prototype global vs localized variations before handing off to stakeholders.
Multi-round revisions: Use saved versions and notes to justify masked refinements over earlier global transformations.

faqItems.question: What exactly is being compared in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The same edit prompt is applied with and without a mask using the GeminiNanoBanana2V2 node (Nano Banana 2.1). The no-mask run shows global changes, while the masked run restricts edits to selected regions. ImageCompare visualizes before/after so you can evaluate control versus cohesion.

faqItems.question: When should I prefer mask-guided local edits over global edits?
faqItems.answer: Use masks when subject identity, product details, or text must remain stable. Masking limits unintended changes and drift. Choose global edits when you want coherent style or mood shifts across the entire image and minor variations are acceptable.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure a fair comparison between the two approaches?
faqItems.answer: Keep the prompt and all GeminiNanoBanana2V2 parameters identical across runs and change only the mask input. If your setup exposes a seed, fix it to reduce randomness. Save outputs with clear names and document settings in MarkdownNote.

faqItems.question: Why do I see seams or halos at the mask edge, and how can I reduce them?
faqItems.answer: Hard mask boundaries can create visible transitions. Use a softened/feathered mask edge, ensure color harmony in your prompt, and consider slightly expanding or refining the mask to blend the edited and protected regions more naturally.

88c94d64ca5d.title: Comfy for Advertising - Storyboard Creation
88c94d64ca5d.metaDescription: Create 6-panel ad storyboards from a shot list, then elevate them to styleframes using OpenAI or Gemini image nodes in ComfyUI.
88c94d64ca5d.extendedDescription: This ComfyUI workflow builds advertising storyboards fast by turning a plain 6‑panel grid and a shot list into clean black‑and‑white sketch frames, then optionally upgrades those sketches into production‑quality styleframes. The STORYBOARD GENERATOR group takes your shot descriptions from INPUT SHOT LIST, merges them with consistent style instructions via StringConcatenate, and feeds them to either OpenAIGPTImage1 (OpenAI’s gpt‑image‑1) or GeminiImage2Node for image generation. The first image you load is used as the panel grid reference, guiding the model to sketch simple line drawings inside each box and place the shot description as a caption beneath each frame. BatchImagesNode handles all six shots in one go, and SaveImage writes the finished storyboard to disk. MarkdownNote nodes in the graph provide in‑canvas guidance, while PrimitiveNode values set defaults like monochrome line style and panel count.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm your API credentials for OpenAIGPTImage1 and/or GeminiImage2Node are configured in their node settings.
In INPUT SHOT LIST, paste up to six clear shot descriptions (one per panel). Keep them concise and visual; leave a shot blank if you want that panel empty.
In INPUT SKETCH + MOODBOARD, LoadImage the storyboard grid as the first image (high-contrast boxes work best). Optionally add moodboard references to steer style later.
Choose your generator: enable either OpenAIGPTImage1 or GeminiImage2Node (bypass the one you’re not using). The StringConcatenate node already packages style guidance and each shot’s text.

Run the STORYBOARD GENERATOR group. BatchImagesNode will process all panels, producing a single 6-panel black-and-white sketch board with simple lines and per-frame captions. Inspect outputs from SaveImage.
Optional: For higher-fidelity visuals, pass the sketch and moodboard images into the STYLEFRAME GENERATOR group to produce production-quality stills, then SaveImage the results.
suggestedUseCases: Pitch decks and client reviews: fast, consistent 6-panel storyboards for TVC or social spots.
Internal previsualization: iterate on framing and product beats before committing to shoots.
Style exploration: convert a rough sketch board plus moodboard into polished keyframes.
E-commerce and product launches: storyboard hero shots and transitions for short ads.
Social cutdowns: quickly adapt a master shot list into multiple 6-panel narratives.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow keep a consistent black‑and‑white sketch style?
faqItems.answer: The StringConcatenate node injects shared style instructions (simple line art, monochrome, no intricate detail) into every panel prompt. Using one generator (OpenAIGPTImage1 or GeminiImage2Node) across the batch further stabilizes style.

faqItems.question: How do I switch between OpenAI and Gemini for generation?
faqItems.answer: Use the provided generator nodes and bypass the one you aren’t using. Both accept the same prompt and reference inputs prepared upstream, so you can A/B compare results without changing your shot list.

faqItems.question: Will it actually draw inside my grid and put Helvetica captions under each frame?
faqItems.answer: The first loaded image is used as the grid reference, and the prompt instructs the model to draw within boxes and place captions below in Helvetica. Generative models approximate typography; if you need exact fonts, add a text overlay/compositing step after generation.

faqItems.question: Can I change the number of panels or leave some blank?
faqItems.answer: This template targets a 6-panel board. You can leave a panel blank by providing no text for that shot. To change panel count, duplicate/adjust the BatchImagesNode path and update prompt text/layout guidance to match a new grid.

88f014a33e2a.title: Grok: Reference to Video
88f014a33e2a.description: Upload a reference image and generate a video using the Grok API, supporting up to 6 reference images for enhanced consistency.
