These images are then processed by the 'GrokVideoReferenceNode', which utilizes the Grok model to interpret and transform the static visuals into a coherent video sequence. Finally, the 'SaveVideo' node allows you to export the generated video for use in various applications.

What sets this workflow apart is its ability to handle multiple reference images, ensuring that the resulting video maintains a consistent style and character portrayal. This is particularly useful for projects requiring character animation or consistent artistic style across video frames. The Grok model's advanced capabilities allow for nuanced interpretation of the input images, making this workflow a powerful tool for creators looking to convert static art into engaging video content.
howToUse: Load the 'Grok: Reference to Video' workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the 'LoadImage' node to upload your reference images (up to 6).
Connect the images to the 'GrokVideoReferenceNode' to process them.
Configure the Grok model settings as needed for your project.
Run the workflow to generate the video.
Use the 'SaveVideo' node to export your final video output.
suggestedUseCases: Creating animated videos from character reference images for storytelling.
Developing consistent style videos for branding purposes.
Generating video content for social media from static art.
Animating concept art for visual presentations.
Producing educational videos with consistent character visuals.

faqItems.question: How many reference images can I use in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: You can use up to six reference images to enhance the consistency of the generated video.

faqItems.question: What is the role of the Grok model in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The Grok model interprets and transforms static reference images into a coherent video sequence, maintaining visual consistency.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the video output settings?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can configure the Grok model settings within the workflow to tailor the video output to your needs.

faqItems.question: What formats are supported for exporting the video?
faqItems.answer: The 'SaveVideo' node allows you to export the video in standard formats such as MP4, suitable for most applications.

8911701d2fed.title: HY Image 3.5 Preview: Image Edit
8911701d2fed.description: Edit images with the HY Image 3.5 Preview model, which deeply understands user intent through optimized text-and-image organization to deliver high-quality results. Takes 1 image input and produces 1 image output. Ideal for portrait editing, commercial posters, and film/TV marketing materials.
8911701d2fed.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: edit a single image via HY Image 3.5 Preview using HunyuanImageEditApi. Load, prompt, and export high-quality edits with SaveImageAdvanced.
8911701d2fed.extendedDescription:
This workflow demonstrates prompt-guided image editing with the HY Image 3.5 Preview model using ComfyUI. It takes one source image, interprets a natural‑language instruction, and returns a single edited image. The core of the graph is the HunyuanImageEditApi node, which sends your image and prompt to the HY Image 3.5 Preview service for multimodal understanding and edit synthesis. LoadImage brings your source (for example, the provided futuristic_brutalist_motorcycle.png), and SaveImageAdvanced writes the result to disk with your preferred filename and format. A MarkdownNote in the canvas provides quick inline tips and links.

Technically, the workflow preserves the input image as a visual anchor while the HunyuanImageEditApi aligns your text prompt to the existing scene. This lets you direct high‑level changes (materials, colorways, backgrounds, lighting, mood) without manually masking or compositing. Because the inference runs through an API, you get consistent edits without managing local model weights, and SaveImageAdvanced gives you control over output naming, format, and quality for production handoff. It’s a practical setup for portrait cleanup, product/hero image variations, and fast turnarounds on marketing visuals.
howToUse: Open ComfyUI (updated to the latest version) and load the workflow titled "HY Image 3.5 Preview: Image Edit".
In the LoadImage node, select your source image (try the provided futuristic_brutalist_motorcycle.png to follow along).

Open the HunyuanImageEditApi node and enter a clear, specific prompt describing what to change and what to keep (e.g., "Keep the motorcycle’s shape and angle; change the body to matte black carbon fiber with neon-blue accents; dusk lighting; wet pavement reflections"). If the node requires an API key or endpoint, add it in the node or ComfyUI settings.
Optionally configure SaveImageAdvanced (subfolder, filename pattern, format/quality).
Click Queue Prompt to run. Inspect the output image; if needed, refine your prompt (simplify conflicting instructions, add camera/lighting cues) and re-queue.
Repeat prompt tweaks until satisfied, then export final assets via SaveImageAdvanced to your desired folder and format.
suggestedUseCases: Portrait and headshot refinement (lighting/style changes, background adjustments) without manual masking.
Product and hero image variations for ecommerce and ads (materials, colorways, backgrounds).
Key art and poster iterations for campaigns, film/TV, and events with consistent composition.
Concept art polish from a photographed mockup to a stylized, presentation‑ready visual.
Thumbnail and social creative refreshes that keep subject framing while changing style or mood.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key or internet access for HunyuanImageEditApi?
faqItems.answer: Yes. HunyuanImageEditApi sends your image and prompt to the HY Image 3.5 Preview service, so an internet connection is required. If the node exposes API credentials or an endpoint field, enter them as instructed by the node’s tooltip or your provider’s docs.

faqItems.question: How should I write prompts for consistent, controlled edits?
faqItems.answer: Be explicit about both changes and constraints. Include "keep" statements (e.g., keep pose, angle, composition), specify materials/colors/lighting, and avoid conflicting directives. Start simple, verify the result, then incrementally add detail.

faqItems.question: What image sizes work best?
faqItems.answer: Use a reasonably sized input (e.g., 1–4 MP) to balance detail and speed. Extremely large images increase upload time and may be resized by the API. If you see cropping or scaling artifacts, try resizing to a standard aspect and re-run.

faqItems.question: How do I preserve subject identity and composition?
faqItems.answer: Anchor the edit by referencing what must remain unchanged (e.g., "keep the same bike shape and camera angle"). Avoid style prompts that imply a full scene replacement when you only want local changes. If the node offers a strength or preserve-structure control, keep it conservative to maintain the original layout.

893dc06973b0.title: Pose Map: SDPose-OOD
893dc06973b0.description: Upload an image to extract pose keypoints and generate a corresponding pose map using the SDPose-OOD model.
893dc06973b0.metaDescription: Extract whole-body keypoints and generate a pose map from any image in ComfyUI using the SDPose-OOD model. Fast, aligned pose maps for pose-guided workflows.
893dc06973b0.extendedDescription:
Pose Map: SDPose-OOD is a simple ComfyUI workflow that turns a reference photo into a clean pose map. It loads your image with LoadImage, runs whole-body 2D keypoint detection using the SDPose-OOD model (checkpoint: sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors), and saves the rendered skeleton map via SaveImage. The custom SDPose node in this workflow (01b6a731-fb78-4070-9a38-c87146da9604) extracts body, hand, and facial keypoints and draws a pose map aligned to your input image.

Technically, the SDPose-OOD model infers pose keypoints and composites them into a single pose image that’s immediately usable as a conditioning input in downstream pipelines (for example, pose-guided generation with ControlNet/OpenPose-like inputs). Because the pose map is generated at the input resolution, it preserves spatial alignment and limb proportions, making it ideal for consistent re-posing, style transfer with pose control, or building a pose reference library. The included MarkdownNote in the canvas provides quick in-UI guidance and model links.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI (drag the file onto the canvas). You’ll see LoadImage → SDPose-OOD (01b6a731-…) → SaveImage, plus a MarkdownNote.

Download the sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors checkpoint from the Comfy-Org/SDPose repository. Place it in the SDPose model folder used by your node (check the model dropdown/path in the SDPose-OOD node UI, then refresh models).
In LoadImage, select your input photo. For best results, use an image where the subject’s body and limbs are clearly visible with minimal occlusion.

Open the SDPose-OOD node (01b6a731-…). Choose the sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors checkpoint. Keep other settings at defaults for a first run; ensure the node is set to run on your GPU if available for speed.
In SaveImage, set a filename prefix and (optionally) an output subfolder. Queue the workflow. The node will extract keypoints and render a pose map aligned to your input.
Inspect the saved pose map in ComfyUI/output. You can now feed this map into pose-conditioned generation workflows (e.g., ControlNet/OpenPose-compatible nodes) for consistent re-posing.
suggestedUseCases: Create pose condition maps for pose-guided image generation and character re-posing.
Build a personal library of consistent pose references for concept art, storyboards, and illustration.
Pre-visualize and compare body mechanics across photo takes before animation or motion studies.
Prepare training or validation visuals when curating datasets that depend on body keypoints.
Generate clean pose inputs to drive style transfer while preserving subject posture.

faqItems.question: Where do I put the sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors file?
faqItems.answer: Place it in the SDPose model directory that the SDPose-OOD node reads from. Open the node, check the model dropdown or path hint, and put the file there. After copying, refresh models or restart ComfyUI so it appears in the list.

faqItems.question: What images work best for accurate pose maps?
faqItems.answer: Images with a clearly visible subject, good lighting, and minimal occlusion. For whole-body maps, include the full figure (head, hands, feet). If multiple people are present, crop to the main subject for the most reliable result.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow support multiple people in one image?
faqItems.answer: The workflow is designed to extract a clean pose map for the primary subject. With multiple people, detection may be less consistent. For multi-person scenes, run separate crops per person to get individual pose maps.

faqItems.question: Do I need a GPU to run SDPose-OOD?
faqItems.answer: A GPU is strongly recommended for speed and to take advantage of the FP16 checkpoint. CPU inference may work but will be significantly slower and may not support half-precision performance benefits.

894c44a995a2.title: Wan2.7: Video Edit
894c44a995a2.description: Upload a video and corresponding images to edit and replace characters or scenes using the Wan2.7 model.
894c44a995a2.metaDescription: Edit videos by swapping characters or scenes using reference images with Wan2.7 in ComfyUI. Load video/images, configure Wan2VideoEditApi, and export.
894c44a995a2.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates reference-guided video editing with Wan2.7. You load a source clip with LoadVideo, provide one or more reference images with LoadImage, and let the Wan2VideoEditApi node apply character or scene replacements consistently across frames. The node calls the Wan2.7 model to infer identity, attire, and style cues from your references, then synthesizes edited frames that preserve the original camera motion and timing. Finally, SaveVideo assembles the frames into a finished MP4/WEBM with your chosen frame rate and quality.

Technically, the Wan2VideoEditApi node takes three essential inputs: the decoded video frames, the reference image tensor(s), and your textual directions (prompt and optional constraints). It uses the Wan2.7 backbone to align reference identity/style with the target footage while maintaining temporal coherence, so edits remain stable over time rather than flickering frame to frame. This makes the workflow especially useful for swapping a character across an entire shot or re-dressing a scene without rotoscoping. The minimalist node set—LoadVideo → LoadImage → Wan2VideoEditApi → SaveVideo—keeps the pipeline simple while still offering strong control through prompts, reference choice, and edit strength settings exposed by the API node.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and verify the four core nodes are present: LoadVideo, LoadImage, Wan2VideoEditApi, and SaveVideo. Ensure Wan2.7 is selected in the API node if a model selector is available.
In LoadVideo, choose your source clip. Short clips (5–10 seconds) are ideal for first runs. If the node exposes trim or frame range, set it to test a small segment before processing the full video.

Add one or more LoadImage nodes and pick high-quality reference images for the character or scene you want to introduce. Prefer images that match the target clip’s angle, lighting, and pose. Connect the LoadImage outputs to the reference inputs on Wan2VideoEditApi.

Open Wan2VideoEditApi and enter a clear prompt describing the desired replacement (e.g., the character’s outfit, identity, or scene style). If available, adjust controls like negative text, edit strength/blend, guidance, and seed to balance fidelity to the original video versus the reference.
Connect the edited video output from Wan2VideoEditApi to SaveVideo. In SaveVideo, choose your output format and frame rate—matching the source fps often yields the most natural motion.

Click Queue Prompt to run. Review the result; if identity or style wavers, improve reference images (closer angle/lighting), refine your prompt, or reduce edit strength. Re-run on the full clip once you’re satisfied.
suggestedUseCases: Character replacement for social content or short films without manual rotoscoping.
Wardrobe or style swaps (e.g., turning a casual outfit into a uniform) while preserving original performance.
Background or scene re-dressing to match a storyboard, season, or theme.
Brand or product visualization by placing a consistent style/look across a sequence.
Continuity fixes when reshoots aren’t possible, e.g., adjusting props or attire across takes.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key or internet connection for Wan2VideoEditApi?
faqItems.answer: The Wan2VideoEditApi node typically calls a remote Wan2.7 service, which may require credentials and an active internet connection. Check the node’s settings or your ComfyUI extension docs to configure any required keys.

faqItems.question: How can I get stable identity and fewer artifacts?
faqItems.answer: Use high-resolution reference images that match the video’s angle and lighting, keep prompts specific (describe attire, colors, and style), and tune the edit strength to avoid overdriving the look. If your node exposes a seed, lock it for reproducibility.

faqItems.question: Can I edit only part of a video?
faqItems.answer: Yes. If LoadVideo or the API node exposes a frame range, use it to test or limit the edit. Otherwise, trim the source clip externally before loading it, then process just that segment in ComfyUI.

faqItems.question: Does the exported video include audio?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo in ComfyUI generally exports silent video. To keep audio, export the edited clip and then remux the original audio track using a video editor or a tool like FFmpeg.

895960b69952.title: Kling O1: Video Edit
895960b69952.description: Edit videos with natural language commands, featuring video reference mode for quick generation of high-quality style transfers, element additions, and background modifications.
895960b69952.metaDescription: Edit videos using natural language commands for style transfers, element additions, and background modifications with Kling O1: Video Edit workflow.
895960b69952.extendedDescription:
The Kling O1: Video Edit workflow is designed to transform video editing by leveraging natural language commands. This workflow utilizes the Kling model, allowing users to perform high-quality style transfers, add elements, and modify backgrounds in videos with ease. At the core of this workflow are nodes like LoadImage, SaveVideo, and KlingOmniProEditVideoNode, which facilitate the seamless integration of reference images and videos. The workflow is particularly effective in scenarios where quick and precise video edits are required, making it a valuable tool for both amateur and professional video editors.

Technically, the workflow begins by loading video components using the LoadVideo and GetVideoComponents nodes. Users can input up to four reference images when providing video input, or up to seven when using image input. The KlingOmniProEditVideoNode processes these inputs, applying the desired edits based on natural language commands. Finally, the CreateVideo and SaveVideo nodes compile and save the edited video, ensuring a smooth and efficient editing process. This workflow's ability to interpret and execute complex editing tasks through simple commands makes it a powerful asset in video production.
howToUse: Load the Kling O1: Video Edit workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadVideo node to import your video file.

8b24ee5765ae.title: Fish Audio: Text to Speech
8b24ee5765ae.description: Generate natural, expressive speech from text with Fish Audio S2 Pro, a text-to-speech model supporting 80+ languages and fine-grained control over emotion, tone, and pacing using inline tags like [whisper] or [excited]. 8b24ee5765ae.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow for Fish Audio S2 Pro TTS. Use preset voices or instant voice cloning, inline style tags, and save high‑quality audio in minutes.
8b24ee5765ae.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns written scripts into natural, expressive speech using the Fish Audio S2 Pro text‑to‑speech model. It supports over 80 languages and lets you direct performance with inline style tags (for example, adding [whisper] or [excited] directly in your text). The core path runs your text through the FishAudioTextToSpeech node and saves a single high‑quality audio file via SaveAudioAdvanced.

You can choose between two voice sources. Option 1 (Preset Audio) uses FishAudioVoiceSelector to supply a curated, ready‑to‑use voice to the TTS node. Option 2 (Voice Clone) uses LoadAudio plus FishAudioInstantVoiceClone to create a temporary voice profile from a short reference clip, then feeds that cloned voice to FishAudioTextToSpeech. Toggle between these options by enabling the corresponding workflow group (Ctrl‑B). A MarkdownNote node on the canvas provides quick reminders, while SaveAudioAdvanced writes the generated speech to disk in your chosen format. Because this uses API nodes, processing happens on the Fish Audio service and is pay‑per‑use once you’re signed in.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and sign in to your account. API nodes (FishAudio*) require authentication and are pay‑per‑use.

Pick your voice source: enable Option 1: Preset Audio (default) to use FishAudioVoiceSelector, or enable Option 2: Voice Clone (select the group and press Ctrl‑B) to use LoadAudio + FishAudioInstantVoiceClone. Only enable one option at a time.
For preset voices: open FishAudioVoiceSelector and choose a voice. It will feed a voice ID to FishAudioTextToSpeech automatically.
For instant cloning: load a clean reference clip (speech only) with LoadAudio, then run FishAudioInstantVoiceClone to produce a temporary voice token/ID that connects to FishAudioTextToSpeech.
Enter your script in the text field of FishAudioTextToSpeech. Add inline tags like [whisper] or [excited] directly in the text where you want style changes. Then queue the workflow to generate audio.
In SaveAudioAdvanced, set your output filename and format (e.g., WAV/MP3) and run. Check the node’s output path for the saved file. Iterate by adjusting text, tags, or voice and re‑queue.
suggestedUseCases: Multilingual voiceovers for tutorials, product demos, and explainer videos
Character dialogue for games, animations, or storyboards using cloned or preset voices
Podcast intros, ad reads, and quick pick‑ups without re‑recording
Rapid localization of training content across 80+ supported languages
Temp VO for animatics and client reviews before final studio recordings

faqItems.question: How do the inline style tags work?
faqItems.answer: Place a tag like [whisper] or [excited] directly in your script before the words you want to affect. The FishAudioTextToSpeech node forwards your text to the Fish Audio S2 Pro API, which interprets these tags to adjust tone, emotion, and pacing. For the full list of supported tags and syntax, consult the Fish Audio documentation.

faqItems.question: What’s the difference between preset voices and instant voice cloning?
faqItems.answer: Preset voices (FishAudioVoiceSelector) are curated, consistent, and ready to use. Instant cloning (LoadAudio + FishAudioInstantVoiceClone) adapts the TTS to a short reference clip so you can match a specific speaker. Cloning quality depends on the reference audio—clean speech with minimal noise typically yields better results.

faqItems.question: How long and what type of reference audio should I use for voice cloning?
faqItems.answer: Use 5–30 seconds of clear, solo speech with no music or heavy reverb. A dry, well‑recorded segment where the speaker talks at a natural pace works best. Load this file in the LoadAudio node, then run FishAudioInstantVoiceClone to generate the voice profile for the TTS node.

faqItems.question: Are there costs or limits when using this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Fish Audio API nodes are pay‑per‑use and require you to be signed in. Usage, quotas, and pricing are managed by your account with the service. If requests fail, check your authentication status, balance, and any rate limits in your account.

Common steps inside this kind of node include detecting clothing regions, pose-aware alignment/warping, and clean blending to avoid artifacts around edges. Because everything runs inside ComfyUI, you can iterate quickly by swapping inputs, adjusting the node’s settings (if exposed in your build), and re-queuing to refine fit, coverage, and output size.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the three core nodes: two LoadImage nodes (Character and Outfit), the Clothes Changer node (a41effc1-fe4c-4b79-a70d-9b7388ef6a23), and the SaveImage node.

Provide inputs: drop your character/person image into the Character LoadImage node, and your outfit reference image into the Outfit LoadImage node. Prefer clear, front-facing images with the full garment visible.
Optional prep: crop or center both images so the subject and garment are well framed. Matching aspect ratios between inputs helps the Clothes Changer node align and blend more cleanly.
Run the graph: queue/execute the workflow. The Clothes Changer node will align the outfit to the character’s pose and composite the clothing onto the person, then pass the result to SaveImage.
Save and review: set a filename prefix in the SaveImage node if desired, then find your output in ComfyUI/output. Inspect the result and iterate by swapping outfits or refining inputs.
Iterate for best fit: if the Clothes Changer node exposes controls (e.g., output size or blend strength), start with defaults, then adjust incrementally to improve edge quality and garment coverage.
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce mockups to preview garments on different body types without a full photoshoot
Character design and concept art to test costume variations fast
Wardrobe planning or cosplay previews to visualize outfits before buying or crafting
Social media content and thumbnails that need quick outfit swaps on the same subject
Marketing A/B tests showing multiple outfit options on the same model

faqItems.question: What image resolutions work best?
faqItems.answer: Use clear, well-lit images between 768–1536 px on the shortest side. Keep both character and outfit images at comparable sizes to help alignment and reduce artifacts.

faqItems.question: Does it change the person’s face or body?
faqItems.answer: The Clothes Changer node is designed to preserve identity (face, hair, and body structure) and only replace clothing. Minor blending around edges may occur; better framing and higher-resolution inputs help.

faqItems.question: Can I use outfit photos with busy backgrounds?
faqItems.answer: Yes, but results are usually cleaner when the garment is well-separated from the background. Flat-lay images or on-model shots with clear contrast work best. Front-facing garments generally align more reliably.

faqItems.question: Where are my results saved?
faqItems.answer: The SaveImage node writes files to the ComfyUI/output folder. Set the filename prefix in the SaveImage node to keep versions organized.

8d3a504fd30d.title: Seedance2.5: Video Editing
8d3a504fd30d.description: Edit existing video clips with Seedance 2.5 by describing changes in natural language, enabling local object removal, background swaps, scene replacements, and style transfers while preserving the original composition and motion. Feed in 1 video and receive 1 edited video output with temporally consistent results across frames. Ideal for e-commerce background replacement, stylized remakes of footage, and ad re-editing with targeted retouching.
8d3a504fd30d.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: edit videos with natural language using Seedance 2.5. Load, slice, and export consistent video edits via ByteDance2ReferenceNode.
8d3a504fd30d.extendedDescription:
Seedance2.5: Video Editing is a text-driven video-to-video editor built in ComfyUI. It loads your source clip with LoadVideo, optionally trims it with Video Slice, and sends the frames to ByteDance2ReferenceNode running Seedance 2.5 in video_editing mode. You describe the change in plain language—such as “replace the background with a minimalist white studio” or “remove the product label and keep everything else the same”—and the model returns a single, temporally consistent edited clip.

Technically, ByteDance2ReferenceNode handles the model/API call and enforces frame-to-frame coherence so objects, lighting, and motion remain stable as the edit carries across time. The workflow inherits the aspect ratio and duration from your input (per the video_editing mode behavior and author notes), preserving original composition and timing while applying local object removal, background swaps, scene replacements, or style transfers. MarkdownNote provides in-graph guidance, and SaveVideo assembles the processed frames into your final output video.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm ByteDance2ReferenceNode is configured (API access or credentials as required by your setup).
Load your source clip with LoadVideo. Scrub or preview to confirm the input is correct.
Optionally trim the clip with Video Slice to focus the edit on a specific range (shorter segments process faster and reduce artifacts).

In ByteDance2ReferenceNode, toggle video_editing to ON and enter a concise instruction describing the change you want (e.g., “replace the background with a clean white studio” or “remove the logo on the box”).
Queue the workflow. The node will process the frames and return an edited sequence with the same aspect and duration as the input. SaveVideo will write the final clip.
Review the result. If needed, refine your instruction (be specific and avoid conflicting requests), adjust the slice range, and re-run for improved consistency.
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce background replacement to unify product listings without reshoots
Targeted ad re-edits (e.g., logo removal, quick color/style harmonization) for regional campaigns
Stylized remakes of existing footage while preserving the original motion and composition
Scene or set replacements in pre-visualization and storyboarding
Localized clean-ups (e.g., object or text removal) across an entire shot

faqItems.question: What does the video_editing toggle do?
faqItems.answer: It switches the model into edit mode so the output follows your source video’s composition, motion, aspect, and timing. Your text instruction is applied as a guided change rather than generating a completely new video.

faqItems.question: Will the output keep the same duration and aspect ratio?
faqItems.answer: Yes. In video_editing mode, the workflow inherits the input video’s aspect and duration, so timing and framing remain intact while the edit is applied.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce flicker or inconsistencies across frames?
faqItems.answer: Keep instructions concise and unambiguous, work on shorter slices with Video Slice (avoid hard cuts within the same run), and iterate in small steps. If the node exposes quality/consistency controls, prefer defaults or moderate values rather than extreme settings.

faqItems.question: Does the workflow preserve audio?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo typically outputs a silent clip in ComfyUI. If you need audio, export the edited video and reattach the original soundtrack in a video editor.

faqItems.question: Any tips on performance and limits?
faqItems.answer: Because ByteDance2ReferenceNode uses an API, processing time depends on clip length, resolution, and network speed. For faster, more stable edits, start with 5–15 second segments at 720p–1080p. If you encounter errors or long waits, reduce duration or resolution.

faqItems.question: What formats are supported for audio input?

faqItems.question: Can I edit the transcribed text within the workflow?

faqItems.question: How accurate is the transcription from the ElevenLabs model?

8e090ccf5a29.title: AI on the Lot 2026 - Z-Image Turbo - t2i

8e090ccf5a29.metaDescription: ComfyUI Z-Image Turbo text-to-image workflow using Qwen 3 4B text encoder; simple T2I with SaveImage output and reproducible seeds.
8e090ccf5a29.extendedDescription:
This template is a compact, text-to-image workflow built around the Z-Image Turbo generator, designed to get from prompt to output with minimal setup. At its core is a single custom Z-Image Turbo T2I node (node id f2fdebf6-dfaf-43b6-9eb2-7f70613cfdc1) that encapsulates text encoding and image generation, paired with a SaveImage node to write results to disk and a MarkdownNote for in-graph guidance. The template is configured to use the Qwen 3 4B text encoder weights (qwen_3_4b.safetensors) for prompt conditioning.

Technically, the Z-Image Turbo node handles the end-to-end generation: it ingests your prompt (and optional negative prompt), encodes it with the specified text encoder, and runs the model’s internal sampler to produce an image tensor. That tensor is passed directly to SaveImage, which exports PNGs to your ComfyUI output folder using the configured filename prefix. Because the heavy lifting is wrapped in a single node, you get a clean, reliable T2I pipeline that’s easy to iterate: tweak prompts, resolution, seed, and sampling controls in one place, then save consistent, reproducible outputs.
howToUse: Load the "AI on the Lot 2026 - Z-Image Turbo - t2i" template in ComfyUI and review the MarkdownNote for any in-graph instructions or links.
Download qwen_3_4b.safetensors from the provided model link and place it in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders (create the folder if needed). Restart ComfyUI so the node can find it.

Open the Z-Image Turbo T2I node (id f2fdebf6-dfaf-43b6-9eb2-7f70613cfdc1) and fill in your Prompt (and optional Negative Prompt). Set resolution, seed (or -1 for random), and other exposed sampling controls as desired.

Start with moderate settings for speed and quality balance (e.g., a mid-size resolution and default sampling values). Increase steps or adjust guidance/CFG only as needed to refine detail or adherence to the prompt.
Run the queue. The node will generate images and pass them to SaveImage, which writes PNGs to your ComfyUI output directory. Adjust the SaveImage filename prefix if you want clearer organization.
Iterate: refine your prompt phrasing, lock the seed for consistent variations, and use a negative prompt to suppress unwanted elements. Re-run until you reach the look you want.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept art and style studies from short text prompts
Product or packaging mockups to explore form, color, and materials
Storyboard frames and previsualization for film or animation
Mood boards and look development for branding or UI themes
Illustrations for articles, blogs, and creative writing prompts

faqItems.question: Where do I put qwen_3_4b.safetensors so the node can find it?
faqItems.answer: Place qwen_3_4b.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders, then restart ComfyUI. Verify the filename matches exactly and that the Z-Image Turbo node points to the correct encoder if a selector is exposed.

faqItems.question: How do I get repeatable results for the same prompt?
faqItems.answer: Set a fixed seed value in the Z-Image Turbo node instead of using random (-1). Keep resolution and sampling controls the same; then re-run to reproduce the same image or make controlled variations by changing only one parameter at a time.

faqItems.question: I’m running out of VRAM or generation is slow. What should I change?
faqItems.answer: Lower the resolution, reduce batch size (if exposed), and keep sampling steps modest. These changes reduce memory and time while preserving most of the visual quality for drafts.

faqItems.question: My images aren’t saving. How do I fix SaveImage issues?
faqItems.answer: Open the SaveImage node and confirm the output directory is valid and writable. Adjust the filename prefix if needed, and re-run the queue. On some systems, creating the output folder manually can resolve permissions or path issues.

8f2837a9a7fc.title: Image Upscale: Recraft Crisp

8f2837a9a7fc.metaDescription: Restore and upscale images in ComfyUI using Recraft Crisp. Reduce noise, enhance details, and compare results side-by-side with ImageCompare.

Technically, the Recraft Crisp upscaler applies model-driven super-resolution with artifact reduction to retain a natural look—far beyond simple bicubic resizing. The pipeline is intentionally minimal to preserve source fidelity: LoadImage -> RecraftCrispUpscaleNode -> SaveImage, with MarkdownNote included for quick reminders on file and resolution limits. This makes it a dependable drop-in step for production image cleanup, portfolio prep, and pre-press upscaling where consistency matters.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI. If you plan to use the side-by-side viewer, enable Nodes 2.0 (Menu -> Nodes 2.0) so ImageCompare is available.
Open the MarkdownNote for quick tips and constraints, then set up LoadImage with your input (<= 5MB, <= 2048×2048). If needed, pre-resize or lightly denoise before loading.
Select the RecraftCrispUpscaleNode and leave defaults for a balanced result. If the node exposes controls (e.g., scale or sharpening), adjust cautiously and preview changes.
Confirm SaveImage has a clear filename pattern and output directory. Optionally wire ImageCompare to visualize original vs. upscaled output.
Queue and run the workflow. Inspect the ImageCompare output (Nodes 2.0) to verify detail recovery and artifact reduction.

Digital art and illustrations: restore scanned or exported assets for print or large-format displays.
Mobile photos and screenshots: cleanly enlarge for presentations or documentation without oversharpening.

Game and 3D textures: enhance small textures for prototypes or modding with a crisp, natural finish.

faqItems.question: What are the input limits for this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Per the author notes, the input should be <= 5MB and <= 2048×2048 pixels. If your image exceeds these limits, downscale or compress it first, or split it into tiles before processing.

faqItems.question: Do I need Nodes 2.0 to run the workflow?
faqItems.answer: No. Nodes 2.0 is only required for ImageCompare. The core path (LoadImage -> RecraftCrispUpscaleNode -> SaveImage) runs without Nodes 2.0. Enable Nodes 2.0 (Menu -> Nodes 2.0) if you want the side-by-side comparison.

faqItems.question: Will Recraft Crisp invent new details?
faqItems.answer: It performs model-based super-resolution and artifact reduction to recover and clarify structure, but it won’t plausibly hallucinate complex missing content. Severely blurred or heavily compressed inputs may see limited restoration.

faqItems.question: Can I run this via the ComfyUI API?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Use ComfyUI’s /prompt HTTP API with the workflow JSON. Ensure the LoadImage node points to an accessible file on the server (or adapt the graph to your upload method). ImageCompare is UI-oriented and can be omitted in headless/API runs.

8f2cf0df5da6.title: LTX Cleanplate for VFX
8f2cf0df5da6.description: Prompt an object, and SAM3 + LTX 2.3 mask-conditioned inpainting remove it and rebuild the clean background plate."
8f2cf0df5da6.metaDescription: Create clean plates for VFX: SAM3 masks + LTX 2.3 mask-conditioned inpainting remove objects and rebuild background in ComfyUI.
8f2cf0df5da6.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds a clean background plate by removing an object from video using SAM3-driven masks and a mask-conditioned LTX-2.3 In‑Outpainting IC‑LoRA. The pipeline loads your clip with VHS_LoadVideo/VHS_VideoInfo, extracts frames via GetVideoComponents, and uses LoadSAM3Model → SAM3VideoSegmentation to seed a mask for the object you want to remove. SAM3Propagate tracks that mask across the shot, and SAM3VideoOutput provides a per‑frame OBJECT_MASK. To ensure seamless fills, LTXVDilateVideoMask expands the mask (e.g., s10/t1) and GrowMaskWithBlur feathers the edges.

The masked region is then green‑filled by LTXVInpaintPreprocess, and CreateVideo re‑encodes those preprocessed frames. That green plate, together with the OBJECT_MASK and your minimal background‑only prompt, feeds the LTX 2.3 In‑Outpainting IC‑LoRA (packaged here as a subgraph node), which is explicitly mask‑conditioned to generate only inside the masked area. Utility nodes like VHS_GetImageCount, ComfyMathExpression, and GetImageRangeFromBatch let you preview limited frame ranges before a full run. Finally, SaveVideo writes the cleanplate result for downstream compositing.
howToUse: Load the workflow, then import your source clip with VHS_LoadVideo. Confirm resolution and FPS with VHS_VideoInfo/GetVideoComponents.

In the SAM3 MASK group: load your SAM3 weights with LoadSAM3Model. Use SAM3VideoSegmentation to mark the object on a clear reference frame (positive/negative points or a box, as supported), then run SAM3Propagate to track the mask. Preview masks with SAM3VideoOutput/MaskToImage.
Refine the mask edges: increase LTXVDilateVideoMask size (start around 10) to cover motion blur/parallax and add feathering with GrowMaskWithBlur (e.g., 12–16 px) to avoid hard seams.

In LOAD FOOTAGE / SET PROMPT TO REMOVE: keep the text prompt empty or describe only the background inside the hole (never the entire scene). Example: “brick wall and window frame, soft shadows, no person.”

Run GENERATE. LTXVInpaintPreprocess will green‑fill the masked area; CreateVideo re‑encodes this guide plate; the LTX 2.3 In‑Outpainting IC‑LoRA subgraph uses the plate and OBJECT_MASK to synthesize new content only inside the hole.

Review the output and save with SaveVideo. If artifacts persist, increase dilation or feather, adjust the prompt to focus on background cues, or test a shorter range using VHS_GetImageCount + GetImageRangeFromBatch before re‑running the full clip.
suggestedUseCases: Building a clean background plate for compositing after removing talent, crew, or boom reflections.
Location cleanup: erase signage, rigs, cables, or production gear from tracking shots.
Product/video retouching: remove labels or stickers while restoring underlying surfaces.
Crowd/object removal in establishing shots where a consistent background can be reconstructed.
Prep plates for 2D/3D inserts by clearing foreground obstructions.

faqItems.question: How should I write the prompt for best results?
faqItems.answer: Keep it empty or describe only the background inside the masked area (e.g., “asphalt road with painted lines, soft shadow”). Avoid mentioning the removed object or unrelated foreground items—this can cause duplication or hallucinations.

faqItems.question: My edges flicker or show seams. What should I tweak?
faqItems.answer: Increase LTXVDilateVideoMask size to cover motion blur and expand beyond the object, then raise GrowMaskWithBlur feather radius to soften transitions. Also re‑seed SAM3 on a clearer frame and re‑propagate if the tracked mask drifts.

faqItems.question: Can I test a short section before processing the full video?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Use VHS_GetImageCount to see the total frames and GetImageRangeFromBatch (optionally with ComfyMathExpression) to select a small frame window for quick iterations, then switch back to the full range once satisfied.

faqItems.question: Does the saved video include audio?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo typically outputs a silent file. If you need audio, re‑mux the original track in your NLE or a tool like ffmpeg. If your setup routes audio via GetVideoComponents, you can also handle pass‑through externally after render.

8f381a482443.title: Kling2.6: Motion Control

8f381a482443.metaDescription: Apply precise character actions from a reference video to your image using Kling2.6 for synchronized motion control.

The 'Kling2.6: Motion Control' workflow is designed to help users apply precise character actions and expressions from a reference video to a character image. This workflow leverages the capabilities of the Kling 2.6 model to synchronize motion control, making it highly effective for animators and video editors who need to create realistic character animations. The workflow begins with the LoadVideo node, which imports the reference video containing the desired motions. The KlingMotionControl node is the core of this workflow, where the motion data is extracted and applied to the character image loaded via the LoadImage node. Finally, the SaveVideo node outputs the animated character video, ensuring that the character's movements are in perfect harmony with the reference video.

This workflow is particularly useful for its ability to maintain the integrity of character expressions and actions, ensuring that the animation looks natural and fluid. By using the Kling model, which is renowned for its precise motion capture capabilities, the workflow allows for detailed motion control that can be customized to fit various animation needs. The inclusion of the MarkdownNote node provides users with the ability to annotate and document their workflow process, making it easier to replicate or modify for future projects.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure all necessary nodes are connected.
Use the LoadVideo node to import your reference video, ensuring it contains the desired motions.
Import your character image using the LoadImage node, keeping the image ratio similar to the video.
Configure the KlingMotionControl node to map the video motions to your character image.
Run the workflow to process the animation and use the SaveVideo node to export the final video.
suggestedUseCases: Creating animated character sequences for video games.
Developing realistic character animations for film production.
Synchronizing character movements for virtual reality applications.
Producing educational videos with animated characters demonstrating specific actions.
Enhancing social media content with dynamic character animations.

faqItems.question: Can I use any video as a reference for motion control?
faqItems.answer: Yes, but for best results, ensure the video is clear and the actions are distinct. The KlingMotionControl node works best with videos that have a clear view of the movements you wish to replicate.

faqItems.question: Do I need to adjust the aspect ratio of the image and video?
faqItems.answer: It's recommended to keep the image and video at a similar ratio to ensure the character's movements are accurately mapped and look natural.

faqItems.question: What if the character image is only half-body?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports both full-body and half-body character images. Ensure the reference video matches the type of character image for optimal results.

faqItems.question: How can I document my workflow process?
faqItems.answer: Use the MarkdownNote node to add annotations and notes throughout your workflow. This will help you keep track of settings and modifications for future use.

8f82ff60ae5e.title: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash: Video Edit
8f82ff60ae5e.description: Edit videos through natural language conversation with Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash. Upload a clip (10 seconds or less) and describe the change: swap backgrounds, restyle scenes, add or remove elements, and the model applies the edit while preserving everything you did not mention. Add \"Keep everything else the same\" for maximum consistency; simple prompts work best. Outputs video with native audio at 16:9 or 9:16, with 1080p/4K output available. Ideal for remixes, style changes, and iterative refinement without re-generating from scratch.
8f82ff60ae5e.metaDescription: Edit 10s videos by prompt with Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash in ComfyUI. Swap backgrounds, restyle, and export 16:9 or 9:16 with audio at 1080p/4K.
8f82ff60ae5e.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow lets you edit a short video by simply describing the change you want. LoadVideo ingests your clip (the template includes input/hooded_wanderer_planet_bridge.mp4 as a ready-to-run test), and GeminiVideoOmniV2 sends both the video and your plain‑language instruction to Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash. The model applies targeted edits—like swapping backgrounds, restyling a scene, or adding/removing elements—while leaving everything else untouched. For maximum fidelity, include a line such as “Keep everything else the same.” Simple, direct prompts tend to produce the most consistent results.

On output, SaveVideo writes the edited clip to disk with the native audio preserved. You can choose 16:9 or 9:16 and render at 1080p or 4K, making it suitable for landscape or vertical content. A MarkdownNote in the graph provides quick tips. The recommended input duration is 10 seconds or less to ensure responsive processing and stable edits. This setup is ideal for rapid remixes and iterative refinement without regenerating entire scenes from scratch.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure you’re on the latest version. Configure your Gemini API key in the ComfyUI settings or directly in the GeminiVideoOmniV2 node (as required by your setup).
In LoadVideo, set the input to input/hooded_wanderer_planet_bridge.mp4 (included) or drag in your own clip (10 seconds or less). Confirm the clip plays correctly in the node’s preview if available.

Select the GeminiVideoOmniV2 node and write a concise instruction describing just the change you want (e.g., “Replace the background with a neon city at night. Keep everything else the same.”). Choose the desired aspect ratio (16:9 or 9:16) and resolution (1080p or 4K) in the node’s settings.
Optionally add brief refinement details (color palette, time of day, or specific objects to add/remove), but avoid overloading the prompt. Keep the instruction simple and unambiguous.
Queue and run the workflow. The model processes the video and returns an edited clip; SaveVideo writes the result to your output directory, preserving the original audio track.
Review the output and iterate. If something drifted, make the prompt more explicit (e.g., “Do not change the subject’s clothing. Keep the camera motion identical.”) and re-run to refine.
suggestedUseCases: Background replacement for B‑roll or social clips without re-shooting (e.g., turn a bridge scene into a futuristic city).
Style restyling and color grading matches (film look, seasonal changes, day-to-night) while preserving composition.
Object cleanup: remove a distracting sign, add a subtle prop, or hide a logo.
Format adaptation for platforms: convert landscape footage to vertical 9:16 with a matching style pass.
Quick concept remixes: iterate on visual ideas before committing to full production.

faqItems.question: What clip length works best?
faqItems.answer: Keep inputs to 10 seconds or less. Shorter clips process faster and maintain better temporal consistency. Longer inputs may be slower or less stable depending on API limits.

faqItems.question: Will the original audio be preserved?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The workflow is designed to export the edited video with its native audio via SaveVideo. If your source has no audio, the output will be silent.

faqItems.question: How do I maximize consistency across frames?
faqItems.answer: Use simple, specific instructions and include “Keep everything else the same.” Avoid bundling many changes at once, minimize rapid camera motion, and keep the subject’s key attributes explicit (e.g., clothing, colors) if they must not change.

faqItems.question: Can it export vertical video for social media?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Set the aspect ratio to 9:16 in GeminiVideoOmniV2 (and select 1080p or 4K as needed). The workflow will render a vertical output with the edit applied.

8f90aec3d12c.title: Realistic 2k Images - Quick Variations

suggestedUseCases: Enhancing personal photographs for printing or digital display.
Creating varied promotional images for marketing campaigns.
Generating high-resolution textures for video game development.
Producing unique art pieces from existing photos for creative projects.
Developing diverse visual content for social media posts.

faqItems.question: What types of images work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Images with clear subjects and distinct features tend to produce the best results, as they allow the models to generate more accurate variations.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the level of variation in the generated images?
faqItems.answer: The workflow is designed to maintain the essence of the original image while introducing creative variations. Specific adjustments can be made by modifying the parameters within the GrokImageNode.

faqItems.question: How long does it take to process an image?
faqItems.answer: Processing time can vary depending on the image size and system capabilities, but typically it takes a few minutes to complete the entire workflow.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to use this workflow for batch processing?
faqItems.answer: Currently, the workflow is optimized for single image processing. For batch processing, you'd need to load and run each image individually.

8fe7ed30c4ec.title: VFX Passes to Video
8fe7ed30c4ec.description: Turn one reference image into a blendable VFX keyframe with chromatic aberration, glow, lens flare, film finish, and generate a Seedance 2.0 cinematic video.
8fe7ed30c4ec.metaDescription: Create layered VFX passes on a still image and generate a Seedance 2.0 cinematic video with chromatic aberration, glow, lens flare, and film finish.
8fe7ed30c4ec.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single reference image into a layered VFX keyframe and then uses that keyframe to drive a Seedance 2.0 cinematic video. In the Generated VFX Passes group, effect layers are built as separate passes—chromatic aberration, glow/bloom, lens flare, and a film finish—then composited with ImageBlend nodes. Glow is created with ImageBlur and blended with Screen; lens flare is a black-background overlay blended with Screen; chromatic aberration is applied as a full-frame pass blended with Normal. Blend strengths are exposed via PrimitiveFloat nodes, and you can preview any stage with PreviewAny or save stills with SaveImage.

Once the composited keyframe looks right, it’s routed into ByteDance2ReferenceNode in the Seedance 2.0 Output group to generate a motion clip that inherits the look of your keyframe. GeminiImage2Node and GeminiNode are used in the graph to construct and refine the image-based passes, while ImageBlend controls how each pass stacks. Finally, SaveVideo writes the Seedance 2.0 output to disk. This setup is useful because you can dial in a cinematic look non-destructively on a still, audition each pass in isolation, and then get a consistent, blendable look carried through to video—all from one reference frame.
howToUse: Load the workflow and drop your reference image into the Input group’s LoadImage node. Use PreviewAny to confirm resolution and framing.
In Generated VFX Passes, adjust PrimitiveFloat sliders that feed each pass (chromatic aberration amount, glow intensity, lens-flare opacity, film finish strength). Preview each pass with PreviewAny.

Verify blend modes in the ImageBlend nodes: use Normal for the chromatic aberration pass, Screen for the glow/bloom pass, and Screen for the black-background lens-flare overlay. Tweak blend strengths until the composite looks balanced.
Optionally SaveImage at key points to compare different looks or archive a final VFX keyframe. Use PreviewAny on the final composite to check edges, highlights, and grain.
Send the final composite output to the Seedance 2.0 Output group’s ByteDance2ReferenceNode. Set the node’s basic generation parameters as needed (e.g., seed or duration if exposed by the node).
Run the Seedance 2.0 section and write the result with SaveVideo. Review the clip; if needed, return to the Blend Controls and PrimitiveFloat values to refine the look and regenerate.
suggestedUseCases: Turn a polished hero still into a short cinematic motion clip with consistent VFX for trailers or social teasers.
Add filmic glow, subtle chromatic aberration, and lens flare to a product shot, then animate it for ad bumpers.
Create a stylized, blendable keyframe for music videos and motion graphics, ensuring the look holds together in motion.
VFX look development: quickly test glow/halation and flare treatments on stills before committing to a longer render.
Thumbnail-to-video workflows where a designed cover image becomes a short, on-brand motion snippet.

faqItems.question: How do I disable a specific pass (e.g., lens flare) without breaking the graph?
faqItems.answer: Set that pass’s PrimitiveFloat strength to 0 or switch its ImageBlend alpha to 0. You can also temporarily bypass it by disconnecting the pass input to the corresponding ImageBlend node.

faqItems.question: Why does the glow look too strong or wash out highlights?
faqItems.answer: Screen blends can quickly blow out bright regions. Lower the glow PrimitiveFloat value feeding the ImageBlend, reduce ImageBlur radius for a tighter bloom, and preview at 100% to judge highlight roll-off.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce visible color fringing from chromatic aberration?
faqItems.answer: Dial back the chromatic aberration pass’s strength (PrimitiveFloat) and keep its ImageBlend mode on Normal. Small values usually sell the effect without distracting edges.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the video matches my keyframe look?
faqItems.answer: Finalize the composite keyframe first (use SaveImage and PreviewAny), then feed that exact output into ByteDance2ReferenceNode. Keep effect strengths moderate and consistent; re-run SaveVideo if you adjust blends.

8ffcc06b70dd.title: Image Upscale: HitPaw Portrait
8ffcc06b70dd.description: Upload a low-quality portrait image and adjust the upscaling factor. Generate a high-fidelity, detailed portrait with enhanced skin textures and facial features.
8ffcc06b70dd.metaDescription: Upscale and enhance portrait photos in ComfyUI using HitPawGeneralImageEnhance. Load, set scale, compare before/after, and save high-fidelity results.
8ffcc06b70dd.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow demonstrates a clean, single-pass approach to upscaling and enhancing portraits using the HitPawGeneralImageEnhance node. You start by importing a low-resolution portrait with LoadImage, route it through HitPawGeneralImageEnhance to increase resolution and restore facial detail, then save the result with SaveImage. For visual QA, the original and enhanced images are fed into ImageCompare for a side-by-side before/after view. A MarkdownNote is included in the graph to provide inline instructions and tips.

Technically, the pipeline is straightforward: LoadImage -> HitPawGeneralImageEnhance -> SaveImage, with a parallel branch to ImageCompare that pairs the original and the enhanced output. The key control is the upscaling factor on HitPawGeneralImageEnhance (e.g., 2x, 3x, 4x). Because the model is tuned for general image enhancement with a portrait emphasis, it tends to recover skin texture and facial features while reducing noise. Note: ImageCompare is part of ComfyUI’s Nodes 2.0 set—if you don’t see it, switch to Nodes 2.0 from the main menu.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI. If the ImageCompare node is missing, open the menu and switch to Nodes 2.0 (as noted in the author notes).
Open the LoadImage node and select your low-quality or small portrait photo. Ensure the subject’s face is clearly visible for best enhancement.
Select the HitPawGeneralImageEnhance node and set the upscaling factor (e.g., 2x, 3x, or 4x). Start with 2x and increase if the source image is very small.
Optionally configure SaveImage (output folder, filename prefix, and format such as PNG or JPG) to organize your results.
Queue/Execute the workflow. The enhanced, upscaled portrait will be saved by SaveImage and displayed alongside the original in ImageCompare for a side-by-side check.
Review the comparison. If the result looks overly sharp or unnatural, try a lower upscale factor or use a higher-quality source crop focusing on the face, then run again.
suggestedUseCases: Restoring old or compressed profile headshots for social media and professional bios.
Preparing higher-resolution portraits for website team pages or press kits.
Upscaling smartphone selfies for small-format printing or large on-screen displays.
Enhancing still frames from interviews or webinars to create usable portrait thumbnails.
Cleaning and enlarging model or talent cards for casting and portfolio decks.

faqItems.question: Which upscaling factor should I use?
faqItems.answer: Start with 2x for most portraits. If the source is very small (e.g., under ~512 px on the short side), try 3x or 4x. If you notice halos or a plastic look, step down to a lower scale.

faqItems.question: Why don’t I see the ImageCompare node?
faqItems.answer: ImageCompare is available under Nodes 2.0. Open ComfyUI’s menu and switch to Nodes 2.0 to enable it, then reload the workflow.

faqItems.question: Does this work on non-portrait images?
faqItems.answer: It will run on general images, but the workflow is tuned for portraits. For landscapes or product shots, a general super-resolution model may be a better fit.

faqItems.question: Can I automate this with the ComfyUI API?
faqItems.answer: Yes. You can set the input path for LoadImage, adjust the HitPawGeneralImageEnhance scale parameter, and define SaveImage outputs via the ComfyUI API to batch process multiple portraits.

Finally, the SaveImage node enables users to save the enhanced image to their desired location. This workflow is particularly effective due to the precision of the Magnific model, which is trained to upscale images while maintaining sharpness and detail, making it a valuable tool for professionals and hobbyists alike.

Use the LoadImage node to upload the image you wish to upscale.
Configure the MagnificImageUpscalerPreciseV2Node with your desired settings for resolution enhancement.
Run the workflow to process the image through the Magnific model.
Use the ImageCompare node to view the original and upscaled images side-by-side.
Save the upscaled image using the SaveImage node to your preferred location.

Upscaling photographs for large-format displays.
Improving image quality for professional portfolios.
Restoring old or low-resolution images for archival purposes.
Preparing images for detailed analysis in scientific research.

faqItems.question: What types of images work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is optimized for images that require detail preservation during upscaling, such as digital art and photographs.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the level of upscaling?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the MagnificImageUpscalerPreciseV2Node allows you to configure the desired resolution enhancement settings.

faqItems.question: How does the ImageCompare node help in this workflow?

faqItems.question: Is the upscaling process time-consuming?
