9038d2d953b6.title: Kling: Virtual Try On
9038d2d953b6.description: Dress a virtual model in any garment by combining a clothing image with a person photo, generating a realistic try-on result alongside a side-by-side comparison view. It accepts flat-lay, mannequin, or on-model clothing shots while preserving the model's face and pose. Ideal for fashion e-commerce previews, styling mockups, and virtual fitting experiences.
9038d2d953b6.metaDescription: Compare Kling virtual try-on using flat-lay vs mannequin vs on-model garment photos with side-by-side ImageCompare to choose the most reliable input style.
9038d2d953b6.extendedDescription:
This workflow compares how different garment image types—flat-lay, mannequin, and on-model—perform in a virtual try-on using the Kling model. Two LoadImage nodes bring in a person photo and a garment image; the KlingTryOnNode then generates a realistic try-on while preserving the subject’s face and pose. The ImageCompare node assembles a side-by-side view of the original person photo and the generated try-on so you can visually judge fit alignment, drape plausibility, color/pattern fidelity, and identity preservation. SaveImageAdvanced stores both the try-on and the comparison output, and a MarkdownNote provides in-graph guidance.

To make this a fair comparison, keep the same person image while swapping the garment source across flat-lay, mannequin, and on-model product shots. Normalize garment framing and scale before each run so the KlingTryOnNode sees similar inputs. Expect trade-offs: flat-lay images are clean and easy to segment but offer fewer 3D cues; mannequin shots add structure without pose conflict; on-model shots carry natural drape cues but may introduce pose/shadow mismatches. The side-by-side ImageCompare output helps you quantify which input style yields the fewest artifacts for your catalog or campaign.
howToUse: Load inputs: Use LoadImage to import a person photo (e.g., model_colorful_outfit.png) and a garment image (e.g., green_floral_dress.png) or your own assets.

Prepare a fair test: Use the same person photo for all runs. Before each run, pick one garment type (flat-lay, mannequin, on-model) and ensure the garment is fully visible, centered, and similarly scaled across tests.
Run the try-on: Connect the person image and garment image to KlingTryOnNode and queue the workflow. The node generates a try-on while preserving the subject’s face and pose.
Compare results: Review the ImageCompare output (original vs try-on). Assess neckline alignment, sleeve articulation, hem placement, pattern warping, and whether the face/pose remains unchanged.

Iterate across garment types: Swap in a new garment photo style (flat-lay vs mannequin vs on-model) and re-run with the same person image. Keep framing and resolution consistent to isolate the effect of garment type.
Save and review: Use SaveImageAdvanced to export both the try-on and the comparison panel. Optionally add notes in MarkdownNote about which input style produced the cleanest result.
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce teams A/B testing which garment photography style (flat-lay, mannequin, on-model) yields the most reliable try-on previews.
Marketplace operations establishing upload guidelines for seller garment photos to minimize try-on artifacts.
Styling and merchandising mockups that need quick, realistic previews while preserving a model’s face and pose.
Creative production choosing the most robust garment input style for batch try-on campaigns and social content.

faqItems.question: Which garment image type typically produces the best try-on results?
faqItems.answer: There’s no universal winner—each has trade-offs. Flat-lay shots are clean and consistent, aiding segmentation but offering fewer 3D shape cues. Mannequin shots add structure without pose conflicts. On-model shots provide natural drape and folds but can introduce pose or shadow mismatches with the target person. The workflow’s ImageCompare output helps you decide which is most reliable for your catalog.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow preserve the person’s face and pose?
faqItems.answer: The KlingTryOnNode is designed to keep the subject’s identity and pose intact while substituting the clothing region. For best results, use a clear person photo with a visible face and minimal occlusions (e.g., avoid heavy scarves covering the jawline) so the preserved areas remain stable.

faqItems.question: How can I ensure a fair comparison between garment types?
faqItems.answer: Keep the person image constant, use similar framing and scale for each garment input, and run at the same resolution. Avoid changing lighting or background between tests. Review the same criteria in ImageCompare—neckline alignment, sleeve fit, hem placement, and pattern fidelity—so differences reflect garment input style rather than setup variations.

faqItems.question: What are common failure modes, and how can I reduce them?
faqItems.answer: Artifacts often arise with extreme poses, crossed arms covering the torso, heavy accessories, or partial garment visibility. Use front or slight 3/4 person shots, select garment images with full visibility (especially neckline and sleeves), and prefer uncluttered backgrounds. If on-model garment shots cause pose conflicts, try the mannequin or flat-lay version of the same item.

90955b8d32d5.title: Aspect Ratio Extend: Kling O3
90955b8d32d5.description: Extend any video to a custom aspect ratio. Convert vertical videos to horizontal format and vice versa. Includes an application mode for easy use.
90955b8d32d5.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Reformat videos between horizontal and vertical using Kling O3 outpainting. Preserve content, extend canvas, and export clean results.
90955b8d32d5.extendedDescription:
Aspect Ratio Extend: Kling O3 is a ComfyUI workflow that reformats videos between horizontal (16:9) and vertical (9:16) by outpainting new content to fill the added canvas—without cropping or stretching your original footage. It loads your clip with LoadVideo, reads width/height/fps via GetVideoComponents, and resizes frames by the shorter side using JWImageResizeByShorterSide so the subject stays intact while empty space is created only along the long axis. That new space is then synthesized by the KlingOmniProEditVideoNode (Kling O3), which generates context-aware extensions that match the look and motion of your source. Frames are optionally limited for previews with Video Slice, reassembled with CreateVideo, and exported using SaveVideo.

The workflow is organized into clear groups—Input Video, Video Resize and Extend, and Video Outpaint—for an "application mode" style experience. You can reframe the subject with simple horizontal/vertical offsets before extension, which helps keep faces and key action centered after the aspect swap. A helper utility node (ID: 7594b5c0-2b90-4aeb-846b-e3eb8fa89f33) is included inside the graph; it supports the internal wiring and typically requires no user changes. This build is optimized for major orientation changes (horizontal ↔ vertical). For minor ratio tweaks or square (1:1) outputs, the Kling video edit approach is not recommended.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and switch to Application Mode (if available). In the Input Video group, use LoadVideo to select your source clip.
In Video Resize and Extend, choose your target orientation (e.g., 16:9 → 9:16 or 9:16 → 16:9). JWImageResizeByShorterSide ensures the original content is preserved along the shorter side.
Use the provided offset controls to reframe the subject before extension. Shift left/right for horizontal outputs or up/down for vertical outputs so the key subject remains centered.

Open KlingOmniProEditVideoNode and confirm your Kling API configuration. If the node exposes edit strength or guidance options, start with conservative values to keep the outpaint subtle and coherent.
For a fast preview, enable Video Slice to process a short segment (e.g., the first few seconds). Execute the graph and verify that motion continuity and background fill look natural.

Disable Video Slice for the full run, then Execute. The workflow assembles frames with CreateVideo and writes the result via SaveVideo. Review the final output and adjust offsets or settings if needed.
suggestedUseCases: Convert landscape YouTube footage to vertical Shorts/Reels/TikTok while preserving the subject and extending the sides with matching context.
Turn portrait phone videos into landscape B-roll by outpainting additional background instead of cropping valuable content.
Reformat webinar clips or talking-head content between platforms with different aspect needs, keeping faces centered via offset controls.
Create cinematic extensions for travel or sports clips when switching between 16:9 and 9:16 without visible stretching.

faqItems.question: How does this differ from simple cropping or letterboxing?
faqItems.answer: Instead of cropping (which removes content) or letterboxing (which adds black bars), the workflow uses Kling O3 (KlingOmniProEditVideoNode) to outpaint new, context-aware imagery into the expanded canvas so the frame looks naturally wider or taller.

faqItems.question: Which aspect ratios work best?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is designed specifically for major orientation changes—horizontal to vertical and vice versa (e.g., 16:9 ↔ 9:16). It is not recommended for slight ratio adjustments or for 1:1 square outputs.

faqItems.question: Can I keep the original audio?
faqItems.answer: The default path focuses on visual processing and typically outputs a silent video via SaveVideo. If you need audio, export the extended video and remux the original audio track using a video editor or ffmpeg, or adapt the graph to an audio-capable save node if available.

faqItems.question: Do I need a GPU or special hardware?
faqItems.answer: Most heavy synthesis happens inside the Kling O3 service accessed by KlingOmniProEditVideoNode. Your local machine still handles decoding/encoding and frame buffering (LoadVideo, CreateVideo, SaveVideo), so enough CPU/RAM and disk space are recommended for smooth processing.

909d7c3867e2.title: Luma UNI-1: Image Creation
909d7c3867e2.description: Generate brand-new original images using the Luma UNI-1 node with up to 9 reference images for style, character, color, lighting, and composition. Create unique compositions with detailed prompts, adjustable aspect ratios, and seed control.
909d7c3867e2.metaDescription: Generate original images with Luma UNI-1 in ComfyUI using up to 9 style/character/lighting references, adjustable aspect ratios, and seed control.
909d7c3867e2.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow shows how to generate brand-new images with Luma UNI-1 using text prompts plus up to nine optional reference images for style, character, color, lighting, and composition. The centerpiece is the LumaImageNode2, which accepts your prompt, aspect ratio, and seed, and can ingest multiple image references to steer the look without copying them. LoadImage nodes bring your references into the graph, and SaveImage writes the results to disk for easy review.

Technically, the grouped reference images (select and press Ctrl+B) are collected by LumaImageNode2 as a single “image reference” bundle. Inside the node, you can assign a role and weight per reference so the model knows whether an image should drive style, subject identity, palette, lighting, or framing. When you queue the prompt, the node sends a generation request to Luma’s API and returns a synthesized image built from your text plus the weighted references. The MarkdownNote in the workflow highlights these controls, while SaveImage ensures outputs are consistently saved with your chosen filename prefix and directory. Seed control lets you reproduce or iterate on a look, and adjustable aspect ratios help you target social, print, or widescreen layouts.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI. Open the LumaImageNode2 and paste your Luma API key if required (or set it via environment/ComfyUI settings).
Add 0–9 reference images with LoadImage nodes. Select the reference images and press Ctrl+B to place them in the Image Reference group used by LumaImageNode2.

In LumaImageNode2, write a clear prompt describing subject, action, style, lighting, and camera. Assign each reference a role (e.g., Style, Character, Color, Lighting, Composition) and adjust weights to control influence.
Set the aspect ratio and seed in LumaImageNode2. Use a fixed seed for reproducibility or change it to explore variations.
Click Queue Prompt. Review the output. If needed, tweak prompt wording, adjust reference roles/weights, or change the seed and run again.
Check the SaveImage node settings (output folder and filename prefix). Results save automatically when the node executes.
suggestedUseCases: Character consistency: Keep a mascot or illustrated character on-model across different scenes using 1–2 character references plus new prompts.
Art direction alignment: Lock in palette and lighting with dedicated references while freely changing subjects and locations.
Product concepting: Maintain a consistent industrial design language by referencing material/finish/style images while exploring new forms.
Storyboards and key art: Use a composition reference for framing and a style reference for look development to rapidly iterate shots.
Poster and cover design: Blend a strong style reference with a separate color reference to hit a precise visual identity.

faqItems.question: Does UNI-1 copy my reference images?
faqItems.answer: No. In Create Mode it generates new compositions. References guide high-level attributes (style, character identity, color, lighting, composition) rather than reproducing the input images.

faqItems.question: How many reference images can I use and how should I weight them?
faqItems.answer: You can use up to nine. Start with 1–3 strong references, assign each a clear role, and increase weights only where you want stronger influence. If a reference overpowers the result, lower its weight or remove it.

faqItems.question: What aspect ratios work best?
faqItems.answer: UNI-1 supports flexible aspect ratios. Common choices like 1:1, 3:2, 2:3, 16:9, and 9:16 tend to be reliable. Extremely wide or tall ratios may need prompt and reference adjustments to maintain composition.

faqItems.question: How do I get reproducible results?
faqItems.answer: Set a fixed seed in LumaImageNode2 and keep the prompt, references, roles, weights, and aspect ratio unchanged. Rerunning with the same setup should yield closely similar images.

90bbb7c2ceda.title: Kling2.6: Storytelling Videos with Audio
90bbb7c2ceda.description: Bring your stories to life with videos featuring synchronized dialogue, music, sound effects, and ambient audio from text prompts.
90bbb7c2ceda.metaDescription: Create storytelling videos with synchronized audio using Kling2.6. Transform text prompts into engaging visual narratives.
90bbb7c2ceda.extendedDescription: The Kling2.6: Storytelling Videos with Audio workflow is designed to transform your text prompts into engaging videos complete with synchronized audio elements. Utilizing the Kling and Kling 2.6 models, this workflow leverages the KlingTextToVideoWithAudio node to generate videos that incorporate dialogue, music, sound effects, and ambient audio. The workflow begins by processing a detailed text prompt that outlines the scene, elements, movement, and audio components. This prompt is then fed into the KlingTextToVideoWithAudio node, which synthesizes the visual and auditory elements into a cohesive video. The MarkdownNote node is used for annotating and organizing the workflow, while the SaveVideo node ensures that the final output is stored for easy access and sharing. This workflow is particularly useful for creators looking to produce dynamic storytelling content without needing extensive video editing skills.
howToUse: Load the Kling2.6: Storytelling Videos with Audio workflow in ComfyUI.
Prepare your text prompt detailing the scene, elements, movement, and audio components.
Input the text prompt into the KlingTextToVideoWithAudio node.
Use the MarkdownNote node to annotate your workflow for clarity and organization.
Run the workflow to generate the video and use the SaveVideo node to store the final output.
Review the video to ensure all elements are synchronized and adjust the prompt as needed for refinement.
suggestedUseCases: Creating narrative-driven video content for social media platforms.
Developing educational videos that combine visual and audio storytelling.
Producing promotional videos with engaging audio-visual elements.
Crafting immersive video experiences for virtual events or presentations.
Generating animated short films with synchronized dialogue and sound effects.

faqItems.question: What type of prompts work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Prompts that clearly describe the scene, elements, movement, and audio components yield the best results. Be specific about dialogue, emotions, and style.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for commercial projects?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow can be used for commercial projects, provided you adhere to any licensing agreements related to the Kling models.

faqItems.question: How can I ensure the audio is synchronized with the video?
faqItems.answer: Ensure that your text prompt includes detailed descriptions of the audio elements, such as dialogue timing, emotion, and tone, to achieve better synchronization.

faqItems.question: What if the video output is not as expected?
faqItems.answer: Try refining your text prompt for more clarity and detail, and ensure all elements are accurately described to improve the output quality.

90d086fef9e3.title: Tattoo Generator
90d086fef9e3.description: Turn your tattoo design ideas into reality with this AI tattoo generator app. Explore unique tattoo styles, get instant design inspiration, and create custom tattoo concepts in seconds — perfect for planning your next piece.
90d086fef9e3.metaDescription: ComfyUI Tattoo Generator: build tattoo prompts, switch styles, set resolution, preview, and save clean concept images for client-ready inspiration.
90d086fef9e3.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI Tattoo Generator turns written ideas into clean tattoo concept images using a streamlined, prompt-first pipeline. You type your idea in a PrimitiveStringMultiline node, optionally provide a small JSON snippet, choose a style with a ComfySwitchNode, and the workflow assembles a polished prompt with StringConcatenate. A ResolutionSelector lets you pick a canvas size that suits patch-style, sleeve elements, or flash-sheet compositions. The core image is produced by the generation node identified as e46f5b18-9edb-4755-bec5-b38521684b4c, wrapped by a CustomCombo that encapsulates the underlying text-to-image model and default inference settings. You can preview instantly with PreviewAny and export final images via SaveImage.

Technically, the prompt flow is handled by string utilities and simple logic: JsonExtractString can pull a field (for example, a preferred style) from a JSON string if you supply one; ComfySwitchNode toggles between built-in tattoo aesthetics (e.g., blackwork, fine-line, geometric) and feeds that choice into StringConcatenate to form the final prompt. ResolutionSelector passes width/height to the generator, ensuring the model inside the CustomCombo receives consistent parameters. The result is a focused, tattoo-oriented text-to-image workflow that encourages clear subject descriptions and style discipline, ideal for iterating fast on client briefs or exploring variations before committing to a stencil.
howToUse: Load the Tattoo Generator workflow in ComfyUI and locate the key I/O nodes: PrimitiveStringMultiline (idea input), ComfySwitchNode (style), ResolutionSelector (size), PreviewAny, and SaveImage.

Enter your idea in PrimitiveStringMultiline. You can write plain text (e.g., "a raven with geometric accents") or a JSON string with fields (e.g., {"idea":"raven with geometric accents","style":"blackwork"}).
If you didn’t provide a style in JSON, choose one with ComfySwitchNode. The selected style is merged into the final prompt with StringConcatenate.
Pick an output size in ResolutionSelector. Use square for flash-style tiles, portrait for forearm/calf concepts, or landscape for bands and panels.
Queue/Run the workflow. The CustomCombo routes your prompt and resolution into the generator node (e46f5b18-9edb-4755-bec5-b38521684b4c), and PreviewAny shows the result as soon as it’s ready.
If you’re happy with the design, trigger SaveImage to export. Iterate by adjusting the idea text, switching styles, or trying alternate resolutions.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid style exploration: generate the same subject across blackwork, fine-line, geometric, or watercolor-inspired looks to compare directions.
Client pre-visualization: turn a short brief into several clean concept options during consultations.
Flash sheet development: batch-create cohesive tiles by fixing a style and resolution while varying the subject prompt.
Motif refinement: iterate on line density and detail by adjusting descriptive terms (e.g., "minimal linework, high contrast" vs. "ornamental, dotwork shading").

faqItems.question: Do I have to use JSON, or can I just type plain text?

faqItems.question: Which model does this workflow use, and can I change it?

faqItems.question: My results look too photographic or colorful. How can I get cleaner tattoo linework?

faqItems.question: Where are images saved?

9102207150b3.title: Video Upscale: ByteDance vCube
9102207150b3.description: Enhance video quality with ByteDance vCube, an AI-driven tool that upscales and restores footage through shot-adaptive processing, fixing compression artifacts and color distortion while preserving original texture. Ideal for improving UGC clips, refining AIGC content, and restoring classic films with vibrant, clear results.
9102207150b3.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: upscale and restore videos with ByteDance vCube using shot‑adaptive enhancement. LoadVideo → ByteDanceVideoEnhanceNode → SaveVideo.
9102207150b3.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow shows you how to upscale and restore videos with ByteDance vCube using a simple, reliable node chain. It starts by decoding your source clip with LoadVideo, enhances and upscales frames through ByteDanceVideoEnhanceNode (calling the vCube model via API), and then re-encodes the result with SaveVideo. A small helper/config node (7e8f7b8b-a2c3-4ebb-a31b-7d3c829a1b76) is included to centralize parameters passed to the enhancer.

Technically, vCube performs shot‑adaptive processing to suppress compression artifacts, repair color distortion, and preserve natural texture as it scales the image. Frames from LoadVideo are sent to ByteDanceVideoEnhanceNode along with your chosen options (scale factor, restoration strength, and related flags when exposed by the workflow), then returned as enhanced frames for SaveVideo to encode. Because the heavy lifting happens on the vCube service, your local GPU load is minimal; performance depends more on your clip length, resolution, and network bandwidth than on VRAM. The result is a clean, sharper, and more stable video suitable for UGC cleanup, AIGC refinement, and archival footage restoration.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the ByteDanceVideoEnhanceNode is installed. If this node uses the vCube API, add your API key/endpoint in the node or its settings as required.

Open the LoadVideo node and select your source clip. If the node exposes options like start/end frames or target FPS, set them to match your project. Keep the original frame rate unless you intend to change motion cadence later.

Configure parameters. This workflow includes a helper/config node (7e8f7b8b-a2c3-4ebb-a31b-7d3c829a1b76) that feeds options to ByteDanceVideoEnhanceNode. Use it (or the enhancer node directly) to choose the upscale factor (start with 2× for most clips) and restoration strength. For heavily compressed UGC, prefer stronger artifact removal; for already clean AIGC, use milder settings to preserve fine detail.

Open ByteDanceVideoEnhanceNode and confirm the selected model/profile corresponds to vCube. If the node exposes shot‑adaptive or color stabilization options, enable them for mixed lighting or edited footage. Apply conservative sharpening if available; aggressive settings can reintroduce halos.

Set up SaveVideo with your desired output path, container, and frame rate. Choose a quality‑oriented codec/bitrate. If your SaveVideo node doesn’t preserve audio, plan to re‑attach the original track after export using a separate tool.

Queue the workflow. Monitor the first few seconds of output for ringing, over‑smoothing, or color shifts, then iterate: lower restoration strength if textures look waxy, or increase it if blocking and mosquito noise remain. If you need a higher resolution, upscale in two passes (e.g., 2× + 2×) rather than a single very large jump.
suggestedUseCases: Clean up smartphone UGC: remove compression artifacts and stabilize color before publishing.
Refine AI‑generated video (AIGC) to reduce ringing and enhance micro‑detail without over‑sharpening.
Restore archival or classic footage by upscaling and correcting age‑related color shifts and artifacts.
Prepare social media deliverables from low‑resolution sources while preserving natural texture.
Improve screen recordings or webinar captures for clearer text and UI elements.

faqItems.question: Do I need a powerful GPU to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Not necessarily. In this workflow, ByteDanceVideoEnhanceNode calls the vCube model via API, so the heavy processing runs in the cloud. Local performance mainly affects video I/O and preview; network bandwidth and clip length determine overall turnaround time.

faqItems.question: How should I choose the upscale factor?
faqItems.answer: Start with 2× for most footage. If the source is very clean and high‑bitrate, 4× can work, but larger jumps amplify artifacts and may require stronger restoration. For best quality, consider two passes (2× + 2×) rather than a single extreme upscale.

faqItems.question: Why is there a node with an ID like 7e8f7b8b‑a2c3‑… in the graph?
faqItems.answer: That custom helper/config node aggregates parameters (such as scale and enhancement options) and feeds them into ByteDanceVideoEnhanceNode. Use it to adjust the settings exposed by this specific workflow rather than wiring multiple inputs manually.

faqItems.question: Will my audio be preserved?
faqItems.answer: Many SaveVideo nodes focus on video only. If your SaveVideo node doesn’t handle audio, export the enhanced video and then re‑mux the original audio track with an external tool. This avoids generational loss and preserves sync.

faqItems.question: How does this workflow reduce flicker or color instability across cuts?
faqItems.answer: The vCube model applies shot‑adaptive processing, which helps keep enhancement consistent across edits and lighting changes. If you still see flicker, reduce aggressive sharpening or color correction settings and ensure the output frame rate matches the input.

91965bb6dc08.title: Video Upscale: Real-ESRGAN
91965bb6dc08.description: Upload a video to upscale it using a fast GAN model. The output resolution is determined by your chosen model (e.g., 2x or 4x). For best results, upscale first, then resize to your target resolution.
91965bb6dc08.metaDescription: Upscale videos 2x–4x in ComfyUI with Real-ESRGAN. Extract frames, upscale per-frame, and recreate the video at the original FPS for fast, quality enhancement.
91965bb6dc08.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow upscales any input video using Real-ESRGAN, a fast GAN-based super-resolution model. It works by extracting frames with LoadVideo and GetVideoComponents, upscaling each frame in a batch with ImageUpscaleWithModel, and then rebuilding the clip with CreateVideo and SaveVideo. The UpscaleModelLoader node selects the exact Real-ESRGAN variant (for example, x2 or x4), and that choice determines the output resolution multiplier.

Technically, the workflow performs per-frame super-resolution on the GPU without diffusion, so it's much faster and well-suited to long clips or quick turnarounds. Real-ESRGAN excels at sharpening edges and restoring textures while keeping the original motion. The pipeline preserves the source frame rate by passing timing info from GetVideoComponents to CreateVideo. If audio is routed through, the original soundtrack can be reattached; otherwise, the result is a silent video. For best quality, upscale to a higher multiple first (such as 4x with RealESRGAN_x4) and, if needed, add a separate resize node afterward to reach your exact delivery resolution.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and verify the core nodes are present: LoadVideo → GetVideoComponents → ImageUpscaleWithModel → CreateVideo → SaveVideo, plus UpscaleModelLoader feeding the upscaler.
In LoadVideo, select your source file. GetVideoComponents will split out the frames and timing info (and audio if present).
In UpscaleModelLoader, choose a Real-ESRGAN model that matches your goal (e.g., RealESRGAN_x2 for 2x or RealESRGAN_x4 for 4x; anime-focused variants work best for line art).

Ensure the frames from GetVideoComponents feed into ImageUpscaleWithModel, and the loaded model from UpscaleModelLoader is connected to it. The upscaled frames should then route into CreateVideo with the original FPS.
Confirm CreateVideo and SaveVideo are wired and set an output path in SaveVideo. If the workflow exposes audio routing, connect the audio from GetVideoComponents to preserve the soundtrack.
Queue and run. For delivery at a non-integer resolution, optionally add a resize node after upscaling to scale down to your exact target.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing low-resolution screen recordings or tutorials before publishing.
Up-resing mobile or archival footage for HD/4K delivery without long render times.
Improving clarity for anime, line art, or gameplay captures using the appropriate Real-ESRGAN variant.
Preparing social media clips by upscaling first, then resizing to platform-specific dimensions.
Fast pre-upscale before further editing, stabilization, or color work in an NLE.

faqItems.question: Which Real-ESRGAN model should I pick?
faqItems.answer: Choose by target scale and content type. Use x2 for modest boosts with lower VRAM, x4 for maximum detail. Anime/cartoon variants (e.g., anime-focused Real-ESRGAN) handle line art and flat colors better. The selected model dictates the output resolution (2x or 4x).

faqItems.question: Will the workflow keep my original audio and frame rate?
faqItems.answer: Frame rate is preserved by passing timing from GetVideoComponents into CreateVideo. Audio can be preserved if the workflow routes the audio output into the video creation/saving nodes; otherwise, the result is silent.

faqItems.question: How do I avoid VRAM errors on large videos?
faqItems.answer: Try a 2x model instead of 4x, process shorter clips, or reduce resolution before upscaling. If your GPU still runs out of memory, split the video into segments and run them sequentially.

faqItems.question: Is GAN upscaling as detailed as diffusion-based super-resolution?
faqItems.answer: No. Real-ESRGAN is much faster and great for sharpening and cleanup, but it won’t hallucinate new detail like diffusion models. For best results, upscale with Real-ESRGAN first, then optionally fine-tune with other tools if needed.

91a17d5206d2.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: use GeminiVideoOmni to generate cinematic text-to-video. Includes a Prompt Constructor for duration/aspect ratio, preview, and SaveVideo output.
91a17d5206d2.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns plain-language prompts into short, cinematic video using the GeminiVideoOmni node. A Prompt Constructor subgraph (node id 3762e4c1-c5e0-4e1b-9449-e5ea5e9948cd) helps you build a well-formed prompt that explicitly includes duration and aspect ratio—two fields Gemini Omni Video expects in the text. Once composed, the prompt is sent through GeminiVideoOmni to the Gemini API, which synthesizes the clip based on your scene description, camera direction, motion cues, and lighting notes.

While the video is generating, PreviewAny provides an inline preview so you can quickly evaluate framing and motion. When you're happy, SaveVideo writes the final result to your output folder as a single video file. A MarkdownNote included in the canvas captures quick tips and reminders (like always specifying duration and aspect ratio). The layout keeps the most important levers up front, making it ideal for rapid iteration, prototyping, and prompt-driven storytelling.
howToUse: Load the "Gemini Omni Flash: Text to Video" workflow in ComfyUI and review the MarkdownNote for on-canvas tips.
Open the GeminiVideoOmni node and set your Gemini API credentials as required by the node (or your environment). Leave advanced settings at defaults if unsure.

Use the Prompt Constructor subgraph (id 3762e4c1-c5e0-4e1b-9449-e5ea5e9948cd) to craft your prompt. Be sure to include clear values for duration (e.g., 6 seconds) and aspect ratio (e.g., 16:9 or 9:16), plus a concise scene description with subject, camera motion, and lighting.
Trigger the graph. Inspect the output with PreviewAny to verify composition, movement, and timing. If something looks off, refine the prompt (especially duration, aspect ratio, and camera cues).

When satisfied, run the full graph to completion. SaveVideo will write the generated clip to your output folder. Optionally set a filename and check the container/codec options in the node if available.
Iterate: adjust only one or two prompt elements at a time (camera direction, motion verbs, lighting) to converge quickly on the look you want.

Rapid product or UI motion mockups without setting up a 3D scene.
Storyboard previsualization with clear camera moves and lighting beats.

faqItems.question: Where is the video saved and does it include audio?

faqItems.question: What settings improve video quality or coherence?
faqItems.answer: Be concrete and structured: define subject, setting, camera move (e.g., slow dolly-in), lighting (e.g., warm golden-hour rim light), and temporal beats (what happens first/next). Keep duration realistic and aligned with the action to avoid rushed or stretched motion.

faqItems.question: What if the request fails or the video is the wrong shape?
faqItems.answer: First, confirm your API credentials in GeminiVideoOmni. Then verify the prompt explicitly states duration (with units like seconds) and a standard aspect ratio (e.g., 16:9, 9:16, 1:1). Mismatched or missing values are common causes of errors or unexpected framing.

Ideal for social media ads, product concept testing, and short-form storytelling where narrative continuity and distribution-ready framing matter.
92d04a68658a.metaDescription: ComfyUI PixVerse V6 tutorial: generate up to 15s 1080p videos from text with multi-shot prompts, multiple aspect ratios, and optional audio, saved via SaveVideo.
92d04a68658a.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow uses PixverseV6TextToVideoNode to turn text prompts into distribution-ready video clips, then saves the result with SaveVideo. PixVerse V6 runs generation via API, so you don’t need a local GPU to produce smooth motion. You can target up to 15 seconds at 1080p, choose common aspect ratios (16:9, 9:16, 1:1), and optionally include integrated audio if enabled in the node. The node handles the request/response with the PixVerse V6 service and returns an encoded video that SaveVideo writes to disk.

What makes this setup especially useful is multi-shot scene direction in a single pass. You can outline a short narrative as a sequence of labeled scenes within your prompt so the model maintains continuity across cuts (character, setting, lighting) without juggling multiple runs. The result is a fast way to prototype social clips, product teasers, and story snippets that are already framed correctly for your target platform.
howToUse: Load the PixVerse 6.0: Text to Video workflow in ComfyUI. If prompted, install the custom PixverseV6TextToVideoNode and restart ComfyUI so the node becomes available.

Open PixverseV6TextToVideoNode and enter your text prompt. Set duration (up to 15s), choose aspect ratio (e.g., 16:9, 9:16, 1:1), and select 1080p for final resolution. If available, enable the audio option to embed a soundtrack.

For multi-shot direction, structure the prompt as clearly separated scenes (e.g., labeled lines like "Shot 1:", "Shot 2:"). Reuse key nouns for continuity (character name, product, setting) so the model keeps the same subject across shots.
If the node exposes reproducibility controls (such as a seed), set them now for consistent iterations. Keep prompts specific about subject, action, and style; avoid conflicting instructions.
Ensure PixverseV6TextToVideoNode’s video output connects to SaveVideo. In SaveVideo, choose an output filename (MP4) and verify the framerate matches your generation settings.

Click Queue/Execute. Wait for the API to finish rendering. When complete, open the saved MP4. If audio was enabled and provided by PixVerse, the exported file will include it; otherwise, you can add audio in post.
suggestedUseCases: Social ads and story posts framed for 9:16 or 1:1, ready for platforms like TikTok, Reels, and Shorts.
Product concept teasers and motion mockups to validate ideas before full-scale production.
Short-form storytelling and sceneboards using multi-shot prompts for narrative continuity.
UI/UX micro-demos or explainer snippets where 15 seconds and 1080p clarity are sufficient.
Title cards and motion bumpers tailored to different aspect ratios from the same prompt.

faqItems.question: What are the maximum duration and resolution supported?
faqItems.answer: This workflow targets up to 15 seconds at 1080p. You can pick common aspect ratios like 16:9, 9:16, and 1:1 to match your distribution channel.

faqItems.question: Do I need a powerful GPU to use this?
faqItems.answer: No. PixverseV6TextToVideoNode uses the PixVerse V6 API for generation. Your local machine runs ComfyUI and saves the output, while rendering happens on the service.

faqItems.question: How do I write a good multi-shot prompt?
faqItems.answer: Break your idea into short, labeled scenes and keep the subject identifiers consistent. For example, name the character and setting in each scene. Limit the number of shots so each has enough time within the total duration, and avoid conflicting style directives across scenes.

faqItems.question: Does the saved video include audio?

9394f9968da3.title: Wan Animate 2: Motion Transfer
9394f9968da3.description: Animate a still character using a driving video with Wan Animate 2, transferring motion directly from video frames without any pose extraction or skeleton preprocessing. The output preserves the reference character's identity while generating a fresh background and camera movement from your text prompt. Ideal for motion transfer, action mimicry, and character animation replacement projects.
9394f9968da3.metaDescription: Animate a still character with Wan Animate 2 by transferring motion from a driving video. Prompt controls background and camera. No pose extraction needed.
9394f9968da3.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates end-to-end motion transfer using Wan-Animate-2 (by Wan-Video/Alibaba): a single reference image (your character) is animated to follow the motion in a driving video, without any pose keypoint or skeleton extraction. The core of the graph is the "Motion Transfer (Wan Animate 2)" subgraph powered by custom Wan-Animate-2 nodes (UUIDs: 11706f8a-428d-4ef9-b24f-863f651c1b0b, 79280513-53b2-4417-93f8-f3e116bb6736, b798a87e-23ec-483d-ab9b-6af5b298d0ad). These nodes accept your reference image, the per-frame motion signal from the driving video, and a text prompt that guides background look and camera feel. Because motion is learned directly from frames, setup is fast and robust—no OpenPose or preprocessing passes.

LoadImage provides the character identity, while LoadVideo and GetVideoComponents extract the driving frames and fps. BatchImagesNode replicates the reference image so each video frame gets its own paired identity input. GetImageSize and ComfyMathExpression are used to keep resolution and aspect ratio consistent between inputs and outputs. PreviewAny lets you inspect intermediate frames, and CreateVideo + SaveVideo assemble the generated frames back into a video using the original fps. For longer clips, you manually duplicate the Motion Transfer subgraph (native looping support is pending upstream) and connect it in sequence so the pipeline can process the entire driving video.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then set your inputs: use LoadImage for the reference character and LoadVideo for the driving video. GetVideoComponents will extract frames and fps automatically.
Confirm output size and aspect. Use GetImageSize on the reference (or driver), then use ComfyMathExpression to set/scale width and height so the model and CreateVideo stay consistent.
Open the Motion Transfer (Wan Animate 2) subgraph and set your text prompt to describe background and camera mood. Keep prompts identity-safe (avoid describing a different character).
Run the first Motion Transfer subgraph. BatchImagesNode will duplicate the reference image to match the number of driving frames, and PreviewAny can be used to spot-check results.

If your driving video is longer than one pass supports: select the bypassed Motion Transfer subgraph above, press Ctrl+B to enable, update it so prompt/size match the first one, and link its image output to BatchImagesNode. Duplicate the subgraph with Ctrl+C then Ctrl+Shift+V as many times as needed to cover the full video.
Finally, feed the generated frames to CreateVideo, set fps from GetVideoComponents, and SaveVideo to write the final animation to disk.
suggestedUseCases: Character replacement: make a mascot or stylized avatar perform motions from a live-action reference.
Action mimicry: transfer dance, sports, or gesture performances onto your character for social clips.
Previsualization: quickly block animation for ads, cinematics, or mockups without rigging.
Educational content: demonstrate motion studies by applying the same movement to multiple characters.
Game/VTuber prototyping: iterate on character motion ideas directly from found footage.

faqItems.question: Do I need OpenPose or a skeleton extraction step?
faqItems.answer: No. Wan-Animate-2 performs direct motion transfer from the driving video frames. The workflow does not require keypoints or pose preprocessing.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the character identity consistent?
faqItems.answer: Use a clean, well-lit reference image with minimal occlusion and a simple background. Keep the aspect ratio consistent, and avoid prompts that describe a different character or facial features that conflict with your reference.

faqItems.question: How do I match the timing and duration of the driving video?
faqItems.answer: GetVideoComponents provides fps for the driving clip—pass that to CreateVideo so playback matches the source timing. To retime, adjust the fps in CreateVideo (higher fps = faster playback, lower fps = slower).

faqItems.question: My clip is long. How do I process the whole video?
faqItems.answer: Native loop support is still under review. For now, duplicate the "Motion Transfer (Wan Animate 2)" subgraph: enable the bypassed copy (Ctrl+B), ensure its prompt and size match the first, connect its image output to BatchImagesNode, then copy-paste (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Shift+V) enough segments to cover the full driving video.

93c182d3aefb.title: LTX-2.5 (Pro): Text to Video
93c182d3aefb.description: Generate video from text with LTX 2.5, a video model built for fast, high-quality production work. Type a prompt and get a cinematic clip with sharp detail, accurate motion, and support for native multishot scenes that hold character and style across cuts.
93c182d3aefb.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate cinematic text-to-video clips with LTX 2.5 using LtxApi25TextToVideo and SaveVideo, including native multi-shot scene support.
93c182d3aefb.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a text prompt into a finished video clip using the LTX 2.5 model via the LtxApi25TextToVideo node. Your prompt (and optional multi-shot structure) is sent to the LTX 2.5 API, which returns generated video content with sharp detail and coherent motion. Technically, the LtxApi25TextToVideo node is the core generator: it packages your prompt and settings, submits them to the remote LTX 2.5 service, and provides the resulting clip to the graph. LTX 2.5 supports native multi-shot scenes, making it possible to maintain character and style across cuts when you structure your prompt appropriately. The SaveVideo node handles final assembly and export, letting you choose a filename and frame rate while keeping the workflow simple and fast.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI. Confirm you can see the LtxApi25TextToVideo node feeding into the SaveVideo node.

Open LtxApi25TextToVideo. Enter your text prompt. If your node version supports it, add multi-shot structure (e.g., separate shots in your prompt) to keep characters and style consistent across cuts. Add your API credentials or endpoint if required.

Optionally adjust any available generation settings in LtxApi25TextToVideo (for example, duration, aspect ratio, or randomness/seed if exposed). Use concise, visual language and consistent character descriptors for best results.
Open SaveVideo and set a clear filename or prefix and your desired FPS. Confirm the output directory is correct.
Queue the workflow and run it. The LtxApi25TextToVideo node will contact the LTX 2.5 service, generate the video, and pass it to SaveVideo for export.
Review the output video. Iterate by refining your prompt or node settings, then re-run. For multi-shot scenes, keep shot descriptions tight and reuse character and style cues to maintain continuity.

Product b-roll and short promotional clips with clear camera and motion cues.
Character-driven scenes that maintain look and style across quick cuts.
Social media teasers and mood pieces requiring fast turnaround.
Concept visualization for directors, clients, or pitch decks.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow run locally or require the internet?

faqItems.question: How do I create multi-shot scenes that keep characters consistent?
faqItems.answer: Structure your prompt as multiple shots with clear, consistent descriptors for characters, wardrobe, lighting, and style. If your node version exposes a multi-shot field or shot list, use it; otherwise, separate shots within the prompt text. Reuse the same character and style cues across shots.

faqItems.question: Can I control duration, resolution, or randomness?
faqItems.answer: Adjust whatever controls your LtxApi25TextToVideo node exposes. Some versions include parameters like duration, aspect ratio/resolution hints, and a seed or randomness setting. If a control is not visible, it may not be supported by your build or API plan.

faqItems.question: Where is the video saved and what format is it?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo writes the rendered clip to your ComfyUI output folder using the filename or prefix you set, at the FPS you choose. The exact container/codec depends on your SaveVideo configuration.

Import your video footage using the WanVideoVAELoader node.
Use the OnnxDetectionModelLoader to detect facial features and generate masks.
Upload a reference image for the desired face using the LoadImage node.
Configure the WanVideoSampler and WanVideoDecode nodes to apply the face swap across the video.
Preview and export the final video using the VHS_VideoCombine node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating realistic de-aging effects for actors in film and television.
Swapping faces in promotional videos to feature different brand ambassadors.
Enhancing video content by replacing faces with digital doubles for stunts or complex scenes.
Producing deepfake-style content for parody or educational purposes with ethical considerations.

faqItems.question: What video formats are supported by the Face Swap Workflow?

faqItems.question: How can I ensure the swapped face looks natural?

faqItems.question: Can this workflow handle multiple faces in a single video?

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for real-time applications?

9471e016e787.title: Arrow 2: Text to SVG
9471e016e787.description: Input a text prompt and optional reference images to generate one or more SVG vector graphics.
9471e016e787.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate clean SVG vector graphics from text prompts with Quiver and save them with SaveSVGNode. Ideal for icons, logos, and pictograms.
9471e016e787.extendedDescription:
Arrow 2: Text to SVG is a compact ComfyUI workflow that turns a text prompt (and optional reference images) into clean, editable vector graphics. At its core is the QuiverTextToSVGNodeV2, which uses the Quiver model to synthesize SVG content—paths, shapes, and groups—directly from your prompt. Instead of raster pixels, the node outputs one or more SVG documents you can open in Illustrator, Figma, or Inkscape.

Technically, your prompt and any provided reference images flow into QuiverTextToSVGNodeV2, which generates SVG markup representing the design. The SaveSVGNode then serializes that markup to disk as .svg files. Because the pipeline is vector-native end-to-end, results scale infinitely without loss of quality, making it ideal for icons, logos, and flat illustrations. You control outcomes primarily through precise wording (e.g., "flat icon", "monoline outline", "duotone pictogram") and by including reference images to anchor style or proportions.
howToUse: Load the Arrow 2: Text to SVG workflow in ComfyUI. Confirm the QuiverTextToSVGNodeV2 and SaveSVGNode are present and not reporting missing dependencies.

Open QuiverTextToSVGNodeV2 and enter a concise, style-aware prompt (e.g., "flat monoline outline of a rocket, minimal, geometric"). If your template exposes a Reference Images input, connect one or more images to guide style or proportions (high-contrast silhouettes work best).
Configure SaveSVGNode with your preferred output directory and base filename so each generated SVG is written to disk where you expect it.
Run the workflow (Queue Prompt). After execution, open the saved .svg in a vector editor (Figma, Illustrator, Inkscape) to review curves, strokes, and fills.
Iterate: refine the prompt (add terms like "outline", "filled", "duotone", "simple geometry"), adjust or swap reference images if used, and run again to explore variations or a cohesive set.
suggestedUseCases: App and web icon sets that must remain crisp at multiple sizes
Logo ideation and quick mark exploration from text briefs
Infographic pictograms and signage symbols
Laser cutting, CNC, or plotter-friendly outlines requiring vector paths

faqItems.question: What makes QuiverTextToSVGNodeV2 different from typical text-to-image nodes?
faqItems.answer: Instead of generating raster pixels, it uses the Quiver model to synthesize vector geometry and returns SVG markup (paths, shapes, groups). This yields resolution-independent graphics suited for design workflows.

faqItems.question: How can I get cleaner, simpler paths?
faqItems.answer: Keep prompts focused on structure and style (e.g., "minimal", "monoline outline", "flat icon"). Avoid overly detailed descriptions. Use high-contrast reference images when available, and simplify further in your vector editor if needed.

faqItems.question: Can I control colors in the SVG?
faqItems.answer: You can nudge color and fill style with prompt wording (e.g., "black outline", "two-color flat fill"). Regardless of the output, colors are easy to edit afterward in any vector editor since the result is an SVG.

faqItems.question: How do I generate multiple variations?
faqItems.answer: Run the workflow multiple times with small prompt tweaks or different reference images. Each run produces its own SVG via SaveSVGNode, making it straightforward to compare and select the best version.

94ed41b87579.title: AI on the Lot 2026 - Z-Image Turbo - t2i + Upscale
94ed41b87579.description: The second workflow released for AI on the Lot 2026, made available for ComfyUI 101 workshop attendees to open and follow along if they choose. Same text-to-image setup using Z-Image Turbo, now with an upscale step added for higher resolution output.
94ed41b87579.metaDescription: Prompt to polished: text-to-image with built-in upscaling and side-by-side compare in ComfyUI. Generate, compare, and save high-quality results fast.
94ed41b87579.extendedDescription:
AI on the Lot 2026 - Z-Image Turbo - t2i + Upscale is a streamlined ComfyUI workflow that takes you from a text prompt to a polished, high-resolution image in one pass. It centers on a custom text-to-image node (Z-Image Turbo; UUID f2fdebf6-dfaf-43b6-9eb2-7f70613cfdc1) to generate the initial image and then routes the output through an integrated upscale stage for added detail and clarity. The SaveImage node captures your outputs to disk, while the ImageCompare node produces a side-by-side composite so you can visually judge how much quality the upscale added—and whether any artifacts were introduced.

Technically, the workflow chains a T2I generation step into an upscaling step, minimizing manual wiring and keeping your iteration loop tight. You enter your prompt (and optional negative prompt) in the Z-Image Turbo node, adjust core generation controls like seed, steps, and guidance (as exposed by the node), and set your target resolution or scale factor for the upscale stage. The ImageCompare node receives both the base and upscaled images to output a comparison image, and SaveImage records each stage with consistent filenames for easy A/B review. Because the T2I node accepts whichever checkpoint you load in your ComfyUI environment, you can pair this workflow with your preferred model without changing the graph.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON into ComfyUI (Drag-and-drop the file onto the canvas or use the ComfyUI Manager to import).

Open the Z-Image Turbo node (UUID f2fdebf6-dfaf-43b6-9eb2-7f70613cfdc1) and enter your prompt and, if available, a negative prompt. Set seed, steps, and guidance to taste. If the node exposes model/vae inputs, point them to your preferred checkpoint.
Set your output size or upscale factor within the same node (or its connected upscale controls). Start with a modest scale (e.g., 2x) for clean detail without oversharpening.
Click Queue Prompt (or run) to execute the T2I stage followed by the upscale stage. The ImageCompare node will generate a side-by-side composite of the base vs. upscaled result.
Review the comparison image to check detail retention and artifacts. Tweak prompts, seed, steps, guidance, or upscale factor as needed and re-run.
When satisfied, let the SaveImage node write both the base and upscaled outputs to disk. Optionally edit the filename prefix in SaveImage to keep your versions organized.
suggestedUseCases: Upscaling concept art or mood boards from quick prompts to presentation-ready images.
Creating higher-resolution product mockups or pack shots directly from text prompts.
Generating social media graphics that need crisp edges and readable text after upscaling.
Storyboards and previsualization where you iterate fast at low res, then upscale the best frames.
Thumbnail and banner creation with built-in A/B comparison to ensure clarity at target sizes.

faqItems.question: Which models does this workflow use for text-to-image?
faqItems.answer: The workflow does not bundle a specific model. The Z-Image Turbo node uses whichever checkpoint you load in your ComfyUI environment (as exposed by that node). Point it to your preferred base model and VAE, and the rest of the graph will work unchanged.

faqItems.question: How do I control the upscale amount and avoid over-sharpening?
faqItems.answer: Use the upscale factor or strength controls attached to the Z-Image Turbo/upscale stage. Start at 2x and increase only if needed. If edges look crunchy, reduce the upscale factor, lower the sharpening/strength (if available), or slightly increase generation steps for a cleaner base before upscaling.

faqItems.question: What is ImageCompare showing me?
faqItems.answer: ImageCompare creates a side-by-side composite of the base (pre-upscale) image and the upscaled image. Use it to check detail gains and spot artifacts. If you don’t see the comparison, confirm both image outputs are connected to ImageCompare’s inputs before running.

faqItems.question: How can I reproduce a result later?
faqItems.answer: Set and record a fixed seed in the Z-Image Turbo node and keep your prompt, steps, guidance, and upscale settings unchanged. SaveImage will write files with consistent naming; keeping the same seed and parameters will yield repeatable outputs with the same model and node settings.

956d363975fe.title: FastH3 OmniRef: Reference to Video
956d363975fe.description: Generate synchronized video with matching audio from a text prompt plus a reference image using the FastH3 OmniRef eight-step distilled model, which renders both streams in just eight sampling steps. Takes 1 input image and produces 1 video output. Ideal for animating reference characters, creating talking avatars, and rapid social media video prototyping.
956d363975fe.metaDescription: Turn a single image and prompt into a synced video with audio using FastH3 OmniRef (MiniMax H3) in just eight steps. Ideal for avatars and quick video prototypes.
956d363975fe.extendedDescription:
FastH3 OmniRef: Reference to Video is a reference-to-video ComfyUI workflow that turns a single image plus a text prompt into a short, synchronized video with matching audio. It’s built around FastVideo’s FastH3 OmniRef checkpoint on MiniMax H3 (the eight-step distilled student, step 3500), so it renders both the visual sequence and an aligned audio track in just eight sampling steps. The User Inputs group collects your reference image (LoadImage), prompt (PrimitiveStringMultiline), and resolution (ResolutionSelector), while RandomNoise sets the run’s seed for repeatability.

Under the hood, the Models group loads the MiniMax/OmniRef components: UNETLoader pulls the FastH3 OmniRef UNet, CLIPLoader loads the MiniMax H3 text encoder, and VAELoader provides the paired decoders used later for frames and audio. The MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo node fuses CLIP text conditioning with the reference image so the subject’s look carries through the entire clip. Sampling is handled by KSamplerSelect with BasicScheduler and SamplerCustomAdvanced, guided by BasicGuider for CFG, and patched by MiniMaxH3SigmaShift to match the model’s eight-step distilled trajectory. After sampling, VAEDecode reconstructs video frames and VAEDecodeAudio reconstructs the audio stream; CreateVideo muxes frames and audio at your chosen fps, and SaveVideo writes the final file. For longer, larger clips (e.g., 1344x768 at ~15s), enabling a VSA sparse-attention backend can be ~2x faster than int8 attention; for shorter 5s/120-frame runs (the template default), speedups are smaller.
howToUse: Load the FastH3 OmniRef: Reference to Video workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the required models are installed: MiniMax-H3 text/UNet components and the FastH3-OmniRef checkpoint. Point UNETLoader and CLIPLoader to the correct files if needed.

In User Inputs: use LoadImage to select your reference image and PrimitiveStringMultiline to write a clear prompt describing motion, style, and speech intent (e.g., camera moves, mood, or simple lines to say).

Set resolution with ResolutionSelector (start modest, e.g., ~1MP) and confirm frame count/fps settings (often controlled via a ComfyMathExpression feeding CreateVideo). Keep the default 120 frames (~5s) if you’re on limited VRAM.

Adjust guidance in PrimitiveFloat (CFG) routed to BasicGuider: lower values track the reference image more strictly; higher values follow the text prompt more strongly. Set the RandomNoise seed for reproducible results.

Queue the workflow. The KSamplerSelect + BasicScheduler + SamplerCustomAdvanced stack, patched by MiniMaxH3SigmaShift, will run the eight-step trajectory. VAEDecode and VAEDecodeAudio will reconstruct frames and audio.

When complete, CreateVideo will mux frames and audio; SaveVideo writes the final file to disk. Review the output; iterate by refining the prompt, adjusting CFG, resolution, or duration/fps to reach your target look and timing.
suggestedUseCases: Talking avatars from a single portrait for announcements, tutorials, or customer support.
Rapid product or character motion studies for previsualization and social media teasers.
Brand mascot animations matching a reference look while following a textual brief.
Education and explainers where a still reference needs quick animated delivery with voice.
Prototype dialogue scenes using a consistent character appearance across takes.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow keep audio and video in sync?
faqItems.answer: FastH3 OmniRef (MiniMax H3) was distilled to produce aligned audiovisual latents in just eight steps. The sampler stack (KSamplerSelect + BasicScheduler + SamplerCustomAdvanced) follows the MiniMaxH3SigmaShift-patched schedule, then VAEDecode and VAEDecodeAudio decode the corresponding frame and audio latents before CreateVideo muxes them together.

faqItems.question: How can I get more faithful likeness to my reference image?
faqItems.answer: Use a clean, well-lit reference with the subject centered and unobstructed. Lower CFG (in PrimitiveFloat feeding BasicGuider) to bias toward the reference look, and keep resolution reasonable to avoid artifacts. Also keep the prompt descriptive but not contradictory to the visual identity of your reference.

faqItems.question: I’m running out of VRAM or it’s slow. What should I change first?
faqItems.answer: Reduce resolution in ResolutionSelector and shorten the clip (fewer frames) via the ComfyMathExpression that drives duration/fps. If your environment supports VSA sparse attention, enable it—at high resolutions and longer clips it can be ~2x faster than int8 attention, though for short ~5s clips gains may be modest.

faqItems.question: Can I swap in other checkpoints or text encoders?
faqItems.answer: You can point UNETLoader and CLIPLoader to compatible MiniMax H3 family weights, but for reference conditioning and eight-step AV generation to behave as expected, use the FastH3 OmniRef checkpoint and the matching MiniMax-H3 CLIP. Mixing incompatible weights may break reference fidelity or audio decoding.

9654558acd06.title: Kling O1: Text to Video
9654558acd06.description: Generate videos from text descriptions using Kling O1. Create dynamic video content with natural language prompts.
9654558acd06.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate text-to-video with Kling O1 using KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode and SaveVideo. Clear steps, tips, and best practices.
9654558acd06.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns plain-language prompts into short videos using the Kling O1 model. At its core is the KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode, which sends your prompt to the Kling service and receives a generated clip. The node handles prompt text and generation options (such as clip length and size), then passes the resulting video to SaveVideo, which writes the output to disk.

Technically, the KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode is the generation engine: it packages your prompt and settings, calls the Kling O1 API, and outputs a video stream or frame sequence as a single node result. The SaveVideo node consumes that output and saves it to a file, where you can control basics like output path and frame rate. For best results, write prompts that clearly define the subject, action, setting, and camera behavior (for example: "wide shot, slow dolly-in, golden-hour lighting"). Keep durations and resolutions within the node’s supported ranges to reduce errors and queue times. If the node exposes a seed, fix it to make variations more reproducible.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON into ComfyUI. Install the Kling node package if prompted, then open the KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode and configure its API credentials (e.g., API key/endpoint) as required by the node.

In KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode, enter a clear prompt that specifies subject, action, setting, and camera cues. Adjust generation options the node provides (e.g., duration, resolution or aspect ratio, frame rate, and optionally a seed if available).
Optionally refine style and motion: add descriptors for lighting, mood, camera movement, and pacing. If the node offers negative cues or safety options, set them to discourage unwanted artifacts.
Open the SaveVideo node and set the output filename/path and frames-per-second. Ensure the video output from KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode is connected to SaveVideo’s input.
Queue and run the workflow. The Kling node will submit the request to the service and return the generated clip when ready. Monitor ComfyUI’s console/log for progress or errors.
Review the saved video, then iterate: keep the seed fixed for controlled changes, tweak the prompt and timing, and adjust size/fps to balance fidelity, motion smoothness, and generation time.

Social media teasers and mood pieces based on short descriptive prompts.
Explainer intros or cutaways illustrating an idea or product in motion.
Style exploration: generate the same scene across different looks and camera moves.
Previsualization for motion, lighting, or composition before full production.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes. KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode calls the external Kling O1 service, which typically requires an API key and endpoint. Configure credentials in the node’s settings or environment as documented by the node.

faqItems.question: What resolutions and durations are supported?
faqItems.answer: Limits depend on the Kling O1 service and the node’s implementation. Use the options exposed by KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode and stay within the recommended ranges shown in the node’s UI or documentation to avoid errors or long queue times.

faqItems.question: How can I get smoother motion and fewer artifacts?
faqItems.answer: Write precise prompts with clear subject focus and camera instructions (e.g., slow pan, tripod shot). Keep clip lengths modest, avoid overly complex multi-subject actions in a single prompt, and choose a frame rate that matches the motion you want. Iterate with small changes and, if available, control the seed.

faqItems.question: What format does SaveVideo output?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo writes the clip to a file using the path and fps you set in the node. The exact container/codec options depend on your ComfyUI setup and the node’s parameters; MP4 is commonly used when available.

96d528e93204.title: Eleven v4: Text to Dialogue
96d528e93204.description: Generate a multi-speaker dialogue from text with Eleven v4: give every entry its own line and its own voice, direct the delivery with audio tags such as [quietly] or [laughs], or clone a voice from a sample and let it take a turn. One audio file is output. Ideal for podcasts, game dialogue, and character conversations.
96d528e93204.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: generate multi-speaker dialogue with ElevenLabs v4. Assign preset or cloned voices per line, add [quietly]/[laughs], and export one audio file.
96d528e93204.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow turns a plain-text script into a polished, multi-speaker dialogue using ElevenLabs v4. Each line you write becomes a distinct “turn,” and each turn can use a different voice—either a preset selected with ElevenLabsVoiceSelector or a custom voice created on-the-fly with ElevenLabsInstantVoiceClone. The core ElevenLabsTextToDialogue node sequences your turns in order and synthesizes a single, continuous audio file, so you end up with one mix-ready track for podcasts, game dialogue, or character conversations. Delivery cues like [quietly] or [laughs] can be embedded directly in your script to influence performance.

Two grouped paths are included: Option 1: Use Preset Voice and Option 2: Create a Voice Clone. If you want clones, bring in a clean reference using LoadAudio or capture one with RecordAudio, feed it to ElevenLabsInstantVoiceClone, and wire that clone to any turns you want it to speak. The template’s inputs parameter sets how many dialogue turns to render (1–10). It ships with 4 turns that alternate two voices by default. SaveAudioAdvanced writes the final result to disk, while Note and MarkdownNote provide inline guidance. Some nodes are bypassed when the template opens—select them and press Ctrl-B to enable before running.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then select any bypassed nodes and press Ctrl-B to enable them. Ensure your ElevenLabs nodes are configured with a valid API key.
Choose your path: Option 1 (Use Preset Voice) with ElevenLabsVoiceSelector, or Option 2 (Create a Voice Clone) using LoadAudio or RecordAudio feeding ElevenLabsInstantVoiceClone.
Set inputs to the number of turns (1–10). Enter one line of dialogue per turn, adding delivery cues like [quietly] or [laughs] where desired.
Assign a voice to every turn: connect the output of ElevenLabsVoiceSelector or ElevenLabsInstantVoiceClone to the corresponding voice input on ElevenLabsTextToDialogue.
Queue/Run the graph. ElevenLabsTextToDialogue will synthesize each turn in order and combine them into a single audio stream.
In SaveAudioAdvanced, set your output path (and any available format options), then run to export the final dialogue as one audio file.
suggestedUseCases: Podcast intros, host–guest banter, and scripted promo segments
Game NPC conversations and interactive dialogue prototypes
Audio drama or audiobook scenes with distinct character voices
E-learning role-plays and customer service training simulations
Product demos or explainer content with alternating narrators

faqItems.question: How do I add more speakers or turns?
faqItems.answer: Increase inputs to the desired number of turns (up to 10 in this template). For each new turn, paste a single line of dialogue and connect a voice source (preset via ElevenLabsVoiceSelector or cloned via ElevenLabsInstantVoiceClone). You can reuse voices across multiple turns or mix several different voices.

faqItems.question: What’s the best way to create a good voice clone?
faqItems.answer: Use a clean, dry recording (1–2 minutes of clear speech, minimal noise, no music). You can capture it with RecordAudio or import with LoadAudio, then feed it into ElevenLabsInstantVoiceClone. Make sure you have rights to use the source voice and avoid background music or strong effects that can degrade clone quality.

faqItems.question: Which delivery tags are supported?
faqItems.answer: This template is designed around ElevenLabs v4’s interpretation of simple bracketed cues. Tags like [quietly] and [laughs] can influence delivery. Keep tags short and natural, and rely on punctuation (commas, periods, ellipses) to shape pacing. If a cue doesn’t change the read, try rewording the line or using a simpler tag.

faqItems.question: Why am I getting an authentication or quota error?
faqItems.answer: Ensure your ElevenLabs API key is set in the ElevenLabs nodes’ settings and that your account has available quota. Check the ComfyUI console/logs for the specific error message. If needed, retry with shorter text or fewer turns to stay within rate and character limits.

977fefa2b934.title: Image → Song → Audio-Reactive Video
977fefa2b934.description: Create songs with ACE Step 1.5 XL and audio-reactive videos with LTX 2.3 and the Audio-Reactive LoRA.
977fefa2b934.metaDescription: Create a song with ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo and turn one image into an audio‑reactive video using LTX 2.3 + Audio‑Reactive LoRA in ComfyUI.
977fefa2b934.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a single image into a music-backed, audio‑reactive video by combining text-to-music generation (ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo) with image-to-video animation (LTX 2.3) enhanced by an Audio‑Reactive LoRA. You provide one image and a short creative brief; the workflow uses a GeminiNode to draft both "style tags" for the visuals and "lyrics" for the song in one pass. A RegexExtract node then splits that text at '---': everything before becomes visual style tags for LTX 2.3, and everything after becomes lyrics fed to ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo. The generated song is saved via SaveAudioMP3 and then drives the reactivity of the video, which is saved with SaveVideo.

Technically, the pipeline is organized into groups: Load Image, Create ACE Step 1.5 Prompts, Create Audio‑Reactive LoRA Prompt, Regex Extract, ACE Step 1.5 XL, and LTX 2.3 with Audio‑Reactive LoRA. The Audio‑Reactive LoRA (see the linked model card) adds motion effects that follow the music; adjust its strength between 1.0 and 2.0 (1.4+ for stronger effects) for best results. PreviewAny helps you check intermediate outputs (prompts, audio, and frames) before final render, while MarkdownNote contains quick tips inside the graph. The result is a streamlined image → song → audio‑reactive video pipeline that’s easy to iterate: tweak style tags and lyrics, re‑generate the track, and re‑render the video until it matches your creative intent.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote group for quick pointers.
Add your source image to the LoadImage node (single image works best).
In the GeminiNode, enter a brief describing visual style and lyrics. Ensure the output is split by '---' with style tags before and lyrics after (you can also paste your own text in that format).
Run the prompt nodes. The RegexExtract group will route everything before '---' to the LTX 2.3 style prompt and everything after '---' to ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo as lyrics.
Generate the song with the ACE Step 1.5 XL group and confirm SaveAudioMP3 is writing the file where you expect. PreviewAny can help you check the audio and prompts.
Set the Audio‑Reactive LoRA strength (1.0–2.0; try 1.4+ for stronger motion), then run the LTX 2.3 group to animate your image. Finally, render with SaveVideo and review the result in PreviewAny.
suggestedUseCases: Turn fan art or album art into a lyric video with motion synced to a freshly generated song.
Create short, reactive social media loops from a product or poster image paired with a custom jingle.
Make podcast or stream intro videos from a cover image with audio‑driven motion.
Generate mood pieces: ambient track + subtle, style‑driven camera movement from a single still.
Rapid concept reels: iterate lyrics and style tags to explore look-and-sound directions quickly.

faqItems.question: How does the '---' split work and why is it needed?
faqItems.answer: The RegexExtract node captures everything before '---' as style tags for LTX 2.3 and everything after as lyrics for ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo. This guarantees each model receives a purpose‑built prompt from a single GeminiNode output.

faqItems.question: How do I control how reactive the motion is?
faqItems.answer: Use the Audio‑Reactive LoRA strength in the LTX 2.3 group. A range of 1.0–2.0 is recommended; try ~1.4 or higher for stronger effects. More dynamic audio (clear percussion, drops, and swells) will also produce more noticeable motion.

faqItems.question: Can I use my own audio instead of generating with ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Replace or bypass the ACE branch and feed your audio into the LTX 2.3 + Audio‑Reactive LoRA input path (use a compatible audio loader node in ComfyUI). Ensure the video duration matches your track length.

faqItems.question: Any tips for better visual results?

Run the workflow. The node sends audio to the Fish Audio ASR service, auto-detects the language, and returns the transcript text plus segments_json.
Find the saved transcript from the SaveText node in your ComfyUI output folder (or the path you configured in the node).
Inspect segments_json in the FishAudioSpeechToText outputs. If precise_timestamps is off, segments_json will be empty; turn it on and re-run to get start/end times.

Podcast and voiceover indexing so you can quickly find and quote key moments.
