9851c174a194.title: ACE-Step 1.5XL Turbo: Text to Music
9851c174a194.description: Generate high-quality music from text prompts using the distilled 4B ACE-Step model. Produces commercial-ready audio in just 8 inference steps without CFG.
9851c174a194.metaDescription: Text-to-music in ComfyUI with ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo: encode prompts, sample in 8 steps without CFG, decode to audio, and export MP3 fast.
9851c174a194.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a plain-language text prompt into finished music using the ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo model. Your prompt is encoded by TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5 (backed by DualCLIPLoader) into audio-aware conditioning. EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio creates a blank latent audio canvas at your chosen length, and UNETLoader loads the distilled 4B ACE-Step checkpoint (acestep_v1.5_xl_turbo_bf16.safetensors). ModelSamplingAuraFlow configures the sampler schedule tuned for ACE-Step, and KSampler performs just 8 diffusion steps to synthesize the latent audio. The audio is then reconstructed with VAELoader + VAEDecodeAudio and saved via SaveAudioMP3.

What makes this workflow practical is its “turbo” configuration: no classifier-free guidance (CFG) is used, enabled by ConditioningZeroOut feeding an intentionally empty negative conditioning. This keeps prompts straightforward (focus only on what you want), while ModelSamplingAuraFlow and KSampler deliver fast, stable results. The graph is organized into Model and Prompt groups for clarity, and uses PrimitiveInt/PrimitiveNode for quick edits to seed, steps, and duration. The result is a tight, teachable text-to-music pipeline you can run repeatedly for variations or integrate as a reusable subgraph.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and install any missing custom nodes required by the listed node types. Keep the Model and Prompt groups expanded for clarity.

Download acestep_v1.5_xl_turbo_bf16.safetensors and place it in ComfyUI/models/diffusion (or your configured diffusion_models folder). In the Model group, confirm UNETLoader points to this file. Ensure VAELoader and DualCLIPLoader are connected.

In the Prompt group, enter your music description in TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5 (e.g., "warm lo‑fi hip‑hop beat, mellow Rhodes, 85 BPM, vinyl crackle, relaxed mood"). Leave negative prompt handling as-is—ConditioningZeroOut disables CFG on purpose.

Set duration in EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio (choose the seconds/samples field provided by the node). Use PrimitiveInt/PrimitiveNode to set seed and confirm KSampler steps are 8. ModelSamplingAuraFlow should be connected to KSampler.
Click Queue/Execute. KSampler will generate the audio latents in ~8 steps, VAEDecodeAudio will reconstruct the waveform, and SaveAudioMP3 will write the result to disk.

Review the output. For new variations, change the seed; for stronger adherence, refine the prompt with genre, instruments, tempo, and production terms. If needed, slightly adjust steps (e.g., 8–12) while keeping CFG disabled.
suggestedUseCases: Quickly producing background beds for social videos, reels, and shorts from concise prompts.
Drafting podcast intros/outros or stingers with consistent style and length.
Creating prototype game loops and ambient soundscapes during early design phases.
Generating ad/jingle ideas for client pitches where fast iteration matters.
Stock music variations for content libraries with prompt-based tagging.

faqItems.question: Why is CFG disabled, and can I use negative prompts?
faqItems.answer: This workflow intentionally disables classifier-free guidance using ConditioningZeroOut for fast, stable sampling. Negative prompts are ignored in this setup. If you need negatives, replace ConditioningZeroOut with an explicit negative encoder path and enable CFG in KSampler—but that changes the workflow’s behavior.

faqItems.question: How do I control duration and structure (e.g., 10–30 seconds)?
faqItems.answer: Set the length in EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio (seconds or samples, depending on the node’s fields). The model interprets structure via text (e.g., “16‑bar trap loop,” “slow build and soft drop”). For longer pieces, generate multiple segments and arrange them in a DAW.

faqItems.question: What sampler settings should I use for best results?
faqItems.answer: Keep KSampler at 8 steps with ModelSamplingAuraFlow connected—this is tuned for ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo. If you hear artifacts, try modest increases (e.g., 10–12 steps). Maintain CFG disabled to match the workflow’s design.

faqItems.question: What format does it export, and can I change it?
faqItems.answer: The graph saves MP3 via SaveAudioMP3. You can adjust its bitrate if the node exposes that option. If you prefer WAV, swap in a compatible WAV saver node and connect it after VAEDecodeAudio.

99451b789a58.title: Image Upscale: SeedVR2

An optional ImageCompare node lets you preview a side‑by‑side before/after to verify gains in clarity.

Technically, the SeedVR2 node consumes the input image tensor and applies the SeedVR2 model’s learned upscaling to reconstruct higher‑frequency details at a larger resolution. Because this is deterministic super‑resolution (not text-to-image), results are driven by the source image’s content and quality rather than prompts. The included MarkdownNote inside the graph provides quick, inline guidance. Note that ImageCompare is available only under Nodes 2.0, so enable that mode if you want the built‑in A/B viewer.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI. If you plan to use the A/B preview, switch to Nodes 2.0 (Menu -> Nodes 2.0) so the ImageCompare node is available.
In the LoadImage node, select your source image (PNG/JPG and other common raster formats are supported).

Locate the SeedVR2 upscaler node (custom node ID c35dd4ba-0fe3-47d6-afce-1c56d9fe5beb). Ensure the SeedVR2 model is installed and selected if the node exposes a model selector. Adjust any available settings the node provides (for example, scale or detail controls, if present).
Optionally connect the original image and the upscaled output to the ImageCompare node to preview a side-by-side comparison inside ComfyUI.
In the SaveImage node, set a filename prefix or destination options as provided. This node writes your result to the ComfyUI output directory.
Click Queue/Execute to run the graph. Inspect the ImageCompare preview (if enabled) and retrieve the final upscaled image from the output folder.
suggestedUseCases: Sharpening product photos or portfolio images for web and print without re-shooting at higher resolution.
Upscaling UI elements, icons, or 2D game textures for higher‑DPI displays.
Enhancing scanned artwork or illustrations to archive in a higher definition.
Improving clarity of screenshots and diagrams for documentation or presentations.

faqItems.question: Do I need to enable Nodes 2.0 to use this workflow?

faqItems.question: Where are my upscaled images saved?
faqItems.answer: SaveImage writes to the ComfyUI output directory, using the filename or prefix configured in the SaveImage node. After running, check the output folder for your result.

faqItems.question: What image formats are supported?
faqItems.answer: LoadImage accepts common raster formats like PNG and JPG. The output format is determined by SaveImage and/or your ComfyUI settings, typically PNG by default.

faqItems.question: Does SeedVR2 add new content like generative models do?
faqItems.answer: No. SeedVR2 performs super‑resolution to enhance and reconstruct detail at a higher resolution. It does not invent new scene content or require prompts.

9974666c3acb.title: Seed Audio 1.0: Text + Image to Audio

Because everything runs inside a simple chain—LoadImage → ByteDanceSeedAudio → SaveAudioAdvanced—you can iterate quickly: swap images to change the perceived character, refine the prompt to adjust performance and sound design, and re-run to compare variations. This makes it practical for rapid voice ideation, scene-building, and audio mockups without leaving ComfyUI.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. Ensure the ByteDanceSeedAudio extension is installed and configured (e.g., any required model or API settings per the node’s documentation).
Open the LoadImage node and select a clear, single-subject character image (ideally a forward-facing portrait). Crop or replace the image if you need a different vocal identity.

In the ByteDanceSeedAudio node, enter your text prompt. Include the spoken script plus guidance for ambience, music, and SFX (e.g., calm narrator, soft lo‑fi beat, light rain, subtle city noise). Adjust any exposed parameters such as seed or clip length if available.
Configure SaveAudioAdvanced with your preferred output path and file format. If the node offers sample rate or normalization controls, set them to match your target workflow.
Queue and run the graph. When it finishes, open the file saved by SaveAudioAdvanced to review. Iterate by refining the prompt, swapping the image, or varying the seed to explore alternate takes.

Game prototype dialogue with built-in ambience and SFX for quick scene feel without full sound design.
Audio drama or podcast character samples to test casting and tone before full production.
Short-form content (reels/shorts) with a stylistic narrator and light background music generated from a single prompt.

faqItems.question: How does the image influence the generated voice?
faqItems.answer: The image conditions the model to infer a fitting vocal identity (e.g., timbre and style cues) for the character. Use a clean, single-subject portrait with good lighting and minimal occlusion for more stable, consistent results.

faqItems.question: Can I control ambience, music, and SFX separately?
faqItems.answer: Control them via the text prompt—be explicit about mood, instruments, intensity, and placement (e.g., soft piano underscore, distant thunder, quiet cafe ambience). The model outputs a single mixed track; stems aren’t provided by this workflow.

faqItems.question: How do I get consistent results or explore variations?
faqItems.answer: Keep the same image and prompt, and if the node exposes a seed parameter, fix it to reproduce a take. To explore alternatives, change the seed or make small prompt edits (pace, emotion, music style) and re-run.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key or extra setup?
faqItems.answer: It depends on your ByteDanceSeedAudio node build. Some variants require API credentials or additional model setup. Open the node, check its fields/tooltips, and follow the extension’s installation notes before running the graph.

999b68cf27cb.title: LTX-2.5 DFR: Image to Video
999b68cf27cb.description: Generate a short video with sound from a single image using LTX-2.5's DFR (Diffusion Fidelity Rendering) path: a half-resolution pass that carries generated detailing keyframes, a spatial x2 detailing pass with the pixel-spatial IC-LoRA, and an optional temporal x2 pass. Suited to cinematic shots, character beats and talking-image clips that need motion and synchronized audio.
999b68cf27cb.metaDescription: Turn a single image into a cinematic video with LTX‑2.5 DFR: half‑res pass, spatial ×2 IC‑LoRA detailing, optional temporal ×2, and synced audio in ComfyUI.
999b68cf27cb.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a single image into a short, cinematic video using LTX‑2.5’s DFR (Diffusion Fidelity Rendering) path. The subgraph “Image to Video (LTX‑2.5 DFR)” runs a half‑resolution generation to establish motion and generate detailing keyframes, then applies a spatial ×2 detailing pass with a pixel‑spatial IC‑LoRA to recover fine texture. For projects that need extra smoothness, you can optionally add a temporal ×2 pass to densify motion between frames. The result is a cohesive clip that preserves your image’s look while adding natural camera movement and subject animation, with synchronized audio when provided by the subgraph.

Technically, the pipeline is compact and easy to drive in ComfyUI: LoadImage brings in your source frame, ResolutionSelector sets aspect and target size, and the DFR subgraph node (97d5d35b-bb0d-4212-b2f2-97ab13cbfb1f) encapsulates the LTX‑2 family model and its IC‑LoRA detailing passes. PreviewImage helps you quickly inspect a representative frame before final encoding, and SaveVideo writes the finished clip (including audio if the subgraph outputs it). MarkdownNote nodes in the template annotate key choices and link to ComfyUI’s Subgraph feature, so you can open the subgraph and tweak options without getting lost.
howToUse: Load the “LTX‑2.5 DFR: Image to Video” workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the LTX‑2/LTX‑2.5 model files are available. Read any in‑graph MarkdownNote tips.
Connect or open the LoadImage node and select your source image (try the provided office_garden_169_outpaint.png to start).
Set your target aspect and size with ResolutionSelector (e.g., 16:9 landscape or 9:16 vertical). The DFR path will first render at half‑resolution, then spatially ×2 detail back to target size.
Open the subgraph node “Image to Video (LTX‑2.5 DFR)” to review its options. Leave Temporal ×2 off for a quick draft; enable it later if you want smoother motion. Keep defaults for your first run.

Queue the workflow. Use PreviewImage to sanity‑check a frame, then review the output from SaveVideo. If the subgraph includes an audio branch, the saved file will contain a synced audio track; otherwise you’ll get a silent clip.

Iterate: adjust ResolutionSelector for your delivery format, toggle Temporal ×2 if motion feels sparse, and re‑queue. For best fidelity, keep the target duration short and avoid extreme aspect changes from the source image.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic establishing shots from a static location photo (subtle dolly/zoom with preserved texture).
Talking‑image or character beat clips where synchronized audio and nuanced head/face motion matter.
Product hero loops for ecommerce or social posts, adding gentle parallax and lighting accents.
Album/cover art brought to life with tasteful motion and optional background audio.
UI backgrounds and splash screens that need short, seamless motion while maintaining brand imagery.

faqItems.question: What does the DFR (Diffusion Fidelity Rendering) path actually do?
faqItems.answer: DFR runs a half‑resolution generation that establishes motion and produces detailing keyframes, then applies a spatial ×2 pass with a pixel‑spatial IC‑LoRA to recover high‑frequency detail. An optional temporal ×2 pass can further densify motion for smoother playback. This sequence improves fidelity and temporal coherence compared to a single‑pass render.

faqItems.question: When should I enable the optional Temporal ×2 pass?
faqItems.answer: Enable Temporal ×2 when motion feels choppy or you need extra smoothness for character beats and slow camera moves. It increases compute time but reduces temporal gaps between frames. For quick drafts or very short clips, leaving it off is faster.

faqItems.question: Will this work with any aspect ratio?
faqItems.answer: Yes—use ResolutionSelector to target 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, etc. For best results, keep the chosen aspect close to your source image to avoid heavy cropping or padding that can reduce detail or introduce stretching.

faqItems.question: How is audio handled in the final video?
faqItems.answer: If the subgraph produces an audio track, SaveVideo will mux it into the output so motion and sound are synchronized. If no audio branch is active, the result will be a silent clip—you can add music or VO later in an editor.

Crafting personalized video messages with character avatars.

faqItems.question: Can I use multiple reference images in this workflow?

faqItems.question: Is it necessary to include an audio or text prompt?

faqItems.question: How does the Kling O3 model ensure character consistency?

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported for the reference image?

99aec65eea89.title: MelBandRoFormer Audio Separation
99aec65eea89.description: Load an audio file and separate it into vocal and instrumental stems using the MelBandRoFormer model. Outputs two MP3 files for isolated vocals and background music.
99aec65eea89.metaDescription: Isolate vocals and instrumentals from any track in ComfyUI using MelBandRoFormer. Load audio, separate stems, and export two MP3 files fast and clean.
99aec65eea89.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow performs high-quality voice isolation using the MelBandRoFormer model. It takes a single mixed audio track and separates it into two stems: isolated vocals and instrumental accompaniment. The pipeline starts with LoadAudio to ingest your source file, then MelBandRoFormerModelLoader loads the pretrained weights (MelBandRoformer_fp16.safetensors) from models/diffusion_models. The core separation happens in MelBandRoFormerSampler, which runs inference and outputs two audio tensors—one for vocals and one for background music—ready for export via paired SaveAudioMP3 nodes.

Technically, MelBandRoFormer applies a transformer-based architecture that operates in band-split, time–frequency space to estimate source components. In practice, that means it learns masks that suppress accompaniment when extracting vocals and vice versa, yielding cleaner stems with fewer musical artifacts. The included MarkdownNote provides inline guidance inside the canvas. Because the workflow is node-driven, you can easily swap SaveAudioMP3 for a WAV saver, change output filenames, or tweak Sampler options like chunking/overlap (if exposed by your node version) to balance speed, memory use, and separation quality.
howToUse: Install the custom node: Add ComfyUI-MelBandRoFormer to ComfyUI/custom_nodes and restart ComfyUI.
Place the model file: Copy MelBandRoformer_fp16.safetensors into ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/.
Load the workflow: Open the MelBandRoFormer Audio Separation workflow JSON in ComfyUI.
Select your input: In the LoadAudio node, browse to your song, podcast, or clip.
Load the model: In MelBandRoFormerModelLoader, confirm the path to MelBandRoformer_fp16.safetensors.
Run separation: Execute the graph. The MelBandRoFormerSampler outputs vocals and instrumental to two SaveAudioMP3 nodes, which write the respective MP3 files to your output folder.
suggestedUseCases: Create karaoke or backing tracks by removing vocals from songs.
Extract clean acapellas for remixes, mashups, or sampling.
Podcast post-production: separate speech from background music for independent leveling and noise control.
Video editing: isolate dialogue from score/ambience for clearer mixes.
Audio restoration: reduce musical bleed under voice-overs before EQ and compression.

faqItems.question: Do I need a GPU to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: A modern GPU is strongly recommended for reasonable speeds. Some setups may run on CPU, but processing will be significantly slower. If you encounter memory issues on GPU, reduce any chunk size or increase overlap settings in the Sampler (if available) to manage VRAM.

faqItems.question: What audio formats can I load and save?
faqItems.answer: LoadAudio typically accepts common formats like WAV, MP3, and FLAC. The provided workflow saves MP3 stems via SaveAudioMP3. If you need lossless output, swap the saver node for a WAV variant in ComfyUI.

faqItems.question: The stems have some bleed or artifacts. How can I improve quality?
faqItems.answer: Try increasing overlap or adjusting chunk size in MelBandRoFormerSampler if those controls are exposed by your node version. Also ensure the input isn’t clipped and avoid overly compressed masters when possible. For final polish, apply light noise gating or spectral denoising to the vocal stem.

faqItems.question: Can this separate more than two stems (e.g., drums, bass, other)?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is configured for two stems: vocals and instrumental. For multi-stem separation, use a model and workflow designed for 4-stem or 5-stem outputs, or create a variant that chains models targeting specific sources.

9a53c1e7dbb7.title: Pose Detection: SDPose Multi-Person
9a53c1e7dbb7.description: Upload an image to detect human poses. Supports detection for both single individuals and multiple people within the same scene.
9a53c1e7dbb7.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow for multi-person human pose detection using SDPose. Generate pose maps, draw boxes, and blend overlays for quick previews and export.
9a53c1e7dbb7.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow detects human poses from any image, with solid support for single subjects and crowded, multi-person scenes. It uses the SDPose family of models (e.g., sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors) to infer whole-body keypoints and generate a clean pose map that you can preview, blend over the source image, and save. The core inference happens in the SDPose Detector node (ID: 01b6a731-fb78-4070-9a38-c87146da9604), which takes your loaded image and returns a pose map along with per-person detections.

Technically, the pipeline flows as follows: LoadImage brings your source into the graph, which is then passed into the SDPose Detector. A PrimitiveInt controls max_detections so you can tune how many people are picked up in the frame. ResizeImageMaskNode aligns dimensions when mixing outputs of different sizes. DrawBBoxes renders bounding boxes for each detected person, and ImageBlend overlays the pose map and/or boxes onto the original for easy visual verification. PreviewImage provides quick checks at key points, and SaveImage exports your final overlay or the raw pose map. The included Preview group makes it simple to inspect results without digging through the full node tree.

This setup is ideal when you need reliable multi-person pose conditioning for image generation, rapid quality control on detections, or visual pose overlays for presentations. It’s lightweight to run once the model is loaded and produces assets that can plug directly into downstream tasks like ControlNet-style pose guidance.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and install the SDPose model from the provided links (Hugging Face or ModelScope). Point the SDPose Detector node to sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors or your chosen SDPose checkpoint.
Use LoadImage to import a photo. If needed, adjust ResizeImageMaskNode to bring the detector input to a practical size (e.g., 768–1024 on the long side) for a balance of speed and accuracy.
Set the PrimitiveInt connected to the SDPose Detector’s max_detections. Start with a value equal to or slightly higher than the number of people you expect in the scene.
Run the workflow. Inspect the Preview group to compare the pose map, bounding boxes (DrawBBoxes), and the blended overlay (ImageBlend) against the original.
If detections are missing or truncated, increase max_detections or input resolution via ResizeImageMaskNode. If you see false positives, reduce max_detections.
When satisfied, connect SaveImage to the output you want (pose map, overlay, or original+boxes) and run to export your results.
suggestedUseCases: Create multi-person pose maps for ControlNet-style pose conditioning in image generation workflows.
Storyboard, choreography, or sports analysis where clear visualization of multiple body poses is needed.
Dataset curation and quick QA of human pose detections before labeling or downstream processing.
Fitness, ergonomics, or movement feedback where an overlaid pose map helps illustrate alignment and form.

faqItems.question: Which SDPose checkpoint should I use and where do I put it?
faqItems.answer: Use a whole-body SDPose checkpoint like sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors from the linked model pages. Place it in a models folder recognized by your ComfyUI setup (or select the file path directly in the SDPose Detector node).

faqItems.question: How do I control how many people are detected?
faqItems.answer: Adjust the PrimitiveInt feeding max_detections on the SDPose Detector node. Set it to at least the number of people you expect. For crowded scenes, raise this value and consider increasing input resolution for better recall.

faqItems.question: What resolution should I use for best results?
faqItems.answer: Keep the long edge around 768–1024 pixels for a good speed/accuracy trade-off. If small or distant people are missed, increase the input resolution in ResizeImageMaskNode. Very large inputs will be slower but can improve detection of tiny figures.

faqItems.question: Can I export keypoints as data instead of an image?
faqItems.answer: This tutorial workflow focuses on visual outputs (pose map and overlays) via SaveImage. If you need structured keypoint data, add a node that can capture the detector’s detection outputs to a JSON or text file, or use a companion exporter node if available.

9aa01ae9dbbc.title: Ideogram v4 Int8: Text to Image
9aa01ae9dbbc.description: Generate images from text prompts using the Ideogram v4 model, a state-of-the-art open-weight text-to-image system with exceptional text rendering and layout control. No file inputs are required, producing 1 image output. Ideal for creating marketing visuals, generating design mockups with precise typography, and producing high-resolution artwork with controlled compositions.
9aa01ae9dbbc.metaDescription: ComfyUI Ideogram v4 Int8 tutorial: build structured JSON prompts to generate images with precise text rendering, layout control, and easy resolution presets.
9aa01ae9dbbc.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow demonstrates how to generate images from text using the Ideogram v4 Int8 model, a state-of-the-art open-weight text-to-image system known for accurate text rendering and layout control. The graph uses a ResolutionSelector to set output dimensions, a dedicated prompt-construction subgraph (Ideogram4 Caption Prompt Template) to help you build structured prompts, and custom Ideogram v4 nodes (UUIDs 83e6e004-48ea-408e-9024-eb49c3d7dc14 and f5f04613-ee09-4cd9-9ada-a880360891d4) that handle model loading/inference. A MarkdownNote provides on-canvas guidance, PreviewAny displays the result, and SaveImage writes the final image to disk. No file inputs are required; the workflow produces a single image from your prompt.

Ideogram v4 is trained on structured JSON captions that include a scene summary, style block, background, and optional per-object descriptions with bounding boxes and hex color palettes. The included Ideogram4 Caption Prompt Template subgraph helps you conform to this schema so the model can leverage its strengths in typography and composition. Under the hood, guidance uses flow-matching, and this workflow runs an Int8-quantized variant of the model to reduce VRAM usage while preserving strong text fidelity and layout control. Model weights can be obtained from the provided links (e.g., Hugging Face/ModelScope for Comfy-Org/Ideogram-4), and the graph is compatible with community node packs such as KJNodes that expose Ideogram-specific nodes and utilities.
howToUse: Install prerequisites: Ensure ComfyUI is up to date. Install or update KJNodes (recommended) and place the Ideogram v4 Int8 model files from the linked repositories (e.g., Hugging Face: Comfy-Org/Ideogram-4) into your ComfyUI models directory as instructed by the node docs.
Load the workflow: Open the provided ComfyUI workflow JSON titled "Ideogram v4 Int8: Text to Image." Read the MarkdownNote on the canvas for quick guidance and links (including the Subgraph guide).
Choose an output size: Use the ResolutionSelector node to pick a preset or set custom width/height. Start with moderate resolutions to fit your GPU memory, then scale up as needed.

Author your prompt with the template: Open the Ideogram4 Caption Prompt Template subgraph and fill the structured fields (scene summary, style, background). For precise layout, add per-object entries with optional bounding boxes and hex color palettes. Keep the structure valid JSON so the model can fully utilize it.

Run inference: Queue the workflow. The custom Ideogram v4 nodes (UUIDs 83e6e004-48ea-408e-9024-eb49c3d7dc14 and f5f04613-ee09-4cd9-9ada-a880360891d4) will load the model and generate an image from your structured prompt.

Review and save: Inspect the result in PreviewAny. If needed, refine prompt structure (especially object boxes and styles) or resolution, then re-run. Use SaveImage to export the final image to your output folder.
suggestedUseCases: Marketing visuals with precise, on-image typography (headlines, taglines, calls-to-action).
Poster and flyer concepts where text hierarchy and layout grids must be respected.
Product mockups combining brand colors, logos, and tightly controlled placement of text elements.
UI/UX design moodboards with labeled components and color-accurate palettes.
Signage or packaging explorations that require high legibility and exact text positioning.

faqItems.question: Do I have to use the structured JSON prompt, or can I write plain text?
faqItems.answer: You can write plain text, but Ideogram v4 was trained on structured JSON captions. Using the provided Ideogram4 Caption Prompt Template (scene, style, background, optional objects with bounding boxes and colors) usually yields better text rendering and more reliable layout control.

faqItems.question: What does the Int8 quantization change?
faqItems.answer: Int8 reduces VRAM usage and can improve accessibility on smaller GPUs. Image quality remains strong, especially for text/layout tasks, though very small differences from full-precision may occur. If you have ample VRAM, you can compare variants, but Int8 is typically a great default.

faqItems.question: How do I control exact placement and colors?
faqItems.answer: In the template subgraph, add per-object entries with bounding boxes (normalized coordinates) and hex color palettes. This mirrors the model’s training schema and helps it place text/objects where you expect while honoring brand or palette constraints.

faqItems.question: Where do I get the model, and do I need extra nodes?
faqItems.answer: Download the weights from the linked repositories (e.g., Hugging Face: Comfy-Org/Ideogram-4). Installing KJNodes is recommended, as it provides Ideogram-compatible nodes. The custom nodes in this workflow (UUIDs 83e6e004-48ea-408e-9024-eb49c3d7dc14 and f5f04613-ee09-4cd9-9ada-a880360891d4) perform model loading and inference within ComfyUI.
