9bccaddaca7d.title: Image Upscale: Topaz Reimagine
9bccaddaca7d.description: Professional image enhancement using Topaz's Reimagine model with face enhancement and detail restoration.
9bccaddaca7d.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow for image upscaling with Topaz Reimagine. Enhance faces, restore details, compare results, and export crisp, high-res images.
9bccaddaca7d.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow upscales and restores images using Topaz’s Reimagine model through the TopazImageEnhanceV2 node. It’s designed for professional-grade enhancement with optional face refinement and detail restoration, making it ideal for portraits, product photos, and archival images. The core path is simple: LoadImage brings your source into the graph, TopazImageEnhanceV2 performs the AI enhancement, ImageCompare previews the before/after, and SaveImage writes the result.

Under the hood, GetImageSize reads the original dimensions to help you choose an appropriate scale, while ResizeImageMaskNode can optionally pre-size the image to a specific target (for example, to meet platform or print requirements) before enhancement. TopazImageEnhanceV2 runs the Reimagine model for upscaling and clarity, with toggles for face enhancement and detail restoration to keep skin natural while recovering fine textures. ImageCompare provides a quick quality check, and SaveImage ensures consistent output naming and format. The result is a clear, reproducible pipeline for high-quality upscaling with minimal manual steps.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the group labeled "Step 1 - Upload image."
Open the LoadImage node and select your source image. The GetImageSize node will read its dimensions to inform your scaling choice.
Optional: Set a target size or scale in ResizeImageMaskNode if you need a specific output resolution before enhancement.
Open TopazImageEnhanceV2: choose the Reimagine model, set your scale (e.g., 2x or 4x), and enable Face Enhancement and Detail Restoration based on your subject.
Run the graph. Use ImageCompare to review the original versus the enhanced output and confirm sharpness, skin texture, and artifact-free edges.
Adjust settings if needed, then save your final image with the SaveImage node.
suggestedUseCases: Portrait and headshot cleanup with face enhancement for natural, sharp results.
Product photo upscaling for e-commerce listings that require high-resolution imagery.
Old photo restoration to recover detail and reduce softness in scanned images.
Social media and marketing assets that need crisp upscales for larger formats.

faqItems.question: Do I need to configure any credentials for TopazImageEnhanceV2?
faqItems.answer: If your TopazImageEnhanceV2 setup relies on an external Topaz service/API, you must configure credentials in the node or extension settings. Check the node’s documentation or ComfyUI console for prompts or errors if credentials are missing.

faqItems.question: Should I pre-resize with ResizeImageMaskNode or let the Topaz model handle all scaling?
faqItems.answer: Use ResizeImageMaskNode if you must hit a specific output resolution (e.g., platform or print specs). Otherwise, let TopazImageEnhanceV2 handle the scale factor. Avoid extreme pre-upscaling before enhancement, as it can introduce softening or artifacts.

faqItems.question: How can I avoid over-sharpened or plastic-looking skin?
faqItems.answer: Try a lower scale (e.g., 2x instead of 4x) and reduce the intensity of detail restoration in TopazImageEnhanceV2. You can also keep Face Enhancement on while dialing back detail to maintain natural skin texture.

faqItems.question: How do I verify quality before saving?
faqItems.answer: Use ImageCompare to inspect the same region in both images. Check edges (hair, text, jewelry), skin texture, and fine patterns (fabric, foliage). If you notice halos or smudging, adjust TopazImageEnhanceV2 settings and re-run.

9bcda9e23e19.title: Image Upscale: Topaz Wonder 3.5
9bcda9e23e19.description: Upscale and enhance a single image using Topaz's Wonder 3.5 generative model, which adds fine detail, reduces noise, and sharpens text and structured graphics while offering Low, Medium, and High enhancement strengths. The workflow takes 1 input image and produces 1 enhanced output alongside a side-by-side comparison view. Ideal for restoring old or compressed photos, improving product shots and marketing visuals, and preparing low-resolution images for print or large-format display.
9bcda9e23e19.metaDescription: Compare Topaz Wonder 3.5 enhancement strengths (Low/Medium/High) in ComfyUI with side-by-side A/B to choose the best upscale for photos, text, and graphics.
9bcda9e23e19.extendedDescription:
This workflow compares the original image against a Topaz Wonder 3.5–enhanced result to help you pick the right enhancement strength for your needs. Using LoadImage to ingest your source, TopazImageEnhanceV2 applies generative upscaling with three selectable strengths—Low, Medium, and High—targeting fine detail recovery, noise reduction, and crisper text/graphics. ImageCompare then outputs a side-by-side composite so you can visually assess changes at a glance, while SaveImageAdvanced saves both the enhanced image and the comparison view.

The key trade-offs lie in how aggressively Wonder 3.5 invents or amplifies detail. Low is conservative and best when you want to preserve natural textures (e.g., skin) with minimal risk of halos. Medium balances clarity and fidelity for most photos. High is most assertive and can dramatically sharpen small text, logos, and structured graphics or rescue heavily compressed images—but it’s also where over-sharpening and hallucinated detail are most likely. By rerunning the same image with different strength settings and reviewing each A/B comparison, you can quickly converge on the best setting for your subject matter.
howToUse: Load your source image with LoadImage; confirm resolution and color look correct.
Set TopazImageEnhanceV2 Strength to Low, Medium, or High based on your goal (start with Medium for a baseline).
Run the workflow. Review the A/B output from ImageCompare to see Original vs Enhanced side-by-side.
Zoom into critical regions (skin, small text, edges, patterns). Check for artifacts: halos, plastic skin, ringing, or oversmoothing.
Repeat the run with another Strength setting (e.g., Low, then High). Compare the saved A/B composites to decide which setting best fits your image.
Use SaveImageAdvanced to keep distinct filenames or subfolders per strength so results don’t overwrite, then export the chosen enhanced image.
suggestedUseCases: Restoring old or compressed family photos while preserving natural skin texture.
Sharpening product shots for e‑commerce listings and hero banners.
Improving legibility in screenshots, UI mockups, and documents with small text or vector graphics.
Preparing low-resolution assets for print or large-format displays.
Enhancing social media thumbnails where fine detail and crisp text boost click-through.

faqItems.question: What’s the practical difference between Low, Medium, and High strength?
faqItems.answer: Low is conservative—minimal risk of halos and detail hallucination; ideal for portraits and lightly compressed photos. Medium balances clarity and fidelity, suitable as a default for mixed content. High is aggressive—great for small text, logos, and heavily compressed images, but can introduce ringing or over-sharpened textures on some photos.

faqItems.question: How should I evaluate the A/B comparison from ImageCompare?
faqItems.answer: Inspect at 100–200% zoom. Check skin, hair, foliage, text edges, and repetitive patterns. Favor results that improve clarity without halos, zippering, waxy skin, or moiré. If artifacts appear, try a lower strength.

faqItems.question: Can the model invent details that weren’t in the original?
faqItems.answer: Yes—Wonder 3.5 is generative and may synthesize fine detail, especially at High strength. This can be desirable for rescuing low-quality sources but may reduce documentary fidelity. Choose a lower strength when accurate texture is more important than perceived sharpness.

faqItems.question: Do I need any preprocessing like denoising before enhancement?
faqItems.answer: Usually no. TopazImageEnhanceV2 already targets noise and clarity. If your source has extreme compression artifacts or heavy sensor noise, start with Low or Medium to avoid amplifying defects, and only move to High if text/graphics still need more bite.

9bd4bdaa49c0.title: Qwen3.0: Text Generation
9bd4bdaa49c0.description: Input a text prompt to generate detailed, reasoned responses using the Qwen3-4B-Thinking model.
9bd4bdaa49c0.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow for Qwen3-4B-Thinking text generation. Load the model, set decoding params, and generate detailed, reasoned responses in PreviewAny.
9bd4bdaa49c0.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns Qwen 3.0 (4B, Thinking variant) into a drop-in text generator you can run inside a node graph. It loads the Qwen3-4B-Thinking weights with CLIPLoader, feeds your prompt and decoding settings to TextGenerate, and displays the final text in PreviewAny for quick copy-out. A MarkdownNote node is included in the graph with usage tips so you can remember the key parameters at a glance.

Under the hood, TextGenerate performs standard autoregressive decoding with adjustable parameters like temperature, top_p, and max new tokens. CLIPLoader is used here to point ComfyUI at the Qwen 3.0 text encoder weights (qwen_3_4b.safetensors) stored in models/text_encoders. The result is a compact, reproducible setup for generating detailed, reasoned responses, ideal for drafting explanations, outlining ideas, and iterating on prompt engineering directly in ComfyUI. As of 2026/03, ComfyUI supports the 4B Qwen 3.0 model for this workflow.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then locate the MarkdownNote for a quick parameter overview.
Download qwen_3_4b.safetensors and place it in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders. In the CLIPLoader node, select this file so the model loads without errors.
Open the TextGenerate node and enter your prompt. Optionally add a system or style instruction at the top of the prompt to steer tone and structure.
Set decoding parameters: start with temperature 0.2–0.7, top_p around 0.9, and choose a max new tokens value large enough for your expected answer length.
Click Queue/Execute. When generation completes, the output text will appear in the PreviewAny node. Copy the result from the preview panel.
Iterate for quality: lower temperature for precision, raise it for creativity; increase max new tokens for longer answers; add explicit formatting instructions (e.g., bullets) to improve structure.
suggestedUseCases: Explain complex topics step by step for documentation, teaching notes, or internal wikis.
Draft outlines, summaries, and alternative phrasings for blog posts or reports.
Brainstorm solution approaches or pros/cons lists for product or engineering decisions.
Generate code comments, function docstrings, or high-level design descriptions.
Create structured responses (bullets, headings, or JSON-like output) for downstream tooling.

faqItems.question: Where do I put the Qwen 3.0 model file and how do I load it?
faqItems.answer: Place qwen_3_4b.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders, then select it in the CLIPLoader node. The TextGenerate node will use the loaded model handle automatically.

faqItems.question: How do I control response style, length, and creativity?
faqItems.answer: Use a clear instruction at the top of your prompt to set style and format. For length, increase max new tokens. For creativity vs. determinism, raise or lower temperature (and optionally adjust top_p).

faqItems.question: The output stops mid-sentence. What should I change?
faqItems.answer: Increase max new tokens so the model can finish, and make sure you are not using stop sequences that prematurely cut output. If you run low on memory, try shorter outputs and iterate.

faqItems.question: Can I run this on CPU or a smaller GPU?
faqItems.answer: Yes, but generation will be slower and you may need to reduce max new tokens. If the node exposes precision or memory-saving options, enable them. Close other GPU-heavy apps to free VRAM.

9be3d7110c75.title: SAM3 - Remove Background via Prompt
9be3d7110c75.description: Isolate any subject from an image using a text prompt — just type what you want to keep (e.g. `character`, `dog`, `car`) and the workflow cuts it out and saves it as a PNG with a transparent background.
9be3d7110c75.metaDescription: Cut out subjects from images via text prompt in ComfyUI. Use SAM3Segment to create clean PNGs with transparent backgrounds—fast, simple, and precise.
9be3d7110c75.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow isolates a subject from any image using a simple text prompt and exports a PNG with a transparent background. It links a LoadImage node to a SAM3Segment node, then into SaveImage. You type what you want to keep (for example, "character", "dog", or "red car"), and the SAM3Segment node generates a precise foreground mask and applies it as an alpha channel so everything else becomes transparent.

Technically, SAM3Segment performs prompt-aware segmentation over the input image, producing a binary mask for regions that best match the prompt. That mask is composited with the original RGB to produce an RGBA cutout. Because the node is designed to work well out of the box, most settings can remain at their defaults. The included MarkdownNote provides a quick reminder of the two essentials: connect an image and provide a clear prompt. SaveImage then writes the final cutout as a PNG, preserving transparency for downstream compositing in design, video, or web workflows.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the nodes: LoadImage → SAM3Segment → SaveImage (plus a MarkdownNote with tips).
In LoadImage, pick your source image. Use the highest-resolution version you have for cleaner edges.
Select the SAM3Segment node and enter a concise prompt describing the subject you want to keep (e.g., "dog", "blue sneaker", "sports car").
Leave other SAM3Segment settings at defaults unless you have a specific reason to change them; the node is tuned for general use.
Run the workflow. Inspect the viewer (if connected) or proceed directly to the SaveImage output to confirm the cutout.
In SaveImage, set an output folder and run. The result is a PNG with transparency where non-matching regions have been removed.
suggestedUseCases: Product shots for e-commerce: Remove backgrounds cleanly for consistent catalog images.
Character isolation for thumbnails and social banners without manual masking.
Quick compositing in design tools by exporting ready-to-place transparent PNGs.
Prepping assets for video overlays or motion graphics where alpha channels are required.

faqItems.question: What kind of prompt works best?
faqItems.answer: Use short, specific nouns with helpful attributes if needed: "red sedan", "white sneaker", "golden retriever". Avoid listing multiple different objects in one prompt—focus on the single subject you want to keep.

faqItems.question: How do I improve edge quality or fine details like hair or fur?
faqItems.answer: Start with the highest-resolution image you can and avoid heavy compression. Clear separation between subject and background also helps. If edges look soft, try a larger source image or crop the image (outside ComfyUI) to focus more on the subject before running the workflow.

faqItems.question: Can it isolate multiple instances of the same object?
faqItems.answer: It may select multiple instances if they all match the prompt, but results depend on the image. If you only want one instance, refine the prompt with distinguishing attributes (e.g., "front red car" vs. "cars") or run on a cropped version containing just the target subject.

faqItems.question: What format is the output and does it include transparency?
faqItems.answer: The SaveImage node writes a PNG with an alpha channel. The background becomes transparent wherever the prompt-based mask excludes the image.

9c0e04762e99.title: SDXL Turbo
9c0e04762e99.description: Generate images in a single step using SDXL Turbo.
9c0e04762e99.metaDescription: Generate stunning images quickly with the SDXL Turbo workflow using ComfyUI. Streamline text-to-image processes in one efficient step.
9c0e04762e99.extendedDescription:
The SDXL Turbo workflow is designed to streamline the process of generating high-quality images from text prompts using the SDXL model. This workflow is particularly efficient because it consolidates the image generation process into a single step, leveraging the power of the SDXL model and the Stability AI framework. At the core of this workflow are several key nodes, including the EmptyLatentImage, which initializes the latent space, and the CLIPTextEncode, which encodes the text prompt into a format that the model can understand.

The workflow utilizes the VAEDecode node to convert latent representations back into images, ensuring that the output is both detailed and visually appealing. The SamplerCustom and KSamplerSelect nodes are employed to fine-tune the sampling process, allowing for greater control over the image's style and composition. The SDTurboScheduler optimizes the generation process for speed without sacrificing quality. Finally, the SaveImage node ensures that the generated images are saved efficiently, while the MarkdownNote node provides documentation and context for each step, making this workflow both powerful and user-friendly.
howToUse: Load the SDXL Turbo workflow in ComfyUI.
Input your desired text prompt into the CLIPTextEncode node.
Run the workflow to initiate the image generation process.
Adjust parameters in the SamplerCustom node if needed for style refinement.
View and save your generated image using the SaveImage node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating digital art from descriptive text prompts.
Generating concept visuals for creative projects.
Rapid prototyping of visual ideas for marketing materials.
Producing unique images for social media content.
Developing educational materials with custom illustrations.

faqItems.question: What is the main advantage of using the SDXL Turbo workflow?
faqItems.answer: The primary advantage is its ability to generate high-quality images in a single step, making it both time-efficient and easy to use.

faqItems.question: Can I customize the style of the generated images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can adjust the parameters in the SamplerCustom node to refine the style and composition of the images.

faqItems.question: What types of prompts work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Descriptive prompts that clearly define the desired image elements tend to yield the best results.

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for beginners?
faqItems.answer: Absolutely. The SDXL Turbo workflow is designed to be user-friendly, with clear documentation provided by the MarkdownNote node.

9c3c4722a8e1.title: Stable Audio 3.0 Medium Base
9c3c4722a8e1.description: Input a short text description of a sound, music, or effect. The workflow expands your prompt with Qwen and generates a stereo audio clip from Stable Audio 3.
9c3c4722a8e1.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow: Expand short prompts with Qwen and generate stereo audio with Stable Audio 3. Includes MP3 export for fast music, SFX, and audio sketching.
9c3c4722a8e1.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a short text idea into finished stereo audio using Stable Audio 3.0 Medium. You type a brief concept (e.g., "warm lo‑fi hip‑hop beat" or "cinematic whoosh impact"), the prompt is expanded for clarity and detail with a Qwen 3.5 2B BF16 text encoder, and the Stable Audio 3 generation node produces a high‑quality stereo clip. The audio is then written to disk by SaveAudioMP3 for easy preview and sharing.

Under the hood, a Subgraph handles prompt expansion and routing so you only need to provide a short input. The core generation is performed by the Stable Audio 3 node (type id 8b66c757-fe2f-4184-91f3-479a19deb565), which loads weights from the Comfy‑Org/stable‑audio‑3 repository and accepts key parameters like duration and seed for control and reproducibility. A MarkdownNote in the graph provides quick in‑UI guidance. The final waveform is passed to SaveAudioMP3, which saves a stereo file to your chosen path. This setup is ideal when you want fast, consistent audio ideation without spending time crafting long prompts.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then open the graph to view the Prompt input, the Stable Audio 3 node, and the SaveAudioMP3 output.

Download the Stable Audio 3 model from Hugging Face (Comfy-Org/stable-audio-3) and place the files per the repo instructions. Download qwen3.5_2b_bf16.safetensors and put it in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders. Restart ComfyUI so the nodes can find the models.

Enter a short idea in the Prompt field (2–10 words works best). Optionally set Duration (seconds) and Seed on the Stable Audio 3 node for clip length and repeatability. Leave other defaults for a first run.
Click Queue Prompt/Run. The Subgraph expands your prompt with Qwen and feeds it to the Stable Audio 3 generation node. Wait for the audio to render.
In the SaveAudioMP3 node, set the output path (and bitrate if available), then run or re‑run to save the MP3. Check the console or node preview for the saved file location.
Iterate: change the seed for variations, adjust duration to fit your use, or simplify the prompt if results feel too busy (the Qwen expansion will still enrich short inputs).
suggestedUseCases: Rapid music sketching for genre, vibe, and instrumentation exploration.
Sound effects prototyping for games, film, and motion graphics (whooshes, hits, risers, textures).
Short branding audio: intros, tags, stingers, and underscore beds.
Ambient backgrounds for prototypes, trailers, or UX sound design.
Idea generation when writer’s block hits—seed multiple variations quickly.

faqItems.question: Do I need the internet once models are installed?
faqItems.answer: No. After downloading the Stable Audio 3 weights and the Qwen 3.5 text encoder locally, the workflow runs fully offline.

faqItems.question: How can I get consistent results or re‑create a clip later?
faqItems.answer: Set a fixed Seed and Duration on the Stable Audio 3 node. Keeping the same prompt, seed, and settings will reproduce the same output.

faqItems.question: What kind of prompts work best?
faqItems.answer: Keep it short and focused. Include genre or sound type, key instruments or source, mood/energy, and any timing cues (e.g., "dark synth drone with evolving texture"). The Subgraph uses Qwen to expand the idea into detailed guidance for the model.

faqItems.question: What hardware do I need?
faqItems.answer: A GPU is strongly recommended for reasonable generation times. CPU-only runs may be possible but are typically very slow. VRAM needs depend on clip length and settings.

9cab2e75bc44.title: Image Edit
9cab2e75bc44.description: Start with an image and an empty prompt, then describe the edit you want. Nano Banana 2 generates a modified image while preserving subject consistency and high visual fidelity.
9cab2e75bc44.metaDescription: Prompt-based image editing in ComfyUI with Nano Banana 2. Load an image, describe the change, and export a high-fidelity, subject-consistent result.
9cab2e75bc44.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow performs prompt-only image editing: you load a source image, leave the base prompt empty, and type a plain-language instruction describing the change you want. The core edit is handled by the Nano Banana 2 model, accessed via an API connection (listed under Models: Google, Nano Banana 2). Because the edit is conditioned on your input image, the workflow is designed to preserve subject identity and composition while applying targeted changes.

Under the hood, LoadImage brings your reference image into the graph. A MarkdownNote in the canvas reminds you to “Describe your edit” so you focus only on what should change, not on re-describing the subject. The custom API edit node (UUID: 4d2ab4f5-8f54-4b5b-a4e2-49b35a60ad9d) submits the image and your instruction to Nano Banana 2, then returns a modified image. SaveImage writes the result to your output folder. This setup excels at quick, high-fidelity tweaks—color swaps, background changes, light retouching, or adding small details—without manual masking or rebuilding the scene.

For best results, write concise, directive prompts that target specific attributes (for example, “change the jacket to red,” “replace the background with a modern office,” or “remove the power lines”). Avoid restating who/what is in the image—the model already sees it—so it can focus on making only the requested change. If you want multiple adjustments, iterate in small steps and re-run to refine.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI. Read the MarkdownNote to confirm you’ll only describe the edit (keep the base prompt otherwise empty).
In the LoadImage node, select the photo you want to modify.
Open the edit/API node (UUID 4d2ab4f5-8f54-4b5b-a4e2-49b35a60ad9d) and type a clear instruction describing only the change you want (e.g., “replace the background with a sunset beach”).
Click Run. The node will send your image and instruction to the Nano Banana 2 model via the API and return an edited image.
Preview the result, then use SaveImage to write the output to your chosen folder.
If needed, refine the instruction (short, specific changes) and Run again. For multiple changes, iterate in small steps.
suggestedUseCases: Product photography variants: swap colors, update textures, or place items on new backgrounds while keeping the product identical.
Portrait and fashion tweaks: adjust clothing color, add simple accessories, or refine backgrounds without losing the subject’s identity.
Content cleanup: remove small distractions (wires, logos, blemishes) and perform light scene corrections.
Branding updates: add or replace simple branded elements in existing visuals while preserving layout and lighting.
Real estate or interior previews: change wall colors or decor elements to explore design alternatives quickly.

faqItems.question: Do I need to provide a mask or select regions manually?
faqItems.answer: No. This workflow is prompt-only. The edit node conditions on your input image and applies the change you describe. For highly precise, localized edits, you can combine this with a separate masking workflow, but it isn’t required here.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the subject consistent?
faqItems.answer: Keep your instruction short and targeted. Avoid re-describing the subject (who/what/where); only state the change (e.g., “make the car blue,” “replace the background with a studio gray”). Making one change at a time and iterating helps preserve identity.

faqItems.question: What image sizes work best?
faqItems.answer: Use a reasonably high-quality input. The workflow passes the image to the API as-is; the exact output size may depend on the model endpoint. If you encounter slowdowns or memory limits, try a smaller input and upscale later if needed.

faqItems.question: Can I chain multiple edits?
faqItems.answer: Yes. You can run another pass with a new instruction on either the original image or the edited result. For complex transformations, break them into smaller, sequential steps to maintain fidelity.

9cc2917611e9.title: Flux.1 Schnell Full: Text to Image
9cc2917611e9.description: Generate images quickly with Flux.1 Schnell full version. Uses Apache2.0 license, requires only 4 steps to generate images while maintaining good image quality.
9cc2917611e9.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Ultra-fast 4-step text-to-image with Flux.1 Schnell. Load models, set size, prompt, sample, and save—quality results with minimal steps.
9cc2917611e9.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow generates images from text using Flux.1 Schnell (full) with a minimal, fast sampling setup. It combines DualCLIPLoader to load both CLIP-L and T5XXL text encoders, CLIPTextEncodeFlux to turn your prompts into Flux-ready conditioning, and UNETLoader to load the flux1-schnell.safetensors diffusion model. EmptySD3LatentImage defines the latent canvas size and batch, KSampler performs denoising in as few as four steps, and VAELoader + VAEDecode reconstruct the final image for SaveImage to write to disk. A ConditioningZeroOut node provides an unconditional branch for classifier-free guidance when you’re not using a negative prompt. MarkdownNote nodes in the canvas clarify what to do at each stage.

Technically, the workflow follows a standard latent diffusion path adapted for Flux/SD3-style latents: initialize an EmptySD3LatentImage, encode text with CLIPTextEncodeFlux, run the UNet through KSampler with a low step-count tuned for the Schnell variant, then decode with the selected VAE. The “Step 1 - Load Models Here” group centralizes model selection: flux1-schnell in UNETLoader, CLIP-L + T5XXL in DualCLIPLoader, and a compatible VAE in VAELoader. “Step 2 - Image Size” sets your width/height and batch, and “Step 3 - Prompt” handles positive/negative prompts. The result is a fast, 4-step text-to-image pipeline that balances speed and quality under the permissive Apache-2.0 license for the Flux.1 Schnell weights.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. Locate the grouped sections: Step 1 - Load Models Here, Step 2 - Image Size, Step 3 - Prompt.

Step 1 - Load Models Here: In UNETLoader, select flux1-schnell.safetensors (place it in ComfyUI/models/unet). In DualCLIPLoader, select CLIP-L and T5XXL encoders (e.g., clip_l.safetensors and t5xxl_fp16.safetensors, commonly stored in models/clip). In VAELoader, choose a compatible VAE file (placed in models/vae).
Step 2 - Image Size: Open EmptySD3LatentImage and set width, height, and batch size. Start with a square frame (e.g., 1024 × 1024) and batch size 1 for lower VRAM use.

Step 3 - Prompt: Enter your positive prompt in CLIPTextEncodeFlux. If you want a negative prompt, enter it there as well; otherwise, leave negative empty and let ConditioningZeroOut provide the unconditional branch.

Sampling: In KSampler, keep steps at 4 for maximum speed. Adjust guidance (CFG) moderately if needed and use the default sampler/scheduler provided by the workflow. If you need more fidelity, try 6–8 steps.

Run and save: Execute the workflow. VAEDecode reconstructs the image, and SaveImage writes it to disk (configure filename prefix/subfolder in SaveImage). Inspect results, refine your prompt or size, and rerun.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept art and mood boards where speed matters more than ultra-fine detail.
Thumbnail and social media asset ideation with quick prompt iterations.
Storyboarding and previsualization for scenes, products, or UI layouts.
Creative writing prompts to visualize characters, settings, or props.
Design exploration: testing styles, color palettes, and compositions fast.

faqItems.question: Which model files do I need and where do they go?
faqItems.answer: You need flux1-schnell.safetensors for the UNet (place in models/unet), CLIP-L and T5XXL encoders for text (e.g., clip_l.safetensors and t5xxl_fp16.safetensors in models/clip), and a compatible VAE (models/vae). Select each in UNETLoader, DualCLIPLoader, and VAELoader respectively.

faqItems.question: Why only 4 steps, and can I increase them?
faqItems.answer: Flux.1 Schnell is tuned for very low step counts, making 4 steps a great speed/quality trade-off. For extra detail or difficult prompts, try 6–8 steps; expect longer render times.

faqItems.question: Do I need a negative prompt?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow includes ConditioningZeroOut to provide an unconditional branch for classifier-free guidance if you leave the negative prompt empty. Use a negative prompt only if you need to steer away from specific artifacts or styles.

faqItems.question: What image sizes work best?
faqItems.answer: Start around 1024 × 1024 or similar pixel counts. Larger resolutions increase VRAM and time. Keep batch size at 1 on lower-memory GPUs and scale up cautiously.

9cca5e2b3dde.title: Video to Normal Map
9cca5e2b3dde.description: Convert a Video to a temporally stable Normal Map
9cca5e2b3dde.metaDescription: Convert video to a stable normal map using ComfyUI for enhanced 3D modeling and animation. Achieve seamless transitions with this workflow.
9cca5e2b3dde.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow is designed to convert video footage into a temporally stable normal map, which is particularly useful for enhancing 3D modeling and animation projects. By leveraging nodes such as the NormalCrafterNode and VHS_LoadVideo, the workflow processes each frame of the video to extract and generate a normal map that maintains consistency across frames. This temporal stability is crucial for applications where seamless transitions between frames are necessary, such as in video games or cinematic visual effects.

The workflow begins by loading the video using the VHS_LoadVideo node, which extracts individual frames and prepares them for processing. The NormalCrafterNode then takes these frames and computes the normal maps, ensuring that the lighting and shading information is accurately represented. The VHS_VideoCombine node is used to reassemble the processed frames back into a video format, while the VHS_VideoInfo node provides metadata about the video, such as frame rate and resolution. This combination of nodes makes the workflow highly effective for creating high-quality normal maps from video content, which can be used to add depth and realism to 3D environments.
howToUse: Load the workflow into ComfyUI and ensure all necessary custom nodes are installed.
Use the VHS_LoadVideo node to import your video file into the workflow.
Configure the NormalCrafterNode to process each video frame and generate normal maps.
Utilize the VHS_VideoCombine node to compile the processed frames back into a video format.
Check the output using the VHS_VideoInfo node to verify frame rate and resolution consistency.
Export the final video with the newly created normal maps for use in your projects.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing realism in video game environments by applying normal maps to textures.
Creating detailed visual effects for films and animations.
Developing training datasets for machine learning models focused on 3D object recognition.
Improving the visual quality of virtual reality experiences.
Augmenting architectural visualization projects with realistic lighting effects.

faqItems.question: What is a normal map and why is it important?
faqItems.answer: A normal map is a texture that stores information about the surface normals of a 3D object. It is used to simulate lighting and shading effects, adding depth and detail without increasing polygon count.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow ensure temporal stability across frames?
faqItems.answer: The workflow processes each frame individually but maintains consistent lighting and shading parameters, ensuring that the normal maps align seamlessly across frames.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow with any video format?
faqItems.answer: The VHS_LoadVideo node supports various common video formats, but it's recommended to use standard formats like MP4 or AVI for best compatibility.

faqItems.question: Do I need any special hardware to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: While no special hardware is required, having a GPU can significantly speed up the processing time, especially for high-resolution videos.

9d588c37e728.title: Dynamic Motion Design
9d588c37e728.description: Create polished motion design videos with Seedance-ready prompts.
9d588c37e728.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Turn UI screenshots into motion design videos using Gemini for Seedance prompts and ByteDance2ReferenceNode for image-to-video animation.
9d588c37e728.extendedDescription: Dynamic Motion Design is an image-to-video ComfyUI workflow that turns static UI screenshots and brand assets into polished motion design clips. It uses GeminiNode or GeminiNanoBanana2 to convert your brief and references into a single Seedance-ready motion prompt, then feeds that prompt—along with your uploaded images—into ByteDance2ReferenceNode to generate the actual animation. You can monitor progress with PreviewImage and PreviewAny, and export the result with SaveVideo. The workflow is organized into three groups for clarity: Generate Seedance Motion Designer Prompt (LLM-driven prompt crafting), Generate UI Frames (quick previews and frame checks), and Generate Video (final render and export).
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and review the MarkdownNote for any in-graph tips.

In the Generate UI Frames section, use LoadImage to import your base image (e.g., a landing page or app screen). Optional: Load additional brand/style references and connect them to ByteDance2ReferenceNode as visual guidance.

In the Generate Seedance Motion Designer Prompt section, write a short creative brief (motion goals, tone, brand cues). Choose GeminiNode (cloud) or GeminiNanoBanana2 (local) to synthesize a concise Seedance-ready prompt. Preview and copy the generated prompt from PreviewAny or MarkdownNote if needed.

Adjust prompt details for motion design specifics: camera moves (pan, zoom, parallax), element emphasis (CTA, logo), pacing, transitions, and timing. Keep it concise and declarative—Seedance prompts work best when unambiguous.

Switch to the Generate Video section. Ensure ByteDance2ReferenceNode receives the Seedance prompt and your image/reference inputs. Set key parameters (resolution, motion strength, duration/frame count, seed) as available on the node. Use PreviewImage/PreviewAny to spot-check initial frames.
When satisfied, render the full sequence and export with SaveVideo. You can also reuse the same Seedance prompt in the external Seedance Motion Designer if you want to iterate outside ComfyUI.
suggestedUseCases: Animating product landing pages for pitch decks or portfolio reels (subtle pans, CTA emphasis, logo animations).
Brand reveal stingers using product shots and style boards as references.
Mobile app UI micro-animation prototypes to showcase flows and transitions.
Social-ready motion snippets that highlight key features or promotions.
Design explorations to establish motion language and pacing for a new brand.

faqItems.question: What is a Seedance-ready prompt, and why use GeminiNode here?
faqItems.answer: A Seedance-ready prompt is a concise, structured text description tailored for the Seedance Motion Designer. The workflow uses GeminiNode or GeminiNanoBanana2 to turn your brief and visual references into a clear, unambiguous prompt that emphasizes motion intent (camera moves, pacing, focal elements). This improves consistency and reduces trial-and-error when driving ByteDance2ReferenceNode or exporting the prompt for Seedance.

faqItems.question: What does ByteDance2ReferenceNode do in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: ByteDance2ReferenceNode is the image-to-video engine that interprets your Seedance prompt alongside the uploaded base image and any style/brand references. It generates the animated sequence based on those inputs and its parameters (e.g., resolution, motion strength, duration/frame count, and seed).

faqItems.question: When should I use GeminiNode vs. GeminiNanoBanana2?
faqItems.answer: Use GeminiNode if you have network access and want the full cloud LLM for richer prompt synthesis. Use GeminiNanoBanana2 if you prefer a local, lightweight option or need to work offline. Both produce Seedance-ready prompts; choose based on connectivity and resource constraints.

faqItems.question: How can I improve results and control the motion?
faqItems.answer: Start with a clean, high-resolution base image. Add clear brand/style references that match your desired look. Keep the Seedance prompt brief and directive—specify camera moves, focal elements, pacing, and transitions. In ByteDance2ReferenceNode, iterate on motion strength, duration/frame count, and seed. Use the Generate UI Frames previews to validate composition before rendering the final video.

9dac2dae8bfc.title: Wan 2.2 14B Fun Camera Control
9dac2dae8bfc.description: Generate videos with camera motion controls including pan, zoom, and rotation using Wan 2.2 Fun Camera Control.
9dac2dae8bfc.metaDescription: Image-to-video with precise pan, zoom, and rotation using Wan 2.2 in ComfyUI. Two-pass denoise for stable, cinematic motion. Optional fast LoRA mode.
9dac2dae8bfc.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single still image into a smooth, camera-driven video using Wan 2.2 14B Fun Camera Control. It loads the Wan 2.2 model with UNETLoader and ModelSamplingSD3, encodes your text prompt with CLIPLoader + CLIPTextEncode, and builds a camera path with WanCameraEmbedding. The WanCameraImageToVideo node fuses your prompt, start image, and camera embeddings to generate temporally consistent frames that follow pan, zoom, and rotation cues. Frames are decoded with VAELoader + VAEDecode, assembled with CreateVideo, and written out via SaveVideo.

Under the hood, the workflow runs a two-pass denoise with KSamplerAdvanced: a High noise phase to establish motion, structure, and parallax, followed by a Low noise phase to refine details and reduce flicker. This separation helps keep subjects stable while letting the virtual camera move dynamically. The template includes an optional LightX2V 4 Steps LoRA (via LoraLoaderModelOnly) to accelerate generation at the cost of motion richness and fine detail; use the Default (Without Lightning LoRA) path for the best dynamics. The provided fp8_scaled Wan 2.2 checkpoint is optimized for 640×640 and, on an RTX 4090D 24GB, typically uses ~84% VRAM and takes about 536s for the first run and ~513s for subsequent runs at that resolution.
howToUse: Step 1 – Load models: Open the workflow and, in the Step 1 - Load models group, set UNETLoader to the Wan2.2 fun camera 14B fp8_scaled model, load the matching VAE in VAELoader, and load CLIP in CLIPLoader. Leave ModelSamplingSD3 as provided.

Step 2 – Provide a start image: In Step 2 - Upload start_image, use LoadImage to select a clean, well-lit source image at or near 640×640. Center your subject and avoid heavy compression artifacts for best stability.

Step 3 – Write your prompt: In Step 3 - Prompt, enter your descriptive prompt in CLIPTextEncode (and adjust any negative text field if present). Keep prompts concise and consistent with the content of the start image.

Step 4 – Define camera motion: In Step 4 - Camera Conditions, set WanCameraEmbedding parameters for pan, zoom, and rotation across the timeline. Use modest ranges (e.g., gentle pans and 5–15% zoom) for stable parallax. These embeddings feed WanCameraImageToVideo to drive motion.

Step 5 – Choose quality vs. speed: Use the Default (Without Lightning LoRA) path for maximum motion fidelity, or enable the LightX2V 4 Steps LoRA via LoraLoaderModelOnly to reduce steps and render time (expect some loss of dynamics/detail).

Step 6 – Generate and export: Run the graph. The High noise pass establishes motion; the Low noise pass refines details. In CreateVideo and SaveVideo, set FPS and output quality, then save your final video.
suggestedUseCases: Product hero shots from a still: slow dolly-in with a subtle orbit to add depth and polish.
Character portraits: gentle arc or roll around a face while preserving identity and texture.
Environment concept art: slow pan-and-zoom to reveal scenery with light parallax.
UI/mockup reels: controlled zooms and pans to highlight interface sections without reanimating in a DCC.
Social posts and teaser loops: quick motion from static key art to increase engagement.

faqItems.question: Do I need a start image, or can this start from noise?
faqItems.answer: This template is designed for image-to-video. Load a start image with LoadImage to anchor content and identity, then use WanCameraEmbedding to add motion.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the subject stable while the camera moves?
faqItems.answer: Use moderate camera ranges (small pans/zooms/rotations), keep the subject centered in the start image, and favor the Default (Without Lightning LoRA) path. If you see drift, reduce the High noise sampler strength/steps slightly and lock the seed.

faqItems.question: How can I speed up generation?
faqItems.answer: Enable the LightX2V 4 Steps LoRA (via LoraLoaderModelOnly), lower the resolution (e.g., stay at 640×640), reduce KSamplerAdvanced steps, and shorten duration/FPS. Note the Lightning/LightX2V path trades speed for motion richness and detail.

faqItems.question: What resolution and VRAM should I expect?
faqItems.answer: The fp8_scaled Wan 2.2 model is set up for 640×640. On an RTX 4090D 24GB, VRAM usage is ~84% with first-run times around 536s and subsequent runs ~513s. Higher resolutions require more VRAM and may reduce stability.

9ded34af89b5.title: Grok Imagine Video 1.5 Lite: Image to Video
9ded34af89b5.description: Generate short videos from a single still image using Grok Imagine Video 1.5 Lite, a faster, lower-cost model that turns one image into a video clip up to 15 seconds at resolutions up to 1080p. Ideal for rapid social content, storyboard previews, and high-volume creative iteration where speed and cost matter more than maximum fidelity.
9ded34af89b5.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow: turn one image into a 5–15s video (up to 1080p) using Grok Imagine Video 1.5 Lite. Fast, low-cost image-to-video for social and previews.
9ded34af89b5.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a single still image into a short video using Grok Imagine Video 1.5 Lite via API. It’s built around four nodes: LoadImage brings your source image into the graph, GrokVideoNode sends that image to the Grok Imagine Video 1.5 Lite model to synthesize motion and camera movement, and SaveVideo writes the returned clip to disk. A MarkdownNote in the canvas provides quick, in-place tips. The Lite model prioritizes speed and cost, making it ideal for rapid iteration, social posts, and storyboard previews.

Technically, the image tensor from LoadImage flows directly into GrokVideoNode, where you set duration (up to 15 seconds), target resolution (up to 1080p), and other generation controls such as FPS and motion strength. The node calls the Grok API, waits for generation to complete, and returns the resulting video to the graph. SaveVideo handles final encoding and file output. Because most of the heavy lifting runs on Grok’s servers, your local machine only needs to orchestrate the request and save the result, enabling fast turnaround even on modest hardware.
howToUse: Open ComfyUI (updated to the latest version) and load the "Grok Imagine Video 1.5 Lite: Image to Video" workflow. Ensure the GrokVideoNode is available and that your Grok API key is configured in the node or your environment.

Load your source image with the LoadImage node. You can start with the provided sample (fur_hat_blue_sunglasses_pink_bg.png) or drag in your own. For best results, match your image’s aspect ratio to your intended output (e.g., 16:9 for landscape, 9:16 for vertical).

Select the GrokVideoNode and set key parameters: duration (up to 15s), resolution (720p for drafts, 1080p for final), and FPS (commonly 24–30). Adjust motion strength or camera movement controls to taste. If a seed or randomness option is present, fix it for repeatable results or randomize for variation.
Optionally add brief notes or reminders in the MarkdownNote to track settings across iterations (e.g., aspect ratio, duration, intended platform).
Run the workflow. The GrokVideoNode will upload your image to the Grok API, generate the clip, and return it to the graph. Monitor the node’s status until it completes.

In SaveVideo, set the output filename and directory, confirm FPS matches your chosen setting, and execute to write the final video file. Preview the result and iterate: tweak duration, resolution, or motion controls and re-run for new variations.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid social media loops and reels where speed and volume matter more than maximum fidelity.
Storyboard and animatic previews to quickly test camera motion and pacing from static frames.
Product teaser spins or subtle parallax motion from a single product shot.
Music cover or podcast episode art animated into short motion loops.
Background motion plates for editing timelines, title cards, or UI mockups.

faqItems.question: What are the clip length and resolution limits?
faqItems.answer: Grok Imagine Video 1.5 Lite in this workflow supports videos up to 15 seconds and up to 1080p resolution. For fast drafts, try 720p; export 1080p for final delivery.

faqItems.question: Do I need a Grok API key and will I be billed?
faqItems.answer: Yes. GrokVideoNode uses the Grok API and requires a valid API key. Usage is billed by Grok according to their pricing and any applicable rate limits. Check your Grok account for details.

faqItems.question: How can I get smoother or more controlled motion?
faqItems.answer: Use clean, well-lit images with a clear subject and background separation. In GrokVideoNode, lower motion strength for subtle parallax, increase it for dynamic movement, and pick an FPS (e.g., 24–30) that fits your delivery. If available, fix the seed for repeatability.

faqItems.question: What does SaveVideo do and which format will I get?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo takes the generated clip from GrokVideoNode and writes it to disk using your chosen filename and FPS. The default output is a standard, shareable video file suitable for most editors and platforms.

9e033fb4e06a.title: Portrait Relight
9e033fb4e06a.description: Upload your target image and a reference lighting image. Relights your target image.
9e033fb4e06a.metaDescription: Transform your images with the Portrait Relight workflow, using reference lighting to enhance and unify your visuals.
9e033fb4e06a.extendedDescription: The 'Portrait Relight' workflow in ComfyUI is designed to enhance your images by altering their lighting based on a reference image. The process involves several key nodes, including the LoadImage node for importing images, and the SaveImage node for exporting the final result. The workflow is particularly useful for photographers and digital artists looking to achieve consistent lighting across different images or to experiment with creative lighting effects without the need for physical lighting equipment.
howToUse: Start by loading your target image using the LoadImage node in ComfyUI.
Upload a reference image with the desired lighting using the same LoadImage node.
Ensure the Qwen-Image-Edit model is selected to process the images for relighting.
Adjust any additional settings or prompts as needed, such as maintaining canny edge details.
Run the workflow to generate the relighted image.
Save the output using the SaveImage node to store your newly relighted portrait.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing portrait photography by applying studio-like lighting effects.
Creating a unified lighting style across a series of images for a cohesive photo album.
Experimenting with different lighting scenarios for digital art projects.
Improving the visual appeal of product photos by adjusting lighting to highlight features.
Testing lighting effects for film or animation pre-production.

faqItems.question: What type of images work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Portrait images with clear lighting and shadow details tend to work best, as the model can effectively adjust these elements to match the reference lighting.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for non-portrait images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, while optimized for portraits, the workflow can be applied to any image where lighting adjustments are desired.

faqItems.question: Do I need any special hardware to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No special hardware is required, but a GPU will significantly speed up the processing time, especially for high-resolution images.

faqItems.question: How do I maintain specific details in the image?
faqItems.answer: You can append additional image edit prompt instructions in the workflow to maintain specific details, such as edges, during the relighting process.

9e910f3b95c2.title: Kling 3.0: Video Generation

9e910f3b95c2.metaDescription: Generate 15-second videos from text or image prompts using Kling 3.0 with multi-shot compositions and complex camera movements.

Use the LoadImage node to input your initial text or image prompt.
Configure the KlingVideoNode to set parameters for video length, camera movement, and subject consistency.
Run the workflow to process the input through the Kling 3.0 model, generating the video sequence.

Developing creative video art projects with complex camera movements.

faqItems.question: What types of prompts can I use with this workflow?

faqItems.question: How long are the videos generated by this workflow?

faqItems.question: Can I customize the camera movements in the generated video?

faqItems.question: Is there a way to ensure subject consistency throughout the video?
