Technically, this workflow excels due to the integration of the Wan2.6 model, which is specifically tuned for video generation from images. It uses advanced interpolation techniques to create fluid motion between frames, ensuring that the resulting video is not only high in quality but also visually coherent. The workflow is particularly useful for content creators and professionals who need to convert images into engaging video content quickly and efficiently, without compromising on quality.
howToUse: Load your image into the workflow using the 'LoadImage' node.
Configure the 'WanImageToVideoApi' node with your desired settings for motion and resolution.
Run the workflow to process the image and generate the video.
Use the 'SaveVideo' node to save the output video to your desired location.
Review the video for quality and make any necessary adjustments by reconfiguring the nodes.
suggestedUseCases: Creating promotional videos from static product images.
Generating dynamic video content for social media from still photographs.
Developing educational content that requires visual transformation from images to videos.
Producing artistic video projects that start from photographic sources.
Enhancing presentations with video content derived from images.

faqItems.question: What types of images work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: High-resolution images with clear details work best, as they provide more data for the Wan2.6 model to generate smooth and high-quality videos.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the motion smoothness in the video?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the 'WanImageToVideoApi' node allows you to configure settings related to motion smoothness and other video characteristics.

faqItems.question: What is the maximum resolution supported by this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports video outputs up to 1080P resolution, ensuring high-quality results suitable for professional use.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to batch process multiple images into videos?
faqItems.answer: Currently, the workflow is designed for single image processing. For batch processing, you would need to run the workflow separately for each image.

a088cfc66619.title: GPT Image 2.5 Flare: Text to Image
a088cfc66619.description: GPT Image 2.5 Flare is a fast image generation and editing template optimized for rapid prototyping and creative iteration. It delivers quick previews for concept exploration, mood boards, poster drafts, character sketches and scene mockups. Balances solid visual quality with low latency, ideal for high-volume trial-and-error creative workflows.
a088cfc66619.metaDescription: ComfyUI template for fast text-to-image and quick edits using OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2, optimized for rapid prototyping and saving outputs via SaveImage.
a088cfc66619.extendedDescription:
GPT Image 2.5 Flare: Text to Image is a lean ComfyUI template for rapid ideation and fast visual drafts. It centers on OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 for generation and optional editing, then hands results to SaveImage for clean, consistent exports. With only two nodes to manage, you can move quickly from prompt to preview, making it ideal for mood boards, poster comps, character studies, and quick scene mockups.

Technically, OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 sends your prompt (and, if provided, a source image and mask) to an OpenAI image model you select in the node’s model field (for example, gpt-image-1). The node returns generated images directly into ComfyUI for preview, and SaveImage writes them to disk with your chosen filename prefix and subfolder. The “Flare” preset emphasizes low latency: keep sizes modest, use standard quality, and generate a small batch to iterate quickly, then scale up resolution or quality once the concept is locked.
howToUse: Load the workflow: Open ComfyUI and load the “GPT Image 2.5 Flare: Text to Image” workflow. Ensure the OpenAI integration/extension that provides OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 is installed and your OpenAI API key is configured.

Configure the generator: Open the OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 node. Select an OpenAI image model (e.g., gpt-image-1), enter a clear prompt, and set size and image count. For fastest previews, use standard quality and moderate resolutions (e.g., 768–1024 on the long side).

Optional image editing: If editing, provide a source image and a mask to indicate edit regions (refer to the node’s tooltip/docs for the expected mask format). Write a prompt that clearly describes the intended change (e.g., “replace the sky with a dramatic sunset”).

Set output naming: In the SaveImage node, set a filename_prefix (e.g., flare_draft) and an optional subfolder to keep iterations organized. This node will save images to your ComfyUI output directory.
Generate: Click Queue Prompt. Review the preview images in ComfyUI. If needed, refine the prompt, adjust size or count, and re-queue to iterate quickly.
Upscale or finalize: Once the concept is right, you can increase resolution or quality in OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 for a cleaner output, then re-run and save with SaveImage.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept thumbnails and mood boards for visual direction alignment
Poster and cover exploration with quick variations on layout and style
Character and prop studies to establish silhouette and vibe before detailing
Scene mockups and set dressing to evaluate composition and color palettes
Targeted image edits (object replacement, background changes) for fast revisions

faqItems.question: Which model does this workflow use?
faqItems.answer: OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 lets you choose the model in its settings (e.g., gpt-image-1). The “Flare” template is tuned for speed: start with standard quality and moderate resolutions for quick feedback.

faqItems.question: Can it edit existing images?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Supply a source image and a mask to specify where changes should occur, then describe the edit in the prompt. Check the node’s documentation for the required mask format and channel (transparent vs. grayscale) to ensure accurate edits.

faqItems.question: Does this run on my GPU or the cloud?
faqItems.answer: Image generation happens through the OpenAI API (cloud). ComfyUI handles the workflow and saving locally. You’ll need an internet connection and an active API key; usage may incur API costs and be subject to rate limits.

faqItems.question: How do I get faster results or better quality?
faqItems.answer: For speed, use standard quality, smaller sizes, and fewer images per batch. For quality, increase resolution and/or quality after you’ve validated the concept. Iterating in small, fast steps is the core idea of this template.

a09d65985659.title: Image Enhancer
a09d65985659.description: Upload your image and add some subtle details and sharpness.
a09d65985659.metaDescription: ComfyUI Image Enhancer: sharpen subtle details and optionally upscale images. Load, compare before/after, and save clean, crisp results in minutes.
a09d65985659.extendedDescription: Image Enhancer is a lightweight ComfyUI workflow that sharpens fine details and optionally upscales your images with minimal fuss. It starts with LoadImage to bring your source image into the graph, then passes it through a single enhancement/upscale node (ID: 33e8ca06-a6ea-4ed7-967d-e8f18733f2ba). That node applies subtle edge-aware sharpening and detail boosting, and—if enabled—scales the image to a higher resolution. Because it’s model-agnostic, the exact method depends on what the node exposes on your setup (for example, a built-in sharpen filter or a third‑party upscaler model).
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI, then click the LoadImage node and select the image you want to enhance.

Select the enhancement node (33e8ca06-a6ea-4ed7-967d-e8f18733f2ba). Set its enhancement strength and, if available, choose an upscale factor or model. Start conservatively (e.g., low/medium strength).
Make sure the original image (from LoadImage) and the enhanced output (from the 33e8… node) are both connected to ImageCompare so you can preview before/after.
Click Queue/Execute. Inspect the result in ImageCompare and watch for halos or over-sharpening. If needed, lower strength or scale and re-run.
When satisfied, open the SaveImage node, set your output folder and filename prefix, ensure it’s wired to the enhanced output, and run the node to export.
Repeat with additional images by changing the file in LoadImage and reusing the same settings, or fine-tune per image for best quality.
suggestedUseCases: Product shots: add clarity to textures, logos, and stitching while keeping a natural look.
Portraits: gently refine hair and eye details without introducing harsh artifacts.
Social media and web images: make compressed images crisper before reposting.
Texture sources for 3D or game assets: upscale and sharpen diffuse maps or scanned materials.
Archival scans: subtly enhance old photos while preserving their original character.

faqItems.question: What model or algorithm does the enhancement node use?
faqItems.answer: The enhancement/upscale behavior comes from the custom node (ID: 33e8ca06-a6ea-4ed7-967d-e8f18733f2ba). Its exact model or method depends on your installation. Check the node’s parameters—some builds expose a selectable upscaler (e.g., ESRGAN/Real-ESRGAN or similar) and a sharpening/detail slider.

faqItems.question: How do I avoid halos or over-sharpened edges?
faqItems.answer: Lower the enhancement strength and avoid very high upscale factors in a single pass. Use ImageCompare to inspect edges at 100% zoom. If the node provides separate ‘sharpen’ and ‘detail’ controls, reduce sharpen first. You can also try a two-pass approach: modest enhancement at native size, then a gentle upscale.

faqItems.question: Will this fix very low-resolution or heavily compressed images?
faqItems.answer: It can improve perceived sharpness, but there are limits. For tiny or blocky sources, use a modest upscale (e.g., 1.5–2× if available) and conservative sharpening. Overshooting scale or strength often amplifies compression artifacts.

faqItems.question: Why do colors or contrast look slightly different after enhancement?
faqItems.answer: Some enhancement pipelines alter micro-contrast. Compare in ImageCompare and adjust the node’s strength or any tone-related settings if available. Also ensure your input is standard sRGB and avoid re-saving as low‑quality JPEG, which can shift tones.

a0ac9fb2f34f.title: HY Image 3.5 Preview: Tex t Image
a0ac9fb2f34f.description: Tencent Hunyuan's preview image model, strengthening three areas over previous versions: multilingual text rendering and typesetting for advertising, infographics and UI design; photorealism and stylistic range covering cinematic, comic, commercial photography and illustration; and editing consistency that preserves key traits of people and products across background, outfit and style changes. Outputs up to 4K resolution.

a0d7f0c8aa8c.title: SDPose: Image Multi-Person Detection
a0d7f0c8aa8c.description: Upload an image to detect human poses. Supports detection for both single individuals and multiple people within the same scene.
a0d7f0c8aa8c.metaDescription: Detect and preview multi-person human poses from any image using SDPose-OOD in ComfyUI. Adjustable max detections, clean overlays, and easy export.
a0d7f0c8aa8c.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow runs SDPose-OOD to detect people and their whole‑body pose in a still image, with built‑in support for multi‑person scenes. The core detector is packaged inside a subgraph (node type id 01b6a731-fb78-4070-9a38-c87146da9604) so the top-level canvas stays clean while you still get fast, accurate detections. The pipeline starts with LoadImage, optionally normalizes dimensions via ResizeImageMaskNode, then forwards the image into the SDPose subgraph. Detected persons are visualized using DrawBBoxes and overlaid on the original image with ImageBlend for a readable, non-destructive preview. You can inspect results live with PreviewImage and export them using SaveImage.

What makes this preset useful is how quickly you can go from a raw photo to clear, multi-person pose detections with minimal setup. A PrimitiveInt node exposes max_detections so you can control how many people are returned—handy for crowded scenes. Under the hood, the workflow expects the sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors checkpoint (see Model Links) and can pair with the RT-DETR variant noted in the workflow for robust person localization. If you need deeper access—like raw keypoints, confidence scores, or custom thresholding—right‑click the subgraph to Unpack Subgraph and wire out the internal outputs you need.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the MarkdownNote for quick tips and model requirements.
Prepare models locally: download sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors to ComfyUI/models/checkpoints (and the RT-DETR file noted in the workflow to the folder indicated). Restart ComfyUI if newly added.
Use LoadImage to select your input image. Optionally adjust ResizeImageMaskNode if you want to standardize dimensions for speed or memory.
Set PrimitiveInt → max_detections to control how many people the SDPose subgraph should return (try values like 1, 5, or 10 for crowded images).
Run the workflow. Inspect detections with PreviewImage; DrawBBoxes and ImageBlend overlay results on the original for clarity.
If you want raw keypoints or custom thresholds, right‑click the SDPose subgraph and choose Unpack Subgraph to expose internal outputs/controls, then SaveImage to export your overlays.
suggestedUseCases: Batch auditing group photos to quickly locate and count people before further editing.
Pre-processing reference images for downstream pose-guided generation or retargeting workflows.
Sports or dance analysis where you need fast multi-person detection as a first pass.
Safety/compliance checks to verify presence of people in frames before automated publishing.
Creating datasets with person-localized overlays (bounding boxes) for manual review.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow support multiple people in one image?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Use the PrimitiveInt node to set max_detections. Increase it for crowded scenes to allow the detector to return more people.

faqItems.question: What models do I need and where do I put them?
faqItems.answer: Download sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors to ComfyUI/models/checkpoints. The workflow also references an RT‑DETR variant; follow the workflow’s Model Links and place it in the folder indicated. Restart ComfyUI after adding models.

faqItems.question: Can I export pose keypoints or just the overlay?
faqItems.answer: The preset focuses on image overlays via DrawBBoxes and ImageBlend. To export raw keypoints or scores, right‑click the SDPose subgraph, select Unpack Subgraph, expose the relevant outputs, and route them to a suitable save node.

faqItems.question: How can I improve detection quality on large or crowded images?
faqItems.answer: Try increasing max_detections, provide a higher-resolution input (use ResizeImageMaskNode thoughtfully), and ensure the correct model files are loaded. A GPU is recommended for faster, more stable results.

a0e9a3b16f63.title: Gemini Omni Flash
a0e9a3b16f63.description: Precisely edit your input video with a simple prompt.
a0e9a3b16f63.metaDescription: Prompt-based video editing with Gemini Omni Video in ComfyUI. Load a clip, add duration and aspect ratio, preview, and export clean edits fast.
a0e9a3b16f63.extendedDescription:
This workflow lets you precisely edit an input video with a single, well-structured prompt using Google’s Gemini Omni Video through the GeminiVideoOmni node. It starts by loading your source clip via LoadVideo, then routes the frames and your instructions to GeminiVideoOmni, which performs the video-to-video transformation. A small, focused subgraph called Prompt Constructor (subgraph id: 331103d2-d660-4a88-abf0-1117dc46b2df) helps you assemble a clean, model-friendly prompt that includes the two required parameters for Gemini Omni Video: duration and aspect ratio. The output can be reviewed instantly in PreviewAny and finalized with SaveVideo.

Technically, the workflow reduces ambiguity by embedding temporal (duration: e.g., 5s) and spatial (aspect ratio: e.g., 16:9) constraints directly into the prompt, which is important for stable, temporally consistent edits. The MarkdownNote node embedded in the graph provides guidance and examples so you can iterate quickly. Together, these nodes create a tight loop for prompt-driven visual effects, color/style changes, or localized alterations, without manual keyframing or complex compositing.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the graph. Locate the core nodes: LoadVideo, Prompt Constructor (subgraph id 331103d2-d660-4a88-abf0-1117dc46b2df), GeminiVideoOmni, PreviewAny, and SaveVideo.
Load your source clip with LoadVideo. Note the clip’s duration and aspect ratio (or resolution) so you can match them in the prompt to avoid cropping, letterboxing, or time mismatch.

Open the Prompt Constructor subgraph. Enter your edit instructions and include the required fields in plain text, for example: "duration: 4.0s; aspect ratio: 16:9; Make the sky a dramatic sunset while keeping the camera motion and timing unchanged." Keep the request specific and concise.

Ensure the Prompt Constructor’s output is connected to GeminiVideoOmni along with the video from LoadVideo. In GeminiVideoOmni, confirm any required configuration (such as API credentials or model selection) is set according to the node’s UI.

Run the workflow. Use PreviewAny to review the generated result. If framing looks off, adjust the aspect ratio in your prompt to match the source. If timing drifts, align the duration to the exact clip length.
When you’re satisfied, finalize the export with SaveVideo. Set your output path and desired settings (e.g., fps or quality if available in your node version) and run to write the edited video.
suggestedUseCases: Look development and color restyling: apply a consistent color grade or film look across a short clip with explicit duration and AR control.
Targeted visual modifications: change sky/weather, adjust lighting, or recolor an object while preserving the original camera motion.
Concept previews for clients: quickly iterate on VFX ideas with prompt-only edits before committing to manual compositing.
Style transfer and mood shifts: give footage a painterly, comic, or cinematic vibe that stays stable over the full duration.
Background cleanup: subtle de-emphasis or smoothing of backgrounds to draw attention to the subject.

faqItems.question: Why do I need to include duration and aspect ratio in the prompt?
faqItems.answer: The Gemini Omni Video model expects both fields to resolve temporal and spatial constraints. Providing them helps prevent timing drift, cropping, or letterboxing and improves overall consistency. Use the Prompt Constructor subgraph to add them correctly.

faqItems.question: What happens if my prompt’s duration doesn’t match the source clip?
faqItems.answer: You may see truncation, repetition, or timing artifacts. For best results, set the prompt duration to the exact clip length (in seconds) from LoadVideo so the edit aligns frame-for-frame.

faqItems.question: How do I avoid stretching or cropped outputs?
faqItems.answer: Match the prompt’s aspect ratio to the source video’s aspect ratio. If the input is 1920x1080, use aspect ratio: 16:9. Mismatches can introduce letterboxing or unintended crops.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow handle audio?
faqItems.answer: This workflow focuses on visual edits. If you need audio, export the edited video and remux it with the original audio track in a video editor or command-line tool.

a19fe4145591.title: PixVerse V6 Max: Text to Video
a19fe4145591.description: Generate videos up to 15 seconds at 1080p from a text prompt with PixVerse V6 Max, the higher-fidelity tier of PixVerse V6, with native audio and multi-shot direction in a single generation. No input files required. Ideal for social ads, product concept clips and short-form storytelling.
a19fe4145591.metaDescription: ComfyUI PixVerse V6 Max text-to-video up to 15s at 1080p with optional audio and multi-shot direction. No inputs. SaveVideo exports your clip.
a19fe4145591.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial shows how to generate short videos directly from a text prompt using PixVerse V6 Max. The core of the workflow is the PixverseV6TextToVideoNode, which calls the PixVerse model to render a single clip from your description with no input images or footage required. You control output fidelity with the quality parameter (long-edge presets for 360p, 540p, 720p, and 1080p). The node can render up to 15 seconds and supports native audio and multi-shot direction in a single generation. A MarkdownNote node provides inline guidance, and SaveVideo writes the returned clip to disk.

Under the hood, the PixverseV6TextToVideoNode sends your prompt and settings to the PixVerse API and receives an encoded video response. The higher-fidelity V6 Max tier prioritizes detail and temporal coherence, making it well-suited for social ads, product concept clips, and short-form storytelling. After generation, SaveVideo persists the clip (typically MP4) to your chosen output folder so you can review, iterate on the prompt, and quickly produce multiple versions at different quality levels.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and locate the PixverseV6TextToVideoNode, MarkdownNote, and SaveVideo nodes.
Open PixverseV6TextToVideoNode: enter a clear text prompt describing subject, action, setting, and style. If required, add your PixVerse API key in the node or ComfyUI settings.

Set quality to your target resolution (e.g., 360p = 640 px, 540p = 1024 px, 720p = 1280 px, 1080p = 1920 px). If the node exposes duration or audio options, choose a length up to 15 seconds and enable native audio as desired.
Optionally add multi-shot direction by outlining consecutive beats in your prompt (e.g., a short sequence of actions within the same clip). Keep timing realistic for the target duration.

Run the workflow. When the PixVerse render completes, the SaveVideo node will write the clip to your configured output folder. Review the result, then iterate on the prompt or quality for refinements.
suggestedUseCases: Social ads and promo shorts that need crisp detail and coherent motion at 1080p.
Product concept reels showing a prototype in context without filming.
Short-form storytelling or mood pieces with multi-beat direction in a single clip.
Explainer intros or logo stingers where optional native audio helps with impact.

faqItems.question: What makes V6 Max different from standard PixVerse V6?
faqItems.answer: V6 Max is the higher-fidelity tier. It focuses on sharper detail and stronger temporal coherence, which is helpful for 1080p outputs and content with fine textures or complex motion.

faqItems.question: Do I need any input images or footage?
faqItems.answer: No. This workflow is text-to-video only. Provide a descriptive prompt and the PixverseV6TextToVideoNode renders a single clip from scratch.

faqItems.question: What are the limits for resolution and length?
faqItems.answer: Quality controls the long edge: 360p ≈ 640 px, 540p ≈ 1024 px, 720p ≈ 1280 px, and 1080p ≈ 1920 px. Clips can be up to 15 seconds, depending on your node settings and account limits.

faqItems.question: How do I enable audio and multi-shot direction?
faqItems.answer: If your PixVerse account supports native audio and the node exposes an audio toggle, enable it before generating. For multi-shot direction, write clear, ordered beats in your prompt so the model can stage them within a single clip.

a1b8c3be20ff.title: PixVerse 6.0: Image to Video
a1b8c3be20ff.description: Turn a still image into a moving video clip with PixVerse V6, generating up to 15 seconds of footage at resolutions from 360p to 1080p. Supports multiple aspect ratios, integrated audio generation, and multi-shot direction for cohesive narrative flow. Ideal for social media ads, product demonstrations, and short-form storytelling.
a1b8c3be20ff.metaDescription: Turn a single image into a 3–15s video in ComfyUI with PixVerse V6. Set aspect ratio and resolution, guide motion, and export with SaveVideo.
a1b8c3be20ff.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow transforms a single still image into a short, cinematic video using the PixverseV6ImageToVideoNode. The graph is intentionally simple and production-focused: LoadImage brings in your source asset, PixverseV6ImageToVideoNode sends it to the PixVerse V6 image-to-video model via API for motion synthesis, and SaveVideo writes the returned clip to disk. The node exposes controls for duration (up to ~15 seconds), resolution selection from 360p through 1080p, and common aspect ratios, so you can quickly target platforms like TikTok, Instagram, or YouTube without additional resizing steps.

Technically, the PixverseV6ImageToVideoNode handles the heavy lifting off-device through the PixVerse service, so you don’t need a local GPU. You can guide motion and subject behavior with text direction in the node (for example, describing camera moves or the action you want). If your build of the node includes multi-shot/storyboard fields, you can specify timed beats or per-shot prompts for cohesive narrative flow; if not, stick with a single continuous shot. A MarkdownNote is included on-canvas to provide quick reminders. Finally, SaveVideo packages the generated clip to your ComfyUI output folder for immediate review and sharing.
howToUse: Open ComfyUI, update to the latest version if needed (see the provided update guide), and load the PixVerse 6.0: Image to Video workflow.
In LoadImage, select your source still. You can test with the provided sunny_pink_high_tops.png from the author notes or drop in your own image.

Open PixverseV6ImageToVideoNode and enter your PixVerse API credentials if required. Set duration (up to ~15s), choose resolution (360p–1080p), and pick an aspect ratio that fits your target platform.

Add motion direction in the node’s prompt/description field (e.g., specify subtle camera pan, product spin, or environmental movement). If your node exposes multi-shot/storyboard inputs, add scene beats there; otherwise, keep it as one continuous shot.
Optionally refine look and feel with any available controls in the node (such as style intensity or motion strength, if present).
Run the workflow. When complete, check the SaveVideo output in your ComfyUI output folder for the rendered clip.
suggestedUseCases: Product teasers from catalog photos (e.g., subtle 360° turns, parallax moves, or soft environmental motion).
Social media shorts and ads tailored to vertical, square, or landscape aspect ratios.
Storyboards and previsualization for creative concepts using multi-shot direction (if available in your node).
Animated cover images or hero banners for landing pages.
Quick motion studies from mood board stills to communicate camera intent.

faqItems.question: Do I need a GPU to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No. PixverseV6ImageToVideoNode calls the PixVerse V6 service over API, so the heavy compute happens remotely. Your local machine just orchestrates the request and saves the result.

faqItems.question: What video lengths and resolutions are supported?
faqItems.answer: The node typically supports clips up to about 15 seconds and common resolutions from 360p to 1080p. Exact limits depend on the PixVerse service settings for your account and the options exposed by your node build.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow generate audio?
faqItems.answer: This template is video-only. There is no audio-generation node in the graph. If you need music or sound effects, add audio in a video editor or extend the workflow with an audio node.

faqItems.question: How do I get consistent results or iterate on a look?
faqItems.answer: Keep your direction text consistent and reuse the same settings. If the node exposes a seed or repeat parameter, lock it for reproducibility. For iterations, duplicate the node and tweak one setting at a time (duration, resolution, or motion phrasing) to see targeted changes.

a1bb55d904c9.title: Wan2.1 VACE Inpainting
a1bb55d904c9.description: Edit specific regions in videos while preserving surrounding content. Great for object removal or replacement.
a1bb55d904c9.metaDescription: Edit video regions with Wan2.1 VACE Inpainting for seamless object removal or replacement while preserving surrounding content.
a1bb55d904c9.extendedDescription:
The Wan2.1 VACE Inpainting workflow is designed to seamlessly edit specific regions in video content while preserving the integrity of the surrounding areas. This is particularly useful for tasks such as object removal or replacement in video sequences. Utilizing the Wan2.1 model, this workflow leverages a combination of nodes including KSampler for sampling, CLIPTextEncode for text encoding, and VAEDecode for decoding video frames. The workflow is structured into several steps, starting from loading models and video files, to creating masks and compositing the final video output.

Technically, the workflow employs the WanVaceToVideo node to convert inpainted frames back into video format, while the TrimVideoLatent and CreateVideo nodes manage the video length and format. The ImageCompositeMasked node is crucial for blending the inpainted regions with the original video, ensuring a natural look. By using core nodes, the workflow avoids the need for additional custom installations, making it accessible and easy to implement. This workflow is particularly valuable for content creators and video editors who need to make precise edits without affecting the overall quality of the video.
howToUse: Load the Wan2.1 VACE Inpainting workflow in ComfyUI.
Import the video you wish to edit using the LoadVideo node.
Create a mask for the region you want to inpaint using the ImageToMask node.
Configure the KSampler and CLIPTextEncode nodes with your desired settings and prompts.
Run the workflow to process the video and generate the inpainted output.
Save the final video using the SaveVideo node.
suggestedUseCases: Removing unwanted objects from a video scene.
Replacing objects in a video with alternative content.
Enhancing video quality by correcting specific regions.
Creating special effects by altering video elements.
Preserving video continuity while making targeted edits.

faqItems.question: What models are used in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow uses the Wan2.1 model, specifically the VACE-1.3B and VACE-14B models, for video inpainting tasks.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow handle high-resolution videos?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the VACE-1.3B model supports 480P resolution, while the VACE-14B model supports up to 720P resolution.

faqItems.question: Do I need custom nodes for this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No, the workflow is designed using core nodes, so no additional custom nodes are required.

faqItems.question: How do I create a mask for the video?
faqItems.answer: You can use the ImageToMask node to define the region you want to inpaint in the video.

a20d3822a38f.title: Wan2.5: Image to Video
a20d3822a38f.description: Transform images into videos with synchronized audio, enhanced motion, and superior quality.
a20d3822a38f.metaDescription: Transform images into videos with synchronized audio using the Wan2.5 workflow. Enhance motion and quality effortlessly.
a20d3822a38f.extendedDescription: The 'Wan2.5: Image to Video' workflow is designed to transform static images into dynamic video content, complete with synchronized audio. This workflow leverages the Wan2.5 and Wan models to enhance motion and ensure superior video quality. The process begins with uploading an image using the LoadImage node, which serves as the foundation for video generation. The optional audio component can be integrated via the LoadAudio or RecordAudio nodes, allowing for a more immersive video experience. The core of the transformation occurs through the WanImageToVideoApi node, which processes the image and audio to produce a cohesive video output. Finally, the SaveVideo node is used to store the resulting video file. This workflow is particularly useful for creators looking to add motion to still images, whether for social media content, marketing materials, or creative projects.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure you have the Wan2.5 and Wan models installed.
Upload your image using the LoadImage node in the 'Step1 - Upload image' group.
Optionally, add audio by using the LoadAudio or RecordAudio nodes. Ensure the audio is between 3-30 seconds and under 15MB.
Connect the audio output to the Wan Text to Video input if using audio.
Run the workflow to process the image and audio through the WanImageToVideoApi node.
Save the resulting video using the SaveVideo node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating engaging social media content by animating still images.
Developing marketing materials that combine static visuals with dynamic motion.
Enhancing personal photo albums with video elements.
Producing educational content that combines images and narration.
Crafting artistic video projects from static artwork.

faqItems.question: Do I need to use audio for this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No, audio is optional. However, adding audio can enhance the final video output by providing a more immersive experience.

faqItems.question: What are the requirements for the audio file?
faqItems.answer: The audio file should be between 3-30 seconds long and smaller than 15MB to be compatible with the workflow.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow without an internet connection?
faqItems.answer: Yes, as long as you are within a secure network environment that allows access from '127.0.0.1' or 'localhost'.

faqItems.question: How do I enable the RecordAudio node?
faqItems.answer: Select the RecordAudio node and press 'Ctrl - B' to enable it for recording.

a2460ab23a60.title: SDXL Revision Text Prompts
a2460ab23a60.description: Generate images by transferring concepts from reference images using SDXL Revision.
a2460ab23a60.metaDescription: Generate images using SDXL Revision by transferring concepts from reference images. Perfect for artists and designers seeking creative inspiration.
a2460ab23a60.extendedDescription: The SDXL Revision Text Prompts workflow is designed to generate high-quality images by effectively transferring concepts from reference images using the SDXL model. This workflow leverages a series of nodes to process both textual and visual inputs, allowing for nuanced image creation based on specific prompts. At its core, it uses the CLIPTextEncode node to interpret text prompts and the CLIPVisionEncode node to analyze reference images. The KSampler node is crucial in synthesizing the final image by sampling from the latent space informed by both text and image inputs. The VAEDecode node then decodes this latent representation into a visible image, which can be saved using the SaveImage node. This workflow is particularly useful for artists and designers who wish to incorporate specific styles or elements from reference images into new creations, offering a seamless blend of textual and visual inspiration.
howToUse: Load the SDXL Revision Text Prompts workflow into ComfyUI.
Import your desired reference images using the LoadImage node.
Enter your text prompts in the CLIPTextEncode node, such as 'car, city, anime style'.
Configure the KSampler node to adjust sampling parameters for desired output quality.
Run the workflow to generate the image, which will be decoded and saved using the VAEDecode and SaveImage nodes.
Review the generated image and make adjustments to prompts or reference images as needed for refinement.
suggestedUseCases: Creating concept art by blending elements from various reference images.
Designing marketing visuals that incorporate specific brand elements.
Generating unique artistic styles by combining textual prompts with visual references.
Developing storyboards for animations or films using thematic prompts and images.
Crafting personalized gifts or merchandise with custom imagery.

faqItems.question: What types of images work best as reference images?
faqItems.answer: High-quality images with clear elements work best, as they provide more detailed information for the CLIPVisionEncode node to process.

faqItems.question: Can I use multiple reference images at once?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can load multiple reference images to provide a richer context for the image generation process.

faqItems.question: How do I adjust the style of the generated image?
faqItems.answer: You can modify the text prompts and adjust the KSampler node settings to influence the style and quality of the output image.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to generate images without reference images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can generate images using only text prompts, but including reference images can enhance the specificity and style of the output.

a262dd6de9ce.title: Seedream 5.0 Pro: Text to Image
a262dd6de9ce.description: Generate images from text prompts using Seedream 5.0 Pro, producing one high-quality output. Ideal for creative concept art, marketing visual mockups, and rapid ideation for design projects.
a262dd6de9ce.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate a single high-quality image from text with ByteDance Seedream 5.0 Pro using ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 and SaveImageAdvanced.
a262dd6de9ce.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns your text prompt into a single, high-quality image using ByteDance’s Seedream 5.0 Pro model, wrapped by the ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2. You type your prompt, optionally set a seed and resolution, and the node makes an API call to Seedream 5.0 Pro to generate one image. The result is then passed to SaveImageAdvanced, which writes the output to disk with your chosen filename pattern and folder.

Technically, ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 handles prompt text and common generation controls such as seed (for reproducibility) and image size (width/height supported by the API). Many versions of this node also expose guidance (CFG) and steps; if available in your build, you can fine-tune detail and prompt adherence. The node returns the generated image tensor, which SaveImageAdvanced persists according to your output directory and naming settings. This design keeps the graph minimal and focused: one model call for a clean, single-image result, ideal for fast iteration on concept art, mockups, and design ideation.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and ensure the ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 custom node is installed. If not, install it (e.g., via ComfyUI Manager) and restart ComfyUI.
Open ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 and add your Seedream/ByteDance API key. Use the node’s API key field or an environment/config method if your installation supports it.

Enter your text prompt. Optionally set a negative prompt (if exposed in your node version), choose a fixed seed for reproducible results, and select a supported width/height. If the node exposes guidance (CFG) or steps, start with moderate values and adjust as needed.
Configure SaveImageAdvanced: set the output directory and a filename prefix (for example, include the project name or seed).
Click Queue/Run. Preview the generated image in ComfyUI and find the saved file in your configured output folder.
Iterate: refine the prompt, tweak seed and resolution, and re-run. For variations, change the seed; to keep a look, reuse the same seed and adjust wording subtly.
suggestedUseCases: Creative concept art and moodboards for films, games, and branding
Marketing visual mockups and campaign ideation
Rapid product ideation and hero image drafts
Social media visuals that need quick, on-brief imagery

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key to use ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Enter your ByteDance/Seedream API key in the node’s API key field or configure it via environment variables if your installation supports that. Without a valid key, the node cannot call the Seedream 5.0 Pro API.

faqItems.question: How do I get consistent, repeatable results?
faqItems.answer: Set a fixed seed in ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2. Using the same prompt, resolution, and parameters with the same seed will produce consistent results, subject to any upstream API changes.

faqItems.question: What image sizes are supported?
faqItems.answer: Use width/height values supported by the Seedream 5.0 Pro API (often specific multiples). If a size isn’t accepted, try common square values like 1024×1024 or consult the node/API documentation for allowed dimensions.

faqItems.question: Can I generate multiple images at once?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is set up for a single high-quality output. If your ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 build supports a batch or count parameter, you can increase it. Otherwise, duplicate the node or re-run with different seeds for variations.

a335e0968d76.title: Music Generator
a335e0968d76.description: This app uses Stable Audio 3 to generate full music tracks, instruments, SFX or one shots.
a335e0968d76.metaDescription: Generate stereo music, instruments, SFX, and one-shots from text using a Stable Audio 3 ComfyUI workflow with duration control and advanced saving.
a335e0968d76.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns short text ideas into stereo audio using Stable Audio 3. At its core is a Stable Audio 3 generator node (UUID: 8b66c757-fe2f-4184-91f3-479a19deb565) that accepts a prompt and timing controls to synthesize full tracks, instrument phrases, sound effects, or one‑shot samples. A PrimitiveFloat node provides precise numeric control (for example, duration in seconds), and SaveAudioAdvanced writes the resulting waveform to disk with your chosen name and location. A MarkdownNote in the graph offers quick, in‑workflow tips.

Technically, your prompt and numeric parameters flow into the Stable Audio 3 node, which renders a stereo waveform guided by style, instrumentation, mood, and length cues in your text. The output plugs directly into SaveAudioAdvanced so you can batch or iteratively export results. This setup is useful for fast ideation and production: short durations (e.g., 0.5–2 s) are great for one‑shots, a few seconds for SFX, and longer spans for music beds—all without leaving ComfyUI.
howToUse: Load the Music Generator workflow JSON in ComfyUI and confirm all nodes are green (loaded).
Open the MarkdownNote in the graph for a quick overview and any author tips.

In the Stable Audio 3 node (UUID: 8b66c757-fe2f-4184-91f3-479a19deb565), enter a concise text prompt that names genre, instruments, mood/energy, and any key descriptors (e.g., "uplifting synthwave, analog bass, punchy drums, 100 BPM feel").

Set the desired duration using the connected PrimitiveFloat node (for example, 0.8 for a one‑shot, 3–5 for SFX, 15–60 for music beds). Adjust any additional controls exposed by the Stable Audio 3 node as needed.
Configure SaveAudioAdvanced to choose the output folder and filename pattern. Enable auto‑save if you want files written without manual intervention.
Click Queue Prompt. When the run completes, listen to the saved file. Iterate by refining the prompt or duration to hone style, tightness, or impact.
suggestedUseCases: Quick background music beds for videos or streams from a plain‑language prompt.
Game and film SFX prototyping (impacts, whooshes, ambience) generated on demand.
Instrument riffs, motifs, and loops for songwriting or beatmaking inspiration.
One‑shot samples (kicks, snares, hits, stingers) to load into a sampler or DAW.
Podcast and content branding (intros, outros, transitions) tailored by mood.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key or special model files?
faqItems.answer: That depends on your Stable Audio 3 node setup. Some installs call a cloud API (you’ll need to add an API key in the node or environment), while others may use a locally available model or backend. Check the node’s settings and your ComfyUI console for credential or model path prompts.

faqItems.question: How long can the audio be?
faqItems.answer: Use the PrimitiveFloat to set duration. Practical maximums depend on the Stable Audio 3 backend and your hardware or API limits. Longer durations take more time and resources; start short (e.g., 5–15 s) and increase as needed.

faqItems.question: What format and quality does it save?
faqItems.answer: The workflow produces stereo audio from Stable Audio 3 and passes it to SaveAudioAdvanced, which writes the file to disk. Check the SaveAudioAdvanced node’s options and the saved file’s metadata in your OS or DAW to confirm format and quality settings available in your setup.

faqItems.question: How do I get more consistent results or controlled variations?
faqItems.answer: Keep prompts consistent in style, instrumentation, and mood terms. If the Stable Audio 3 node exposes a seed or variation parameter, fix the seed for repeatability or change it to explore variations. Small, targeted prompt edits (e.g., "add muted guitar" or "lower reverb") help guide iterative refinement.

a39b591d8c3b.title: Qwen Image Layer Decomp for Illustration v1
a39b591d8c3b.description: Workflow example for using Qwen Image layer decomposition tools to help separate layers in a scene.
a39b591d8c3b.metaDescription: Tutorial workflow for Qwen-based image layer decomposition in ComfyUI. Separate an illustration into clean layers and masks for compositing or editing.
a39b591d8c3b.extendedDescription:
Qwen Image Layer Decomp for Illustration v1 is a guided layer-separation workflow for turning a flat illustration into editable layers and masks. It routes a loaded image through ImageScaleToMaxDimension to a recommended working size (640 px for speed, 1024 px for detail), then drives a custom Qwen-based decomposition stage that predicts per-element mattes you can save as PNGs. A PrimitiveStringMultiline node provides an optional, high-level text prompt so you can nudge the model toward the objects you want isolated (for example: "character, foreground props, midground buildings, sky").

Technically, the core is implemented with two custom nodes (f754a936-daaf-4b6e-9658-41fdc54d301d and 1ea4fa01-a81b-4420-a03c-f60019e69a92). The first performs the Qwen image layer decomposition using diffusion-style sampling controls (the author’s baseline is 50 steps, CFG 4.0), trading runtime for mask quality. The second is used for selection/refinement of the predicted layers (cleaning edges or exporting specific passes). LoadImage and SaveImage handle I/O, while MarkdownNote contains on-canvas guidance and links. The result is a practical, prompt-guided layer extraction pipeline that’s ideal for compositing, recoloring, and 2.5D motion work.
howToUse: Update ComfyUI to the latest version and ensure the required Qwen decomposition custom nodes and model files are installed (follow the node’s README). Open the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote for any prerequisites.
Load your source artwork with LoadImage. Set ImageScaleToMaxDimension to 640 for faster iteration or 1024 for higher-fidelity edges while keeping aspect ratio intact.

In PrimitiveStringMultiline, enter an optional prompt describing the scene and desired layers (e.g., "main character, sword, foreground flowers, background sky"). You can leave it empty to run with the node’s defaults.

Open the custom decomposition node (ID: f754a936-daaf-4b6e-9658-41fdc54d301d) and start with the provided sampler settings: Steps = 50, CFG = 4.0. Increase steps for cleaner mattes; decrease for speed. Then run the graph.

Inspect the outputs. If edges look soft or bleed into neighbors, try a higher input size (1024) or a few more steps. If halos appear, slightly lower CFG. Use the refinement/selection node (ID: 1ea4fa01-a81b-4420-a03c-f60019e69a92) to pick specific layers or clean transitions.
Save per-layer images or masks via the connected SaveImage nodes. For compositing, prefer PNG with alpha. Iterate on the prompt (naming the elements you care about) to improve the separation.
suggestedUseCases: Isolating characters and props from illustrated scenes for recoloring, relighting, or texture edits.
Preparing clean foreground/midground/background passes for parallax and 2.5D motion graphics.
Separating UI/mockup elements from flat renders to quickly iterate on layout and styling.
Extracting objects from concept art to build reusable asset libraries for game or film previz.
Creating precise masks for targeted inpainting or localized image-to-image edits.

faqItems.question: What models or files do I need, and where do they go?
faqItems.answer: This workflow relies on custom Qwen image layer decomposition nodes. Install the node repo as instructed by its README and place the required model weights in the paths it specifies (typically under ComfyUI/models or a subfolder the node creates). Then restart ComfyUI so the nodes detect the weights.

faqItems.question: It feels slow—how can I speed it up?
faqItems.answer: Reduce Steps (e.g., from 50 to 30–40), lower the working size to 640 px in ImageScaleToMaxDimension, and keep CFG around 3.5–4.0. These changes noticeably cut runtime with modest quality tradeoffs. For the final pass, switch back to 1024 px and a few more steps.

faqItems.question: Do I have to write a prompt?
faqItems.answer: No—the PrimitiveStringMultiline prompt is optional. However, short, concrete descriptions of the elements you want (e.g., "character, cape, sword, sky") often produce more accurate and neatly separated layers than running with defaults.

faqItems.question: How do I get crisper edges and fewer halos?
faqItems.answer: Use a larger input (1024 px), increase Steps slightly (e.g., +10), and avoid very high CFG values. After decomposition, use the refinement/selection node to clean transitions. If needed, lightly feather or contract the mask in your compositor for final polish.

a3e50e79cb89.title: Hunyuan Video 1.5 Text to Video
a3e50e79cb89.description: Generate high-quality 720p videos from text prompts with cinematic camera control, emotional expressions, and physics simulation. Supports multiple styles including realistic, anime, and 3D with text rendering.
a3e50e79cb89.metaDescription: Text-to-video with Hunyuan Video 1.5 in ComfyUI. Generate 720p clips from prompts, with optional 1080p upscaling, camera control, and super-resolution.
a3e50e79cb89.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns text prompts into coherent 720p videos using the Hunyuan Video 1.5 model, with optional 1080p upscaling and super-resolution. It’s organized into clear groups: Step 1 - Load models, Step 3 - Prompt, Step 4 - Video Size, Custom Sampler, and an optional Video Upscale 1080P (Ctrl-B to enable). The pipeline loads Hunyuan’s text encoders with DualCLIPLoader and encodes your prompt via CLIPTextEncode. EmptyHunyuanVideo15Latent defines the temporal canvas (resolution, frame count, FPS), while RandomNoise sets the seed. UNETLoader brings in the Hunyuan Video 1.5 UNet, and SamplerCustomAdvanced (driven by KSamplerSelect, BasicScheduler, and CFGGuider) performs diffusion steps to synthesize video latents at 720p. VAELoader plus VAEDecode (or VAEDecodeTiled for memory efficiency) converts latents to frames, which CreateVideo stitches into a final clip, saved with SaveVideo.

For higher fidelity, the workflow includes a latent-space upscaling path. LatentUpscaleModelLoader and HunyuanVideo15LatentUpscaleWithModel can boost resolution before decoding, and HunyuanVideo15SuperResolution refines details after generation. EasyCache is available to accelerate repeated runs by caching encodings, at the cost of some visual quality. The default step count is set to 20 for reasonable render times; increasing steps (e.g., toward the Hunyuan team’s original settings) improves detail but extends inference time. If you encounter VRAM limits, set weight_dtype to fp8_e4n3fn and switch to VAEDecodeTiled.
howToUse: Load the template in ComfyUI and ensure the required Hunyuan Video 1.5 weights and text encoders are downloaded. In Step 1 - Load models, point VAELoader, DualCLIPLoader, and UNETLoader to the correct files. If VRAM is low, set weight_dtype to fp8_e4n3fn.

Open Step 3 - Prompt and enter a detailed prompt describing subject, style, and camera moves (e.g., “low-angle dolly shot, shallow depth of field, cinematic lighting”). If a negative prompt path exists in your template, fill it to suppress unwanted artifacts.
Go to Step 4 - Video Size. Set width/height for 720p (e.g., 1280x720), choose frames and FPS (e.g., 48–96 frames at 16–24 fps for 2–6s clips). Set a seed in RandomNoise for reproducibility.

In Custom Sampler, keep 20 steps for faster drafts or raise to 30–50 for higher quality. Adjust CFGGuider (e.g., 3–7) to balance prompt adherence vs. naturalness. Leave KSamplerSelect and BasicScheduler at their defaults unless you’re experimenting.

Run the base path to produce a 720p video. The UNet sampling will output latents, VAEDecode (or VAEDecodeTiled) will convert to frames, CreateVideo will assemble them, and SaveVideo will write the file.

Optional: Enable Video Upscale 1080P (Ctrl-B). Load a latent upscaler in LatentUpscaleModelLoader, run HunyuanVideo15LatentUpscaleWithModel, then HunyuanVideo15SuperResolution for extra sharpness. Use VAEDecodeTiled if decoding becomes slow or memory-heavy.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic concept previews for film or advertising with controllable camera motions.
Stylized shorts (realistic, anime, or 3D look) for social media or motion moodboards.
Product hero shots and explainer clips with guided camera paths and text rendering.
Educational micro-simulations and physics-inspired sequences (e.g., falling, gliding, collisions).
Animatics and previsualization where timing, framing, and movement need quick iteration.

faqItems.question: How can I improve quality without huge render times?
faqItems.answer: Start at 20 steps for drafts. For finals, raise to 30–40 steps, keep 720p base resolution, and enable HunyuanVideo15SuperResolution. If you need 1080p, use the latent upscaler path but expect longer runtimes.

faqItems.question: I get OOM errors or black frames. What should I change?
faqItems.answer: Lower width/height and/or frame count, set weight_dtype to fp8_e4n3fn, switch to VAEDecodeTiled, and disable the 1080p upscaler group. Close other GPU apps and reduce CFG or steps if needed.

faqItems.question: How do I control camera movements and emotion in the video?
faqItems.answer: Describe shots explicitly in the prompt (e.g., “handheld close-up, slow push-in, rack focus, emotional smile”). Mention lens and lighting cues (“35mm, golden hour, volumetric light”). Keep sentences concise and avoid conflicting directives.

faqItems.question: What does EasyCache do, and when should I use it?
faqItems.answer: EasyCache stores intermediate encodings to speed up iterations (useful when only small prompt tweaks change). It trades some visual fidelity for speed; use it for look development, then disable for final renders.

a4e8aec9d618.title: Wan2.7: Image to Video
a4e8aec9d618.description: Upload an image and audio file to generate a video with synchronized sound, using the first and last frames for control.
a4e8aec9d618.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Convert image(s) and audio into a synchronized video using Wan2.7 with first/last frame control for guided motion.
a4e8aec9d618.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow shows you how to turn a still image (or a pair of start/end images) and an audio track into a coherent video with sound using Wan2.7. The core is the Wan2ImageToVideoApi node, which takes your reference image(s) and audio, then synthesizes the in-between frames so the video begins on your first frame, transitions naturally, and lands on your last frame. LoadImage nodes feed the first and last control frames, while SaveVideo writes the final output to disk.

Technically, the first and last frames act as strong compositional anchors: Wan2.7 preserves the subject and layout at those endpoints and generates motion between them. The audio you provide is used to align timing and pacing so the video duration matches the track and motion evolves in sync. Keep your start and end images aligned in aspect ratio and subject framing for cleaner transitions. The SaveVideo node then packages the generated frames (and the synchronized audio from the API) into a playable video file.
howToUse: Open ComfyUI and load the "Wan2.7: Image to Video" workflow.
On the first LoadImage node, choose your starting reference image (this will be the first frame).
Optionally set a second LoadImage node as the ending control frame. If you skip this, the first image will guide both start and end.
Open the Wan2ImageToVideoApi node and select your audio file. Review any available settings (e.g., resolution/aspect ratio or duration if exposed) to match your image and desired runtime.
Queue and run the workflow. The Wan2.7 model will generate in-between frames guided by your first/last images and the audio timing.
When the run completes, the SaveVideo node will write the final video. Open the saved file to review motion and audio sync.
suggestedUseCases: Social posts that animate a still brand image to music for short promos.
Before-and-after reveals where the first and last frames bookend a smooth motion transition.
Cinemagraph-style loops that start and end on nearly identical frames for seamless playback.
Portrait or product hero shots that gain subtle camera motion synced to a soundtrack.
Title cards or splash screens that animate in and settle on a final design.

faqItems.question: Do I need two images, or can I use just one?
faqItems.answer: You can use one or two. One image will guide both the start and end, creating motion that returns to the original framing. Adding a second image as the last frame lets Wan2.7 transition toward a different final composition.

faqItems.question: How does the audio affect the output?
faqItems.answer: The audio defines the video’s duration and helps align motion pacing. Choose a track with the length you want. If the node exposes timing controls, keep them consistent with the audio to avoid truncation or extra silence.

faqItems.question: What resolution and aspect ratio should I use?
faqItems.answer: Match the aspect ratio between your first and last frames, and keep a reasonable resolution your hardware or API quota can handle. Higher resolutions need more compute and time—start smaller to validate motion, then scale up.

faqItems.question: How can I get cleaner, more stable motion?
faqItems.answer: Use sharp, well-lit images with consistent subject size and framing across the first and last frames. Avoid drastic changes in viewpoint or lighting between endpoints. If available, reduce motion intensity settings for subtler moves.

howToUse: Load your starting image using the 'LoadImage' node in ComfyUI.

a63de8f04c27.title: Replace Background: Bria
a63de8f04c27.description: Upload a video and a background image. Detect the main subject and replace the original background with the provided image. Ideal for content creation, virtual production, and background cleanup in video projects.
a63de8f04c27.metaDescription: Replace any video background with a custom image using BRIA in ComfyUI. Load video, choose a backdrop, and export a clean composite in minutes.
a63de8f04c27.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow replaces the background of a video with a custom image using BRIA’s background replacement model. It chains four nodes: LoadVideo brings in your source footage, LoadImage provides the new backdrop, BriaVideoReplaceBackground detects the primary subject and composites it over the new background, and SaveVideo encodes the final output. The BRIA model is purpose-built for subject extraction, allowing the node to generate a clean matte for each frame and produce a seamless composite suitable for social content, product demos, and virtual backdrops.

Technically, the BriaVideoReplaceBackground node takes the video frames from LoadVideo, isolates the main subject via learned segmentation, and merges it with the image from LoadImage. Because it operates on sequences rather than single frames, you can expect more consistent edges and fewer artifacts than naive, frame-by-frame cutouts. SaveVideo then packages the processed frames into a standard video file. For best results, match your background image’s aspect ratio to the source video and choose a backdrop that aligns with your scene’s lighting and perspective.
howToUse: Open the “Replace Background: Bria” workflow in ComfyUI and confirm that the BRIA model/service is available for the BriaVideoReplaceBackground node (configure credentials or model access if required by your setup).
Use the LoadVideo node to select your source video. Prefer stable, well-lit footage with a clear subject for the cleanest cutout.
Use the LoadImage node to choose your new background image. For best results, match the video’s aspect ratio and use an image at least as large as the video resolution.
Connect LoadVideo and LoadImage to BriaVideoReplaceBackground as shown in the workflow. The node will segment the main subject and composite it onto the provided background.

Preview a short segment by queuing the workflow. If edges look harsh or the background doesn’t fit, try a higher-resolution background image or adjust your source video (e.g., better contrast, steadier framing).
Run the full workflow and export using the SaveVideo node to generate the final composite video.
suggestedUseCases: Social media clips: Quickly swap busy or cluttered backdrops for clean, on-brand images.
Product videos: Isolate products from distracting environments and place them on studio-like backgrounds.
Corporate and educational content: Standardize presenter backgrounds for a consistent, professional look.
Virtual set previews: Test different scene backgrounds for pre-visualization or pitch materials.
Background cleanup: Remove unwanted elements from location shoots by replacing with a neutral plate.

faqItems.question: What input and output formats should I use?
faqItems.answer: Use widely compatible inputs like MP4 (H.264) for the LoadVideo node. The SaveVideo node will export a standard video file (often MP4, depending on your configuration). If a file doesn’t load or save correctly, transcode it to MP4/H.264 with a common tool and try again.

faqItems.question: Can I use a video as the new background?
faqItems.answer: This workflow uses LoadImage for the background, so it expects a still image. To use a video background, you’d need to extend the workflow with a video background source and a compositor that supports frame-synchronized layering.

faqItems.question: How do I get cleaner edges and fewer artifacts?
faqItems.answer: Start with footage that has clear separation between subject and background, steady camera work, and good lighting. Use a background image that matches the video’s aspect ratio and general lighting direction. Slightly blurring the replacement background can also reduce haloing and make the composite look more natural.

faqItems.question: Will my audio be preserved?
faqItems.answer: This simple pipeline focuses on visual compositing. If the SaveVideo output doesn’t include your original audio, combine the exported video with the source audio in a video editor or add an audio-handling step to the workflow.

a6b2c3fe248c.title: AI on the Lot 2026_Qwen-Image-Edit-2511
a6b2c3fe248c.description: A bonus workflow for AI on the Lot 2026, made available for ComfyUI 101 workshop attendees to open and follow along if time allows. An image editing workflow powered by Qwen-Image-Edit-2511.
a6b2c3fe248c.metaDescription: Instruction-based image and video frame editing in ComfyUI using Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 and Qwen2.5-VL encoder, optimized for fast 4-step Lightning inference.
a6b2c3fe248c.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow shows how to perform fast, instruction-based image edits using Qwen-Image-Edit-2511. It wires a simple I/O path—LoadImage (or VHS_LoadVideo for frames) into a compact Subgraph node (ID cdb2cf24-c432-439b-b5c8-5f69838580c9)—and ends with SaveImage. Inside the subgraph, the edit is driven by the Qwen 2.5 VL text encoder (qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled.safetensors) and a lightweight LoRA tuned for speed (Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning-4steps-V1.0-bf16.safetensors). The subgraph encapsulates the model plumbing so you can focus on a plain-language instruction like “make the sky overcast” or “remove the background,” then preview results quickly.

Technically, the workflow routes your source image (or video frames) into the subgraph, where the Qwen 2.5 VL encoder interprets your instruction text and conditions the edit. The Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 Lightning LoRA applies the learned edit behavior while keeping inference fast with very few sampling steps. Because this is packaged as a Subgraph, you get a clean graph and consistent defaults—you can double-click or open the subgraph to inspect or tweak internals as needed. SaveImage captures each result frame to disk; when fed by VHS_LoadVideo, you’ll get a numbered image sequence you can reassemble externally if you want a final video.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then read the MarkdownNote for a quick overview.

Download the models from the Author Notes: place qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled.safetensors in models/text_encoders and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning-4steps-V1.0-bf16.safetensors in models/loras. Restart ComfyUI if needed so they appear in dropdowns.

Choose your input: use LoadImage for a single image, or VHS_LoadVideo to bring in a clip (the node outputs frames). Make sure the chosen input is connected to the Subgraph node (ID cdb2cf24-c432-439b-b5c8-5f69838580c9).

Open the Subgraph node and enter a clear instruction for the edit (e.g., “remove the background to white,” “replace the sky with sunset clouds,” or “turn the car red”). Keep defaults for the Lightning 4-step flow unless you specifically need stronger/weaker edits.
Click Queue Prompt to run. Watch the preview; iterate on your instruction wording if needed for precision (e.g., specify colors, materials, or style adjectives).
Find your results in the SaveImage output folder. If you edited a video, you’ll get an image sequence (one file per processed frame) you can reassemble into a video using your preferred tool.
suggestedUseCases: Product photo cleanup: remove backgrounds, unify lighting, or standardize surface colors for catalogs.
Quick look development: swap skies, adjust time of day, or add simple scene elements for previsualization.
Brand consistency passes: nudge color tones and accessories across multiple shots to match a style guide.
Social content polish: refine thumbnails and hero images with small, targeted edits in seconds.
Frame-by-frame video touch-ups: apply the same light edit across a short clip and export as an image sequence.

faqItems.question: Do I need any extra extensions or custom nodes?
faqItems.answer: Core nodes (LoadImage, SaveImage, MarkdownNote) are built-in. The workflow uses a Subgraph node (ID cdb2cf24-…) and optionally VHS_LoadVideo for video frames. If you don’t see VHS_LoadVideo, install the VideoHelperSuite (VHS) extension. Then place the provided model files in models/text_encoders and models/loras as noted.

faqItems.question: Where do I put the model files?
faqItems.answer: Place qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning-4steps-V1.0-bf16.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/loras. Restart ComfyUI so they appear in any model/LoRA selectors inside the subgraph.

faqItems.question: How can I get cleaner or more accurate edits?
faqItems.answer: Use high-quality input images, write precise instructions (mention target objects, colors, and context), and keep the edit scope focused. If results are too strong or weak, adjust the subgraph’s exposed edit controls (e.g., strength/intensity if available) or try slightly different phrasings. Running at moderate resolutions also helps stability.

faqItems.question: Can this do masked or region-specific edits?
faqItems.answer: This template focuses on instruction-based global edits and does not include masking nodes. You can often localize changes by writing specific instructions (e.g., “only change the jacket color to navy”), or you can extend the workflow by adding a masking path if you need precise region control.

faqItems.question: How do I turn edited frames back into a video?
faqItems.answer: This workflow saves frames via SaveImage. After processing, import the numbered image sequence into a video editor or use a command-line tool (e.g., ffmpeg) to encode a video. If you prefer an in-graph export, add a video writer node and connect it after the edit stage.

a6f4d96872e1.title: YouTube Thumbnail Generator
a6f4d96872e1.description: Generate high-contrast, clickable YouTube thumbnails using Nano Banana Pro. Creates dramatic compositions with exaggerated subjects and bold color strategies for maximum engagement.
a6f4d96872e1.metaDescription: Create striking YouTube thumbnails with Nano Banana Pro using ComfyUI. Enhance engagement with bold colors and dramatic compositions.
a6f4d96872e1.extendedDescription: The YouTube Thumbnail Generator workflow is designed to create eye-catching and engaging thumbnails for YouTube videos using the Nano Banana Pro model. This workflow leverages the power of the GeminiNanoBanana2 node to produce high-contrast, dramatic compositions that highlight subjects with exaggerated features and bold color schemes, ensuring maximum viewer engagement. The workflow includes nodes such as BatchImagesNode, which allows for processing multiple images simultaneously, and SaveImage, which conveniently stores the generated thumbnails. By integrating reference images through the LoadImage node, users can guide the style and composition of their thumbnails, ensuring consistency and relevance to their video content.
howToUse: Load the YouTube Thumbnail Generator workflow in ComfyUI.
Select the BatchImagesNode and press Ctrl-B to enable batch processing.
Add reference images using the LoadImage node to guide the thumbnail style.
Configure the GeminiNanoBanana2 node to adjust the exaggeration and color intensity.
Run the workflow to generate thumbnails and use the SaveImage node to save them.
Review and refine the thumbnails as needed to ensure they meet your engagement goals.
suggestedUseCases: Creating thumbnails for a new YouTube video series to maintain a consistent style.
Enhancing older video thumbnails to improve click-through rates.
Designing thumbnails for promotional videos that require high viewer engagement.
Generating thumbnails for educational content where clarity and emphasis are crucial.
Developing thumbnails for entertainment channels that rely on bold visuals.

faqItems.question: How do I enable batch processing in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Select the BatchImagesNode and press Ctrl-B to enable batch processing, allowing you to process multiple images at once.

faqItems.question: Can I use multiple reference images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can add multiple reference images using the LoadImage node to guide the style and composition of your thumbnails.

faqItems.question: What is the role of the GeminiNanoBanana2 node?

faqItems.question: How can I save the generated thumbnails?
