a720f3751905.title: Seedance2.5 Draft: Reference to Video
a720f3751905.description: Generate draft preview videos from reference images using Seedance 2.5's two-phase draft mode: stage one turns your references and prompt into a fast, low-cost 480p preview plus a reusable draft task ID, and stage two renders the 1080p final from that ID. Ideal for locking in a character or storyboard reference before committing to a full-quality render.
a720f3751905.metaDescription: Two-phase ComfyUI workflow: create Seedance 2.5 draft videos from references, save the draft task ID, then render consistent 1080p finals.
a720f3751905.extendedDescription:
This workflow demonstrates Seedance 2.5's two-phase draft mode for reference-to-video generation. In Stage 1, it turns your reference images and prompt into a fast, low-cost 480p preview and returns a reusable draft task ID. The key nodes are LoadImage (to bring in one or more reference images such as a character sheet or storyboard), ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2 (which submits the prompt and references to the Seedance 2.5 API for a draft render), SaveVideo (to write the 480p preview to disk), and SaveText (to persist the draft task ID for later). The included MarkdownNote blocks label each stage and summarize what to edit.

Stage 2 uses ByteDance2DraftToFinalVideoNode to request a 1080p final render from the saved draft task ID, guaranteeing the final matches the approved draft content. SaveVideo captures the full-resolution output. This staged approach is useful because it lets you iterate quickly on character consistency or shot composition from references before committing compute to the final. The draft task ID effectively “locks” the generation; when you promote it to final, you get the same motion/content at higher quality, making reviews and approvals more predictable.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and review the two groups: Stage 1 (Create and preview the draft video) and Stage 2 (Render the final video from the draft task ID).
In Stage 1, open the LoadImage nodes and select your references (e.g., yellow_mech_character_sheet.png for look consistency and mech_comic_storyboard.png for framing).
Open ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2 and enter a clear prompt that describes the motion and style. Adjust any available parameters your installation exposes. Queue Stage 1 to generate the 480p draft.
Check the saved preview from SaveVideo. If it’s not what you want, tweak the prompt or references and re-queue Stage 1 until satisfied.
When the draft looks good, copy the draft task ID saved by the SaveText node.
Open Stage 2, paste the draft task ID into ByteDance2DraftToFinalVideoNode, then queue Stage 2 to produce and save the 1080p final via SaveVideo.
suggestedUseCases: Locking a character’s look and motion using a character sheet before rendering final-quality shots.
Turning a storyboard image into a quick animatic-style draft to validate pacing and composition.
Client reviews: share low-cost 480p drafts for feedback, then finalize to 1080p only when approved.
Batch finalization later: archive draft task IDs and re-render finals on demand without redoing drafts.
Style-matching previous shots by reusing the same references and prompt to maintain continuity.

faqItems.question: What is the draft task ID and why is it important?
faqItems.answer: It’s a handle returned by Seedance 2.5 in Stage 1 that represents the specific draft generation (content and motion). Stage 2 uses this ID to render a 1080p final that matches the approved draft.

faqItems.question: Can I change the prompt or references between draft and final?
faqItems.answer: No—changing inputs requires a new draft. The final render is derived from the draft task ID, so adjust your prompt/references in Stage 1 and regenerate the draft before promoting to final.

faqItems.question: How do I use multiple reference images?
faqItems.answer: Load each image with LoadImage and connect them to ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2’s reference input. Use a character sheet for look consistency and a storyboard for layout, as in the included mech examples.

faqItems.question: What resolutions does this workflow produce?
faqItems.answer: Stage 1 targets a fast 480p preview to iterate cheaply. Stage 2 renders a 1080p final from the same draft task ID, preserving the approved content at higher quality.

a781503cf508.title: MiniMax H3: Image to Video
a781503cf508.description: Turn a starting image into a short, high-quality video clip with MiniMax H3, a unified multimodal model that generates visuals and synchronized audio in a single pass. The workflow takes 1 input image and produces 1 video output, with optional text or reference media to steer motion, style, or sound. Ideal for rapid concept visualization, character-driven animation tests, and creating shareable social media clips with built-in sound design.
a781503cf508.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: convert one image into a short video with synchronized audio using MiniMax H3, auto-scaled resolution, and one-click MP4 export.
a781503cf508.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a single still image into a short, coherent video clip with synchronized stereo audio using MiniMax H3. At its core is the MiniMax H3 generation node (id: 4c314f31-ecda-4b08-ae98-faaba1bf613f), which performs a single forward pass to synthesize both video frames and audio that match the scene. The image you provide through LoadImage sets the subject and overall style; you can optionally add short text guidance inside the MiniMax H3 node to suggest motion, pacing, or mood.

To help the model run efficiently and preserve composition, the workflow routes the input through GetImageSize and a Use Image Size group that keeps aspect ratio intact. ResolutionSelector and ImageScaleToTotalPixels work together to pick a target size that fits MiniMax H3’s recommended megapixel budgets and the multiple-of-32 constraint required by the model. The generated clip is then written out by SaveVideo as a single MP4 containing the video stream (and the model’s generated audio, if enabled), ready for quick review or sharing. Model assets used by the generator include the video VAE (minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors) and the audio VAE (minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors).
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote inside the graph for any inline tips.

Install the MiniMax H3 assets: download minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors and minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors from the provided links, then point the MiniMax H3 node (id: 4c314f31-ecda-4b08-ae98-faaba1bf613f) to these files if paths are required.
Add your starting image via the LoadImage node. The GetImageSize node and Use Image Size group will propagate its aspect ratio to downstream resolution nodes.

Choose a target size: use ResolutionSelector to pick a megapixel budget appropriate for your GPU (for example, 0.4–0.8 MP for mid-tier cards). ImageScaleToTotalPixels will compute width/height in multiples of 32 while keeping your image’s aspect.

Open the MiniMax H3 node and (optionally) enter brief text guidance for motion or mood, set duration and fps, and pick a seed. Keep prompts concise and descriptive (e.g., "slow push-in, gentle breeze, soft ambient music").

Run the graph. Review the MP4 saved by SaveVideo. If you see artifacts or drift, try a lower resolution, a shorter duration, or a new seed; if the motion feels too subtle or too strong, adjust the guidance inside the MiniMax H3 node and rerun.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept visualization for scenes, environments, or product shots with ambient sound.
Character animation tests to explore personality and motion beats from a single pose.
Social media teasers or loops that need built-in sound design without a separate audio pass.
Mood boards and previsualization clips for pitches or storyboards.
Stylized kinetic stills for marketing thumbnails, banners, or hero images made dynamic.

faqItems.question: Which files do I need to download for MiniMax H3 to generate video and audio?
faqItems.answer: Download the MiniMax video VAE (minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors) and audio VAE (minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors) from the links in the workflow notes. In the MiniMax H3 node (id: 4c314f31-ecda-4b08-ae98-faaba1bf613f), set the paths if the node exposes them, then reload models if required.

faqItems.question: How do I pick the right resolution?
faqItems.answer: Use ResolutionSelector with a megapixel budget that matches your GPU VRAM. The ImageScaleToTotalPixels node will output dimensions that are multiples of 32 and preserve your input image’s aspect via GetImageSize. If you encounter OOM errors, lower the MP target or shorten the duration.

faqItems.question: Can I get silent video only?
faqItems.answer: Yes. In the MiniMax H3 node, disable audio generation (if exposed) or ignore the audio output when wiring to SaveVideo. The SaveVideo node will still write the video stream as MP4.

faqItems.question: How do I control motion and style?
faqItems.answer: Your input image anchors style and identity. For motion, add concise guidance in the MiniMax H3 node (e.g., camera moves, tempo, ambience). Keep prompts short and concrete. For stronger effects, try a higher duration or different seed; for more subtle motion, reduce duration or simplify the guidance.

a791f273fc7d.title: FLUX 3 Image: Image Edit
a791f273fc7d.description: Edit or combine up to ten reference images from a text instruction with FLUX 3 Image, referring to them in the prompt as image 1, image 2, and so on. One image is output at any of sixteen aspect ratios and up to 4K, with web and image search grounding on by default. Ideal for character-consistent edits, product and object placement, and multi-reference scene compositing.
a791f273fc7d.metaDescription: Edit or combine up to 10 images with FLUX 3 Image. Prompt with “image 1…10,” choose aspect ratio up to 4K, and save results. Great for consistent edits and compositing.
a791f273fc7d.extendedDescription:
This workflow demonstrates multi-reference image editing and compositing with the FLUX 3 Image model using the Flux3ImageNode. You can load up to ten images with LoadImage, then instruct the model in plain text by referring to them as image 1, image 2, and so on. The node generates a single output at one of sixteen aspect ratios and up to 4K resolution. It’s especially effective for character-consistent edits, product or prop placement, and building scenes that combine elements from several references.

Technically, each LoadImage node feeds the Flux3ImageNode as a reference tensor; the order of these inputs defines the mapping used in your prompt (for example, “replace the background from image 2” or “keep the face from image 1”). In this template, web and image search grounding are enabled by default in the Flux3ImageNode, which can help interpret named entities or fill in context from your prompt; you can disable grounding if you prefer a strictly reference-driven edit. The SaveImageAdvanced node writes the result to disk with flexible filename patterns, while ImageCompare lets you quickly review the generated output against your chosen reference. A MarkdownNote in the graph provides quick reminders on prompt wording and best practices.
howToUse: Open the FLUX 3 Image: Image Edit template in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote for quick guidance.

Load your references with the existing LoadImage nodes (the template includes a sample: fashion_model_green_pilot_coat.png). Add or duplicate LoadImage nodes to supply up to ten inputs, keeping their order consistent with how you’ll reference them in the prompt.

In the Flux3ImageNode, write a clear instruction that references images by index, for example: “Keep the face from image 1. Replace the coat in image 1 with a red leather jacket. Use the background from image 2.”

Choose the target aspect ratio preset in Flux3ImageNode and set a size appropriate for your needs; the workflow supports up to 4K output. Higher resolutions take longer and may consume more resources.
If desired, toggle web/image search grounding in Flux3ImageNode. Leave it on for extra context understanding, or turn it off for a purely reference-driven edit.
Queue or run the graph. Inspect the result with ImageCompare and save with SaveImageAdvanced. Refine your prompt or swap references and rerun until you reach the desired look.
suggestedUseCases: Character-consistent portrait edits across multiple shots by reusing a primary face reference.
Product placement in lifestyle scenes using one image for the product and another for the environment.
Object replacement or wardrobe changes while preserving pose and lighting from the main reference.
Scene compositing that merges backgrounds, subjects, and props from several source images.
Catalog unification, ensuring consistent style or setting across varied product photos.

faqItems.question: How do I reference multiple images in the prompt?
faqItems.answer: Load your images in the order you want, then refer to them in the prompt as “image 1,” “image 2,” etc. For example: “Keep the face from image 1 and use the background from image 2.” The numbering must match the input order to Flux3ImageNode.

faqItems.question: How many inputs and outputs does this workflow support?
faqItems.answer: You can supply up to ten reference images to Flux3ImageNode. The workflow produces one composited output image per run.

faqItems.question: Can I control aspect ratio and resolution?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Pick from the aspect ratio presets in Flux3ImageNode and set a target size up to 4K. For best quality at higher resolutions, use sharp, well-lit references and concise prompts that clearly state what to keep or replace.

faqItems.question: What does web/image search grounding do, and when should I disable it?
faqItems.answer: With grounding enabled (the template default), the model may better interpret named entities or general context from your prompt. Disable grounding if you want the result to rely strictly on your provided references and instructions.

a84541c0018a.title: Image Stitch  2x2 Grid
a84541c0018a.description: Combine four input images into a 2x2 grid. Automatically resizes mismatched images and outputs a single 2048x2048 image.
a84541c0018a.metaDescription: Create a 2x2 image grid from four images, resized and combined into a 2048x2048 output using ComfyUI's Image Stitch workflow.
a84541c0018a.extendedDescription: This ComfyUI workflow is designed to seamlessly combine four separate images into a cohesive 2x2 grid, outputting a single image with a resolution of 2048x2048 pixels. The workflow employs several key nodes to ensure each image fits perfectly within the grid, even if the input images vary in size. The `LoadImage` nodes are used to bring in the individual images, which are then processed through the `ResizeImageMaskNode` to standardize their dimensions. This resizing step is crucial for maintaining the grid's uniformity and ensuring each image aligns correctly. The `ImageStitch` nodes are the core of this workflow, first joining the top-left and top-right images into a single row, and then the bottom-left and bottom-right images into another row. Finally, a third `ImageStitch` node stacks these two rows vertically to complete the grid. The resulting image is saved using the `SaveImage` node. This workflow is particularly useful for creating composite images for presentations, social media posts, or any application where a unified image layout is desired.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and prepare your four images.
Use the `LoadImage` nodes to import each of the four images into the workflow.
The `ResizeImageMaskNode` will automatically adjust any mismatched image sizes to ensure uniformity.
The `ImageStitch` nodes will combine the images into a 2x2 grid, first horizontally, then vertically.
Finally, the `SaveImage` node will output the completed 2048x2048 image grid to your desired location.
suggestedUseCases: Creating Instagram posts with a cohesive visual layout.
Designing mood boards or inspiration grids for creative projects.
Compiling product images into a single promotional image.
Generating comparison grids for side-by-side image analysis.
Crafting digital photo albums or collages.

faqItems.question: What happens if my images are different sizes?
faqItems.answer: The `ResizeImageMaskNode` will automatically resize all images to ensure they fit perfectly within the grid.

faqItems.question: Can I use more than four images?
faqItems.answer: This specific workflow is designed for four images. For more images, you would need to modify the workflow to accommodate additional images and grid configurations.

faqItems.question: What format should my images be in?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports common image formats such as JPEG and PNG. Ensure your images are in a compatible format before loading them.

faqItems.question: Is there a limit to the image resolution I can use?
faqItems.answer: While there is no strict limit, using very high-resolution images may increase processing time. The final output will always be 2048x2048 pixels.

a8749454536e.title: ElevenLabs: Text to Speech
a8749454536e.description: Input text to generate speech with ultra-realistic voices, or upload a voice sample to clone it for synthesis.
a8749454536e.metaDescription: Convert text to speech with realistic voices or clone a voice using ElevenLabs in ComfyUI. Perfect for content creation and voice synthesis.
a8749454536e.extendedDescription: This ComfyUI workflow leverages the power of ElevenLabs to transform written text into ultra-realistic speech. Utilizing nodes like ElevenLabsTextToSpeech and ElevenLabsVoiceSelector, users can either select from a range of preset voices or upload a sample to clone a specific voice for synthesis. The workflow is versatile, allowing for both text-to-speech conversion and voice cloning, making it a powerful tool for content creators, educators, and developers who need high-quality audio outputs. By integrating nodes such as LoadAudio and SaveAudioMP3, users can manage audio inputs and outputs efficiently, ensuring a seamless experience from text input to audio file generation.
howToUse: Load the ComfyUI workflow for ElevenLabs: Text to Speech.
Choose between using a preset voice or creating a voice clone by selecting the appropriate workflow group.
For preset voices, use the ElevenLabsVoiceSelector node to pick your desired voice.
If cloning a voice, upload a voice sample using the LoadAudio node and configure the ElevenLabsInstantVoiceClone node.
Input your text into the ElevenLabsTextToSpeech node.
Save the generated speech using the SaveAudioMP3 or SaveAudioOpus nodes to export your audio file.
suggestedUseCases: Creating voiceovers for video content with realistic human-like voices.
Developing interactive voice applications that require high-quality speech synthesis.
Producing audiobooks or educational materials with customized narrator voices.
Generating personalized voice messages or automated announcements.
Cloning a specific voice for branding or character development in multimedia projects.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow to clone any voice?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can upload a voice sample using the LoadAudio node and use the ElevenLabsInstantVoiceClone node to clone it for synthesis.

faqItems.question: What audio formats are supported for saving the output?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports saving audio in MP3 and Opus formats using the SaveAudioMP3 and SaveAudioOpus nodes, respectively.

faqItems.question: How do I switch between using a preset voice and cloning a voice?
faqItems.answer: Select the appropriate workflow group: 'Option 1: Use Preset Voice' for preset voices or 'Option 2: Create a Voice Clone' for cloning a voice.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to edit the generated speech after synthesis?
faqItems.answer: The workflow focuses on generating speech, but you can export the audio and use external audio editing software for further modifications.

a8d139dba458.title: Veo3: Image to Video
a8d139dba458.description: Generate high-quality 8-second videos from text prompts or images using Google's advanced Veo 3 API. Features audio generation, prompt enhancement, and dual model options for speed or quality.
a8d139dba458.metaDescription: Generate high-quality 8-second videos from text or images using Google's Veo 3 API with options for speed or quality.
a8d139dba458.extendedDescription: The Veo3: Image to Video workflow leverages Google's cutting-edge Veo 3 API to transform static images or text prompts into dynamic, high-quality 8-second videos. This workflow is designed to cater to both speed and quality preferences by offering dual model options. The core component, the Veo3VideoGenerationNode, processes inputs to generate videos with or without accompanying audio. Users can enhance their prompts for more creative outputs, making this workflow versatile for various artistic and commercial applications. Additionally, the workflow includes nodes like SaveVideo to store the generated content and LoadImage for users who prefer starting with an image input. The integration of MarkdownNote and Note nodes ensures that users can document their process and settings for future reference.
howToUse: Load the Veo3: Image to Video workflow in ComfyUI.
Enable the Load Image node using Ctrl+B if starting with an image input.
Enter your text prompt or load an image as the input source.
Select your preferred model option for speed or quality in the Veo3VideoGenerationNode.
Run the workflow to generate your 8-second video.
Use the SaveVideo node to store the generated video on your device.
suggestedUseCases: Creating promotional videos from product images for marketing campaigns.
Generating artistic video content for social media platforms.
Developing educational videos from text descriptions for e-learning modules.
Producing short video clips for digital storytelling projects.
Enhancing static image galleries with dynamic video elements.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow without an image input?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can start with a text prompt instead of an image. The workflow supports both text-to-video and image-to-video generation.

faqItems.question: What are the model options available in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow offers dual model options: one optimized for speed and the other for high-quality video output.

faqItems.question: How can I ensure a secure connection to the API?
faqItems.answer: Ensure you are in a secure network environment that allows access from `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`, and use API Node in website services starting with `https`.

faqItems.question: Is audio generation included in the video output?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the Veo3VideoGenerationNode can generate videos with accompanying audio if desired.

a8d874e28508.title: Flux.2 Klein 9B: Image Extend
a8d874e28508.description: Use the FLUX.2 Klein 9B model to intelligently extend and expand image content. Input an image to generate seamless outpainting and extended compositions.
a8d874e28508.metaDescription: Extend images seamlessly with the Flux.2 Klein 9B model using ComfyUI's outpainting workflow. Perfect for artists and designers.
a8d874e28508.extendedDescription:
The 'Flux.2 Klein 9B: Image Extend' workflow is designed to expand and enhance images using the FLUX.2 Klein 9B model. This workflow excels at outpainting, a technique that extends the boundaries of an image while maintaining its original style and content. It leverages a combination of advanced nodes such as SamplerCustomAdvanced, CLIPLoader, and RandomNoise to generate seamless extensions of the input image. By using the ComfyUI-Color-Matcher and comfyui-kjnodes, the workflow ensures color consistency and style coherence, making it particularly useful for artists and designers looking to create expansive compositions from limited source material.

Technically, the workflow begins by loading an image and encoding it into a latent space using the VAEEncode node. The image is then padded using the ImagePadForOutpaint node to create space for the new content. The Flux2Scheduler and UNETLoader nodes work together to generate new image data that blends naturally with the existing content. The process is guided by the CFGGuider and KSamplerSelect nodes, which help refine the image generation based on the input prompts and conditions. Once the outpainting is complete, the VAEDecode node converts the latent representation back into a visible image format, ready for saving or further editing.
howToUse: Load the 'Flux.2 Klein 9B: Image Extend' workflow in ComfyUI.
Upload your image using the LoadImage node to serve as the base for outpainting.
Adjust the ImagePadForOutpaint settings to define the outpainting area.
Input a prompt in the CLIPTextEncode node, such as 'remove the green part', to guide the outpainting process.
Run the workflow to generate the extended image using the VAEDecode node.
Save the final image with the SaveImage node for further use or sharing.
suggestedUseCases: Creating panoramic images from standard-sized photos.
Extending artwork to fit larger canvas sizes while maintaining style consistency.
Generating additional content for storyboards or concept art.
Enhancing background scenery in digital illustrations.
Filling in missing parts of historical photographs for restoration projects.

faqItems.question: What is outpainting?
faqItems.answer: Outpainting is a technique used to extend the boundaries of an image by generating new content that blends seamlessly with the existing image.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow with any image?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can use this workflow with any image, but results may vary based on the image's complexity and the prompt provided.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow maintain color consistency?
faqItems.answer: The workflow uses the ComfyUI-Color-Matcher node to ensure that the colors of the extended areas match those of the original image.

faqItems.question: What prompts work best for this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Prompts that clearly describe the desired changes or extensions, such as 'extend the horizon' or 'remove the green part', tend to yield the best results.

a8ef15a4ae2c.title: Recraft: Crisp Upscale Image Restoration
a8ef15a4ae2c.description: Upload a low-resolution or noisy image to restore and upscale. Generate a high-resolution output with enhanced details, reduced artifacts, and preserved natural look.
a8ef15a4ae2c.metaDescription: Restore and upscale images with Recraft: Crisp Upscale Image Restoration for enhanced details and reduced artifacts.
a8ef15a4ae2c.extendedDescription:
The 'Recraft: Crisp Upscale Image Restoration' workflow is designed to transform low-resolution or noisy images into high-quality, high-resolution outputs. This workflow leverages the Recraft model, renowned for its ability to enhance image details while minimizing artifacts, thus preserving the natural look of the original image. The process begins with the LoadImage node, which imports the image into the workflow. The RecraftCrispUpscaleNode then processes the image, applying sophisticated algorithms to upscale and refine the image quality. Finally, the SaveImage node outputs the enhanced image, ready for use.

This workflow is particularly useful for applications where image quality is paramount, such as in digital art restoration, professional photography, or any scenario requiring high-resolution visuals. By utilizing the ImageCompare node, users can assess the before and after states of their images, ensuring that the enhancements meet their expectations. The MarkdownNote node provides a space for users to document their workflow process or any specific adjustments made, facilitating easy replication or sharing of results.
howToUse: Load the Recraft: Crisp Upscale Image Restoration workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadImage node to upload your low-resolution or noisy image (ensure it's under 5MB and 2048×2048 resolution).
Configure the RecraftCrispUpscaleNode to apply desired enhancement settings.
Run the workflow to process the image and upscale it using the Recraft model.
Compare the original and enhanced images using the ImageCompare node.
Save the high-resolution output with the SaveImage node.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing digital art for print or display.
Restoring old photographs with improved clarity.
Improving image quality for professional photography portfolios.
Upscaling images for use in high-resolution video projects.
Refining images for e-commerce product listings.

faqItems.question: What image formats are supported?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports standard image formats such as JPEG and PNG. Ensure your image is under 5MB and within 2048×2048 resolution.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the level of detail enhancement?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the RecraftCrispUpscaleNode allows you to configure enhancement settings to suit your specific needs.

faqItems.question: How can I compare the original and enhanced images?
faqItems.answer: Use the ImageCompare node to view side-by-side comparisons of the original and upscaled images.

faqItems.question: Is there a way to document changes made in the workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the MarkdownNote node can be used to document any adjustments or notes about the workflow process.

a8f813117159.title: Wan2.1 SCAIL
a8f813117159.description: One-Touch SCAIL Pose Control based on the composition of the Reference Image
a8f813117159.metaDescription: Transfer video pose to images with Wan2.1 SCAIL in ComfyUI, preserving original composition for dynamic animations.
a8f813117159.extendedDescription:
The Wan2.1 SCAIL workflow in ComfyUI is designed to seamlessly transfer motion and pose information from a video source onto a reference image, while maintaining the original composition of the image. This is achieved using the Wan2.1 SCAIL model, which excels in adapting pose data to fit the proportions and framing of the reference image. The workflow utilizes several custom nodes, including ComfyUI-WanAnimatePreprocess and ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper, to preprocess and wrap video data efficiently. These nodes work in conjunction with the comfyui-scail-pose node, which is responsible for the precise scaling and alignment of pose data. By leveraging these tools, users can create dynamic animations that preserve the aesthetic qualities of the original reference image.

This workflow is particularly useful for applications that require high fidelity in pose transfer, such as creating animated sequences from static images or enhancing video content with consistent stylistic elements. The integration of nodes like LoadImage, SaveVideo, and LoadVideo ensures a smooth workflow from input to output, allowing users to easily import their media, apply the SCAIL technique, and export the final animated video. This makes the workflow not only technically robust but also user-friendly, providing a one-touch solution for complex pose control tasks.
howToUse: Load the Wan2.1 SCAIL workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadVideo node to import your source video containing the desired motion and pose.
Import your reference image using the LoadImage node.
Configure the ComfyUI-WanAnimatePreprocess node to preprocess the video data.
Apply the comfyui-scail-pose node to transfer the pose onto the reference image.
Export the final animation using the SaveVideo node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating animated sequences from static images for digital art projects.
Enhancing video content with consistent stylistic elements by transferring poses.
Developing promotional videos where specific poses need to be maintained across different scenes.
Animating character designs for video games or simulations.
Producing educational content where visual consistency is crucial.

faqItems.question: What types of videos work best with the Wan2.1 SCAIL workflow?
faqItems.answer: Videos with clear and distinct motion patterns are ideal, as the workflow relies on accurately capturing and transferring pose data.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow with any image format?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the LoadImage node supports various image formats, allowing flexibility in choosing your reference image.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to adjust the intensity of the pose transfer?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the comfyui-scail-pose node allows for adjustments in pose scaling and alignment to match your desired intensity.

faqItems.question: How can I ensure the final video maintains high quality?
faqItems.answer: Ensure your source video and reference image are of high resolution, and configure the SaveVideo node to export in a high-quality format.

a9241caf70ac.title: Character Portrait Relighting
a9241caf70ac.description: Upload a portrait of your character and create multiple cinematic lighting conditions while maintaining character consistency.
a9241caf70ac.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Relight a character portrait into cinematic variants using GeminiImage2Node with the Nano Banana Pro model—fast, consistent identity.
a9241caf70ac.extendedDescription:
Character Portrait Relighting is a compact ComfyUI workflow that takes a single portrait and renders it under different, cinematic lighting conditions while keeping the character’s identity consistent. It uses three nodes end-to-end: LoadImage to ingest your source portrait, GeminiImage2Node to perform image-to-image relighting through an external API, and SaveImage to write the results. The workflow is configured to run the Nano Banana Pro model inside GeminiImage2Node, which is well-suited for photoreal portrait work.

Technically, the relighting happens by conditioning the generation on your uploaded image plus a text prompt that describes the lighting setup you want (for example: "soft key light from camera-left, warm rim light, low-fill, filmic contrast"). GeminiImage2Node sends the image and prompt to the API, returning a relit image that preserves pose and facial structure based on the input. You can keep identity tight by favoring higher image-to-image preservation (often exposed as a strength or guidance setting). To produce multiple looks from the same portrait, duplicate GeminiImage2Node (each with a different lighting prompt) and route them all from the same LoadImage, then save each result with its own label via SaveImage.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure GeminiImage2Node is installed and authorized (set your API key per the node’s instructions). In GeminiImage2Node, select the Nano Banana Pro model.
Load your source portrait with the LoadImage node. Use a clean, front-facing or 3/4 view image with good detail; higher resolution inputs generally yield better results.

Open GeminiImage2Node and enter a precise lighting prompt (e.g., "Rembrandt lighting, warm key from left, cool rim from right, soft fill, cinematic contrast"). Set the image preservation/strength so features stay consistent; set a seed if you want repeatable outputs.

To generate multiple lighting looks in one run, duplicate GeminiImage2Node (and a corresponding SaveImage) for each lighting prompt. Connect each GeminiImage2Node’s image input to the same LoadImage output.
For each SaveImage node, set a clear filename prefix (e.g., relight_rembrandt, relight_rimlight) and choose your output directory. Connect each GeminiImage2Node output to its SaveImage.
Queue the workflow. Review results, then adjust prompts or the preservation/strength setting to tighten identity or add drama (harder shadows, stronger rim) and re-queue as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Previsualizing portrait lighting setups for photo or film shoots (key/fill/rim variations) without reshooting.
Creating consistent character sheets for games/animation with multiple moods from the same face.
Marketing and social assets: fast A/B testing of headshot lighting for different platforms or campaigns.
Concept art lighting studies (no re-sculpting or repainting required) while preserving core likeness.
Storyboards and pitch decks needing fast, cinematic portrait variants from a fixed character.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow keep the character’s identity consistent?
faqItems.answer: GeminiImage2Node performs image-to-image generation conditioned on your uploaded portrait. Keep a higher image-preservation/strength setting, avoid prompts that describe changes to facial features or makeup, and start from a clean, well-lit input. Using a fixed seed also helps repeatability.

faqItems.question: What resolution do I get back?
faqItems.answer: By default, the output matches the resolution returned by the API for the selected model (often similar to the input). SaveImage writes exactly the resolution produced by GeminiImage2Node. If the node exposes size controls, set them there before running.

faqItems.question: Do I need a powerful GPU to run this?
faqItems.answer: No. GeminiImage2Node calls an external API, so heavy compute runs remotely. ComfyUI orchestrates the request and saves the results. A local GPU is not required for this workflow.

faqItems.question: Can I relight only parts of the image (e.g., keep background unchanged)?
faqItems.answer: This minimal workflow doesn’t include masking. You can often constrain changes with careful prompting, but for precise control consider extending the graph with masking/inpainting steps or pre-masking your input before LoadImage.

a9294d9380a6.title: Image Upscale: Traditional Interpolation
a9294d9380a6.description: Upload an image and select an interpolation method. Upscale the image using traditional algorithms for faster processing with minimal detail changes.
a9294d9380a6.metaDescription: Efficiently upscale images using traditional interpolation methods with this ComfyUI workflow. Ideal for fast processing with minimal detail changes.
a9294d9380a6.extendedDescription: This ComfyUI workflow focuses on upscaling images using traditional interpolation methods, providing a balance between speed and quality. The workflow employs a series of nodes, starting with 'LoadImage' to import the original image. The 'ImageScaleBy' node is then used to upscale the image by a specified factor, utilizing traditional interpolation algorithms such as bilinear or bicubic. These methods are known for their efficiency and ability to preserve the overall look of the image without introducing significant artifacts. Finally, the 'SaveImage' node allows you to export the upscaled image, while the 'ImageCompare' node can be used to evaluate the differences between the original and upscaled images. This workflow is particularly useful for users who need quick image enlargement without the computational overhead of AI-based methods.
howToUse: Load your image into the workflow using the 'LoadImage' node.
Select the 'ImageScaleBy' node and choose your preferred interpolation method (e.g., bilinear, bicubic).
Specify the scale factor to determine how much larger the image should be.
Use the 'SaveImage' node to export the upscaled image to your desired location.
Optionally, utilize the 'ImageCompare' node to visually compare the original and upscaled images.
Review the results and adjust the scale factor or interpolation method if necessary for optimal quality.
suggestedUseCases: Quickly enlarging images for presentations or reports where processing time is critical.
Upscaling images for web use where minimal detail change is acceptable.
Preparing images for print with traditional methods to maintain a natural look.
Creating larger versions of digital artwork for display without AI-induced artifacts.

faqItems.question: What interpolation methods are available in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports traditional interpolation methods such as bilinear and bicubic, which are efficient and maintain the image's natural appearance.

faqItems.question: How does this workflow differ from AI-based upscaling?
faqItems.answer: This workflow uses traditional algorithms, which are faster and require less computational power, whereas AI-based methods often provide more detail but at a higher processing cost.

faqItems.question: Can I compare the original and upscaled images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can use the 'ImageCompare' node to visually assess the differences between the original and the upscaled images.

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for all types of images?
faqItems.answer: While it works well for most images, the results may vary depending on the image's original quality and the selected interpolation method.

a94f1664e753.title: Video Upscale: Wan 2.2 Creative
a94f1664e753.description: Upload a video and upscale it to a higher resolution with Wan 2.2
a94f1664e753.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: upscale short videos with Wan 2.2. Load, set a 64-divisible resolution, tune detail/denoise, preview, and export a sharper clip.
a94f1664e753.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow upscales short video clips to higher resolutions using the Wan 2.2 model. It loads your source clip with LoadVideo, extracts frame data, fps, and (optionally) audio via GetVideoComponents, and then routes each frame through a Wan 2.2 upscaler node (ID e0ef1fc8-f374-4aa1-8965-c7a9efc7a0f0). A ResolutionSelector block helps you choose valid target sizes, and the final video is reconstructed with CreateVideo and written to disk using SaveVideo. ImageFromBatch is used in the Before vs After Comparison group to quickly preview frames side-by-side.

Technically, the pipeline operates frame-by-frame: frames are decoded, upscaled with Wan2.2 (with controls for detail and denoise strength in the Utility Video Upscale group), and then re-encoded to a video using the original fps and (if connected) audio. Because Wan 2.2 requires dimensions divisible by 64, the Target Resolution group guides you toward valid sizes (for example, 1088 instead of 1080, or 3840×2176 instead of 3840×2160) to avoid model/runtime errors. The workflow is optimized for short sequences—up to about 121 frames—as both clip length and target resolution are gated by your available VRAM.

This is especially useful when you need sharper, cleaner deliverables from lower-resolution sources while keeping control over how much detail Wan 2.2 invents versus preserves. By dialing denoise lower, you’ll retain more of the original look; by increasing detail, you can push for crisper textures. The Before vs After Comparison group lets you validate results on representative frames before committing to a full render, and CreateVideo ensures the upscaled frames are rebuilt with the correct timing (fps) and, when connected, the original audio.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the Load Video and Utility Video Upscale groups.
In Load Video, select your source file with LoadVideo. GetVideoComponents will expose frames, fps, and (if present) audio.
Open Target Resolution and pick your output size with ResolutionSelector. Ensure width and height are divisible by 64 (e.g., 1920×1088 for FHD or 3840×2176 for 4K).
In Utility Video Upscale, set Wan 2.2 parameters (e.g., detail intensity and denoise strength). Keep clips under ~121 frames for reliability and VRAM headroom.
Use the Before vs After Comparison group (ImageFromBatch) to preview representative frames. Adjust resolution or denoise/detail if you see over-sharpening or flicker.
Queue/Run the graph. CreateVideo rebuilds the upscaled clip using the original fps and (if connected) audio, and SaveVideo writes the result to disk.
suggestedUseCases: Upscale 1080p screen recordings to crisp FHD or 4K for tutorials and product demos.
Sharpen mobile-captured B-roll for social posts while preserving original timing and audio.
Improve archival or legacy 720p footage for modern displays with controlled denoise.
Enhance gameplay clips to higher resolutions for highlight reels.
Prepare clean upscaled inserts for video edits where source footage is soft or compressed.

faqItems.question: What’s the maximum clip length I can upscale?
faqItems.answer: This workflow targets short clips—about 121 frames maximum with Wan 2.2—due to model and VRAM limits. For longer content, split your video into segments under this threshold and process them sequentially.

faqItems.question: Why must width and height be divisible by 64?
faqItems.answer: Wan 2.2 operates on internal tile sizes that require 64-divisible dimensions. Use the ResolutionSelector to choose valid sizes (e.g., 1088 instead of 1080, 2176 instead of 2160) to avoid errors or misalignment.

faqItems.question: How do I reduce flicker or over-sharpening across frames?
faqItems.answer: Lower the detail parameter and/or increase denoise slightly in the Utility Video Upscale group. Lower denoise preserves the source look; higher denoise and aggressive detail can introduce more synthetic texture differences between frames.

faqItems.question: Does the workflow keep my original audio and frame rate?
faqItems.answer: Yes. GetVideoComponents provides fps and audio from the source. If those outputs are connected into CreateVideo, the saved result will maintain the original timing and include the audio track.

faqItems.question: I’m hitting out-of-memory (VRAM) errors. What should I change?
faqItems.answer: Reduce the target resolution, shorten the clip (fewer frames), or both. Higher resolutions and longer sequences require significantly more VRAM with frame-by-frame upscaling.

a9f66528e0d7.title: Kling O3: FLF2V
a9f66528e0d7.description: Upload reference images or specify start and end frames. Generate a video with precise semantic control, longer duration, and improved narrative coherence.
a9f66528e0d7.metaDescription: Create coherent, semantically controlled videos with Kling O3: FLF2V, using reference images or frame specifications for enhanced storytelling.
a9f66528e0d7.extendedDescription: The Kling O3: FLF2V workflow is designed to generate videos with precise semantic control and enhanced narrative coherence. This workflow leverages the Kling O3 model, which is known for its ability to maintain consistency across frames while allowing for detailed control over the video’s storyline. By using nodes such as SaveVideo, LoadImage, and BatchImagesNode, users can upload reference images to guide the video's context or specify start and end frames for a structured narrative. The KlingOmniProFirstLastFrameNode is particularly crucial as it facilitates the seamless transition between frames, ensuring that the narrative flow remains uninterrupted. This makes the workflow especially useful for creating longer-duration videos where maintaining thematic consistency is essential.
howToUse: Load the Kling O3: FLF2V workflow into ComfyUI.
Upload up to 6 reference images via the LoadImage node, or specify start and end frames using the KlingOmniProFirstLastFrameNode.
Adjust the BatchImagesNode settings to define the sequence and duration of your video.
Use the Note node to annotate any specific instructions or narrative elements you want to include.
Run the workflow to generate your video, and use the SaveVideo node to export the final output.
suggestedUseCases: Creating narrative-driven videos for storytelling or educational purposes.
Producing marketing videos that require precise thematic consistency.
Developing video content for social media with a coherent storyline.
Generating training videos where semantic control is crucial for clarity.
Crafting artistic video projects that require detailed narrative guidance.

faqItems.question: Can I use both reference images and end_frame specifications simultaneously?
faqItems.answer: No, you must choose between using reference images or specifying start and end frames for the workflow.

faqItems.question: What is the maximum number of reference images I can upload?
faqItems.answer: You can upload up to 6 reference images to guide the context of your video.

faqItems.question: How does the KlingOmniProFirstLastFrameNode enhance video coherence?
faqItems.answer: The KlingOmniProFirstLastFrameNode ensures smooth transitions between frames, maintaining narrative coherence throughout the video.

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for short videos?
faqItems.answer: While it can be used for short videos, the workflow is optimized for longer durations where narrative coherence is more critical.

aa0ea76f6bcd.title: Image Upscale: Wan 2.2 Two-Stage
aa0ea76f6bcd.description: Upload an image and set a resize factor. Generate an AI prompt from your image and upscale it in two controlled stages to enhance detail and fidelity.
aa0ea76f6bcd.metaDescription: Two-stage ComfyUI upscaler using Wan2.2. Auto-generate a prompt from your image, then upscale in coarse and fine passes to maximize detail and fidelity.
aa0ea76f6bcd.extendedDescription:
This two-stage ComfyUI workflow turns a low- or mid-resolution image into a high-fidelity result using the Wan2.2 diffusion model in controlled image-to-image mode. After you LoadImage, GeminiNodeV3 analyzes the picture and generates a concise descriptive prompt that conditions Wan2.2 during upscaling. The pipeline then runs in two passes inside the Image Controlled Upscale group: a coarse first pass to establish structure at a larger size, followed by a fine second pass to restore and enhance details while keeping the original look.

Stage 1 and Stage 2 are implemented with the custom upscaler nodes (8c62a455-6744-43c8-9352-543905ed4db7 and 058e194e-5740-4f04-a9ca-7c741daecfcc), which accept your resize factor, denoise strength, and sampler steps. Author notes provide practical ranges: use 0.20–0.40 denoise for a more creative, coarse pass and 0.10–0.20 for detail-preserving refinement; 25 steps for quick results, or 50+ for maximum quality. PreviewAny gives you live feedback, ImageCompare shows side-by-side before/after in the Image Compare group, and SaveImage exports the final output. A MarkdownNote inside the workflow summarizes the guidance so you can quickly dial in the right settings for different images.

This iterative approach is especially effective for AI-generated images or stylized art that benefit from prompt-guided reconstruction. By pairing auto-prompting (GeminiNodeV3) with Wan2.2’s image-to-image strengths, the workflow preserves identity while recovering edges, textures, and fine details that simple pixel upscalers can miss.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then open the MarkdownNote to review recommended settings.
Use LoadImage to select your source image and set a resize factor (e.g., 2x–4x for Stage 1; you can refine smaller in Stage 2).
Let GeminiNodeV3 analyze the image to auto-generate a conditioning prompt. Optionally edit or replace this prompt if you want a specific style.
Configure Stage 1 (coarse) denoise strength around 0.20–0.40 and choose steps: 25 for quick results or 50+ for higher quality.
Configure Stage 2 (fine) with a lower denoise strength around 0.10–0.20 and a modest additional resize (or keep scale 1.0 if you only want detail refinement).
Run the graph. Use PreviewAny to check intermediate outputs, ImageCompare to view original vs upscaled, and SaveImage to export the final image.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing AI-generated artwork while preserving composition and style.
Upscaling product shots for e-commerce listings without over-smoothing textures.
Improving clarity in anime, manga, and line art while keeping clean edges.
Reviving low-res social media images or portraits with controlled detail recovery.
Preparing illustrations or concept art for print with prompt-guided refinement.

faqItems.question: What does the two-stage process improve compared to a single upscale?
faqItems.answer: Stage 1 establishes structure at a larger size with a higher denoise strength, while Stage 2 uses a lower denoise to restore fine details and reduce artifacts. Splitting the process helps Wan2.2 re-synthesize textures more faithfully than a single aggressive pass.

faqItems.question: What do the denoise values (0.10–0.40) control?
faqItems.answer: They control how much the diffusion model can deviate from the input image. Higher denoise (0.20–0.40) allows more creative reinterpretation—useful for the coarse pass. Lower denoise (0.10–0.20) preserves identity and fine details—ideal for the refinement pass.

faqItems.question: Can I skip the auto-generated prompt from GeminiNodeV3?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The GeminiNodeV3 output is optional conditioning. You can edit or replace it with your own prompt if you want a specific style or to fine-tune how Wan2.2 interprets the image during upscaling.

faqItems.question: How should I pick the resize factor and steps?
faqItems.answer: Start with 2x–4x in Stage 1 at 25–50 steps, then refine in Stage 2 with 1.0–1.5x and lower denoise. If you see over-smoothing or drift, reduce Stage 1 denoise or steps. For maximum quality, use 50+ steps, but expect longer runtimes.

aa132af071d4.title: Ideogram 4.5: Image Edit
aa132af071d4.description: Generate edited or combined images from a text prompt and up to five input images using Ideogram 4.5, where image 1 is the image to edit and images 2-5 are references for design, material, or colour. Canvas size, quality level, and seed are adjustable, and one image is output. Ideal for product and outfit swaps, applying a reference design or palette to an existing photo, and recomposing a shot into a different aspect ratio.
aa132af071d4.metaDescription: Edit images with Ideogram 4.5 using prompts, bounding boxes, and up to 5 images. Control canvas, quality, and seed; preview, compare, and save polished results.
aa132af071d4.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates localized image editing and style transfer using Ideogram 4.5. You provide one primary image to edit (image 1) and up to four additional reference images (images 2–5) to guide design, material, or color. The CreateBoundingBoxes node lets you draw regions to change and label them with short captions like "remove it" or "make it blue velvet." The BuildJsonPromptIdeogram node assembles your global text prompt, box annotations, canvas size/aspect ratio, quality level, seed, and any reference images into a structured payload for the IdeogramEditApi node.

Under the hood, IdeogramEditApi calls the Ideogram model to apply your instructions, constrained by the bounding boxes and informed by the references. PreviewAny shows the generated result, ImageCompare provides a side-by-side with your original, and SaveImageAdvanced saves the final image with organized filenames/metadata. The workflow is ideal for product recolors, outfit swaps, applying a reference pattern or palette to an existing photo, or recomposing a shot into a new aspect ratio—while keeping direct control over what changes through precise bounding boxes. A MarkdownNote in the graph includes quick tips and a link for enabling Nodes2.0 if you don’t see the editor.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI. If nodes don’t appear, enable Nodes2.0 (see the MarkdownNote in the graph).

Load your main image to edit (image 1) with LoadImage. Optionally load up to four reference images (images 2–5) for style, material, or color guidance. The sample asset interior_orange_sofa.png is provided for testing.
Use CreateBoundingBoxes on the main image to draw tight boxes around areas you want changed. Add short, clear captions per box (e.g., "remove it", "change to teal", "swap to denim texture").

Open BuildJsonPromptIdeogram and write a concise global prompt describing the goal (e.g., "Apply the first reference’s fabric and the second reference’s color to the sofa."). Set canvas size/aspect ratio, choose quality level, and fix a seed for repeatability.
Run IdeogramEditApi to generate the edit. Inspect the output with PreviewAny and compare against the original using ImageCompare. If needed, refine box placement, captions, or prompt and re-run.
When satisfied, export with SaveImageAdvanced, customizing the filename pattern, output directory, and metadata options.
suggestedUseCases: Product recolor or material swap: Apply a brand palette or a fabric reference to an existing catalog photo.
Outfit or accessory swap: Transfer patterns, materials, or colors from references onto garments in a model photo.
Interior styling: Re-skin sofas, rugs, or decor using design references while preserving room lighting and layout.
Aspect ratio recomposition: Reframe a shot to 1:1 or 9:16 while retaining subject context and visual continuity.
Mood and palette alignment: Harmonize an image to match a campaign’s color references without full scene regeneration.

faqItems.question: Which images are edited versus used as references?
faqItems.answer: Image 1 is always the edit target. Images 2–5 are references that guide design, materials, or color. They influence the look but are not directly pasted into the scene.

faqItems.question: How should I write bounding box captions for best results?
faqItems.answer: Keep them short and literal (e.g., "remove it", "change to matte black", "replace with marble texture"). Draw tight boxes around only the areas you want changed. Use one action per box to avoid conflicting instructions.

faqItems.question: How do seed, quality, and canvas size affect outputs?
faqItems.answer: A fixed seed stabilizes results for iteration; changing it explores alternatives. Higher quality increases detail and coherence at the cost of speed. Canvas size/aspect ratio controls recomposition—match the original for minimal shift, or set a new ratio to reframe the scene.

faqItems.question: My edit bleeds outside the box or looks inconsistent. What can I adjust?
faqItems.answer: Tighten the bounding box, simplify its caption, and reduce the number of reference images to only what’s essential. Also try raising quality and aligning the canvas size to your source image before changing aspect ratio.

aa1e24da3f2b.title: Video to Lineart / Canny
aa1e24da3f2b.description: Convert a Video to Lineart/Canny for Control Processors
aa1e24da3f2b.metaDescription: Convert videos to lineart or Canny edges for enhanced control processing using ComfyUI's specialized workflow.
aa1e24da3f2b.extendedDescription: This ComfyUI workflow is designed to convert video footage into lineart or Canny edge representations, which are particularly useful for control processors in various applications. By leveraging specific nodes such as the LineArtPreprocessor and VHS_LoadVideo, the workflow efficiently processes each frame of a video to extract its lineart features. The VHS_VideoCombine and VHS_VideoInfo nodes are utilized to manage video data and ensure seamless integration of processed frames back into a cohesive video format. This technique is especially useful for enhancing video content with stylized effects or for preparing data for further processing in machine learning models that require simplified visual inputs.
howToUse: Load the workflow into ComfyUI by importing the provided JSON file.
Use the VHS_LoadVideo node to upload your video file into the workflow.
Configure the LineArtPreprocessor node to set the desired parameters for lineart extraction.
Run the workflow to process the video, converting each frame into lineart or Canny edges.
Use the VHS_VideoCombine node to compile the processed frames back into a video format.
Preview and save the final video output for your intended use.
suggestedUseCases: Creating stylized animations from live-action video footage.
Preparing video data for machine learning models that require simplified visual inputs.
Enhancing video content with artistic lineart effects for creative projects.
Generating edge maps for video-based computer vision applications.
Producing instructional videos with clear, simplified visual representations.

faqItems.question: What types of videos can be processed with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: This workflow can process most standard video formats. Ensure your video is compatible with the VHS_LoadVideo node.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the level of detail in the lineart output?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the LineArtPreprocessor node allows you to configure parameters to control the level of detail in the lineart output.

faqItems.question: How does this workflow handle large video files?
faqItems.answer: The workflow processes each frame individually, which may require significant computational resources for large files. Ensure your system meets the necessary specifications.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to revert the processed video back to its original form?
faqItems.answer: No, the process is not reversible as it simplifies the video into lineart or edge maps, which do not retain the original color and texture information.

aac8b0d80e73.title: SeedVR2: Video Upscaling
aac8b0d80e73.description: Upload a video to upscale and enhance its resolution using the SeedVR2 model for high-definition output.
aac8b0d80e73.metaDescription: Enhance video resolution with SeedVR2: Video Upscaling workflow. Transform low-res videos into high-definition with advanced upscaling techniques.
aac8b0d80e73.extendedDescription:
The SeedVR2: Video Upscaling workflow is designed to enhance the resolution of videos, making them suitable for high-definition displays. It utilizes the SeedVR2 model, which is specifically tailored for video upscaling tasks. The workflow begins by loading a video using the LoadVideo node, which is then processed to extract individual frames through the GetVideoComponents node. These frames are upscaled using the SeedVR2_VideoUpscaler custom node, which leverages advanced algorithms to increase the resolution while maintaining visual quality. The upscaled frames are then reassembled into a video using the CreateVideo node and saved with the SaveVideo node. This process is particularly useful for improving the quality of older or lower-resolution videos, making them appear sharper and more detailed.

Technically, the workflow operates by processing each frame of the video individually, allowing for precise control over the upscaling process. The ImageScale node is used to adjust the resolution settings, which are based on the height of the output video. This ensures that the aspect ratio is preserved, providing a seamless viewing experience. The SeedVR2 model is known for its ability to enhance details without introducing artifacts, making it an excellent choice for video upscaling tasks. By using this workflow, users can transform standard-definition videos into high-definition content, suitable for modern viewing platforms.
howToUse: Load your video into the workflow using the LoadVideo node.
Use the GetVideoComponents node to extract frames from the video.
Apply the SeedVR2_VideoUpscaler node to upscale each frame to the desired resolution.
Reassemble the upscaled frames into a video using the CreateVideo node.
Save the final high-definition video using the SaveVideo node.
suggestedUseCases: Upscaling old family videos to modern high-definition formats.
Enhancing low-resolution video content for streaming platforms.
Improving the quality of surveillance footage for better detail recognition.
Converting standard-definition educational videos to HD for clearer presentations.
Preparing archival footage for high-definition broadcast.

faqItems.question: What resolution settings should I use for optimal results?
faqItems.answer: The resolution setting in the SeedVR2_VideoUpscaler node is based on the height of your output video. Choose a setting that matches your desired output format, such as 1080p or 4K.

faqItems.question: Can I process multiple videos at once?
faqItems.answer: Currently, the workflow is designed to process one video at a time. You can load and upscale each video sequentially.

faqItems.question: Will the upscaling process introduce artifacts?
faqItems.answer: The SeedVR2 model is designed to minimize artifacts while enhancing details. However, results may vary depending on the quality of the original video.

faqItems.question: How long does the upscaling process take?
faqItems.answer: The processing time depends on the length of the video and the chosen resolution. Higher resolutions and longer videos will take more time to process.

ab9d40a74f02.title: Luma Ray 3.2: Video Edit
ab9d40a74f02.description: Edit videos using natural language commands with Luma Ray 3.2, processing one input video and generating an edited output based on your textual instructions.
ab9d40a74f02.metaDescription: Edit and extend videos with natural language using Luma Ray 3.2 in ComfyUI. Load a clip, prompt your changes, preview, save, and optionally extend with generation_id.
ab9d40a74f02.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow demonstrates how to edit an existing video using natural language instructions with Luma Ray 3.2. The core path runs your clip from LoadVideo into LumaRay32VideoEditNode, which sends the video and your text instruction to the Luma backend and returns an edited result plus a generation_id. PreviewAny lets you quickly inspect the output and also exposes that generation_id via a text preview, while SaveVideo writes the edited clip to disk.

A second, grouped path shows how to extend a result so you can continue the look, motion, or scene beyond the original runtime. LumaRay32ExtendVideoNode consumes source_generation_id (wired from the prior edit by default) to synthesize additional frames that stay consistent with the preceding output. If you want to extend from a previous run instead of the current one, disconnect the source_generation_id link and paste the stored generation_id taken from PreviewAny’s "Preview as Text (generation_id)" output. Optional grouped sections in the graph can be enabled by selecting the group and pressing Ctrl+B, as noted by MarkdownNote blocks embedded in the workflow.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then enable the relevant grouped section(s) by selecting the group frame and pressing Ctrl+B (refer to the MarkdownNote hints in the canvas).
In LoadVideo, choose your input clip. Confirm it connects into LumaRay32VideoEditNode.

Open LumaRay32VideoEditNode and enter a clear natural-language instruction describing the edit you want (e.g., overall look/mood, style direction, motion emphasis). If the node exposes extra parameters (like duration caps, strength, or guidance), adjust them as needed.
Run the workflow. Use PreviewAny to check the edited output. If preview text is available, copy the generation_id shown under "Preview as Text (generation_id)" for later use.
Set SaveVideo’s output path and run it (or re-run the graph) to export the edited result to disk.

To extend the result, enable the LumaRay32ExtendVideoNode group. By default it uses the upstream source_generation_id. To extend from a prior run, disconnect that input, paste your saved generation_id into the node, then run to generate the extended segment.
suggestedUseCases: Quickly restyle or adjust the overall look of a clip (mood, lighting, tone) without manual color grading.
Create alternate social cuts by prompting different stylistic directions from the same base footage.
Extend a shot to match music or timing requirements while keeping visual continuity.
Rapid previsualization of creative directions before committing to full post-production.
Generating consistent variations for A/B testing thumbnails, teasers, or short format edits.

faqItems.question: What’s the difference between LumaRay32VideoEditNode and LumaRay32ExtendVideoNode?
faqItems.answer: LumaRay32VideoEditNode applies your natural-language edit to the input video and returns a new, edited clip plus a generation_id. LumaRay32ExtendVideoNode uses a source_generation_id to synthesize additional frames that continue the visuals from the edited result (or from an older run if you paste a saved generation_id).

faqItems.question: How do I extend from a previous session rather than the current run?
faqItems.answer: In the extend section, disconnect the auto-wired source_generation_id. From PreviewAny, copy the value shown under "Preview as Text (generation_id)" from your earlier run, paste it into LumaRay32ExtendVideoNode’s generation_id input, and run the extend node.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key or special setup?
faqItems.answer: This workflow calls Luma Ray 3.2 via its node. Ensure your Luma credentials are configured as required by LumaRay32VideoEditNode (via environment, ComfyUI settings, or node fields, depending on your installation). If authentication is missing or invalid, the node will fail to return results.

faqItems.question: Will audio be preserved?
faqItems.answer: AI video edit/generation nodes often return video-only. If audio is not present in the output, export the edited video and reattach the original or new audio in your NLE. Check the node’s parameters and logs to confirm whether audio passthrough is supported in your setup.

abafa1d4f1f1.title: Wan3.0: Reference to Video
abafa1d4f1f1.description: Generate a video from two reference images using Wan3.0's reference-to-video capability, which produces up to 30 seconds of footage with character consistency and lifelike visuals. Ideal for creating consistent character animations, scene replication from visual references, and producing audiovisual content from static imagery.
abafa1d4f1f1.metaDescription: Turn two reference images into a consistent, lifelike video with Wan3.0 in ComfyUI. Load images, call the API, and save up to 30s MP4 results.
abafa1d4f1f1.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow demonstrates Wan3.0’s reference-to-video generation: starting from two images, it produces a lifelike, up-to-30-second video that preserves character identity and visual style. Two LoadImage nodes bring in your references (for example, a clean subject image and a context/pose or style image). These feed directly into the Wan3ReferenceToVideoApi node, which sends the request to the Wan3.0 service and returns a ready-to-save video. A SaveVideo node then writes the final clip to disk as an MP4.

Technically, the pipeline is lean and reliable: the heavy lifting happens remotely via the Wan3ReferenceToVideoApi node, so your local GPU is not a bottleneck. The MarkdownNote node in the graph includes inline tips and reminders about inputs and expected outputs. Because the generator is reference-driven, the quality and composition of your two images strongly influence identity lock, motion coherence, and background fidelity. Use this when you want consistent character animation from stills, quick scene mocks from storyboards, or product visuals derived from brand imagery.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and review the MarkdownNote for on-canvas instructions.

In the two LoadImage nodes, set your reference files (the template includes input/vortex_shoe.png; replace it and the second reference with your own if desired). Use clear, well-lit images that match your target aspect ratio.

Open the Wan3ReferenceToVideoApi node and add your API credentials or key as required. Configure core settings such as duration (up to 30 seconds) and any available text prompt or style fields the node exposes.
Optionally adjust SaveVideo: set output filename, location, and fps to match your creative intent (e.g., 24 or 30 fps).
Click Queue Prompt (or Render). The API node will submit the job and return the generated clip when ready.
Review the saved MP4. Iterate by refining your references (cleaner subject, better framing), adjusting duration/fps, or tweaking prompt/style settings for improved motion and consistency.
suggestedUseCases: Character animation from a subject portrait plus a style/pose reference for shorts, intros, or story beats.
Product visuals (e.g., a shoe or gadget) animated using a clean product shot and a brand mood or environment image.
Scene replication from storyboard frames to quickly preview motion and continuity.
Social media loops and ads where identity consistency and quick iteration are key.
Concept-to-motion tests for pitching ideas to clients or teammates.

faqItems.question: Do I need two different images, or can I use just one?
faqItems.answer: The workflow is designed for two references to guide identity and style/motion. If you only have a single image, you can feed the same image into both LoadImage nodes, but using two complementary references typically yields better motion and scene coherence.

faqItems.question: How long can the generated video be?
faqItems.answer: Up to 30 seconds, as supported by the Wan3.0 reference-to-video capability. If you need shorter clips, reduce the duration or fps to match your target runtime.

faqItems.question: What image prep leads to the best character consistency?
faqItems.answer: Use a high-quality, well-lit subject image with minimal background clutter. Keep the subject large in frame, avoid motion blur, and try to match the output aspect ratio. For the second reference, choose an image that clearly conveys the desired style, pose, or environment.

faqItems.question: Why did my job fail or return an error?
faqItems.answer: Most failures stem from API issues: missing/invalid credentials, quota limits, or network timeouts. Double-check the Wan3ReferenceToVideoApi node’s key/headers, ensure you have internet access, and review the ComfyUI console/logs for the specific error message. Try shorter durations or smaller resolutions if the service imposes limits.

ac37ba4d362c.title: Flux.2 [Klein] 4B Distilled: Image Edit
ac37ba4d362c.description: The fastest variant in the Klein family. Built for interactive applications, real-time previews, and latency-critical production use cases.
ac37ba4d362c.metaDescription: Fast image editing with Flux.2 Klein for real-time previews and latency-critical applications using ComfyUI.

This ComfyUI workflow, titled 'Flux.2 [Klein] 4B Distilled: Image Edit', is designed to facilitate rapid image editing with a focus on interactive applications and real-time previews. Utilizing the Flux.2 Klein model, this workflow is optimized for latency-critical production environments where speed is paramount. Additionally, it features a 'MarkdownNote' node for documentation and guidance within the workflow itself.

Technically, the workflow leverages the power of the Flux.2 Klein model, known for its efficiency in processing and generating high-quality image edits quickly. The inclusion of the 'Multiple input example' workflow group allows users to toggle between different input configurations, enhancing flexibility and user control. This setup is particularly useful for users who need to make quick adjustments or iterations in a production setting, such as graphic designers or digital artists working under tight deadlines.
howToUse: Load the 'Flux.2 [Klein] 4B Distilled: Image Edit' workflow into ComfyUI.
Use the 'LoadImage' node to import your image file into the workflow.
Adjust the parameters in the '7b34ab90-36f9-45ba-a665-71d418f0df18' node to customize your image edits.
Preview the real-time edits using the interactive interface.
Once satisfied with the edits, use the 'SaveImage' node to export the final image.

suggestedUseCases: Rapid prototyping of image edits for digital marketing campaigns.
Real-time image adjustments during live streaming or broadcast production.
Interactive design sessions where immediate feedback is required.
Editing images for social media posts with quick turnaround times.
