faqItems.question: What makes the Flux.2 Klein model suitable for real-time applications?
faqItems.answer: The Flux.2 Klein model is optimized for speed and efficiency, making it ideal for applications where latency is critical, such as live previews and interactive editing.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for batch processing multiple images?
faqItems.answer: While the workflow is optimized for real-time single image editing, you can adapt it for batch processing by iterating over multiple images using the 'LoadImage' node.

faqItems.question: How do I adjust the image editing parameters?
faqItems.answer: You can adjust the parameters within the '7b34ab90-36f9-45ba-a665-71d418f0df18' node to customize the image edits according to your needs.

faqItems.question: Is there documentation available for understanding subgraphs in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can refer to the [Subgraph docs](https://docs.comfy.org/interface/features/subgraph) for detailed information on how subgraphs function within the workflow.

accb717be9dc.title: Luma Ray 3.2: Text to Video
accb717be9dc.description: Generate cinematic-quality videos from text prompts using Luma Ray 3.2, with optional video extension by providing a generation ID from a previous run. Ideal for creating short film sequences, marketing content, and iterative video refinement.
accb717be9dc.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate text-to-video with Luma Ray 3.2 and extend clips via generation_id. Preview results and save MP4s in a single, modular workflow.
accb717be9dc.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial shows how to generate and iteratively extend text-driven videos using Luma Ray 3.2. The core path uses LumaRay32TextToVideoNode to send your prompt to the Luma API and return a playable clip plus metadata, including a generation_id. PreviewAny provides quick feedback on both the video and text metadata, while SaveVideo writes the final MP4 to disk. A MarkdownNote in the canvas includes quick reminders for first-time setup and tips.

For longer or refined sequences, the LumaRay32ExtendVideoNode uses a source_generation_id to continue motion and style from a prior generation. By default, it’s wired to the upstream LumaRay32TextToVideoNode so you can generate and extend in one run. If you want to extend an older clip, disconnect that link and paste a generation_id surfaced by the PreviewAny node labeled “Preview as Text (generation_id).” The workflow is organized into groups you can toggle with Select + Ctrl-B, making it easy to run just the base generation or just the extension stage.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the Luma Ray 3.2 custom nodes are installed and authenticated (API key or credentials as required by your setup).
Decide which path to run. Select the relevant workflow group (Text to Video or Extend Video) and press Ctrl-B to enable it.

Text-to-video: Open LumaRay32TextToVideoNode, enter your prompt, and adjust any available parameters (for example, duration or size if exposed by your node version). Queue the prompt and use PreviewAny to monitor progress. SaveVideo will write the resulting MP4 to your output folder.

Extend from the current run: Leave the default wiring so LumaRay32ExtendVideoNode receives source_generation_id from the upstream node. Enable the Extend group, queue, and SaveVideo will output the longer clip.

Extend from a previous run: Disconnect the source_generation_id input on LumaRay32ExtendVideoNode, copy the ID from the PreviewAny node labeled “Preview as Text (generation_id)” (or from your saved notes), paste it into the extend node, then queue.
Iterate: Tweak your prompt or parameters and re-run. For longer videos, you can chain multiple extensions by reusing the latest generation_id.
suggestedUseCases: Storyboards and previsualization: Quickly explore camera moves and mood, then extend promising shots.
Social ads and teasers: Generate short, stylized clips and lengthen them to fit platform runtimes.
Cinematic b‑roll and title sequences: Create atmospheric motion shots and iterate until pacing feels right.
Concept reels and mood films: Build a sequence from text prompts and extend selected moments.
Rapid iteration for client reviews: Lock a look with the base clip, then extend or revise without starting over.

faqItems.question: Do I need a Luma account or API key?
faqItems.answer: Yes. These nodes call the Luma Ray 3.2 API. Provide credentials as required by your install (node field, config, or environment). If authentication is missing or invalid, requests will fail.

faqItems.question: Where do I find the generation_id for extending a video?
faqItems.answer: After a successful run, the LumaRay32TextToVideoNode outputs metadata that includes a generation_id. In this workflow, use the PreviewAny node labeled “Preview as Text (generation_id)” to view and copy it.

faqItems.question: Can I extend a video from a previous session?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Disconnect the automatic source_generation_id link on LumaRay32ExtendVideoNode and paste the generation_id from your earlier run. Then enable the Extend group and queue.

faqItems.question: My video didn’t save—what should I check?
faqItems.answer: Confirm SaveVideo is connected to the branch you ran and that its output path is valid. PreviewAny shows results for quick inspection, but only SaveVideo writes the MP4 to disk.

ad315e41d8c2.title: Character Turnaround Sheet Generator
ad315e41d8c2.description: Create orthographic multi-view character turnaround sheet from one reference image, keep consistent character features across front, side and back views, for sci-fi mech and armor character design.
ad315e41d8c2.metaDescription: Create consistent orthographic side and back views from one front reference using GeminiImage2Node in ComfyUI. Perfect for mech armor turnaround sheets.
ad315e41d8c2.extendedDescription:
This workflow generates a clean, orthographic character turnaround (front, side, and back) from a single reference image—ideal for sci‑fi mechs and armor designs. It starts with LoadImage to bring in a front orthographic reference (a sample white_mech_front_ortho.png is included). That image is then passed to GeminiImage2Node, which calls a Google Generative image API and uses your text instructions plus the reference to synthesize additional angles while preserving key features like silhouette, plate layout, decals, and color scheme. SaveImageAdvanced writes each view to disk with predictable filenames so you can assemble them into a final sheet in your design tool. A MarkdownNote in the graph provides inline guidance and prompt tips.

Technically, consistency across views is encouraged by conditioning GeminiImage2Node with the same reference image and carefully worded prompts (e.g., “orthographic side view of the same mech as the reference; match plating, helmet, and markings; no perspective; white background”). Because this template relies on an external API rather than local checkpoints, it’s quick to set up—no model downloads are required—making it a practical tool for concept artists and product designers who need fast, multi‑view explorations of a single design.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and update ComfyUI to the latest version. Ensure GeminiImage2Node is installed and configured with your Gemini/Google image API credentials per the node’s instructions.
In LoadImage, select your front orthographic reference (use the provided white_mech_front_ortho.png to test). Aim for a neutral, centered, no‑perspective image with clean background.

Open GeminiImage2Node and write a precise prompt for the side view, for example: “Orthographic side view of the same mech as the reference. Match armor plates, proportions, decals, and color palette. No perspective. White studio background.” Run the workflow to generate and preview the side view.

Repeat for the back view by adjusting the prompt to “Orthographic back view of the same mech as the reference...” Keep phrasing consistent across runs so features stay aligned. If you get perspective drift, explicitly say “flat orthographic, no lens, no foreshortening.”
Use SaveImageAdvanced to set a clear output path and file naming pattern (e.g., mech_turnaround_side, mech_turnaround_back). Run again to write final images to disk.
Assemble the exported front, side, and back renders into a single turnaround sheet in your image editor (or add a tiling step in ComfyUI if you prefer a one‑page layout).
suggestedUseCases: Sci‑fi mech and powered armor concept turnarounds for game or film pre‑production
Hard‑surface product design sheets (e.g., drones, helmets, tools) for design reviews
Cosplay or prop fabrication references with consistent front/side/back blueprints
Indie game dev character sheets for modeling and rigging handoff
Toy/figure concept art requiring multi‑view packaging or manufacturing references

faqItems.question: Do I need local Stable Diffusion models for this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No. The core generation is handled by GeminiImage2Node via an external Google image API. You just need a valid API configuration; no local checkpoints are required.

faqItems.question: How do I keep features perfectly consistent across views?
faqItems.answer: Use the same reference image every time and keep prompts tightly scoped: specify “orthographic,” “no perspective,” and call out key elements to match (helmet shape, plating, decals, color). If results drift, tighten language (e.g., “exact same chest plate geometry and markings as the reference”) and keep background simple.

faqItems.question: Can this make a single sheet with all views automatically?
faqItems.answer: This template saves each view as a separate file via SaveImageAdvanced. You can assemble them in your editor, or add a tiling/composition step in ComfyUI if you prefer an all‑in‑one sheet.

faqItems.question: Will it work for organic characters or only mechs?
faqItems.answer: It works for both, but hard‑surface designs tend to hold consistency more easily. For organic characters, be extra explicit about proportions, clothing details, and pose (neutral T‑pose, arms down, etc.).

ad33556e4665.title: Video Upscale: WaveSpeed FlashVSR
ad33556e4665.description: Upload a video to upscale it to 720p, 1080p, 2K, or 4K. The workflow enhances detail, reduces artifacts, and ensures consistent motion for a high-quality, natural-looking output.
ad33556e4665.metaDescription: Compare FlashVSR vs WaveSpeed upscaling in ComfyUI—from 720p to 4K. See quality vs speed trade-offs with stable motion to choose the best option for your video.
ad33556e4665.extendedDescription:
This comparison workflow evaluates two upscaling approaches available through the WavespeedFlashVSRNode: a FlashVSR-focused pass versus a WaveSpeed-accelerated pass. Both aim to enhance detail, suppress artifacts, and maintain stable motion while upscaling to 720p, 1080p, 2K, or 4K. The key question it helps answer is whether you should prioritize maximum perceived fidelity (FlashVSR) or faster turnaround with strong quality (WaveSpeed), especially as you push to higher output resolutions.

Methodology is straightforward and controlled: the same input is loaded with LoadVideo, then processed twice through WavespeedFlashVSRNode—first with FlashVSR, then with the WaveSpeed-accelerated mode—keeping the target resolution and all other parameters identical. Outputs are saved with SaveVideo using consistent settings. You can then compare detail retention (skin texture, fabric, line art), artifact suppression (ringing, halos, blockiness), temporal stability (flicker, texture popping), and practical considerations like render time and memory usage. Differences are typically most visible at higher scales (e.g., 4K), on noisy/grainy footage, or in high-motion scenes.
howToUse: Load your source clip with LoadVideo. Verify the clip plays correctly and note its frame rate and duration so you can keep output settings consistent.
In WavespeedFlashVSRNode, select your target resolution (720p, 1080p, 2K, or 4K) and choose the FlashVSR mode. Run the graph and SaveVideo to an output labeled clearly (e.g., myclip_1080p_flashvsr).
Switch the mode in WavespeedFlashVSRNode to the WaveSpeed-accelerated option, keep the same target resolution and other settings, then run again. Save to a second file (e.g., myclip_1080p_wavespeed).
Optionally repeat both passes at another resolution (e.g., 4K) to see how scaling level affects artifacts, sharpness, and runtime.

Compare the two outputs side-by-side. Inspect fine detail (hair, text, edges), look for halos or ringing, and scrub through motion to check for flicker or texture popping. Note render times from the ComfyUI log for a practical speed comparison.
suggestedUseCases: Long-form or high-volume batches where turnaround time matters: validate whether WaveSpeed meets quality needs at 1080p before scaling up.
Film restoration or archival footage where de-noising and artifact suppression are critical: test if FlashVSR provides visibly cleaner, more stable results.
Social content pipelines with tight deadlines: confirm whether WaveSpeed at 720p/1080p delivers acceptable quality for rapid publishing.
Animation and line art: compare edge fidelity and stability across frames to decide which mode preserves lines without shimmer.
Screen captures or UI videos: assess text sharpness and haloing at 2K/4K to pick the mode that balances clarity and speed.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow ensure a fair comparison between FlashVSR and WaveSpeed?
faqItems.answer: It holds all variables constant: the same input from LoadVideo, identical target resolution and node settings in WavespeedFlashVSRNode, and consistent SaveVideo settings. Only the model/mode is changed, so differences you see reflect the approach rather than configuration drift.

faqItems.question: Which mode should I choose for 4K upscaling from a low-resolution source?
faqItems.answer: Start by comparing both at 1080p to gauge noise and artifact control, then test 4K. FlashVSR often suits challenging or noisy footage thanks to stronger artifact suppression, while WaveSpeed may be preferable for cleaner sources or when you need faster delivery. If 4K amplifies artifacts, consider stopping at 1080p or 2K.

faqItems.question: Why do render times and memory usage differ between the two passes?
faqItems.answer: WaveSpeed focuses on faster inference, while a FlashVSR-focused pass prioritizes fidelity. Runtime and VRAM scale with target resolution, clip length, and content complexity. For quicker results, use WaveSpeed at 720p/1080p; for maximum quality on difficult footage, allocate more time and choose FlashVSR.

faqItems.question: How should I judge temporal consistency and motion stability?
faqItems.answer: Scrub through fast motion and complex textures. Look for flicker, edge shimmer, or texture popping between frames. Keep SaveVideo’s frame rate identical across outputs and compare the same timeline segments to assess stability objectively.

ad8614720882.title: Looped Restyler
ad8614720882.description: Upload a starting image and its prompt to generate a looping video from the first to the last frame.
ad8614720882.metaDescription: Create seamless looping videos from images with the Looped Restyler workflow using ComfyUI. Transform static visuals into dynamic loops effortlessly.
ad8614720882.extendedDescription: The 'Looped Restyler' workflow in ComfyUI is designed to transform a static image into a dynamic looping video. By utilizing advanced AI models like Nano Banana, Google Gemini, and Wan2.2, this workflow seamlessly transitions from the first frame of an image to the last, creating a continuous loop. The process begins with loading an initial image and its corresponding prompt, which guides the transformation process. The workflow employs nodes such as LoadImage to import the starting image, and SaveVideo to compile the frames into a video format. The node identified by 3313ce14-acfd-4a9c-9f0c-a1b01147e934 plays a crucial role in generating intermediate frames that ensure a smooth transition between the start and end of the sequence. PreviewImage is used to monitor the progress and make necessary adjustments before finalizing the output.
howToUse: Load the 'Looped Restyler' workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadImage node to upload your starting image and input its prompt.
Configure the node 3313ce14-acfd-4a9c-9f0c-a1b01147e934 to generate intermediate frames for smooth transitions.
Monitor the progress using the PreviewImage node to ensure the loop is seamless.
Once satisfied, use the SaveVideo node to compile and save your looping video.
Review the final output to ensure it meets your expectations.
suggestedUseCases: Creating animated loops for digital art projects.
Generating engaging social media content from static images.
Producing dynamic video backgrounds for websites or presentations.
Developing creative visual effects for film and multimedia projects.
Enhancing storytelling in visual narratives with seamless loops.

faqItems.question: What type of images work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: High-resolution images with clear focal points tend to produce the best results, as they provide more detail for the AI to work with.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the speed of the looping video?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can adjust the frame rate in the SaveVideo node to control the speed of the loop.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to add audio to the looping video?
faqItems.answer: This workflow focuses on visual output. However, you can add audio using video editing software after exporting the video.

faqItems.question: How can I ensure the loop is seamless?
faqItems.answer: Use the PreviewImage node to check transitions between frames and adjust parameters in the 3313ce14-acfd-4a9c-9f0c-a1b01147e934 node for smoother results.

adca306765ce.title: LTX-2.3: Image Audio to Video
adca306765ce.description: Upload an image and an audio file to generate a high-quality video with synchronized lip movements using LTX-2.3.
adca306765ce.metaDescription: Create a lip-synced talking video from a single image and audio using LTX-2.3 in ComfyUI. Load image/audio, generate frames, and export an MP4.
adca306765ce.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single image and a voice recording into a lip-synced talking video using the LTX-2.3 model. You load a portrait with LoadImage and provide speech via LoadAudio or capture it live with RecordAudio. Both streams feed the LTX-2.3 generator node (98ee9e5b-467b-40aa-a534-36033f27d0b4), which synthesizes a sequence of frames where the subject speaks in time with the audio. The resulting frames are encoded to an MP4 using SaveVideo.

Under the hood, LTX-2.3 conditions on the visual identity from your reference image and the temporal features of the provided audio to drive mouth shapes and subtle facial motions over time. The node typically exposes settings like output resolution and FPS, and many builds also include a seed for reproducibility and an optional text prompt to guide motion or style. The MarkdownNote in the graph documents quick tips and links to the official Lightricks model repositories so you can download the required weights.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the LTX-2.3 weights are installed per the Lightricks repo/Hugging Face instructions. Restart ComfyUI so the LTX-2.3 node is available.
Open LoadImage and choose a clear, front-facing portrait where the mouth is fully visible. Square or centered crops generally produce the most stable results.
Provide audio: either drop in a file with LoadAudio (clean, speech-focused audio preferred) or record directly with RecordAudio. Keep background noise minimal.

Configure the LTX-2.3 generator node (98ee9e5b-467b-40aa-a534-36033f27d0b4): set FPS (e.g., 24 or 25), output resolution (match your image or a square size), and choose a seed if you want repeatable output. If a prompt field is available, describe desired motion (e.g., slight head turns, natural blinks).

Connect the node outputs as shown in the workflow so the generated frames feed into SaveVideo. If your SaveVideo build supports audio muxing, connect the same audio there; otherwise, you’ll add audio in post.

Click Queue Prompt to run. When complete, SaveVideo will write an MP4 of the synthesized talking head. Review lip sync and motion; adjust FPS, resolution, prompt, or image crop for refinements and re-run.
suggestedUseCases: Voiceover announcements where a brand mascot or presenter speaks a short script from a single still image.
Educational explainers with a talking avatar created from a photo of a host or character.
News-style shorts or social clips generated quickly from a portrait and a recorded message.
Localization or drafts of dubbed content where you need a fast lip-synced visual for review.
Animated profile intros or podcast promos using a host’s image and teaser audio.

faqItems.question: Do I need a specific image type for best results?
faqItems.answer: Use a front-facing portrait with good lighting and the mouth unobstructed (no hands, mics, or heavy objects covering lips). Center the face and use a reasonable resolution (e.g., 512–1024 px on the short side). Avoid extreme angles and busy backgrounds.

faqItems.question: What audio format works best?
faqItems.answer: Clean, speech-focused audio produces the most accurate mouth movements. WAV or high-bitrate MP3 typically work; mono voice tracks are preferred. Minimize reverb and background noise to improve alignment and realism.

faqItems.question: Will the exported video include the audio track?
faqItems.answer: That depends on your SaveVideo node build. Some variants can mux audio; others export a silent MP4. If yours is silent, combine the output video with the same audio in an editor or a separate muxing step.

faqItems.question: How can I improve lip sync and overall quality?
faqItems.answer: Start with a clear, centered portrait and clean audio. Match FPS to your target platform (e.g., 24–30). If a prompt field is available, describe subtle motions (blinks, small head turns) to avoid a static look. Try different seeds for variety, and consider cropping the face tighter if the mouth region appears too small.

ae12a241076c.title: Relight Composited Product
ae12a241076c.description: Upload a composited image of your product, draw a mask in the mask editor and relight your product into the scene.
ae12a241076c.metaDescription: Relight your composited product images seamlessly with this ComfyUI workflow. Perfect for enhancing product photos with realistic lighting.
ae12a241076c.extendedDescription: The 'Relight Composited Product' workflow in ComfyUI is designed to enhance product images by allowing users to adjust the lighting of a specific area within a composited image. This is particularly useful for product photographers and e-commerce businesses looking to create visually appealing images that stand out. The workflow leverages the Qwen-Image-Edit model, known for its advanced image editing capabilities, to achieve realistic lighting adjustments. By using the 'comfyui-inpaint-cropandstitch' custom node, users can precisely target areas of the image to relight, ensuring seamless integration with the existing scene. This workflow is beneficial for improving the visual aesthetics of product images without the need for complex photo editing software.
howToUse: Load your composited product image into the ComfyUI interface using the LoadImage node.
Use the mask editor to draw a mask over the area of the product you wish to relight.
Apply the Qwen-Image-Edit model to adjust the lighting within the masked area.
Utilize the comfyui-inpaint-cropandstitch node to ensure the relighted area blends seamlessly with the rest of the image.
Save the edited image using the SaveImage node to complete the process.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing product images for e-commerce websites to attract more customers.
Adjusting lighting in product photos for marketing materials.
Creating consistent lighting across a series of product images for a catalog.
Improving the visual appeal of product images for social media promotions.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for non-product images?
faqItems.answer: While designed for product images, this workflow can be adapted for any composited image where specific relighting is needed.

faqItems.question: What if the relighted area doesn't blend well with the image?
faqItems.answer: Ensure that the mask is accurately drawn and make use of the comfyui-inpaint-cropandstitch node to achieve a seamless blend.

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for beginners?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow is user-friendly and does not require advanced photo editing skills, making it accessible for beginners.

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported for the input image?
faqItems.answer: The LoadImage node supports common formats like JPEG and PNG, ensuring compatibility with most image files.

aeb71e383642.title: Qwen3.5: Text Generation
aeb71e383642.description: Use the Qwen3.5 model to analyze an input image and generate descriptive text prompts. This workflow performs image captioning and reverse prompt engineering.
aeb71e383642.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Use Qwen3.5 to caption images and auto-generate reverse-engineered prompts with TextGenerate, from model setup to exporting results.
aeb71e383642.extendedDescription:
This workflow demonstrates how to use Qwen3.5 inside ComfyUI to analyze an image and generate descriptive text that doubles as ready-to-use prompts. It performs both image captioning and reverse prompt engineering: you provide an image via LoadImage, and the TextGenerate node, powered by Qwen3.5, returns structured descriptions or prompt candidates you can paste into your image-generation pipelines.

Technically, the CLIPLoader node is pointed at the Qwen3.5 weights (qwen3.5_4b_bf16.safetensors) stored under models/text_encoders/. That model handle feeds into the TextGenerate node, which accepts the loaded image and an instruction prompt (for example, "Produce 3 concise, diffusion-ready prompts"). The node then runs inference and returns text, which you can view with PreviewAny. A MarkdownNote in the graph provides inline guidance and prompt tips, making it easy to iterate on instruction wording, temperature, and token length to dial in results.
howToUse: Download qwen3.5_4b_bf16.safetensors and place it in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/. Restart ComfyUI so the model is indexed.
Load the provided workflow. Verify the CLIPLoader node points to the Qwen3.5 model and shows as loaded (node turns ready).
Open LoadImage and select the image you want to analyze. Use a clear, well-lit source for the best descriptions.

Open TextGenerate and confirm it is connected to the Qwen3.5 model (from CLIPLoader). Edit the instruction/system prompt (e.g., request 2–4 diffusion-ready prompts including subject, medium, camera/lens, lighting, style, and optional negatives). Adjust generation parameters like temperature and max tokens if exposed.
Queue the workflow. When it finishes, read and copy the generated text from PreviewAny. If needed, tweak the instruction or parameters and re-run for refinement.
Optionally, use MarkdownNote in the workflow as a place to store your favorite instruction templates and examples for consistent outputs across images.
suggestedUseCases: Reverse prompt engineering: derive SD/SDXL/FLUX-friendly prompts from reference images.
Alt-text and SEO descriptions for product images or blog visuals.
Dataset bootstrapping: quick, consistent captions to seed annotation workflows.
Creative briefs and shot lists based on visual references.
Asset tagging and library organization with detailed, style-aware descriptors.

faqItems.question: How is this different from basic image captioning?
faqItems.answer: Beyond plain descriptions, the workflow can generate structured, diffusion-ready prompts (subject, medium, lens, lighting, style, and optional negatives) when you specify that format in the TextGenerate instruction.

faqItems.question: Do I need an internet connection to run this?
faqItems.answer: No. Once you download qwen3.5_4b_bf16.safetensors into ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/, the workflow runs locally in ComfyUI.

faqItems.question: How can I improve the quality or usefulness of the generated prompts?
faqItems.answer: Use clear, high-quality images; provide a precise instruction template (e.g., ask for 3 concise prompts with subject, medium, lens, lighting, style, and negatives); and tune generation parameters like temperature (for more or less creativity) and max tokens (for longer outputs).

faqItems.question: Can I swap in a different Qwen3.5 variant?
faqItems.answer: Yes, as long as it’s packaged for use with the TextGenerate node and placed where CLIPLoader can load it (models/text_encoders/). Update the CLIPLoader selection to the desired variant and keep the instruction format consistent.

aeb81743ddf7.title: Step 3: Contact Sheet Workflow
aeb81743ddf7.description: Upload 8 images (in order) to be used as keyframes for 7 Kling 3.0 FFLF videos.
aeb81743ddf7.metaDescription: Create a 1080p contact sheet and 7 FFLF clips from 8 keyframes using ComfyUI with Kling 3.0. Batch images, verify order, and generate smooth, controlled transitions.
aeb81743ddf7.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial walks you through a contact sheet workflow that turns 8 ordered images into a structured storyboard and 7 adjacent keyframe pairs for Kling 3.0 FFLF video generation. The pipeline starts with LoadImage and BatchImagesNode to ingest your files in a strict left-to-right timeline. A set of utility/custom nodes (IDs: f7abaa3a-5e87-4354-bab6-f43320cd490f, 02da9128-7c15-4c46-96bc-1dd68e5bc490, 3426003b-7b3a-4d37-8a2f-e0f8adb05712, c61d617f-c72d-4f4c-8659-bd6f884d1a1e, 4b301c11-bc16-4096-9441-e0648a04aa4d, 2ab1ef49-3518-4f71-b703-f8ef12f32214, b3fe4254-e196-429e-9f45-96c92113e406) handle layout, pairwise splitting (1-2, 2-3, …, 7-8), and packaging to downstream video nodes. PrimitiveNode exposes the core knobs—1080p resolution, frame rate, per-shot duration, and optional padding—while Reroute keeps the graph readable. SaveVideo exports a 1080p preview so you can quickly verify sequencing and framing before running the heavier generations.

For FFLF (first/last-frame–guided) generation, each adjacent image pair is passed to the Kling 3.0 node to synthesize motion constrained by your start and end frames—ideal for consistent, controllable transitions across a 7-shot sequence. If enabled, a Gemini-3.1-flsih-lite helper node can auto-summarize shot intents between each pair to keep prompts consistent (optional metadata only; it’s not required for rendering). The result is a fast, reliable way to validate continuity, then batch-generate seven cohesive clips at a clean 1920×1080 output.
howToUse: Load the “Step 3: Contact Sheet Workflow” JSON in ComfyUI and confirm all nodes are green (LoadImage, BatchImagesNode, PrimitiveNode, SaveVideo, Kling 3.0, and helper nodes).

Import 8 images in the exact storytelling order. Use BatchImagesNode for a single multi-file load (ensure filenames sort correctly) or update individual LoadImage nodes. Keep all images at or near 16:9 to avoid cropping at 1080p.
Open PrimitiveNode parameters and set 1920×1080 resolution (author note: 1080p), FPS, and per-shot duration. These control both the preview pacing and the Kling 3.0 request timing.
Optionally enable the Gemini-3.1-flsih-lite node if you want brief auto-generated descriptors between keyframe pairs. These notes can be passed as lightweight guidance to the Kling 3.0 prompts.
Queue the graph to generate a 1080p contact sheet preview with SaveVideo. Review the output to confirm frame order, aspect ratio, and pacing before running the FFLF jobs.
Run the Kling 3.0 FFLF nodes to create 7 videos (pairs 1–2, 2–3, …, 7–8). Check the output/video directory for saved clips. If anything looks off, adjust order/duration in PrimitiveNode and re-queue.
suggestedUseCases: Storyboard-to-motion: Validate a visual narrative, then convert each transition into a guided clip.
Product feature reveals: Morph between feature shots for smooth, controlled transitions.
Character turnarounds: Interpolate between posed keyframes for stylized motion studies.
Before/after sequences: Create clear, steady transitions between states or designs.
Location shifts: Guide scene changes while preserving composition across cuts.

faqItems.question: Why does the workflow require exactly 8 images?
faqItems.answer: It’s designed to create 7 FFLF videos from adjacent pairs. With 8 ordered keyframes, the pairs are 1–2, 2–3, …, 7–8. If you need more or fewer shots, duplicate/remove the pair-splitting path accordingly.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the frames are in the correct order?
faqItems.answer: Use BatchImagesNode with naturally sorting filenames (e.g., 01, 02, …, 08). If loading individually, double-check each LoadImage path. The contact sheet preview from SaveVideo is the quickest way to verify.

faqItems.question: My images don’t match 16:9—will they be cropped or stretched?
faqItems.answer: Set the PrimitiveNode output to 1920×1080 and choose consistent image sizes. If your sources vary, add a resize/crop step before batching to avoid unwanted letterboxing or distortion in the preview and Kling outputs.

faqItems.question: Kling 3.0 calls are failing or timing out—what should I check?
faqItems.answer: Confirm your Kling node/API configuration, rate limits, and per-shot duration. Try lowering resolution or length, queueing fewer segments at a time, and ensuring stable network connectivity before re-running.

aeda3ae212cd.title: 3x3 Brand Icon Assets Grid

By uploading a reference image of an icon and entering specific brand information, this workflow generates nine unique icons that maintain consistency with your brand's style. The workflow utilizes a combination of models and nodes, including the Gemini3 Pro Image Preview and Nano Banana Pro, to ensure high-quality output. Key nodes such as LoadImage, GeminiImage2Node, and SaveImage work together to process the input image and apply the desired stylistic transformations.

Technically, the workflow integrates custom nodes like comfyui-kjnodes and comfyui_essentials to enhance functionality and flexibility. Nodes like PrimitiveInt and PrimitiveStringMultiline allow for precise input adjustments, while RegexReplace ensures that the output aligns with specified brand parameters. The use of Reroute nodes facilitates efficient data flow between processes, ensuring that each icon is generated with the intended characteristics. This workflow is particularly useful for brand designers and marketing teams looking to quickly produce a cohesive set of icon assets without sacrificing creativity or brand integrity.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure all required models and nodes are installed.
Upload your reference icon image using the LoadImage node.
Enter your brand information and stylistic preferences in the input fields provided by PrimitiveStringMultiline nodes.
Adjust any additional parameters using the PrimitiveInt nodes to refine icon characteristics.
Run the workflow to generate a 3x3 grid of unique, brand-aligned icons.
Save the generated icons using the SaveImage node for use in your branding materials.
suggestedUseCases: Creating a cohesive set of icons for a new product line.
Developing branded icons for a website or mobile app.
Designing promotional materials with consistent branding.
Generating unique icons for social media branding.
Producing customized icons for corporate presentations.

faqItems.question: Can I use any image as a reference for the icons?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can upload any image as a reference, but for best results, use an image that closely aligns with your desired icon style.

faqItems.question: What if the generated icons don't match my brand's colors?
faqItems.answer: You can adjust the brand information and stylistic preferences in the input fields to better match your brand's color scheme.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the icons are unique yet consistent?
faqItems.answer: The workflow uses advanced models like Gemini3 Pro Image Preview to ensure each icon is unique while maintaining stylistic consistency.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to generate more than 9 icons at once?
faqItems.answer: The current workflow is optimized for a 3x3 grid. For more icons, you can run the workflow multiple times with different parameters.

af474291cb93.title: Video Upscale: Topaz Astra Fast
af474291cb93.description: Enhance videos with Topaz AI. Supports resolution upscaling using Starlight (Astra) Fast model and frame interpolation with apo-8 model.

af5265f57b43.title: Video Upscale: FLUX 3
af5265f57b43.description: Upscale video clips to 1080p, 2K, or 4K using FLUX 3 super-resolution, with a precise mode that preserves source fidelity and a creative mode that enhances fine detail. It accepts 1 video input, up to 20 seconds long, and produces 1 upscaled mp4 output with an optional prompt to guide detail enhancement. Ideal for restoring low-resolution footage, preparing clips for large-screen delivery, and adding crispness to AI-generated video.
af5265f57b43.metaDescription: Upscale videos to 1080p–4K in ComfyUI with FLUX 3. Choose precise or creative mode, keep audio, add an optional prompt. Ideal for clips up to ~20s, output at 24 fps.
af5265f57b43.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow demonstrates how to upscale short video clips to 1080p, 2K, or 4K using the FLUX 3 super-resolution model. It accepts a single input video (up to ~20 seconds), processes frames with the FluxVideoUpscaleNode, and writes a single mp4 output via SaveVideo while preserving the original audio track. A key choice is between Precise mode (fidelity-first) and Creative mode (detail-enhancing), with an optional text prompt to guide fine detail in Creative mode.

Technically, the FluxVideoUpscaleNode performs 1.5x–3x super-resolution using the Flux model family, either by a direct scale factor or by targeting common output resolutions (1080p/2K/4K) within that range. The workflow is straightforward: LoadVideo ingests your source clip, FluxVideoUpscaleNode handles the upscaling and optional prompt conditioning, and SaveVideo assembles the result to mp4 at 24 fps with the source audio track. This setup is practical for restoring low-resolution footage, preparing clips for larger displays, and adding extra crispness to AI-generated video without rebuilding a complex graph.
howToUse: Open the "Video Upscale: FLUX 3" workflow in ComfyUI and verify the Flux model is available in your environment.
In the LoadVideo node, browse to your source clip (up to ~20 seconds). You can test with the sample: color_spin_flower.mp4.
Select the FluxVideoUpscaleNode and choose your target: either set a scale (1.5x–3x) or select a resolution preset (1080p, 2K, or 4K) that falls within that scale range.
Pick the processing mode: Precise for maximum fidelity to the source, or Creative for enhanced micro-detail. If using Creative, optionally enter a short prompt to steer textures and fine features.
Run the workflow. The node will process frames, preserve the source audio track, and SaveVideo will write the upscaled mp4 at 24 fps.

Review the output. If you see over-sharpening or unwanted texture, switch to Precise or remove the prompt; if the image feels too soft, try Creative or a slightly higher scale within the 1.5x–3x limit.
suggestedUseCases: Restoring low-resolution phone or archival clips to 1080p for clean social media delivery.
Prepping B-roll for a 4K editing timeline while retaining audio and consistent cadence.
Adding crispness to AI-generated videos by upscaling to 2K or 4K with Creative mode.
Improving screen recordings or gameplay captures where text and UI need cleaner edges.
Client review cuts that require quick resolution boosts without re-rendering the original.

faqItems.question: What clip lengths and formats are supported?
faqItems.answer: The workflow is designed for a single video up to roughly 20 seconds. Input via LoadVideo and output via SaveVideo are mp4-focused; the output is written as mp4 with audio preserved.

faqItems.question: Does it keep my original audio and what frame rate is used?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The SaveVideo output keeps the source audio track, and the final mp4 is standardized at 24 fps.

faqItems.question: When should I use Precise vs. Creative mode?
faqItems.answer: Use Precise to preserve source fidelity (logos, UI, faces, brand assets) with minimal added texture. Use Creative when you want more perceived sharpness and fine detail; add a short prompt to guide textures. For neutral results in Creative, keep prompts subtle and avoid overly broad descriptors.

faqItems.question: Can I choose any resolution, like 4K, from a very small source?
faqItems.answer: Upscaling operates within about 1.5x–3x. If your target (e.g., 4K) requires more than 3x from the input size, the node will cap within its supported range. In that case, consider an intermediate pass or select a closer preset like 1080p or 2K.

af9d2d3845c6.title: Muse Image 1.0: Image Edit
af9d2d3845c6.description: Edit an image with precision using Muse Image 1.0, following natural language instructions to alter specific elements while preserving the rest of the scene. Takes 2 input images and produces 1 edited output image. Ideal for product photography touch-ups, creative style transfers, and iterative visual refinement.
af9d2d3845c6.metaDescription: Edit images with Muse Image 1.0 via natural-language instructions. Two inputs (base + reference) in, one precise edited image out—no masking required.
af9d2d3845c6.extendedDescription:
This workflow uses Muse Image 1.0 to edit an image with natural-language instructions while preserving the rest of the scene. Two LoadImage nodes supply inputs: one is the primary image you want to edit, and the second is a visual reference that guides the look (style, color palette, material cues) of the edit. The MetaMuseImageEditApi node sends both images plus your instruction to the hosted Muse Image 1.0 service and returns a single edited image. SaveImageAdvanced then writes the result to disk with your chosen filename and subfolder.

Technically, the graph is simple and reliable: LoadImage → MetaMuseImageEditApi → SaveImageAdvanced, with a MarkdownNote included to summarize usage. The API node interprets your instruction (e.g., "make the house red while keeping the desert sky unchanged") and applies targeted changes while maintaining scene layout and context. Example inputs included with the template—deep_blue_whale_swim_scene.png and desert_red_modern_house.png—let you try style- or color-guided edits immediately.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote for a quick overview.
In the two LoadImage nodes, set your files: use the first as the primary image to edit and the second as a visual reference (or keep the provided sample assets to test).

Open the MetaMuseImageEditApi node and enter a clear instruction describing exactly what to change and what to preserve (e.g., "Recolor the house to deep red; keep the desert sky and lighting unchanged"). Ensure your API endpoint/key are configured if required.
Optionally adjust SaveImageAdvanced to set the output subfolder and filename pattern so each iteration is saved distinctly.
Click Queue Prompt to run the graph. When it completes, view the saved output from SaveImageAdvanced.
Iterate: refine your instruction for more precise results or swap the reference image to steer style, color, or material closer to your target.
suggestedUseCases: Product photography touch-ups: recolor packaging or materials while preserving background and lighting.
Creative style alignment: match a scene’s palette and texture to a brand or mood reference image.
Architectural concept tweaks: change facade color/materials or accents without altering overall composition.
Scene consistency for campaigns: harmonize color grading across shots using a single reference image.
Iterative visual refinement: quickly explore variations by adjusting text instructions and references.

faqItems.question: What are the two image inputs used for?
faqItems.answer: The first (primary) image is the one being edited. The second is a visual reference to guide the edit’s style, palette, or material cues. If you don’t want external guidance, you can use the same image for both inputs.

faqItems.question: Do I need an internet connection or API key?
faqItems.answer: Yes. MetaMuseImageEditApi calls a hosted Muse Image 1.0 service. Ensure your endpoint and credentials are set in the node or ComfyUI’s API settings before running the workflow.

faqItems.question: How can I get precise edits on just one object?
faqItems.answer: Be explicit and constraint-focused: name the object and change ("Make the door matte black"), and add preservation cues ("keep walls, lighting, and background unchanged"). Using a closely matched reference image further improves locality and style consistency.

faqItems.question: Why did the background change slightly?
faqItems.answer: Increase instruction specificity (e.g., "leave background untouched"), choose a closer-matching reference image, and iterate. Small phrasing adjustments often reduce unintended global changes.

afa2656c1d4e.title: Seedance2.5 1080P: Text to Video
afa2656c1d4e.description: Generate cinematic 1080P video clips from text descriptions using Seedance 2.5, supporting clips up to 30 seconds with synchronized sound, music, and dialogue across any aspect ratio. Ideal for short comedy scenes, product showcases, and creative storytelling.
afa2656c1d4e.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate 1080p text-to-video with audio using Seedance 2.5 via ByteDance2TextToVideoNode and SaveVideo. Up to 30s, any aspect ratio.
afa2656c1d4e.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns plain text descriptions into cinematic 1080p video clips with optional synchronized sound using Seedance 2.5. At its core is the ByteDance2TextToVideoNode, which sends your prompt and generation settings (duration, resolution, aspect ratio, FPS, seed) to the Seedance 2.5 backend and returns a finished video stream that can include music, ambience, and simple dialogue aligned to the scene. The SaveVideo node then writes the result to disk as an MP4, preserving the audio track when present.

Technically, you control the visual output by setting width/height (1920x1080 by default) or any custom aspect ratio the model supports, plus a duration cap of up to 30 seconds. The node also exposes a seed so you can iterate with reproducible variations. Because generation is API-based, you get consistent performance without local GPU setup. The simple two-node graph keeps things lean: ByteDance2TextToVideoNode handles synthesis; SaveVideo handles encoding and file naming—ideal for quick iterations, social-ready formats (landscape, square, vertical), and prompt-driven story beats.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then open the ByteDance2TextToVideoNode and SaveVideo nodes.

faqItems.question: What are the limits for clip length and resolution?

faqItems.question: Can I reproduce a result exactly using the same seed?

afd30ccf8238.title: ACE-Step 1.5 Music Generation AIO
afd30ccf8238.description: Input style tags and lyrics to generate a full song. The workflow uses the ACE-Step 1.5 model to produce commercial-grade music in under 10 seconds on consumer hardware.
afd30ccf8238.metaDescription: Generate songs from style tags and lyrics using ACE‑Step 1.5 in ComfyUI. Set duration, prompt, and export MP3 fast with a clean, reproducible workflow.
afd30ccf8238.extendedDescription:
ACE-Step 1.5 Music Generation AIO is a text-to-audio ComfyUI workflow that turns style tags and lyrics into a complete song. You provide short descriptors like "modern pop, female vocal, lush synths" plus your lyrics, and the graph handles the rest—sampling, decoding, and exporting MP3—so you can audition ideas in seconds on consumer hardware. It’s organized into clear groups—Step 1: Load Model, Step 2: Duration, Step 3: Prompt—so you always know where to set the checkpoint, how long the track should be, and what the model should sing or sound like.

Under the hood, CheckpointLoaderSimple loads the ACE-Step 1.5 checkpoint (ace_step_1.5_turbo_aio.safetensors). TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5 converts your style tags and lyrics into ACE-specific conditioning vectors. ConditioningZeroOut is used to cleanly disable unused conditioning channels (for example, when you’re not providing a secondary or negative prompt), preventing unintended bias. EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio creates an empty latent audio canvas for the exact duration you request. ModelSamplingAuraFlow configures the correct sampler/scheduler combination for ACE-Step 1.5, and KSampler iteratively refines the latent into a coherent track based on your prompt. VAEDecodeAudio turns the final latent into waveform audio, and SaveAudioMP3 writes the result to your ComfyUI output folder. PrimitiveNode widgets expose practical knobs like steps, CFG, seed, and seconds so you can tweak speed, quality, and reproducibility.

This setup is useful for fast songwriting demos, genre exploration, and content beds. You get precise control over duration and a repeatable workflow via the seed. The graph ships with sensible defaults so you can generate a short track quickly, then dial in higher quality by raising steps or refining style tags and lyric phrasing.
howToUse: Place the ACE-Step checkpoint in ComfyUI/models/checkpoints (e.g., ace_step_1.5_turbo_aio.safetensors), then load the provided workflow JSON in ComfyUI.
Step 1 – Load Model: Open the CheckpointLoaderSimple node and select the ACE-Step 1.5 checkpoint. This provides the model weights to the rest of the graph.
Step 2 – Duration: In EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio (via its connected PrimitiveNode controls), set the target length in seconds. This defines how long the generated audio will be.
Step 3 – Prompt: In TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5, enter concise style tags (genre, mood, instrumentation, vocal type) and paste your lyrics. Keep tags focused and lyrics clear for best intelligibility.

Quality and speed: Adjust KSampler parameters exposed via PrimitiveNode—steps (more steps = higher quality but slower), CFG (start moderate), and seed (fixed for reproducibility or -1/random for variety). ModelSamplingAuraFlow is preconfigured; leave it as-is for correct ACE-Step sampling.

Run the workflow. When it completes, VAEDecodeAudio will output audio that SaveAudioMP3 writes to your ComfyUI output directory. Preview the result and iterate by refining style tags, lyrics, or sampler settings.
suggestedUseCases: Songwriting drafts: Turn lyric snippets and style directions into quick melody-and-arrangement ideas.
Genre exploration: Test how the same lyrics sound across pop, hip-hop, EDM, rock, or cinematic tags.
Ad/jingle prototypes: Rapidly generate short, on-brief music cues for pitches and client approvals.
Social/video beds: Produce background tracks tailored to mood and pacing from a simple prompt.
Education: Demonstrate text-to-music conditioning and sampling concepts in a classroom or workshop.

faqItems.question: Where do I put the model and how do I load it?
faqItems.answer: Place ace_step_1.5_turbo_aio.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/checkpoints. In the workflow’s Step 1 – Load Model group, open CheckpointLoaderSimple and select the file.

faqItems.question: How do I control the length and structure of the song?
faqItems.answer: Set the duration in EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio (via its PrimitiveNode control). This sets the exact seconds of audio. You can hint at structure with your lyrics and style tags, but explicit verse/chorus segmentation is not guaranteed.

faqItems.question: My output is noisy or unclear. What should I adjust first?
faqItems.answer: Try increasing KSampler steps moderately, lower CFG if artifacts appear, and refine style tags to be specific (e.g., "warm pop ballad, intimate female vocal, soft piano"). Ensure unused conditioning is disabled via ConditioningZeroOut and keep lyrics concise and well-punctuated.

faqItems.question: Can I reproduce a result exactly?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Set a fixed seed in the PrimitiveNode feeding KSampler. Using the same model, prompts, duration, steps, and CFG will produce highly consistent results.

b12a11bee2a3.title: Image Upscale: Nano Banana Pro Product
b12a11bee2a3.description: Upload a product image to enhance its detail and sharpness. Generate an upscaled, high-quality output with improved typography and realistic coherence using the Nano Banana Pro model.

The Nano Banana Pro model is tuned for product imagery—reinforcing edges, materials, and label regions—so you get cleaner type, crisper contours, and more believable surface detail at a higher resolution.

Technically, GeminiImage2Node serves as an API-backed image-to-image processor. It takes the input from LoadImage, requests an upscaled, detail-enhanced version from the Nano Banana Pro model, and returns a refined output while aiming to maintain color and structure. Because the heavy lifting is done via API, the workflow stays lightweight inside ComfyUI: no local checkpoints to manage, consistent outputs between runs (given the same settings), and straightforward saving through SaveImage to your preferred format and path.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the three-node path: LoadImage → GeminiImage2Node (model: Nano Banana Pro) → SaveImage.
In GeminiImage2Node, add your API credentials if required and confirm the model is set to Nano Banana Pro. Review any available controls (e.g., target size or quality).
Click the LoadImage node and select your product photo. Use a clean, well-lit source image for best results—centered subject, minimal compression artifacts.

Catalog and line-sheet preparation where consistent, high-resolution assets are required.
Social media and ad creatives that need clean, high-detail crops of products.
Marketplace re-uploads of legacy product images to meet modern resolution requirements.
Packaging mockups where label details and typography clarity matter.

faqItems.question: Does it actually fix blurry text on labels or packaging?
faqItems.answer: It often improves clarity and sharpness, but it can’t recover text that’s extremely small or severely blurred. Start from the highest-quality source you have, crop tighter around the product if needed, and try a moderate upscale rather than an extreme jump.

faqItems.question: Do I need internet access or an API key?
faqItems.answer: Yes. GeminiImage2Node is API-backed, so an internet connection and valid API credentials are typically required. Check the node’s configuration in your setup for how to add or test keys.

faqItems.question: How do I control file format and quality on export?
faqItems.answer: Use the SaveImage node to set the output path, filename, and format (e.g., PNG or JPEG). If JPEG is used, adjust its quality setting in SaveImage to balance size and fidelity.

b1ab45b906ca.metaDescription: ComfyUI text-to-image with Ideogram P-Image. Control quality and resolution, preview results, and save outputs for fast, cost-effective visual iteration.
b1ab45b906ca.extendedDescription:

howToUse: Load the workflow into ComfyUI and open the graph. Locate the key nodes: BuildJsonPromptIdeogram, IdeogramPImage, PreviewAny, CreateBoundingBoxes, and SaveImageAdvanced.
Open IdeogramPImage and enter your Ideogram API credentials as required by the node. Select the P-Image model (if selectable), then choose your desired quality preset and resolution.

Optional: Use CreateBoundingBoxes to define composition guides (e.g., rule-of-thirds or text-safe regions). These boxes display in PreviewAny for planning but do not constrain the model’s output.

When satisfied, configure SaveImageAdvanced (output folder, filename pattern, format) and run. The node will save your final images for sharing or further processing.

High-volume content generation for social posts or blog hero images with consistent settings.
Cost-sensitive A/B testing of ad visuals by varying prompt phrasing, quality, and resolution.
Early-stage product mockups or concept art to explore materials, lighting, and composition.
Internal creative reviews where previews, bounding-box guides, and named exports streamline feedback.

faqItems.question: Do I need a local GPU to use this workflow?

faqItems.question: What do the quality and resolution settings affect?

faqItems.question: Do the bounding boxes change how the image is generated?
faqItems.answer: No. CreateBoundingBoxes is used here as a visual guide in PreviewAny to help plan composition. The boxes are not sent to the Ideogram API and do not constrain the model’s output.

faqItems.question: How can I get more consistent results across runs?
faqItems.answer: Keep your prompt wording, quality, and resolution identical between renders. If the node exposes a seed parameter, fix it for repeatability. Otherwise, duplicate runs and select the closest match; then iterate with small, controlled prompt edits.

b27220a578ee.title: Chatter Box: Voice Cloning Audio Conversion

Finally, the 'SaveAudioMP3' node exports the converted audio in MP3 format, making it easy to share and use across various platforms. Select a short reference clip of the target voice and process it with the 'FL_ChatterboxVC' node.
Optionally, use the 'AudioCrop' node to trim the audio to the desired length.
Run the workflow to perform the voice conversion.
Export the converted audio using the 'SaveAudioMP3' node.

Developing custom voice applications for virtual assistants.
Producing audiobooks with consistent voice characteristics across different narrators.

faqItems.question: How long should the target voice reference clip be?

faqItems.question: What output format is supported?

b3437893d89d.title: HY 3D 2.0

This workflow is particularly useful for creating 3D models from photos or concept art, providing a bridge between 2D creativity and 3D application.

Ensure the Hunyuan3D model is loaded using the ImageOnlyCheckpointLoader node.
Upload your 2D image using the LoadImage node.
Adjust the configuration settings, such as setting the cfg value between 4 and 8.
Run the workflow to process the image and generate a 3D model.

howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm both nodes are present: MinimaxHailuo03TextToVideoNode and SaveVideo.

Short-form social media clips (vertical 9:16) with native audio for immediate posting.
Advertising and film pre-visualization: quick animatics to explore camera moves and blocking.

faqItems.question: What video length can I generate?

faqItems.question: Does the output include audio?

faqItems.question: How can I improve prompt results?

b35c9fa7658c.title: Grok Imagine Image Quality: Edit
b35c9fa7658c.description: Enhance image quality with advanced text rendering and creative control using Grok Imagine Image Quality. Input images or prompts for improved detail and fidelity.
b35c9fa7658c.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: enhance images and fix text with Grok Imagine Image Quality using LoadImage → GrokImageEditNode → SaveImage for clean, detailed results.

Technically, GrokImageEditNode acts as the bridge to the Grok Imagine Image Quality endpoint, applying server-side upscaling, denoising, and advanced text rendering to improve clarity and readability while respecting your guidance. Your text prompt steers the edit (e.g., “sharpen details, clean signage text, preserve colors”), and any available controls in the node (such as strength, guidance, or resolution—depending on the node version) modulate how strongly the API alters the input. SaveImage then captures the returned image frames to your chosen output folder with your preferred filename prefix.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI. Confirm the nodes are connected: LoadImage → GrokImageEditNode → SaveImage.

Provide input: either select a source image in LoadImage for image-to-image enhancement, or (if supported by your GrokImageEditNode version) run prompt-only without a source image to generate a new one.

Open GrokImageEditNode and enter a clear instruction prompt (e.g., “enhance detail, sharpen edges, fix garbled text, preserve layout”). If your node exposes options like strength, guidance, or output size, adjust them to control how aggressive the edit should be.
In SaveImage, set a descriptive filename prefix and verify the output directory. This helps you track iterations as you refine prompts.
Queue and run the workflow. Watch the GrokImageEditNode status; when complete, check the output folder for the enhanced image.
Iterate: refine your prompt for text-heavy scenes (keep wording concise, specify exact phrases, and ask for high contrast) and rerun to converge on the cleanest result.

Polishing product photos by improving label legibility and fine surface details.
Restoring scanned posters or flyers with better text clarity and reduced noise.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key to use GrokImageEditNode?

faqItems.question: Can I generate an image from text only, without an input image?

faqItems.question: How do I preserve composition while improving text and details?

b37902cee452.title: LTX-2.5: Image to Video
b37902cee452.description: Generate video from a single image using LTX-2.5, producing a high-fidelity clip with industry-leading pixel quality and native multishot capability that holds character, environment, and lighting across connected scenes. Ideal for cinematic production, VFX shot creation, and content pipelines requiring fast, locally deployable video generation.
b37902cee452.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: convert a single image into a high-quality video with LTX-2.5. Load, set resolution, render frames, and save to MP4—fully local.
b37902cee452.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single still image into a smooth, high-fidelity video using LTX-2.5, Lightricks’ open video generation model. The pipeline is intentionally simple and production-minded: LoadImage ingests your source frame, ResolutionSelector locks in a model-friendly size (multiples of 32) and aspect ratio, the LTX-2.5 generator node (UUID: 6e397a2b-68f7-48f6-8930-f3a5491a163c) synthesizes a coherent motion sequence, and SaveVideo encodes the frames to a ready-to-use MP4. A MarkdownNote in the graph provides in-UI guidance and links.

Under the hood, LTX-2.5 uses a keyframes-first "Pixel Diffusion" approach to propagate detail and structure consistently across time. This helps preserve subject identity, lighting, and scene composition from your source image while introducing controllable motion. ResolutionSelector ensures your chosen 16:9 dimensions conform to model stride (multiples of 32), which is critical for stability and VRAM efficiency. Because it runs locally, you can iterate quickly, tune duration (frames/fps), and adjust motion strength to meet the needs of previz, VFX look development, and content pipelines.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then read the MarkdownNote for an overview and tips.
Open the LoadImage node and select your source image (e.g., input/neon_cyborg_portrait.png) or browse to your own asset.
Set output size in ResolutionSelector. Choose a 16:9 preset that matches your VRAM (e.g., 0.6 MP -> 1056x608). Keeping dimensions as multiples of 32 is required.

On the LTX-2.5 node (UUID 6e397a2b-68f7-48f6-8930-f3a5491a163c), set clip length and tempo by adjusting frame count and FPS. Optionally tune seed and motion intensity for more or less camera/subject movement.
Confirm SaveVideo settings (output path and FPS should match the generator). Queue the workflow and run.
When the job completes, retrieve the MP4 from the SaveVideo output folder and review. Iterate on resolution, frames/FPS, or motion settings as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic previz: generate quick moving plates from style frames to evaluate mood, lighting, and camera feel.
VFX look development: create motion studies from key concept art to test continuity of materials and lighting.
Product hero shots: turn a single packshot into a subtle orbit or parallax clip for promos and landing pages.
Social shorts and loops: produce eye-catching micro-animations from stills for reels, stories, and ads.
Animatic building blocks: rapidly assemble moving beats from boards before committing to full production.

faqItems.question: Why does the workflow use ResolutionSelector and multiples of 32?
faqItems.answer: LTX-2.5 (like many diffusion models) operates on stride-aligned dimensions. Using multiples of 32 prevents internal padding/resize artifacts, improves stability, and is more VRAM-efficient. The ResolutionSelector node helps you pick valid 16:9 sizes (e.g., 1056x608 for ~0.6 MP).

faqItems.question: How long can my clip be, and what affects render time?
faqItems.answer: Clip duration is frames ÷ FPS (e.g., 96 frames at 24 FPS ≈ 4 seconds). Render time and memory scale with resolution, frame count, and motion complexity. Start with modest settings (e.g., 0.6–0.8 MP, 64–96 frames, 16–24 FPS) and increase as your VRAM and iteration time allow.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the subject stable and avoid jitter?
faqItems.answer: Use a clean, high-resolution source image with a clear subject and lighting. Keep output resolution stride-aligned, reduce motion intensity for more conservative movement, and consider raising FPS while keeping motion moderate. Re-seed if you see unwanted artifacts; stability often improves after a few trials.

faqItems.question: Does this support multishot timelines?
faqItems.answer: This template focuses on a single image-to-video clip. LTX-2.5 is designed to maintain coherent style and identity across shots, but to build a multishot timeline in ComfyUI, duplicate this block with Subgraph, render each shot, and stitch the resulting clips in your editor (or a separate combine step).

SaveVideo then encodes the generated frames into a single video file (e.g., MP4/WebM) at your chosen frame rate.

Technically, ByteDance2TextToVideoNode conditions a video diffusion process on your prompt and iteratively produces a temporally consistent stack of images. Fixing the seed and keeping motion cues clear in the prompt helps maintain stable visuals across frames. Describing camera-like behavior in the text (e.g., “slow dolly in,” “static tripod,” “handheld”) guides motion without extra nodes. SaveVideo collects the node’s frame output and writes it to disk; if you need music or sound effects, export your video and sync audio later in a video editor.
howToUse: Load the Seedance 2.0: Text to Video workflow in ComfyUI and confirm ByteDance2TextToVideoNode is connected to SaveVideo.
Open ByteDance2TextToVideoNode and select the Seedance 2.0 model (or ensure it’s already loaded). Set resolution, frame count (duration), and fps.
Write a concise prompt describing subject, setting, mood, and motion (e.g., lens or camera feel). Optionally set a seed for repeatable results.
Run a short preview first (lower resolution and fewer frames) to check composition, motion, and style.
Refine the prompt and settings for stability (e.g., keep motion cues simple), then increase frames/resolution for a final render.
In SaveVideo, match the fps to the generation node, choose the container/codec and output path, then run to encode and save your video.
suggestedUseCases: Concept teasers and storyboards that visualize scripts or scene ideas quickly.
Social media intros and loops with controlled pacing and mood.
Product and feature previews where stable framing and motion are important.
Mood films for music tracks by timing clip duration to an external soundtrack.

faqItems.question: How do I keep visuals stable across frames?

faqItems.question: How can I control camera motion?
faqItems.answer: Describe the motion in the prompt (e.g., “static shot,” “slow dolly-in,” “smooth pan left”). Clear, simple motion language tends to produce more predictable results than mixing multiple complex moves.

faqItems.question: What resolution and fps should I start with?

b594a01df1d6.extendedDescription:
Seedream 5.0 Pro: Image Edit is a precision image-to-image and inpainting workflow that lets you change exactly what you want while keeping the original lighting, depth, and texture intact. It starts with LoadImage to bring in your source photo, then optionally uses Painter to create a clean mask for targeted edits. The core transformation happens in ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2, which conditions on your input image (and mask if provided) to apply prompt-driven changes without destroying structure. Finally, SaveImageAdvanced writes out clean results with controllable filenames and folders.

Technically, the mask from Painter constrains edits to specific regions, while the input image conditioning helps Seedream preserve scene geometry and materials. You’ll get two outputs: a main edited image from ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 and a second preview that reflects the Painter-guided variant—useful for quick QA and before/after comparisons. Tuning typical parameters like prompt/negative prompt, denoise strength (how much to change vs. preserve), steps, guidance (CFG), and seed lets you dial in subtle retouches for product shots, keep consistent faces across a series, or lay out multilingual text in a structured composition.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and confirm the nodes: LoadImage → (optional) Painter → ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 → SaveImageAdvanced.
Open LoadImage and select your source photo (PNG/JPG). Keep the native resolution when possible for best structure retention.
Optional: Double-click Painter to brush a mask over areas you want changed. Paint white where edits should apply and leave black where the image must be preserved.

Configure ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2: set your prompt and negative prompt, choose a modest denoise strength for subtle edits (e.g., 0.2–0.45), adjust steps and guidance/CFG, and fix a seed for repeatable results.
Run the graph. The model will condition on your input (and mask if used) to produce two outputs: the main edited image and a Painter-informed preview for quick review.
In SaveImageAdvanced, set the output folder and filename pattern. Inspect both results, compare changes, and iterate by tweaking prompts, denoise strength, or the mask as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Product photography cleanup: remove dust, add subtle highlights, or swap labels while preserving material and lighting.
Portrait consistency: nudge hairstyle, makeup, or attire details across a series with a fixed seed and controlled denoise.
Structured layouts with multilingual text: place or refine text in specific areas using a mask for clean alignment.

faqItems.question: What does ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 do in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: It’s the core image-to-image/inpainting model node. It conditions on your input image (and optional mask) plus your prompt to apply localized, structure-preserving edits.

faqItems.question: How do I limit changes to only part of the image?
faqItems.answer: Use the Painter node to create a mask: paint white where edits should occur and black where they should not. Feed this mask into ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 so only the painted region is modified.

faqItems.question: How can I keep results consistent across multiple images?
faqItems.answer: Use the same prompt, negative prompt, seed, steps, guidance/CFG, and keep denoise strength low to moderate. Consistent framing and lighting in your source images also help Seedream preserve structure.

faqItems.question: Why do I get two outputs, and which one should I use?

This workflow leverages the LivePortrait model, a cutting-edge AI model that excels in transferring facial expressions from video to image. The process begins with the 'LoadImage' node, where a static portrait is uploaded, and the 'VHS_LoadVideo' node, which imports the reference video containing the desired expressions. The 'LivePortraitProcess' node plays a crucial role by analyzing and extracting facial movements from the video, which are then applied to the portrait using the 'LivePortraitComposite' node. To ensure precision, the 'LivePortraitCropper' and 'LivePortraitLoadMediaPipeCropper' nodes are employed to align facial features accurately. The final animated video is compiled using the 'VHS_VideoCombine' node and saved with the 'SaveImage' node.

This workflow is particularly useful for creating dynamic animations from static images, making it invaluable for content creators and marketers looking to enhance visual storytelling. By utilizing nodes like 'DownloadAndLoadLivePortraitModels' and 'ImageResizeKJv2', users can ensure that the models and images are optimized for the best performance and quality. The workflow's integration with custom nodes such as 'comfyui-kjnodes' and 'comfyui-liveportraitkj' further enhances its capability to deliver realistic and expressive animations.
howToUse: Load your portrait image using the 'LoadImage' node.
Import the reference expression video via the 'VHS_LoadVideo' node.
Ensure the LivePortrait models are downloaded and loaded using 'DownloadAndLoadLivePortraitModels'.
Run the 'LivePortraitProcess' node to map expressions from the video to the portrait.
Use 'LivePortraitComposite' to apply and refine the expressions on the portrait.
Save the final animated video using 'VHS_VideoCombine' and 'SaveImage' nodes.
suggestedUseCases: Create engaging social media content by animating static profile pictures with expressive movements.
Enhance digital marketing campaigns with personalized video messages that feature dynamic facial expressions.
Develop interactive storytelling experiences in video games or virtual reality by animating character portraits.
Produce educational content where historical figures or characters come to life with realistic expressions.

b6e55869de51.title: HiDream I1 Full
b6e55869de51.description: Generate images with HiDream I1 Full - Complete version with 50 inference steps for highest quality output.
b6e55869de51.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial for HiDream I1 Full: SD3-style text-to-image with 50 steps, UniPC sampler, and shift=3.0 for high-quality, prompt-accurate results.
b6e55869de51.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow generates high-quality images with the HiDream I1 Full model using a clean, SD3-style pipeline. It loads the HiDream UNet via UNETLoader, the matching text encoders with QuadrupleCLIPLoader, and prepares the canvas with EmptySD3LatentImage. Prompts are processed by CLIPTextEncode (positive and negative), sampling is configured through ModelSamplingSD3 (including the model-specific shift parameter), and KSampler performs 50 inference steps with the UniPC sampler and Simple scheduler for stable, detailed outputs. Finally, VAEDecode converts latents back to RGB and SaveImage writes the results to disk.

The included settings mirror HiDream’s official recommendations: steps=50, sampler=uni_pc, scheduler=simple, cfg=5.0, and shift=3.0. This combination is optimized for fidelity and prompt adherence, making it a strong starting point for cinematic, moody, or stylized scenes. Because the workflow uses EmptySD3LatentImage and QuadrupleCLIPLoader, it stays compatible with SD3-style prompts and latent geometry, while VAELoader ensures proper decoding for consistent color and detail.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. In the “Step 1 - Load Models” group, point UNETLoader to your HiDream I1 Full weights (e.g., hidream_i1_full_fp16.safetensors or the fp8 variant) and set VAELoader to a HiDream-compatible VAE.
Use QuadrupleCLIPLoader to load the provided HiDream text encoders. Ensure all four encoders resolve correctly so CLIPTextEncode can process both positive and negative prompts.
In “Step 2 - Image size,” set EmptySD3LatentImage width/height, seed, and batch size. Use dimensions divisible by 8 (commonly by 64) for best stability and speed.
In “Step3 - Prompt,” enter your positive prompt in one CLIPTextEncode node and your negative prompt (e.g., "bad, ugly, jpeg artifacts") in the other. Keep prompts concise but descriptive.

Open ModelSamplingSD3 and confirm the official HiDream Full settings: shift=3.0. In KSampler, set steps=50, sampler=uni_pc, scheduler=simple, and cfg=5.0. Adjust only if you understand the trade-offs.
Run the graph. Inspect the decoded output from VAEDecode and retrieve final images from SaveImage. If needed, vary the seed or tweak width/height and prompts to iterate.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic concept art and moody environment design
Lo‑fi, grungy photography aesthetics (e.g., Polaroid-style looks)
Stylized product mockups with strong prompt control
Album covers and poster art requiring high detail and coherence
Atmospheric landscapes with dramatic lighting and color

faqItems.question: Which files do I need and where do they go?
faqItems.answer: Place the HiDream I1 Full UNet weights (e.g., hidream_i1_full_fp16.safetensors or the fp8 variant) in ComfyUI/models/unet. Load the HiDream text encoders via QuadrupleCLIPLoader (store them in your models/clip or text_encoders directory, matching your setup). Load a compatible VAE via VAELoader.

faqItems.question: What do the official sampling settings do?
faqItems.answer: They match HiDream’s recommended configuration: steps=50, sampler=uni_pc, scheduler=simple, cfg=5.0, and shift=3.0 (set in ModelSamplingSD3). This balance typically yields strong detail and prompt adherence with stable convergence.

faqItems.question: Can I change resolution, steps, or sampler?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Increase width/height (divisible by 8) for more detail at the cost of VRAM/time. Fewer steps (e.g., 30–40) are faster but may reduce fidelity. You can try other samplers/schedulers in KSampler, but UniPC + Simple is the recommended baseline for HiDream Full.

faqItems.question: How do I reduce artifacts or oversharpening?
faqItems.answer: Use a clear negative prompt (e.g., "bad, ugly, jpeg artifacts"). Keep CFG near 5.0, and avoid overly long prompts. If images look harsh, try a slightly lower CFG or reduce resolution. Ensure the correct VAE is loaded to prevent color or contrast issues.
