c3c9d32dc9fd.metaDescription: ComfyUI text-to-image tutorial using Nano Banana 2 via GeminiNanoBanana2V2. Generate one image per prompt and auto-save with SaveImage—fast, no file inputs.
c3c9d32dc9fd.extendedDescription:
Nano Banana 2: Text to Image is a minimal, fast text-to-image workflow built around two nodes: GeminiNanoBanana2V2 for generation and SaveImage for output. You type a prompt, the GeminiNanoBanana2V2 node calls the Nano Banana 2 model (via API) to synthesize a single image, and SaveImage writes the result to disk—no file inputs or extra wiring required. This makes it ideal for rapid prototyping, concept art exploration, and testing prompt ideas without managing complex graph pieces.

Technically, GeminiNanoBanana2V2 encapsulates the full text-to-image process: it accepts your prompt (and any parameters the node exposes, such as seed, size, or guidance), sends the request to the Nano Banana 2 model, then returns an image tensor to ComfyUI. The SaveImage node then handles file naming and persistence to the ComfyUI output folder. Because the heavy lifting runs through an API, setup overhead is low, and iteration speed is high. For consistency across runs, set a fixed seed if the node provides it; otherwise expect natural variation between generations.
howToUse: Load the workflow: In ComfyUI, click Load and open the "Nano Banana 2: Text to Image" workflow JSON.
Enter your prompt: Open the GeminiNanoBanana2V2 node and type a clear, specific text prompt. If the node exposes fields like negative prompt, guidance/CFG, steps, or size, adjust them as needed.
Control consistency (optional): If a Seed field is available, set a fixed seed for reproducible results. Leave it random for more variation across runs.
Configure saving: In the SaveImage node, set a filename prefix (e.g., nano_banana_test) and verify the output directory (ComfyUI/output by default).
Generate: Click Queue Prompt. Watch the generated image appear in the viewer. The final file will be saved automatically by SaveImage to the configured output directory.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept art and mood boards from quick prompt iterations
Product thumbnail or hero image drafts for early-stage design
Creative writing aids—visualizing scenes, characters, or settings
UI/UX ideation mockups and decorative assets
Teaching prompt engineering basics with a minimal, low-friction graph

faqItems.question: Do I need a local GPU to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No. The GeminiNanoBanana2V2 node is API-based and runs the Nano Banana 2 model remotely. You just provide text prompts; the result streams back into ComfyUI.

faqItems.question: Where are my images saved?
faqItems.answer: The SaveImage node writes files to ComfyUI/output (by default). You can set a custom filename prefix in the node to keep results organized.

faqItems.question: How can I make results reproducible?
faqItems.answer: If the GeminiNanoBanana2V2 node exposes a Seed field, set it to a fixed value and keep prompt/parameters unchanged. Without a fixed seed, results may vary across runs.

faqItems.question: How do I improve prompt adherence or detail?
faqItems.answer: Use precise, descriptive prompts and, if available, increase guidance/CFG or steps moderately. Also try providing a negative prompt to steer away from unwanted elements.

c3db37d05338.title: HiDream O1 Dev
c3db37d05338.description: Input a text prompt and optional reference images. Generate a high-resolution image (up to 2048x2048) with support for text-to-image, image editing, and subject-driven personalization.
c3db37d05338.metaDescription: HiDream O1 ComfyUI tutorial for text-to-image and image editing with reference images. Generate up to 2048×2048 with LCM or standard sampling.
c3db37d05338.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow shows how to generate high‑resolution images with HiDream O1 using either pure text prompts or image‑guided editing and personalization. It loads the HiDream-O1-Image checkpoint with CheckpointLoaderSimple, encodes your prompt via CLIPTextEncode (fed from a PrimitiveStringMultiline prompt field), and routes conditioning from up to 10 reference images through the HiDreamO1ReferenceImages node for subject‑driven control. For text‑to‑image, an EmptyHiDreamO1LatentImage node initializes the canvas at your chosen size; for image edit, LoadImage feeds through ImageScaleToTotalPixels (optional) and GetImageSize so the latent shape matches the source. Sampling is handled by either SamplerLCM for fast, low‑step generation or SamplerCustom for traditional diffusion control, with BasicScheduler and ModelNoiseScale to match HiDream O1’s training noise characteristics. The result is decoded by VAEDecode, previewed with PreviewAny, and saved with SaveImage. A ComfySwitchNode and PrimitiveBoolean switches make it easy to toggle between text‑to‑image and image‑editing paths and to enable features.

Technically, the workflow is tuned around HiDream O1’s preferred training resolutions for best fidelity (e.g., 2048×2048 square, 2304×1728 and 2304×1792 landscape, per the Author Notes). Sticking close to these sizes improves detail and composition stability. The ImageScaleToTotalPixels utility prevents oversized edits from exceeding memory by down‑scaling to a pixel budget, while ModelNoiseScale provides fine control over how much the sampler explores versus adheres to reference images and the prompt (lower noise can better preserve identity; higher noise allows more creative deviation). This setup is practical for high‑resolution character portraits, product shots, and consistent subject renderings, all within a clear, switchable pipeline that supports both text‑only ideation and image‑guided refinement.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then open the Model group. In CheckpointLoaderSimple, select the HiDream-O1-Image model (from Hugging Face or ModelScope).
Enter your description in the User Prompt (PrimitiveStringMultiline). Keep it clear and specific; this feeds CLIPTextEncode for text conditioning.
Choose a mode: in the I2V or Image Edit Switch / Feature Switch group, use the ComfySwitchNode or PrimitiveBoolean to toggle between Text-to-Image and Image Edit.

For Image Edit: add one or more LoadImage nodes with your source and optional reference images, then connect references to HiDreamO1ReferenceImages. If the input is too large, Select the ImageScaleToTotalPixels node and press Ctrl+B to enable it, then set a safe pixel budget.

Set resolution: for Text-to-Image, configure EmptyHiDreamO1LatentImage in the Size: Text to Image group (prefer trained sizes like 2048×2048 or 2304×1728). For Image Edit, sizes flow from GetImageSize; optionally rescale via ImageScaleToTotalPixels.

Pick a sampler: use SamplerLCM for fast low-step results or SamplerCustom for fine control. Leave BasicScheduler at its default initially and adjust ModelNoiseScale if you need stronger identity adherence. Run the graph, review in PreviewAny, then save with SaveImage.
suggestedUseCases: Subject-driven portraits: Generate consistent character or person portraits by supplying 2–6 clear reference images.
Product visualization: Create clean, high-res product shots from text or refine existing photos while preserving design details.
Style-lock branding: Maintain a brand’s visual style across variations using the same reference set and prompt template.
Photo-to-illustration edits: Transform input photos into stylized illustrations while keeping subject identity recognizable.
Scene upgrades: Replace backgrounds or enhance composition in existing images while guiding results with reference imagery.

faqItems.question: How many reference images can I use with HiDream O1?
faqItems.answer: Up to 10. Add additional LoadImage nodes and connect them to the HiDreamO1ReferenceImages node to condition the model on multiple references.

faqItems.question: What resolutions work best?
faqItems.answer: Stick to HiDream O1’s trained sizes or close aspect ratios for best fidelity. The Author Notes list 2048×2048 (square), 2304×1728 and 2304×1792 (landscape). For Image Edit, consider resizing inputs to these ratios.

faqItems.question: When should I use SamplerLCM vs SamplerCustom?
faqItems.answer: Use SamplerLCM for fast drafts and good quality at low steps (often under a dozen). Use SamplerCustom for maximum control (more steps, different algorithms) when you need fine detail or tighter prompt adherence.

faqItems.question: My source image is very large and causes VRAM issues. What should I do?
faqItems.answer: Enable ImageScaleToTotalPixels (Select it and press Ctrl+B) to downscale the input by a pixel budget. This keeps memory usage manageable while preserving the input’s aspect ratio.

faqItems.question: How do I encourage stronger identity preservation from references?
faqItems.answer: Use high-quality, well-lit reference images, keep 2–6 diverse angles, and lower ModelNoiseScale slightly to reduce randomness. Avoid extreme size changes from the reference aspect ratio.

c3e308dab99b.title: Product Placement (Flux.2 Klein)
c3e308dab99b.description: Drop in up to 3 product shots and a reference composition, and this workflow places your products into the scene with accurate label text, packaging detail, and lighting that matches the reference. Fully open source stack: Qwen3-VL reads your inputs and writes the edit prompt, Flux.2 Klein 9B handles the multi-image composite, and LTX-2.3 animates the final placement into a product spot. Batch concatenation and auto-scaling keep inputs sharp at any resolution. Runs on Comfy Cloud out of the box, or locally on your own hardware. No closed APIs.
c3e308dab99b.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow for product placement using Qwen3-VL, Flux.2 Klein, and LTX-2.3. Drop in products + reference, get a realistic composite and short video.
c3e308dab99b.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow automates realistic product placement using an open-source stack. You provide up to three product shots plus a reference composition, and the graph places the products into the scene with text-aware detail and lighting that follows the reference. A Qwen3-VL stage inspects your inputs and writes a context-rich edit prompt, Flux.2 Klein 9B performs the multi-image composite, and LTX-2.3 turns the final still into a short, polished product spot. Core utility nodes like LoadImage, PreviewImage, PreviewAny, BatchImagesNode, StringConcatenate, and SaveVideo make it easy to iterate and export.

Technically, the product and reference images are loaded, batched, and auto-scaled so Flux.2 Klein receives sharp, consistent inputs regardless of your source resolution. The prompt is assembled by Qwen3-VL (guided via StringConcatenate) and passed into the Flux.2 sampler to condition placement, label fidelity, and scene lighting. After the composite is approved in PreviewImage/PreviewAny, LTX-2.3 generates a short motion segment from the final placement and SaveVideo writes the result to disk. The custom inference nodes (461b058e-342d-497e-aac1-a5fb6551e33a, fdd45ff8-8dff-43e8-b2c0-2d26053388b8, 6dbca6ef-ca4b-4af8-a99b-b834745f3a9b, 5c2c98c8-2e8f-47ca-9403-686e35a5ef94, 04e3b3b1-a711-485c-be05-f59f9507bd4e, ffacbfba-7659-45df-a3b8-7560f4800088) encapsulate the model runners and scaling/conditioning logic so you can run fully locally or on Comfy Cloud—no closed APIs.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the models are available: Qwen3-VL for prompt generation, Flux.2 Klein 9B for image compositing, and LTX-2.3 for image-to-video. If missing, download and point the custom inference nodes to their weights.

Import your assets: up to three product shots and one reference composition using the LoadImage nodes. Prefer high-resolution PNGs (alpha backgrounds if available) for products, and a well-lit, on-brand reference image.

Generate and review the edit prompt: run the Qwen3-VL stage to analyze the inputs. Inspect the generated instructions in PreviewAny/PreviewImage. If needed, refine the wording or add constraints (e.g., placement, scale, orientation, lighting) in the StringConcatenate node.

Place the products: execute the Flux.2 Klein composite stage. The BatchImagesNode and the auto-scaling node (04e3b3b1-a711-485c-be05-f59f9507bd4e) handle batching and resolution. Review outputs in PreviewImage; iterate on the prompt or input order until labels, edges, and shadows look right.

Animate the result: send the approved still into the LTX-2.3 stage to create a short motion segment (e.g., subtle camera move or lighting emphasis). Adjust duration and fps as exposed by the node, then render.
Export: verify the result in PreviewAny and save using SaveVideo. If you hit memory limits, reduce resolution or animation length, or disable unused product slots before re-running.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid mockups for social ads and marketplace listings using real packaging and on-brand scenes.
A/B testing hero images by swapping different SKUs into the same reference composition.
Pitch decks and client reviews where you need fast, realistic product-in-context visuals.
E-commerce refreshes: update packaging or flavor variants while keeping consistent lighting and framing.
Previsualization for product videos before committing to a full shoot.

faqItems.question: Do I have to use all three product slots?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow supports 1–3 products. Leave unused LoadImage nodes empty; the BatchImagesNode will process only the images you provide.

faqItems.question: How do I get sharp labels and accurate packaging detail?
faqItems.answer: Use high-resolution product shots (ideally with clean, front-facing labels) and transparent PNGs if possible. Keep the reference image close to your target output resolution. If text or edges look soft, increase input resolution, refine the Qwen3-VL prompt via StringConcatenate, or reduce the final output size.

faqItems.question: Can I run this fully offline?
faqItems.answer: Yes. All stages run locally with open models (Qwen3-VL, Flux.2 Klein 9B, LTX-2.3) through the custom inference nodes (e.g., 461b058e…, fdd45ff8…, 6dbca6ef…, 5c2c98c8…, 04e3b3b1…, ffacbfba…). Ensure you have the model weights installed and paths set in the node settings.

faqItems.question: What if I run out of VRAM or the video render is slow?
faqItems.answer: Lower the working resolution, shorten the LTX-2.3 duration, or disable any unused image slots. You can also run the composite first at a smaller size, lock a good seed, then upscale for a final pass if your hardware allows.

c4144012a64c.title: Rodin Gen2.5: Image to Model
c4144012a64c.description: Upload single or multi-view images to create a 3D model with adjustable quality and enhanced texture
c4144012a64c.metaDescription: Turn single or multi-view photos into a textured 3D GLB using Rodin Gen2.5 in ComfyUI. Adjustable quality and enhanced textures for fast, clean results.
c4144012a64c.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial walks you through Rodin Gen2.5: Image to Model, a compact workflow that turns one or more reference photos into a textured 3D asset. It uses three nodes end-to-end: LoadImage to bring your photo(s) into the graph, Rodin3D_Gen25_Image to reconstruct geometry and textures using the Rodin Gen2.5 model, and SaveGLB to export a ready-to-share GLB file.

Under the hood, the Rodin3D_Gen25_Image node sends your single- or multi-view inputs to the Rodin Gen2.5 backend and returns a normalized mesh with UVs and embedded textures. The node exposes practical controls like a quality setting (to trade speed for fidelity) and a texture enhancement option (to sharpen and upscale surfaces). Single-view inputs rely on strong learned priors to infer hidden geometry; multi-view inputs enforce cross-view consistency to reduce holes and improve texture accuracy. The SaveGLB node then packages everything into a single GLB so you can preview in a web viewer, import into Blender, or drop into an engine.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and confirm the three core nodes are present: LoadImage → Rodin3D_Gen25_Image → SaveGLB.

In LoadImage, select your reference photo. For multi-view, add additional views of the same object (front/side/back/top) and feed them to the Rodin3D_Gen25_Image images input if your node version supports batches.

Open the Rodin3D_Gen25_Image node and choose a quality level that fits your deadline and fidelity needs. Enable texture enhancement if you want sharper surface detail (this may increase processing time).
Queue the workflow. The Rodin3D_Gen25_Image node will process your image(s) and output a reconstructed mesh with textures.
The SaveGLB node writes the result to your ComfyUI output directory as a single .glb. Open it in a GLB viewer or import into DCC tools (e.g., Blender) to inspect.
If you see missing areas or soft textures, add more viewpoints with consistent lighting, increase quality and texture enhancement, then re-run.
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce: Generate quick 3D previews of products from a few controlled photos.
Concept art and game prototyping: Block out textured assets rapidly before manual cleanup.
AR/VR previews: Create lightweight GLB models for web or mobile AR try-ons and scene mockups.
Industrial or design reviews: Share quick 3D turntables of physical prototypes without full photogrammetry.
Education and documentation: Produce illustrative 3D references of objects for training materials.

faqItems.question: How many images should I use for best results?
faqItems.answer: The node accepts single or multi-view inputs. A single well-framed photo can work, but 6–12 views around the object (covering front, sides, slight up/down angles) significantly improves completeness and texture consistency. Keep lighting and exposure consistent across views.

faqItems.question: What does the quality and texture enhancement do?
faqItems.answer: Quality increases reconstruction fidelity (at the cost of longer processing). Texture enhancement focuses on sharper, higher-detail textures. If you need a fast preview, start with lower quality and enhancement off; for final results, raise quality and enable texture enhancement.

faqItems.question: What format do I get, and can I use it elsewhere?
faqItems.answer: This workflow saves a single .glb via the SaveGLB node, with the mesh and embedded texture(s) in one file. You can open it in most web viewers, Blender, or convert to other formats (e.g., OBJ/FBX) using DCC tools if needed.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key or internet connection?
faqItems.answer: The Rodin3D_Gen25_Image node uses the Rodin Gen2.5 backend (tagged as API). If your installation requires authentication, add your API key in the node or environment settings. An internet connection is required while the node processes your images.

c4dd9da11fe4.title: Tripo P1: Multiview to Model
c4dd9da11fe4.description: Upload an image or multi-view references to generate a clean low-poly 3D model with controlled polygon count and organized topology, ready for export to game engines.
c4dd9da11fe4.metaDescription: Convert single or multi-view images to clean low‑poly 3D with Tripo in ComfyUI. Control polycount, UVs, optional rigging, and export GLB for game engines.
c4dd9da11fe4.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow reconstructs a low‑poly 3D asset from one or multiple reference images using the Tripo model, then prepares it for real‑time use. Starting with LoadImage, your references feed into TripoP1MultiviewToModelNode, which estimates geometry from single or multiview inputs to produce a clean base mesh. TripoTextureNodeV2 then unwraps UVs and bakes a texture atlas from your images, while TripoConversionNode handles practical cleanup like scaling to units, recentering, normal orientation, and decimation so you can precisely control polygon density.

For animation‑ready output, the optional TripoRigNode adds a simple rig, and TripoRetargetNode can adapt that rig to a reference skeleton you provide. Finally, SaveGLB exports a compact GLB that imports cleanly into engines like Unity or Unreal. The result is a game‑ready asset with controlled polycount, organized topology, and consistent UVs—ideal for rapid prototyping, asset libraries, or previews.
howToUse: Open the workflow and enable the Tripo Toolset group: select the group named "Tripo Toolset" and press Ctrl+B to enable it.

Load your references: use one or multiple LoadImage nodes. Connect the loaded image(s) to TripoP1MultiviewToModelNode. For best reconstruction, provide front, 3/4, and side views with consistent lighting and minimal background clutter.
Configure reconstruction: in TripoP1MultiviewToModelNode, set quality or multiview options as available. Keep inputs consistent in subject scale and framing to help the model align features.

Generate UVs and textures: in TripoTextureNodeV2, set the texture resolution (e.g., 1K–4K) and padding/margin if exposed. Connect its output to downstream nodes so the final mesh includes a baked texture atlas.

Optimize the mesh: in TripoConversionNode, adjust scale and origin, fix normals if needed, and set your target poly budget using decimation or target‑face controls. Preview intermediate outputs to confirm silhouette quality before exporting.

Optional animation prep and export: if needed, run TripoRigNode to create a basic rig and use TripoRetargetNode to match your reference skeleton. Finally, connect to SaveGLB and run the workflow to export a GLB ready for import into your game engine or DCC.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid prototyping of environment props from quick phone photos, with controlled poly budgets for real‑time scenes.
Creating lightweight hero previews of products or characters from studio turnarounds.
Generating textured placeholders for level design before commissioning high‑detail assets.
Converting moodboard or concept turnarounds into rough 3D block‑ins for look‑dev and layout.

faqItems.question: Do I need multiple images, or will a single photo work?
faqItems.answer: A single photo works, but multiview inputs (front, 3/4, side) significantly improve shape accuracy and texture coverage. Use consistent lighting and framing for best results.

faqItems.question: How do I control the polygon count?
faqItems.answer: Use TripoConversionNode to decimate the mesh. Adjust its decimation or target‑poly settings to meet your budget while preserving key silhouettes.

faqItems.question: My model imports too large/small or off‑center. How do I fix that?
faqItems.answer: In TripoConversionNode, set scale units and recenter the origin. You can also ensure normals are consistent and the mesh is oriented to your engine’s up‑axis before exporting with SaveGLB.

faqItems.question: Can I rig and animate the result?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Use TripoRigNode to create a basic skeleton, then TripoRetargetNode to map it onto a reference skeleton you provide. Export the rigged GLB and animate in your DCC or game engine.

c51538d3e644.title: Prompt Multi Batch Generation
c51538d3e644.description: Send multiple prompts simultaneously to generate independent outputs in a single queue. Connect to Blueprint or Partner Nodes for batch processing of any modality. Use for prompt variation comparisons and batch generation.
c51538d3e644.metaDescription: Compare multiple prompts simultaneously with ComfyUI's batch generation workflow, optimizing time and resources for prompt variation analysis.
c51538d3e644.extendedDescription: The 'Prompt Multi Batch Generation' workflow in ComfyUI offers a powerful approach to comparing multiple prompts simultaneously. By utilizing the FL_PromptMulti node, users can send different prompts at the same time, each generating its own output independently. This setup is ideal for batch processing where variations in prompts need to be evaluated quickly and efficiently. The workflow is particularly useful when connected to Blueprint or Partner Nodes, enabling users to process different modalities in a batch, thus saving time and resources. One of the key differences in this workflow is the ability to handle multiple prompts in a single queue entry, which contrasts with traditional methods that require sequential processing. This parallel processing capability allows for faster iteration and comparison, although it requires careful management of resources, as each prompt slot equates to a separate run, potentially increasing costs when using Partner Nodes.
howToUse: Open ComfyUI and load the 'Prompt Multi Batch Generation' workflow.
Configure the FL_PromptMulti node with your desired prompts, filling each slot with a different variation.
Connect the workflow to Blueprint or Partner Nodes if batch processing across modalities is needed.
Run the workflow to generate outputs for each prompt simultaneously.
Review the generated images, noting differences and similarities to assess prompt effectiveness.
Adjust prompts as needed and rerun to refine results or explore new variations.
suggestedUseCases: Testing multiple creative concepts for a marketing campaign to determine which resonates best.
Conducting A/B testing for visual elements in user interface design.
Exploring different artistic styles or themes in digital art projects.
Batch processing of prompts for rapid prototyping in game development.
Evaluating prompt effectiveness in generating specific image attributes for research purposes.

faqItems.question: How does the FL_PromptMulti node improve efficiency?
faqItems.answer: The FL_PromptMulti node allows multiple prompts to be processed simultaneously, reducing the time needed for sequential runs and enabling quicker comparisons.

faqItems.question: What should I consider when using Partner Nodes?
faqItems.answer: Each prompt slot corresponds to a separate run, which can increase costs when using Partner Nodes, so it's important to manage resources carefully.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow handle different modalities?
faqItems.answer: Yes, when connected to Blueprint or Partner Nodes, the workflow can process different modalities in a batch, making it versatile for various applications.

faqItems.question: What are the benefits of using this workflow for prompt variation comparisons?
faqItems.answer: This workflow allows for rapid testing and iteration of multiple prompts, providing immediate insights into which variations are most effective for your goals.

c5cbee07611f.title: Comfy for Advertising - OOH Visualization
c5cbee07611f.metaDescription: Reformat a poster and place it into realistic OOH scenes. Batch aspect ratios, optional prompt-guided scene notes, and perspective placement for fast ad mockups.
c5cbee07611f.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow helps brand and creative teams quickly place an existing poster into realistic Out-of-Home (OOH) scenarios. It’s organized in two clear stages. STEP 1 – POSTER REFORMAT takes your source poster and non-destructively reformats it to multiple aspect ratios (vertical, horizontal, square, or custom) while preserving the original design. This stage is driven by LoadImage, PrimitiveNode (for width/height values), PrimitiveBoolean (to enable/disable formats), ComfySwitchNode (to route only the formats you want), and BatchImagesNode (to package multiple outputs). SaveImage captures clean, reformatted versions ready for placement.

STEP 2 – OOH VISUALIZATION composites a chosen reformatted poster into a real or described environment. You can supply a location photo with LoadImage via the IMAGE ENVIRONMENT group or describe a scene in plain language (for example, "OOH billboard in downtown San Francisco, on top of a two-story building, pedestrian eye level") in the PROMPT ENVIRONMENT group. GeminiImage2Node is used as a prompt helper to convert your plain-language description into structured scene notes and file-name context. Two custom processing nodes (ae42e662-5e2b-4f52-b31d-267bd68f1c6f and 88b611c3-ce43-4e7a-a59f-dd16f57a8853) handle the perspective mapping and blending of the poster onto the target surface, so you can fine-tune scale, skew, and overlay strength for believable placement. SaveImage then outputs the final mockups, optionally in batches, so you can compare formats and scenes side by side.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the STEP 1 – POSTER REFORMAT group. Use LoadImage to import your source poster.

Set your desired aspect ratios and sizes with PrimitiveNode values (e.g., vertical, horizontal, square). Toggle which formats to generate with the PrimitiveBoolean switches; ComfySwitchNode will route only the ones you enable.
Run STEP 1 to produce clean, reformatted poster variants. BatchImagesNode organizes these, and SaveImage will write them to disk for review.

Choose your environment input path: either load a real photo in the IMAGE ENVIRONMENT group with LoadImage, or enter a plain-language description in PROMPT ENVIRONMENT. If you write a description (e.g., “downtown San Francisco billboard, two-story rooftop, pedestrian POV”), GeminiImage2Node will turn it into helpful scene notes and naming context.

In STEP 2 – OOH VISUALIZATION, select which reformatted poster to place. Use the OOH placement/blending controls exposed by the custom nodes (ae42e662-5e2b-4f52-b31d-267bd68f1c6f and 88b611c3-ce43-4e7a-a59f-dd16f57a8853) to adjust scale, perspective, and blend so the poster aligns with the billboard surface.
Preview, then SaveImage your final mockups. If you enabled multiple aspect ratios or environments, let BatchImagesNode and SaveImage export a consistent set for stakeholder review.
suggestedUseCases: Pitch decks: Rapidly visualize a campaign poster across vertical, horizontal, and square formats on real-world billboards.
Client reviews: Show the same creative on different OOH locations (street-level, rooftop, transit shelter) for context and scale.
Market testing: Generate consistent mockups for A/B testing across aspect ratios and placements.
Brand guidelines: Demonstrate safe area and legibility by placing reformatted artwork onto typical OOH frames.
Portfolio and case studies: Create compelling, realistic environment visuals from a single master poster.

faqItems.question: Do I need to use the prompt-based environment, or can I use my own photos?
faqItems.answer: You can do either. Use IMAGE ENVIRONMENT with LoadImage to supply a real location photo, or use PROMPT ENVIRONMENT if you want GeminiImage2Node to turn your plain-language description into scene notes and file-name context. You can switch between paths with the provided switches.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow keep my poster’s aspect ratio intact when reformatting?
faqItems.answer: STEP 1 reformats by resizing and padding/cropping according to the PrimitiveNode dimensions you set, driven by toggles in PrimitiveBoolean and routing via ComfySwitchNode. This preserves your design while producing standard OOH-friendly canvases (vertical, horizontal, square, or custom).

faqItems.question: What do the custom nodes (ae42e662-5e2b-4f52-b31d-267bd68f1c6f and 88b611c3-ce43-4e7a-a59f-dd16f57a8853) do?
faqItems.answer: They handle the OOH placement step: warping the selected poster to match the billboard plane and blending it into the scene. Use their UI controls to fine-tune perspective (corner/scale/rotation) and the blend for a realistic result.

faqItems.question: Can I batch-export multiple formats and placements at once?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Enable the formats you want with the PrimitiveBoolean switches in STEP 1. Then, in STEP 2, connect those outputs to your chosen environment path. BatchImagesNode and SaveImage will export a consistent set of mockups in one run.

c5e28a935db5.title: Bria: Virtual Try-On
c5e28a935db5.description: Dress the person in a photo with a garment from a separate product shot using Bria. One person photo plus one to three garments or accessories produces a worn look in which the face, pose and background stay untouched and the garment is refitted to the body. Ideal for fashion catalogs and lookbooks without a photoshoot.
c5e28a935db5.metaDescription: Dress a person photo with 1–3 product garments using Bria Virtual Try-On in ComfyUI. Preserves face, pose, and background—ideal for catalogs and lookbooks.
c5e28a935db5.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial shows how to use the BriaVirtualTryOn node (BRIA model) to dress a person in a photo with one to three product images. You feed one person photo and one or more garment or accessory shots through LoadImage nodes, then the BriaVirtualTryOn node sends them to Bria’s API to generate a realistic worn look. The workflow keeps the person’s face, pose, and background intact while refitting the product to the body. Results return at roughly one megapixel, ready to preview, compare, and export.

Under the hood, BriaVirtualTryOn performs body parsing and pose-aware garment warping, then composites the result with occlusion handling so sleeves, collars, and edges look natural around arms and torso. In this workflow, LoadImage nodes provide the inputs, ImageCompare helps you review before/after, and SaveImage writes the final image to disk. Because this node calls Bria’s cloud service, you’ll need a Bria API key, and your images are processed remotely.
howToUse: Open the Bria: Virtual Try-On workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the BriaVirtualTryOn node is present alongside LoadImage, ImageCompare, and SaveImage.
Enter your Bria API key in the BriaVirtualTryOn node (or in your global settings, depending on your Bria node install).

Use LoadImage to import a single-person photo where the upper body (or relevant area) is clearly visible. Use additional LoadImage nodes to import 1–3 product shots (e.g., catalog or flat-lay) of the garments or accessories you want to try on.

Connect the person image and the garment image(s) to the BriaVirtualTryOn node as indicated by the workflow. Keep product shots clean (solid or simple backgrounds) and front-facing for best alignment.
Queue/Execute the workflow. The BriaVirtualTryOn node will call the BRIA API and return a composited try-on image at about 1 MP. Use the ImageCompare node output to review the before/after.
Adjust inputs (different product photo, tighter crop on the person, or a clearer garment image) if needed, then SaveImage to export the final result.
suggestedUseCases: Ecommerce catalog and lookbook generation without organizing full photoshoots
A/B testing garment styles, colors, or accessories on the same model photo
Rapid content creation for marketplaces and storefronts using consistent model imagery
Styling previews for brand pitching, social content, and merchandising mockups
Batch asset preparation for seasonal updates or localized campaigns

faqItems.question: What input images work best?
faqItems.answer: Use a person photo with exactly one subject, clear visibility of the area you plan to dress (torso/full body), and minimal occlusion (e.g., avoid crossed arms over the garment area). For products, use front-facing catalog or flat-lay shots on a clean background with good lighting.

faqItems.question: How many garments can I apply at once?
faqItems.answer: The BriaVirtualTryOn node supports one to three garments or accessories in a single run. For best realism, avoid heavy overlap between items and stick to compatible categories (e.g., top + outerwear + accessory).

faqItems.question: Will the face or background change?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow is designed to preserve the person’s face, pose, and background. Only the garment area is refitted and composited.

faqItems.question: What about resolution and publishing?
faqItems.answer: The result is approximately one megapixel. For higher-resolution needs, export with SaveImage and optionally run a separate upscaling step in another workflow. Keep in mind the try-on is generated via Bria’s API, so you’ll need a valid API key and your images are processed in the cloud.

c5ed0bca3748.title: FLUX 3 Image Klein Distilled: Image Edit
c5ed0bca3748.description: Edit an existing image with FLUX 3 Image Klein by pairing one input image with one text prompt, producing a single edited result and a side-by-side comparison view. Ideal for targeted retouching, restyling a photo, or swapping details while keeping the rest of the scene intact.
c5ed0bca3748.metaDescription: Compare prompt-only, reference-guided, and box-constrained image edits in FLUX 3 Image Klein with side-by-side results to choose the best editing strategy.
c5ed0bca3748.extendedDescription:
This workflow compares three editing strategies within the same model—FLUX 3 Image Klein—so you can decide how to best modify an existing photo while preserving what matters. Using a fixed sampler setup (KSampler, 50 steps, CFG ~3.5, Euler/Simple) and a locked seed, it produces a side-by-side view (ImageCompare) of the original versus the edited result. You can run multiple passes, toggling only the technique under test, to make an apples-to-apples judgment.

The three approaches are: 1) prompt-only edits using CLIPTextEncode, 2) reference-guided edits by inserting one or more images into ReferenceMultiLatent and calling them in the prompt (<ref_image_0>, <ref_image_1>, …), and 3) localized, box-constrained edits that pair CreateBoundingBoxes with Flux3LayoutPrompt for precise, region-specific changes. ConditioningZeroOut is available to isolate local instructions when testing box-only effects. Keep image size constant via EmptyFlux2LatentImage to ensure a fair comparison of content retention, style changes, and edit locality.
howToUse: Load your base photo with LoadImage and set your target resolution using EmptyFlux2LatentImage (keep size fixed across tests).

Pick one strategy to start: A) Prompt-only (CLIPTextEncode), B) Reference-guided by plugging images into ReferenceMultiLatent and using <ref_image_0> tokens in the prompt, or C) Box-constrained by drawing regions with CreateBoundingBoxes and binding text via Flux3LayoutPrompt.

Optionally toggle prompt enhancement paths with ComfySwitchNode (e.g., switch between PrimitiveStringMultiline and TextGenerate) to compare raw vs enhanced prompts while keeping other parameters identical.
Set KSampler with the same seed, 50 steps, CFG ~3.5, and adjust denoise strength for the edit intensity (start 0.25–0.45 for gentle edits). Keep these settings fixed when comparing approaches.

Run the workflow. Review ImageCompare to assess subject preservation, background stability, and how precisely changes were applied. Use PreviewAny to sanity-check intermediate conditioning or layout if needed.

Repeat with the other strategies or different reference assets (<ref_image_1>, <ref_image_2>, …). For fair comparisons, change only one factor at a time (technique, denoise, or prompt) and save outputs with SaveImage.
suggestedUseCases: Portrait retouching: compare prompt-only tweaks versus box-constrained touch-ups for localized fixes (skin, eyes, accessories).
Product restyling: test reference-guided edits to transfer material or color from a reference image versus global prompt changes.
Set dressing and prop swaps: evaluate box-constrained replacements to keep the scene intact while changing a small object.
Brand consistency checks: compare results when using multiple references (<ref_image_0>, <ref_image_1>) to maintain logos, type, or palettes.
Creative restyle tests: iterate prompt-only vs reference-guided to balance identity preservation with stronger stylistic shifts.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure a fair comparison between the three edit strategies?
faqItems.answer: Lock seed, steps (50), CFG (~3.5), image size (via EmptyFlux2LatentImage), and the base prompt. Change only the variable you’re testing (strategy, denoise, or references). Use ImageCompare for side-by-side review.

faqItems.question: When should I use reference images and how do <ref_image_n> tokens work?
faqItems.answer: Use ReferenceMultiLatent when you need to preserve identity or transfer specific details (e.g., fabric, accessories). Add images to the node in order and call them in the prompt as <ref_image_0>, <ref_image_1>, etc., so FLUX 3 Image Klein can condition on those visual cues.

faqItems.question: What’s the best way to localize edits without altering the whole image?
faqItems.answer: Use CreateBoundingBoxes to define regions and Flux3LayoutPrompt to bind text instructions to those boxes. If global text conditioning interferes, use ConditioningZeroOut to emphasize the box-specific instructions and reduce spillover.

faqItems.question: How do I control how much of the original image is preserved?
faqItems.answer: Adjust the KSampler denoise strength: lower values (~0.2–0.35) retain more of the original; higher values (~0.4–0.6) allow stronger changes. For consistent comparisons, vary denoise in small increments and keep other settings fixed.

c666b9b4014e.title: Squish Anything with LTX-2 I2V and LoRA
c666b9b4014e.description: Upload any image to apply the Squish It LoRA effect. Generate a squished animation using the LTX-2 I2V model.
c666b9b4014e.metaDescription: Transform images into squished animations with LTX-2 I2V and LoRA in ComfyUI. Perfect for creative video content.
c666b9b4014e.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow, titled 'Squish Anything with LTX-2 I2V and LoRA', enables users to transform static images into dynamic, squished animations. Leveraging the LTX-2 I2V model, this workflow takes an uploaded image and applies the Squish It LoRA effect to create a unique animated sequence. The workflow is designed to be intuitive, utilizing nodes such as LoadImage for importing images and SaveVideo for exporting the final animation. The b7c2d337-c38d-4c04-922b-2d638449d13e node plays a crucial role in managing the transformation process, ensuring that the animation maintains a smooth and consistent flow.

Technically, the workflow operates by first loading an image using the LoadImage node. The image is then processed through a subgraph node, which applies the Squish It LoRA effect. This effect is particularly effective at creating exaggerated, cartoon-like animations that can be both entertaining and visually striking. The LTX-2 I2V model is pivotal in this process, as it interprets the image data and generates a video sequence that reflects the squished effect. The final video is saved using the SaveVideo node, allowing for easy sharing and further editing if needed. This workflow is particularly useful for artists and content creators looking to add a playful, animated twist to their images.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure all necessary nodes are connected.
Use the LoadImage node to upload your desired image for transformation.
Ensure your image dimensions are divisible by 64 for optimal processing.
Adjust the frame count to be divisible by 8 + 1 to ensure smooth animation.
Run the workflow to apply the Squish It LoRA effect and generate the animation.
Use the SaveVideo node to export your final squished animation.
suggestedUseCases: Create engaging social media content with unique animated effects.
Enhance digital marketing materials with eye-catching animations.
Develop creative video intros or transitions for YouTube channels.
Produce fun and interactive educational content for children.
Add a whimsical touch to personal photo collections.

faqItems.question: What image formats are supported by the LoadImage node?
faqItems.answer: The LoadImage node supports common image formats such as JPEG, PNG, and BMP.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the squish effect intensity?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the intensity of the squish effect can be adjusted within the subgraph node settings.

faqItems.question: What resolution is recommended for the final video?
faqItems.answer: The default resolution is 720p, but you can use 1920x1088 if your system supports it.

faqItems.question: Will using invalid parameters cause errors?
faqItems.answer: No, the workflow will automatically adjust to the closest valid parameters without causing errors.

c671a3e5c6bc.title: Vidu Q1: Reference to Video
c671a3e5c6bc.description: Generate videos with consistent subjects using multiple reference images (up to 7) for character and style continuity across the video sequence.
c671a3e5c6bc.metaDescription: Create consistent subject videos using multiple reference images with the Vidu Q1 workflow in ComfyUI. Ideal for animation and branding.
c671a3e5c6bc.extendedDescription: The 'Vidu Q1: Reference to Video' workflow in ComfyUI is designed to generate videos with consistent subjects by utilizing multiple reference images. This technique is particularly useful for maintaining character and style continuity throughout a video sequence. The workflow leverages the Vidu Q1 and Vidu models, which are specialized for video generation tasks. Key nodes in this workflow include the ViduReferenceVideoNode, which processes up to seven reference images to ensure that the generated video maintains a coherent visual style and subject matter. The LoadImage and ImageBatch nodes are used to input and manage the reference images, while the SaveVideo node finalizes the output by saving the generated video file. This workflow is especially beneficial for creators looking to produce videos where character consistency is crucial, such as in animated storytelling or branding videos. c68aa1ba6830.title: PixVerse 6.0: Reference to Video
c68aa1ba6830.description: Create reference-driven videos with PixVerse V6, generating clips that follow the style, motion, and subject traits of your uploaded reference footage. Ideal for matching a specific visual identity across variations, extending a character or scene’s look to new actions, and producing consistent branded content from a single source clip.
c68aa1ba6830.metaDescription: Create reference-driven videos in ComfyUI with PixVerse V6: fuse subject and style images to generate consistent, brand-ready motion clips.
c68aa1ba6830.extendedDescription:
This workflow demonstrates reference-driven video generation in ComfyUI using the PixVerse V6 model. Two LoadImage nodes bring in your references (for example, a subject image like street_rider.png and a style/look image like futuristic_urban_editorial.png). These feed into a single PixverseV6FusionVideoNode, which fuses subject identity with a target art direction while following your text prompt to create motion. The resulting clip is written to disk by a SaveVideo node. A MarkdownNote in the graph provides quick, in-context guidance.

Technically, the PixverseV6FusionVideoNode encodes your reference images to anchor the character’s appearance and the overall visual language, then synthesizes a temporally coherent sequence guided by your prompt. This lets you adapt a consistent subject or brand look to new actions and scenes while maintaining recognizability. By controlling prompt phrasing and basic generation options (such as target duration, resolution, and how strongly the references influence the output), you can iterate from the same references to produce multiple, matching variations. The setup is lightweight—images in, video out—making it practical for style-matched content without rebuilding a pipeline each time.

For best results, use clean, well-lit references that match your target aspect ratio, and describe motion and framing explicitly in the prompt (e.g., "three-quarter body shot, slow dolly forward, sunset backlight"). Keep the subject image focused on the character you want to preserve, and choose a style image that clearly represents the palette, texture, and lighting you want across frames.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and review the MarkdownNote for a quick overview of inputs and tips.

Load your reference assets: connect a subject image (e.g., street_rider.png) and a style/look image (e.g., futuristic_urban_editorial.png) to the PixverseV6FusionVideoNode via the provided LoadImage nodes.

Open the PixverseV6FusionVideoNode and enter a clear prompt describing the subject’s action, camera movement, mood/lighting, and any key scene details. Set basic options like target resolution and clip duration (and, if available in your install, seed for reproducibility).
Queue and run the workflow. The PixVerse node generates the video sequence based on your references and prompt.
The SaveVideo node writes the result to your ComfyUI output folder. Preview the file and note where the style or subject fidelity needs adjustment.
Iterate: refine the prompt wording, swap or update the style or subject reference, and re-run. Keep aspect ratios consistent between references and output for fewer artifacts.
suggestedUseCases: Character continuity: keep a hero character’s face, outfit, and silhouette consistent while generating new actions or angles.
Branded content variations: apply a house style across multiple short clips for social posts, intros, or product teasers.
Look development: quickly test motion, lighting, and camera treatments against a fixed subject identity.
Editorial/advertising mockups: preview how a campaign style will translate to motion before committing to a full production.

faqItems.question: Do I need two images, or can I use just one reference?
faqItems.answer: You can use a single subject image if that’s all you have. Adding a second style/look image helps lock the palette, texture, and lighting for stronger visual consistency.

faqItems.question: How do I maintain a consistent character across multiple clips?
faqItems.answer: Keep the same subject reference image, reuse the same prompt phrasing for core traits, and (if your node exposes it) reuse the same seed. Avoid cropping the subject differently between runs.

faqItems.question: What image sizes and aspect ratios work best?
faqItems.answer: Use clean, sharp images with the same aspect ratio as your target video. At least 512 px on the short edge is a good baseline; higher-resolution references generally improve fidelity.

faqItems.question: Does this require a PixVerse account or API key?
faqItems.answer: Depending on your PixverseV6FusionVideoNode implementation, you may need to configure credentials for API-based generation. Check the node’s documentation or settings in your ComfyUI install.

These images are then processed through the FluxKontextProImageNode, where users can apply various edits such as color changes or style transformations. Preview the edits using the PreviewImage node to ensure they meet your expectations.

c7b233293bca.title: Recraft 4.1: Text to Vector
c7b233293bca.description: Generate a clean, flat vector logo from a text prompt using Recraft V4.1, producing one scalable SVG output with no file input required. Ideal for branding and logo design, vector illustration projects, and creating consistent flat-color graphics for presentations or merchandise.
c7b233293bca.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate flat SVG logos from text using Recraft V4.1. Guide colors with Recraft Controls and save clean vectors with SaveSVG.
c7b233293bca.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a plain text prompt into a clean, flat vector logo using the Recraft V4.1 model, and saves it as a single scalable SVG—no image input required. The core of the pipeline is the RecraftV4TextToVectorNode, which interprets your prompt and produces vector paths instead of pixels, making the result immediately usable for branding, icons, and merch. A SaveSVGNode writes the output to disk, so you can open it directly in tools like Figma, Illustrator, or Inkscape.

For creative control, the RecraftControls node accepts one or more palette hints from RecraftColorRGB nodes. You can chain multiple RecraftColorRGB nodes to suggest a limited brand palette or enforce flat-color constraints. The MarkdownNote node is included for inline guidance inside the graph. Everything is organized in the Recraft Toolset group (select it and press Ctrl+B to enable), providing a tidy, API-driven text-to-vector workflow optimized for consistent, flat-color graphics.
howToUse: Load the "Recraft 4.1: Text to Vector" workflow in ComfyUI, select the Recraft Toolset group, and press Ctrl+B to enable it (un-bypass).

Open the RecraftControls node and enter your text prompt (e.g., "minimal flat fox logo, geometric, bold silhouette"). If your setup requires an API key, configure it per the Recraft Toolset instructions.

Add color constraints: place one or more RecraftColorRGB nodes, set their RGB/hex values, and connect them as instructed by the workflow to the RecraftControls. You can chain multiple RecraftColorRGB nodes to define a small, consistent palette.
Confirm the SaveSVGNode output path and filename so you know where the SVG will be written.
Click Queue Prompt to run the graph. The RecraftV4TextToVectorNode generates a single vector result, and the SaveSVGNode writes the SVG to disk.
Open the saved SVG in your vector editor. If you want a different look, refine the prompt (simplify language, specify shapes or style) and adjust the color nodes, then re-queue.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid logo exploration for brand concepts without raster-to-vector tracing.
Consistent flat icon sets for apps, dashboards, or design systems.
Flat illustrations and badges for presentations, stickers, and merchandise.
Fallback vector marks for social profiles, thumbnails, and promo graphics.

faqItems.question: What file format does this workflow produce?
faqItems.answer: The workflow outputs a single SVG file. The RecraftV4TextToVectorNode generates vector geometry, and the SaveSVGNode writes it to disk as an SVG for infinite scaling.

faqItems.question: How can I control the colors used in the logo?
faqItems.answer: Use the RecraftControls node with one or more RecraftColorRGB nodes. Chain multiple RecraftColorRGB nodes to define a limited palette. These act as guidance for flat-color results and brand consistency.

faqItems.question: Do I need any image input or preprocessing?
faqItems.answer: No. This is a text-to-vector workflow. Provide only a text prompt; the model returns a clean vector output directly—no raster generation or tracing is required.

faqItems.question: Can I create multiple variations in one run?
faqItems.answer: This template generates one SVG per run. For variations, tweak the prompt and/or palette (add/remove RecraftColorRGB nodes or change their values) and queue the workflow again.

c7c1eb5d5df4.title: Cinematic Product Advertisement — Seedance 2.0
c7c1eb5d5df4.description: A one click workflow to create luxurious cinematic ad videos. Upload images of your product, length of the video, number of unique cuts/shots, and add custom instructions (optional). An LLM processes all this and creates a structured prompt for Seedance 2.0 to generate consistent, on brand product video.
c7c1eb5d5df4.metaDescription: One-click multishot product ads in ComfyUI using Seedance 2.0 with hero/detail image references and LLM-made time-coded prompts for consistent, cinematic results.
c7c1eb5d5df4.extendedDescription:
This workflow, Cinematic Product Advertisement — Seedance 2.0, builds multi-shot, cinematic product ads from a single, time-coded prompt. You provide a hero/environment image and product detail references via LoadImage nodes, set the total length and number of cuts using PrimitiveInt nodes, and optionally add a creative brief. GeminiNodeV2 then synthesizes a structured, time-cued shot plan that Seedance 2.0 consumes as one prompt. The ByteDance2ReferenceNode conditions the generator with your hero and detail images, helping maintain brand consistency and product fidelity across every shot.

Technically, the pipeline is organized into four groups: Inputs; LLM Prompt Generation; Edit Prompt?; and Generate and Save Video. After GeminiNodeV2 outputs the time-coded script, you can lock it into a PrimitiveStringMultiline node and bypass the LLM for reproducibility. The custom utility node (id: 0e2c3eaa-706c-41fd-b300-b6bd9e84a0a4) handles prompt routing/formatting, while the Seedance 2.0 generator node (id: 2b10af74-c412-4c88-b235-6b170aed965c) renders the full sequence in one pass. PreviewAny lets you quickly inspect intermediate outputs, and SaveVideo exports the final clip. This single-prompt, time-cued design makes it easy to iterate on pacing, camera direction, and product emphasis without juggling multiple, per-shot prompts.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the Inputs group. Use LoadImage nodes to add references: Image 1 is the hero/environment image (used for all shots), and Images 2–3 are product detail references. Add more images by wiring additional LoadImage nodes.

Set the total video length (seconds) and the number of unique cuts/shots using the PrimitiveInt nodes. If the workflow includes a text field wired to GeminiNodeV2 (PrimitiveStringMultiline), add optional brand/style instructions for the LLM.

Run the LLM Prompt Generation group. GeminiNodeV2 will create a single, time-coded prompt (e.g., 00:00–00:03, 00:03–00:06 ...) describing each shot. Use PreviewAny to inspect the generated prompt and ensure it matches your creative intent.

Lock the prompt: copy the LLM’s structured prompt into the Edit Prompt? group’s PrimitiveStringMultiline field. Then bypass/disable the LLM Prompt Generation group so subsequent runs always use your locked prompt for consistent results.

Generate the video in the Generate and Save Video group. The ByteDance2ReferenceNode feeds your hero/detail images into the Seedance 2.0 node (id: 2b10af74-c412-4c88-b235-6b170aed965c), which renders the full sequence. Use PreviewAny to monitor progress and framing.

Save the result with the SaveVideo node. If timing or emphasis needs refinement, edit the time codes or shot descriptions in the locked prompt, adjust the number of cuts or overall duration, and re-render.
suggestedUseCases: DTC product launch teasers highlighting materials, finishes, and brand mood across multiple shots.
E-commerce hero videos for PDPs, combining a stable environment with consistent product angles.
Social ad variations (A/B tests) by iterating shot pacing and copy within a locked environment.
Brand styleboards and pitch comps that keep a unified look while testing different shot plans.
Packaging or hardware close-ups where detail reference images must remain consistent across cuts.

faqItems.question: What is the role of the hero image versus the detail images?
faqItems.answer: The hero image defines the persistent environment/look for every shot. Detail images focus the generator on specific product features (logos, textures, materials). The ByteDance2ReferenceNode conditions Seedance 2.0 with both so the video stays on-brand and product-accurate throughout.

faqItems.question: How do I control what happens in each shot?
faqItems.answer: Edit the time-coded segments in the Edit Prompt? group’s PrimitiveStringMultiline field. For each time range, describe the camera move, product position, lighting, and any transitions. Ensure your segments cover the total duration and reflect the number of cuts you set.

faqItems.question: Can I reuse a great prompt without re-running the LLM?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Paste the prompt into the Edit Prompt? PrimitiveStringMultiline, then bypass the LLM Prompt Generation group. This locks the plan for reproducible renders and faster iteration.

faqItems.question: Any tips for getting the most consistent results?
faqItems.answer: Use a clear, wide hero/environment photo, high-quality product detail images, and concise time-coded directives. Keep the first draft short (fewer cuts, shorter duration), then lengthen or add shots as needed. If you see drift, tighten language in each time segment and avoid conflicting descriptors.

c7e06a7b2cda.title: Qwen Image Edit 2511 Int8: Image Edit
c7e06a7b2cda.description: Edit images with Qwen Image Edit 2511 Int8, using a quantized model for faster inference while maintaining high quality. Input one image and receive one edited output. Ideal for character-consistent portrait editing, multi-person group photo fusion, and industrial design modifications.
c7e06a7b2cda.metaDescription: Fast, instruction-based image editing in ComfyUI using Qwen Image Edit 2511 Int8. Load one image, apply edits, and export with SaveImageAdvanced.
c7e06a7b2cda.extendedDescription:
This workflow performs instruction-based image editing using the Qwen Image Edit 2511 Int8 model inside ComfyUI. It’s designed for single-image inputs: you load one image and receive one edited output. The pipeline is straightforward: LoadImage brings your source into the graph, a Qwen Image Edit subgraph node (ID cdb2cf24-c432-439b-b5c8-5f69838580c9) runs the edit according to your text instructions and parameters, and SaveImageAdvanced writes the result to disk with your chosen naming and format options. A MarkdownNote in the canvas provides quick guidance and tips.

Technically, the core editing is handled by the Qwen-Image-Edit model distributed via Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI, here in an Int8-quantized build for faster inference and lower VRAM usage while maintaining strong visual quality. The subgraph encapsulates the model call and exposes practical controls such as your edit instruction and sampler settings. As a starting point, use 20 steps and CFG 4.0 (ComfyUI-side) per the provided reference table, then refine based on your image and goal. This setup is well-suited for character-consistent portrait tweaks, multi-person composition/fusion, and rapid product or industrial design variations where iteration speed matters.
howToUse: Install the Qwen Image Edit assets: from the Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI repo (Hugging Face or ModelScope), follow the readme to place the model and any required custom node files so ComfyUI recognizes the Qwen Image Edit subgraph.
Load the provided workflow in ComfyUI. You’ll see LoadImage, a Qwen Image Edit subgraph node (ID cdb2cf24-c432-439b-b5c8-5f69838580c9), MarkdownNote, and SaveImageAdvanced.
In LoadImage, select the source image you want to edit. If you encounter memory limits, try a smaller input image.

Open the Qwen Image Edit subgraph node and enter a clear, specific edit instruction (e.g., "make the background soft teal and add gentle rim lighting") and set initial parameters: Steps = 20, CFG = 4.0 (recommended starting point). Optionally set a seed for repeatability.

Run the workflow. Review the output saved by SaveImageAdvanced. If needed, iterate: refine the instruction, adjust Steps (more for complex edits) or CFG (lower to preserve the original more, higher for stronger changes).
Use SaveImageAdvanced to control output format, quality, and filename pattern. When you’re happy, save your settings for future runs.
suggestedUseCases: Character-consistent portrait edits (wardrobe, background, lighting) while preserving identity.
Multi-person group photo fusion or harmonization to match style, lighting, or background.
Industrial/product design variations: color/material swaps, label/layout trials, and quick visual iterations.
Creative retouching: subtle makeup adjustments, background cleanup, or mood relighting.
Concept exploration for moodboards by rapidly iterating on one base photo.

faqItems.question: What does the Int8 quantization change?
faqItems.answer: Int8 quantization reduces VRAM use and speeds up inference, enabling faster iterations and larger images on the same hardware. Image quality remains strong, though very fine textures may occasionally benefit from slightly more steps to match full-precision results.

faqItems.question: How should I set Steps and CFG?
faqItems.answer: Start with Steps = 20 and CFG = 4.0 (ComfyUI-side) as a balanced default. Increase Steps for complex or global edits; reduce Steps for quick drafts. Lower CFG to better preserve the original image; raise CFG for stronger adherence to the instruction.

faqItems.question: Can I get consistent results across runs?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Use a fixed seed and keep your instruction wording and parameters the same. For character consistency, be descriptive (e.g., hair style, color, clothing descriptors) and keep CFG moderate so the model respects the source identity.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow support batching?
faqItems.answer: This graph is set up for one image per run. To process multiple images, duplicate the path or adapt the workflow by adding batching nodes (e.g., ImageBatch) upstream of the Qwen Image Edit subgraph.

c98e5c457e1e.title: Product Advertisement Video

Upload up to 3 reference images of your product 
A one click workflow to create a cinematic advertisement video of your product. Upload up to 3 images of your product, duration, number of unique cuts/shots, and add custom instructions (optional). An LLM processes all this and creates a structured prompt for MiniMax H3 to generate a consistent, on brand product video.
c98e5c457e1e.metaDescription: Create cinematic multi-shot product ads from images in ComfyUI. Gemini scripts MiniMax H3 with time-coded shots; SaveVideo exports the final video.
c98e5c457e1e.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds a cinematic, multi-shot product advertisement video from up to three reference images. In the Inputs group, you supply Image 1 as the hero/environment reference (the scene this image defines is maintained across all shots) and use Images 2–3 for product detail references. Duration and number of unique shots are controlled with PrimitiveInt nodes, while optional brand/style guidance goes into a PrimitiveStringMultiline input. The LLM Prompt Generation group uses GeminiNodeV2 to transform your inputs into a single, time-cued prompt that MiniMax H3 understands (for example: 0–3s Shot 1, 3–6s Shot 2, etc.). The structured prompt, plus your references, then drives the MiniMax H3 node to render a consistent, on-brand video.

What makes this workflow especially efficient is its one-prompt multishot design. MiniMax H3 expects a single prompt containing all shots and their time windows, so the GeminiNodeV2 node formats a clean shot list with camera moves, transitions, and product highlights. You can preview and verify the shot script using PreviewAny and MarkdownNote. Once satisfied, paste the final script into the Edit Prompt? group to "lock" it and bypass the LLM step for fast, repeatable iterations. The Generate and Save Video group then renders the ad and writes it to disk via SaveVideo, giving you a repeatable pipeline for quickly producing consistent product spots.
howToUse: Load the workflow and open the Inputs group. Add up to 3 images using LoadImage: Image 1 = hero/environment (persists across all shots); Images 2–3 = product detail references. You can wire more LoadImage nodes if needed.

Set the PrimitiveInt nodes for total duration and number of unique shots/cuts. Optionally, add brand tone, specific angles, transitions, or must-show features in the PrimitiveStringMultiline instructions.

Run the LLM Prompt Generation group. GeminiNodeV2 will create a single, time-cued multishot script for MiniMax H3. Use PreviewAny/MarkdownNote to inspect the structured prompt and confirm timing and content.

If you want deterministic, repeatable results: copy the generated prompt into the Edit Prompt? text input, then bypass the LLM Prompt Generation group so the MiniMax H3 node uses your locked script directly.

Go to Generate and Save Video and execute the graph. The MiniMax H3 node renders the video from your references and shot list. Use PreviewAny to spot-check output; SaveVideo writes the final clip to your output directory.
Iterate: adjust duration, number of shots, or the prompt (either via GeminiNodeV2 or the Edit Prompt? input) to refine pacing, angles, and product emphasis, then re-run the final group.
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce hero videos and product detail reels for storefronts or landing pages
Social media ad variations (A/B tests) with consistent branding and different shot orders
Product launch teasers highlighting key features across multiple cuts
Rapid client previews/storyboards of ad concepts without a full video shoot
Brand consistency checks by locking a script and swapping product detail references

faqItems.question: What does “one-prompt multishot” mean with MiniMax H3?
faqItems.answer: MiniMax H3 expects a single prompt that contains all shots with explicit time ranges (e.g., 0–3s, 3–6s). The GeminiNodeV2 builds this time-cued shot list so H3 can render multiple cuts from one structured prompt.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the environment consistent across cuts?
faqItems.answer: Use a strong, on-brand Image 1 as the hero/environment reference. The workflow locks its scene for every shot. Avoid instructions that drastically change locations mid-prompt if you want consistency.

faqItems.question: Can I add more than three reference images?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The template supports up to three by default, but you can wire additional LoadImage nodes and feed them into the same prompt and generator inputs as needed.

faqItems.question: Do I need API keys or internet access?
faqItems.answer: GeminiNodeV2 and MiniMax H3 often call external services. Depending on your node configuration, you may need valid API keys and network access. Check each node’s settings and your ComfyUI console for requirements.

cb1b1f5d4d80.title: Layer Decomposition: Seedream 5.0 Pro
cb1b1f5d4d80.description: Split any image into independent, editable layers — subject, product, background, and text — with a single text instruction using Seedream 5.0 Pro. A single poster can yield 10+ layers, with design-grade text separation supporting multilingual headlines and CJK fonts. Ideal for brand design, e-commerce asset creation, and layout iteration.
cb1b1f5d4d80.metaDescription: Decompose any image into editable subject, product, background, and text layers with Seedream 5.0 Pro in ComfyUI. Preview, re-layout, and export clean RGBA assets.
cb1b1f5d4d80.extendedDescription:
This workflow uses the Seedream 5.0 Pro layer separation model to break a single image into clean, editable layers such as subject, product, background, and text. At its core is the ByteDanceSeedreamLayerSeparationNodeV2, which accepts your input image and a plain-language instruction (for example: "separate product, person, headline text, logo, and background"). The node returns a set of per-layer images and masks, enabling design‑grade text isolation (including multilingual and CJK headlines) and often producing 10+ layers from a single poster.

Around the core, utility nodes organize, preview, and export the results. LoadImage brings your asset into the graph; BatchImagesNode and BatchMasksNode collect the multiple outputs produced by the separation node; JoinImageWithAlpha pairs each RGB layer with its mask to create clean RGBA cutouts; and ImageCompositor (open it via Nodes2.0 > Open Compositor) lets you toggle visibility, re-order layers, and audition layout changes. Finally, SaveImageAdvanced saves individual layers or composites with preserved alpha, making the workflow ideal for brand design, e‑commerce asset generation, and rapid layout iteration.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI, update ComfyUI to the latest version if needed, switch to Nodes2.0, and click Open Compositor. Load your image with the LoadImage node (try the provided victory_cover.png to start).

In ByteDanceSeedreamLayerSeparationNodeV2, enter a clear instruction describing the layers you want (e.g., "separate: product bottle, person, headline text, logo, background"). Be explicit about categories you care about.
Queue/Run the workflow. The Seedream 5.0 Pro node analyzes the image and outputs multiple per‑layer images and corresponding masks. BatchImagesNode and BatchMasksNode will group these results.
Use JoinImageWithAlpha to pair each image with its mask, producing RGBA layers. Open ImageCompositor to preview, toggle, re-order, and position layers to test layouts or isolate elements.

If a layer needs refinement, adjust your instruction (be more specific or add/exclude elements) and re-run. You can iterate quickly to get cleaner separations, especially for small logos or dense typography.
Export final assets with SaveImageAdvanced. Save individual PNGs (alpha preserved) for each layer or a composed preview from ImageCompositor for quick reviews and downstream design tools.
suggestedUseCases: Brand and campaign design: isolate logos, headlines, and hero subjects from key visuals for fast layout variations.
E‑commerce: extract product cutouts and background alternatives from catalog or lifestyle photos.
Multilingual poster iteration: separate CJK and Latin headlines for language swaps without redoing the whole layout.
Creative retouching: remove or replace backgrounds while keeping people, products, and text intact as independent layers.
Social templates: rapidly recombine assets (subject, product, text) into platform-specific crops and aspect ratios.

faqItems.question: What kinds of layers can it separate?
faqItems.answer: Common outputs include subject/person, product objects, background plates, logos, and text (including multilingual/CJK). Results depend on your instruction and the visual clarity of the source image.

faqItems.question: Will text be vectorized or keep its original font?
faqItems.answer: Layers are raster cutouts, not vectors. The workflow isolates text as its own image + alpha layer for clean editing, but it does not convert fonts to editable typography.

faqItems.question: How do I get cleaner masks or more precise layers?
faqItems.answer: Use high‑resolution inputs, give explicit, itemized instructions (e.g., list each element you want), and avoid overly compressed images. If a category is missed, name it directly and re-run. You can also recombine outputs in ImageCompositor to verify coverage.

faqItems.question: What formats can I export?
faqItems.answer: Use SaveImageAdvanced to export PNGs with alpha for each layer or a composed preview image. PNG is recommended for preserving transparency in downstream tools like Figma or Photoshop.

faqItems.question: Does this work on photos, or only on illustrations?

cb783cb4c20c.metaDescription: Animate a still image into video with MiniMax H3 Max in ComfyUI. Optional prompt enhancement and 2K upscale, with aspect ratio and identity preserved.
cb783cb4c20c.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial template shows how to turn a single image into an animated video using MiniMax H3 Max via the MinimaxHailuo03ReferenceNode. The core path is simple: you load a still frame with LoadImage, describe the motion in PrimitiveStringMultiline, and the MinimaxHailuo03ReferenceNode generates a video while preserving the source composition and aspect ratio. SaveVideo writes the final clip to disk, and SaveText can archive the exact prompt and response metadata for reproducibility.

Two optional paths are controlled by red ComfySwitchNode gates. The Prompt Enhancer (Optional) stage lets you route an alternate or refined prompt into the generator if you want cleaner wording without changing your base prompt field. The Upscale Video to 2K (Optional) stage adds a post-process branch for higher-resolution output, but it only accepts a 768p source—so you must generate at 768p in the core node if you plan to upscale. For more advanced control, MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode can be added to supply context/image-reference signals for stronger identity retention, and MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode enables quick re-runs with new seeds without reconfiguring inputs. This makes the template practical for animating character portraits, product shots, and concept visuals with prompt-driven motion while keeping the original look intact.
howToUse: Load the workflow and confirm MiniMax H3 Max nodes are installed and authenticated (configure the MiniMax API key per the node’s documentation).
In User Inputs, set your text prompt in PrimitiveStringMultiline and load your reference image with LoadImage (try the provided sample: burdened_warrior_in_dreamscape.png).
If you plan to upscale, set the MinimaxHailuo03ReferenceNode output to 768p and switch ON the PrimitiveBoolean for Upscale to 2K. Toggle the red ComfySwitchNode for the upscale branch to ON.

Optionally enable the Prompt Enhancer path by turning ON its red ComfySwitchNode and routing your refined prompt to the generator. You can also add MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode for extra identity/context guidance if provided in the template.

Queue and run the graph. The Create Video (Core) path will generate the base clip with MinimaxHailuo03ReferenceNode. If the upscale switch is ON and the source is 768p, the clip will pass through the 2K branch.
Use MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode to iterate quickly with new seeds or slight prompt tweaks, then check SaveVideo for your output and SaveText for the prompt/metadata log.
suggestedUseCases: Animating character portraits or concept art while preserving facial structure and outfit details.
Creating subtle motion for product hero shots from a single still (e.g., camera drift, lighting shifts).
Turning mood boards or keyframes into short motion studies for pitch decks.
Adding cinematic micro-movements to static illustrations for social posts or trailers.
Rapidly exploring motion directions from a single design frame without full 3D or traditional animation.

faqItems.question: What do the red switches control?
faqItems.answer: They are ComfySwitchNode gates for optional branches. One toggles the Prompt Enhancer path, and the other toggles the Upscale to 2K path. Leave them OFF for a simple reference-to-video run, or turn them ON to enable those stages.

faqItems.question: Why doesn’t the 2K upscale run?
faqItems.answer: The upscale branch only accepts a 768p source. Set the MinimaxHailuo03ReferenceNode to generate at 768p, turn ON the PrimitiveBoolean (Upscale to 2K), and toggle the upscale ComfySwitchNode to ON. If the source isn’t 768p, the upscale path will be skipped.

faqItems.question: How do I preserve my character or product identity?
faqItems.answer: Use a clear, high-quality reference image with a stable composition. Keep your prompt descriptive but not contradictory to the image. If available in the template, route MinimaxHailuo03ContextIRNode to add context/image-reference signals, which can further stabilize identity.

faqItems.question: How can I iterate quickly without re-entering everything?
faqItems.answer: Use MinimaxHailuo03RegenerateNode to re-run with a new seed or minor variations. SaveText logs your prompt and response metadata, so you can track what changed between iterations.

The VAELoader and UNETLoader nodes are crucial for preparing the model components, while the EmptyLatentImage node initializes the latent space for image generation. The SaveImage node ensures that the final output is stored for user access. This workflow is particularly useful for artists and content creators who wish to quickly generate anime-style visuals from textual descriptions, providing a creative tool for concept art, storyboarding, and digital illustration.

Set your desired image size using the Image Size node, typically around 1MP for optimal results.
Input your text prompt into the CLIPTextEncode node, describing the anime-style image you wish to generate.

faqItems.question: What is the Anima model?

faqItems.question: How can I improve the quality of the generated images?

faqItems.question: Why do my images look non-realistic?

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for high-resolution images?
