d78377cf53f4.title: LTX-2.5: FLF2V
d78377cf53f4.description: Generate a video from first and last frame reference images using LTX-2.5, blending both frames into a single animated sequence. Ideal for creating transition shots, morphing between two subjects or scenes, and building multi-shot narratives from still references.
d78377cf53f4.metaDescription: Generate smooth transitions from first and last images using LTX-2.5 in ComfyUI. Load two frames, synthesize in-betweens, and export to MP4/WebM.
d78377cf53f4.extendedDescription:
LTX-2.5: FLF2V is a focused ComfyUI workflow for turning two still images—your intended first and last frames—into a single, coherent video. It’s ideal for creating smooth transitions, morphs between subjects, or bridging shots in a sequence when you only have still references. Two LoadImage nodes supply the start and end visuals, which feed into a single LTX-2.5 FLF2V generator node (cf70afc4-5a03-47ce-8210-734b1de6c6bc). The resulting frames are handed to SaveVideo for encoding to a playable clip. A MarkdownNote is included with inline tips.

Under the hood, the LTX-2.5 node leverages Lightricks’ open video generation model and its keyframes-first “Pixel Diffusion” approach to synthesize in-between frames from your bookend images. Typical controls you’ll use are target resolution, number of frames (or duration), frames-per-second, and a random seed for reproducibility. Many builds also expose blending/easing options to bias the motion toward the first or last frame. SaveVideo then encodes the output at your chosen fps (MP4/WebM, depending on your ffmpeg setup).

For best results, match the aspect ratio and general lighting/composition of your two reference images. Larger frame counts and consistent content between the first and last frames usually produce smoother motion. If you see stretching or cropping, pre-crop your inputs to the same size before loading them into the workflow.
howToUse: Load the LTX-2.5: FLF2V workflow JSON in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote for any inline tips or defaults.
Open the two LoadImage nodes and select your starting image (first frame) and ending image (last frame). Ensure they share the same aspect ratio for clean interpolation.

In the LTX-2.5 FLF2V node (cf70afc4-5a03-47ce-8210-734b1de6c6bc), set your target resolution, number of frames (or duration), frames-per-second, and a seed if you want repeatable results. If the node exposes a blend/easing control, adjust it to favor a linear transition or an ease-in/ease-out feel.
Configure the SaveVideo node: confirm the fps matches your generator settings, choose a filename/output path, and select the desired container (MP4/WebM, depending on your ffmpeg setup).
Click Queue Prompt to generate. Inspect the output; if the motion is too fast or abrupt, increase the frame count or tweak the blend/easing, then re-run.
When satisfied, let SaveVideo write the final clip to disk. Review it in your media player and iterate on parameters as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic transitions between two storyboard frames or scene stills.
Portrait or character morphs for social content and concept visualization.
Before/after product reveals that smoothly interpolate between two shots.
Bridging two environment stills to create a connective sequence in an edit.
Logo-to-scene or icon-to-product transitions for titles and openers.

faqItems.question: Do my two images need to be the same size or aspect ratio?
faqItems.answer: Matching aspect ratios is strongly recommended. The generator will resize inputs to its working resolution, but mismatched aspects can introduce stretching or unwanted cropping. Pre-crop or pad both images to the same dimensions before loading for the cleanest results.

faqItems.question: How do I control the pace and smoothness of the transition?
faqItems.answer: The perceived duration is frames ÷ fps. To slow the transition and make it smoother, increase the number of frames while keeping fps the same. Some builds also include a blend/easing control—use it to ease-in or ease-out of the start/end frame for a more natural feel.

faqItems.question: Can I get repeatable results?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Set a fixed seed in the LTX-2.5 FLF2V node (if exposed). Using the same inputs and parameters with the same seed will reproduce the same video frames, which is useful for iterative tweaks.

faqItems.question: What if I run into performance or memory issues?
faqItems.answer: Reduce the target resolution and/or the number of frames, and ensure both images are pre-sized to the model’s working aspect to avoid extra scaling. A modern GPU is recommended for smooth local generation; if you still see out-of-memory errors, lower the resolution further and iterate.

Next, load your style reference image using another LoadImage node.
Connect both images to the MagnificImageStyleTransferNode.
Configure the MagnificImageStyleTransferNode with desired parameters for style intensity and blending.
Run the workflow to process the images and generate a new styled image.
Save the resulting image using the SaveImage node for further use or sharing.

d833dc5abe59.title: Seedance 2.0 Multiframe Stitch
d833dc5abe59.description:
This workflow uses a lot of credits!

This workflow allows you to create a stitched multiframe video using seedance 2.0. Great of iterating and inbetweening quickly.
d833dc5abe59.metaDescription: Create smooth in-between frames from two images with Seedance 2.0 in ComfyUI, then stitch them into a video. Fast iteration for motion tests and transitions.
d833dc5abe59.extendedDescription:
Seedance 2.0 Multiframe Stitch is a ComfyUI workflow for generating smooth in-between frames between two key images, then assembling them into a video. At its core is the ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode, which uses the Seedance 2.0 model to synthesize a sequence that transitions from your first frame to your last. This makes it ideal for rapid iteration, motion studies, and quick inbetweening without writing code or handling external tools. Note: running Seedance 2.0 can be credit-intensive, so plan your frame count and resolution accordingly.

Technically, the workflow starts by loading your start and end images with LoadImage. Those images are passed into ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode to generate a multiframe batch of interpolations. ImageBatch ensures the frames are properly grouped for video creation. GetVideoComponents can be used to set or match video properties (such as frame rate) if you are aligning to a reference. Finally, CreateVideo assembles the frame batch into a video stream, and SaveVideo writes the result to disk. The result is a stitched, coherent transition clip built entirely from two stills.

What makes this useful is the combination of controllability and speed: you pick the anchor frames, the node interpolates the motion, and the rest of the graph reliably compiles and saves the output. Keep both input images the same resolution and aspect ratio for best results, and manage cost by reducing frame count, resolution, or iterations if exposed in your node configuration.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm all nodes are available: LoadImage, ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode, ImageBatch, GetVideoComponents, CreateVideo, and SaveVideo.
Use the two LoadImage nodes to select your first (start) and last (end) keyframes. Ensure both images share the same resolution and aspect ratio.

Open ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode and set the key parameters for interpolation (e.g., number of in-between frames and any quality/strength controls the node exposes). Lower values reduce cost; higher values increase smoothness.
If you want a specific playback speed, either connect GetVideoComponents to a reference clip to pull its FPS or manually set the FPS on CreateVideo.
Run the graph to generate the interpolated frame batch and compile it into a video with CreateVideo.
Preview the result in ComfyUI, then use SaveVideo to write the final stitched video to disk. Adjust frame count, FPS, or node settings and re-run as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Product or logo transitions between two designed states for motion tests and quick previews.
Storyboard inbetweens to visualize timing between key panels without full animation production.
Portrait or character pose morphs to explore motion direction and pacing between two poses.
Before/after scene transitions for motion design pitches and concept explorations.
Time-lapse smoothing by interpolating between two representative frames of a longer sequence.

faqItems.question: What does ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode do in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: It uses the Seedance 2.0 model to generate the in-between frames from your first and last images. The output is a multi-frame batch that smoothly transitions between the two inputs.

faqItems.question: Why does this workflow use a lot of credits?
faqItems.answer: Seedance 2.0 inference can be resource-intensive. Credit use scales with frame count, resolution, and any quality settings. To reduce cost, lower the number of in-between frames, reduce output resolution, or dial back quality/iterations if those controls are available.

faqItems.question: How do I control the speed and duration of the final video?
faqItems.answer: Two factors matter: the number of generated frames and the FPS used in CreateVideo. More frames or higher FPS result in longer/smoother clips. Use GetVideoComponents to match a reference FPS, or set the FPS manually in CreateVideo.

faqItems.question: My output flickers or morphs unpredictably. How can I improve stability?
faqItems.answer: Use start and end images with consistent framing, lighting, and subject scale. Keep both images the same resolution/aspect ratio. If the node exposes a seed or strength/smoothness parameter, try locking the seed for repeatability and adjusting strength toward more conservative motion.

d8bd574de179.title: Wan2.6: Text to Video
d8bd574de179.description: Generate high-quality videos from text prompts with enhanced image quality, smoother motion, 1080P resolution support, and improved prompt understanding for natural, professional results.
d8bd574de179.metaDescription: Transform text prompts into high-quality videos with the Wan2.6 model, featuring enhanced image quality and smoother motion.
d8bd574de179.extendedDescription:
The 'Wan2.6: Text to Video' workflow in ComfyUI is designed to transform text prompts into high-quality video content. This workflow leverages the Wan2.6 model, which is renowned for its ability to generate videos with enhanced image quality and smoother motion transitions. The use of the WanTextToVideoApi node is central to this process, as it interprets textual descriptions and converts them into video sequences with 1080P resolution. This workflow is particularly useful for users looking to create natural and professional-looking videos directly from text, thanks to its improved prompt understanding capabilities.

Technically, the workflow operates by taking a text input and processing it through the WanTextToVideoApi node, which is specifically optimized for video generation tasks. The generated video is then saved using the SaveVideo node, allowing for easy access and storage. This setup ensures that users can produce videos that are not only visually appealing but also aligned with the descriptive nuances of the input text. The combination of these nodes and the advanced capabilities of the Wan2.6 model makes this workflow a powerful tool for content creators and developers alike.
howToUse: Load the 'Wan2.6: Text to Video' workflow in ComfyUI.
Enter your desired text prompt into the input field of the WanTextToVideoApi node.
Configure the video settings, such as resolution and frame rate, if necessary.
Run the workflow to generate the video.
Once processing is complete, locate the output file saved by the SaveVideo node.
Review and use the video as needed for your project.
suggestedUseCases: Creating promotional videos from product descriptions.
Developing educational content with visual explanations.
Producing social media content with dynamic visuals.
Generating concept videos for creative storytelling.
Enhancing presentations with custom video elements.

faqItems.question: What text prompts work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Descriptive and detailed text prompts yield the best results, as they provide the model with more context to generate accurate and visually appealing videos.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the video resolution?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow supports 1080P resolution, and you can configure other video settings within the WanTextToVideoApi node.

faqItems.question: How long does it take to generate a video?
faqItems.answer: The processing time varies based on the complexity of the text prompt and the length of the video, but typically ranges from a few minutes to longer for more detailed outputs.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to use this workflow for commercial projects?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow can be used for commercial projects, provided you comply with any licensing terms associated with the Wan2.6 model and ComfyUI.

d99717df8788.title: Create seamless transitions with LTX 2.3
d99717df8788.description: Create seamless transitions between shots with this LTX 2.3 workflow, featuring the FLW LoRA from Systsms
d99717df8788.metaDescription: ComfyUI LTX 2.3 + SYSTMS FLW LoRA workflow for seamless video-to-video transitions between two clips with prompt-guided control.
d99717df8788.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds seamless, text-guided transitions between two source clips using the LTX 2.3 video diffusion model and the SYSTMS FLW transition LoRA. The MODELS group loads the transformer-only LTX 2.3 backbone via DiffusionModelLoaderKJ, the matching VAE with VAELoaderKJ, and applies the FLW LoRA using LoraLoaderModelOnly to bias the model toward natural, flow-like shot changes. Prompts are encoded with CLIPTextEncode (optionally auto-generated by a Gemini node), then routed through LTXVConditioning and LTXVAddGuide to steer the transition content and style.

Under the hood, the workflow allocates a timeline in EmptyLTXVLatentVideo, manages A/V latent streams with LTXVSeparateAVLatent and LTXVConcatAVLatent, and localizes denoising to the handoff region using SolidMask and SetLatentNoiseMask. Sampling is handled by SamplerCustomAdvanced with CFGGuider, KSamplerSelect, BasicScheduler, and RandomNoise for reproducibility. After inference, VAEDecode reconstructs frames and VHS_VideoCombine assembles them into a final video. LTXVCropGuides provides compositional guides to keep subjects aligned between shots, helping the model generate cleaner, more believable morphs.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and install the required models: LTX 2.3 (22B, transformer only) from https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/tree/main/diffusion_models into models/diffusion_models, the SYSTMS FLW transition LoRA from https://huggingface.co/systms/SYSTMS-FLW-IC-LORA-LTX-2.3 into models/loras, and a compatible VAE into models/vae. (An optional distilled LoRA is available here: https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/blob/main/loras/ltx-2.3-22b-di...).
In the MODELS group, point DiffusionModelLoaderKJ to the LTX 2.3 transformer file, VAELoaderKJ to the VAE, and LoraLoaderModelOnly to the FLW LoRA. Leave LoRA strength at its default to start.

Add your two source clips in the INPUT VIDEOS group and set a frame load cap for each. The frame cap determines how many frames from each clip are used before and after the transition. If provided, use LTXVCropGuides to keep subjects framed similarly across both clips.

Set your prompt in the PROMPT group. You can keep the Google Gemini node to auto-generate a description from the inputs, or disconnect it and type directly into CLIPTextEncode. Recommended formula: "FLW, [Action A] seamlessly transforms into [Action B], [environment/style specifics]".

Open LTX SETTINGS and define resolution and total length on EmptyLTXVLatentVideo (width, height, and total frames). Transition length is computed as: total frames − frames from Clip A − frames from Clip B. Optionally refine where denoising happens by adjusting SolidMask and SetLatentNoiseMask to focus more noise in the transition region and less on the stable parts of each clip.

In SAMPLING, pick your KSampler in KSamplerSelect, set steps and scheduler in BasicScheduler, choose a CFG scale in CFGGuider (3–5 is a good start), and set a seed in RandomNoise for repeatability. Press Queue. The pipeline will sample with SamplerCustomAdvanced, decode with VAEDecode, and export the video with VHS_VideoCombine.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic shot bridges: morphing an establishing shot into a character close-up without a hard cut.
Stylized scene transitions: transforming one environment into another (e.g., desert to cyberpunk city) while maintaining motion continuity.
Product reveal edits: transitioning from a moving prototype shot to the final product aesthetic mid-motion.
Music video edits: fluid transformations between performance and narrative shots guided by lyrical or thematic prompts.
Trailer teasers: rapid, coherent morphs between key scenes to imply a narrative arc.

faqItems.question: Do I have to use the Google Gemini node for prompts?
faqItems.answer: No. It is optional. Disconnect its string output from CLIPTextEncode and enter your own prompt. Use the template: "FLW, [Action A] seamlessly transforms into [Action B], [details]".

faqItems.question: How do I set the transition duration?
faqItems.answer: Set the frame load caps on Clip A and Clip B, then set the total frame count on EmptyLTXVLatentVideo. Transition length = total frames − Clip A frames − Clip B frames.

faqItems.question: Which files go where in ComfyUI?
faqItems.answer: Place the LTX 2.3 transformer model in models/diffusion_models, the SYSTMS FLW LoRA in models/loras, and the VAE in models/vae. Load them via DiffusionModelLoaderKJ, LoraLoaderModelOnly, and VAELoaderKJ respectively.

faqItems.question: How can I improve stability and reduce drift or flicker?
faqItems.answer: Keep CFG scale moderate (around 3–5), ensure subjects are similarly framed using LTXVCropGuides, and restrict heavy denoising to the handoff region with SolidMask + SetLatentNoiseMask. You can also lower resolution or steps slightly to avoid over-cooking details outside the transition.

d9d6f1309cbc.title: WaveSpeed: Image Upscale
d9d6f1309cbc.description: Upload an image to upscale its resolution. Generate an enhanced 2K, 4K, or 8K output that preserves details and reduces artifacts in JPEG, PNG, or WEBP format.
d9d6f1309cbc.metaDescription: Enhance image resolution with WaveSpeed: Image Upscale. Upscale to 2K, 4K, or 8K with detail preservation and artifact reduction.
d9d6f1309cbc.extendedDescription:
The WaveSpeed: Image Upscale workflow is designed to enhance the resolution of your images, allowing you to upscale them to 2K, 4K, or even 8K. This workflow utilizes the WavespeedImageUpscaleNode, a powerful tool that leverages advanced algorithms to preserve intricate details while minimizing artifacts commonly introduced during the upscaling process. The workflow begins with the LoadImage node, where you upload your image, followed by the core upscaling process handled by the WavespeedImageUpscaleNode. Once the image is enhanced, the SaveImage node allows you to save the output in your preferred format, such as JPEG, PNG, or WEBP.

The inclusion of the ImageCompare node provides a valuable feature for users who wish to assess the quality difference between the original and the upscaled image. This node is particularly useful for ensuring that the upscaling process meets your quality expectations. Additionally, the MarkdownNote node offers a space for annotations or additional instructions, which can be crucial for collaborative projects or personal documentation. Overall, this workflow is a robust solution for anyone looking to improve image quality for both personal and professional projects.
howToUse: Load the WaveSpeed: Image Upscale workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadImage node to upload your image file.
Configure the WavespeedImageUpscaleNode for your desired resolution (2K, 4K, 8K).
Optionally, use the ImageCompare node to compare the original and upscaled images.
Save the enhanced image using the SaveImage node in your preferred format.
Review the MarkdownNote for any additional instructions or notes.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing digital art for high-resolution prints.
Upscaling photographs for large format displays.
Improving image quality for professional portfolios.
Preparing images for high-resolution video production.
Restoring and preserving old photographs with enhanced detail.

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported for output?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports saving images in JPEG, PNG, and WEBP formats.

faqItems.question: Can I compare the original and upscaled images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the ImageCompare node allows you to visually compare the original and upscaled images to ensure quality.

faqItems.question: Is the WavespeedImageUpscaleNode suitable for all types of images?
faqItems.answer: While it excels with most image types, results may vary depending on the original image quality and content.

faqItems.question: How do I switch to Nodes 2.0 for the ImageCompare feature?
faqItems.answer: To access ImageCompare, open the menu and select Nodes 2.0 to switch to the updated node system.

da307762d0d9.title: Pose Map: DWPose OpenPose
da307762d0d9.description: Convert a Video to a temporally stable Pose Control Map
da307762d0d9.metaDescription: Convert video to a temporally stable OpenPose-style pose map with DWPose in ComfyUI. Load, preprocess, and recombine frames for ControlNet-ready pose videos.
da307762d0d9.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns any input video into an OpenPose-style pose control map that stays consistent from frame to frame. It uses VHS_LoadVideo (from ComfyUI-VideoHelperSuite) to decode the video into a stable, fixed-resolution frame sequence, then runs each frame through the DWPreprocessor from comfyui_controlnet_aux with the DWPose backend. DWPose extracts 2D body keypoints (optionally including hands and face) and renders them as clean pose maps suitable for ControlNet pose conditioning. Finally, VHS_VideoCombine stitches the pose frames back into a video so you can preview, share, or feed them into downstream generation pipelines.

Technically, the temporal stability comes from deterministic, per-frame inference with identical settings, consistent frame sampling (no dropped frames), and top-down human detection that keeps keypoint associations coherent across time. Because the pipeline does not introduce randomness and maintains a constant image size and FPS, pose jitter is minimized relative to ad-hoc, frame-by-frame preprocessing. The included MarkdownNote documents parameters and reminders in-graph, while the DWPreprocessor (DWPose) provides OpenPose-format outputs that plug directly into ControlNet Pose for image or video-to-video generation.
howToUse: Install requirements: update ComfyUI, then add custom nodes Fannovel16/comfyui_controlnet_aux and Kosinkadink/ComfyUI-VideoHelperSuite. Restart ComfyUI. Ensure ffmpeg is installed so VHS_VideoCombine can encode video.
Load the workflow, open VHS_LoadVideo, and select your source video. Set the target resolution and FPS (matching the source FPS helps). Optionally trim by start/end frame to limit processing.

Open DWPreprocessor and choose the DWPose-based OpenPose preprocessor variant (e.g., whole-body if you need hands/face). Set detect/image resolution to match (or slightly exceed) your video resolution for accurate keypoints.
Run a short test range to preview the pose frames from DWPreprocessor. If limbs flicker, try a higher detect resolution or ensure subjects are large enough in frame; keep FPS and resolution constant.

When satisfied, execute the full range. Use VHS_VideoCombine to assemble the pose frames into a video, choosing your codec/container (e.g., MP4 H.264) and output path. The result is a temporally stable pose control map ready for ControlNet.
suggestedUseCases: Create ControlNet Pose conditioning videos to drive consistent character motion in video-to-video or image sequences.
Pre-visualize choreography or athletic motion as clean skeleton overlays for animation blocking or rotoscoping.
Generate privacy-preserving motion references by sharing pose maps instead of the original footage.
Build pose datasets or keyframe guides for training or manual annotation workflows.

faqItems.question: What makes the pose maps "temporally stable"?
faqItems.answer: The pipeline processes frames in order with identical settings, uses deterministic DWPose inference, and preserves a constant resolution/FPS via VHS_LoadVideo. This avoids randomness and dropped frames, reducing pose jitter versus ad-hoc preprocessing.

faqItems.question: Should I enable hands/face keypoints?
faqItems.answer: Enable them if your subject’s hands and face are clearly visible and you need fine-grained control in ControlNet. If subjects are small or low-resolution, disabling hands/face can speed up processing and reduce noisy detections.

faqItems.question: How can I improve accuracy on challenging footage?
faqItems.answer: Use higher detect/image resolution in DWPreprocessor, ensure good lighting and minimal motion blur, match or slightly upscale the working resolution, and keep subjects reasonably large in frame. Trim out-of-focus sections and avoid heavy compression.

faqItems.question: What formats can I export?
faqItems.answer: VHS_VideoCombine uses ffmpeg to assemble a video (e.g., MP4 with H.264). You can also save the intermediate pose frames as an image sequence if you prefer to encode externally.

da6947213b75.title: Meshy 7.1: Image to 3D
da6947213b75.description: Generate a 3D model from a single image using Meshy 7.1's Ultra 4K geometry mode, which produces 4096³ meshes so fine surface detail like stitching, wood grain, and scales becomes real geometry rather than texture. Takes one input image. Ideal for high-fidelity asset creation, detailed prop modeling, and product visualization.
da6947213b75.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow: convert a single image to a high‑fidelity 3D mesh with Meshy 7.1 Ultra 4K geometry, then refine, texture, rig/animate, and export.
da6947213b75.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow turns a single image into a high‑fidelity 3D asset using Meshy 7.1’s Ultra 4K geometry mode. Starting with LoadImage, your reference photo flows into MeshyImageToModelNode, which requests a dense reconstruction at Ultra 4K (4096³) so fine surface detail—like stitching, wood grain, or scales—becomes real mesh geometry, not just texture. The result is a detailed, production‑ready model ideal for props, products, and hero assets where close‑up fidelity matters.

After the base mesh is generated, the pipeline branches into post steps: MeshyRefineNode for cleanup/topology polishing, MeshyTextureNode for PBR texturing, and optional rigging/animation via MeshyRigModelNode and MeshyAnimateModelNode. Save3DAdvanced wraps up the process by exporting to formats like GLB/GLTF, OBJ, or FBX with control over scale and axis. The Meshy Toolset group (enable it with Ctrl+B) keeps the workflow modular—run only the nodes you need, skip what you don’t, and iterate quickly from one reference image to a polished 3D asset.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI, select the “Meshy Toolset” group, and press Ctrl+B to enable it. Ensure your Meshy API credentials are configured in the Meshy nodes or global settings (internet required).
Load your source image in the LoadImage node (try the provided clay_heart_girl.png). Use a clean, centered subject with minimal occlusion for best reconstruction.
In MeshyImageToModelNode, select Ultra 4K geometry mode (4096³) to capture fine detail as real geometry. Queue the graph to generate the initial mesh.

Route the result through MeshyRefineNode to clean and optimize geometry, then through MeshyTextureNode to generate PBR textures. Adjust quality or resolution settings as needed for your target platform.
Optionally, pass the textured model to MeshyRigModelNode to auto‑rig, then to MeshyAnimateModelNode to apply a simple motion preview. Skip these if you only need a static asset.
Configure Save3DAdvanced with your desired format (e.g., GLB/GLTF, OBJ, FBX), axis/up‑direction, and scale, then execute to export the final model.
suggestedUseCases: Product visualization: turn a packshot into a polished, exportable 3D model for web viewers or catalogs.
Game and film props: create detailed hero props where fabric stitching, wood grain, or embossed logos need to hold up in close‑ups.
AR/VR experiences: quickly generate high‑fidelity 3D assets from reference photos for immersive apps.
Concept iteration: convert moodboard images into tangible 3D studies for art direction and prototyping.
Digital collectibles: build detailed assets for showcase reels or interactive galleries from a single image.

faqItems.question: Do I need a Meshy account or API key to run this?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Meshy* nodes call the Meshy 7.1 API, so you’ll need a valid API key and an internet connection. Add your credentials in the node or ComfyUI settings before running.

faqItems.question: What kind of images produce the best 3D results?
faqItems.answer: Use a sharp, well‑lit image with a clear, centered subject and minimal occlusions. Three‑quarter or front views work well. Avoid motion blur, heavy compression, and busy backgrounds.

faqItems.question: How can I control polygon count and file size?
faqItems.answer: Ultra 4K produces very dense meshes. For lighter assets, use MeshyRefineNode to simplify/clean the geometry and reduce texture resolution in MeshyTextureNode if available. You can also export compact GLB/GLTF via Save3DAdvanced.

faqItems.question: Can I skip rigging and animation?
faqItems.answer: Absolutely. MeshyRigModelNode and MeshyAnimateModelNode are optional. For static assets, run MeshyImageToModelNode → MeshyRefineNode → MeshyTextureNode, then export with Save3DAdvanced.

faqItems.question: Does this work offline?
faqItems.answer: No. The Meshy nodes communicate with the Meshy service over the API, so an active internet connection is required for model generation, refinement, texturing, and rigging.

daa5bce3fc54.title: Wan ATI Trajectory Control
daa5bce3fc54.description: This workflow allows you to manually edit complicated animation trajectories using a path editor node.
daa5bce3fc54.metaDescription: Edit complex animation trajectories with precision using the Wan ATI Trajectory Control workflow in ComfyUI.
daa5bce3fc54.extendedDescription:
The 'Wan ATI Trajectory Control' workflow is designed to offer precise manual control over animation trajectories, making it an invaluable tool for creators looking to refine complex animations. At its core, the workflow utilizes a combination of nodes such as VHS_VideoCombine, FL_KsamplerPlus, and FL_PathAnimator, which work together to allow users to edit and control animation paths with precision. The Path Editor Node is particularly noteworthy, as it enables users to manually adjust trajectories, offering a level of customization that is often required in professional animation production. 

This workflow is especially useful because it bridges the gap between static image manipulation and dynamic video creation. By using nodes like VHS_DuplicateImages and LoadImage, users can start with a single image or a series of images and transform them into a fluid animation. The PrimitiveInt node is employed to handle integer values that might be needed for various parameters, ensuring that the workflow remains flexible and adaptable to different project requirements. This makes the workflow not only technically robust but also highly practical for a range of animation tasks.
howToUse: Load the Wan ATI Trajectory Control workflow in ComfyUI.
Import your initial image(s) using the LoadImage node.
Use the VHS_DuplicateImages node to create a sequence from your images.
Adjust the animation paths using the FL_PathAnimator node for precise trajectory control.
Combine the edited paths into a video using the VHS_VideoCombine node.
Export your final animation for use in your projects.
suggestedUseCases: Creating detailed animations from static images for marketing videos.
Developing educational content that requires precise animation paths.
Producing animated sequences for film or game development.
Enhancing motion graphics with customized trajectory controls.
Designing interactive media that involves complex animation paths.

faqItems.question: What is the main advantage of using the Path Editor Node?
faqItems.answer: The Path Editor Node allows for manual adjustment of animation trajectories, providing precise control over the movement paths, which is essential for complex animations.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow be used with any image format?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the LoadImage node supports various image formats, making it versatile for different types of projects.

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for beginners?
faqItems.answer: While it offers advanced features, the workflow is designed to be user-friendly, making it accessible to both beginners and experienced users with some initial guidance.

faqItems.question: How does the VHS_VideoCombine node contribute to the workflow?
faqItems.answer: The VHS_VideoCombine node is used to compile the edited image sequences into a cohesive video, ensuring smooth transitions and consistent animation flow.

faqItems.question: Can I customize the length of the generated audio?

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the audio matches my text prompt accurately?

faqItems.question: Is it possible to annotate my audio files?

db4717458b6a.title: LTX-2.3: ID LoRA
db4717458b6a.description: Generate personalized videos with synchronized audio from a text prompt, reference image, and short audio clip. Use ID-LoRA to adapt a person's appearance and voice in a single generative model.
db4717458b6a.metaDescription: Create personalized, lip-synced videos in ComfyUI using LTX-2.3 with ID-LoRA from a prompt, a face image, and a short audio clip.
db4717458b6a.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds personalized, lip-synced video clips by conditioning LTX-2.3 on three inputs: a reference image (appearance), a short audio clip (timing and vocal style), and a structured prompt (scene, transcript, and sound context). The core logic is encapsulated in a subgraph (the custom node with ID 98ee9e5b-467b-40aa-a534-36033f27d0b4), which orchestrates LTX-2.3 generation with ID-LoRA identity conditioning. LoadImage provides the face/pose reference, LoadAudio or RecordAudio supplies your speech, and SaveVideo writes the final video. A MarkdownNote in the canvas summarizes the structured prompt format and links to the LTX-2.3 and ID-LoRA resources.

Technically, ID-LoRA injects a lightweight identity adapter into the LTX-2.3 video diffusion process so the generated person matches the reference image without a full fine-tune. The prompt is split into three tags the subgraph expects: [VISUAL] (scene and appearance), [SPEECH] (the exact words to say), and [SOUNDS] (speaker style and ambient cues). The audio drives mouth shapes and timing, while [SPEECH] helps the model resolve phoneme-level detail for clearer lip articulation. The result is a short video of your subject speaking the provided line, visually aligned to the reference image and temporally synced to the audio.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the LTX-2.3 model files are available locally (see the Lightricks/LTX-2.3 repository if you need to download weights).
Add a clear, front-facing reference image via the LoadImage node (good lighting, minimal occlusion).
Provide the voice clip: either record a short, clean sample with RecordAudio or import one with LoadAudio (avoid music/noise; keep the speech steady).

Compose the structured prompt in the text field used by the generation subgraph, using three sections: [VISUAL]: describe scene and appearance; [SPEECH]: write the exact transcript; [SOUNDS]: describe vocal style and ambient sounds. Example: [VISUAL]: close-up interview lighting, neutral background. [SPEECH]: "Welcome to our channel; new videos drop every Friday." [SOUNDS]: warm, calm voice; quiet studio room tone.

Run the workflow. The subgraph (98ee9e5b-467b-40aa-a534-36033f27d0b4) will condition LTX-2.3 with ID-LoRA, align mouth movements to your audio and transcript, and produce frames. SaveVideo assembles the output as a video file.

Review the result. If needed, refine by: using a sharper reference image, cleaning the audio, tightening the [SPEECH] transcript to match the clip exactly, or unpacking the subgraph to adjust generation and save settings (e.g., resolution, fps).
suggestedUseCases: Personalized greetings or announcement videos using your own face and voice.
Creator intros/outros where a consistent on-screen identity delivers scripted lines.
Training or onboarding clips featuring a company spokesperson for multiple variations of the same script.
Localized or alternate-language lines: supply the new audio and transcript to keep identity consistent.
Quick previz for dialogue sequences where timing must match a reference read.

faqItems.question: Do I need to train anything to match the person’s identity?
faqItems.answer: No full training is required. The workflow uses ID-LoRA as a lightweight identity adapter applied at generation time. Provide a high-quality reference image to improve likeness.

faqItems.question: What should I put in the structured prompt?
faqItems.answer: Use three tags: [VISUAL] for scene and appearance details, [SPEECH] for the exact words to say (match your audio), and [SOUNDS] for the speaker’s vocal style and any ambient room tone. A precise [SPEECH] section helps produce clearer lip shapes.

faqItems.question: How do I get the best lip sync?
faqItems.answer: Use a clean, dry voice recording (no background music), speak at a steady pace, and ensure the [SPEECH] transcript matches the audio exactly. Choose a front-facing, well-lit reference image so the mouth region is clear.

faqItems.question: Does the output include audio?
faqItems.answer: The workflow drives visual sync from your audio. Whether the final video file contains an embedded audio track depends on the SaveVideo configuration in your setup. If you get a silent video, you can mux the original audio in a video editor or unpack the subgraph to integrate audio muxing.

dba8340fd0f3.title: Qwen-Image ControlNet Model Patch
dba8340fd0f3.description: Control image generation using Qwen-Image ControlNet models. Supports canny, depth, and inpainting controls through model patching.
dba8340fd0f3.metaDescription: Enhance image generation with Qwen-Image ControlNet models using canny, depth, and inpainting controls for customized results.
dba8340fd0f3.extendedDescription:
The Qwen-Image ControlNet Model Patch workflow is designed to provide enhanced control over image generation through the use of Qwen-Image models. This workflow integrates several advanced nodes, including KSampler, CLIPTextEncode, and QwenImageDiffsynthControlnet, to allow for precise manipulation of image attributes such as canny, depth, and inpainting. By leveraging the ModelPatchLoader node, users can apply patches to models, enabling dynamic adjustments and improved image quality. This workflow is particularly useful for artists and designers who need to generate images with specific stylistic or thematic elements, as it allows for detailed customization using ControlNet techniques.

Technically, the workflow operates by first loading the necessary models and reference images, then processing these inputs through a series of nodes that encode, decode, and apply the desired transformations. The VAELoader and UNETLoader nodes play a crucial role in managing the image data, while the CLIPLoader and CLIPTextEncode nodes handle text-based prompts to guide the image generation process. The integration of the QwenImageDiffsynthControlnet node allows for the application of ControlNet models to refine image details, making this workflow a powerful tool for generating high-quality, customized images.
howToUse: Load the Qwen-Image ControlNet Model Patch workflow in ComfyUI.

dc1311a65bc4.title: Seedance2.0: First-Last-Frame to Video
dc1311a65bc4.description: Upload the first and last frames of your video. Generate a high-quality video sequence using the Seedance2.0 model.
dc1311a65bc4.metaDescription: Seedance 2.0 FLF2V in ComfyUI: generate stable, identity-consistent videos from first and last frames using boundary-conditioned diffusion.
dc1311a65bc4.extendedDescription:
Seedance 2.0 brings a boundary‑conditioned approach to video generation: supply the first and last frames, and the model synthesizes the in‑between motion with striking temporal stability. Instead of guessing a trajectory from a single image or relying on text prompts, the pipeline conditions on both endpoints to infer a coherent path for objects, lighting, and camera movement. In ComfyUI, this is encapsulated by the ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode, which takes two images and produces a full sequence that faithfully lands on your final frame.

This first‑last‑frame to video (FLF2V) method reduces identity drift, flicker, and composition shifts that commonly plague single‑frame or text‑to‑video methods. Unlike basic frame interpolation—which can only warp what already exists—Seedance 2.0 synthesizes novel content between your keyframes while preserving structure and intent. The result is cleaner motion planning, stronger subject consistency, and more predictable outcomes for real productions.
howToUse: Prepare two images: the exact first and last frames you want. Use the same resolution and aspect ratio for both to ensure clean conditioning.
Add two LoadImage nodes in ComfyUI and load your first and last frames. Connect their outputs to the corresponding inputs on ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode.
Ensure the Seedance 2.0 model is available and selected by the ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode (follow your installation’s model placement conventions).
Configure the generation timeline in ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode (e.g., desired frame count and FPS). For reproducible results, fix the seed in your ComfyUI session or node settings.
Execute the graph to preview the generated sequence. If motion is too aggressive or not reaching the desired composition, refine your end frame or adjust duration.
Connect the node’s video output to SaveVideo, set your target FPS and encoding, and run to export the final clip.
suggestedUseCases: Storyboard-to-shot: animate between two keyframes to quickly validate motion and timing before full production.
Product demos: rotate or reposition a product from A to B with stable identity and controlled end composition.
UI/UX motion design: craft polished transitions between interface states using precise start and end visuals.
Cinematic blocking: previsualize camera or subject repositioning with reliable landings on the final frame.
Before-after visualizations: show transformations (e.g., environment, space planning) with a coherent narrative arc.

faqItems.question: How is this different from frame interpolation between two images?
faqItems.answer: Interpolation warps existing pixels from the endpoints. Seedance 2.0 synthesizes new in-between frames using two-endpoint conditioning, enabling plausible motion and detail that aren’t present in either input while still honoring both boundaries.

faqItems.question: Do my first and last frames need to match in size or aspect ratio?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode expects matching resolutions for stable results. Prepare both frames at the same size before loading them with LoadImage to avoid unintended rescaling or artifacts.

faqItems.question: Can it handle large viewpoint or subject changes between the first and last frames?
faqItems.answer: It can infer substantial motion, but extreme jumps may increase artifacts or ambiguity. For best results, keep the endpoints visually related and adjust duration (more frames) to give the model room to plan a coherent path.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure consistent, repeatable outputs?
faqItems.answer: Use a fixed seed and keep inputs constant. In ComfyUI, set or lock the seed at the graph or node level, then rerun to reproduce the same sequence deterministically.

dc4b3f6dab6e.title: Step 2: Contact Sheet Workflow
dc4b3f6dab6e.description: Upload the fashion editorial and product image. Generate 8 distinct angle variations with product consistency from only 2 Nano Banana generations.

dc4b3f6dab6e.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds a fast, repeatable contact-sheet generator for fashion products. You provide two inputs—a fashion editorial reference and a clean product image—and the graph produces eight distinct angle variations while preserving product identity. The pipeline pivots on Nano Banana Pro for image generation and uses a small, consistent set of prompts to drive variety without drifting from the product look. Outputs are compiled into a vertical 9:16 contact sheet at 4K resolution (2160x3840) for quick review or social/merchandising handoff.

Technically, the graph uses LoadImage to bring in your editorial reference and product packshot. A PrimitiveStringMultiline node holds the eight angle directives (you can edit these to change viewpoints), while a PrimitiveNode stores simple numeric settings (such as the number of angles or seeds). GeminiImage2Node (configured for gemini-3-pro-image-preview) can be used as a helper to analyze the editorial reference or produce caption text that feeds into your prompt block. Two essentials nodes (UUIDs 68c58c16-e698-45a4-97f9-54ae8eb9dee9 and 487baed2-dc27-49c3-a6b2-0bf45a53e64d from comfyui_essentials) handle image collation and layout with BatchImagesNode assembling the eight results, RegexReplace cleaning file names, and SaveImage writing a single 8-up contact sheet plus optional individual frames. The result is a compact, reliable step that expands only two Nano Banana generations into eight consistent angles.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the nodes panel. Confirm custom nodes from comfyui_essentials are installed so UUIDs 68c58c16-e698-45a4-97f9-54ae8eb9dee9 and 487baed2-dc27-49c3-a6b2-0bf45a53e64d resolve correctly.
Use the LoadImage nodes to import your fashion editorial reference and your product image (ideally a clean packshot or masked image). Verify both preview correctly.

Open the PrimitiveStringMultiline node and review the angle directives (e.g., front, three-quarter, profile, low-angle, over-shoulder, back, etc.). Edit or replace this list to match the eight angles you want.

Select Nano Banana Pro as the model in the generation nodes in the graph (where applicable) and confirm the output resolution is set for vertical 9:16 at 4K (2160x3840). Use the PrimitiveNode to set any numeric parameters (e.g., seed or count = 8).

Optionally enable or wire GeminiImage2Node (gemini-3-pro-image-preview) to extract captions or angle hints from the editorial image, then feed those into your prompt block. If you prefer manual control, leave the multiline prompt as your sole driver.

Run the workflow. BatchImagesNode will collect the eight results, the essentials layout nodes will assemble the 8-up grid, RegexReplace will sanitize file names, and SaveImage will write the final contact sheet (plus optional individual frames) to your chosen output folder.
suggestedUseCases: E‑commerce PDP build-outs: generate a consistent set of eight product angles to complement editorial imagery.
Art direction alignment: quickly validate camera angles and styling against an editorial reference before a full render pass.
Social and campaign planning: produce a vertical 9:16 4K contact sheet for decks, storyboards, or Instagram/TikTok story previews.
Marketplace listing standardization: enforce a repeatable set of angles across SKUs to improve visual consistency.
Client review rounds: share a single consolidated sheet of eight angles for faster approvals.

faqItems.answer: No. GeminiImage2Node (gemini-3-pro-image-preview) is an optional helper for deriving captions or angle hints from the editorial reference. You can rely entirely on the manual directives in PrimitiveStringMultiline if you prefer full control.

dcf86ba5de5a.title: Tripo P2: Text to Model
dcf86ba5de5a.description: Generate production-ready 3D meshes from text prompts with Tripo P2, featuring native quad topology and mesh budgets up to 50,000 triangles or 25,000 quads. dcf86ba5de5a.metaDescription: Turn text prompts into clean, quad-based 3D models with Tripo P2 in ComfyUI. Texture, rig, retarget, convert, and export as FBX or GLB.
dcf86ba5de5a.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns text prompts into production-ready 3D models using the Tripo P2 generator. At its core, the TripoPSeriesTextToModelNode calls the Tripo API to synthesize geometry directly from your prompt, with controllable mesh budgets up to 50,000 triangles or 25,000 quads and an optional native quad topology toggle. From there, you can branch into downstream steps—TripoTextureNodeV2 for PBR-style texturing, TripoRigNode for automatic rig generation, TripoRetargetNode for animation reuse, TripoConversionNode for compatibility adjustments, and Save3DAdvanced for final export.

Technically, the workflow orchestrates an end-to-end text-to-3D pipeline within ComfyUI. The TripoPSeriesTextToModelNode handles model creation via the Tripo P2 service, while optional post-processing nodes refine the asset for real-world use. If the quad option is enabled, the model is generated with native quads suited to rigging and deformation; if disabled, the mesh is triangle-based for lightweight real-time deployment. Save3DAdvanced enforces the correct export pathway: FBX when quads are enabled (connect to the right slot) and GLB when quads are disabled. Helpful MarkdownNote nodes embedded in the graph provide setup reminders and tips.

This setup is ideal for game characters and props, hard-surface assets, and high-volume pipelines that need clean, predictable topology. Because rigging, retargeting, texturing, conversion, and export are integrated, you can go from prompt to engine-ready asset in one place, while keeping full control over topology and file format.
howToUse: Load the Tripo P2: Text to Model workflow in ComfyUI, then enable the Tripo Toolset group (select the group and press Ctrl+B). Review any MarkdownNote nodes for setup tips.

Open the TripoPSeriesTextToModelNode and enter your text prompt. Set your mesh budget (up to ~50k tris or 25k quads) and choose whether to enable the quad option based on your target use (rigging vs lightweight real-time).
Run the graph to generate the base mesh. Inspect the preview or intermediate outputs to confirm geometry quality before proceeding.

Optional: Add textures with TripoTextureNodeV2 (choose desired resolution and maps as available). If your asset is a character, generate a rig with TripoRigNode, then use TripoRetargetNode to apply animations from a source skeleton or clip.
Use TripoConversionNode if you need to conform the asset to downstream requirements (for example, adjusting scale, orientation, or ensuring a preferred format pipeline).
Export with Save3DAdvanced: when the quad option is enabled, connect Save3DAdvanced to the right FBX slot; when it’s disabled, export the GLB output. Save and validate in your DCC or game engine.
suggestedUseCases: Game-ready props and characters with clean, rig-friendly quad topology for reliable deformation.
Hard-surface concept assets (weapons, tools, gadgets) at controlled triangle/quad budgets for real-time engines.
Rapid prototyping of AR/VR assets with predictable export formats (GLB for quick previews, FBX for DCC pipelines).
High-volume 3D content generation where consistent topology and automated rig/retarget steps reduce manual labor.

faqItems.question: When should I enable the quad option, and how does it affect export?
faqItems.answer: Enable quads for assets that need clean deformation (characters, cloth, flexible props). With quads enabled, connect Save3DAdvanced to the right slot to export FBX. If you leave it disabled, the mesh is triangle-based and should be exported as GLB.

faqItems.question: How should I set the mesh budget?
faqItems.answer: Use lower budgets for lightweight real-time previews and higher budgets (up to ~50,000 triangles or 25,000 quads) for final game assets or detailed props. Start conservative and iterate upward based on silhouette and detail needs.

faqItems.question: Can I rig and retarget animations in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Use TripoRigNode to generate a rig (especially for humanoids), then TripoRetargetNode to apply animations from a source skeleton or clip. Verify joint names and scale in your target engine after export.

faqItems.question: What texture outputs can I expect from TripoTextureNodeV2?
faqItems.answer: TripoTextureNodeV2 can generate PBR-oriented textures (for example, base color and normal), depending on settings and model specifics. Choose your desired resolution and verify material hookup in your DCC or engine.

def270551fbe.title: WaveSpeed: FlashVSR Video Upscale

This workflow allows users to upscale videos to 720p, 1080p, 2K, or 4K, providing a detailed analysis of how each resolution affects video quality. By employing the WavespeedFlashVSRNode, the workflow enhances video detail, reduces artifacts, and maintains consistent motion, ensuring a natural-looking output. howToUse: Load your video into the workflow using the LoadVideo node.
Select the desired resolution for upscaling: 720p, 1080p, 2K, or 4K.
Process the video through the WavespeedFlashVSRNode to upscale it.
Save the upscaled video using the SaveVideo node.
Compare the outputs by examining detail, artifact presence, and motion consistency.
Decide on the best resolution based on your quality requirements and processing capacity.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing home videos to a higher resolution for improved viewing experience.
Upscaling marketing videos to ensure high-quality presentation across different devices.

Optimizing video content for streaming platforms that require various resolution outputs.

faqItems.question: What is the main advantage of using FlashVSR for video upscaling?
faqItems.answer: FlashVSR enhances video detail and reduces artifacts while maintaining consistent motion, providing a natural-looking output at various resolutions.

faqItems.question: How does the choice of resolution affect processing time?
faqItems.answer: Higher resolutions, such as 2K and 4K, typically require more processing time due to the increased detail and data involved in upscaling.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow be used for any video format?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports common video formats, but compatibility should be verified based on the LoadVideo node's capabilities.

faqItems.question: How do I decide which resolution to choose for upscaling?
faqItems.answer: Consider your quality requirements, the intended display size, and processing capacity. Higher resolutions offer better detail but require more resources.

The integration of these nodes allows users to seamlessly convert creative ideas into visual representations, making it particularly useful for artists, designers, and content creators who require quick and reliable image generation from text descriptions.
howToUse: Load the ComfyUI workflow and ensure all necessary nodes are present: RunwayTextToImageNode, LoadImage, SaveImage, and MarkdownNote.
Enter your text prompt into the RunwayTextToImageNode. This is where you describe the image you want to generate.
Ensure your network environment is secure and allows access from '127.0.0.1' or 'localhost' to connect to the API.

Use the SaveImage node to save the generated image to your desired location.
Review any notes or instructions in the MarkdownNote node for additional guidance or troubleshooting tips.
suggestedUseCases: Creating concept art for video games or films based on textual descriptions.
Generating visual content for marketing materials or social media posts.
Assisting writers in visualizing scenes from their novels or scripts.
Designing unique artwork or illustrations for personal projects.
Developing educational materials that require illustrative support.

faqItems.question: What types of text prompts work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Descriptive and detailed prompts yield the best results. Including specific characteristics like colors, styles, and objects can help the AI model generate more accurate images.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow without an internet connection?
faqItems.answer: No, this workflow requires an internet connection to access Runway's API, which is essential for processing the text prompts into images.

faqItems.question: How can I troubleshoot connection issues with the API?
faqItems.answer: Ensure your network settings allow access from '127.0.0.1' or 'localhost'. Check your firewall and security settings to confirm they permit API connections.

faqItems.question: Is there a limit to the number of images I can generate?
